All have believed in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers, saying, “We make no distinction between any of His messengers.” And they say, “We hear and we obey. We seek Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination.”
interpretation: This verse presents faith as a complete, integrated submission: the Messenger and the believers accept the revelation from God and affirm all the essential objects of belief—God, His angels, His revealed books, and His messengers—without dividing loyalty among them by accepting some prophets and rejecting others. The believer’s response to divine guidance is not selective belief but hearing and obeying, joined with humility and a request for forgiveness, because even sincere obedience is accompanied by human shortcomings. The verse thus teaches that true faith unites believers around God’s revelation, honors the whole prophetic chain, and orients the heart toward accountability and final return to God.

translation: Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. It will have the good it earned, and it will bear the evil it earned. Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or err. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse teaches that divine obligation and accountability are always proportionate to human ability: God never commands a soul to do what is beyond its strength, and each person is answerable only for what he or she freely chooses and earns. The believer is therefore not crushed by despair over weakness, because the door of repentance and supplication remains open. The verse then trains the heart to ask God for mercy regarding forgetfulness and mistakes, for relief from unbearable burdens, and for pardon, forgiveness, and compassion. It ends by affirming that true protection and victory come only from God, so the believer relies on Him alone against every form of opposition to faith.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: The letters Alif, Lam, Meem are among the disjointed letters that open certain surahs; their exact meaning is known only to Allah, and they serve as a sign of the Quran’s divine origin and inimitability, since it is composed of the same Arabic letters known to its first audience yet cannot be matched.

translation: Allah — there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence.
interpretation: This verse affirms pure monotheism: Allah alone is the only true God, with no partner or rival in divinity. He is the Ever-Living, whose life is perfect and eternal, and the Sustainer/Self-Subsisting, who exists independently and upon whom every created thing depends for its existence, order, and continued being. Therefore all worship, reliance, and ultimate need belong to Him alone.

translation: He has sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it, and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur’an is a revelation from God, sent to the Prophet Muhammad with truth and justice, and that it authenticates the earlier divine scriptures in their original, God-given form. Naming the Torah and the Gospel shows that they too are revealed books, not merely human writings, and that God’s guidance to humanity has been continuous through His prophets. The Qur’an is thus presented as the confirming and guarding revelation: it verifies the truth in what came before it and remains the final authoritative criterion for belief and guidance.

translation: before, as guidance for mankind; and He sent down the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment; and Allah is All-Mighty, Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: The earlier scriptures were revealed before the Qur’an and served as guidance for people, while al-Furqan is the decisive revelation that separates truth from falsehood and right from wrong. Rejecting Allah’s revealed signs is not a light matter; it brings a severe punishment because it amounts to denying the clear guidance sent by the All-Mighty, who has full power and from whom retribution is certain for those who persist in disbelief.

translation: Indeed, Allah—nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah’s perfect and all-encompassing knowledge. Nothing whatsoever—whether in the earth or in the heavens, whether outward or inward, present or future, small or great—escapes His awareness. It establishes that He alone is fully aware of every hidden reality, and therefore all creatures are completely subject to His knowledge and accountability. This truth calls the believer to sincerity, vigilance, and reliance upon Allah, knowing that no deed, intention, or secret is overlooked, and that perfect justice belongs to Him.

translation: He is the One Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. There is no god but Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God alone is the Creator and Fashioner of human life, exercising absolute authority over the formation of each person in the womb according to His infinite wisdom. It negates any claim to divinity besides Him and grounds every stage of creation in His power and wise purpose, so that human beings should recognize their total dependence on Him and worship Him alone.

translation: He is the One who sent down to you the Book. In it are clear and precise verses—they are the mother of the Book—and others that are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what is ambiguous from it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation. But none knows its interpretation except God. And those firmly grounded in knowledge say, “We believe in it; all is from our Lord.” And none take heed except people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur’an has a foundational core of clear verses that define belief, worship, law, and guidance, and other verses whose full meaning may not be immediately evident. The clear verses are the criterion by which ambiguous passages must be understood, so no one may isolate ambiguity to generate confusion or division. Those whose hearts are crooked pursue ambiguous verses to cause fitnah and to claim hidden meanings, but the ultimate reality of such verses is known only to God. The truly learned are not shaken by what they cannot fully grasp; they submit, affirm that the whole revelation is from their Lord, and refuse to place their limited understanding above divine guidance. Only those with sound reason and purified hearts take heed.

translation: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
interpretation: It teaches that guidance is not a one-time possession to be presumed upon; the believer constantly depends on God to keep the heart firm on the path He has shown. The plea “do not let our hearts deviate” means protect us from turning away from truth through doubt, desire, or misguidance after having known the right way. Asking for “mercy from Yourself” is a request for a special, divinely sourced mercy that preserves faith, forgives shortcomings, and strengthens the heart. The closing name al-Wahhab grounds the supplication in God’s generous, repeated giving: He alone freely grants guidance, steadfastness, and mercy without being obliged by anyone. Thus it combines humility, gratitude for guidance, and reliance on God for continuing grace.

translation: Our Lord, indeed You will gather mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse affirms the certainty of resurrection and final judgment. Allah, as Lord and Sovereign, will inevitably gather all people—past and future—for the Day of Reckoning, and His promise of reward and punishment is absolutely truthful and unchanging. It teaches that awareness of this meeting should shape human conduct: the believer lives with accountability, hope, and trust in divine justice, while the denier is warned that no promise of Allah can ever be broken.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve—their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against Allah; and those are the fuel of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse teaches that rejection of God cannot be compensated or shielded by worldly resources or descendants. Wealth and children, which people often treat as extensions of their power and security, have no value in averting divine judgment when faith is absent. Such people do not merely miss reward; they become the very material that sustains the Fire, meaning their destiny is ruin and their worldly supports collapse into the punishment they earned.

translation: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject God's signs are following the same destructive path as Pharaoh's people and earlier nations. Their denial was not merely an intellectual disagreement; it was a rejection of clear divine guidance, and so God took them to task for their sins. The verse establishes that God's punishment is severe for those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing, and that no worldly power or wealth can protect them from it.

translation: Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This is a decisive warning that disbelief is not merely an intellectual error but a rebellion against God that will inevitably fail. Those who persist in rejecting the truth will be defeated in this world and then gathered into Hell in the Hereafter, where their final abode is the most miserable resting place. The verse assures the faithful that God's judgment is certain and that no worldly power or denial can escape it.

translation: There has already been a sign for you in the two groups that met: one group fighting in the way of Allah and another disbelieving. They saw them as twice their number with the eye. And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those who have insight.
interpretation: This refers to the Battle of Badr, where Allah caused the disbelievers to perceive the small Muslim force as twice their own number, a divine sign and means of support that struck fear into the enemy. It teaches that victory and aid come from Allah alone, not from numbers or material strength, and that this event is a profound lesson for those who possess inner insight to recognize Allah's power and trust in His help.

translation: Beautified for people is the love of desires—of women, children, heaped-up sums of gold and silver, fine branded horses, cattle, and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return [i.e., Paradise].
interpretation: This verse explains that human beings are naturally drawn to the pleasures and attractions of this world, which have been made to appear appealing: relationships, children, wealth, fine animals, and property. These are part of the temporary enjoyment of worldly life, not the ultimate goal. The verse does not forbid them in themselves, but warns against letting love of them dominate the heart and distract from God. The true and lasting good is what is with Allah: the best final destination and return.

translation: Say, "Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who fear Allah, with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah. And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants."
interpretation: This verse calls people to measure all worldly attractions against what God has prepared for the God-conscious, and it declares that the reward with their Lord is far better. Those who adopt taqwa—guarding themselves from disobedience and living in awareness of God—are given gardens beneath which rivers flow, perpetual dwelling therein, purified companions, and, above all, God’s pleasure and approval. The greatest element is divine ridwan, because it is God’s own acceptance and good pleasure, beyond any material or sensory delight. The ending, “And Allah is Seeing of His servants,” means God fully observes the inner and outer states of people, so He knows who truly deserves this reward and will recompense with perfect justice and mercy.

translation: Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse describes the true believers as those who, having professed faith, do not become complacent or self-satisfied; rather, they humbly turn to God in prayer, acknowledging their sins and asking for forgiveness, while seeking refuge from the torment of Hellfire. It teaches that faith must be accompanied by repentance, supplication, and a deep awareness of accountability before God.

translation: The patient, the truthful, the devoutly obedient, those who spend [in the way of Allah], and those who seek forgiveness in the early dawn.
interpretation: These are among the distinguishing marks of true faith: enduring hardship and remaining steadfast in obedience; truthfulness in belief, speech, and conduct; constant humble devotion and submission to Allah; generous giving from what Allah has provided; and earnestly seeking forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours, when hearts are most attentive, supplication is most sincere, and reliance on Allah’s mercy is deepest.

translation: Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge, maintaining justice. There is no deity except Him, the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute oneness of God by the highest possible testimony: God Himself testifies that none is worthy of worship except Him, and the angels and those endowed with true knowledge join in that testimony. It teaches that authentic knowledge leads to recognition of God's exclusive divinity, and that His lordship is inseparable from justice—He governs all affairs with perfect equity, wronging no one. The repetition of “there is no deity except Him” confirms this truth without doubt, while the names the Mighty and the Wise show that His sole authority is neither weak nor arbitrary but is joined to perfect power and perfect wisdom.

translation: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Book did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse declares that the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam—sincere submission to Him alone, the universal message brought by all prophets. The People of the Book did not split over this truth because of ignorance, but after clear knowledge reached them, motivated by envy and rivalry among themselves. Thus, rejecting Allah’s revelations after they have been made clear invites a swift reckoning from Allah.

translation: Then if they dispute with you, say, 'I have submitted myself wholly to Allah, and so have those who follow me.' And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, 'Have you submitted?' If they submit, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance. And Allah is Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet's answer to stubborn argumentation is not endless disputation but total surrender of his whole self to God, and that the true criterion of faith is whether a person, whether given earlier scripture or unlettered, accepts that same submission. Guidance is not something the Prophet can force upon hearts; it follows from willing submission, while rejection leaves him responsible only for delivering the message. Since God fully sees His servants, outward claims and inward loyalties are known to Him, and final judgment belongs to Him alone.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and kill the prophets unjustly and kill those who enjoin justice among the people — give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that combining rejection of Allah’s revelation with unjust violence against His prophets and against those who call people to justice merits an agonizing punishment; the command to “give them tidings” is an ironic announcement of inevitable retribution rather than good news.

translation: Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse describes people whose apparent good works are rendered null and void because they are cut off from faith in God and from accepting His messengers and signs. Since deeds are only truly fruitful when rooted in correct belief and sincere submission to God, all their efforts lose their benefit in worldly life and earn no reward in the Hereafter. On the Day of Judgment they will find no protector, intercessor, or helper to rescue them from God’s punishment or to restore what they have lost.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They are invited to the Book of Allah so that it may judge between them, then a group of them turns away while they are averse.
interpretation: This verse censures the People of the Book who, though granted knowledge of revelation, refuse to submit to God's Book when it is invoked to settle their disputes. Their turning away shows that their claim to scripture is not sincere; they accept only what suits their desires and reject divine judgment when it contradicts their whims. It is a warning against selective faith and a call to wholehearted submission to Allah's ruling.

translation: That is because they said, 'The Fire will not touch us except for a limited number of days.' And what they used to fabricate deceived them in their religion.
interpretation: This verse refutes a false sense of security invented by some who claim a special exemption from divine punishment: that Hell will only touch them briefly. Such a claim is not from God but a fabrication, and because they kept repeating and trusting it, it deluded them in their religion, making them careless about God's commands and judgment. The verse teaches that no inherited privilege, ethnic or religious identity, or self-serving doctrine can override accountability before God; lies about God's mercy and justice become a veil that prevents repentance and submission to revealed truth. It is a warning against letting humanly devised assurances replace the clear standards of the Book of God.

translation: So how [will it be] when We gather them together for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be repaid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical warning meant to awaken heedlessness and false security. It confronts those who live as though accountability can be postponed, asking how they will fare when God gathers all creation for the inevitable Day whose coming admits no doubt. On that Day, divine justice will be exact and complete: every soul will receive precisely what its deeds deserve, nothing withheld and nothing added unjustly. The verse thus calls the conscience to take responsibility now, before a reckoning where no one can be wronged and no one can escape.

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that ultimate authority, dominion, honor, and humiliation belong exclusively to Allah. No king, ruler, or person possesses power independently; whatever status or authority anyone has is granted by Allah according to His wisdom and can be removed by Him at any time. Therefore, believers are taught to turn directly to Allah as the true Owner of all authority, not to fear or rely absolutely on worldly powers. The phrase 'in Your hand is all good' means every decree, including the granting and removal of power, ultimately serves a wise and good purpose, even when its immediate appearance may be painful or confusing. Since Allah is over all things competent, His disposal of worldly affairs is governed by perfect knowledge, will, and power.

translation: You cause the night to enter into the day and You cause the day to enter into the night. You bring the living out of the dead and You bring the dead out of the living. And You provide for whom You will without measure.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah’s sole sovereignty over the alternation of time, the transformation of life and death, and the giving of sustenance. It teaches that He directly governs these opposites—night and day, life and death—and that His provision is not restricted by human calculations or causes. Therefore, believers should recognize His absolute power, rely on Him alone, and trust that He can create life from death and provide beyond all expectation.

translation: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. And whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, except that you fear a danger from them. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final destination.
interpretation: The verse forbids believers from giving the disbelievers loyalty, support, or allegiance in preference to the believers, because such loyalty separates a person from Allah's protection and guidance. It allows only a limited outward caution when believers genuinely fear harm or persecution, provided the heart remains firm in faith and does not approve of disbelief or betray the Muslim community. The warning that Allah warns you of Himself means that His punishment is severe and His rights must not be neglected; He alone is the ultimate judge, and every person will return to Him for accountability.

translation: Say, "If you conceal what is in your chests or disclose it, Allah knows it. And He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. And Allah is capable of all things."
interpretation: This verse establishes that God’s knowledge is absolute and indivisible: He knows the secret intentions of the heart just as He knows outward words and deeds, and His knowledge encompasses the whole of creation. Because His power is unlimited, He is able to bring every hidden motive and every open action to account. The servant is therefore called to inward sincerity and vigilance, realizing that nothing within the self is outside God’s knowledge or beyond His power to judge, forgive, and recompense.

translation: On the Day when every soul will find what it did of good brought present, and what it did of evil; it will wish that between it and that evil there were a far distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Compassionate to His servants.
interpretation: This verse teaches that on the Day of Judgment every deed will become manifest and unavoidable, so that each person sees the true worth of their good and the true burden of their evil. The soul’s wish for an immense distance from its evil reflects the horror of guilt and the dread of accountability. Allah’s warning is itself an act of mercy: He cautions people against His displeasure so they may repent and return, and His compassion toward His servants means He does not leave them unaware of the consequences of their choices.

translation: Say, 'If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.'
interpretation: True love of God is not a mere claim or sentiment; it is proven by following the Prophet’s guidance. That following attracts God’s love and brings forgiveness of sins, for God’s nature is forgiving and merciful.

translation: Say, 'Obey Allah and the Messenger.' But if they turn away, then indeed, Allah does not love the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that obedience to the Messenger is inseparable from obedience to God, since the Messenger conveys God's commands. To turn away from that obedience is to reject God's authority, and such rejection places a person among the disbelievers, whom God does not love.

translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds.
interpretation: This means that God singled out these prophets and righteous families for special favor, prophethood, and guidance, making them exemplary among humanity and raising their mention and rank above others. It affirms that divine selection is by God’s wisdom, not by human lineage or claim, and that He chooses whom He wills to carry His message and to be honored in both this life and the Hereafter.

translation: Descendants, one from another. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This means that the chosen families and prophets mentioned are a single connected line of spiritual descendants: they share the same divinely guided creed, mission, and selection, one generation succeeding another. Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, so He hears all words and knows all hearts, and He knows best whom to choose, guide, and entrust with His message.

translation: When the wife of Imran said, “My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated [to Your service], so accept it from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.”
interpretation: The wife of Imran consecrates the child in her womb exclusively to God’s service, seeking His acceptance of this vow. She calls upon God as the One who hears her supplication and knows her sincere intention, expressing complete reliance on Him and hoping that her offering will be accepted and her child devoted to worship and obedience.

translation: When she delivered her, she said, 'My Lord, I have delivered a female.' And Allah knew best what she delivered. 'And the male is not like the female. And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the rejected.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s knowledge and purpose surpass human expectations. The mother of Mary had hoped for a son, likely because a male could more readily serve in the temple, but God knew the true worth of the female child she bore. The statement that the male is not like the female indicates that the child God gave—Mary—was not to be measured by the ordinary expectations attached to gender or service; she was chosen for a unique and exalted role. Naming her Mary and seeking refuge for her and her descendants from Satan expresses a deep parental supplication: true protection comes from God alone, and the greatest legacy a parent can seek for a child is safety from the accursed enemy and preservation in faith. The verse thus affirms God’s wisdom in granting what is best, the special status of Mary, and the need for continual reliance upon God for oneself and one’s offspring.

translation: So her Lord accepted her with gracious acceptance, and caused her to grow in a beautiful growth, and put her under the care of Zakariyya. Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said, 'O Maryam, from where is this to you?' She said, 'It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without measure.'
interpretation: The passage presents Maryam as a locus of divine grace from the outset: her acceptance and growth are attributed directly to her Lord, indicating that sanctity is not merely a human achievement but a divine cultivation. Zakariyya's guardianship serves as the visible means, while the recurring provision in the mihrab reveals a hidden economy of grace: the servant devoted to God may receive sustenance through means that bypass ordinary calculations. Maryam's answer—'It is from God'—is the interpretive key: it denies any independent power to creatures and ascribes all sustenance to God's unrestricted will, whose giving is not constrained by scarcity, merit, or accounting.

translation: Thereupon Zechariah prayed to his Lord; he said, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."
interpretation: This verse shows Zakariyya turning to God in sincere supplication after witnessing a sign of God's power. He does not ask for a child merely as a personal desire, but asks for "good offspring"—a pure, righteous, and blessed descendant who would worship and serve God. By saying "from Yourself," he acknowledges that such a gift can only come from God's grace, not from ordinary means. His closing words, "Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication," express confident trust that God hears, accepts, and answers prayer according to His wisdom and mercy.

translation: Then the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the mihrab, saying: Allah gives you good tidings of John, confirming a word from Allah, and honorable, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse depicts the divine response to Zakariyya's earnest supplication. While he was absorbed in prayer in the sanctuary, the angels announced that God would grant him Yahya, a son whose very existence would defy the usual causes. Yahya's mission would include affirming the truth of Jesus, described as a word from Allah, meaning the Messiah brought into being by God's command. The titles given to Yahya—master, chaste, and prophet—signify his moral excellence, self-restraint from unlawful desires, and high standing among God's righteous servants. Thus the verse teaches that God's grace can surpass human expectations and that true honor lies in piety, purity, and prophethood.

translation: He said, "My Lord, how can I have a boy when old age has reached me and my wife is barren?" He said, "Thus Allah does what He wills."
interpretation: This verse shows that Zakariyya’s question was not a denial of Allah’s power but an inquiry into how the promise would come about, given the apparent impossibility of his old age and his wife’s barrenness. The divine answer teaches that Allah is not bound by ordinary causes: when He wills something, He brings it about however He wishes. Old age and barrenness cannot prevent His decree, so the believer should trust His promise and not judge His power by visible means alone.

translation: He said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and morning."
interpretation: Zakariyya asked for a sign to reassure his heart concerning the promised son. The sign given was that his tongue would be withheld from ordinary conversation with people for three days, so that he could communicate only by gestures. This temporary restraint was itself a miraculous indication of God's power and of the truth of the glad tidings. It was joined with the command to remember God abundantly and glorify Him at the two ends of the day, showing that the sign was not merely a deprivation but an invitation to deeper devotion, gratitude, and remembrance of God.

translation: And [mention] when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds.'
interpretation: This means that Allah singled Maryam out for His special favor: He chose her for sincere worship and for the miraculous birth of Jesus, purified her from sin, disbelief, and every impurity, and elevated her above the women of her time through her piety, chastity, and the great signs He worked through her. Her being chosen twice points to a selection for righteousness and service, and then a further distinction and honor that made her an exemplary believer and a sign for humankind.

translation: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow.
interpretation: This is a directive to Maryam that true service to God begins with inward qunut—steadfast, humble devotion—and expresses itself in the physical acts of prayer: prostration and bowing. By adding “with those who bow,” it directs her not to a private piety alone but to worship in the company of the believing worshippers, making her a participant in the communal submission to God and a model of humble obedience.

translation: That is from the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you. And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to determine] which of them would take charge of Mary; nor were you with them when they disputed.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine origin of the Qur’anic account: the events surrounding Mary’s upbringing and guardianship belonged to unseen history that the Prophet could not have witnessed or learned from his surroundings. Their precise disclosure therefore serves as proof of revelation and prophethood. It also shows that God directly arranged Mary’s protection and nurture through the casting of lots and the ensuing dispute among her guardians, turning their rivalry into the means by which His chosen servant was cared for.

translation: When the angels said, “O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a Word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, eminent in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near.”
interpretation: The angels announce to Mary that God grants her the glad tidings of a Word from Him: Jesus, the Messiah, son of Mary. He is called a “Word” from God because he came into being by God’s command “Be” without a father, as a direct act of divine creative power. God names him the Messiah and Jesus, son of Mary, and declares him honored, eminent, and of high rank in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near to God in the highest station.

translation: And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This is a prophecy about Jesus: he will miraculously speak as an infant to defend his mother Mary and declare his servitude to Allah, and he will also speak as a grown man with prophetic wisdom; Allah affirms that he is one of the righteous, meaning he is a chosen, obedient servant, not a divine being.

translation: She said, “My Lord, how will I have a child when no man has touched me?” He said, “Thus Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s creative power is not restricted by ordinary causes or human expectations. Mary’s question expresses wonder at a miraculous event, not disbelief, and the answer directs her to God’s absolute will: He creates however He pleases, without needing a father, a means, or a natural process. The command “Be” signifies that when God decrees something, it immediately comes into existence by His power and permission. Therefore, the birth of Jesus without a human father is a sign of divine omnipotence, not a claim that Jesus shares in divinity or sonship; he is a created servant brought into being by God’s command.

translation: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: Allah Himself will be Jesus’s teacher, granting him knowledge of divine scripture, profound prophetic understanding and right judgment, the Torah revealed to Moses, and the Gospel revealed to him. This shows that Jesus’s prophethood and knowledge are not acquired by human instruction but are a direct divine gift, preparing him to call the Children of Israel to Allah and to confirm what was revealed before him while receiving the Gospel.

translation: And [make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [saying]: 'I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then I breathe into it, and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission. And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that Jesus’s miracles were divine signs granted to him as a prophet to the Children of Israel, not works of independent divine power. Every supernatural act—creating the form of a bird, healing congenital blindness and leprosy, reviving the dead, and revealing hidden matters—is explicitly tied to Allah’s permission, proving that he was a servant and messenger of Allah. The miracles served as decisive evidence for his truthfulness and as a call for the Children of Israel to affirm faith in Allah alone and in His messenger.

translation: And [I have come] confirming what was before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This is Jesus addressing the Children of Israel, explaining that his prophetic mission authenticates the Torah revealed before him and does not abolish it entirely. He was sent by God to relax certain prohibitions that had been imposed on them, as a mercy and as a clear sign of his truthfulness. The sign from God includes the miracles granted to him, which prove he is a messenger sent by God, not a divine being. Therefore, they are called to be mindful of God's authority and to follow Jesus in what he conveys from God, since obedience to God's messenger is obedience to God Himself.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: This verse establishes pure monotheism: Allah alone is the Lord, Sustainer, and Sovereign of the speaker and all people, so worship must be directed to Him alone. The “straight path” is the unwavering way of recognizing His exclusive lordship and devoting all acts of worship to Him, without associating any partner with Him. In its context, it also clarifies that even a noble prophet like Jesus is a servant of Allah, calling others not to himself but to the worship of the one true God.

translation: When Jesus sensed disbelief from them, he said, “Who are my helpers for Allah?” The disciples said, “We are Allah’s helpers. We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that when Prophet Jesus perceived the entrenched rejection and hostility of his people, he did not seek support for himself or any worldly cause; he called for helpers wholly devoted to God. The disciples’ response is the model of true faith: they immediately identified themselves as God’s helpers, affirmed belief in Him alone, and testified to their submission to His will. Their loyalty was not to a person, clan, or nation but to the divine mission. Thus, genuine support for God’s religion comes from hearts surrendered to Him, and such people are willing to stand with His messengers even when most others turn away.

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and have followed the Messenger, so write us among the witnesses.
interpretation: This is the supplication of the disciples of Jesus: they affirm faith in the revelation God sent down, commit themselves to following the Messenger, and ask God to inscribe them among those who bear witness to the truth—those who testify to God's oneness, to the truth of His messengers, and to the message they accepted, so that they may be counted among the faithful witnesses rather than among those who deny or ignore it.

translation: And they plotted, and Allah plotted; and Allah is the best of plotters.
interpretation: This affirms that the schemes of those who oppose Allah and His messengers cannot defeat His decree. They devised deceit, but Allah, in His wisdom and power, arranged their plans to fail and brought about His own just outcome. Allah is the best of planners: His planning is perfect, wise, and ultimately victorious, whereas the plotting of His creatures is limited and self-defeating.

translation: And [remember] when Allah said: 'O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve, and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that Jesus, peace be upon him, is wholly under Allah's care and authority: his life, death, elevation, purification from the accusations and plots of the disbelievers, and the honor granted to his true followers all occur by Allah's command. It declares that those who genuinely follow his prophetic message will remain spiritually and historically uppermost over those who reject it until the Day of Resurrection, and that every dispute among people—especially concerning Jesus and true faith—will finally be settled by Allah alone, whose judgment is perfectly just.

translation: Then as for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who persist in disbelief and rejection of God's signs will not escape His judgment: God Himself will inflict upon them a severe punishment that encompasses both the worldly life and the Hereafter, and no helper, ally, or intercessor will be able to rescue them from it. It affirms God's absolute authority in requiting deeds and the seriousness of kufr, whose consequences are both present and eternal.

translation: And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full; and Allah does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: God’s promise to the believers is that faith must be embodied in righteous conduct; when it is, He will grant them their due reward completely, without any loss or injustice. The closing statement affirms that God’s rejection of wrongdoers is itself an expression of perfect justice: He never wrongs anyone, and those who persist in oppression place themselves outside His love and favor.

translation: That is what We recite to you of the verses and the Wise Reminder.
interpretation: This verse declares that the revelation being conveyed to the Prophet Muhammad—including the accounts, laws, and admonitions in these passages—is not human speech but part of God's signs and the Wise Reminder, that is, the Qur'an. It is called 'wise' because it is founded on perfect wisdom: it clarifies truth, distinguishes right from wrong, warns, consoles, and guides with commands and lessons that are precise, coherent, and purposeful. The verse also affirms the Prophet's mission as the one to whom God recites and who faithfully conveys these signs to humanity.

translation: Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is as the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then He said to him, 'Be,' and he was.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Jesus’s miraculous creation does not make him divine, for Adam was created without either father or mother from dust by God’s command. If Adam is not worshipped as God despite that, then Jesus, created without a father, is likewise a servant and prophet of God. God’s act of creation is not bound by ordinary causes; His command “Be” brings into existence whatever He wills, so Jesus’s birth without a father is a sign of God’s power, not evidence of Jesus being God or the son of God.

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so never be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the decisive reality concerning faith, revelation, and the matters God has made clear comes from Him alone, not from human speculation or shifting opinions. It therefore calls the believer to settle firmly upon divine truth and warns against hesitancy, self-doubt, or yielding to skepticism after the truth has become manifest.

translation: So whoever disputes with you concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you, then say: 'Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us humbly invoke Allah and place the curse of Allah upon the liars.'
interpretation: This is the verse of Mubahala. It teaches that after decisive knowledge has come, continued argument about Jesus is no longer a sincere search for truth but obstinate disputation. The Prophet is commanded to propose a solemn mutual invocation: both sides bring those dearest to them and ask God to curse whichever party is lying. His willingness to include his own family and self shows absolute certainty in the message. In the event, he brought Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, indicating that they are the 'selves,' 'women,' and 'sons' meant, and that the truth he proclaimed is inseparable from his purified household.

translation: Indeed, this is the true account. And there is no deity except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the revelation concerning Jesus and his true story is the authentic and unquestionable truth, not the distorted accounts or false claims that attribute divinity to him or to anyone else. It then declares the core truth of divine oneness: there is no being worthy of worship, obedience, or ultimate reliance except Allah alone. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah is al-Aziz, the Almighty whose power is absolute and irresistible, and al-Hakim, the Wise whose decrees, revelations, and judgments are perfectly ordered and just. Thus, the true account leads necessarily to pure monotheism and to trusting that Allah’s power and wisdom govern all matters, including the revelation of prophetic history and the final judgment between truth and falsehood.

translation: But if they turn away, then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This means that if people reject the truth and turn away from it after it has been made clear, their rejection does not harm God or escape His knowledge. God is fully aware of those who corrupt themselves and others by opposing the truth, spreading disorder, and obstructing guidance. Their turning away exposes the corruption in their hearts and conduct, and God will judge them with perfect knowledge and justice.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and that we associate no partner with Him, and that none of us takes others as lords besides Allah.' But if they turn away, say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].'
interpretation: This verse invites the People of the Book to the common ground of pure monotheism: the exclusive worship of Allah alone, without associating any partner with Him, and without treating any human being or religious authority as a lord whose commands may override or rival Allah's. It clarifies that true religion is not divided loyalty but wholehearted submission to the One God. If they refuse this call, the believers are not to compromise; they simply declare and bear witness that they are Muslims—those who submit to Allah alone.

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed except after him? Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse reproaches the Jews and Christians who disputed over Abraham, each claiming him as one of their own. Since the Torah and the Gospel were revealed only after Abraham, he could not have belonged to either later religious community or followed their revealed laws. Their argument is therefore anachronistic and baseless. The verse calls them to reason and recognize that Abraham’s pure monotheism preceded both scriptures, so neither group has a valid claim to him based on its later revelation.

translation: Here you are — you have disputed about that of which you have knowledge. Then why do you dispute about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the inconsistency of arguing confidently about matters one knows while plunging into disputes over matters beyond one’s knowledge. It teaches that human knowledge is limited and that Allah alone possesses complete and certain knowledge. Therefore, claims about the unseen, about past prophets, or about religious truths should not be based on conjecture, inherited rivalry, or desire to win arguments, but on revealed knowledge and humble submission to God. It warns against speaking about what one does not know as though one knows it, and directs the heart toward reverence for God’s all-encompassing knowledge.

translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Prophet Ibrahim’s true faith was not the later Judaism or Christianity, but pure, sincere monotheism: he turned away from all false worship and submitted wholly to Allah alone. His religion was the original submission to the One God, free from any partnership ascribed to Him, so he cannot be claimed by either Jews or Christians as one of their own in the sectarian sense. Thus, the verse teaches that true religion is not defined by later labels or communities, but by exclusive devotion, submission, and loyalty to Allah without associating any partner with Him.

translation: Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the Guardian of the believers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true closeness to Abraham is not based on lineage or inherited identity, but on following his pure monotheistic faith. Those most entitled to be called his followers are those who adhered to his message, along with Prophet Muhammad and the believers who accept God's revelation to him. Thus, spiritual kinship with the prophets is determined by faith and obedience, not ancestry, and God's protection, support, and care belong to the believers.

translation: A group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray, but they lead none astray except themselves, and they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hidden envy and malicious intent of some among the People of the Book who wanted to turn the believers away from true guidance. Their desire to mislead others does not actually harm the guided; rather, the sin and failure of their scheme return upon them, because God protects His guidance and the hearts of the faithful. They are unaware that their plot only deepens their own loss and that they cannot misguide anyone whom God has guided.

translation: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while you witness [them]?
interpretation: This verse reproaches the People of the Book for denying God's revelations even though they possess knowledge and testimony that confirm they are true. Their disbelief is not due to ignorance but is a deliberate rejection of what they themselves witness and recognize, making it obstinate and blameworthy.

translation: O People of the Book, why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?
interpretation: This is a divine rebuke to the People of the Scripture for knowingly obscuring the truth by blending it with falsehood and suppressing clear divine evidences—especially the signs confirming the final Prophet—out of envy, partisanship, or worldly gain, even though their own scriptures and knowledge bear witness to that truth.

translation: And a group of the People of the Book said: 'Believe in that which was revealed to the believers at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, so that they may return [from their faith].'
interpretation: This verse exposes a deceptive plot by some of the People of the Book. They conspired to outwardly accept Islam in the morning and then openly reject it by the end of the day, not out of sincere belief, but to cast doubt in the hearts of weak or new Muslims. Their aim was to make others think that these learned people had examined the faith, found it false, and abandoned it, so that the believers might also turn away from Islam. It is a warning against those who use religion as a tool of deception and a lesson that faith must be based on truth, not on the shifting behavior of deceitful people.

translation: And do not believe except one who follows your religion. Say, 'Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah'—[they say this] lest anyone be given the like of what you were given, or they argue with you before your Lord. Say, 'Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.'
interpretation: These words reject the idea that God's guidance and favor can be fenced in by a particular religious community or hierarchy. Guidance is not a possession inherited or controlled by any group; it is Allah's own act, and He grants it according to His wisdom. The exclusivist attitude that resents others receiving revelation, knowledge, or divine favor—or that seeks to silence them before God—is exposed as envy and false entitlement. Divine bounty is not distributed according to human sectarian loyalty but by Allah's sovereign choice, and His generosity, knowledge, and authority are limitless. Thus no believer should accept any claim that Allah's mercy is restricted to one faction or that His giving to others is a loss to them.

translation: He singles out for His mercy whom He wills; and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: Allah alone, by His will and wisdom, chooses whom among His creation to favor with His special mercy—such as faith, guidance, forgiveness, and eternal reward. No one can compel or earn this favor independently; it is a free gift from His boundless grace, and His bounty is immeasurable.

translation: And among the People of the Book is he who, if you entrust him with a qintar, he will return it to you; and among them is he who, if you entrust him with a dinar, he will not return it to you unless you keep standing over him. That is because they say, 'There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered.' But they utter a lie about Allah, knowingly.
interpretation: This verse teaches that trustworthiness is an individual moral quality, not something guaranteed by belonging to a particular religious community. Some of the People of the Book are so honest that they return even a huge trust, while others betray even a small one. Their false justification is that they owe no moral duty to the 'unlettered'—meaning those outside their group—so they treat exploiting them as permissible. The Qur'an condemns this as a fabricated claim against God: they know it is not from Him. The verse therefore rejects religious or ethnic supremacism and affirms that justice, honesty, and fulfillment of trusts are universal obligations. No claimed chosenness, identity, or group loyalty can justify cheating, exploitation, or denying others their rights.

translation: Yes, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears Allah — then indeed, Allah loves the God-fearing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah’s love is not earned by mere claims, lineage, or outward affiliation, but by faithfully honoring one’s covenant and living with taqwa. The one who keeps his commitments to Allah and to people, and who guards himself against disobedience out of reverence for Allah, is among the muttaqin whom Allah loves. True piety is therefore proven through integrity, loyalty, and God-conscious action, not through empty assertion.

translation: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price — those will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This is a severe warning that whoever trades away Allah’s covenant and solemn oaths for some fleeting worldly gain forfeits every good in the Hereafter and is cut off from divine mercy. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will not address them with kindness, will not regard them with compassion, and will not purify or commend them; instead, they will suffer a painful torment. The verse teaches that covenants and oaths made in God’s name are sacred trusts, not bargaining tools for material advantage, and that breaking them for a paltry price is a catastrophic loss of one’s eternal standing before God.

translation: And indeed, among them is a party who distort their tongues with the Book, so that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book. And they say, 'It is from Allah,' but it is not from Allah. And they knowingly utter lies against Allah.
interpretation: This verse exposes a deliberate tactic of deception among a faction of the People of the Book: they manipulate their speech, alter words, or fabricate passages and then pass them off as authentic revelation, aiming to deceive believers into accepting falsehood as part of God's Book. Their crime is compounded by falsely attributing these inventions to God, knowingly lying against Him. The verse thus establishes that not everything claimed to be from Scripture or from God is genuine, and that truth must be judged by its actual source, not by the assertion of those who claim it. It also serves as a warning to the faithful against being misled by religious authorities who tamper with revelation and abuse trust.

translation: It is not for any human being that Allah should give him the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood, and then he should say to the people, ‘Be servants to me besides Allah’; rather, ‘Be devoted servants of the Lord, because you have been teaching the Book and studying it.’
interpretation: This verse means that divine scripture, prophetic wisdom, and prophethood can never justify a prophet or religious guide calling people to worship him or submit to him as if he were a lord besides Allah. The true prophetic mission forms people into rabbaniyyin—God-centered, deeply grounded in revealed knowledge, and devoted to their Lord alone—by teaching and studying the Book. Knowledge and religious leadership are therefore a trust meant to produce sincere servitude to Allah, not personal allegiance to the teacher or prophet.

translation: Nor would he command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you have submitted [to Allah]?
interpretation: This verse categorically denies that any prophet could ever call people to worship angels or prophets as lords, because all prophets were sent to establish pure monotheism. The rhetorical question—'Would he command you to disbelief after you have become Muslims?'—underscores the absurdity of such a claim: a true prophet would never lead people away from faith into disbelief. The verse thus refutes those who deify righteous beings, whether angels or prophets, and affirms that the only rightful object of worship and obedience is Allah alone. It also shows that accepting Islam means submitting exclusively to Allah, not to any created being.

translation: And [remember] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets, [saying], 'Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom, then a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.' He said, 'Do you affirm and accept My covenant upon that?' They said, 'We affirm.' He said, 'Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.'
interpretation: This means that Allah bound every prophet by a solemn covenant: whenever a messenger comes after them confirming the revelation they already possess, they must believe in him and support him. The covenant extends to their followers, so adherence to any earlier prophet is genuine only when it leads to accepting the final messenger who confirms all previous scriptures. Allah made the prophets witnesses to this pledge and declared Himself a witness with them, showing that this obligation is universal, decisive, and inseparable from true prophetic faith.

translation: So whoever turns away after that — then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse declares that turning away after a binding covenant, clear testimony, and knowledge is not a light matter; such people are the truly corrupt and disobedient, having broken their pledge and departed from the path of faith and obedience.

translation: Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him have submitted all those in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?
interpretation: This verse rebukes those who desire a way other than Allah’s revealed religion, for all creation is already subject to His lordship and decree. Whether willingly through faith or unwillingly through the order of creation, every creature submits to His will, and every soul will ultimately return to Him for judgment. Therefore, the only true religion is sincere submission to Allah alone.

translation: Say, “We have believed in Allah and in what was revealed to us, and in what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and in what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.”
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith in God requires accepting the whole chain of divine revelation as coming from the same Lord, not restricting guidance to one prophet or community. It affirms the original messages given to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the tribes, Moses, Jesus, and all prophets, and it forbids rejecting some while accepting others. “We make no distinction” means believers do not treat some prophets as true and others as false; all are truthful messengers from God, though their ranks and missions may differ. The verse also defines the believer’s identity as one who submits wholly to God alone, making islam the enduring response of faith to every divine message.

translation: And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God accepts only the religion of Islam—understood as sincere submission to Him alone, as revealed through His prophets and finalized in Muhammad—and that any deliberate adoption of a different religious path, after the truth has reached one, will not be accepted as valid worship or obedience; such a person will incur loss in the Hereafter.

translation: How would Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had witnessed that the Messenger is true and clear proofs had come to them? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse affirms that divine guidance is withheld from those who knowingly turn away after faith and after acknowledging the truth of the Messenger and receiving clear evidence. Their disbelief is not born of ignorance but of deliberate rejection, making them wrongdoers who wrong themselves. God’s refusal to guide them is a just consequence of their persistent defiance, not a denial of guidance before they culpably rejected it; it expresses the divine principle that those who choose injustice and reject clear truth forfeit the guidance that leads to success.

translation: Those — their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of all mankind.
interpretation: This verse establishes the fate of those who reject faith after clear guidance and die in disbelief: they are severed from God's mercy, and this severance is affirmed by the angels and by all people on the Day of Judgment. The curse is a state of complete exclusion from divine compassion, accompanied by universal condemnation, indicating that their rejection is not merely a private matter but an offense against the whole moral order.

translation: Abiding therein forever; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be granted respite.
interpretation: This describes the state of those who persist in disbelief until death: their punishment is eternal and unrelenting. “The punishment will not be lightened for them” means its severity never decreases, not even momentarily. “Nor will they be granted respite” means they are given no delay, pause, or opportunity for relief; it is not that they are waiting for a reprieve, but that no reprieve will ever come. The verse emphasizes the absolute permanence and inescapability of the consequence for rejecting faith and dying upon it.

translation: Except those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This exception means that the lasting disgrace and rejection attached to the sin of falsely accusing chaste people is not irreversible for one who sincerely turns back to God and corrects his conduct. Repentance must be genuine and accompanied by reform, not merely words, and when it is, God’s forgiveness and mercy override the permanence of the previous condemnation. The verse thus affirms both the seriousness of the offense and the openness of divine mercy to those who truly mend their ways.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief—their repentance will never be accepted, and it is they who are the astray.
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning about apostates who, after having entered faith, deliberately abandon it and then persist and deepen in denial. Their repentance is not accepted because it is not a sincere return to God while they still have the freedom to choose; it is either the false repentance of one who only turns when punishment has already come, or the state of those who die in rejection. Having knowingly left guidance and continued in it, they are truly the lost, cut off from the path that leads to God.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will the fill of the earth in gold be accepted from any one of them, even if he were to offer it as ransom. Those will have a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that dying in a state of rejection of Allah seals one’s fate in the Hereafter. At that point, no compensation or ransom is accepted, even if the person were to possess and offer all the gold the earth could hold. Such wealth cannot buy relief, delay, or exemption from the consequences of persistent disbelief. Their punishment is painful, and no one will be able to help them or avert it.

translation: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. And whatever you spend, indeed Allah knows it well.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true righteousness is not merely outward observance or belief in words; it is proven by sacrificial generosity. A person reaches the reality of faith and moral excellence only when he is willing to give away something he genuinely values—wealth, property, time, or another beloved blessing—for God’s sake and for the needy. The verse thus exposes the difference between giving from surplus and giving from the heart’s attachments. Its ending, “Allah knows it well,” means that no act of giving is unnoticed or wasted, however hidden or small, and that God is fully aware of both the gift and the sincerity behind it. The standard of righteousness here is love-driven sacrifice, not reluctant charity.

translation: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel [Jacob] made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, 'Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim that the dietary restrictions observed by the Jews were established by Jacob or were part of the original religion of the Children of Israel. It states that all foods were lawful for them until the Torah was revealed; the only earlier exception was a restriction Jacob imposed on himself. The later Torah contained specific prohibitions as a legislation from God, not as an eternal law from Jacob. The challenge to bring and recite the Torah exposes the falsehood of those who asserted otherwise, since their own Scripture would confirm that these restrictions were revealed after Jacob. Thus the verse vindicates the Quran's consistency with earlier revelation and rejects man-made or misattributed prohibitions.

translation: So whoever fabricates a lie against Allah after that—then those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This is a severe rebuke to those who, after clear evidence and divine guidance have come, persist in inventing claims about God—such as falsely ascribing laws, prohibitions, or teachings to Him—to serve their own interests or distort the truth. It defines such fabricators as the unjust in the fullest sense: their act is not an innocent mistake but a deliberate trespass against God’s authority and truth, harming both themselves and those they mislead. Thus the verse teaches that culpability for wrongdoing increases with knowledge and intent; the clearer the truth one has received, the graver the sin of knowingly replacing it with falsehood.

translation: Say, Allah has spoken the truth. So follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the authentic religion to be followed is the pure, primordial monotheism of Abraham: a total turning of the heart and worship to Allah alone, free from any association of partners with Him. Abraham’s way is presented as the standard of true faith, and his being declared free of shirk shows that true submission to God is incompatible with idolatry, compromise in divine lordship, or invented religious affiliations. Therefore, the verse calls people to sincerity in belief and action, following the prophetic example of exclusive devotion to Allah rather than the claims and sectarian labels that later people attached to Abraham.

translation: Indeed, the first House established for mankind is the one at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Ka'bah in Mecca is the earliest house of worship appointed by God for humanity. Its being “blessed” means it is a source of spiritual and worldly good, and its being “guidance for all the worlds” means it directs people toward pure monotheism and the worship of God alone, serving as a universal center of divine guidance rather than the possession of any one group.

translation: In it are clear signs, the standing place of Abraham. And whoever enters it is safe. And for Allah upon the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need from the worlds.
interpretation: This verse identifies the Sacred House as a place where God's clear proofs are manifest, especially the station of Abraham, and invests it with a divinely granted sanctuary so that anyone who enters it is secure. The Hajj is thus an obligation grounded in gratitude and capacity: God requires it only from those He has given the means, and He is not enriched by pilgrimage or harmed by its rejection. Disbelief or refusal therefore exposes only the servant's own need, for God is utterly independent of all creation.

translation: Say, "O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?"
interpretation: This verse is a divine rebuke addressed to the People of the Book—the Jews and Christians—who knowingly rejected the clear signs and verses of Allah, including the proofs confirming His final Messenger and the Qur’an. The question is rhetorical: their disbelief was not due to any lack of evidence, but due to stubbornness, envy, or attachment to worldly interests. By ending with “Allah is Witness over what you do,” the verse warns that God sees their outward denial and inner motives, and He will hold them accountable for every action. Thus, rejecting Allah’s signs cannot harm Him; it only harms those who turn away.

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, why do you turn away from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked, while you are witnesses? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those among the People of the Book who, despite recognizing the truth and bearing witness to it in their own scriptures and conscience, actively obstruct others from following God’s straight path. Their motive is not sincere correction but a desire to make that path appear twisted, doubtful, or unjust, using their religious authority and knowledge to mislead. The verse warns that such deliberate distortion and hindrance are fully seen by God, who will hold them accountable; it is not a condemnation of every Jew or Christian, but of those who knowingly wage this campaign against faith in God and His final Messenger.

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you back, after your belief, [to being] unbelievers.
interpretation: This verse warns believers that heeding the religious guidance or authority of a faction among the People of the Book—those who seek to divert them from Islam—can lead them back to disbelief after they have believed. It teaches that faith must be guarded by adhering to God’s revelation and not by submitting to those whose direction opposes it; obeying them in matters of belief is spiritually ruinous.

translation: And how can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are being recited to you and His Messenger is among you? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has certainly been guided to a straight path.
interpretation: This is a reproach and a wonder at the possibility of disbelief after such clear evidence: divine revelation continuing to be recited and the Messenger present as a living exemplar. “Holding firmly to Allah” means entrusting oneself completely to Him, clinging to His guidance and obedience, and seeking protection in His covenant; such a person is established on the straight path that leads to His pleasure.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except while you are Muslims.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to maintain genuine, lifelong God-consciousness: taqwa must be given its due right by obeying Allah’s commands, avoiding His prohibitions, fulfilling His obligations, and not treating His rights lightly. The phrase “do not die except while you are Muslims” does not mean a person can control the moment of death; rather, it means one must persist in Islam, faith, and submission throughout life so that death finds one in that state. It is a call to steadfastness until the end and a warning that salvation is tied to dying upon Islamic monotheism and submission to Allah.

translation: And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah, and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you: you were enemies, then He united your hearts, so by His favor you became brothers. And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, then He saved you from it. Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, so that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse makes unity an obligation grounded in divine grace. The “rope of Allah” is His revelation and covenant, the only bond that can truly unite people beyond tribal, ethnic, or personal loyalties; to divide from it is to abandon the means of salvation He has given. The reminder of former enmity turned into brotherhood shows that reconciliation of hearts is not merely a human achievement but a favor from God, and remembering that favor is what sustains gratitude and prevents the return of hostility. Being “on the brink of a pit of Fire” signifies the spiritual and communal peril of enmity and disbelief, from which God rescued them by faith and brotherhood. Therefore, His clarified signs call people to guidance that is both inward—faith and gratitude—and outward—unity and loyalty to His covenant.

translation: And let there arise from among you a community inviting to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong; and it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the collective duty of calling to good, commanding what is right, and forbidding what is wrong. The phrase “from among you” means that the Muslim community must ensure a group exists to carry out this mission, though the responsibility belongs to the whole community to support, uphold, and participate in according to ability and knowledge. “Al-khayr” is comprehensive good, especially faith in Allah and obedience to Him; “al-ma‘ruf” is what Allah and His Messenger have made known as right; and “al-munkar” is what they have prohibited as evil. Those who fulfill this duty are “al-muflihun”—the truly successful—because they attain Allah’s acceptance, righteousness, and eternal felicity. Thus this verse identifies da‘wah and moral reform as a defining mark of the believing community and a path to salvation.

translation: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them; and those will have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse prohibits the believers from imitating those who split into sects and fell into disputation after divine guidance and unmistakable signs had already reached them. Their disagreement was not caused by any deficiency in the proof, but by partisanship, arrogance, and refusal to submit to the truth once it became clear. Therefore, it warns that such willful division and contention after knowledge carries a severe and painful punishment from God.

translation: On the Day when faces will be bright and faces will be dark. As for those whose faces are dark, [they will be asked], 'Did you disbelieve after you had believed? Then taste the punishment for what you used to reject.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the Day of Judgment as the moment when the inner reality of every soul becomes visible. The brightening of faces signifies joy, acceptance, and honor for those who held fast to faith and lived according to divine guidance. The darkening of faces signifies humiliation, regret, and the burden of betrayal for those who turned away after having been given belief or knowledge of the truth. The rebuke 'Did you disbelieve after your belief?' exposes the gravity of knowingly abandoning faith or breaking a covenant with God; it is not a question seeking information but a reproach that makes the offense clear. Their punishment is portrayed as the direct consequence of their own persistent denial and ingratitude, not an arbitrary decree. Thus the verse warns that faith is not merely a verbal label but a trust that must be safeguarded, and that on that Day one's spiritual condition will be manifest for all to see.

translation: And as for those whose faces have turned white, they will be in the mercy of Allah; therein they will abide forever.
interpretation: This verse describes the people of faith and obedience whose faces are brightened and whitened on the Day of Judgment as a sign of acceptance, joy, and honor.
