Their being “in the mercy of Allah” means they are enveloped by His grace and admitted into Paradise, the abode of His mercy. The phrase “therein they will abide forever” affirms that this state of bliss and divine pleasure is eternal and never interrupted.

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. And Allah does not intend injustice to the worlds.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the revelations being recited to the Prophet are God’s true signs, free from falsehood and distortion. It then declares that God’s will is never toward injustice: He does not desire to wrong any of His creation, nor is oppression ever an intended outcome of His commands or decrees. Any punishment or hardship that befalls people is a just consequence of their own choices, while God Himself is absolutely just and free from all wrongdoing toward all the worlds.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse establishes that absolute ownership and sovereignty belong to Allah alone over everything in the heavens and earth, and that every affair—human deeds, provision, judgment, and final destiny—ultimately returns to Him. He alone has the authority to decide, recompense, and bring all matters to their conclusion, so accountability, trust, and submission are due to Him.

translation: You are the best nation ever brought forth for mankind: you enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah. If the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are transgressors.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the excellence of the Muslim ummah is not an unconditional privilege but is tied to its fulfillment of three duties: commanding good, forbidding evil, and believing in Allah. Its being 'brought forth for mankind' means it is raised as a witnessing, guiding community whose example and call are meant for all people. The verse also clarifies that the earlier People of the Book are not rejected wholesale: had they accepted faith, it would have been to their own benefit; some among them did believe, while the majority are described as fasiqun—those who break God's covenant and disobey His commands.

translation: They will not harm you except annoyance; and if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped.
interpretation: This is a divine assurance to the believers that their enemies’ hostility cannot inflict real or lasting damage upon them; at most it reaches the level of nuisance, slander, or petty injury. If those enemies resort to armed confrontation, they will be put to flight and defeated, and they will find no helper or divine support. The verse thus trains the believers to rely on Allah’s promise, to remain steadfast, and not to be intimidated by the apparent strength or threats of their opponents.

translation: Humiliation has been struck upon them wherever they are found, except by a rope from Allah and a rope from people. They have incurred wrath from Allah, and misery has been struck upon them. That is because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.
interpretation: This verse sets out a divine pattern: disgrace and wretchedness follow persistent rejection of God’s signs and unjust violence against His messengers. The exception clause means that their security and standing can only be preserved through a covenant with God—faith, obedience, and adherence to His guidance—and a covenant with people—just conduct, peace, and protected coexistence. Their incurring God’s wrath and being struck with misery is therefore not arbitrary; it is the consequence of their own rebellion and transgression. The verse warns that whenever a community abandons its covenant with God and violates the rights of His prophets and people, it invites humiliation and ruin, and any relief depends on returning to that covenant and rectifying its conduct.

translation: They are not all alike. Among the People of the Book is an upright community, reciting the verses of Allah during the hours of the night, and they prostrate.
interpretation: This verse repudiates the assumption that all People of the Book are identical in disbelief or corruption. It identifies among them a steadfast group who are sincere in faith, devoted to worship, and humble before God, reciting His revelations in the night and prostrating themselves. Their worth is not determined by communal label but by genuine devotion and adherence to divine guidance, showing that righteousness exists wherever hearts submit to God.

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to [do] good deeds. And those are among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse presents righteousness as a living combination of sound belief and righteous action: sincere faith in Allah and in the accountability of the Last Day must express itself in striving to establish good and resist evil, and in eagerly racing toward every act of obedience and benefit. Such people are not righteous merely by name, lineage, or affiliation; they are counted among the righteous because their faith has become a motivating force for reform, moral courage, and constant good works, and Allah does not waste the reward of such sincerity.

translation: And whatever good they do, it will never be denied them. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse assures that no good deed done sincerely by a believer will be lost or unrewarded; Allah will not overlook it or deprive the doer of its reward. The ending, “And Allah is Knowing of the righteous,” clarifies that the true value of deeds is measured by taqwa—God-consciousness and sincerity—and that Allah fully knows those who act out of faith and piety, even if others do not recognize or appreciate their good.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve—their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah in the least. And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: The verse teaches that rejection of God cannot be compensated by worldly advantages. Wealth and children, though often seen as sources of security and influence, have no power to avert divine judgment or to stand in place of faith. Those who persist in disbelief are identified as the people of the Fire, and their punishment is described as eternal. It emphasizes the absolute priority of belief in God over material and familial ties when it comes to ultimate salvation.

translation: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind containing bitter cold; it struck the crop of a people who wronged themselves and destroyed it. And Allah did not wrong them, but they wrong themselves.
interpretation: This parable means that the wealth and charitable deeds of those who disbelieve or act hypocritically in this world cannot benefit them before God, because such deeds are not founded on true faith and sincere obedience. Their works are like a harvest ruined by a destructive freezing wind: the apparent investment is lost at the time of greatest need. The loss is not injustice from God; it is the consequence of their own rejection, hypocrisy, and wrongdoing, which corrupt their deeds and bring ruin upon themselves.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those outside your own, for they will not spare you any ruin. They wish you distress. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater. We have certainly made clear to you the signs, if you will reason.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against entrusting their secrets and close counsel to people outside the community of faith who are hostile, because such people do not sincerely desire the believers’ good; they seek to corrupt, weaken, and distress them. Their outward speech already reveals resentment, while their hearts conceal even greater malice. Allah has made His guidance clear so that believers may use their reason to discern loyal counsel from hidden enmity and avoid placing confidence in those who wish them harm.

translation: Here you are, loving them while they do not love you, and you believe in all the Book. And when they meet you, they say, “We believe.” But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. Say, “Die in your rage. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.”
interpretation: This verse reproaches the believers for extending sincere affection and loyalty to a people whose hearts are not inclined toward them, even though the believers accept all of God’s revealed Books. It exposes the hypocrisy of those opponents: publicly they profess faith to deceive and flatter, but privately they are consumed by rage, envy, and resentment toward the believers. The command “Die in your rage” is a declaration that their malice is impotent and self-destructive; it cannot harm the believers or thwart God’s plan. The ending affirms that God knows the hidden thoughts and intentions of every heart, so nothing of their secret hatred or the believers’ sincerity is lost to Him. The verse thus teaches that ultimate loyalty belongs to God and faith, and that believers should not be deceived by outward professions when inward realities are hostile.

translation: If good touches you, it grieves them; and if adversity strikes you, they rejoice at it. But if you are patient and God-conscious, their plotting will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah encompasses whatever they do.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hostile mindset of the believers’ enemies: they are pained by any good that comes to the believers and delighted by any harm or setback that befalls them. It then prescribes the believers’ defense: sabr (patient perseverance in obedience and trials) and taqwa (God-consciousness and avoidance of wrongdoing). When these qualities are present, the enemies’ schemes cannot ultimately harm the believers, because Allah’s knowledge and power encompass all their actions; He sees, records, and will either thwart or requite them. The verse thus teaches that the believers’ security is not determined by the enemies’ pleasure or displeasure, but by their own steadfastness and piety, and that no conspiracy can escape God’s all-encompassing control.

translation: And [remember] when you went forth from your household in the morning, assigning the believers to positions for battle. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse points to the Prophet Muhammad’s careful leadership before the Battle of Uhud: he rose early, left his home, and personally organized the believers into their battle stations. Its lesson is that outward preparation, order, and discipline are part of faith, but they must be joined to reliance upon Allah, who hears every word and knows every intention. The names All-Hearing and All-Knowing at the end assure the believers that no sincere effort, hidden motive, or unspoken anxiety is lost to Allah. Therefore, the verse teaches that success in any collective struggle depends not only on planning and obedience but also on the awareness that Allah fully perceives and governs all affairs.

translation: When two groups among you were about to lose heart — but Allah was their Protector; and in Allah let the believers place their trust.
interpretation: This verse teaches that when believers face fear, pressure, or the danger of wavering, their protection and firmness come from Allah alone. The two groups who nearly faltered were not abandoned; Allah guarded them and remained their Helper. Therefore, true believers should not rely on their own strength or numbers, but place their complete trust in Allah, especially in times of trial and apparent weakness.

translation: And Allah had already given you victory at Badr while you were weak. So fear Allah, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers that their victory at Badr was granted by Allah despite their being few, weak, and lacking in material means, so the triumph was not due to their own power but to divine help. Therefore, they are commanded to maintain taqwa—God-consciousness and obedience—as an expression of gratitude, because true thankfulness for Allah’s aid is shown by continued devotion, trust, and adherence to His commands.

translation: [Remember] when you said to the believers, 'Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?'
interpretation: This verse is a divine reassurance to the believers that victory and support come from Allah, not from numbers or material strength. The rhetorical question corrects any faltering confidence and affirms that Allah’s help is fully sufficient. The angels are described as “sent down” to show that they are a means created and commanded by Allah, not independent sources of power. Their mention strengthens the believers’ hearts and binds their trust to Allah alone, while they still take the outward means required of them.

translation: Yes, if you are patient and God-conscious, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked.
interpretation: This verse establishes that divine help is tied to the believers’ steadfastness and God-consciousness, not to their mere wishes or numbers. The promise of five thousand marked angels means that when God’s servants fulfill the conditions of patience and piety, His aid arrives in a decisive and recognizable form, beyond ordinary calculation. The ‘marking’ signifies that this support is specifically appointed by God for the moment of need, distinguishing His forces and making clear that victory is from Him alone.

translation: And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you and so that your hearts might be reassured by it. And victory is only from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the aid, glad tidings, or apparent means Allah sends are not themselves the source of victory; their purpose is to comfort the believers and strengthen their hearts with certainty. True triumph, support, and deliverance come solely from Allah, the All-Mighty who cannot be overcome, and the All-Wise who orders all affairs with perfect wisdom. Therefore, the believer’s trust and reliance must ultimately rest on Allah alone, while receiving His reassuring signs with gratitude and steadfast faith.

translation: That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieved, or abase them, so that they may turn back frustrated.
interpretation: This verse states a purpose of Allah’s aid to the believers: to break the power of the disbelieving enemy by eliminating one part of them, or by humiliating and suppressing them, so that they withdraw from the conflict having failed and attained nothing. Divine support is thus directed toward defeating falsehood and frustrating its adherents, causing their efforts to end in loss and disappointment.

translation: You have no say in the matter at all, whether He turns in mercy to them or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that ultimate authority over guidance, forgiveness, and punishment belongs exclusively to God, not to the Prophet or any human. The Prophet’s duty is to convey the message, while hearts and outcomes remain in God’s hands. Even toward those who committed grave wrong and opposition, God may grant forgiveness if they repent, or punish them if they persist in injustice. Thus the verse combines absolute divine sovereignty with the possibility of mercy, and it warns believers not to assume control over others’ fate or to seek revenge, since only God knows and judges rightly.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: All dominion and ownership belong exclusively to Allah, so He is free to govern His creation as He wills, and no one can compel or prevent His decree. His forgiveness and punishment flow from His perfect will, wisdom, and justice, not from any deficiency or need. Those who turn to Him in sincere repentance find His forgiveness and mercy, while those who persist in rebellion against Him remain subject to His justice; therefore His names al-Ghafur and al-Rahim affirm that mercy is His chosen way for the penitent.

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied. And fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse forbids the exploitative taking of riba, especially when debt is compounded and multiplied against the debtor, and it directs believers to taqwa—God-consciousness and obedience—as the path to true success in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This is a warning to believers to protect themselves from the punishment of Hellfire by adhering to faith and obedience, and to avoid the path of disbelief that leads to it; the Fire is already prepared for those who knowingly reject God and His guidance.

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger, so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse makes divine mercy contingent upon wholehearted obedience to God and to His Messenger. Obeying God means carrying out His revealed commands; obeying the Messenger means accepting his prophetic authority, following his example, and implementing his teachings. This obedience is not merely outward compliance but a fruit of faith that draws down God’s mercy, forgiveness, guidance, and ultimate success in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse urges believers to move quickly and earnestly toward God’s forgiveness and toward Paradise, showing that the path of repentance, obedience, and seeking divine mercy should not be delayed. Forgiveness is described as coming from “your Lord,” reminding the servant that mercy belongs to God alone and is obtained by turning back to Him. Paradise is portrayed as immeasurably vast—its width extending across the heavens and the earth—to awaken longing for what God has prepared and to show that its reality surpasses human imagination. It is prepared specifically for the muttaqīn: those who guard themselves against sin, live with God-consciousness, fulfill His commands, and avoid His prohibitions. Thus the verse combines hope with responsibility: the believer races toward forgiveness and Paradise while striving to be among the God-fearing.

translation: Those who spend in ease and hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon people — and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse describes the character of those whom God praises: they give generously whether they are in comfort or in difficulty, they control their rage even when provoked, and they forgive those who wrong them. Such conduct is not merely social virtue; it is an expression of ihsan, excellence in faith and action. God’s love here means His approval, favor, and reward for those who perfect their conduct toward Him and toward people.

translation: And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who can forgive sins except Allah?—and do not persist in what they have done while they know.
interpretation: This verse describes the character of true believers when they fall into sin: they do not defend it, minimize it, or continue in it knowingly. Instead, they immediately remember Allah—His mercy and His accountability—acknowledge their wrongdoing, and ask Him to forgive them. Their confession is joined to the realization that no one forgives sins except Allah, so they do not persist in the sin but abandon it with knowledge and resolve. Thus repentance in this verse is not mere lip-service; it is awareness, remorse, seeking forgiveness, and desisting from the wrong, combined with hope in Allah’s exclusive power to forgive.

translation: Those — their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever; and excellent is the reward of the workers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the sincere servants who turn back to God and mend their ways receive a twofold recompense: first, forgiveness from their Lord, which removes the burden of sin and brings them near to Him; and second, gardens of eternal bliss with rivers flowing beneath them, symbolizing continuous grace, refreshment, and life. Their abiding therein forever shows that this reward is not temporary but secure and everlasting. The closing praise, “and excellent is the reward of the workers,” affirms that God’s recompense for those who labor in faith, repentance, and obedience is the best and most worthy outcome, encouraging believers to persevere in righteous action.

translation: There have already passed before you [God's] ways of dealing [with nations]; so journey through the earth and observe how the end of those who denied [the truth] was.
interpretation: God directs people to study history as a moral and spiritual lesson: His established pattern is that societies which reject His messengers and signs eventually meet ruin, disgrace, or defeat; the ruins and remnants of past nations are witnesses that denial does not escape consequence, and traveling with reflection should awaken repentance and steadfastness in faith.

translation: This is a clear statement for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing.
interpretation: The verse declares that the Qur’an’s message is an open, universal exposition available to all people, yet its function as guidance and moral warning becomes effective for those who adopt taqwa—God-consciousness and guarding against disobedience. Thus the same revelation is a proof and proclamation for everyone, while its saving guidance and corrective admonition are received by hearts disposed to reverence and accountability.

translation: Do not lose heart nor grieve, for you are the uppermost, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse forbids the believers from yielding to defeatism or sorrow over worldly loss or opposition, because their faith gives them true honor and ultimate ascendancy. It teaches that inward weakness and grief become blameworthy when they cause one to abandon resolve and trust in Allah; the believer’s dignity, strength, and final success are tied to sincere faith and steadfastness.

translation: If a wound has touched you, a similar wound has touched the people. And these days We alternate among people, so that Allah may make evident those who believe and take from among you martyrs. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse consoles the believers after a setback by reminding them that suffering is not one-sided and that victory and defeat alternate by Allah’s decree. The alternation of days is a trial: it exposes sincere faith, purifies the believers, and allows some to attain martyrdom. Allah’s refusal to love the wrongdoers affirms that oppression and injustice are not His way and will not ultimately prevail.

translation: And so that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse clarifies a divine purpose behind trials, conflicts, and the alternation of ease and hardship: they are a means of spiritual refinement for the faithful. For believers, such experiences purge away sins, hypocrisy, and weak intentions, and they strengthen sincere commitment to God. For those who persist in rejection, the same unfolding of events leads to their gradual diminishment and ultimate failure, because falsehood cannot stand against the truth. Thus, hardship functions as a filter that distinguishes and purifies the sincere while eroding the power of disbelief.

translation: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strive and made evident the patient?
interpretation: This verse rejects the notion that Paradise is entered merely by wishful thinking or outward claim. It teaches that Allah tests His servants so that the truth of their faith becomes manifest in action: who sincerely struggles in His cause and who remains steadfast under hardship. Allah’s knowledge is eternal and nothing is hidden from Him; the “knowledge” here refers to the testing and outward manifestation by which people are distinguished in this life and judged accordingly. Thus striving and patience are not needed because Allah learns something new, but because they are the means by which faith is proven, purified, and rewarded.

translation: And you had certainly wished for death before you met it. So you have seen it while you look on.
interpretation: This verse reproaches those believers who, before the battle, eagerly desired death and martyrdom, imagining it as something easy to claim. But when the enemy appeared and death became visibly present, they were confronted with the reality of their wish. It teaches that true faith is not proven by mere longing for martyrdom or trials, but by steadfastness, sincerity, and obedience when the trial actually comes. It also reminds them that death is unavoidable and that their earlier words had now been put to the test before their own eyes.

translation: And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have already passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all. And Allah will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the Prophet Muhammad is a mortal messenger, not a divine being, and that the truth of his message does not depend on his remaining alive. Faith must be grounded in God and His revelation, not in the person or survival of the messenger. If believers were to abandon faith after his death or killing, they would only harm themselves, for God is in no need of them. The verse calls for steadfastness, gratitude, and loyalty to the message, promising that God will reward those who remain thankful and firm.

translation: And no soul can die except by Allah’s permission, a decree with an appointed term. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him some of it; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him some of it. And We will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that death is not subject to human control or accident; it occurs only by God’s decree, at a fixed time that no one can delay or advance. Therefore, a believer should not fear death or compromise faith for the sake of survival or worldly gain. It further shows that people differ in what they seek: one who aims only at worldly reward may receive a limited portion, but one who seeks the Hereafter is given from it as well. The verse closes by promising reward to the grateful, indicating that true success belongs to those who recognize God’s authority, accept His decree, and respond with thankfulness rather than greed or rebellion.

translation: And how many a prophet has fought, with whom were many devoted men; yet they did not lose heart because of what afflicted them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken, nor did they submit. And Allah loves the patient.
interpretation: This verse teaches that steadfastness in Allah’s cause is not measured by freedom from hardship, but by fidelity under hardship. When believers suffer loss, injury, or opposition while striving for Allah, they are not to collapse inwardly, lose moral strength, or capitulate to falsehood. The prophets and their devoted followers are presented as models of this sabr: a firm endurance that remains obedient, courageous, and hopeful even when afflicted. Allah’s love is attached to such patience, meaning that trials in His path become a means of nearness to Him when met with unwavering trust, resolve, and refusal to surrender to despair or defeat. Thus the verse calls the believer to interpret suffering not as divine abandonment, but as a field for the patience that Allah loves.

translation: And their saying was nothing except that they said: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, and make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the mark of sincere faith in hardship is not despair or complaint, but humble supplication to God. The believers’ only response to trials was to admit their shortcomings, seek forgiveness for both ordinary sins and excesses—overstepping limits, poor judgment, or immoderation—and then ask for steadfastness and divine help. The order is significant: first purification from sin, then firmness of heart and resolve, then victory over those who reject the truth. “Make firm our feet” means grant constancy in testing and battle, not merely physical stability. “Victory over the disbelieving people” is sought in defense of faith and truth, not for aggression or personal dominance. Thus the verse portrays true reliance on God: acknowledging one’s own weakness, correcting oneself before God, and then asking Him alone for strength and triumph.

translation: So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This means that God grants those who are sincere and steadfast a share of good in worldly life—such as relief, victory, provision, and honor—but the reward He has prepared for them in the Hereafter is far better and more perfect. His love is for the muhsinin: those who worship Him with excellence and sincerity and who do good to others, seeking His pleasure alone.

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers that submitting to the guidance or counsel of those who reject faith in matters of religion will lead them to abandon their faith and retreat from the truth. Such obedience causes a reversal from guidance to misguidance, resulting in loss in this world and the Hereafter.

translation: Nay, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true guardianship, protection, and support belong to Allah alone. It directs the believer away from relying on any created being for ultimate security or victory, and calls them to place their trust in God, whose help is perfect, sufficient, and superior to all other aid.

translation: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they associate with Allah what He has not sent down any authority for. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the dwelling of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse means that the dread cast by God is a just consequence of the disbelievers' false worship: they set up partners with God without any revealed warrant, so their hearts are deprived of peace and certainty. Their final home is the Fire, which is the worst place for those who wrong themselves by rejecting and associating others with God.

translation: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until when you lost heart and disputed about the command and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love. Among you are those who desire the worldly life and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them so that He might test you. And He has certainly pardoned you. And Allah is possessor of bounty toward the believers.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers at Uhud: God’s promise of victory was true, and their early success came only by His permission. The reversal came when they became divided over the Prophet’s order and disobeyed after seeing the victory and spoils they desired. This shows that divine help is conditioned on obedience and unity, and that blessings themselves can become a test. The mixed motives—some seeking worldly gain, others seeking the Hereafter—were exposed so they could be purified. God then allowed them to be turned back from the enemy as a trial, not because He had abandoned them, and He forgave them. The closing statement affirms that His grace remains with the believers, and their failure does not cancel His mercy when they return to Him.

translation: [Remember] when you were climbing up and not turning back to anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you. So He repaid you with distress upon distress, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you or what befell you. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the painful confusion and setback at Uhud were a merciful correction from Allah: by allowing the believers to taste loss after their lapse in obedience, He purified them from attachment to spoils, victory, or personal safety and redirected their hearts toward the Prophet’s call and to reliance upon Allah. Their grief over missed gain and suffered harm was, in this sense, a discipline meant to prevent a deeper grief—the grief of disobedience and misplaced priority—while Allah’s awareness of their deeds means nothing of their intentions, weaknesses, or repentance is hidden from Him.

translation: Then He sent down upon you, after distress, security—drowsiness overtaking a group of you—while another group worried about themselves, thinking about Allah unjustly, thoughts of ignorance. They say, "Do we have any say in the matter?" Say, "Indeed, the matter entirely belongs to Allah." They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say, "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here." Say, "If you had remained in your houses, those for whom killing was decreed would have gone forth to their places of death." And so that Allah may test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse interprets the aftermath of Uhud as a moment of divine testing that separated sincere trust from hidden doubt. For the believers, Allah replaced fear with a profound sense of security, even causing sleep to overcome them—a sign that their hearts were anchored in reliance upon Him despite danger. The other group, however, was consumed by anxiety over their own selves and entertained false assumptions about Allah, resembling the fatalistic and resentful mindset of ignorance. They questioned whether they had any real say or choice, but the Quran corrects this by declaring that the entire affair—victory, defeat, life, and death—belongs to Allah’s decree and wisdom, not to human calculation alone. Their secret objections are exposed: had they stayed behind, those decreed to die would still have gone out to their appointed places of death. Therefore, the painful event was not a failure of planning or counsel but a means by which Allah tests inner convictions and purifies the heart from hypocrisy, complaint, and doubt. True faith submits to Allah’s decree with trust and seeks purification, while hypocrisy resents outcomes and secretly challenges divine wisdom. Allah fully knows the hidden thoughts and intentions within the breasts.

translation: Indeed, those among you who turned back on the day the two hosts met — it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some [misdeeds] they had earned. But Allah has pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.
interpretation: This refers to the believers who fled at the Battle of Uhud. The Qur'an explains their retreat as a spiritual slip induced by Satan, exploiting weaknesses resulting from earlier sins or worldly attachments. The lesson is that sin weakens resolve and opens the door to Satan's influence, so believers must guard their hearts and actions. Yet the verse immediately offers hope: Allah pardoned them, showing that failure after faith does not necessitate eternal rejection. His names al-Ghafur and al-Halim mean He covers sins and forbears, not punishing immediately, thus inviting repentance and return. So the verse combines warning about the consequences of sin with assurance of divine mercy for those who acknowledge and mend their ways.

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers when they traveled in the land or were fighting: ‘If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed.’ [That was] so that Allah might make it a regret in their hearts. And Allah gives life and causes death, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against adopting the disbelievers’ way of thinking, which measures life and death merely by physical circumstances. The disbelievers claimed that if their relatives had stayed behind rather than traveling or fighting, they would not have died. The Qur’an declares this to be false: Allah alone decrees life and death, and no place or situation can delay or hasten the appointed term. Their false regret does not change reality; rather, it becomes a source of grief and loss in their hearts because they rely on their own calculations instead of Allah. Believers are taught to place their trust in Allah, continue fulfilling their duties, and remember that He sees every action and intention.

translation: And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die, then forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they accumulate.
interpretation: This verse teaches that dying or being killed in God's cause is not a loss, because the forgiveness and mercy that await such a person are far greater and more valuable than all the worldly wealth, possessions, and gains that people gather in this life. It calls believers to prioritize God's pleasure and the eternal reward over material interests and fear of death.

translation: And if you die or are killed, indeed to Allah you will be gathered.
interpretation: This means that whether a person’s life ends by natural death or by being slain, the final destination and gathering is before Allah alone, who will judge with perfect justice. It teaches that death in Allah’s path is not annihilation but a return to Him, and it urges the believer to live and strive with the awareness that every soul will ultimately meet Allah and be held accountable.

translation: So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them. And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you. So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him.
interpretation: This verse teaches that gentle, merciful leadership is a gift from Allah and the strongest means of keeping people united. Harshness and hardness of heart drive people away, whereas forgiveness, seeking Allah’s forgiveness for others, and consulting them in matters build loyalty and shared responsibility. After consultation and resolve, the believer must place final trust in Allah alone, for Allah loves those who rely upon Him after taking the proper means.

translation: If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you? And in Allah let the believers place their trust.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all victory and defeat, help and abandonment, ultimately come from Allah alone. If He grants His support, no power can prevail against the believers; if He withholds it, no created being can substitute for Him or provide aid after Him. Therefore, true faith requires that believers place their reliance and trust wholly in Allah—not in material strength, numbers, or human alliances—while still taking the necessary means. Trust in Him is the foundation of the believer’s stance in both triumph and trial.

translation: It is not for a prophet to misappropriate [spoils]. And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be repaid in full for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse establishes that prophets are far above treachery or embezzlement, especially in handling spoils and public trusts. It warns that any illicit gain, particularly from a trust, will not be forgotten but will be brought forth as a burden and disgrace on the Day of Judgment. Divine justice is exact: every soul receives precisely what its deeds deserve, with no reduction or injustice. The verse thus trains the conscience to regard secret betrayal in wealth or responsibility as a serious matter that cannot escape God’s reckoning.

translation: Is then he who follows the pleasure of Allah like he who has incurred wrath from Allah, and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This rhetorical question denies any equality between those who sincerely pursue God's good pleasure and those who earn His anger by choosing disobedience. The former live oriented toward divine approval and its eternal reward; the latter carry God's displeasure and end in Hell, the worst final home. The verse thus teaches that moral and spiritual choices are not indifferent: seeking God's pleasure leads to salvation, while persisting in what provokes His wrath leads to ruin.

translation: They are [varying] ranks in the sight of Allah, and Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that people are not equal before Allah in station and reward; their ranks differ according to their faith, obedience, and deeds. Allah is fully aware of every action, intention, and hidden motive, so His judgment and recompense are perfectly just and correspond exactly to what each person has earned.

translation: Indeed, Allah conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although before that they were in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights that true favor and blessing come from Allah through the sending of His Messenger. The Messenger is from among the believers themselves, so he shares their nature, language, and circumstances, making guidance accessible and imitable. He performs three essential functions: he recites Allah’s signs, which awaken hearts and minds to divine truth; he purifies them, cleansing their beliefs and conduct from idolatry, hypocrisy, and moral corruption; and he teaches them the Book and wisdom, meaning revelation and its correct understanding and application. Their prior state was one of clear misguidance, so the sending of the Prophet is a mercy and grace that rescues them from error and establishes them upon knowledge, purification, and obedience.

translation: And when a calamity struck you—you had already inflicted twice as much—you said, “How is this?” Say, “It is from your own selves.” Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the setback the believers suffered was not a breach of Allah’s promise but a consequence of their own choices, disobedience, and internal discord. Their question, “How is this?”, is answered by placing responsibility on themselves: failure came through their own actions, not through any weakness in Allah’s power. At the same time, Allah’s statement that He is over all things competent affirms that He remains fully able to decree victory or trial, to forgive, and to bring about His wise purpose through all events.

translation: And whatever befell you on the day the two hosts met was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might make evident the believers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the setback suffered by the believers at the meeting of the two armies did not escape Allah’s decree; it happened by His will and permission. Its deeper purpose was to manifest true faith, testing and distinguishing those who remained sincere, steadfast, and trusting in Allah despite hardship.

translation: And so that He might know those who are hypocrites. And it was said to them, 'Come, fight in the cause of Allah or defend.' They said, 'If we knew fighting, we would have followed you.' They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith. They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts. And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.
interpretation: This verse exposes the inner reality of the wavering hypocrites during a time of danger: when the call to struggle or at least defensive support was made, they declined under a cover of ignorance and excuse. Their claim that they would have followed if they knew fighting was false, since the issue was not lack of information but lack of sincerity and resolve. Their outward profession of faith was not matched by their hearts, so on that day their words and conduct placed them nearer to disbelief than to faith. The verse teaches that trials uncover what people conceal, that verbal allegiance is worthless without inward commitment, and that God's knowledge encompasses the hidden motives and unspoken reservations of every soul.

translation: Those who said about their brothers while they themselves remained behind, 'If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed.' Say, 'Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse rebukes the hypocrites who stayed back from battle and then claimed that those believers who fought and were killed would have survived had they followed their advice. God responds that if their cautiousness could truly ward off death, they should be able to prevent death from reaching themselves. The verse thus exposes their claim as false: death is decreed by God and cannot be postponed or avoided by human calculation, cowardice, or disobedience. It also refutes the idea that obeying God's command to strive in His cause is the cause of death; rather, the appointed term is fixed, and martyrdom is not a failure of prudence but a fulfillment of divine decree.

translation: And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for.
interpretation: This verse teaches that those who die fighting sincerely in God’s cause are not to be regarded as dead in the ordinary sense; their life continues in a special, exalted state with their Lord, where He grants them sustenance and honor. It is a consolation and assurance that their sacrifice is not loss, but a transition to nearness to God and ongoing divine provision, even though we cannot perceive that life.

translation: Rejoicing in what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty, and they receive glad tidings about those who have not yet joined them from behind them—that no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This describes the state of those slain in the way of Allah: they are alive with their Lord, rejoicing in His favor, and they are given joyful news concerning the believers still left behind who have not yet joined them. Their joy includes the assurance that those still striving in faith will also be safe from fear and sorrow, because Allah’s promise to the steadfast is true and His bounty is not lost.

translation: They rejoice in grace from Allah and bounty, and that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true joy for the believer comes from God’s favor and generosity, and from the firm conviction that He is perfectly faithful in rewarding faith. It assures that God’s accounting is not like human accounting: no effort, sacrifice, or steadfastness of a believer is ever lost or forgotten; rather, it is preserved and recompensed according to His wisdom, justice, and mercy.

translation: Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after they had suffered wounds—for those among them who did good and feared Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that genuine faith is proven by steadfast obedience when hardship follows loss. The great reward is promised to those who combine righteous conduct with God-consciousness, showing that outward response to Allah and His Messenger must be joined to inward sincerity, restraint, and piety.

translation: Those to whom people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.' But it increased them in faith, and they said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the response of true believers to intimidation and fear campaigns: instead of being weakened by warnings of overwhelming opposition, their conviction deepens, because they measure power not by numbers but by God's sufficiency. Their declaration 'Sufficient for us is Allah' is an act of entrusting all affairs to Him and a recognition that no coalition, however large, can harm or help without His permission. It teaches that faith is strengthened when tested, and that the believer's ultimate security lies in reliance upon God, the best Guardian and Disposer of all matters.

translation: So they returned with grace and bounty from Allah; no harm had touched them, and they sought Allah’s pleasure. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: God’s grace and favor protect and reward those who act sincerely for His sake. Safety from harm and the attainment of good are gifts from Him, not merely human achievements. The believer’s highest aim is God’s pleasure, and because His bounty is immense, He grants beyond what the deed itself deserves.

translation: That is only Satan who frightens you of his allies. So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the fear of hostile powers, opponents, or worldly forces is a deception cast by Satan to weaken the believers’ resolve. Satan uses his allies as an intimidating image to make people abandon truth, obedience, or steadfastness. The believer is therefore told not to let the fear of any created being—no matter how powerful or numerous—control the heart. Instead, the reverent fear and awe of God alone should govern one’s choices and loyalties. The closing condition, “if you are believers,” shows that true faith requires trusting God’s power and protection more than fearing the threats of His enemies, and that overcoming such fear is a sign of sincere iman.

translation: And do not let those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. Indeed, they will never harm Allah at all. Allah intends that He will not give them any share in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and the believers not to grieve over those who rush eagerly into disbelief, whether by rejecting faith, hypocrisy, or apostasy. Their conduct cannot harm Allah in any way; it only harms themselves and forfeits their own good. Allah’s will to give them no portion of reward in the Hereafter is the just consequence of their chosen disbelief and persistence in it. They are deprived of eternal good and will face a severe punishment. The verse teaches believers to place their concern with God’s pleasure rather than being distressed by the wrongdoing of others, leaving final judgment to Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who have purchased disbelief in exchange for faith will not harm Allah at all, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This means that whoever trades away faith for disbelief—whether by apostasy, hypocrisy, or preferring denial over belief—cannot diminish Allah’s majesty, authority, or dominion in any way. The loss falls entirely upon the person who makes that exchange, and the painful punishment is the just consequence of choosing disbelief after faith had been made clear.

translation: And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is good for themselves. We only grant them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that worldly ease, long life, and apparent success given to those who reject faith are not signs of God’s favor or true benefit. Rather, such respite is a test and a gradual means by which they fall deeper into wrongdoing. The delay of punishment does not mean they are safe; it allows their sins to accumulate, and their final outcome is a disgraceful, humiliating torment.

translation: Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He separates the evil from the good. Nor would Allah reveal to you the unseen, but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Allah, then for you is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s way with the believing community is one of testing and refinement: He does not leave people merely on claims of faith, but through trials, commands, and circumstances He distinguishes the corrupt from the pure, the hypocritical from the sincere, and the false from the true. The unseen remains God’s exclusive knowledge; no person can claim access to it or to the secrets of hearts, except to the extent that God chooses and grants revelation to whom He selects among His messengers. Therefore, the proper response is not to demand hidden knowledge or to rely on outward labels, but to believe in God and His messengers, and to combine faith with God-consciousness and obedience; this is what leads to a great reward from God.

translation: And let not those who are miserly with what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is evil for them. They will be collared with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is well aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse condemns stinginess and hoarding, especially withholding wealth from the poor and from the obligations Allah has enjoined. It warns that refusing to spend from God-given blessings is not a gain but a loss: on the Day of Judgment, the very wealth they hoarded and refused to use for good will become a collar of torment around their necks. Since Allah is the ultimate Owner and Inheritor of the heavens and the earth, giving in His way does not diminish one's true inheritance, and He is fully aware of every act, intention, and hidden motive.

translation: Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich." We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."
interpretation: This verse exposes the arrogance and disbelief of those who mocked God when they were called to give charity, claiming that God was in need while they were wealthy. It affirms that God is fully aware of every word and deed, and that such blasphemy, along with their unjust slaughter of prophets, is recorded and will be brought forth as evidence against them. Their punishment is the blazing Fire, a just recompense for their defiance, their falsehood about God, and their violent rejection of His messengers.

translation: That is for what your hands have sent ahead, and Allah is not unjust to His servants.
interpretation: This verse means that the punishment or consequence being addressed is the direct result of people’s own freely chosen deeds, which they have sent ahead for themselves. It then affirms God’s perfect justice: He does not wrong His servants in any way, and any recompense He gives is exactly deserved. Therefore, no one is punished unjustly; rather, people are held accountable for what they themselves have committed, and God is free of any injustice toward His creation.

translation: Those who said, 'Indeed, Allah has taken our promise not to believe any messenger until he brings us an offering which fire consumes.' Say, 'There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with that which you described; then why did you kill them, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse exposes the false pretext of those who claimed that God had bound them by covenant not to accept any messenger unless he produced a miracle of a sacrifice consumed by heavenly fire. Their claim was not a sincere condition but a stubborn excuse for rejecting faith. The Prophet is commanded to reply that earlier messengers had already come to them with clear signs and with the very sign they demanded, yet their forefathers killed those messengers. Therefore their professed condition cannot be true, since if they were genuinely truthful in it, they would have believed and not slain the messengers who fulfilled it. The verse thus unmasks their rejection as willful disbelief and shows that demanding new signs was merely a way of avoiding submission to the truth.

translation: So if they deny you, messengers before you were also denied—who came with clear proofs, scriptures, and the illuminating Book.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and the believers by placing the rejection they face within the long pattern of human resistance to divine guidance. It teaches that the truth of a message is not diminished by people’s denial of it, nor is a messenger’s failure measured by whether his audience accepts him. Earlier messengers were also rejected even though they brought clear evidences of their truthfulness, revealed writings, and a Book that illuminates the path to God. Therefore, the believer should remain steadfast, knowing that opposition to revelation is not new and that God’s messengers are judged by faithful delivery of the message, not by the acceptance of their people.

translation: Every soul will taste death, and you will only be paid your rewards in full on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has truly succeeded. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse teaches that death is an inescapable reality for every living being, so no one should be deceived into treating worldly life as permanent or ultimate. True recompense is deferred to the Day of Resurrection, when every person will receive the full measure of their deeds. The only real success is being saved from Hellfire and entered into Paradise; all other gains are secondary and temporary. Therefore, the life of this world is a passing enjoyment that can delude people into prioritizing it over the eternal Hereafter.

translation: You will surely be tested in your possessions and in yourselves, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much abuse. But if you are patient and fear Allah, indeed, that is among the matters of firm resolve.
interpretation: This verse prepares the believers for unavoidable trials in two dimensions: loss or hardship regarding wealth and property, and affliction regarding life, health, family, or personal suffering. It also forewarns that they will hear painful and offensive speech from the People of the Book and the polytheists. The intended lesson is that the believer’s faith is not proven by ease alone; it is tested by adversity and by the hostility of others. The command is to respond with sabr—patient perseverance without despair or unlawful reaction—and taqwa—God-consciousness that keeps one obedient to Allah despite provocation. Such patience and piety are described as being among the matters of firm resolve, meaning they are not optional virtues but essential marks of true faith and high determination. The verse thus teaches that trials are part of the divine plan, that opposition from others is expected, and that the believer’s success lies in remaining steadfast and righteous rather than being shaken or led into resentment and retaliation.

translation: And [remember] when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture: “You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it.” But they cast it behind their backs and sold it for a paltry price. So evil is what they purchase.
interpretation: This verse condemns the People of the Book for breaking the solemn covenant Allah took from them: to openly convey the revealed truth, especially the clear signs and prophecies pointing to the final Messenger, and never to hide or distort them. By casting the covenant behind their backs, they treated it as worthless and disregarded their sacred obligation. Their motive was worldly gain—status, influence, favor, or material benefit—which the Qur’an calls a paltry price because it is temporary and insignificant compared with the truth and its reward. Thus they are rebuked: what they chose to acquire through concealment and betrayal is evil, and its consequence is loss and divine displeasure.

translation: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done—do not think them safe from punishment; and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against self-satisfaction with one’s own deeds and the desire to be praised for virtues or accomplishments one does not actually possess. It exposes the spiritual danger of conceit, hypocrisy, and seeking credit falsely. Such people may feel secure because of what they imagine they have achieved or because others flatter them, but God declares that they are not beyond His punishment. Their rejoicing is misplaced and their craving for undeserved praise does not remove their accountability; instead, it earns them a painful chastisement. The verse teaches that true safety lies in sincerity, humility, and deeds done for God alone, not in self-congratulation or public admiration.

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This affirms that all creation, visible and hidden, is Allah’s property and under His sole authority; nothing occurs outside His will. His absolute power means He is fully able to bring the dead to life, reckon every deed, and fulfill every promise or warning, so trust and worship are due to Him alone.

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the vast, ordered universe and the precise, recurring cycle of night and day are not random or meaningless; they are clear signs pointing to the existence, power, wisdom, and oneness of God. However, these signs benefit only those who use their God-given intellect with reflection and sincerity—people of sound understanding who look beyond the surface of creation to recognize the Creator and live in awareness of Him.

translation: Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and who reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth: “Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
interpretation: This describes the believer’s life as continuous remembrance of God in every posture and circumstance, joined with deep reflection on the universe as God’s creation. Such reflection is not mere curiosity; it leads to the realization that creation has purpose and meaning, to glorifying God above any foolishness or injustice, and to seeking refuge from the Fire. Thus, remembrance and contemplation together produce humility, gratitude, and accountability before God.

translation: Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him, and the wrongdoers have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that entry into the Fire is the ultimate disgrace, stripping a person of honor and exposing the ruin of those who persist in wrongdoing. It affirms that no helper, intercessor, or ally can rescue the unjust from God’s judgment once His decree is enacted, so the servant must flee from sin and seek God’s mercy and protection.

translation: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' so we have believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our evil deeds, and cause us to die with the righteous.
interpretation: This is the prayer of those who truly receive the call to faith: they confess that guidance begins with hearing and obeying the divine invitation, then turn that faith into humble supplication. They seek three things: pardon for sins, erasure of the traces and consequences of bad deeds, and a death in the company of the righteous—meaning not merely forgiveness in the Hereafter but transformation in this life and a good end. It shows that faith is not a passive label; it moves the heart to gratitude, repentance, and the desire to be gathered with the people of righteousness.

translation: Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You never break Your promise.
interpretation: This is a believer’s plea that God’s promise, conveyed through the prophets, be fulfilled in their favor—namely forgiveness, mercy, and the reward of the Hereafter—and that they be spared the humiliation of being exposed and disgraced on the Day of Resurrection. The supplication rests on God’s perfect truthfulness: His promise is never revoked, delayed beyond its appointed time, or altered, so trusting in it is both an act of worship and a source of hope.

translation: So their Lord responded to them: “I will never let the work of any worker among you be lost, whether male or female. You are from one another. So those who emigrated and were driven out of their homes and were harmed in My cause and fought and were killed — I will surely remove their misdeeds and admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah. And with Allah is the best reward.”
interpretation: This verse establishes that God answers His servants’ supplications and that no sincere deed is ever wasted before Him. It teaches the fundamental equality of men and women in moral responsibility and divine recompense: neither gender has lesser standing in the sight of God, and both are mutually connected in faith, support, and accountability. The verse then highlights a particular community of believers who endured severe trials for God’s sake—migration, displacement, persecution, and fighting, even to the point of being killed. Their sacrifices are met with God’s promise to erase their sins and admit them into gardens of eternal rivers, not as a human repayment but as a reward from God Himself. The closing statement emphasizes that God’s reward is the most excellent, secure, and enduring; it surpasses all worldly compensation and reflects His generosity, justice, and faithfulness to those who remain steadfast for His cause.

translation: Do not let the movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you.
interpretation: This verse warns believers not to be misled by the apparent prosperity, power, or free movement of those who reject faith. Their worldly success is temporary and is not a sign that their path is true or that they are favored by God; it is only a fleeting enjoyment. The believer should remain firm in faith and not measure truth by worldly advantage, for the final outcome and true success belong to God.

translation: A brief enjoyment; then their refuge will be Hell — and how wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse teaches that whatever worldly ease, wealth, power, or prosperity the disbelievers enjoy is only a fleeting and insignificant provision. It is not evidence of divine favor, but a temporary respite that soon ends. Their final destination and eternal abode is Jahannam, and it is the worst possible resting place and bed. The verse therefore warns against being deceived by worldly success and directs attention to the final outcome: the brief pleasures of this life cannot compare with the lasting consequence of one’s deeds in the Hereafter.

translation: But those who fear their Lord will have Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, as hospitality from Allah. And what is with Allah is better for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse declares that true success belongs to those who are mindful of their Lord, guarding themselves against His displeasure by faith and obedience. Their reward is not a passing worldly enjoyment but eternal Gardens with rivers flowing beneath them, granted as a generous welcome and provision from God Himself. It teaches that whatever God has prepared for the pious is far superior to all temporary delights and gains of this world, and that the ultimate good is reserved for those who remain righteous and devoted to Him.

translation: And indeed, among the People of the Book there are those who believe in Allah and in what was revealed to you and in what was revealed to them, humbly submitting to Allah. They do not exchange the signs of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the People of the Book are not all alike in unbelief; among them are sincere believers who accept God, the revelation sent to the Prophet Muhammad, and the earlier revelations sent to their own prophets. Their faith is marked by humility before God, not arrogance or partisanship. They refuse to sell God's signs for a petty worldly price—meaning they do not conceal, distort, or abandon divine truth for wealth, status, popularity, or communal approval. For such people, God Himself guarantees their reward, and His reckoning is swift and perfectly just: no sincere deed is ignored, and no hidden motive is missed. The verse thus affirms that righteousness is measured by genuine faith, humility, and fidelity to God's revelation rather than by communal label, and it warns against treating religion as a means of worldly gain.

translation: O you who have believed, be patient, and persevere, and remain stationed, and fear Allah, so that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers to combine three inseparable dimensions of faith: patient endurance in obeying Allah and avoiding sin, mutual perseverance and steadfastness with one another when trials come, and constant vigilance and readiness in the path of truth. Then it crowns all of this with taqwa—God-consciousness that purifies intention and keeps effort within divine obedience. Success and true flourishing are therefore not promised by endurance alone, but by perseverance joined to taqwa: remaining firm together, guarding one’s duty to Allah, and refusing to abandon faith, community, or moral restraint under pressure.

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate, and spread from them many men and women. And fear Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, Allah is ever, over you, a Watcher.
interpretation: This verse calls all humanity to God-consciousness by reminding them that they descend from a single soul and its mate, making all people equal in origin and bound by shared humanity. It then commands reverence for Allah and safeguards the ties of kinship, since the rights of people are joined to the rights of Allah. Allah’s attribute of being a Watcher means He observes every deed, so no violation of His commands or of people’s rights is hidden from Him.

translation: And give the orphans their wealth, and do not exchange the bad for the good, and do not consume their wealth along with your wealth. Indeed, it has been a great sin.
interpretation: This is a directive to guardians and executors of orphans: their property is a sacred trust to be returned in full when they are capable of managing it. It forbids any misappropriation—whether by swapping the orphan’s superior or lawful assets for one’s own inferior or unlawful ones, or by absorbing their wealth into one’s own under the pretext of guardianship. Such betrayal is not a minor infraction but a grave sin, because it exploits the weak and violates both justice and trusteeship.

translation: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry those that please you of women—two, three, or four. But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one, or what your right hands possess. That is more suitable, so that you may not be unjust.
interpretation: The verse makes justice the condition and limit of polygamy. It addresses guardians who feared they could not be equitable toward orphan girls under their care—especially if they wished to marry them for their wealth or status. Such men are directed toward other women, but even then not without restriction: the maximum is four, and plurality is permitted only if the husband can treat co-wives fairly. If he fears partiality or injustice, he must restrict himself to one wife, or to what his right hand lawfully possesses in the historical setting. Thus the verse establishes monogamy as the safer and preferable choice whenever justice among multiple wives is doubtful, and it forbids using marriage as a means of exploitation or injustice.

translation: And give the women their bridal gifts as a free gift. But if they willingly give up to you anything of it, then consume it with pleasure and ease.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the bridal gift (mahr) is a right belonging to the wife, which the husband must give willingly as an obligatory gift, not as a favor or a price. It may not be withheld, reduced, or taken back by coercion, deceit, or pressure. If the wife, of her own free will and without compulsion, chooses to forgo or return some part of it to her husband, then that portion becomes lawful and wholesome for him to use. The verse thus protects the wife’s financial dignity while allowing her, through autonomous consent, to show generosity within the marriage.

translation: And do not give the foolish your wealth, which Allah has made a means of support for you; but provide for them from it, clothe them, and speak to them a kind word.
interpretation: This verse teaches that wealth is a trust from Allah and a means of sustaining life, so it must not be handed over to those who are unable to manage it responsibly—such as the immature, reckless, or mentally incapable. At the same time, they are not to be neglected: their guardians must manage the property for their benefit, use it to feed and clothe them, and address them with respectful and gentle words. Thus the verse balances protecting wealth from waste with showing compassion, care, and dignity to those under guardianship.

translation: And test the orphans until they reach marriage [age]; then if you perceive in them sound judgment, deliver to them their property. And do not consume it extravagantly or hastily before they grow up. And whoever is rich, let him abstain; and whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is fair. And when you deliver to them their property, take witnesses over them. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner.
interpretation: This verse makes the orphan’s wealth a sacred trust in the guardian’s care. The guardian must not hand it over merely because the child reaches a certain age; he must first test the orphan’s maturity and discern whether he has become capable of managing money responsibly. Puberty and sound judgment together are the signs that the orphan is ready to receive his property. Until then, the guardian is forbidden to waste, exploit, or quickly consume the orphan’s wealth out of fear that the orphan will grow up and claim it. If the guardian is wealthy, he should restrain himself and not take payment; if he is poor and genuinely in need, he may take only what is reasonable and just. When the property is finally returned, witnesses must be brought so that rights are preserved and disputes are prevented. In the end, Allah is the all-sufficient Reckoner who sees every act of faithfulness or betrayal.

translation: For men there is a share of what parents and near relatives leave, and for women there is a share of what parents and near relatives leave, whether it be little or much—an allotted share.
interpretation: This verse establishes inheritance as a divinely ordained right for both male and female heirs among close relatives. It abolishes the pre-Islamic custom of excluding women and the weak from inheritance, affirming that entitlement is based on kinship and is not a favor granted by male relatives. The phrase “an allotted share” means these portions are fixed and obligatory by God’s command; they must be given exactly as prescribed, whether the estate is small or large, and no one may arbitrarily withhold, reduce, or trade them away. Thus it affirms women’s independent financial rights and the obligation to distribute the estate according to God’s decree.

translation: And when the division [of inheritance] is attended by relatives, orphans, and the needy, give them something from it and speak to them a kind word.
interpretation: This verse instructs the heirs, at the time of distributing an estate, not to ignore the vulnerable who are present but have no legal share—such as distant relatives, orphans, and the poor. They should voluntarily give them something from the inheritance as a gesture of compassion and generosity, and if they cannot give, they must at least speak gently and respectfully, avoiding harshness or humiliation. Thus the division of inheritance is not merely a legal transaction but also an occasion for social mercy, preserving the dignity of the needy and strengthening communal ties.

translation: And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them. So let them fear Allah and speak a just word.
interpretation: This verse commands guardians, executors, and all who deal with the property and welfare of orphans and dependent children to act with the same protective care they would desire for their own helpless children. It warns them not to wrong the weak through unfair wills, delay, harshness, or misuse of authority. The fear of Allah here means conscientious justice and mercy, and the “just word” means speech that is truthful, fair, and constructive, securing rights and avoiding harm to the vulnerable.

translation: Indeed, those who unjustly devour the wealth of orphans only devour fire into their bellies, and they will enter a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning that consuming an orphan’s property wrongfully is not merely taking wealth but is, in reality, swallowing fire that will become torment within the person. The wrongfully acquired gain is depicted as fire because it burns away blessing, corrupts the soul, and inevitably leads to the punishment of Sa‘ir, the blazing Fire. The word “unjustly” distinguishes unlawful appropriation from rightful and just dealings with an orphan’s property, such as lawful guardianship, maintenance, or agreed compensation. The verse affirms God’s protection of the weak and orphaned, and declares that those who exploit them will face certain and painful accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male is the like of the share of two females.
