translation: So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on your sides. Then when you are secure, establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer has been prescribed upon the believers at fixed times.
interpretation: This verse teaches that remembrance of God is not limited to the formal ritual prayer: in danger, illness, travel, or battle, a believer must continue to remember and invoke God in whatever posture is possible. The concessions allowing shortened or fear-based prayer are only temporary; once security and normal conditions return, the full prescribed prayer must be established. The final clause makes prayer a permanently binding, time-specific obligation upon every believer, not an optional devotion whose appointed times may be neglected. Thus the verse joins divine mercy in hardship with firmness in obligation: the spirit of worship remains continuous, while the ritual prayer resumes its complete ordered form when circumstances permit.

translation: And do not weaken in seeking the people [of the enemy]. If you are suffering, indeed they are suffering as you suffer, but you hope from Allah what they do not hope. And Allah is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers not to lose heart or resolve in pursuing the hostile people, even when hardship, wounds, or exhaustion are real. Their pain is not unique: the enemy also suffers as they suffer. What distinguishes the believers is hope in Allah—His help, reward, victory, and mercy in this life and the Hereafter—which the disbelievers do not have. So faith supplies a strength and motivation that mere worldly endurance cannot. The ending affirms that Allah knows the believers’ struggles and the enemies’ condition, and that His commands, promises, and decrees are wise and just.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book with truth, so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you; and do not be a pleader for the treacherous.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the revealed Book is the criterion for judging among people, not personal inclination or group loyalty. The Prophet is to rule by what God has made clear to him, and by extension anyone entrusted with judgment must do the same. It specifically forbids standing up for those who betray trusts or commit treachery, meaning that judicial or political authority must never be used to protect the guilty, even if they are close or powerful. Justice requires siding with truth and against betrayal, not with the betrayer.

translation: And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The command is to turn to Allah in repentance and ask His pardon. It teaches that awareness of one’s shortcomings should lead to seeking forgiveness, not despair, and it grounds that command in Allah’s unchanging attributes: He is Ghafur, repeatedly forgiving those who repent, and Rahim, whose mercy embraces them. Thus seeking His forgiveness is both a duty and a means of drawing near to His mercy.

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful.
interpretation: This verse forbids defending or pleading for those who wrong themselves through betrayal and dishonesty. It teaches that Allah’s love is not for those who persist in treachery and sin, so loyalty to family, group, or self must never lead a believer to support falsehood or shield a wrongdoer from justice. True faithfulness requires upholding truth and justice, even when it is against those one might otherwise wish to defend.

translation: They conceal themselves from people, but they do not conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of speech. And Allah encompasses what they do.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who fear human disapproval while ignoring God’s constant presence and knowledge. It teaches that true accountability is before Allah, who is with His servants even in their most hidden moments and who hears every secret word and intention. Concealing evil from people is worthless if one does not conceal it from God, because His knowledge encompasses all deeds—public and private—and no plot or hidden speech escapes His awareness. Thus the verse calls believers to sincerity, God-consciousness, and shame before their Creator above all created beings.

translation: Here you are—you who argued on their behalf in the life of this world. But who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who use worldly arguments and advocacy to shield wrongdoers from blame or consequences. It reminds them that such pleading carries no weight before God, who knows all hidden realities. On the Day of Judgment, no one can contend with God on their behalf or take charge of their affair as a protector. Therefore, the only true refuge is sincere repentance and alignment with truth, not partisanship or defending falsehood.

translation: And whoever does an evil deed or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that whether a person's sin harms others or only wrongs his own soul, the door of repentance remains open: sincere seeking of Allah's forgiveness removes the sin and places the servant under Allah's forgiveness and mercy, so no one should despair of His pardon.

translation: And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every sin a person commits is a burden upon his own soul; its harm and accountability return to him alone, not to Allah or to others. It rejects the notion that one can damage God by disobedience or transfer one’s guilt to another. The names “Knowing, Wise” affirm that Allah is fully aware of every deed and intention, and that His judgment, commands, and recompense are perfectly wise and just, so no soul is wronged and each is held responsible only for what it itself has earned.

translation: And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it upon an innocent person, he has surely carried a false accusation and a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse condemns committing a wrong and then shifting its blame onto someone innocent. Such a person bears guilt for two grave matters: the original fault or sin, and the added sin of slander and injustice against an innocent person. It establishes that one cannot escape responsibility by falsely accusing another; the guilt remains and is made more severe.

translation: And if it were not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have intended to lead you astray. But they do not mislead anyone except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know. And the favor of Allah upon you is great.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It reassures him that the schemes of a faction to misguide him are thwarted by Allah’s grace and mercy; their deception recoils only upon their own souls and cannot harm him because Allah is his protector. It further establishes that the revelation—the Book and the Wisdom—is a pure divine gift, and that the knowledge granted to him was not acquired by himself. Thus it combines a rebuke of those who plot against the truth, a vindication of the Prophet’s integrity in receiving and conveying revelation, and a proclamation of Allah’s immense favor upon him.

translation: There is no good in much of their secret talks, except for one who enjoins charity, kindness, or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that private conversations and secret counsel are not good merely because they are private; their value depends on their purpose. Much whispered talk among people is blameworthy when it serves gossip, plotting, division, or harm. The exception is whoever uses such private discussion to encourage charity, to call to recognized good, or to reconcile people who are estranged. Such counsel is praiseworthy because it repairs what is broken and promotes benefit. The verse further stresses sincerity: the one who does this must seek Allah's pleasure, not praise, influence, or personal gain. For such a person, Allah promises a great reward, showing that the worth of an act is tied both to its righteous aim and to the purity of the intention behind it.

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows a path other than that of the believers — We will turn him over to what he has turned to and drive him into Hell; and evil is the destination.
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning against knowingly departing from the Prophet’s guidance and from the collective way of the believers. After truth has been made clear, opposition to the Messenger and choosing a path contrary to the Muslim community is not mere disagreement but a rejection of divinely guided authority. The consequence is that God leaves such a person to the direction he has chosen, allowing his self-chosen path to define him, and ultimately he is cast into Hell, the worst end. The verse therefore binds Muslims to the Prophet’s teaching and the united way of the believers, and warns that deliberate deviation after knowledge invites divine abandonment and ruin.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates partners with Allah has indeed strayed far away.
interpretation: This verse means that shirk—associating any partner, rival, or equal with God in worship, lordship, or divine attributes—is the gravest transgression and is not forgiven for one who dies upon it without repentance. Sins below shirk are left to God’s will: He may forgive them by His mercy or punish them by His justice. The verse warns that shirk is not a minor error but a radical departure from truth and guidance, placing one far from the straight path.

translation: They do not invoke besides Him except female deities, and they do not invoke except a rebellious Satan.
interpretation: This verse exposes the polytheists’ worship of idols as utterly false: the beings they call upon besides Allah are merely female names or imagined female deities with no power to create, benefit, or harm, and the real force driving such worship is obedience to a rebellious Satan who leads them away from the worship of the One true God. Thus their supposed devotion to gods is, in reality, submission to Satan’s deception.

translation: Allah has cursed him; and he said, 'I will surely take from Your servants a determined share.'
interpretation: This is Satan’s declaration after Allah cursed him: he vows to mislead a fixed portion of humankind, claiming them as his followers and turning them away from obedience to Allah. It reveals his open enmity and persistent deception, and warns people to seek Allah’s protection so they do not become part of that appointed share.

translation: And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely entice them with false hopes, and I will surely command them and they will cut off the ears of livestock, and I will surely command them and they will alter Allah's creation. And whoever takes Satan as a protector besides Allah has indeed suffered a clear loss.
interpretation: This is Satan's declaration of how he will deceive humanity. He promises to lead people away from the truth, fill them with false desires and wishful thinking, and command them to commit acts of superstition and corruption, such as mutilating livestock and changing Allah's creation. The alteration of Allah's creation refers to corrupting the natural order and the God-given human disposition, whether through physical mutilation or through perverting religion, laws, and values. The verse warns that whoever accepts Satan as a guardian and ally instead of Allah has entered into obvious ruin, because he has traded divine guidance for deception and loss.

translation: He promises them and arouses in them false hopes, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion.
interpretation: This verse exposes Satan’s method: he does not compel people but seduces them through promises and wishful thinking, making false hopes appear attractive and attainable. His promises are inherently empty and deceptive, designed to mislead, delay repentance, and draw people away from God’s guidance. It warns against being lulled by delusions, procrastination, and hollow assurances, and calls one to measure every promise by its source and ultimate truth.

translation: Those—their refuge is Hell, and they will not find any escape from it.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who persist in following Satan’s deceptive path and reject God’s guidance will end in Hell, and they will have no means of fleeing, avoiding, or escaping it. It affirms the certainty of divine judgment and the utter helplessness of such people to escape their punishment.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds — We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true. And who is more truthful than Allah in speech?
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith is inseparable from righteous action: those who believe must let that belief bear fruit in deeds. The eternal gardens with rivers flowing beneath them symbolize unending divine provision, refreshment, and life, while “abiding therein forever” affirms that the reward is permanent and never cut off. The statement “the promise of Allah is true” is a decisive assurance that Allah’s pledge cannot fail or be revoked; it rests on His absolute truthfulness, not on human merit. The rhetorical question “who is more truthful than Allah in speech?” closes the matter by declaring that no word, promise, or report is more reliable than Allah’s, so the believer’s confidence, hope, and effort should be anchored in His truthful promise.

translation: It is not according to your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse establishes that salvation and divine acceptance are not determined by mere claims, communal affiliation, or wishful expectations—neither those of the Muslims nor those of the People of the Book. God's judgment is based on actual deeds, and anyone who commits evil will be held accountable for it. No one can escape that accountability through any guardian, intercessor, or helper apart from God, so true deliverance depends on sincere faith and righteous action combined with God's mercy and forgiveness.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged even as much as a speck on a date stone.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God’s reward is not based on gender or worldly status but on two joined conditions: true faith and righteous action. Men and women are addressed equally and are equally capable of entering Paradise when they believe and do good. The word naqir refers to the tiny groove or speck on a date seed, expressing the smallest imaginable amount; thus God promises perfect justice, meaning no good deed will be lost or diminished, and no believer will be wronged in the least.

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while doing good and follows the way of Ibrahim, the upright? And Allah took Ibrahim as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the worthiest religion is total self-surrender to God alone, joined to sincere righteous conduct and adherence to the original monotheistic path of Abraham, who turned away from all false worship. God’s taking Abraham as an intimate friend shows that such pure devotion and uprightness raise a person to nearness, love, and special honor with God, and that true faith is measured not by claims or labels but by submitting one’s whole being to the One God while doing good.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is, over all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that absolute ownership, authority, and control over all creation—everything in the heavens and the earth—belong to Allah alone. His knowledge, power, and providence encompass every existent, so nothing is outside His dominion, nothing escapes His will, and all creatures depend entirely upon Him.

translation: And they ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, “Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also] what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them, and concerning the helpless among children, and that you stand for orphans with justice. And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it.”
interpretation: This verse answers a question about women’s rights, especially those of orphan girls under a guardian’s authority. It condemns the practice of withholding an orphan woman’s rightful property, dowry, inheritance, or fair treatment while wanting to marry her for her wealth or beauty. Allah commands that such women be given their full rights and that guardians either marry them with justice or leave them alone. The verse also commands justice and protection for vulnerable children and all orphans. It teaches that authority over the weak must not become a means of exploitation; rather, it is a trust requiring fairness. Any good done for women, orphans, or the oppressed is fully known to Allah and will not be lost.

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or turning away, there is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves. And peace is better. And souls are prone to stinginess. And if you do good and fear Allah, indeed Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses marital discord in which the wife perceives harshness, aversion, or withdrawal from her husband. It permits the spouses to negotiate a reconciliation even if it involves the wife relinquishing some of her rights, because preserving the marriage and restoring mutual peace may be better than insisting on every entitlement while the relationship collapses. Yet this is not a license for coercion or injustice: the standard is that peace is better, and both spouses are urged to resist the selfishness and greed naturally present in human souls by choosing excellence and God-consciousness. Since Allah is fully aware of hidden motives and outward actions, any settlement must be sincere and fair, not a pretext for oppression. The verse thus combines realistic recognition of human weakness with a moral call to generosity, justice, and accountability before God.

translation: And you will never be able to be perfectly just between women, even if you eagerly desire to. So do not incline completely [toward one], leaving the other as if suspended. And if you reconcile and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse recognizes that absolute equality in the heart’s inclination and affection among co-wives is beyond human capacity, so God does not burden people with what they cannot control. What is prohibited is deliberate, complete partiality in treatment that abandons the neglected wife in a state of suspension—neither fully married nor properly released. The command is therefore to maintain justice in rights, provisions, time, and fair dealing as much as possible, and to correct any wrong by reconciliation and God-consciousness. Where a person falls short despite sincere effort, God’s forgiveness and mercy encompass that weakness, provided one does not persist in injustice.

translation: And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His vast bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse gives divine assurance that when a marriage cannot be repaired and separation becomes the rightful course, neither spouse should remain trapped by fear of poverty, loneliness, or loss. Allah Himself will provide for each from His limitless resources; His generosity is not narrowed by human circumstances. The mention of His being All-Encompassing and All-Wise teaches that His provision reaches every need, and that His decree permitting separation is not arbitrary but rooted in perfect wisdom, knowing what is best for each soul and arranging outcomes beyond human calculation.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have certainly enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you, and you as well, to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is ever Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God's sovereignty over the heavens and earth is absolute: no one can add to or subtract from His kingdom. The shared obligation of all revealed religions is taqwa—living in reverent awareness of God, obeying His commands, and avoiding His prohibitions. Disbelief does not injure God or diminish His lordship, since all things remain His and He is eternally free of all need, praiseworthy in Himself and in all His decrees.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all creation, in the heavens and the earth, is Allah’s property and under His absolute authority; therefore He alone is the one to be relied upon, entrusted with all matters, and depended upon for protection, provision, and judgment, for His sufficiency is perfect and no other trustee can compare to Him.

translation: If He wills, He could take you away, O people, and bring others. And Allah is ever competent to do that.
interpretation: This verse declares God's absolute freedom and power: no individual, community, or generation is indispensable to His plan. If humanity turns away, He is not diminished; He can remove them and replace them with others who will serve Him. It is both a warning against self-reliance and a call to humility, since existence and role are granted by His will, and He has full ability to enact whatever He decrees.

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse corrects the mindset that limits one’s pursuit to worldly gain alone. It teaches that the reward of this life and the reward of the Hereafter both belong to Allah, so the believer should not fix his aspiration only on what is temporary, nor imagine that worldly success is outside Allah’s hand. Since Allah is Hearing and Seeing, He knows every request, motive, and hidden intention; therefore one should seek Him sincerely, aiming for His pleasure and the lasting reward, while trusting that He alone apportions both worldly and eternal good according to His wisdom and justice.

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow desire, lest you not be just. And if you distort [testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to make justice a steadfast commitment and to bear witness truthfully for God alone, not for personal, familial, or social advantage. It teaches that no relationship, whether to oneself, to parents, or to close relatives, and no consideration of wealth or poverty, may be allowed to bend one’s testimony or judgment. God has a greater right over both the rich and the poor, so fear of their displeasure, desire for their favor, or pity for their condition must not override truth. Following one’s whims, prejudices, loyalties, or interests corrupts justice. Whether one twists the facts, suppresses evidence, or turns away from giving testimony altogether, God is fully aware of every action and motive. The verse therefore grounds justice in God-consciousness, moral courage, and accountability before the All-Knowing.

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse directs those who already profess faith to renew and deepen it, not by mere verbal repetition but by wholehearted adherence to God, His Messenger, the Qur’an revealed to him, and the earlier revealed scriptures as they originally came. It teaches that faith is a unified whole: rejecting any of its essential objects—God, His angels, His revealed books, His messengers, or the Last Day—constitutes a radical deviation from the straight path, because these articles are interconnected and cannot be selectively accepted.

translation: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief — Allah will never forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: This describes those who persist in this cycle until disbelief becomes their settled end: their repeated betrayal of faith and growth in denial seal the heart against sincere repentance, so Allah does not forgive them or guide them to the straight path. That withholding is the just recompense for deliberate, persistent rejection, not a denial of mercy to anyone who truly turns back.

translation: Give tidings to the hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites with a sharp, ironic announcement: the word “tidings” is normally used for good news, but here it is used to mock and expose them, declaring that their hidden disbelief and deceit have earned them a painful punishment. It is a severe warning that hypocrisy is not a light matter before God, and that those who outwardly claim faith while inwardly reject it will meet an agonizing consequence.

translation: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers—do they seek honor with them? Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah.
interpretation: This verse censures those who seek strength, protection, or prestige by aligning themselves with those who reject faith rather than with the believers. It exposes the mistaken idea that worldly alliances can bestow true dignity, for honor belongs entirely to Allah, not to any created power. Therefore, whoever desires honor should seek it through obedience to Allah and loyalty to Him and the believers, not through allegiance to His enemies.

translation: And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a conversation other than that. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together.
interpretation: This verse establishes that faith demands guarding oneself from gatherings where Allah’s revelation is rejected or ridiculed. A believer is not to remain seated in such a setting, because remaining may signal consent, normalization, or participation in the mockery. The command is to withdraw until the discussion changes to something else. If a person willingly stays and accepts or is pleased with the ridicule, then that person shares in the same guilt and ruling as those who mock. The verse then warns that hypocrisy and open disbelief, though different in appearance, are alike in deserving punishment; Allah will gather both groups together in Hell. Thus it teaches separation from environments of kufr and mockery, protection of one’s faith, and seriousness about one’s allegiance to Allah.

translation: Those who wait and watch concerning you: if there comes to you a victory from Allah, they say, 'Were we not with you?' But if the disbelievers have a share [of victory], they say, 'Did we not gain the upper hand over you and protect you from the believers?' Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection. And never will Allah give the disbelievers a way over the believers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the opportunistic hypocrisy of those whose loyalty is tied only to worldly outcomes. They present themselves as allies of the believers when the believers appear to be winning, and as allies of the disbelievers when the disbelievers seem to have the advantage, trying to secure favor with both sides. Their claim of support is not sincere faith but calculated self-protection, and it cannot deceive God. The decisive judgment belongs to Allah alone on the Day of Resurrection, when hidden loyalties and intentions will be exposed. The closing promise is a firm assurance to the faithful: whatever temporary trials, setbacks, or apparent gains the disbelievers may have in this worldly life, Allah will not grant them a final, ultimate victory or a valid claim against the believers in His judgment.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but it is He who deceives them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little.
interpretation: The hypocrites imagine they can conceal their disbelief and manipulate God by outward conformity, but their scheming cannot touch Him; His “deceit” is His just recompense, leaving them entangled in their own self-deception and hypocrisy. Their prayer exposes their inner state: they rise to it with reluctance and heaviness because they have no sincere desire for God, and they perform it for human notice rather than divine pleasure. Their remembrance of God is slight because their hearts are attached to created approval, not to the Creator, so their worship is hollow and their faith is only a veneer.

translation: Wavering between that—neither to these nor to those. And whom Allah sends astray, never will you find for him a way.
interpretation: This describes the hypocrites as being unstable and indecisive in faith: they are not sincerely with the believers, nor openly committed to the disbelievers, but remain suspended between the two. Because they refuse steadfast truth and choose duplicity, Allah leaves them in misguidance as a just consequence, and no one can then guide them or find for them a path to rightness.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah against you a clear authority?
interpretation: This verse forbids the believers from taking those who reject faith as intimate allies, patrons, or protectors in preference to the believers, because such loyalty contradicts the loyalty owed to God and to the community of faith. The rhetorical question warns that by doing so they would hand God a manifest proof against themselves, meaning they would deserve His judgment and punishment for choosing the side of disbelief over faith.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and never will you find for them a helper.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who outwardly profess faith while concealing disbelief and betrayal are placed in the deepest and most severe level of Hell. Their punishment is especially severe because they combined rejection of Allah with deception, hypocrisy, and harm toward the believers, corrupting the community from within while claiming to belong to it. On the Day of Judgment, no intercessor, ally, or supporter will be able to rescue them from Allah’s punishment or lessen their torment.

translation: Except those who repent, reform, hold fast to Allah, and make their religion sincerely for Allah. Those will be with the believers. And Allah will give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse excludes from the warning those who turn back from hypocrisy and disbelief and mend their lives. They must repent sincerely, correct their outward and inward conduct, place their reliance and loyalty in Allah alone, and purify their worship so that it is exclusively for Him. When they do so, they are no longer counted among the hypocrites but are joined with the believers in this life and in the Hereafter, and Allah promises the believers an immense reward.

translation: What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question affirming that Allah has no need or desire to punish those who turn to Him with gratitude and faith. Punishment is not arbitrary; it is the natural consequence of ingratitude and denial. When a person responds to Allah’s blessings with shukr—acknowledging them, using them rightly, and thanking the Giver—and with iman—belief that shapes conduct—the reason for punishment falls away. Allah is al-Shakir, the Appreciative, who recognizes even the smallest good and rewards it abundantly, and He is al-Alim, the All-Knowing, who knows the sincerity, intentions, and true condition of every heart. Thus the verse invites the reader away from fear of arbitrary wrath and toward a life of thankfulness and faith, trusting that Allah’s dealing with His servants is rooted in wisdom, justice, and mercy.

translation: Allah does not love the public utterance of evil, except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God dislikes spreading foul, harmful, or slanderous speech openly. However, it makes an exception for a person who has suffered injustice: they may speak publicly about the wrong done to them in order to seek justice, defend their rights, or warn others, but only within the limits of truth and fairness. It is not permission for insults, lies, or vengeance. The closing names “All-Hearing, All-Knowing” assure that God hears the complaint of the wronged and knows the intention and facts of both sides.

translation: If you disclose a good deed, or conceal it, or pardon an evil, then indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Powerful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that goodness is accepted whether it is done openly or kept hidden, for Allah sees the intention and does not let any good go unrewarded. It also elevates forgiveness: when a person has the right to retaliate but pardons the wrong done to them, that act reflects a noble character and reliance on Allah. Since Allah is ever Pardoning and Powerful, He can forgive sins and is fully able to reward hidden good and to deal justly with all matters, so the believer should seek His pardon and leave vengeance to His wisdom and power.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and wish to separate between Allah and His messengers, and say, “We believe in some and disbelieve in others,” and wish to adopt a way in between —
interpretation: This verse condemns selective faith: one cannot truly believe in Allah while rejecting some of His messengers, because the messengers are His chosen conveyors of revelation. Claiming to accept part of the prophetic message and reject another part is not a valid middle path; it is itself a form of disbelief. God has made faith in Him inseparable from faith in all His messengers, so those who seek a compromise between belief and rejection are only choosing rejection under another name.

translation: Those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who accept some messengers and reject others are not partially believers but truly disbelievers, because faith in God cannot be separated from faith in all His messengers. The 'humiliating punishment' is the disgrace prepared for such rejection in the Hereafter.

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them — those, He will give them their rewards. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith in God requires accepting all of His messengers without separating one from another, since they all conveyed the same divine guidance. Partial belief—accepting some prophets while rejecting others—is not complete faith. Those who embrace God and the full line of His messengers are promised their full reward from Him. The verse concludes by emphasizing God’s forgiveness and mercy, indicating that He pardons the shortcomings of those who sincerely turn to Him and that His mercy encompasses those who hold fast to comprehensive faith.

translation: The People of the Book ask you to bring down upon them a Book from heaven. They asked Moses for something even greater than that, saying, 'Show us Allah openly,' so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf [for worship] after the clear proofs had come to them, but We pardoned that, and We gave Moses a manifest authority.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the demand for a physical, heavenly book is not a sincere search for truth but a continuation of the obstructive mentality of earlier communities. Their ancestors asked Moses for a more astonishing sign—to see God directly—and were destroyed by a thunderbolt because of their transgression. Even after clear proofs, they fell into calf worship, yet God forgave them and granted Moses unmistakable authority. The passage thus establishes that miracles cannot compel faith in a heart set on defiance; the real issue is submission to God and His messenger. It also displays God's forbearance and the gravity of rejecting clear revelation, while affirming Moses' prophetic standing and the continuity of divine guidance.

translation: And We raised above them the Mount, by their covenant, and We said to them, 'Enter the gate, prostrating,' and We said to them, 'Do not transgress the Sabbath,' and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse stresses the gravity of the covenant taken from the Children of Israel: it was reinforced by an awesome sign, the Mount raised above them, and by clear commands requiring humility, obedience, and observance of the Sabbath. Their covenant was not a casual agreement but a binding, solemn pledge before God. The passage thus warns that receiving divine signs and covenants increases responsibility, and that breaking such pledges—whether through arrogance, disobedience, or transgression—brings severe accountability.

translation: So for their breaking of their covenant, their disbelief in the signs of Allah, their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, 'Our hearts are covered.' Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief, so they do not believe except a few.
interpretation: This verse explains that those who broke their covenant did so through a chain of persistent sins: violating their pledge, rejecting Allah's signs, unjustly killing prophets, and claiming that their hearts are impervious to guidance. Their claim is not an excuse; it is the very condition Allah confirms as a consequence of their chosen disbelief. Because they knowingly persisted in unbelief, Allah stamped their hearts with disbelief, preventing the light of faith from entering. Thus they are not guided to belief except for a small number among them.

translation: And [We cursed them] for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a tremendous slander.
interpretation: This verse condemns the Israelites for two grave sins: their rejection of faith and their atrocious fabrication against Maryam. The 'great slander' refers to their accusation of unchastity against her, though she was innocent, chaste, and chosen by Allah. It was a monstrous lie because it attacked the honor of a righteous woman, denied the clear miracle of the virgin birth of 'Isa, and reflected a deeper disbelief in Allah's power and revelation. The verse thus exposes how kufr can lead to shameless falsehood and warns against the enormity of slandering chaste believers.

translation: And [for] their saying, 'Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah.' But they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; rather, it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ concerning him are surely in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the pursuit of conjecture. And they did not kill him for certain.
interpretation: This verse denies that Jesus, peace be upon him, was killed or crucified by his enemies. What they thought they saw and did was only a resemblance or illusion; the reality was otherwise, and God protected His messenger and raised him to Himself. Those who dispute about his fate are therefore not grounded in certain knowledge but are following doubt and conjecture. The claim that they killed him with certainty is false: they did not kill him with certainty. The verse affirms God’s power to safeguard His chosen messenger and cautions against relying on surmise in matters of divine decree.

translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is ever Almighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Jesus was not killed or crucified as his enemies claimed; rather, God raised him to Himself, rescuing and honoring him. It declares God's absolute power to protect whom He wills and His perfect wisdom in governing all affairs, so no human scheme can defeat His decree.

translation: And there is none among the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Jesus, peace be upon him, was neither killed nor crucified. It means that before Jesus’ own death—after Allah returns him to the earth near the end of time—the remaining Jews and Christians will be compelled to acknowledge the truth about him: that he is Allah’s servant and messenger, not God or the son of God. Yet such acknowledgment at that stage will not benefit those who had persisted in rejecting or distorting his message. On the Day of Resurrection, Jesus himself will testify concerning them: he delivered the truth, and their disbelief and alterations were their own doing, so the judgment against them will be just.

translation: So because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things that had been lawful for them, and because of their turning many away from the path of Allah.
interpretation: This verse explains that the prohibition of certain wholesome things for the Jews was not because those things were inherently evil, but as a consequence of their own wrongdoing and their persistent obstruction of people from Allah’s path. Their wrongdoing includes injustice, breaking covenants, exploiting others, and corrupting what was entrusted to them; their “turning away” means they not only strayed themselves but actively hindered many others from faith and obedience. Thus, the restriction was a punitive recompense and a sign that divine blessings may be withdrawn when a people persist in oppression and misguidance. It is a manifestation of God’s justice and a warning to others against following the same conduct.

translation: And [because of] their taking usury although they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming people’s wealth unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse exposes the gravity of two intertwined injustices: knowingly taking riba after it was prohibited, and unlawfully consuming the wealth of others. Such acts are not merely economic violations; they reflect a defiance of divine command and a disregard for justice and trust. The phrase “the disbelievers among them” shows that the punishment is specifically for those who persisted in denial and these unlawful practices, not for every member of that community. It teaches that religious identity offers no protection when a person knowingly transgresses Allah’s limits and exploits others’ wealth, and that Allah has prepared a painful recompense for such persistent rejection and wrongdoing.

translation: But those firmly grounded in knowledge among them, and the believers, believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you; and those who establish prayer, give zakah, and believe in Allah and the Last Day — those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: This verse praises those among the People of the Book who are deeply rooted in religious knowledge, together with the believers, because they accept the revelation sent to Prophet Muhammad and the revelations sent to earlier prophets. Their faith is not merely intellectual; it is expressed through establishing prayer, giving zakah, and believing in God and the Last Day. The verse teaches that true knowledge leads to humble acceptance of divine guidance, and that faith is validated by worship, generosity, and accountability before God. God’s promise of a great reward shows that He honors those who combine sound knowledge, sincere belief, and righteous action, regardless of their previous community.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon; and to David We gave the Zabur.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the revelation given to Muhammad is not an isolated or novel claim but belongs to the same continuous divine guidance granted to Noah, the prophets after him, and the Abrahamic and Israelite prophetic line. By naming these messengers together, it confirms that God is the sole source of revelation, that He chose and inspired prophets across generations, and that Muhammad’s mission stands in harmony with them. The special mention of David receiving the Zabur underscores that God grants scripture to whom He wills, while the broader list teaches that prophethood is a unified chain of guidance calling humanity to the same Lord, even if particular scriptures and laws differ.

translation: And [We sent] messengers whom We have related to you before, and messengers whom We have not related to you. And Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech.
interpretation: This means that God sent many prophets, only some of whom He named in the Qur’an, so divine guidance was not limited to the messengers mentioned; others were also sent to their peoples. It also affirms that God truly speaks and that Moses was uniquely honored by being addressed directly by God, without an intermediary.

translation: Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that mankind would have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And Allah is ever Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse explains that Allah sent prophets and messengers to convey both glad tidings to the obedient and warnings to the disobedient. Their coming removes any valid excuse people might otherwise raise on the Day of Judgment, such as claiming they did not know or were not warned. Once the divine message has been delivered through messengers, accountability is established, and no one can justly argue against Allah that He left them without guidance. Allah’s sending of messengers is itself an act of wisdom and justice, and His being Almighty means no one can frustrate His purpose or escape His judgment, while His being All-Wise means His commands, warnings, and reckoning are perfectly ordered and fair.

translation: But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you: He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: Allah Himself testifies that the revelation sent to Muhammad is true and originates from Him. It was sent down with His knowledge, meaning it is free of falsehood, error, and ignorance, and contains true guidance and wisdom. The angels also testify to its truth, yet Allah’s testimony alone is fully sufficient. Therefore, despite the deniers’ rejection, the Prophet’s message is established by the greatest and most conclusive witness.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and turn [people] away from the way of Allah have certainly strayed far away.
interpretation: This verse states that those who reject faith and also block others from the path of Allah fall into a profound and distant misguidance: their disbelief corrupts themselves, and their prevention of others from guidance spreads corruption, so their deviation becomes compounded and far removed from truth, rectitude, and the way that leads to Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and commit wrongdoing—Allah will never forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who combine denial of faith with injustice and persist in it without repentance place themselves outside the reach of God's forgiveness and guidance. It does not mean that God is unable to forgive, but that His justice and wisdom require that those who deliberately reject the truth and wrong others are not granted the path of salvation. Their own refusal and oppression bar them from the way that leads to Him, so they remain subject to the consequences of their deeds.

translation: except the path of Hell, wherein they will abide forever. And that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing are left with no path except the path leading to Hell, where they will remain eternally. It emphasizes that their punishment and endless confinement are not difficult for God; His decree is effortless, and His power to carry it out is absolute. It also indicates that because they have rejected guidance and chosen injustice, divine guidance is withdrawn from them, leaving only the way of perdition as their final outcome.

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses all humanity, declaring that the Prophet Muhammad has brought the truth from God, not a message of human invention. Faith is commanded because it is genuinely beneficial to the believer, not because God needs anyone’s belief. Disbelief cannot diminish God in any way, for He alone owns and sustains everything in the heavens and the earth; He is utterly self-sufficient. His perfect knowledge encompasses all that people conceal and reveal, and His wisdom governs both His command to believe and His warning against disbelief. Thus the verse calls every person to respond to divine truth with sincere faith, recognizing that obedience is for their own good and that God is free of all need.

translation: O People of the Book, do not exceed the limits in your religion, and do not say about God anything but the truth. The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only a messenger of God, and His word which He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him. So believe in God and His messengers. And do not say, 'Three.' Desist — it is better for you. Indeed, God is only one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is God as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, especially Christians, warning against exaggeration in religion and speaking falsely about God. It defines Jesus as the Messiah, a human messenger born of Mary, created by God's command—described as His word conveyed to Mary—and granted a spirit from Him. These descriptions affirm Jesus's prophethood and God's creative power, not his divinity or equality with God. The command to believe in God and His messengers calls for pure monotheistic faith that honors all prophets without deifying any. The prohibition 'do not say three' rejects the Trinity and any plurality within God. God is one, utterly transcendent, far above having a son or partner. He owns all that is in the heavens and earth and is all-sufficient as guardian and disposer, needing no offspring or intermediary. Thus the verse corrects doctrinal excess and returns to tawhid: God alone is divine, and Jesus is His honored servant and messenger.

translation: The Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels brought near. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant — He will gather them all to Himself.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true honor before Allah is not compromised by servitude to Him; rather, servitude is the highest station of created beings. The Messiah, Jesus, and the angels nearest to Allah are presented as worshipping servants who never consider obedience to Allah beneath them. Therefore, any claim that Jesus or the angels share in divinity, or that worshipping Allah alone is somehow degrading, is false. Arrogance toward Allah's worship is a grave spiritual disease: those who reject or belittle it will not escape Him, for He will gather all of them together for judgment and recompense. Thus the verse calls every creature to humble submission to Allah alone and warns that pride cannot avert the final gathering before Him.

translation: So as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. And as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse contrasts two responses to divine servitude. The believers who combine faith with righteous action receive their due reward completely, and God adds to it out of His grace, showing that reward is not merely earned but also granted by divine generosity. In contrast, those who feel too proud to worship and obey God, whether out of disdain for servitude or self-exaltation, face a painful punishment. Their arrogance cannot save them; they will have no guardian to protect them and no helper to aid them against God's decree. The verse affirms that all protection and support belong to God alone, and that pride before Him is the path to ruin.

translation: O mankind, there has come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: This verse addresses all humanity, announcing that God has provided an undeniable evidence and an illuminating guidance. The "conclusive proof" is the messenger and the revelation that establishes the truth of God's message, while the "clear light" is the Qur'an, which exposes falsehood, dispels doubt, and guides people to the straight path. It calls every person to recognize this divine evidence and follow the light sent for their guidance.

translation: As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy and grace from Him and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse establishes that deliverance rests on faith in Allah joined with clinging to Him alone—trusting Him, relying upon Him, obeying Him, and seeking refuge in His guidance. Such people are promised entrance into His mercy and favor, not by their own strength, and a guidance granted directly from Him that leads straight to His pleasure, without deviation or crookedness. Holding fast to Allah is therefore both the way and the means: whoever adheres to Him sincerely is drawn nearer to Him and kept firm upon the path of truth.

translation: They ask you for a ruling. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalalah: if a man dies without a child and has a sister, she receives half of what he leaves; and he inherits from her if she has no child. If there are two sisters, they receive two-thirds of what he leaves. And if there are brothers and sisters, the male receives the like of the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you lest you go astray; and Allah is Knowing of all things.'
interpretation: This verse provides the divine ruling for the inheritance case known as kalalah, which refers to a person who dies leaving neither descendants nor parents. It specifies the shares of siblings when they are the heirs: a single sister receives one half of the estate, two sisters together receive two-thirds, and if both brothers and sisters inherit, the estate is distributed according to the rule that a male receives twice the share of a female. The verse presents these details as Allah's own clarification to protect people from error in dividing inheritance, and it concludes by affirming that His knowledge encompasses all things, so His laws are perfectly wise and just.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O you who have believed, fulfill all contracts. Lawful for you are the grazing livestock, except what is recited to you, without making hunting lawful while you are in a state of consecration. Indeed, Allah decrees what He intends.
interpretation: This verse establishes covenant fidelity as a core religious obligation: believers must honor all pledges, including their covenant with Allah, oaths, treaties, financial agreements, and social responsibilities. It then clarifies that the grazing livestock are made lawful as food, except those specific categories later prohibited in revelation, and it forbids hunting while one is in ihram during Hajj or Umrah. The closing statement affirms that Allah alone has absolute legislative authority and disposes of all matters according to His wisdom and will, so His commands are to be accepted with submission and trust.

translation: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the sacrificial animals, nor the garlands, nor those heading to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and pleasure. And when you have exited ihram, you may hunt. And do not let hatred of a people—because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque—cause you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and God-consciousness, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the sacred rites, months, offerings, and the safety of pilgrims are inviolable, and that ritual restrictions are to be observed until released. Its central moral demand is that anger or past injustice must not justify transgression: justice and restraint remain obligatory even toward those who were hostile. It also defines the believer's social ethic: mutual assistance is permitted only for good and taqwa and forbidden for sin and aggression, with the warning that violating these limits exposes one to Allah's severe punishment.

translation: Forbidden to you are the dead animal, blood, swine flesh, and that over which any name other than Allah has been invoked; and the strangled, the struck, the fallen, the gored, and that which a wild beast has eaten, except what you have slaughtered properly; and what has been sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek division by divining arrows. That is wickedness. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion. But whoever is compelled by hunger, without deviating toward sin, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the right to declare foods lawful or unlawful belongs to Allah alone, and the prohibitions it lists are tied either to harm, to the sanctity of life and blood, or to the corruption of worship through association with other than Allah. The animals that die by strangling, beating, falling, goring, or being partly eaten by predators are forbidden unless they are reached alive and slaughtered in the divinely prescribed way, which shows that intentional, pure slaughter in Allah’s name is the criterion. Sacrificing on stone altars and seeking decisions through divining arrows are condemned as fasiq, meaning a departure from faith and obedience, because they belong to pre-Islamic superstition and idolatrous practice. The announcement that the disbelievers have despaired marks the decisive triumph and preservation of the Muslim community’s religion, so fear is redirected from human opposition to Allah alone. The completion of religion and perfection of favor mean that the essential guidance, law, and blessing of Islam have been finalized and accepted by Allah, so no later system may claim to supersede it. Finally, the concession for one driven by severe hunger, without intending sin, reveals that the Law aims at purification and mercy, not at destroying the desperate; necessity removes the prohibition, while deliberate transgression remains blameworthy. This interpretation emphasizes tawhid, ritual purity, the finality and sufficiency of Islam, and divine mercy within accountability.

translation: They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say, 'Lawful for you are the good things, and what you have trained of hunting animals, training them as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah upon it. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that the basic criterion for lawful food is that it be good and pure, not a set of arbitrary prohibitions. It then specifically permits the catch of trained hunting animals—such as dogs or birds of prey—because their training is a skill God has enabled humans to acquire. However, the permission is conditional: the animal must be trained for hunting, it must catch for its owner, and God's name must be mentioned over it. The verse concludes by commanding God-consciousness and reminding that God's reckoning is swift, meaning that people must be careful to observe these limits sincerely and not misuse what has been made lawful.

translation: Today the good and pure things have been made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful to you, and your food is lawful to them. And lawful to you in marriage are chaste believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you give them their due dowers, taking them in marriage, not committing illicit sexual relations, nor taking them as secret lovers. And whoever rejects faith, his deed has become void, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine permission and a moral boundary. It declares that pure and wholesome things are lawful, and it regulates two sensitive areas of communal life: food and marriage. Food prepared by the People of the Book is permitted to Muslims, and Muslim food is permitted to them, acknowledging a shared legal and social space despite theological differences. Marriage to chaste women from among the believers and from the People of the Book is also permitted for Muslim men, but only through a proper marriage contract with dower paid and with the intention of chastity, not fornication, casual sexual relations, or secret love affairs. The closing warning teaches that these permissions must not be treated as a rejection of faith; whoever denies the faith or rejects its rulings nullifies the value of his deeds and will be among the losers in the Hereafter.

translation: O you who have believed, when you rise for prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe over your heads and your feet up to the ankles. And if you are in a state of ritual impurity, then purify yourselves. And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the toilet, or you have touched women, and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make any hardship for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse grounds ritual purity in the believer's standing before God. The washing and wiping it commands are not mere bodily acts; they signify the consecration of the whole person—face, limbs, head, and feet—to worship. The provision for full purification after janabah and for tayammum when water is unavailable or harmful shows that divine legislation is oriented toward mercy and accessibility, not burden. Tayammum is therefore not a lesser escape from purity but a real dispensation by which the servant remains connected to prayer. The verse's conclusion names the divine purpose: purification and the completion of favor, so that gratitude becomes the believer's response to a law designed to cleanse rather than constrain.

translation: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you, when you said, 'We hear and we obey.' And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse calls the believers to recall two things: Allah's blessings, especially the blessing of faith and guidance, and the solemn covenant they made with Him—expressed in the words 'We hear and we obey.' That pledge means accepting Allah's commands and the Prophet's teachings with willing submission, not mere verbal profession. The command 'And fear Allah' reinforces that obedience must be accompanied by God-consciousness and sincerity. The closing statement, 'Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts,' warns that Allah is aware of hidden intentions, thoughts, and motives, so outward compliance alone is insufficient; the heart must be sincere. Thus, the verse teaches gratitude, fidelity to covenants, and inward piety.

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes justice as an essential act of faith and worship, not merely a social or legal preference. Believers are commanded to stand firmly for Allah, bearing witness truthfully and equitably, and to refuse allowing hostility, resentment, or hatred toward any people to push them away from fairness. Justice must be impartial and unconditional: it is owed even to those one dislikes, and it is not suspended because of others’ wrongdoing. Acting justly is closer to taqwa, meaning God-consciousness, moral restraint, and protection from sin. The verse therefore roots justice in reverence for Allah and in the awareness that He is fully aware of all actions, intentions, and hidden motives, so no injustice can escape His knowledge or accountability.

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God’s promise is assured for those who combine sincere faith with righteous action: He will forgive their sins and grant them an abundant, excellent reward in the Hereafter.

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses — those are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who reject faith and knowingly deny God's revealed signs and revelations are the rightful inhabitants of the blazing Fire, where they will remain, because their disbelief and denial cut them off from the path of guidance and divine mercy.

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people intended to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah, and upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the believers’ safety from hostile plots is a direct favor and protection from God. Human beings may intend harm, but God’s power can restrain them, so the believer must respond with taqwa—remaining conscious of God, obeying Him, and avoiding what displeases Him—and with tawakkul, placing complete trust in God alone. It shows that relying on God is not a passive act but a firm confidence in His sufficiency, especially when facing enmity, danger, or fear. True faith therefore combines gratitude for God’s protection, dutiful awareness of Him, and sincere dependence on Him rather than on human strength or schemes.

translation: And indeed Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We appointed from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and lend Allah a goodly loan, I will surely expiate your evil deeds from you and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the right way.
interpretation: This verse presents the covenant with the Children of Israel as a binding divine commission: God appointed twelve leaders to represent and guide their tribes, and His promised support is tied to faithful observance. Establishing prayer, giving zakah, believing in and honoring God's messengers, and spending in His cause as a beautiful loan are all expressions of a living covenant, not mere outward rituals. The reward is forgiveness and entry into gardens with flowing rivers, while rejection after such a clear covenant is described as straying from the straight, balanced path. Thus the verse teaches that divine guidance entails communal responsibility, loyal support for God's messengers, and sincere sacrifice, and that turning away after knowing the covenant is a grave deviation from the path God set.

translation: So because of their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their proper places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of. And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them. So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse explains that covenant-breaking against God produces a spiritual consequence: removal of divine mercy and a hardening of the heart that then enables distortion of revealed words and forgetfulness of sacred reminders. The treachery will continue among them, except for a faithful remnant, so the Prophet is instructed not to answer betrayal with betrayal. Pardoning and overlooking here is an exercise of prophetic magnanimity where retaliation is possible but not obligatory; it leaves ultimate judgment to God. The closing phrase identifies the standard: God’s love is for those who practice ihsan—goodness that remains kind, restrained, and beneficent even when wronged.

translation: And from those who said, “We are Christians,” We took their covenant; but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse states that Allah also took a binding covenant from those who identify as Christians, just as He took covenants from others, obligating them to uphold what was revealed to them and to follow the reminders sent through His prophets. When they neglected and abandoned a share of what they had been commanded to remember—including true faith, obedience, and the signs pointing to the final Messenger—Allah caused mutual hostility and hatred to fall among them as a consequence of their breach. This enmity is not merely a passing social quarrel but a divinely imposed condition that persists among their factions until the Day of Resurrection. On that Day, Allah will fully inform them of everything they did, and He will judge them with perfect justice.

translation: O People of the Book, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Jews and Christians, declaring that God has sent Muhammad as His Messenger to clarify much of what they had hidden, altered, or misinterpreted in their revealed scriptures, while pardoning and not exposing much else. It then announces that from God has come a guiding light—the Prophet and the message he brought—and a clear Book, the Qur’an, which removes confusion and makes the truth distinct.

translation: By it Allah guides those who follow His pleasure to the paths of peace, and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: This means that Allah grants His guidance through the revealed light and Book to those who sincerely seek His good pleasure, leading them to the ways of safety and peace in belief and conduct, delivering them from the darkness of disbelief and misguidance into the light of faith and truth by His will, and directing them to the upright path that leads to Him.

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary.' Say, 'Then who could do anything against Allah if He willed to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth?' And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse decisively refutes the claim that Jesus is God. It argues from Jesus' creaturely contingency: if Jesus were God, he could not be subject to God's will to destroy him, nor could his mother and all people share in that vulnerability. The fact that God can will the destruction of Jesus, Mary, and all creation shows that they are all under His decree and power. God alone owns and rules the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them; He creates as He wills. Therefore Jesus is among the created and governed, not the Creator. True divinity belongs exclusively to Allah, whose sovereignty and omnipotence are absolute. The claim that God is the Messiah is disbelief because it ascribes to a created servant what belongs only to the Creator.

translation: And the Jews and the Christians say, 'We are the sons of Allah and His beloved.' Say, 'Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings from among those He created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the final destination.'
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim that any religious community has an inherent, guaranteed status as God's children or beloved. Such a claim is not accepted as literal lineage or unconditional privilege, for it is tested by the reality of divine punishment for sin: if their closeness to God were absolute, punishment would be meaningless. They are instead placed among all created human beings, subject to God's moral order and accountable to Him. Forgiveness and punishment belong to God's sovereign will and perfect justice, not to ethnic, communal, or hereditary entitlement. Since all dominion belongs to Him and the final return is to Him, salvation is not a birthright but rests on faith, repentance, and submission to His will. Thus every claimant is called to humility, sincere obedience, and hope in God's mercy rather than reliance on identity.

translation: O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you after an interval between the messengers, lest you say, “There came to us no bringer of good tidings nor a warner.” Now there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book—the Jews and Christians—and informs them that God has sent His Messenger Muhammad to clarify the truth after a long period in which no prophet had come. The purpose is to remove any excuse they might make, such as claiming that no one came to give them glad tidings of reward or to warn them of punishment. By sending Muhammad as both a bearer of glad tidings and a warner, God has established the proof against them and completed His guidance. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah has full power over all things, including the sending of messengers and the resurrection and final accountability. Therefore, they are called to accept the Messenger and follow the message he brought.

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his people: 'O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you kings and gave you what He had not given to anyone among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah’s favors toward the Children of Israel were both spiritual and worldly: He raised prophets from among them to guide them, granted them authority and dominion after generations of bondage, and bestowed upon them unique blessings and signs not granted to others of their era. Remembering these favors is meant to awaken gratitude, obedience, and readiness to fulfill Allah’s commands, not to foster pride or a sense of exclusive entitlement. It shows that divine favor carries responsibility, and that past blessings become a proof against those who later reject Allah’s guidance and messengers.

translation: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has decreed for you, and do not turn back on your heels, lest you return as losers.
interpretation: This verse records Moses addressing the Children of Israel, commanding them to obey God’s decree to enter the sanctified land and warning that retreating from that command is not merely a military withdrawal but a spiritual reversal. The land was “written” for them in the sense that God had promised and ordained it, so entering it became a test of trust and obedience. “Do not turn back on your heels” forbids cowardice, disobedience, and apostasy—including fear of the inhabitants or reluctance to leave familiar ways. The resulting “loss” is comprehensive: forfeiting God’s promise, blessing, and success in this life and the Hereafter. Thus the verse teaches that divine promises call for courageous obedience, and that turning away from God’s command turns opportunity into ruin.

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed there are in it a people of tyrannical strength, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. But if they leave it, then indeed we will enter."
interpretation: This verse exposes the Israelites’ refusal to obey Moses out of fear of the inhabitants described as jabbārīn—powerful, oppressive, or giant-like. Their vow not to enter unless the inhabitants first depart shows that they made obedience conditional on their own safety and on the removal of the obstacle by others, rather than trusting in God’s command and aid. It is a warning against allowing fear of worldly power to paralyze faith, and against substituting excuses and conditions for sincere reliance upon God.
