translation: Jesus, son of Mary, said: O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from heaven that may be a feast for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, for You are the best of providers.
interpretation: This supplication expresses Jesus' perfect servitude: he turns to God alone for a miraculous table, not to satisfy idle desire but to establish a lasting festival and a clear sign of God's power and His approval of Jesus' mission. It teaches that true blessings are sought from God, that divine signs should deepen faith and communal gratitude, and that all provision—material and spiritual—rests in God's hand, the best of providers.

translation: Allah said, "I will surely send it down upon you. So whoever disbelieves after that among you — indeed, I will punish him with a punishment with which I will not punish anyone among the worlds."
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah answers the disciples’ request as a clear sign, but the sending down of the table is not merely a provision; it is a binding proof and a test. After such manifest divine evidence, willful rejection is no longer simple ignorance but deliberate denial of Allah’s power and mercy. The severity of the threatened punishment corresponds to the severity of the offense: disbelief after direct, unmistakable revelation and after being included in a special favor. It teaches that greater divine gifts and clearer proofs bring greater accountability, and that mercy, when met with rejection, can become the basis of a unique and exemplary punishment.

translation: And [mention] when Allah will say, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"' He will say, 'Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene on the Day of Judgment in which Allah questions Jesus about the false divinization of himself and his mother. Jesus' answer is a complete disavowal: he glorifies Allah, denies ever claiming divinity or Lordship for himself or Mary, and affirms that he only speaks what is true and rightful. His statement that Allah would have known if he had said it establishes Allah's perfect knowledge and Jesus' truthfulness. By saying that Allah knows what is within him while he does not know what is within Allah, Jesus acknowledges the absolute distinction between the Creator and the creature: Allah alone knows the innermost secrets and the unseen. The verse thus refutes all worship of Jesus or Mary as divine, presents Jesus as a pure servant and prophet of Allah, and confirms that divine knowledge and Lordship belong to Allah alone.

translation: I did not say to them anything except what You commanded me: “Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.” And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things.
interpretation: This is Jesus’s testimony before God, declaring that his teaching was nothing but pure monotheism: the command to worship Allah alone as his Lord and their Lord. It affirms his own servanthood and God’s exclusive lordship, denying any claim that he taught or authorized worship of himself. His role as witness and guardian over his people was limited to the time he remained among them; after God took him, God alone became the Watcher over them, fully aware of what they said and did, including any later distortion or alteration of his message. The verse establishes that ultimate knowledge, oversight, and judgment belong to God alone, and that every affair is under His witnessing and authority.

translation: If You punish them, they are indeed Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse is Jesus's address to God on the Day of Judgment, and it expresses absolute submission to God's sovereignty. All people, whether obedient or disobedient, are God's servants and remain under His authority. Jesus does not claim the right to judge or to intercede independently; he refers the entire matter to God alone. By mentioning that God is the Almighty and the All-Wise, the verse shows that any punishment God gives is never unjust or beyond His power, and any forgiveness He grants is never a sign of weakness or ignorance. God's mercy and justice are both perfect and proceed from His might and wisdom. Thus forgiveness belongs to God alone, and no one can compel Him either to forgive or to punish; He decides with perfect knowledge and authority.

translation: Allah will say, 'This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. That is the great attainment.'
interpretation: This verse declares that on the Day of Judgment, when all hidden realities are exposed, the only profit that will matter is truthfulness—sincerity in faith, honesty in speech, and fidelity in deeds. Those who were true to Allah and to their covenant will find their truthfulness itself becoming the means of their salvation and honor. Their reward is eternal gardens with flowing rivers, symbolizing unending delight, purity, and life. The greatest bliss, however, is not merely the gardens but the mutual pleasure between Allah and His truthful servants: Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, a state of perfect contentment, love, and closeness. This is the supreme success, beyond which no success exists.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse affirms that absolute sovereignty, ownership, and authority belong exclusively to Allah over the heavens, the earth, and everything within them. Because His power is unrestricted and complete, nothing in creation can escape His will, control, or judgment. He alone governs all affairs, sustains all existence, and has full capability over every matter, including resurrection, reckoning, reward, and punishment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve equate others with their Lord.
interpretation: This praise affirms that all true praise and worship belong solely to Allah, because He alone originated the heavens and the earth and brought into being the contrasting realities of darkness and light. The plural darknesses and singular light point to the many paths of falsehood, confusion, and misguidance, while truth and guidance ultimately return to one source. The verse then expresses astonishment and censure: after such manifest signs of His sole creative power, those who reject faith still set up equals with their Lord, attributing to creatures what belongs only to the Creator. Its core meaning is the condemnation of shirk—associating partners with Allah—as a contradiction of the very order He created.

translation: He is the One who created you from clay, then decreed a term; and a term named with Him; then you doubt.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God alone originates human life and determines its ultimate destiny. Creating humankind from clay points to humanity’s humble origin and complete dependence on Him, while the first appointed term refers to each person’s lifespan and death, and the second, “a term named with Him,” refers to the fixed, final time of resurrection and judgment known only to God. The closing rebuke means that despite these clear signs of God’s creative power and sovereign decree, people still dispute and doubt.

translation: And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth; He knows your secret and your open [deeds], and He knows what you earn.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the true deity and sovereign in the heavens and the earth, and that His knowledge encompasses both the hidden and the manifest. Nothing people conceal or reveal, and nothing they do or earn, is absent from His knowledge; therefore, they are fully accountable to Him for their deeds.

translation: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse condemns the disbelievers’ entrenched habit of rejecting every divine proof. It clarifies that the fault is not in the absence of signs—whether Qur’anic verses, prophetic miracles, or signs in creation—but in their own willful aversion. Because the signs come from “their Lord,” the One who creates, nurtures, and sustains them, their rejection is especially ungrateful and arrogant. The phrasing “they were” together with “turning away” indicates that this is not a one-time lapse but a persistent condition: whenever truth reaches them, they habitually avert themselves from accepting or heeding it, thus veiling themselves from guidance by their own choice.

translation: So they have indeed denied the truth when it came to them; but soon there will come to them the news of what they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse declares that the disbelievers rejected the revelation and the Messenger when the truth reached them, persisting in denial and mockery. Its meaning is that the very matters they ridiculed—warnings of punishment, resurrection, accountability, and the truth of the message—will eventually be disclosed to them, and they will taste the reality and consequence of what they mocked when the foretold judgment comes upon them.

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them whom We had established in the land with power such as We have not established for you, and We sent the sky upon them with abundant rain and made rivers flow beneath them, yet We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them another generation.
interpretation: This verse confronts the heedless with a lesson from history: worldly power, prosperity, rain, and rivers are not proofs of divine favor or immunity from judgment; they are trusts and tests. The earlier nations were given greater material strength than the Makkan contemporaries, but when they persisted in sin and ingratitude, God destroyed them and raised another people in their place. Thus it warns that God’s laws of rise and fall are impartial, and no community should feel secure in its blessings while persisting in disobedience.

translation: And even if We had sent down to you a written Scripture on parchment, and they had touched it with their own hands, those who disbelieve would still say, 'This is nothing but clear magic.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the nature of obstinate disbelief: it is not caused by a lack of evidence or by the absence of a tangible miracle. Even if revelation were delivered as a physical book that the disbelievers could touch with their own hands—leaving no room for doubt about its material reality—they would still reject it and dismiss it as sorcery. Their demand for signs is therefore often a pretext, not a sincere search for truth. The verse teaches that outward proofs do not compel inward faith; hearts that are determined to reject will reinterpret even the most direct evidence. Guidance ultimately depends on Allah and on a person's willingness to submit, not merely on sensory confirmation.

translation: And they say, 'Why has not an angel been sent down to him?' But if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be given respite.
interpretation: This verse exposes the insincerity of the demand for an angel to be sent as a sign. If God were to send an angel in the manner they demand, their case would be sealed at once: the angel’s visible coming would bring the decisive judgment, and they would have no time left to repent or believe. Thus their request is not a sincere search for guidance but a pretext for rejection; God’s wisdom delays punishment and sends human messengers so that people may reflect and return to Him before the appointed term.

translation: And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered over for them what they are covering over.
interpretation: This verse addresses the demand of the disbelievers that a messenger be an angel rather than a human being. Allah says that even if He sent an angel as a messenger, the angel would have to appear in human form for people to be able to see, hear, and receive guidance from him; otherwise they could not bear his angelic nature. But then the same objections and doubts would remain, because the obstacle is not the messenger’s form but the people’s own resistance and self-deception. Thus, their demand is not a sincere route to faith; it is a pretext. The phrase “We would have covered over for them what they are covering over” means that their confusion and obscuring of the truth would only be increased or left upon them, since they themselves are covering and mixing the truth with falsehood. The verse establishes that divine guidance comes through human messengers by wisdom, and that no sign will benefit those who are determined to reject and distort the truth.

translation: And already were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet Muhammad and the believers by reminding them that mocking divine messengers is not new; previous prophets were also ridiculed. Yet the mockers did not escape: the very punishment and warning they laughed at eventually overwhelmed them. It establishes that derision of God’s message never defeats the truth, and those who persist in mocking it will be confronted by the reality they denied.

translation: Say, 'Travel throughout the earth, then observe how was the end of those who denied.'
interpretation: This verse commands people to journey through the earth and reflect upon the ruins and histories of past nations who rejected their messengers. Their denial did not save them; rather, it brought about their destruction and a painful end. The verse thus warns the deniers of the Prophet Muhammad that if they persist in rejection, they may face a similar fate, and it invites them to learn from the lessons of history before it is too late.

translation: Say, 'To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'To Allah.' He has prescribed mercy upon Himself. He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who have lost their souls—they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all dominion, ownership, and authority over existence belong exclusively to God, so any devotion, fear, or hope directed to other than Him is founded on an illusion. God's prescribing mercy upon Himself means that mercy is not an incidental attitude but the governing principle of His relation to creation; it is His own binding promise, not a debt owed to anyone. The certainty of being gathered to the Day of Resurrection means that human life is not self-enclosed: every soul will be returned to its Lord, and denial of that meeting is a rejection of reality itself. The deepest loss is therefore not external but inward: disbelief ruins the self by cutting it off from the mercy and purpose for which it was made, so those who persist in unbelief are already the losers even before the final accounting.

translation: And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This affirms that every creature that exists, rests, moves, or remains throughout the night and day is created, owned, and sustained by God alone, under His absolute dominion. Nothing in existence is outside His authority, and no sound or hidden state escapes Him: He hears all things and knows all things, wholly aware of every creature and every deed at every moment.

translation: Say, 'Shall I take other than Allah as a guardian, while He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth, and He feeds and is not fed?' Say, 'Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit, and do not be among the polytheists.'
interpretation: The verse establishes that guardianship, protection, and ultimate loyal dependence belong exclusively to Allah. He alone originates and sustains the heavens and earth; He provides food and needs no food, so He is absolutely self-sufficient while all creation depends on Him. Therefore, taking any creature as a guardian in the place of Allah is false and irrational. The Prophet is commanded to declare that he has been ordered to be first in submission to Allah alone—foremost in sincere surrender and in abandoning every form of shirk—and to refuse any association of partners with Him. This is pure tawhid: exclusive devotion, reliance, and obedience to the Creator, with no share of divinity, worship, or ultimate allegiance given to any created being.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day.'
interpretation: This command directs the Prophet—and every believer—to openly acknowledge that disobedience to God carries the dread of a tremendous punishment on the Day of Resurrection. It teaches that no rank or nearness to God grants exemption from accountability; rather, the more one knows God, the more one fears falling short. The 'great Day' is the Day of Judgment, whose terror and suffering are immense. Therefore, the verse instills taqwa (God-consciousness), urges steadfast obedience, and reminds the servant that true safety lies only in submission to the Lord and seeking His mercy.

translation: Whoever is averted from it on that Day—He has surely shown him mercy. And that is the manifest success.
interpretation: This means that the true and decisive mercy is God's shielding a person from the punishment of the Hereafter; such protection is the clearest and most manifest success, because it saves one from ruin and brings one to divine pleasure.

translation: And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all harm and benefit are entirely under Allah’s decree and power. No created being can remove an affliction He has sent, nor can anyone prevent or withhold a good He has granted. Thus, hearts should turn to Him alone in fear and hope, seeking relief from harm and gratitude for good, while affirming that His power encompasses and governs all things.

translation: And He is the Subjugator over His servants, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah alone possesses absolute, irresistible authority over all His creation: nothing and no one can escape His power, decree, or control. His being "above His servants" signifies both His exalted transcendence and His complete mastery over them, so all creatures are utterly dependent upon Him and subject to His will. At the same time, His attributes of wisdom and all-awareness mean that His dominion is never arbitrary or unjust; He governs with perfect wisdom and knows completely the outward and inward realities of His servants. This calls the believer to humble submission, sincere reliance upon Allah, and reverent awareness that Allah sees and knows all that they do.

translation: Say, 'Which thing is greatest in testimony?' Say, 'Allah is Witness between me and you. And this Qur’an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it, and whoever it reaches. Do you indeed testify that there are other gods with Allah?' Say, 'I do not testify.' Say, 'He is only One God, and indeed I am free of what you associate with Him.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that the greatest testimony is God's own testimony. When the idolaters demanded a sign or witness for Muhammad’s prophethood, God commanded him to point to Allah as the supreme Witness between him and them. Allah bears witness to His own oneness and to the truth of the revelation sent to His Messenger. The Qur’an is not merely for the immediate audience; it is a warning to everyone it reaches, making the Prophet’s message universal. The verse then rejects polytheism: the Prophet refuses to testify to their claim of other deities alongside Allah, affirms that there is only One God, and declares himself free from all that they associate with Him.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize him as they recognize their own sons. Those who have lost their souls—they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse states that the People of the Book, who were given earlier divine scriptures, know the truth of Prophet Muhammad just as clearly as they know their own children, because their books contain descriptions and signs pointing to him. Yet those who deny this clear knowledge have ruined themselves by choosing disbelief, and so they will not attain faith.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse declares that the gravest form of wrongdoing is knowingly attributing falsehood to God—such as falsely claiming something is His command, revelation, or law—or rejecting the clear signs He has sent. It establishes that those who persist in such injustice cannot attain true success, deliverance, or flourishing, either in this world or in the Hereafter.

translation: And on the Day We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, 'Where are your partners whom you used to claim?'
interpretation: This verse confronts the polytheists on the Day of Judgment with the utter falsehood of their beliefs: the partners they invented and claimed shared in Allah's divinity will be nowhere to be found, unable to help, intercede, or vindicate them. The rhetorical question is not seeking information but exposing their delusion, establishing their guilt, and showing that all false objects of worship vanish when Allah's sole authority is made manifest.

translation: Then their only excuse will be to say, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not those who associated others with Him.'
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, when the polytheists are questioned about the partners they claimed besides Allah, they will have no valid proof or defense. Their only response will be a false oath, swearing by Allah that they never committed shirk. This exposes their desperation and self-deception: they acknowledged Allah as their Lord, yet denied His exclusive right to be worshipped and associated others with Him. Their lying denial will not benefit them, for Allah knows all things and their own deeds, limbs, and the angels will testify against them. The verse warns that shirk is a grave injustice and that on that Day no excuse or false oath can conceal the truth or escape Allah's judgment.

translation: Look how they lied against themselves, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the idolaters will deny their former shirk, but this denial is itself a lie against their own souls; their self-deception will be exposed, and the false gods and intercessors they fabricated will abandon them, leaving them in loss.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed coverings over their hearts lest they understand it, and deafness in their ears. And even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. Until, when they come to you, arguing with you, those who disbelieve say, “This is nothing but legends of the former peoples.”
interpretation: This verse depicts the spiritual condition of those who reject the truth despite outwardly hearing it. Their listening is not receptive, because their hearts have been veiled from understanding the Qur’an and their ears made heavy to its guidance — a consequence of their persistent arrogance and deliberate denial. Therefore, even the most compelling signs will not bring them to faith, since they are not seeking truth. When they approach the Prophet, it is only to dispute and mock, dismissing the revelation as ancient fables. The verse warns that continual rejection can blind the heart and deafen the ear to divine guidance, and that quarreling against the Qur’an does not refute it but reveals the diseased state of the one who argues.

translation: And they forbid [others] from him and keep away from him; and they destroy none but themselves, but they do not perceive.
interpretation: The verse exposes a double hypocrisy and self-ruin: those who block others from the Prophet and the revelation while also withdrawing themselves think they are harming the call or the Messenger, but in reality every barrier they erect and every distance they keep only damages their own souls. Their tragedy is compounded by unawareness—they do not realize that their rejection is self-destruction, not a victory over the truth.

translation: And if you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire and they say, 'If only we were returned, we would not deny the signs of our Lord and we would be among the believers.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbelievers' futile regret in the Hereafter: when they are confronted with Hellfire, they will wish for a second chance to return to worldly life, promising to accept God's signs and join the believers. Their plea shows that faith extracted only by witnessing the punishment is not true repentance, and it warns that the time for belief and obedience is in this life, before the moment when regret can no longer benefit anyone.

translation: But what they used to conceal before has become apparent to them. And if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the insincerity of those who, only when faced with punishment or death, admit the truths they had hidden and promise to reform. Their confession is not genuine repentance but forced exposure. Allah, knowing their inner reality, declares that even if they were sent back to worldly life, they would relapse into the very disbelief and sins they were forbidden from. Therefore their claim that they would believe and amend is false. It teaches that Allah's judgment rests on His perfect knowledge of the hearts, and that promises made merely out of fear, without a real change of will, are worthless.

translation: And they said, "There is nothing but our life of this world, and we are not to be resurrected."
interpretation: This verse reports the denial of the afterlife by those who confine reality to worldly existence and reject being raised for judgment. It expresses a materialistic and heedless outlook that refuses accountability to God, denies His power to resurrect, and treats this present life as the only end. The Qur'an cites this claim as a grave error and as a symptom of attachment to worldly desires and rejection of divine truth.

translation: And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord. He will say: 'Is this not the truth?' They will say: 'Yes, by our Lord!' He will say: 'Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when those who rejected faith are brought before their Lord and confronted with the very reality they denied. Their standing before God means the truth of resurrection, accountability, and divine judgment becomes undeniable. Their admission, 'Yes, by our Lord,' is not repentance but a compelled acknowledgment once all excuses are gone. God then orders them to taste punishment because their disbelief was deliberate and persistent. The verse teaches that denial of divine truth may continue in worldly life, but it collapses in the face of God's presence and justice, and the punishment is the direct consequence of rejecting what was true.

translation: Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost. When the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, 'Oh, our regret for what we neglected in it!' And they will bear their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear.
interpretation: The verse declares that the real loss belongs to those who reject resurrection and accountability before God. They live as if the encounter with Him will never happen, so they do not prepare for it. When the Hour overtakes them unexpectedly, their regret is intense, but it cannot change their state: they see too late how much they wasted of the opportunity to believe and do good. Their sins do not disappear; they carry them as a crushing load on their backs, and the verse condemns that load as an evil burden. Thus the ultimate ruin is not mere death, but arriving before God with denial and accumulated sins after the time for repentance has passed.

translation: And the worldly life is nothing but play and amusement, and the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse teaches that when worldly existence is pursued as the ultimate goal, it reduces human life to passing diversion and idle entertainment, because its pleasures are temporary and do not satisfy the soul’s deepest purpose. The Hereafter is better for the God-conscious because it is the enduring abode where righteous effort yields lasting reward. The closing question is a rebuke and a call to rational reflection: one who truly reasons will not sacrifice eternal good for fleeting amusement, but will live with accountability and taqwa, prioritizing what remains over what perishes.

translation: We certainly know that what they say grieves you. They are not denying you, but the wrongdoers are rejecting the signs of Allah.
interpretation: This is a consolation to the Prophet: their mockery and accusations wound him, yet their rejection is not a sincere verdict that he is false. Inwardly they recognize his truthfulness, but their wrongdoing expresses itself as stubborn denial of God's revealed signs. The offense is therefore against God and His revelations, not against the Prophet's personal integrity, so he should not bear their denial as if it were a judgment on his character.

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were denied, but they patiently endured the denial and persecution until Our help came to them. And there is no changer of the words of Allah. And there has already come to you some of the news of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and the believers by showing that rejection and harm are not unique to them; earlier messengers also faced denial, mockery, and suffering. Their response was patient perseverance and trust in Allah, not despair or abandonment of the mission. The coming of Allah’s help at the appointed time demonstrates that divine support is certain and never fails, even if it is delayed. The phrase that none can alter the words of Allah means His promises and decrees are unchangeable; what He has guaranteed for His messengers will inevitably come to pass. The reference to the news of past messengers serves as confirmation and encouragement: the same pattern of trial followed by divine aid has already been established, so the Prophet should remain steadfast and confident in Allah’s promise.

translation: And if their turning away is hard on you, then if you can seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign—[do so]. But if Allah willed, He could have gathered them all upon guidance; so do not be among the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet for his grief over the disbelievers’ rejection and teaches that faith is not produced merely by extraordinary signs. Even if he were to exhaust every possible means—descending into the earth or ascending into the heavens to bring them a miracle—their guidance would still depend on Allah’s will. Allah has power to compel all people toward guidance, but He does not; He tests through choice, invitation, and patience. Therefore, the Prophet must not fall into the ignorance of being consumed by sorrow over what is beyond his control, nor imagine that he can force belief. His duty is to convey the message, while guidance belongs to Allah alone.

translation: Only those who hear will respond. And the dead — Allah will resurrect them; then to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse distinguishes between two conditions of the human heart. True response to divine guidance comes from one who “hears” in the deeper sense: a living, attentive, willing heart that recognizes the truth and submits to it. Mere physical hearing is not enough if the heart remains unmoved. Those described as “dead” are not outside Allah’s power; their present inability or refusal to respond does not thwart God’s ultimate plan. Allah will raise them, just as He raises the physically dead, and every soul will ultimately return to Him for judgment and recompense. Thus the verse affirms human responsibility to respond to the truth while alive in heart, and at the same time affirms God’s absolute sovereignty over life, death, resurrection, and the final return.

translation: And they say, "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers’ demand for a miraculous sign as a condition for faith, exposing that their demand is not a sincere search for truth but a challenge rooted in obstinacy. The response affirms that Allah is fully capable of sending any sign He wills; His power is not in question. The delay or refusal is a matter of divine wisdom: signs are not sent merely to satisfy human whims or to compel belief, because even overwhelming miracles do not benefit hearts that are determined to reject. Most people do not know this deeper reality—that the greatest sign is the revelation itself, and that Allah’s governance of signs, faith, and accountability follows perfect knowledge and justice.

translation: And there is no moving creature on the earth, nor any bird that flies with its two wings, except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse declares that all living creatures are not random or forgotten but are created as ordered communities under God’s care, each with its own pattern of life, provision, and purpose, comparable to human societies in being subject to His wisdom and decree. The “Book” is God’s all-encompassing record and decree, in which nothing—whether of creation, sustenance, guidance, or judgment—has been omitted. Their being gathered to their Lord means that every creature ultimately returns to God’s just disposal and accounting; His justice extends even to the animal creation, while moral responsibility and final reward or punishment in the revealed sense apply to beings addressed by divine command.

translation: And those who deny Our signs are deaf and mute, in darkness. Whomever Allah wills, He sends astray; and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse portrays rejection of God's revelations as a spiritual paralysis: such people lose the ability to hear the truth, speak it, or find their way out of confusion. Their being in darkness is the consequence of persisting in denial. At the same time, the verse affirms that guidance and misguidance ultimately rest under God's sovereign will: He allows those who choose denial to wander astray, and He grants whom He wills the clarity and steadfastness to follow the straight path of faith and obedience. Thus it combines a warning about the debilitating effects of rejecting divine signs with a call to recognize God's absolute authority over guidance.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah should come to you, or the Hour should come to you, would you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse confronts the polytheists with the reality of their inner conviction at the moment of overwhelming distress. When Allah’s punishment or the Hour arrives, they will instinctively turn to Allah alone, not to the idols they associate with Him. Their own conduct in that crisis would testify that only Allah can answer and rescue, while the false deities they invoke in ease are powerless. Thus the verse establishes that worship and supplication belong exclusively to Allah, and it exposes the inconsistency of calling upon others besides Him while claiming sincerity in their false religion.

translation: Nay, it is Him you call upon, and He removes that for which you call upon Him if He wills, and you forget what you associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse exposes the inconsistency of those who associate others with God: when severe hardship strikes, their innermost being turns exclusively to God alone, recognizing that no idol, intercessor, or created power can remove the harm; the very things they joined with Him in worship are then abandoned and forgotten. It affirms that true deliverance belongs solely to God, who answers and removes distress only by His will, not because anyone can compel Him or share His authority. Thus the falsehood of shirk is laid bare: it is a loyalty maintained in ease but discarded in desperate need, while the natural recognition of God's exclusive lordship emerges when all other hopes fail.

translation: And We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, then We seized them with adversity and hardship, so that they might humble themselves [before Us].
interpretation: This verse teaches that when earlier nations rejected God’s messengers, God did not immediately annihilate them; rather, He tested them with poverty, loss, and suffering as a merciful call to return. The purpose of such trials was to break their arrogance and lead them to humble supplication and repentance, showing that hardship can be a means of spiritual awakening before final punishment.

translation: So why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made attractive to them what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse explains that divine punishment is meant to awaken repentance: when hardship and chastisement came, those nations should have turned to God in humility and supplication. Their failure was not due to a lack of warning, but because their hearts had already become hard through persistent sin. Satan then exploited that hardness by making their corrupt deeds appear good and desirable, so they remained deluded. The verse thus teaches that continuous disobedience can deaden the heart until even calamity no longer produces humility, and that Satan’s deception is most effective where the heart has already turned away from God.

translation: So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of all things, until, when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair.
interpretation: This verse describes divine gradual punishment (istidrāj): when people turn away from the reminders and warnings sent to them, God may increase their worldly blessings—wealth, health, pleasure, power—not as a reward but as a test and a means of leading them further into heedlessness. Their joy in these gifts blinds them to accountability, so the punishment comes suddenly, without warning, stripping away their false security. The result is 'mublisūn': utterly despondent, regretful, and hopeless, unable to escape or recover what they lost. The verse teaches that prosperity is not proof of God's approval, and that persistent rejection of divine guidance can bring a swift, devastating reckoning.

translation: So the people who did wrong were cut off completely. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: It means that God eradicated the unjust people, leaving no trace or remnant of them, as a just recompense for their persistent wrongdoing. The praise that follows affirms that God's decree and judgment are wise and praiseworthy, and that He is the Lord and Sustainer of all worlds, who ultimately establishes justice and vindicates the truth.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should take away your hearing and your sight and seal your hearts, which deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?" Look how We diversify the signs; yet they still turn away.
interpretation: This verse is a forceful rhetorical challenge to those who set up rivals with Allah. It calls them to reflect on the fact that hearing, sight, and the heart’s ability to understand and believe are entirely in Allah’s hand. If He were to remove these faculties or seal the heart against guidance, no false god or imagined partner could restore them or bring any substitute. The verse therefore establishes Allah’s exclusive power over both outward senses and inward perception, and it exposes the irrationality of relying on anything besides Him. It also shows that the repeated, varied presentation of divine signs is meant to awaken people, yet their persistence in turning away is not due to a lack of evidence but to a deliberate rejection of the truth. The mention of sealing the hearts warns that continued heedlessness can lead to spiritual insensitivity, after which no created being can guide or rescue.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah should come upon you suddenly or openly, will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?'
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a call to reflect: divine punishment, whether it strikes suddenly without warning or comes visibly in the open, does not fall upon the innocent or the righteous. It only befalls those who have chosen injustice—those who reject God's signs, persist in disobedience, and wrong themselves by denying the truth. The question is rhetorical, emphasizing that God's justice is not arbitrary; His punishment is the consequence of human wrongdoing, and it is meant to awaken people to repent before it is too late.

translation: And We do not send the messengers except as bearers of glad tidings and warners. So whoever believes and reforms, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: God sends His messengers only to convey good news to those who accept faith and reform themselves, and to warn those who reject. The one who combines true belief with righteous action is promised safety from the terror of the Hereafter and from sorrow over what has passed or been missed; his faith and reform remove the causes of both fear and grief.

translation: And those who deny Our signs, the punishment will touch them because they used to transgress.
interpretation: This verse teaches that rejecting God's signs is not a neutral intellectual stance but a moral rebellion that places a person outside the bounds of obedience. The punishment is described as touching them directly, indicating that it is the inevitable consequence of their own persistent fasiq—their deliberate transgression—rather than an arbitrary act of divine wrath. It underscores that divine justice is tied to human responsibility: those who continually deny and violate God's guidance bring suffering upon themselves, and their denial itself is the root of their ruin.

translation: Say: I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say to you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me. Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet is a human messenger, not a possessor of God's treasures, not a knower of the unseen, and not an angel. His only path is to follow the revelation given to him. The comparison of the blind and the seeing is a call to reflect: those who accept divine guidance and think deeply are like the seeing, while those who reject it and ignore the signs are like the blind. It urges people to recognize the clear difference between guidance and misguidance and to follow what God has revealed.

translation: And warn by it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord: they have no protector or intercessor besides Him, so that they may become righteous.
interpretation: The verse directs the Prophet—and every bearer of the Qur’an—to use divine revelation as a warning that awakens hearts already alive to accountability, not to coerce the heedless. Its core meaning is that on the Day of Gathering, every claim of patronage and intercession collapses before God’s exclusive sovereignty: no one besides Him can shield a soul or plead its case. The warning is therefore medicinal and preventive; it is given so that fear of that meeting becomes taqwa—a guarding of the self through obedience and avoidance of divine displeasure.

translation: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face. You are not accountable for them at all, nor are they accountable for you at all, so that you would drive them away and be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse forbids excluding or dismissing sincere believers—especially those of humble or low social standing—in order to accommodate the wealthy, powerful, or influential. True worth before God is based on devotion, sincerity, and seeking His pleasure, not on status, lineage, or worldly prestige. Since every person’s account is with God alone, no human being has the right to reject a sincere servant of God or treat such a person as unworthy of company and religious fellowship. To drive away the humble worshippers for worldly reasons is to commit injustice and to place oneself among the wrongdoers.

translation: And thus We have tried some of them by means of others, so that they say, 'Are these the ones whom Allah has favored among us?' Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?
interpretation: Allah tests people by placing them in differing conditions and social ranks, so that the proud and worldly-minded look at the poor or lowly believers and mockingly ask whether these could really be the ones favored by Allah. Their question assumes that divine favor must appear as wealth, status, or power, but the verse answers that Allah knows best who is truly grateful. The real favor is guidance, faith, and gratitude to Allah, and the test exposes who responds with humility and thankfulness and who responds with arrogance and contempt.

translation: And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, 'Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed mercy upon Himself: that whoever among you does evil out of ignorance and then repents afterwards and reforms, then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s mercy is not merely hoped for but is a commitment He has bound Himself to for those who turn to Him. The greeting of peace given to believers is an assurance of safety, acceptance, and divine favor. The phrase “out of ignorance” points to human weakness, heedlessness, or sin committed without full defiant rejection of God; it is not a permission for deliberate wrongdoing. The path of return requires repentance followed by reform—sincere regret must produce a changed life and repair of what was wrong. Thus God’s forgiveness and mercy are presented as an open door for the repentant, calling believers to hope in Him rather than despair over their failures.

translation: And thus We explain the verses in detail, and so that the way of the criminals may become clear.
interpretation: God clarifies His revelations with enough detail, evidence, and distinction that truth is separated from falsehood. The path of the criminals is then made unmistakably evident—not as something to follow, but as a warning: it is the route of those who reject God's guidance, spread corruption, and persist in sin. By exposing both the right way and the way of wrongdoing, the verse teaches that divine explanation is meant to give insight, moral discernment, and a clear warning against choosing the path that leads to ruin.

translation: Say, 'I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah.' Say, 'I will not follow your desires. If I did, I would have gone astray, and I would not be among the rightly guided.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that worship must be directed to God alone. The Prophet is commanded to declare his refusal to worship the false deities the people call upon besides God, and to reject any pressure to compromise or follow their whims in matters of faith. Following human desire in belief and worship leads away from the straight path; had he done so, he would have been astray and deprived of divine guidance. True guidance is not determined by majority preference or inherited custom but by God's revelation, and the Prophet's unwavering adherence to it is a model of fidelity to monotheism.

translation: Say, "Indeed, I am on clear evidence from my Lord, but you have denied it. I do not have what you seek to hasten. Judgment is only for Allah; He decides with truth, and He is the best of deciders."
interpretation: The verse presents the Prophet’s answer to those who rejected him and impatiently demanded that punishment or a miraculous sign come immediately. His certainty rests on clear insight and evidence from God, so their denial does not make his message doubtful. He does not control the timing of divine decree; what they are impatient for belongs to God alone. All ruling, requital, and final distinction between truth and falsehood are God’s prerogative. He judges by truth and is the best of judges, so His decision is always just, wise, and perfectly timed.

translation: Say, "If I had what you seek to hasten, the matter would have been decided between me and you. And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse addresses those who mockingly demanded that the Prophet ﷺ hasten the punishment or divine judgment they were warned about. He is instructed to tell them that he has no authority to bring about such matters on his own; if it were up to him, the affair would already have been settled and the punishment would have come upon them. But the timing and execution of judgment belong solely to Allah, who knows best who the wrongdoers are—their identities, intentions, and the wisdom in delaying or hastening their reckoning. It teaches reliance upon Allah, humility before His decree, and trust that divine justice will occur at the appointed time.

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is in the land and the sea. Not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear Record.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the knowledge of the unseen belongs exclusively to Allah; no creature can access it independently. His knowledge is all-encompassing, reaching every event and object in the visible and hidden realms, from the vastness of land and sea to the fall of a single leaf, a seed hidden in the earth, and every moist or dry thing. The 'clear Record' signifies the Preserved Tablet, in which all things are recorded and preserved by His knowledge and decree. Thus, it calls believers to humble themselves before Allah, trust His wisdom, and acknowledge that nothing escapes His awareness or governance.

translation: And He is the One who takes your souls at night and knows what you have earned during the day, then He raises you up in it so that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse presents sleep as a likeness of death and waking as a likeness of resurrection. When a person sleeps, God takes the soul temporarily, yet He still knows every deed committed during the day. Waking is not merely a natural event but a renewed grant of life until the appointed term decreed by God is completed. The alternation of night and day thus manifests God's exclusive authority over life, death, and resurrection, and it reminds the human being that the final return is to God alone, where every action will be disclosed and held to account.

translation: And He is the Supreme over His servants, and He sends guardians over you, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take his soul, and they do not neglect.
interpretation: This verse affirms God’s absolute sovereignty and overwhelming control over all His creation: nothing escapes His dominion, and all beings remain beneath His authority. The “guardians” are angels assigned to watch over people, recording their deeds and guarding them by God’s command. When a person’s appointed time of death arrives, these angels carry out God’s decree without fail or delay, taking the soul exactly as commanded. Thus the verse teaches that life, death, and every moment in between are governed by God’s precise will, and that His agents execute His command with perfect obedience and without negligence.

translation: Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, to Him belongs all judgment, and He is the swiftest of reckoners.
interpretation: This means that after death, every soul is brought back to Allah alone, its real Guardian and Owner, not to any false patron or idol. All authority to decree, judge, reward, and punish belongs exclusively to Him. He is the swiftest in reckoning: His accounting is immediate, exact, and just, and no one can evade or delay it.

translation: Say, 'Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea, when you call upon Him in humility and in secret, saying, "If He saves us from this, we will surely be among the grateful"?'
interpretation: This verse establishes that when people are overwhelmed by the perils and terrors of land and sea, they instinctively turn to God alone, abandoning their false deities. Their supplication is sincere: humble, hidden, and accompanied by a vow of gratitude if delivered. The question posed is a proof against them: since only God answers in such moments, only He deserves worship. Their later return to idolatry and ingratitude is therefore a betrayal of their own testimony and of the covenant they made in distress.

translation: Say, "It is Allah who saves you from it and from every distress; then you associate others with Him."
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to answer those who themselves admit that only Allah rescues them from dangers and hardships. It establishes that rescue from every calamity belongs solely to Allah, so after He alone delivers them, their worship of other beings besides Him is false, contradictory, and ungrateful.

translation: Say, 'He is able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to divide you into factions and make some of you taste the violence of others.' Look how We explain the signs in various ways so that they may understand.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God alone has full power over all punishment and that His warning can take many forms: harm descending from above, calamity rising from below, or a more subtle but severe punishment in which a community is split into competing groups and turns against itself. The mention of being clothed in sects and tasting one another’s violence shows that internal division, partisanship, civil strife, and mutual oppression are not merely human accidents; they can be manifestations of divine chastisement when people persist in heedlessness. The verse then calls attention to how God varies and repeats His signs, arguments, and warnings so that people might grasp the truth with deep understanding and turn back before such consequences fall upon them.

translation: And your people have denied it, though it is the truth. Say, 'I am not a guardian over you.'
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet to remain steadfast when his people reject the revelation: their denial does not make it false, for it is the truth from God. His duty is only to deliver the message, not to force faith, control their choices, or bear responsibility for their acceptance. Their ultimate reckoning and guidance belong to God alone.

translation: For every announcement there is a fixed time and place, and you will come to know.
interpretation: This verse declares that every report, promise, and warning—especially the Qur’anic tidings of resurrection, judgment, and divine punishment or reward—has an appointed term and a definite reality in which it will inevitably come to pass. Those who reject or mock it will soon discover its truth when its fixed time arrives, and no one can hasten or delay it.

translation: And when you see those who engage in vain discourse about Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a discourse other than that. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse establishes a boundary for believers: gatherings in which God’s revelations are mocked, belittled, or treated as mere material for idle argument are not places to remain. Withdrawing from such talk is not fleeing from truth but refusing to give it legitimacy or an audience. If one forgets or is distracted and stays, then once reminded, one must separate from those who persist in that injustice. The verse protects faith, honors revelation, and prevents complicity through silence or continued presence.

translation: And there is no blame upon those who fear Allah for their account whatsoever, but it is a reminder, so that they may become God-fearing.
interpretation: The God-conscious are not held responsible for the deeds or final reckoning of those who mock God’s signs; their duty is only to remind, not to answer for others or enforce faith. If they avoid participating in the mockery and wrongdoing, no sin attaches to them because of the mockers’ account. The reminder is given so that the mockers may awaken to God-consciousness and turn away from their defiance.

translation: And leave those who take their religion as amusement and play, and whom the life of this world has deluded. And remind with it, lest a soul be doomed for what it has earned; it will have no protector or intercessor besides Allah, and even if it offers every compensation, it will not be accepted from it. Those are the ones doomed for what they earned; for them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they disbelieved.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reduce religion to amusement and are deceived by worldly life are accountable for their own ruin. The Qur’an is to be used as a reminder, because on the Day of Judgment a soul that has earned destruction will find no ally, helper, or intercessor besides Allah, and no ransom or compensation, however great, will be accepted. Their recompense is described as boiling water and painful punishment, corresponding to their rejection of faith. Thus the verse teaches that mockery of religion and absorption in worldly pleasures cannot avert accountability, and that salvation depends solely on Allah’s mercy through faith and obedience.

translation: Say, 'Shall we invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us? Like one whom the devils have enticed in the earth, bewildered; he has companions calling him to guidance, [saying], 'Come to us.' Say, 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [true] guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical condemnation of associating partners with Allah. It asks how one could invoke beings that can neither help nor harm, and abandon the guidance already received. Such a return is depicted as a bewildered person lured by devils, lost in the earth, while companions call him to the right way. It teaches that only Allah's guidance is genuine guidance, and true faith requires wholehearted submission to the Lord of all worlds. The remedy for confusion is not following powerless objects or deceptive impulses but responding to divine guidance and remaining steadfast in tawhid.

translation: And [He commanded] that you establish prayer and fear Him; and He is the One to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse is a divine directive to uphold the ritual prayer (salah) consistently and to cultivate taqwa—God-consciousness, awe, and obedience—by avoiding what He forbids. The command is not merely to perform prayer mechanically but to make it a stable, ongoing practice, and to let reverence for God govern one’s conduct. The closing statement—that He is the One to whom all will be gathered—grounds this command in accountability: prayer and taqwa are not ends in themselves but preparation for resurrection and standing before God. Since all will be gathered to Him alone, worship and restraint must be sincere, directed solely to Him, and sustained with the awareness that every deed will be presented before the One who has full authority over the final gathering.

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the Day He says, 'Be,' and it is, His word is the truth. And His is the dominion on the Day the Horn is blown. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone originated the heavens and the earth with perfect wisdom and for a true purpose, not in play or falsehood. His creative command is absolute: whenever He wills something, He merely says “Be,” and it instantly comes into existence. His promise and word are true and unavoidable. All sovereignty and authority belong exclusively to Him, especially on the Day of Resurrection when the Horn is blown and the dead are raised for judgment. He knows both the unseen and the seen—what is hidden from creation and what is witnessed—and He is All-Wise in His decrees and All-Aware of every condition and consequence.

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his father Azar, 'Do you take idols as gods? Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error.'
interpretation: This verse conveys that Prophet Abraham confronted his own father and his community with the core error of idolatry: treating lifeless, man-made idols as divine beings worthy of worship. Abraham's question is a rebuke of both the absurdity and the injustice of shirk, because idols can neither create, sustain, guide, nor harm. By declaring his father and people to be in manifest error, he identifies their worship as a clear deviation from the truth that God alone is Creator and Sovereign. The verse teaches that the call to pure monotheism must be clear and unreserved, even when directed at close kin, and that loyalty to God takes precedence over inherited custom and family allegiance. It also shows that guidance is not guaranteed by lineage or community; a whole people can be engulfed in falsehood while one person, by God's favor, recognizes and proclaims the truth.

translation: And thus We showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, so that he would be among those who are certain.
interpretation: God unveiled to Abraham the inner reality of His absolute dominion over all creation, not merely as hearsay but as experiential knowledge that settles in the heart. This was to raise his faith to unwavering certainty, so that his monotheism would be grounded in direct conviction, free from doubt, and firm against the idolatry around him.

translation: When the night covered him, he saw a star. He said, 'This is my Lord.' But when it set, he said, 'I do not love those that set.'
interpretation: Abraham uses the star’s disappearance as a rational proof against worshipping created things: whatever sets, vanishes, or changes cannot be the ultimate Lord. His statement 'This is my Lord' is not his final belief but a way of engaging his people’s false premise, so that when the star sets he can expose its inability to be divine. The true Lord must be eternal, ever-present, and free from the impermanence and decline that mark all created phenomena.

translation: And when he saw the moon rising, he said, 'This is my Lord.' But when it set, he said, 'If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the misguided people.'
interpretation: This verse conveys that Abraham was demonstrating, through his people's own observations, that no created heavenly body can be Lord, since rising and setting are signs of contingency and change, whereas true Lordship is eternal and unchanging. His statement about needing guidance expresses that human reason alone cannot reach sound belief without God's direction, and that turning to anything other than God is the essence of being astray.

translation: When he saw the sun rising, he said, 'This is my Lord; this is greater.' But when it set, he said, 'O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate [with Allah].'
interpretation: Abraham is not confessing the sun as his Lord; he is guiding his people by demonstrating the absurdity of worshipping a created sign. The sun's setting shows that it is subject to change and disappearance, so it cannot be the eternal, self-subsisting Lord. His declaration of freedom from their associations is a rejection of all shirk, affirming that only the One who is not subject to setting or decline deserves worship.

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face [in worship] toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, being upright in faith, and I am not among those who associate partners [with Allah].
interpretation: This is a declaration of pure, unreserved monotheism: the speaker directs his entire self—his worship, purpose, and inward orientation—exclusively toward Allah, the sole Creator and Sustainer of all existence. To turn one's face to Him means to abandon every competing loyalty, false object of devotion, and self-invented path, and to stand firmly on the original, upright faith (hanifiyyah) that acknowledges God alone as Lord. The final negation—'I am not of the polytheists'—is not merely a rejection of idol worship but a complete disavowal of any partner, intermediary, or authority that would share in the Creator's exclusive right to be worshipped, obeyed, and trusted.

translation: And his people argued with him. He said, “Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? And I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then take heed?”
interpretation: True guidance comes from Allah alone, and no amount of disputation or intimidation can overturn it. A believer trusts that false objects of worship have no independent power to harm or benefit; all things occur only by Allah’s will. Therefore, fear, worship, and reliance belong to Allah alone, whose knowledge encompasses everything. The verse calls people to reflect and remember, so they abandon blind adherence to inherited falsehood and recognize the proofs of Allah’s exclusive lordship.

translation: And how should I fear what you associate [with Him], while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? So which of the two parties is more deserving of security, if you know?
interpretation: This verse exposes the inconsistency in the polytheists' fear and security. They wished Abraham to fear the idols they associated with Allah, yet they did not fear the greater wrong of attributing partners to Allah without any revealed proof or authority. The rhetorical question declares that true security belongs to the party of pure monotheism, not to those who join false gods with Allah. Fear should not be directed toward powerless created things, and security cannot be grounded in shirk; it belongs to those who worship Allah alone, because He alone has authority, power, and the right to be feared and trusted.

translation: Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided.
interpretation: This means that true security and guidance belong to those whose faith remains pure and uncorrupted by shirk or any injustice that nullifies it. The Prophet explained that the “wrongdoing” intended here is shirk, as in Luqman’s words, “Indeed, shirk is a great injustice” (31:13). So whoever preserves tawhid and keeps faith free from association with God will be safe from the fear of punishment and guided to the truth in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And that is Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people. We raise in degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the decisive proof and clear reasoning by which Abraham confronted his people’s idolatry and false worship were granted by Allah, not acquired by human cleverness alone. Allah establishes His chosen servants with evidence that exposes falsehood and vindicates truth, and He alone elevates people in ranks of knowledge, faith, and honor according to His wisdom. His raising some above others is not arbitrary but flows from perfect wisdom and all-encompassing knowledge, so He knows whom to support, how to test, and what station each soul deserves.

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob; each We guided. And Noah We guided before; and from his descendants David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse presents divine guidance as a pure favor from Allah that He grants to those He chooses, and it shows that the prophetic line among Ibrahim’s descendants was not a matter of inherited privilege but of Allah’s selecting and guiding the upright. The mention of Noah before them establishes that guidance is one continuous divine pattern across generations, while the closing statement means that Allah’s recompense for those who excel in faith, worship, and righteous conduct is precisely this: He guides them, honors them, and makes them bearers of prophetic light. In this sense, being guided and made a means of guidance is the reward of ihsan—doing good with sincerity and excellence.

translation: And Zechariah, John, Jesus, and Elijah—all were among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse affirms that these prophets are among God’s righteous servants, praised for their piety, guidance, and faithful fulfillment of the prophetic mission. Placing Jesus alongside Zechariah, John, and Elijah shows that he belongs to the same line of honored prophets and righteous worshippers of God, and that true nobility before God is measured by righteousness and sincere servitude, not by worldly status or claims of divinity.

translation: And Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot—each We favored above the worlds.
interpretation: God honors these prophets by stating that He chose them and raised them above the people of their time through prophethood, revelation, and guidance. Their favor was not merely worldly distinction but a spiritual selection that made them models of truth, patience, and obedience, and recipients of God’s special care and commission to call others to Him.

translation: And from among their fathers, their descendants, and their brothers; We chose them and guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This means that God’s election and guidance are not inherited automatically by family line or tribe; He chooses whom He wills from among forebears, offspring, and siblings, and He grants them the special guidance that leads to the straight path—the path of pure monotheism, truth, and obedience to Him.

translation: That is the guidance of Allah, by which He guides whom He wills of His servants. And if they had associated others with Him, all that they used to do would have been nullified.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true guidance is not a human achievement or inherited privilege but a pure gift from Allah, granted to whom He wills among His servants. It then lays down a universal principle: the acceptance of any deed is conditional upon pure monotheism (tawhid). The plural 'they' refers to the prophets and righteous figures just mentioned; the conditional statement is hypothetical and impossible—they never committed shirk—yet it serves as an emphatic warning that if even such exalted servants were to associate partners with Allah, their lifelong righteous works would be rendered null and void. Thus, no lineage, miracle, or good deed can compensate for shirk, and no one is exempt from the obligation of exclusive worship of Allah. The verse also teaches that guidance ultimately rests with Allah's will, so believers should humbly ask Him for it and never boast of their own efforts.

translation: Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, the Judgment, and the Prophethood. So if these disbelieve in it, We have indeed entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it.
interpretation: The verse states that God’s favor of revelation, sound judgment, and prophethood is not tied to any particular nation or generation. When those first addressed reject or deny that divine guidance, God will raise and entrust it to others who accept it with faith and safeguard it. Thus disbelief cannot harm God or stop His guidance; it only removes the rejecters from its blessing and transfers its custodianship to a believing people.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so follow their guidance. Say, 'I do not ask you for it any reward. It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet Muhammad to follow the divinely guided path of the earlier prophets, whose guidance was not a separate or conflicting religion but the same essential call to pure monotheism, sincere worship, moral rectitude, and patient perseverance in conveying God's message. The command to follow their guidance confirms that the prophetic tradition is unified and that the final Prophet is the inheritor and confirmer of that same way, not an innovator seeking personal authority. He is then told to declare that he asks no payment or worldly compensation for delivering the revelation; his only concern is to convey the reminder. The message is therefore described as a universal admonition for all creation, meant to awaken hearts, remind them of their Lord, and guide them toward truth. This excludes any motive of material gain or sectarian advantage and affirms that the Prophet's mission is purely for the benefit of humanity and all worlds, calling them to the same guidance accepted by the chosen prophets before him.

translation: And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal when they said, 'Allah has not sent down to any human being anything.' Say, 'Who sent down the Scripture which Moses brought as a light and guidance for the people? You make it into sheets, showing some and concealing much. And you were taught what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers.' Say, 'Allah.' Then leave them in their discourse, playing.
interpretation: This verse exposes the contradiction and ingratitude of those who deny divine revelation. They fail to honor God as He deserves by claiming He never sent guidance to any human, yet they themselves acknowledge the Book of Moses as a light and guidance. By asking who sent it down, the verse compels the admission that it is Allah alone. It further condemns their manipulation of revelation: they reduce it to scattered pages, publicizing what suits them and hiding what does not. It also reminds them that God has taught them what neither they nor their ancestors knew, so their denial is not due to lack of evidence but to stubbornness. The command to leave them in their idle play indicates that after the truth has been made clear, argument with such people is futile.

translation: And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed and confirming what was before it, so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it. And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are steadfast in their prayers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Qur’an as a blessed revelation from God, not a new or isolated message but one that confirms the earlier scriptures and stands as their trustworthy guardian. Its purpose is universal warning: the “Mother of Cities” is Mecca, and “those around it” signifies the surrounding peoples and, by extension, all humanity. The verse also joins two marks of true faith: inward conviction in the Hereafter and outward fidelity to prayer. Whoever genuinely believes in the final accounting will inevitably accept this Book and guard the prescribed prayers, because prayer is the practical expression of that belief and the covenant of the believers with their Lord.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah, or says, “It has been revealed to me,” while nothing has been revealed to him, and one who says, “I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down.” If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are stretching out their hands: “Deliver up your souls! Today you will be repaid the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth, and for being arrogant toward His signs.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the gravest form of injustice: speaking falsely in God’s name, falsely claiming divine revelation, or claiming the ability to produce guidance like God’s revelation. Such claims are not mere errors but arrogant usurpations of God’s authority, made by those who reject His signs while pretending to rival them. At the moment of death, their falsehood collapses: the wrongdoers are engulfed in the throes of death, and the angels stretch out their hands to seize their souls, commanding them to surrender themselves. They are then told that their recompense is a humiliating punishment because they attributed falsehood to God and proudly turned away from His revealed signs. The verse thus warns that whoever invents lies about God, claims revelation falsely, or exalts himself above divine guidance will face disgrace when the soul is taken and will find no escape from the consequence of his arrogance and false speech.

translation: And you have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We had granted you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners with you. Indeed, the bond between you has been severed, and what you used to claim has gone astray from you.
interpretation: This verse depicts the disbelievers’ condition on the Day of Resurrection: they return to God individually, stripped of wealth, children, worldly rank, and all false supports. The “intercessors” or partners they imagined—whether idols, leaders, or objects of reliance—are absent and powerless. Every claim of shared divinity or independent mediation collapses. The verse teaches that ultimate accountability is personal and that no created being can shield a person from God’s judgment without His permission. It warns against trusting in anything other than God and affirms that His sole authority, ownership, and lordship will be manifest when all false attachments are severed and all deceptive claims vanish.
