translation: Indeed, Allah is the Cleaver of the grain and the date-seed. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living. That is Allah, so how are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah’s exclusive lordship and power as the proof of His oneness: He alone splits the seed and the pit to bring forth life, and He alone governs the cycle of life and death, bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living. Since such creative and life-giving power belongs to Him alone, turning away from Him to false objects of worship or dependence is a delusion.

translation: He is the Cleaver of the dawn, and He made the night a place of rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: God alone brings light out of darkness and governs the alternation of time; the night is made for stillness and restoration, while the sun and moon move with exact measure to serve human need. This ordered cosmos is not accidental but the decree of the Almighty, whose power creates and sustains, and the All-Knowing, whose wisdom arranges every detail with purpose and precision. Therefore, lordship, authority, and worship belong to Him alone.

translation: And it is He who made the stars for you, so that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea. We have certainly made the signs clear for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah placed the stars as purposeful signs of guidance, especially for travelers and sailors who navigate through the darknesses of land and sea. The "darknesses" point to both physical night and the broader human condition of uncertainty, where people need a reliable guide. The stars are not divine themselves; they are created means through which Allah shows mercy and order. The statement that the signs have been made clear indicates that creation and revelation together provide sufficient evidence for those willing to use knowledge and reflection. Thus, true knowledge should lead a person from observing the stars to recognizing the Creator's power, wisdom, and guidance, and to gratitude and worship of Him alone.

translation: And it is He who originated you from one soul, then [there is] a place of settlement and a place of deposit. We have certainly detailed the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: God is the sole creator of humanity, bringing all people forth from a single soul and appointing for each person a phase of settled existence and a phase of temporary entrustment—such as the womb as a place of settlement and the loins as a place of deposit. By clarifying these signs in detail, He provides clear evidence of His oneness, wisdom, and power to those who use their understanding to reflect on creation, the stages of life, and the certainty of resurrection and accountability.

translation: And it is He who sent down water from the sky, and We brought forth thereby every kind of plant, and We brought forth from it green growth, from which We bring forth clustered grain; and from the palm tree, from its spathe, are hanging clusters; and gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, similar and not similar. Look at its fruit when it bears fruit, and its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse calls the human being to read the ordinary order of nature as a continuous sign of God’s creative lordship. Rain, vegetation, grain, date clusters, grapes, olives, and pomegranates are not presented as self-sufficient natural events but as effects of the One who sends down water and brings forth life. The movement from water to every plant, then to green growth, then to grain and fruit, reveals a unified divine purpose beneath the diversity of forms. The description of fruits as both similar and dissimilar points to the balance of order and variation in creation: sameness shows a single wise design, while difference shows the richness of divine power and mercy. The command to look at fruit when it forms and ripens invites careful observation of process, not mere consumption, because such reflection can awaken the heart to the Creator. For the believer, these signs also imply resurrection: the One who brings forth ripe fruit from dead-looking branches and seeds can surely bring the dead to life. Thus the verse establishes tawhid, providence, wisdom, and accountability, and its signs become truly effective only for those whose faith makes them attentive and grateful.

translation: And they made for Allah partners among the jinn, though He created them; and they falsely attributed to Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse condemns the polytheists’ associating created beings with Allah in worship and lordship, since the jinn themselves are His creation and can never share in His divinity. It further rejects the baseless inventions that Allah has sons or daughters, a claim made out of ignorance and false speculation. Allah is absolutely perfect and far exalted above every false attribute, likeness, or relationship that people invent about Him.

translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a child when He has no mate? And He created all things, and He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes God’s absolute uniqueness and transcendence. He is the Originator who brought the heavens and the earth into existence without any prior model or partner. The idea that He could have a son is impossible because having offspring requires a consort or spouse, and He has none. Since He created everything, all beings are His creation and servants, not His offspring. His knowledge is all-encompassing, so He knows all things perfectly, including what His creatures falsely attribute to Him.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the only true Lord is Allah, who alone deserves worship because He alone is the Creator and Sustainer of everything. Since He originates and manages all creation, He is the sole object of worship, and He is the trustee and disposer of all affairs, fully capable of managing and sustaining everything.

translation: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse declares God’s absolute transcendence over created perception: no human or created eye can fully encompass, contain, or comprehend His divine essence, for He is beyond the limits of space, form, and sensory apprehension. Yet His own perception is perfect and all-encompassing; He sees every glance, every hidden intention, and every reality open or concealed. As “al-Latif,” He is subtle, unfathomable, and intimately aware of the finest and most hidden matters; as “al-Khabir,” He is fully informed of all things, inward and outward. Thus the verse joins God’s unknowable majesty with His total knowledge and awareness, teaching that He observes all while remaining beyond the grasp of human sight in this worldly existence.

translation: There have come to you clear insights from your Lord. So whoever sees [the truth], it is for his own soul; and whoever is blind [to it], it is against it. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: The "insights" are inward discernments and clear evidences from God that enable a person to see spiritual reality, not merely to acquire information. Each person's response is his or her own responsibility: whoever uses this light to perceive and accept the truth benefits his own soul, while whoever chooses blindness and rejection brings harm upon it. The Messenger is not sent to force hearts, control choices, or stand as a guardian over people; his task is to convey the message, and God alone is the ultimate guardian and reckoner.

translation: And thus do We diversify the verses, and so that they may say, 'You have studied,' and that We may make it clear to a people who know.
interpretation: God explains His revelations in various ways and repeats them from different angles so that the truth becomes unmistakable. One purpose is to expose the disbelievers' false excuse: when the clear signs come, they claim the Prophet merely studied or learned them from others, rather than acknowledging them as divine revelation. Another purpose is that God clarifies and establishes the message for those who possess knowledge, so that they recognize it, understand it, and benefit from its guidance.

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord—there is no god but Him—and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This means that the Prophet, and every believer after him, must make the revelation from God the sole authority and guide, sincerely affirming that no being deserves worship except God. It also commands disengagement from the path of the polytheists: not imitating their beliefs or practices, not seeking their approval in matters of faith, and leaving their rejection to God after the message has been conveyed.

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated [anything with Him]. And We have not made you a keeper over them, nor are you a trustee over them.
interpretation: This verse teaches that if God had willed, He could have compelled all people to believe and avoid associating partners with Him, since His will is absolute and nothing occurs outside it. However, He did not force them; He granted them the capacity to choose, and He holds them accountable for their choices. The Prophet is therefore not a guardian charged with forcing faith into their hearts, nor a trustee responsible for managing their affairs or ensuring their obedience. His role is only to convey the message clearly. Guidance belongs to God alone, and the Prophet is not blameworthy for their rejection after he has delivered the truth.

translation: And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah, lest they revile Allah out of enmity without knowledge. Thus have We made fair-seeming to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse prohibits believers from insulting the false deities or objects of worship of polytheists, not because those things deserve honor, but because such insults provoke the polytheists to insult Allah in hostility and ignorance. Preventing a greater harm takes precedence over expressing contempt for false gods. God then states that every community has been made to see its own conduct as fair and justified as part of its trial; this is not divine approval, but a test and a reason for accountability. Ultimately, all people return to their Lord, who knows the truth of their deeds and will inform them of what they used to do, judging them with perfect justice.

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, 'The signs are only with Allah.' And what will make you perceive that when it comes, they will not believe?
interpretation: This verse exposes the futility of demanding miracles as a condition for faith. The disbelievers' oaths are emphatic, but Allah declares that signs belong solely to Him; He sends them according to His wisdom, not human ultimatums. The real obstacle is not the absence of proof but the corruption of their hearts. Even if the requested sign were sent, they would still not believe, because their denial is rooted in arrogance and rebellion, not in lack of evidence. Thus miracles do not force faith; guidance is Allah's grant. The address also cautions the Prophet and believers not to be deceived by such oaths or to measure faith by supernatural demands, since Allah alone knows the hidden rejection within them.

translation: And We turn their hearts and their eyes away [from the truth], as they did not believe in it the first time; and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse describes the consequence for those who deliberately reject faith after the truth has come to them: because they refused to believe at the first opportunity, God turns their hearts and sight away from guidance, so they no longer perceive or accept it. Their continued arrogance and transgression are not forced upon them; rather, God abandons them to the path they chose, leaving them blind and confused.

translation: And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered before them all things together, they would not have believed unless Allah willed. But most of them are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith is not produced by overwhelming miracles or signs alone. Even if every possible proof were brought—angels descending, the dead speaking, and all things assembled as evidence—those whose hearts are set against belief would still not believe unless Allah grants them the will and ability to do so. Guidance therefore rests ultimately with Allah, not with the sheer force of supernatural testimony. The statement that most of them are ignorant points to their failure to understand this reality: they suppose that signs compel faith, when in truth faith depends on Allah’s enabling and decree.

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy—devils from among mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech as a delusion. And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it. So leave them and what they fabricate.
interpretation: This verse establishes that hostility to prophetic truth is a recurring divine test: every prophet has faced opposition, and that opposition can come not only from human beings but also from unseen jinn, all cooperating to beautify falsehood and make it seem attractive. Their “adorned speech” is deceptive rhetoric, propaganda, and insinuation meant to turn people away from guidance. Yet their scheming is not outside God’s will; if He had willed, they could not have done it, so they cannot ultimately frustrate His purpose. The Prophet is therefore directed to turn away from their fabrications, not to be shaken by them, and to leave their lies to God’s judgment while continuing faithfully with the truth.

translation: And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing.
interpretation: This verse clarifies the effect and aim of the devils’ whispered, adorned speech: it reaches the hearts of those who reject the Hereafter, so they lean toward it, become satisfied with it, and persist in the evil deeds they are earning. Their denial of the Hereafter is the root of their susceptibility: because they do not fear accountability, false embellishment appeals to them, pleases them, and drives them to commit the sins they commit.

translation: Should I seek a judge other than Allah, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, explained in detail? Those to whom We gave the Scripture know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth. So never be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the right to judge, legislate, and define religious truth belongs exclusively to Allah. Because He alone revealed the Book with its commandments and guidance made clear and distinct, turning to any other authority for ultimate judgment in matters of faith and law is unjustified. The earlier recipients of Scripture recognize this revelation as truly sent down from the Lord, so their recognition confirms its truth rather than casting doubt on it. The command not to be among the doubters is a firm instruction to the Prophet and, through him, to the believers to remain certain that Allah’s revealed judgment is sufficient, true, and binding, and not to waver toward rival claimants to religious authority.

translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah’s decree, revelation, promises, and judgments are perfect and complete: true in everything He reports, just in everything He commands and decides, and free from any deficiency, falsehood, or injustice. No one can alter, replace, or annul His words—neither the Qur’an He revealed nor the decrees and promises He issued. Since He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, He encompasses every spoken word and every hidden intention, so His words are perfectly wise and His rulings are perfectly fair.

translation: And if you obey most of those on the earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow nothing but conjecture, and they do nothing but guess.
interpretation: This verse warns that the majority’s agreement or popularity is not a valid criterion for truth in matters of faith and guidance. Most people, when they are not guided by revelation, base their beliefs and conduct on inherited assumptions, desires, and speculation rather than on certain knowledge. To follow their ways in religion would lead a person away from the straight path of Allah. The believer is therefore required to judge by divine revelation and sound evidence, not by the number of people who hold a view or practice. The verse also exposes the claims of the deniers as mere conjecture and false guessing, not knowledge.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His path, and He is most knowing of the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse establishes that ultimate knowledge of guidance and misguidance belongs exclusively to God. He alone knows the hidden realities of every heart—who will turn away from His path and who will accept His guidance. It teaches that the responsibility of the believer is to convey the message sincerely, not to force or judge outcomes, because God is fully aware of those who are rightly guided and those who go astray.

translation: So eat of that on which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His verses.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers to eat only from what has been slaughtered with the name of Allah pronounced over it, and it ties this obedience to true faith in Allah’s revelations. It teaches that acknowledging Allah’s signs requires following His laws regarding lawful and unlawful food, and that refraining from what is dedicated to other than Allah is a practical proof of sincere belief in Him.

translation: And why do you not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has already explained to you what He has forbidden to you, except when you are compelled by necessity? And indeed, many mislead others by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse rebukes those who avoid lawful food out of baseless scruples or man-made prohibitions. Allah has already clarified what is forbidden, so believers must not add restrictions from desire, custom, or ignorance. The only concession is necessity, when one is forced to eat what is otherwise unlawful. Many people lead others astray by imposing their own whims as if they were divine law, without true knowledge. Allah knows best those who overstep His limits, and He will hold them accountable for distorting what He made lawful and unlawful.

translation: And abandon the outward sin and the inward sin. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit.
interpretation: The verse establishes that sin is not only what appears in external deeds but also what is concealed in the heart, such as hidden intentions, inner disbelief, hypocrisy, and secret wrongdoing. It commands a total avoidance of both categories, since God's judgment covers the visible and the hidden alike, and anyone who persists in acquiring sin—by choosing it, doing it, or harboring it—will inevitably face the just recompense for that which they committed. This is a warning that no sin is outside divine accountability, whether public or private.

translation: And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is defiant disobedience. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to argue with you; and if you obey them, indeed, you are polytheists.
interpretation: This verse forbids eating meat that was not slaughtered with Allah’s name, because invoking a name other than Allah over it, or deliberately omitting His name, is a rejection of pure monotheism. Such an act is fisq—a departure from obedience to Allah. The devils whisper to their allies among humans and jinn, stirring them to dispute with the believers and to make what Allah has forbidden seem lawful or debatable. If believers obey these whisperers by accepting their false claims, following their desires, or treating their authority as equal to Allah’s command, they fall into shirk, since obedience and allegiance in matters of halal and haram belong to Allah alone.

translation: Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among people like him whose likeness is in the darknesses, never coming out of them? Thus what the disbelievers used to do was made fair-seeming to them.
interpretation: This verse contrasts two spiritual conditions. The one who was “dead” is a person dead in heart through unbelief, ignorance, and sin; when Allah grants him faith, repentance, and knowledge, it is a resurrection of the soul. The “light” is divine guidance—sound belief, revealed truth, and the ability to distinguish right from wrong—by which he conducts himself among people with clarity and purpose. The one in “darknesses” is trapped in disbelief, heedlessness, and evil deeds, unable to find his way out because he has rejected the light. The two are not equal in insight, conduct, or final outcome. The closing words mean that those who persist in denying Allah become so deluded that their corrupt actions appear attractive and justified to them; this is a consequence of their own choices and a veil over their hearts. Thus, guidance is a life-giving light from Allah, while persistence in denial leaves a person in ever-deepening darkness.

translation: And thus We have placed in every city its greatest criminals, so that they may plot therein. But they do not plot except against themselves, and they do not perceive.
interpretation: This means that Allah, in His wisdom, allows the most powerful and influential wrongdoers in every society to rise and scheme against the truth and against the believers. Yet their plotting does not harm Allah or His message; it only returns upon their own souls, increasing them in sin and leading them toward their own ruin, though they are unaware of that outcome and mistakenly believe their schemes are succeeding.

translation: And when a sign comes to them, they say, “We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah.” Allah knows best where to place His message. Those who committed crimes will be struck with humiliation before Allah and a severe punishment because of what they used to plot.
interpretation: The verse exposes the disbelievers’ arrogant refusal: they do not reject merely for lack of evidence, but because they demand prophethood or the same privileges granted to Allah’s messengers, making faith conditional on their own elevation. Allah replies that messengership is not earned by human ambition or status; He alone, in His perfect wisdom, knows who is worthy of carrying His revelation. Thus their scheming against the truth and their attempt to control divine selection brings disgrace before Allah and a severe punishment.

translation: So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whoever He intends to lead astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus Allah places impurity upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true guidance is a gift and act of mercy from Allah: He opens a person’s heart to accept Islam with willingness, peace, and submission. In contrast, those who persist in rejection are left with hearts that become narrow and closed to faith, so accepting Islam feels as difficult and suffocating as trying to ascend into the sky. The “impurity” or punishment is therefore placed upon those who knowingly refuse belief, as a just consequence of their rejection, not an arbitrary burden. The verse calls the believer to recognize that a receptive heart is from Allah’s favor, and to seek Him with humility rather than arrogance.

translation: And this is the straight path of your Lord. We have indeed explained the signs in detail for a people who remember.
interpretation: This is a declaration that the way of God—His religion, His commands, and His guidance—is upright and free from deviation. He has clarified His revelations with distinct and detailed explanations so that those who take heed, reflect, and remember His signs, warnings, and covenant may recognize the truth and remain firmly upon that straight path.

translation: For them is the home of peace with their Lord, and He is their Protector because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward of those who believe and act righteously: Allah has prepared for them the Abode of Peace—Paradise—where they will dwell in security, free from every harm, anxiety, and deficiency, in the presence of their Lord. He is their Guardian and Protecting Friend, meaning He will protect, support, and grant them success and safety, in accordance with His promise, because of the righteous deeds they used to perform. Their deeds are not a price that obligates Allah, but rather the means by which His grace and guardianship are attained.

translation: And [mention] the Day He will gather them all together, [and say], "O company of jinn, you have taken many among mankind." And their allies among mankind will say, "Our Lord, we have benefited from one another, and we have reached the term which You appointed for us." He will say, "The Fire is your abode, abiding therein forever, except as Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing."
interpretation: This verse portrays the judgment of rebellious jinn and their human associates as a mutual partnership of exploitation and misguidance. The jinn boast of the many humans they led astray, while the humans who allied with them admit that the relationship served both sides: the jinn gained obedience and influence, and the humans gained worldly desires, false promises, and a false sense of support. At the appointed term of death and resurrection, that partnership collapses, and neither party can shift blame. God's decree consigns them to the Fire, a dwelling that is subject to His sovereign will; the exception 'except as Allah wills' affirms that punishment and duration are entirely under His decree, not independent of Him. Since He is Wise, His judgment is perfectly just, and since He is Knowing, He is fully aware of every hidden intention, act of deception, and degree of responsibility.

translation: And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: Allah decrees that the unjust become close associates and supporters of one another, and that some oppressors are subjected to others, as a consequence of their own evil deeds. Their mutual alliance in wrongdoing is not outside divine decree; it is both a punishment and a natural outcome of their disobedience. Thus they lead one another into sin, are bound together by the same corrupt actions, and will share in the consequences of what they earned.

translation: O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? They will say, 'We bear witness against ourselves.' And the worldly life deluded them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that divine accountability is perfectly just: God did not leave jinn or humans without guidance and warning, but sent messengers from their own ranks so the message would be clear, relevant, and impossible to dismiss as foreign or inaccessible. On the Day of Judgment, those who rejected faith will not be able to claim ignorance or blame God; they will themselves admit that the warnings reached them and that they knowingly turned away. Their confession is the final self-condemnation. The verse also identifies the deeper cause of their ruin: the life of this world deceived them. Its fleeting pleasures, status, and distractions made them prioritize the temporary over the eternal. Thus the real danger is not a lack of divine evidence, but the seduction of dunya, which blinds the heart and leads a person to deny the meeting with God. Ultimately, every soul will either benefit from the messengers' warning or be forced to testify against itself on the Day when no excuse remains.

translation: That is because your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah does not destroy a people for their sins until He has first sent them messengers and warnings, so that they are not caught unaware without excuse. It establishes divine justice: punishment only comes after the truth has been clearly conveyed, and no one is held accountable for what they were never warned about.

translation: And for each there are degrees according to what they did, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every soul receives a rank or station corresponding exactly to its deeds: the obedient rise in degrees of reward, while the disobedient descend in degrees of recompense and punishment. It also affirms that God’s knowledge fully encompasses every action, hidden or open, so no deed is lost, overlooked, or misjudged; everyone will be repaid with perfect justice according to what they actually did.

translation: Your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of Mercy. If He wills, He could take you away and bring after you whatever He wills, just as He brought you into being from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah’s absolute self-sufficiency does not contradict His mercy: He has no need of His creatures, yet He nurtures, warns, and forgives. Human beings are not indispensable before Him; if they persist in rebellion, He can remove them and raise up another creation or community in their place, just as He already originated them from the progeny of earlier peoples. The verse therefore calls the soul to humility, gratitude, and repentance, recognizing that existence, succession, and divine mercy are pure gifts, and that Allah acts with perfect wisdom and unrestricted power.

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is sure to come, and you cannot escape [it].
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute certainty of what Allah has promised—especially the resurrection, reckoning, and recompense—and declares that no one can thwart His decree or escape His grasp. It warns every denier and heedless person that human power, schemes, or resistance cannot render Allah powerless or avert the appointed outcome; His promise is inevitable, and all will be brought before Him for judgment.

translation: Say: 'O my people, act according to your position; indeed, I am acting. Then you will know who will have the outcome of the [final] home. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse is a decisive address to those who reject the Prophet’s message: each party should persist in its chosen course, and time will reveal who truly holds the rightful claim to the final abode. It teaches that the ultimate good end—success in the Hereafter—belongs to those who follow divine guidance, not to those who persist in wrongdoing, injustice, or denial. The command to act according to one’s position is not approval of their ways but a declaration that the Prophet will remain steadfast in his mission, and the outcome will expose the truth. The wrongdoers’ failure is absolute: they will not attain the felicity of the eternal home.

translation: And they assign to Allah a portion of what He created of crops and livestock, and they say, “This is for Allah,” by their claim, “and this is for our partners.” But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches their partners. Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse condemns the polytheists’ fabricated system of dividing God’s own provisions between Him and false deities. Their practice exposes a deeper corruption: they honor and prioritize their idols while depriving God of what they falsely assign to Him, thereby revealing that their allegiance is not truly to God. It establishes that God alone is the Creator, Owner, and rightful recipient of all worship and gratitude, and that humans have no authority to invent religious shares, rituals, or laws that elevate created beings to His level. The verse declares such distorted judgment to be evil because it replaces divine right with self-invented injustice.

translation: And likewise, their partners made the killing of their children appear fair to many of the polytheists, to ruin them and to confuse them in their religion. And if Allah had willed, they would not have done it. So leave them and what they fabricate.
interpretation: This verse condemns a practice in which polytheists were led by their so-called partners—jinn/devils or false deities—to regard killing their own children as acceptable or religiously sanctioned. The purpose was to drive them into ruin and to make their religion obscure and corrupted. It teaches that shirk does not only misdirect belief but can deaden conscience and turn people against their own offspring. At the same time, the verse affirms that nothing escapes Allah’s overarching will; if He had willed, they would not have done it, but their choice remains a test and a cause for accountability. The instruction to “leave them and what they fabricate” means the Prophet should not be consumed by their plots and lies; their falsehood and its consequences are left to Allah’s judgment.

translation: And they said, “These are livestock and crops that are forbidden; none may eat them except those we wish,” by their claim. And there are livestock whose backs are forbidden, and livestock over which they do not mention the name of Allah, inventing lies against Him. He will recompense them for what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of inventing religious laws and prohibitions in God’s name without His authority. The polytheists of pre-Islamic Arabia arbitrarily designated certain animals and crops as sacred or forbidden, restricted who could eat from them, prohibited the use of certain animals’ backs, and slaughtered some animals without invoking God’s name—or invoked names other than His—then falsely attributed these man-made rules to God. The verse teaches that declaring something lawful or unlawful is a divine prerogative, not a matter of human whim, custom, or self-serving claims. Such fabrications against God are serious because they corrupt worship, mislead people, and turn religion into a tool of human control. The closing warning, “He will recompense them for what they used to invent,” affirms that God will hold them accountable for every false teaching and distorted practice they attributed to Him.

translation: And they say, 'What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives; but if it is a dead birth, then they are partners in it.' He will recompense them for their description. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse condemns the polytheists' self-invented rules concerning livestock. They arbitrarily reserved certain unborn animal offspring for men and prohibited women, except if the offspring was stillborn, in which case both shared it. Such distinctions were not from God but were fabrications falsely ascribed to His law. God will repay them for the lies they invent about Him, and His wisdom and knowledge encompass all things, so His judgment and recompense are perfectly just.

translation: Indeed, those who killed their children out of foolishness without knowledge have lost, and they forbade what Allah provided them, inventing a lie against Allah. They have indeed gone astray and were not guided.
interpretation: This verse condemns the pre-Islamic practice of killing children—especially daughters—out of false pride, fear of poverty, or ignorant custom, and it condemns the practice of declaring lawful things forbidden as a man-made religion attributed to Allah. Such people are in utter loss because they violate the sanctity of life, reject Allah’s provision by forbidding what He has made lawful, and fabricate lies about Him. Their actions arise from ignorance and misguidance, not from divine authority. The verse establishes that the right to legislate what is lawful and unlawful belongs to Allah alone, and that those who transgress this by following inherited false taboos or sinful customs remain astray, unable to reach true guidance.

translation: And He it is who produces gardens trellised and untrellised, and the date-palm and crops of varying taste, and the olive and the pomegranate, similar and not similar. Eat of their fruit when they bear fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest, and do not waste. Indeed, He does not like the wasteful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah alone is the Creator and Provider of all cultivated sustenance, and that the diversity of plants, fruits, and tastes is a sign of His power, wisdom, and generosity. Humans are therefore commanded to receive these blessings with gratitude, to give the rightful share owed to the poor and needy at the time of harvest, and to avoid excess, waste, and ingratitude. The prohibition of wastefulness is not merely economic but spiritual: it rejects misuse of Allah’s provisions and arrogance toward His gifts, while the command to give at harvest affirms social justice, charity, and responsible stewardship of the earth’s produce.

translation: And among the grazing livestock are those for carrying burdens and those for other uses. Eat from what Allah has provided you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse teaches that livestock are part of Allah’s provision: some are suited for carrying loads and travel, while others are for milk, meat, wool, and other benefits. People are commanded to eat what Allah has made lawful and good with gratitude, and to avoid Satan’s paths. Satan tries to lead people into either forbidding what Allah has permitted or consuming what He has forbidden, as well as into ingratitude and disobedience. Since he is an open enemy, his suggestions should be rejected and Allah’s commands followed.

translation: Eight pairs: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say, 'Is it the two males He has forbidden, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse is a decisive rhetorical challenge to those who invented prohibitions and attributed them to Allah. By pointing to the male and female of sheep and goats, and to the unborn young in the females' wombs, Allah exposes the inconsistency of their claims: if He had truly forbidden these animals, which exact category would be unlawful—the males, the females, or the fetuses? Since their prohibitions do not follow any coherent divine rule, they are shown to be baseless and falsely ascribed to Allah. The demand to bring knowledge if they are truthful establishes that halal and haram must rest on revealed evidence, not on inherited custom, conjecture, or self-appointed religious authority.

translation: And of the camels two, and of the cattle two. Say, 'Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you? Then who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah to mislead the people without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse confronts the pre-Islamic practice of declaring certain animals lawful or unlawful according to inherited superstitions and arbitrary distinctions of sex or offspring. It demands consistency: if God had truly forbidden camels and cattle, what exactly was forbidden—the males, the females, or what the wombs contain? Their prohibitions were not based on a clear divine command but on conjecture. The question 'were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this?' exposes that they had no direct knowledge or authority for attributing such laws to God. Therefore, the gravest injustice is to fabricate lies about God in order to mislead people without knowledge. Such people persist in wrongdoing, and God does not guide those who choose injustice and false attribution over truth and accountability.

translation: Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden for an eater who eats it, except that it be carrion, or poured-out blood, or swine flesh—for indeed it is impure—or a sinful offering over which other than Allah has been invoked. But whoever is compelled by necessity, neither craving nor transgressing, then indeed your Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the fundamental divine prohibitions concerning food are limited to carrion, flowing blood, pork, and what is slaughtered as a sacrifice to other than Allah. It rejects humanly invented or superstitious prohibitions, affirming that only God has the authority to declare what is unlawful. The fourth category is described as disobedience because it involves dedicating the animal to other than God. The verse then grants a concession under necessity: if a person is forced by hunger or danger of death and does not intentionally seek the forbidden pleasure nor exceed what is necessary to survive, God’s forgiveness and mercy cover the act. Thus the law is not meant to impose unbearable hardship, and necessity is measured by genuine need rather than desire or transgression.

translation: And to those who are Jews, We forbade every animal with claws. And of cattle and sheep, We forbade to them their fat, except what their backs carry, or the entrails, or what is mixed with bone. That is how We recompensed them for their transgression. And indeed, We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that these particular dietary restrictions were imposed specifically on the Jews as a just recompense for their rebelliousness, not as a universal law for all humanity. It teaches that some divine legislation may function as disciplinary punishment for a people’s wrongdoing, while God’s reports about His laws and His dealings with previous communities are absolutely true.

translation: So if they deny you, say, "Your Lord is possessor of vast mercy, but His punishment cannot be averted from the criminal people."
interpretation: This verse teaches that when the Prophet is rejected, he should not respond with despair or vengeance but should announce the truth about God: His mercy is vast, giving people respite, provision, and the opportunity to repent. Yet that same mercy does not cancel accountability. Those who persist in denial, arrogance, and wrongdoing remain subject to God's punitive justice, which cannot be turned back by anyone. Thus mercy invites correction, while justice assures that the unrepentant guilty will not escape consequences.

translation: Those who associate others with Allah will say, “If Allah had willed, we would not have associated others with Him, nor would our forefathers, nor would we have forbidden anything.” Likewise, those before them denied until they tasted Our punishment. Say, “Do you have any knowledge, so that you can produce it for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you are only guessing.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the false excuse of those who justify shirk and self-invented prohibitions by appealing to God’s will. Their argument is not evidence of divine approval; it is mere conjecture. If God’s decree were a valid excuse for disobedience, then earlier nations who used the same claim would not have been punished. God’s will does not cancel human accountability, because He has sent messengers, revealed commands, and distinguished lawful from unlawful. Claiming “if God had willed we would not have done this” while persisting in false worship and arbitrary prohibitions is not knowledge but baseless guessing. The verse therefore summons them to bring real proof, and it establishes that following conjecture cannot replace revealed truth.

translation: Say, 'To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all together.'
interpretation: This verse declares that the final, decisive proof belongs exclusively to God, and no one can overturn or escape it. It means that God’s evidence and authority are complete and irrefutable, leaving no valid excuse for rejecting Him. The statement that He could have guided all people if He willed shows that universal guidance is entirely within His power, but He has not compelled it; rather, He has established clear proofs and messenger guidance so that people may respond freely and be held accountable. Thus the verse affirms God’s absolute sovereignty over guidance while also asserting that His argument against those who deny Him is final and just.

translation: Say, "Bring forward your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this." But if they testify, do not testify with them. And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our verses and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who equate others with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet, and believers after him, to reject false religious claims that are not based on divine revelation. When people assert that God has forbidden something, they must produce true witnesses and clear proof; if their testimony is false or merely follows inherited assumptions and desires, believers must not join them or approve their claim. The verse warns against letting the desires of those who reject God's signs, deny the Hereafter, and associate partners with God shape one's understanding of lawful and unlawful. True religion is defined by God's revelation alone, not by human conjecture, custom, or the authority of false witnesses.

translation: Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden to you: Do not associate anything with Him; and be good to parents; and do not kill your children because of poverty—We provide for you and them; and do not approach immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed; and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. This has He instructed you that you may use reason."
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational moral covenant of tawhid and human dignity. Its prohibitions are not arbitrary taboos but the necessary conditions for a just order: exclusive worship of God grounds all value and loyalty; filial devotion protects the family as the first school of justice; the ban on killing children out of fear of poverty rejects the logic of scarcity and replaces it with trust in God as the sole Provider; the prohibition of approaching both outward and inward indecencies guards the inner life and public society from corruption; and the sanctity of life, qualified only by rightful legal justice, makes human existence inviolable. The closing phrase 'so that you may understand' presents these obligations as rational and knowable, calling people to use the reason God has placed in them to recognize and obey His moral order.

translation: And do not approach the orphan’s property except in the best way, until he reaches his maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not burden a soul beyond its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it is a relative. And fulfill the covenant of Allah. This He has instructed you with, so that you may remember.
interpretation: This verse establishes core moral and legal duties: guarding an orphan’s wealth only for their benefit and never exploiting it before they mature; dealing honestly and fairly in trade by giving full measure and weight; recognizing that God never imposes on anyone more than they can bear; speaking with justice even when the truth concerns a close relative; and honoring every covenant made with God. Together these commands train the believer in trustworthiness, justice, mercy, and faithfulness, so that they remain mindful of God and heed His guidance.

translation: And [know] that this is My straight path, so follow it; and do not follow the [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path. That is what He has commanded you, so that you may attain righteousness.
interpretation: This verse declares that God’s guidance is one straight and undeviating path: the way of pure monotheism and submission to Him as revealed through His prophets. To follow it is to remain united upon His command, while following the many divergent paths—whether of false beliefs, sectarian innovation, egoistic desire, or man-made ideologies—causes people to be torn away from His way. The command is not arbitrary but purposeful: God ordains this so that people may cultivate taqwa, a guarding of oneself against disobedience and a life lived in awareness of and reverence for Him.

translation: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, complete [Our favor] upon the one who did good, and an explanation of all things, and a guidance and a mercy, so that they may believe in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: This means that after sending earlier messengers, God granted Moses the Torah as a perfected revelation and completed His favor upon those who live righteously; it clarifies all that people need for faith and practice, and it serves as guidance and mercy, aiming to bring them to faith in the meeting with their Lord—namely resurrection and accountability—so they may live in accordance with that belief.

translation: And this is a blessed Book which We have sent down, so follow it and fear Allah, so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse identifies the Qur’an as a blessed Book sent down by God, meaning its guidance is a source of good and blessing for those who accept it. It commands people to follow it in belief and action, and to have taqwa—guarding themselves against disobedience and divine displeasure. The promised outcome is God’s mercy: mercy is attained by adhering to His revelation and living with God-consciousness, not merely by claiming faith.

translation: Lest you say, ‘The Book was sent down only upon two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of their study.’
interpretation: This verse removes a false excuse: that divine guidance had been given only to the Jews and Christians, while the Arabs remained ignorant of what those earlier scriptures contained. God therefore sent the Qur’an as a clear, blessed Book in their own language, so that no one could claim that revelation had passed them by or that they had no access to divine instruction. It teaches that ignorance of previous Scriptures cannot justify rejecting the final revelation once it has come, and that God’s mercy is shown in making His guidance plainly available to be studied, understood, and followed.

translation: Or lest you say, "If only the Book had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they." But there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, and guidance and mercy. So who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our signs with the worst punishment because they used to turn away.
interpretation: This verse closes the door on the excuse that guidance was inaccessible or that one would have surpassed earlier recipients had a scripture been given. The coming of the clear proof, guidance, and mercy from God through the Qur'an places the responsibility squarely upon the hearer. To deny God's signs after they have come, and to turn away from them, is the height of injustice because it rejects not ignorance but evidence. The punishment is described as especially severe because it corresponds to a persistent, deliberate turning away: they did not merely fail to find the truth; they refused and diverted themselves from it. Thus the verse establishes that God's justice is exact—no one is blamed for what they never received, but rejecting and turning away from what has clearly arrived brings deserved ruin.

translation: Do they wait only for the angels to come to them, or for your Lord to come, or for some of your Lord’s signs to come? On the Day when some of your Lord’s signs come, no soul’s faith will benefit it if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith. Say, “Wait; indeed, we too are waiting.”
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who postpone faith and righteous action. They are waiting for death, divine judgment, or the major portents of the Hour, but when those decisive signs arrive, the opportunity to choose faith will be over. At that point, faith will not benefit a person who had not already believed, nor will good deeds performed only after the signs appear be accepted as they would have been before. Therefore the verse urges immediate belief and sincere good conduct while there is still time, and it declares that the believers also await Allah’s promise, which will certainly come to pass.

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects — you are not with them in anything. Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This is a severe warning against splitting the religion into factions, partisanship, and competing sects. It declares that the Prophet has no part in the way of those who turn the unified religion into divisions, even if they claim to belong to it. Their judgment is left entirely to Allah, and He will inform them of the reality of their deeds. The verse teaches that sectarian division is not a minor disagreement but a violation of the unity and obedience demanded by the religion, and every group will be held accountable before God for what it did.

translation: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof; and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This establishes God's absolute justice joined with immense mercy: the reward for a good deed is multiplied tenfold as a minimum, while punishment for an evil deed is only its equivalent. No one is treated unjustly; the increase is pure favor, and the limiting of evil's recompense to its own measure is pure justice. Thus the verse encourages hope in divine generosity and warns against sin without ever suggesting that God wrongs anyone.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path: a firmly established religion, the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not one of the polytheists.'
interpretation: This verse declares that true guidance comes from God and leads to one straight, upright path: pure and exclusive worship of Him. That path is identified with the creed of Abraham, who was a hanif—turning away from all falsehood and false gods toward the truth. Abraham’s way was not polytheism, and therefore the religion being affirmed is not a new invention but the restoration and continuation of original Abrahamic monotheism. The verse thus teaches that authentic faith is measured by sincere devotion to God alone, unmixed with any association of partners with Him, and that this is the firmly established religion to which the Prophet and his followers are guided.

translation: Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my sacrificial rites, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of pure and exclusive devotion to God. It teaches that prayer, sacrifice, and every act of worship must be directed to Allah alone, and that one's whole life and death should be lived in His service and for His pleasure. Since He is the Lord and Sustainer of all creation, no created being shares in His lordship or deserves the worship, loyalty, and ultimate purpose that belong to Him alone.

translation: He has no partner. And that is what I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse declares pure monotheism: Allah is absolutely one, with no partner, equal, or associate in His lordship, divinity, or worship. The speaker affirms that this pure devotion and exclusive worship is not a personal choice but a divine command. By saying “I am the first of the Muslims,” he expresses complete, unreserved submission to Allah and signifies that he is foremost among his people in embracing and proclaiming that submission, not that no one before him ever submitted to Allah.

translation: Say, 'Is it other than Allah I should seek as lord, while He is Lord of all things? And every soul earns only against itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that in which you used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet and every believer to declare that no one besides Allah deserves to be taken as lord, because Allah alone is the Lord and Sustainer of all existence. The rhetorical question exposes the irrationality of turning to any other being for lordship. It then establishes personal moral responsibility: each soul's deeds are credited or charged to itself alone. No person can carry the sin or guilt of another, and no one inherits responsibility for another's choices. After death, all return to their Lord, who will judge with perfect knowledge and reveal the truth about the matters over which people disputed, including matters of faith, obedience, and divine guidance. Thus the verse affirms God's exclusive lordship, individual accountability, the reality of resurrection, and God's final authority to resolve all disagreements.

translation: And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees, so that He may test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God alone appoints human beings as successive stewards and generations upon the earth. The differences in rank, wealth, power, knowledge, ability, and provision are not signs of inherent superiority; they are a divine test. Every advantage or disadvantage is a trust through which a person is tried in how they respond: with gratitude or ingratitude, justice or oppression, obedience or rebellion. The warning that God is swift in punishment confronts those who misuse what they have been given, while the declaration that He is Forgiving and Merciful opens the door for repentance, reform, and seeking His pardon. Thus the verse combines accountability with hope, reminding humanity that earthly distinctions are temporary and that true success lies in faithfully using what God has entrusted to us.

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem, Sad.
interpretation: These are among the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'at) at the beginning of Surah Al-A'raf. Their exact meaning is known only to Allah; they serve as a reminder that the Qur'an is composed of the same Arabic letters the disbelievers use, yet they cannot produce anything like it, thus highlighting its miraculous nature and calling people to reflect on its message.

translation: A Book has been sent down to you, so let there be no tightness in your chest because of it, so that you may warn by it, and as a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the revelation is a divine Book whose burden is not meant to constrict his heart with anxiety, doubt, or fear of how people will receive it. He is commanded to deliver its warnings without hesitation, trusting in God. For the believers, it is a source of remembrance, admonition, and strengthening of faith, turning their hearts toward God’s guidance.

translation: Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow besides Him any protectors. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This is a command to make the revelation sent by Allah alone the guide for belief, worship, law, and life, and a prohibition against taking any being, authority, tradition, desire, or leader besides Him as a guardian whose commands are obeyed as if they can guide independently of Him. The ending rebukes heedlessness: people are reminded only rarely, though the right response is constant remembrance and submission to their Lord.

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed, and Our punishment came upon it at night or while they were taking a midday rest.
interpretation: This verse is a warning that divine punishment arrives with suddenness and cannot be escaped. It teaches that those who persist in denial and wrongdoing may be seized by Allah’s judgment during ordinary moments of security and rest—at night or at midday—when they least expect it. The mention of these times emphasizes human heedlessness and the illusion of safety; no period is exempt from Allah’s decree. It affirms Allah’s absolute power, the certainty of accountability, and the necessity of responding to guidance before the decree comes.

translation: So their only plea when Our punishment came upon them was that they said, 'Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse means that when Allah’s punishment finally came, the evildoers had no excuse, argument, or false defense left; all they could do was admit that they had wronged themselves through their disbelief and disobedience. Their confession did not benefit them at that point, because it came only after the punishment had arrived. It shows that divine punishment exposes the truth and silences denial, and that those who reject the truth will ultimately acknowledge their own guilt and Allah’s justice.

translation: Then We will surely question those to whom [messengers] were sent, and We will surely question the messengers.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will hold both the recipients of the divine message and the messengers themselves accountable: the people will be questioned about how they responded to the guidance brought to them, and the messengers will be questioned about whether they faithfully conveyed it. This questioning is not because God lacks knowledge, but to establish perfect justice, leave no excuse, and vindicate the messengers while exposing those who rejected the truth.

translation: Then We will surely recount to them with knowledge, and We were not absent.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will inform every soul of what it did with precise and complete knowledge, because He was never absent from them nor unaware of their actions; nothing escapes His knowledge or record.

translation: And the weighing on that Day will be the truth. Then whoever's scales are heavy — those are the successful.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will judge deeds with absolute truth and justice, weighing them accurately so that no one is wronged. Whose good deeds outweigh his evil deeds will attain success, meaning deliverance from punishment and entry into eternal bliss and divine pleasure.

translation: And whoever's scales are light—those are the ones who have lost their own souls because they used to wrong Our signs.
interpretation: This verse describes the consequence for the one whose good deeds do not weigh heavily in the divine balance on the Day of Judgment. The lightness of the scales is not an arbitrary punishment; it reflects a life in which God's signs were met with rejection, neglect, or distortion. Such a person's ultimate loss is not merely a loss of reward but the loss of the self—its true purpose, dignity, and eternal well-being. The verse thus teaches that injustice toward God's revelations is self-injustice: by refusing to let them guide and shape one's deeds, one empties the scale and ruins the soul.

translation: And We have certainly established you on the earth and provided for you therein means of livelihood. Little are you grateful.
interpretation: Allah reminds humankind that their dwelling, authority, and ability to obtain sustenance from the earth are all His gifts. Every means of living and every capacity to benefit from it comes from Him alone. The rightful response is therefore gratitude, worship, and obedience, yet people often respond with only scant thankfulness.

translation: And We certainly created you, then We fashioned you, then We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' so they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated.
interpretation: This means that God created and formed humankind, then honored Adam by commanding the angels to prostrate before him as an act of obedience to God and recognition of Adam's God-given status, not as worship of Adam; Iblis's refusal was a willful, arrogant disobedience, not a lack of ability, and so he was excluded from the ranks of the obedient.

translation: [Allah] said, “What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?” [Iblis] said, “I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the essence of Iblis’s disobedience: it was not confusion or inability but arrogant self-elevation. Allah’s question establishes that a clear command had been given, so refusal was a deliberate rejection of divine authority. Iblis then justifies his disobedience by claiming superiority based on his created substance, fire over clay. The meaning is that pride blinds a person to truth and leads them to override God’s command with their own reasoning; superiority is not determined by material origin, race, or natural qualities, but by obedience and God’s own decree. Thus the verse condemns the attitude that treats one’s presumed excellence as a license to disobey Allah.

translation: He said, "Then descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant in it. So get out; indeed, you are among the humiliated."
interpretation: This verse records God's sentence upon Iblis after he refused to prostrate to Adam out of pride: he is driven down from the exalted station he occupied and expelled, because arrogance has no place in the realm of divine command. His claim to superiority is exposed as false; the one who exalts himself against God's order is instead brought low. Thus his punishment is both banishment and humiliation, showing that pride before God leads not to honor but to disgrace, and that true elevation comes only through humble submission to Him.

translation: He said: 'Grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: Iblis is asking for a delay of his punishment and death until the Day of Resurrection, not out of remorse but so that he may continue trying to mislead humanity. It reveals his arrogance, defiance, and resolve in enmity, while the respite granted to him becomes a trial and test for people.

translation: He said, “Indeed, you are among those granted respite.”
interpretation: This means that God granted Iblis the delay he requested: his death was postponed and his term extended until the appointed Day, so that he would remain alive to tempt and mislead humanity. It is not a sign of honor or acceptance, but a decree of testing and a postponement of his punishment until the fixed time.

translation: He said, "Because You have caused me to err, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path."
interpretation: Iblis responds with defiance and deceit: he treats Allah’s decree of misguidance as an excuse, then vows to ambush humankind on the path of truth. He cannot force anyone, so he stations himself where people seek guidance—using whispers, false beautification, doubt, and distraction—to turn them away from sincere worship and obedience. The verse exposes his permanent enmity and the danger of following his suggestions instead of seeking Allah’s protection and steadfastness.

translation: Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful.
interpretation: This is Iblis’s vow to besiege humankind from every direction, meaning he will approach them through every avenue of temptation and deception—before them with hopes and worldly desires, behind them with heedlessness and attachment to what is past, and from their right and left with doubts, falsehoods, and corrupt inclinations—so as to turn them away from recognizing God’s favors and from thankfulness and obedience. His aim is that most people will not be grateful to God, but this is his claim and scheme; God’s sincere servants remain protected by His guidance and mercy.

translation: He said: 'Get out of it, disgraced and expelled. Whoever follows you among them — I will surely fill Hell with all of you together.'
interpretation: This is God's address to Iblis after his arrogant refusal to obey the command to prostrate to Adam. 'Get out of it' means expulsion from the elevated state and presence he had occupied, coupled with disgrace and banishment from divine mercy. 'Madh'uman' conveys being blamed, despised, and humiliated; 'mad'huran' conveys being driven away and rejected. The verse then declares that Satan's power is not coercive: only those who freely follow him will share his fate. The warning is that God will fill Hell with Iblis and all his followers together, emphasizing perfect justice and the severity of choosing Satan's path over God's command. It also affirms God's sovereign decree: rebellion leads to expulsion and ruin, while the responsibility for following or rejecting Satan rests upon the accountable creation.

translation: And O Adam, dwell you and your wife in Paradise, and eat from wherever you both wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you both be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This is Allah’s address to Adam and his wife, granting them residence in Paradise and freedom to enjoy its bounties, while imposing one restriction as a test of obedience. The command not to “approach” the tree, rather than only not to eat from it, teaches that one must avoid not only the forbidden act itself but also the steps and inclinations that lead to it. The warning that they would become “among the wrongdoers” means that disobedience would be an injustice against their own souls, bringing loss upon themselves by violating the command of their Lord. Thus the verse establishes that divine favor is accompanied by responsibility, and that free choice is accountable before Allah.

translation: Then Satan whispered to them to reveal to them what was hidden from them of their private parts, and he said, 'Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except that you become angels or become of the immortal.'
interpretation: This verse uncovers the strategy of Iblis: he does not compel but whispers, and he targets the human longing for loftier status and endless life. His lie reframes God's protective prohibition as an arbitrary deprivation, as if the only reason for the command were to keep Adam and Eve from becoming angels or immortals. That false promise is designed to make disobedience look like self-elevation, while its real effect is to expose what God had covered—human shame and vulnerability. The lesson is that Satan's temptation often arrives as a plausible explanation or a promise of a greater good, and that divine limits are not barriers to human dignity but safeguards of it; transgressing them leads not to transcendence but to exposure, loss, and ruin.

translation: And he swore to them both, “Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers.”
interpretation: Iblis reinforced his deception with a solemn oath, presenting his counsel as pure goodwill and sincere concern so that Adam and Eve would trust him and act on his advice. The verse exposes how falsehood can disguise itself in the language of sincerity and how an oath may be misused to lend credibility to misguidance.

translation: So he made them fall through deception. And when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called to them, 'Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?'
interpretation: This verse shows that Satan’s deception works by making disobedience appear desirable and by diminishing the seriousness of God’s command. The exposure of Adam and Eve’s nakedness after eating signifies that sin strips away dignity and brings shame, while their attempt to cover themselves with leaves reflects the innate human awareness of modesty and the need to conceal moral failure. God’s address is a merciful summons to accountability: He reminds them of His prior prohibition and of Satan’s openly declared enmity, so that they might recognize that the real harm came not from the tree itself but from trusting the deceiver over their Lord. The passage thus teaches that transgression begins with heedlessness and deceptive persuasion, but God’s rebuke is meant to awaken repentance and return, not to abandon the sinner.

translation: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse expresses the essence of sincere repentance: the human being recognizes that the wrong done to oneself is real and cannot be undone by excuses or self-justification. True reform begins with owning one’s fault before God, then seeking His forgiveness and mercy as the only means of safety. It teaches that without divine pardon and compassion, a person is left in a state of loss, no matter what other apparent gains they may possess. Thus, humility, confession, and hope in God’s mercy are the path back to Him.

translation: He said, 'Descend, being to one another enemies. And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that earthly life is a temporary stage appointed by God, not the final abode. It declares that human beings will live on earth with mutual enmity and conflict, yet God has made the earth a place of stability and a source of benefit for them until a fixed term. Thus the world is a realm of testing and transient enjoyment, while the ultimate return and reckoning belong to God.

translation: He said, "In it you will live and in it you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."
interpretation: This verse declares that the earth is the appointed dwelling place for human beings in this worldly life: it is where they live, where their bodies die and are buried, and from it they will be raised out of their graves on the Day of Resurrection for judgment. Thus life, death, and resurrection are all tied to the earth as part of God's decree, and it reminds people that their worldly existence is temporary while the return to God and the resurrection are certain.

translation: O children of Adam, We have sent down upon you clothing to cover your private parts and as adornment. But the clothing of righteousness — that is best. That is from the signs of Allah, so that they may remember.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah has provided outward clothing to conceal human shame and to serve as dignity and adornment, but the truest and most valuable covering is taqwa: God-consciousness, moral integrity, and obedience to Him. Physical garments cover the body, yet they are temporary and cannot conceal the inner self before Allah. The garment of taqwa covers the soul, guards it from sin, shame, and degradation, and adorns a person with honor before God and creation. Therefore, while people naturally seek decent and beautiful clothing, they must not neglect the far superior covering of a righteous heart and character. This guidance is among Allah’s signs, calling people to reflect, take heed, and remember their accountability to their Creator.

translation: O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he expelled your parents from the Garden, stripping from them their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you—he and his tribe—from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse warns all humanity against letting Satan deceive them, using the example of Adam and Eve: Satan's enmity led to their removal from Paradise and the exposure of their shame. It teaches that Satan's aim is not merely to cause physical loss but to strip people of modesty, obedience, and divine protection, drawing them toward sin and disgrace. Though Satan and his forces cannot be seen by humans, they observe and whisper from the unseen realm, so believers must remain vigilant through faith, remembrance of God, and adherence to His commands. The final statement explains that Satan's authority as an ally belongs only to those who reject faith; their disbelief leaves them vulnerable to his influence, whereas sincere believers are guarded by God.

translation: And when they commit an immorality, they say, “We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.” Say, “Indeed, Allah does not command immorality. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?”
interpretation: This verse rejects the false reasoning that inherited custom or ancestral practice can make an evil act permissible, and it decisively denies that God would ever command fahishah—any grave indecency, lewdness, or transgression. God’s commands are never directed toward moral corruption; they are wise, just, and intended to purify human conduct. The verse also condemns the arrogance of attributing laws and commandments to God without revealed knowledge, warning that people must not speak about God’s will based on conjecture, tradition, or desire. Thus, neither ancestral precedent nor self-invented religious authority can justify what God has not commanded.

translation: Say, 'My Lord has commanded justice. And set your faces upright at every place of worship, and call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion. As He originated you, you will return.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s command is rooted in justice and equity, and that true worship must be directed to Him alone. Turning one’s face at every masjid means directing one’s prayer and devotion exclusively toward God wherever one worships, refusing to associate any partner with Him. Calling upon Him with sincere religion means that supplication and worship must be purified from hypocrisy, showing off, and polytheism, seeking only His pleasure. The closing statement affirms the resurrection: just as God created human beings in the beginning, He will bring them back after death for judgment, so justice and sincere worship are duties before the One who originates creation and returns it to Himself.
