interpretation: This verse exposes the insincerity of those who only relent under affliction. Their promise to believe was conditional and false; as soon as the punishment was lifted, they reverted to rejection. The respite granted to them until an appointed term was not an acceptance of their repentance but a test and a proof against them, showing that signs and relief do not reform hearts that are resolved to break their covenants with God.

translation: So We took retribution from them and drowned them in the sea, because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse teaches that divine punishment comes as a just consequence of persistently rejecting God’s signs and refusing to heed them. Their drowning was not arbitrary; it was the inevitable outcome of arrogant denial and culpable neglect of clear proofs, showing that no earthly power can escape God’s judgment once His patience ends.

translation: And We caused the people who were being oppressed to inherit the eastern parts of the land and its western parts, which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they were patient. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people used to make and what they used to erect.
interpretation: The verse presents a divine law and a lesson in justice: Allah rescues the weak and oppressed when they endure with patience and trust in Him. Their inheritance of the blessed land is not merely a historical settlement but a sign that Allah's promise to the righteous is certain and that He replaces tyrannical power with those who were wronged. The destruction of Pharaoh's works and structures signifies that the might, monuments, and schemes of arrogant oppressors are ultimately fragile and erased, while patient faith leaves a lasting legacy. It also teaches that worldly power is not the criterion of divine favor; rather, steadfastness upon truth, even under severe persecution, is what earns Allah's help and the fulfillment of His good word.

translation: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, then they came upon a people devoted to idols of theirs. They said, “O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods.” He said, “Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly.”
interpretation: This verse exposes how deliverance from external oppression does not by itself purify the heart’s attachments: a people who had just witnessed God’s power at the sea could still desire a visible, familiar deity modeled on the worship of others. Moses does not treat their request as harmless cultural accommodation or as a need for a ritual symbol; he identifies it as jahl—ignorance that mistakes imitation for devotion and treats the incomparable God as something that can be manufactured, compared, and managed like an idol. The lesson is that true worship cannot be blended with the religious patterns of a surrounding society when those patterns compromise God’s oneness, and that the demand to have “a god like theirs” is already a turning away from the God who alone saves.

translation: Indeed, these [people]—that which they are engaged in is destroyed, and vain is what they used to do.
interpretation: This is a declaration that the idolaters’ religious path and all the works they perform upon it are doomed to ruin and are ultimately worthless, because they are founded on falsehood and directed to other than God. Their apparent devotion cannot save them, and their deeds carry no lasting value or reward.

translation: He said, 'Should I seek for you a god other than Allah, while He has favored you over all the worlds?'
interpretation: This is a rebuke from Moses to the Children of Israel after they asked him to make for them an idol-god like the gods of the people they encountered. He questions how they could seek a deity other than Allah after He had favored them with guidance, miracles, deliverance from Pharaoh, and preference over the peoples of their time. The verse affirms that worship belongs to Allah alone and warns against exchanging His favor for ingratitude and idolatry.

translation: And [recall] when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Children of Israel of His favor in delivering them from Pharaoh's oppressive rule, which subjected them to the worst kind of persecution: killing their newborn sons and keeping their women alive for humiliation and servitude. This oppression was a severe trial from their Lord, testing their patience and faith, and His rescue of them was therefore a manifest blessing and a lesson for those who reflect.

translation: And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was completed in forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron: Take my place among my people, and do right, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God prepared Moses for the revelation of the Torah through an appointed period of forty nights, showing that divine guidance is received through preparation, obedience, and nearness to God. Moses’ appointment of Aaron as his deputy over the Children of Israel indicates that leadership and spiritual responsibility must be entrusted with care during absence. His command to Aaron to set things right and not follow the path of the corrupters teaches that a leader’s duty is to reform, uphold justice and uprightness, and refuse any alliance with those who spread corruption, even when the foremost prophet is temporarily away.

translation: And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, “My Lord, show me, that I may look at You.” He said, “You will not see Me, but look at the mountain: if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me.” So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell unconscious. Then when he recovered, he said, “Glory be to You! I turn to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers.”
interpretation: This verse teaches the absolute transcendence and majesty of God and the incapacity of human beings to see or encompass Him in this worldly life. Moses, despite his closeness to God and his having been spoken to by Him, is moved by longing to ask for direct vision. God’s answer, “You will not see Me,” is a decisive declaration that unveiled vision of God is beyond mortal capacity; it does not imply any deficiency in God but rather the limitation of created faculties before His infinite being. The mountain is given as a sign: if it could remain stable under God’s manifestation, Moses could see, but when God manifested Himself to it, it was crushed to dust and Moses fell unconscious. This shows that direct divine self-disclosure overwhelms all created things. When Moses awakens, he glorifies God, repents for the boldness of his request, and declares himself the first of the believers—first in his time to submit to God’s incomparability and to acknowledge that He cannot be grasped by human sight. The passage thus calls for humility, awe, and repentance before God, and it affirms that faith, not sensory sight, is the proper response to God’s transcendent majesty.

translation: He said: O Moses, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech. So take what I have given you and be among the thankful.
interpretation: This verse conveys that Allah singled out Moses by entrusting him with prophethood and by speaking to him directly, a rank that placed him above the people of his time in these particular honors. It then instructs him to receive what Allah has given him—the revelation, guidance, and miraculous signs—with firm acceptance, obedience, and gratitude. Gratitude here is not merely verbal thanks but using the bestowed favor in the way the Giver intended, remaining humble, and not letting such a high station lead to pride or neglect of the command.

translation: And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of all things — instruction and explanation for all things, [saying], 'Take them with determination and order your people to take the best of them. I will show you the home of the defiantly disobedient.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that the revelation given to Musa was comprehensive: the Tablets contained admonition sufficient to deter people from evil and detailed clarification of the laws, truths, and rulings needed for guidance. The command to 'take them with strength' means to receive and implement the revelation with resolve, seriousness, and unwavering commitment, not with neglect or half-heartedness. Ordering his people to 'take the best of them' means they were to adhere to the most excellent and virtuous of its commands, or to implement its teachings in the best and most complete manner. The warning 'I will show you the home of the defiantly disobedient' is a severe threat: those who reject or neglect these teachings will be made to see the dwelling place and ultimate fate of the corrupt — either the ruined abodes of past nations as a lesson in this world, or the Fire in the Hereafter. Thus the verse teaches that divine guidance is not merely to be acknowledged but obeyed firmly, and that refusal brings inevitable and visible consequences.

translation: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant in the land without right. And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the way of guidance, they will not take it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse means that unjust arrogance blocks a person from benefiting from God’s signs and guidance. When someone exalts himself over the truth and refuses humility before God, his heart becomes veiled, so even the clearest proofs fail to bring him to faith. His rejection is not due to a lack of evidence but due to persistent denial and heedlessness. As a result, his moral perception becomes inverted: he avoids the path of right guidance and chooses the path of deviation. The verse thus teaches that guidance is received through humble submission and attentive remembrance, while arrogance and negligence lead to spiritual blindness and ruin.

translation: And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter—their deeds have become worthless. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: The verse means that rejecting Allah’s revelations and denying the meeting with Him in the Hereafter strips a person’s deeds of all value before Allah. Such deeds cannot earn reward, because acceptance depends on faith in the One to whom the deed is offered and in final accountability. The rhetorical question declares that their recompense is strictly according to what they actually did: deeds performed in denial and heedlessness, so they will face the just consequence of their own conduct, not any reward for apparent good that was without faith.

translation: And the people of Moses, after him, took from their ornaments a calf, a body with a lowing sound. Did they not see that it did not speak to them nor guide them to a way? They took it, and they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse condemns the Israelites’ turning to a fabricated idol immediately after Moses’ departure. The golden calf could make a sound, but it could not speak, respond, or guide anyone to truth. Their worship of it was therefore an act of profound moral and spiritual wrongdoing: they exchanged the living guidance of God for a dead object shaped by their own hands. The verse teaches that anything taken as an object of worship besides God is exposed by its inability to guide, hear, or help, and that abandoning divine guidance for man-made substitutes is both irrational and unjust.

translation: And when they fell into remorse and saw that they had gone astray, they said, 'If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment of awakened conscience: after the sin of worshipping the calf, the Children of Israel recognized their deviation not merely as a mistake but as a ruinous loss of guidance. Their repentance is expressed through humility, self-accusation, and desperate reliance on Allah alone. They admit that no effort, apology, or regret can save them unless Allah grants mercy and forgiveness, for forgiveness is His prerogative, not something earned by human deserving. The verse teaches that true repentance begins with seeing one's sin as straying, feeling remorse in the heart, and turning to Allah with the acknowledgment that without His mercy one is among the losers. It also shows that fear and hope meet in sincere repentance: fear of being lost, and hope in Allah's mercy and forgiveness.

translation: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, 'Wretched is what you have done in my place after me. Did you hasten the command of your Lord?' And he cast down the tablets and seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. He said, 'O son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and were about to kill me; so do not let the enemies gloat over me, and do not place me among the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: Moses's anger is prophetic zeal for God's exclusive worship and grief over Israel's betrayal of the covenant; casting the tablets expresses the severity of their sin against the revealed law, not contempt for revelation. His rough handling of Aaron shows how leadership is answerable for the community's state, yet Aaron's plea reveals that a leader can be overpowered by a rebellious crowd and must not be counted among the unjust. The passage warns against rushing ahead of God's command, following false worship, and letting internal failure become a cause for enemies' mockery; it teaches collective accountability, mercy toward those who did their duty, and the need to align with God's faithful command rather than with wrongdoing.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: This supplication expresses profound humility and reliance upon God: even a prophet seeks forgiveness, showing that no one is beyond the need for divine pardon. Including his brother in the prayer teaches that a believer should seek good not only for himself but also for others, especially family and fellow believers. Asking to be admitted into God's mercy means requesting His encompassing grace, protection, forgiveness, and ultimate salvation. The closing acknowledgment that God is the most merciful of the merciful affirms that all mercy is derived from Him and that His compassion is infinite, surpassing every form of human mercy.

translation: Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will incur wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world. And thus do We recompense those who invent falsehood.
interpretation: This means that the Israelites who adopted the calf as an object of worship during Moses’ absence were struck with God’s anger and disgrace in this worldly life; and God recompenses all who fabricate lies against Him—by inventing false gods, false doctrines, or false claims about Him—with a similar punishment of wrath and humiliation.

translation: And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed — indeed, your Lord, after that, is surely Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah’s forgiveness and mercy are not closed off to those who have fallen into sin; rather, whoever commits evil deeds and then turns back to Him with genuine repentance and faith will find Him Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful. The phrase “after that” emphasizes that even after serious wrongs, sincere repentance and belief erase despair and open the door to divine pardon, showing that Allah’s mercy prevails over His wrath for those who return to Him.

translation: And when the anger of Moses subsided, he took up the tablets, and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord.
interpretation: This verse concludes the aftermath of the golden calf incident. Moses’ anger was a righteous indignation for God’s sake; once it calmed, he retrieved the tablets he had cast down, showing that divine revelation and the path of repentance were not withdrawn. The tablets contained guidance and mercy—guidance to truth and mercy for those who heed it—but this benefit is specifically for “those who fear their Lord,” meaning those who hold God in reverent awe, take His commands seriously, and seek to avoid His displeasure. Thus the verse teaches that revelation becomes a source of guidance and mercy according to the heart’s readiness: it guides and shows compassion to the God-fearing, while also demonstrating that even a prophet’s intense anger passes and God’s mercy remains available to those who return to Him.

translation: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment. Then when the earthquake seized them, he said, “My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me [too]. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did? It is only Your trial by which You cause to stray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of forgivers.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that divine testing can overtake even a chosen group, and that the proper response to calamity is humble intercession and repentance, not self-justification. Moses acknowledges that God’s will is absolute: had He willed, He could have destroyed them earlier, and He alone decides whom to guide and whom to leave astray through trials. Moses does not claim exemption from accountability; he appeals to God as the sole protector and guardian, seeking forgiveness and mercy for himself and his people. The verse thus affirms that leadership requires turning to God in complete reliance, especially when the consequences of a community’s foolishness bring danger, and it rests hope in God’s attribute as the best of forgivers.

translation: And ordain for us good in this world and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. He said, “My punishment — I afflict with it whom I will; and My mercy encompasses all things. So I will ordain it for those who fear Me, give zakah, and those who believe in Our signs.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s mercy is vast and all-encompassing in His creation and worldly provision, but the special mercy that leads to ultimate good and reward in the Hereafter is decreed for those who combine God-consciousness and avoidance of sin, charitable giving and purification through zakah, and sincere faith in God’s revealed signs. It also shows that divine punishment and mercy are governed by God’s will and wisdom; a servant should not presume upon mercy while neglecting the conditions of faith and righteousness. The plea “we have turned to You” expresses repentance and reliance, and God’s answer directs the seeker to the path by which His mercy is attained: piety, purifying charity, and firm belief.

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find described in the Torah and the Gospel with them. He commands them to do what is right and forbids them from what is wrong; he makes lawful for them the good things and makes unlawful for them the bad things; and he relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honor him, support him, and follow the light that was sent down with him — it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse presents the final prophetic mission as the fulfillment of earlier scripture: the sign of the true Prophet is not merely prediction but moral and spiritual liberation. The 'good things' and 'bad things' are not arbitrary categories but correspond to what purifies or corrupts human nature, so his law restores balance rather than adding oppressive restrictions. The burdens and shackles symbolize the accumulated legalisms, corrupt interpretations, and despair-heavy obligations that had come to weigh on earlier religious communities; the Prophet's coming removes these by returning them to a clear, merciful monotheism. Success therefore depends on a total response — belief, reverence, practical support, and following the revealed light — because the light is the criterion by which the community is guided into true prosperity in this life and the next.

translation: Say, 'O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all—[the One] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death.' So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him so that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Muhammad's messengership is universal, addressed to all people, because it is issued by Allah, the sole sovereign of the heavens and earth, the only God, who alone gives life and causes death. Therefore, true guidance requires faith in Allah and in His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet—meaning the one who did not acquire prophethood through human learning or prior scripture, but through divine revelation. His faith in Allah and His revealed words is a mark of his truthfulness. Following him in belief and obedience is the divinely appointed path to guidance.

translation: And among the people of Moses there is a community who guide by the truth and act justly by it.
interpretation: This verse affirms that within the descendants of Moses, despite the deviations and corruption that arose among many of them, there remained a faithful group who upheld divine truth, guided others by it, and established justice according to it. It shows that God's guidance is never wholly absent from any people, and that a righteous remnant may preserve and apply the revealed truth with fairness and integrity.

translation: And We divided them into twelve tribes [as] nations. And We inspired Moses when his people asked him for water, [saying], 'Strike with your staff the stone.' Then there gushed forth from it twelve springs. Each people knew its drinking place. And We shaded them with the clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails, [saying], 'Eat from the good things We have provided you.' And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse recounts Allah's favors to the Children of Israel and reveals a principle about disobedience: divine blessings are precise, sufficient, and meant to lead people to gratitude and obedience. When they rejected these favors and wronged the messengers, they did not harm Allah in any way; the harm of sin returns to the sinners themselves. Thus ingratitude and rebellion do not diminish God but corrupt and damage the human soul.

translation: And [mention] when it was said to them, 'Dwell in this city and eat from it wherever you wish, and say, "Hittah" (we seek the removal of our sins), and enter the gate bowing down; We will forgive you your sins. We will increase the doers of good.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that God's forgiveness and favor are secured through humility, repentance, and obedience. The command to say 'Hittah'—a plea for the removal of sins—shows that sincere acknowledgment of one's wrongs opens the door to divine pardon. Entering the gate in prostration symbolizes casting off pride and approaching God with submissive reverence. Eating freely from the city's provision indicates that God's gifts are to be received with gratitude and within His command. The promise 'We will forgive you your sins' reveals God's readiness to pardon those who turn to Him, while 'We will increase the doers of good' establishes that righteous conduct brings an increase of reward and blessing. Thus the verse presents a principle: humility and repentance attract mercy, and goodness attracts divine increase.

translation: Then those who were unjust among them changed the saying to other than what had been said to them, so We sent upon them a torment from the heaven because they were doing injustice.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Children of Israel who, when commanded to enter the city in humility and to utter a specific word seeking God's forgiveness, deliberately replaced that word with a mocking distortion. Their offense was not a minor slip of speech but a defiant alteration of God's command, revealing arrogance and contempt for revelation. The punishment from heaven was a fitting recompense: because they corrupted with their tongues a word that had come down from above, God sent down upon them a chastisement from above. The verse teaches that tampering with divine instructions out of pride or mockery brings severe consequences, and that God's justice does not overlook persistent wrongdoing.

translation: And ask them about the town that was situated by the sea, when they transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath: when their fish came to them on the Sabbath day, visibly, but on the day they did not keep Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus We tested them because they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet to remind the Children of Israel of a coastal town whose people were tested by God: on the Sabbath, fish appeared in abundance, but on other days they were absent. Their test was whether they would obey God's command to honor the Sabbath or use trickery to catch fish anyway. Their violation showed that they treated God's law as something to circumvent for worldly gain. The verse teaches that God tries people through blessings and restrictions, and that true obedience is shown when one submits to God's command even when desire and opportunity coincide. It also warns against legalistic evasion and persistence in disobedience.

translation: And [recall] when a community among them said, “Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy, or punish with a severe punishment?” They said, “As an excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they may fear [Allah].”
interpretation: This verse teaches that enjoining good and forbidding evil is an obligation that must be fulfilled even when the outcome is uncertain or when a people seem bent on destruction. The admonishers did not preach in order to guarantee immediate reform, nor because they expected the transgressors to inevitably escape punishment; rather, they preached so that they would have a valid excuse before their Lord—that is, they would be cleared of negligence in delivering His warning. At the same time, they left the final judgment to Allah and hoped that the warning might still awaken the people to repentance and God-consciousness. Thus, the believer’s duty is to convey the truth with sincerity, while guidance and punishment remain entirely in Allah’s hands.

translation: So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment because they used to disobey.
interpretation: This verse declares that once a people abandon the divine warnings and reminders they were given, thereby persisting in wrongdoing, God distinguishes between the corrupt and those who at least uphold the duty of forbidding evil. The latter are delivered, while the wrongdoers are overtaken by a severe, humiliating punishment as a just consequence of their continued rebellion and defiance.

translation: So when they insolently transgressed against what they had been forbidden, We said to them, 'Be despised apes.'
interpretation: This is a declaration of divine punishment for a people who knowingly and defiantly violated God's command after repeatedly being warned. Their transformation into apes was a literal, humiliating degradation, expressing that those who persist in rebellion against divine limits may be stripped of their human dignity and made an example of disgrace, cut off from God's mercy and subjected to His contempt.

translation: And [mention] when your Lord declared that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would inflict upon them the worst punishment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This is a decree concerning the Children of Israel: because of their repeated transgressions and breaking of the covenant, God will continue to raise up oppressors over them until the Day of Judgment, causing them severe suffering. Yet the verse also declares that God's punishment is swift for those who persist in wrongdoing, while His forgiveness and mercy remain open to those who repent and return to Him. It is a warning against arrogance and corruption, and a call to hope in God's mercy.

translation: And We divided them throughout the earth as nations. Among them are the righteous, and among them are those less than that. And We tested them with good things and bad things, so that they might return.
interpretation: This verse states that Allah dispersed the Children of Israel across the earth as separate communities, and that they were not all of one moral level: some were righteous, while others fell short of that standard. Their scattering and their differing conditions were part of a divine test. Allah tried them both with blessings and ease and with hardships and adversity, not to destroy them arbitrarily, but so that they might turn back to Him, repent from disobedience, show gratitude in prosperity, and remain patient and reform in adversity. The verse teaches that both good and bad circumstances are means of testing and reminders intended to bring people back to obedience and guidance.

translation: Then there succeeded them successors who inherited the Scripture: they take the fleeting goods of this lower life and say, 'It will be forgiven us.' And if there comes to them goods the like thereof, they take it. Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them that they should not say about Allah except the truth, and they studied what was in it? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse exposes a people who inherited the Book but treated it as a cover for worldly acquisition: they seize whatever passing gain appears, console themselves with the presumption of forgiveness, and repeat the offense whenever similar profit returns. Their covenant with God obligated them to speak only the truth about Him and to live by what they had studied, yet they violated that covenant. The verse thus rejects using religion to justify desire and false hope, and it calls the mind to judge rightly: the eternal home is better for the God-conscious than any illicit or compromised worldly gain. It affirms that inheriting sacred knowledge increases responsibility, not privilege; that divine forgiveness is not a license for persistence in sin; and that true success belongs to those who restrain themselves out of taqwa.

translation: And those who hold firmly to the Book and establish prayer—indeed, We do not let the reward of the reformers be lost.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God preserves and fully rewards the efforts of those who cling faithfully to His revealed Scripture, live by its guidance, and establish prayer as a constant act of worship and obedience. Their striving is not merely private devotion; it is part of setting things right in themselves and in the world. God’s promise here is that such sincere reform rooted in revelation and prayer will never be wasted or overlooked, for He is just and never diminishes the reward of those who work righteousness and repair what is broken.

translation: And when We raised the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them, [We said], 'Take what We have given you with firmness, and remember what is in it, so that you may be mindful of God.'
interpretation: This verse recounts the awe-inspiring sign given to the Children of Israel at Mount Sinai: the mountain was lifted above them like a covering, and they were certain it would collapse upon them. This was a powerful lesson that divine revelation is not to be received lightly or half-heartedly. The command “Take what We have given you with strength” means to accept God’s scripture and commandments with serious resolve, sincerity, and steadfast obedience. “Remember what is in it” means to keep its teachings present in mind and practice, reflecting on its commands, prohibitions, warnings, and guidance. The purpose “so that you may be mindful of God” shows that firm adherence to revelation and constant remembrance of it produce taqwa—guarding oneself against disobedience and living in awareness of God’s presence. Thus the verse teaches that fear of God’s power should lead to wholehearted commitment to His guidance, and that revelation is a trust to be upheld with strength and remembrance.

translation: And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."
interpretation: This verse establishes the primordial covenant in which God brought forth all of Adam’s future descendants and made them acknowledge His exclusive Lordship. Their affirmative response, “Yes,” is a testimony embedded in the very constitution of the human soul, meaning every person possesses an innate inclination to recognize God as Creator and Lord. This covenant stands as decisive evidence against humanity, removing any excuse of ignorance on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore, turning away from tawhid is not merely an intellectual error but a violation of one’s own primordial witness, and human accountability rests upon this direct, though ordinarily unremembered, acknowledgment of God’s sovereignty.

translation: Or [lest] you say, 'Our fathers only associated others [with Allah] before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?'
interpretation: This verse exposes a second excuse people might offer on the Day of Resurrection: that they merely inherited shirk from their ancestors and were born into it. Such an excuse is invalid. Allah had already taken from every soul the covenant of His lordship and endowed them with the innate recognition of Tawhid, and He sent messengers and revealed books, so no one is punished merely for the sins of forebears. Each person is accountable for his own choice. The plea “will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?” is rejected because by following the falsifiers’ way after reaching responsibility, they made those deeds their own. Thus the verse establishes individual moral responsibility and cuts off the argument of blind imitation in matters of faith.

translation: And thus do We explain the verses in detail, so that they may return.
interpretation: Allah clarifies His signs and spells out His revelations in this manner so that people may come back to the truth, abandon disbelief and falsehood, and turn to their Lord in repentance and obedience.

translation: And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan followed him, and he became one of the astray.
interpretation: This verse warns that receiving divine guidance is a trust and a test: if a person knowingly turns away from the signs of God after having understood them, that deliberate detachment opens the door for Satan to gain influence over him. His becoming one of the astray is not an arbitrary punishment but the natural result of choosing ingratitude and abandoning the light he was given, showing that knowledge and blessings without faithful adherence can lead to ruin.

translation: And if We had willed, We would have raised him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his desire. So his example is like that of a dog: if you drive him away, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories, so that they may reflect.
interpretation: This verse teaches that divine elevation through revealed knowledge depends on free choice and is not granted to one who abandons it for worldly attachment and selfish desire. The dog simile portrays a soul driven by insatiable craving and restlessness: whether it is warned or left alone, it remains trapped in the same lowly state because guidance no longer affects it. Such is the condition of those who reject God's signs—they persist in heedlessness regardless of admonition. The command to recount these accounts is a call to awaken reflection and to avoid the fate of the one who sells his higher purpose for the earth.

translation: Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs, and they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who reject God’s signs make themselves an ugly and warning example, not because God’s signs are defective, but because their denial corrupts their own selves. Their wrongdoing is reflexive: they wrong no one but themselves, cutting themselves off from guidance, truth, and mercy. God is not harmed by their rejection; they harm their own souls and bring about their own loss. The verse thus teaches divine justice—punishment and ruin follow from their own chosen disbelief—and serves as a caution that rejecting revelation turns a person into a lesson for others rather than a recipient of light.

translation: Whoever Allah guides, he is the rightly guided; and whoever He sends astray, those are the losers.
interpretation: True guidance comes only from Allah; the one whom He guides to the straight path is the truly guided, while those whom He leaves in misguidance, because of their own rejection and turning away, are the ones who lose themselves and their share of good in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And indeed We have created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like cattle; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse declares that many jinn and humans are destined for Hell because of their own persistent rejection of the truth, not because they were deprived of the faculties needed to know it. God has given them hearts, eyes, and ears, but they do not use them for the purpose for which they were created: to understand divine realities, to see the signs of God, and to hear His revelation and admonition. Their hearts are closed to comprehension, their eyes blind to spiritual evidence, and their ears deaf to guidance. As a result, they descend to the level of grazing cattle, driven by appetite and immediate desire without higher moral or spiritual discernment. Yet the verse states that they are even more astray than animals: animals follow instinct and are not morally accountable, while these people possess reason, revelation, and warning, but still choose ignorance and heedlessness. Thus they are the heedless ones, unconcerned with God, the Hereafter, and the true purpose of their existence.

translation: And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every name of perfection and beauty belongs exclusively to Allah, and He alone is to be invoked through them. Calling upon Him by His names means directing worship, supplication, hope, and fear to Him alone, seeking Him through the attribute that fits one’s need, such as mercy, forgiveness, provision, or protection. The command to leave those who commit ilhad concerning His names warns against any distortion of them—whether by denying them, emptying them of their true meaning, interpreting them falsely, likening Allah to His creation, or using them in ways that oppose His majesty. Such deviation is not overlooked; those who persist in it will be repaid according to their deeds, for Allah’s names are not mere labels but truths that demand reverence, correct understanding, and sincere worship.

translation: And among those We created is a community that guides by the truth and establishes justice thereby.
interpretation: This verse affirms that within humanity God has preserved a group who adhere to His revealed truth, direct others toward it, and judge their affairs with justice according to it. They are not merely recipients of guidance but active guides, making the truth the standard for belief and conduct and establishing equity by it.

translation: And those who deny Our signs — We will gradually draw them [to ruin] from where they do not know.
interpretation: This verse means that those who reject God's revelations are not always seized immediately; rather, God may let them continue in ease, health, wealth, and success, so that they become more deeply entrenched in denial and sin. They misinterpret this delay and these favors as acceptance or good fortune, unaware that it is a gradual entrapment: each blessing they misuse and each day of respite increases their accountability and draws them closer to a sudden punishment they never anticipated. Thus, the very things they enjoy become the means of their being taken step by step toward destruction from a direction they do not perceive.

translation: And I will grant them respite. Indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: This is a divine warning that God may extend the time and worldly ease of those who persist in denial and wrongdoing, but such delay is not approval or neglect. It is part of His unbreakable decree and wise plan, allowing them to continue until the appointed punishment overtakes them suddenly, when no escape or defense will avail. God's plan is firm and cannot be resisted, altered, or thwarted.

translation: Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion. He is only a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse calls the disbelievers to reflect deeply on the Prophet Muhammad, whom they knew well as their trustworthy companion. It denies the accusation that he was possessed by jinn or afflicted with madness. His message was not the product of a disturbed mind; it was a clear warning from God. By pointing to the Prophet’s soundness and the clarity of his call, the verse removes any excuse for rejecting him and urges them to recognize the truth he brought.

translation: Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and whatever things Allah has created, and that it may be that their appointed term has drawn near? Then in what message after this will they believe?
interpretation: This verse summons people to reflect deeply on the vast dominion and orderly creation of the heavens and earth, for such reflection exposes Allah's absolute power, wisdom, and sole right to be worshiped. It also presses upon them the nearness of their own death and the end of their opportunity to respond, warning that heedlessness is dangerous because no one knows when their term will close. The final rhetorical question censures those who reject the Qur'an despite its clear signs: if they will not believe in this final and most complete divine message, then what message or proof could possibly move them to faith? Thus the verse combines a call to contemplate creation, an urgent reminder of accountability, and a severe rebuke of willful disbelief.

translation: Whoever Allah sends astray, there is no guide for him; and He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse declares that true guidance is solely in Allah’s hand. Those whom He leaves astray because of their persistent rejection of truth cannot be guided by any created being. Their being left in transgression means they remain heedlessly immersed in their own arrogance and rebellion, unable to find the right path, wandering in confusion and spiritual blindness.

translation: They ask you about the Hour, when is its arrival. Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None shall reveal it at its time except Him. It is heavy in the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except suddenly." They ask you as if you were well-acquainted with it. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know."
interpretation: The exact timing of the Final Hour is an exclusive divine secret, beyond the knowledge of any prophet, angel, or human. To press for its date is to seek what God has deliberately withheld; the faithful response is to affirm that its appointed time rests solely with Him. Its “heaviness” signifies the overwhelming cosmic magnitude and moral weight of that event for all creation, and its sudden arrival means no one can prepare for it through calculated timing, only through readiness of faith and deeds. The repetition that knowledge belongs to Allah and that most people do not know critiques the human tendency to fixate on timing while neglecting accountability: true knowledge is not knowing the date but living in heedful awareness that it will certainly come.

translation: Say, 'I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm, except what Allah wills. And if I had known the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no evil would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.'
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to declare that he has no independent power over benefit or harm; all that occurs is by Allah's will. The conditional statement about knowing the unseen expresses that such knowledge belongs to Allah alone, and if the Prophet had it he would have used it to attain every good and repel every evil. His role is therefore not to control outcomes or disclose hidden knowledge, but to convey Allah's warning and glad tidings. The verse establishes pure monotheism, the human servitude of the Messenger, and the necessity of faith for receiving the message's warning and good news.

translation: He is the One who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate, that he might find tranquility in her. Then when he covered her, she conceived a light burden and went about with it. Then when it grew heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord: 'If You give us a righteous child, we will surely be among the grateful.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that marriage, intimacy, pregnancy, and the longing for righteous offspring are all rooted in God’s original creative order. The single soul signifies the shared human origin and equal dependence of male and female on their Creator, while the mate is given as a source of calm and companionship. The movement from a light burden to a heavy one marks the hidden growth of life under God’s care. At the moment of greatest need, the parents instinctively turn to their Lord and pledge gratitude for a sound, righteous child. Their vow shows that a blessed child is not merely a biological event but a trust requiring thankfulness; yet human beings often remember God in distress and then forget or compromise their devotion once the blessing arrives. Thus the verse calls for pure gratitude and faithful remembrance in family life.

translation: But when He gave them a righteous child, they ascribed partners to Him in what He had given them. Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse condemns the sin of shirk in the blessing of offspring: after Allah grants a couple a healthy child, they—or those among their descendants—associate partners with Allah in the gift He bestowed, crediting others alongside Him or dedicating the child to false deities. It declares that Allah is far exalted above any partners they set up with Him, and that all blessings, including children, come from Him alone.

translation: Do they associate with Allah those who create nothing, while they themselves are created?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical condemnation of shirk: the false deities and idols they set up as partners with Allah possess no creative power whatsoever, because they are themselves created and entirely dependent. True divinity belongs only to the One who originates and creates all things, so worship and absolute allegiance must be directed to Him alone.

translation: And they cannot give them any help, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse exposes the utter helplessness of the false deities that are worshipped besides Allah: they are unable to assist their worshippers in any way, nor can they even protect or benefit themselves. It shows that anything created and dependent cannot deserve divine worship, since true power, help, and harm belong to Allah alone.

translation: And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or remain silent.
interpretation: This verse exposes the utter helplessness of the false deities that the polytheists worship besides Allah. They are not living, knowing, or capable beings who can hear, respond, or guide anyone. Therefore, whether one invites them to guidance or stays silent makes no difference: they cannot follow, answer, or benefit anyone. The verse rebukes the futility of relying on idols and affirms that guidance, help, and response belong to Allah alone.

translation: Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah are servants like yourselves. So invoke them and let them respond to you, if you are truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a decisive argument against associating partners with Allah. It states that the so-called gods invoked besides Allah are merely created servants like human beings, lacking any divine power to hear, benefit, harm, or answer. The command to call upon them is a challenge to the idolaters: if their claim that these beings are gods worthy of worship is true, they should prove it by getting an answer. Their inability to respond exposes the falsehood of their worship and confirms that true supplication and worship belong to Allah alone.

translation: Do they have feet with which to walk, or hands with which to grasp, or eyes with which to see, or ears with which to hear? Say, “Call upon your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite.”
interpretation: This verse is a decisive Qur’anic argument against associating partners with Allah. It exposes the utter helplessness of false deities: they have no legs to move, no hands to act, no eyes to see, and no ears to hear. They cannot benefit or harm, create or provide, answer prayer or defend themselves. Therefore, relying on them or fearing them is irrational. The Prophet is then commanded to challenge the idolaters and their alleged partners to gather all their forces and scheme against him without delay, because he trusts completely in Allah’s protection and knows that false gods have no power whatsoever. The verse establishes that absolute power, knowledge, perception, and action belong to Allah alone, and every object of worship besides Him is utterly incapable and dependent.

translation: Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book; and He takes care of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse declares that true guardianship, help, and protection belong exclusively to Allah, the One who revealed the Scripture. Because He sent down the Book and Himself undertakes the care of the righteous, reliance must be placed in Him alone; whoever follows His guidance enters under His providential protection, and no other claimed protector can rival His care.

translation: And those whom you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse establishes that any being or object invoked besides Allah is utterly powerless: it can neither bring benefit to its worshippers nor ward off harm from them, nor can it even benefit or protect itself. Therefore, turning to such false objects of worship for aid is futile, and all true reliance and supplication belong to Allah alone.

translation: And if you call them to guidance, they will not hear. And you see them looking at you, but they do not see.
interpretation: This verse exposes the utter incapacity of false deities and all that is worshipped besides God: they cannot hear a call to guidance, nor can their apparent attention or gaze benefit anyone, because they possess no real perception or power. It also warns that those who persist in turning away from divine guidance resemble such lifeless objects—outwardly facing the truth, yet inwardly blind and unable to receive it—so true hearing and sight come only from God.

translation: Take to forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet and the believers to adopt a generous and forbearing moral character: to pardon people’s faults, not insist on retaliation or exacting redress, and to make dealings easy rather than harsh. It further commands them to encourage and command what is universally recognized as good, decent, and just, and to avoid engaging with those who behave ignorantly or provoke with abuse. Turning away from the ignorant is not surrender to falsehood but a refusal to lower oneself to futile argument and sinful reaction, preserving one’s dignity and focusing on what is right.

translation: And if an evil suggestion from Satan stirs you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: When Satan provokes you with a whisper, impulse, or stirring toward anger, sin, or heedlessness, do not yield to it or try to overcome it by your own strength; instead turn immediately to Allah and seek His protection. He hears your plea and knows your condition, so He is fully able to guard you from the harm and deception of Satan.

translation: Indeed, those who fear Allah — when a visitation from Satan touches them, they remember, and at once they see clearly.
interpretation: The God-conscious are not people who never experience Satanic prompting; rather, when a whisper, impulse, or provocation from Satan reaches them, they immediately bring Allah to mind and turn back to Him. This remembrance restores their spiritual insight, so they recognize the deception, distinguish truth from falsehood, and return to the right path. The verse teaches that taqwa is shown not by never being touched by temptation, but by swift awareness, repentance, and renewed clarity.

translation: And their brothers (among the devils) extend them in misguidance, then they do not stop.
interpretation: This verse describes the heedless who align themselves with demonic companions: those companions continuously reinforce and deepen them in error, and the devils never abate or grow weary in drawing them further away from guidance. It contrasts the swift repentance and clarity of the God-conscious with the relentless persistence of evil allies upon those who have chosen to follow misguidance.

translation: And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, 'Why have you not devised it?' Say, 'I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. This is clear insight from your Lord, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.'
interpretation: The verse repudiates the demand that the Prophet produce revelations according to human whim. He has no authority to choose, invent, or tailor signs; his mission is solely to follow the revelation sent by God. The Qur'an is itself inner light, guidance, and mercy, but its saving benefit is received only by those who submit in faith. Prophetic authority is therefore bound entirely to divine revelation, and the true miracle is the revealed message that opens hearts to God.

translation: And when the Qur’an is recited, then listen to it and remain silent, so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This command teaches that the Qur’an is not merely to be heard outwardly, but received with attentive stillness of both body and heart. Listening in silence is a spiritual discipline: it removes distractions, expresses reverence for God’s words, and prepares the heart to be affected, guided, and corrected by them. The promised outcome, mercy, shows that divine mercy is not earned by mere proximity to recitation but by humble receptivity to it. This applies especially when the Qur’an is recited in prayer and in gatherings of remembrance, where talking, noise, or inattention obstructs the purpose of revelation.

translation: And remember your Lord within yourself, in humility and fear, and without loudness in speech, in the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless.
interpretation: This verse commands the believer to keep God present in the heart through inward remembrance, marked by humble supplication and reverent fear rather than ostentatious or loud utterance. It teaches that the most sincere remembrance is hidden between the servant and God, free from show, and that devoting the beginning and end of the day to such remembrance protects the soul from negligence and spiritual forgetfulness. The prohibition against being among the heedless shows that remembrance is not merely a verbal act but a state of ongoing awareness, gratitude, and accountability before God.

translation: Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain to worship Him; they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate.
interpretation: This verse describes the angels who are closest to God: their nearness does not make them proud or too exalted to worship Him. Instead, it increases them in humility, constant glorification, and prostration before Him alone. It teaches that true honor before God is accompanied by humble devotion, not by disdain toward worship.

translation: They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils of war belong to Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah and set right that which is between you, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the spoils of war are not private property or a matter of human entitlement, but are to be disposed of according to Allah's command and through His Messenger. The real test of faith after victory is not who gains the most, but whether believers practice taqwa, repair their mutual relations, and submit to Allah and His Messenger. Thus material gain must never divide the community; faith is proven by God-consciousness, reconciliation, and obedience.

translation: The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble with awe, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely.
interpretation: True faith is not a mere claim but a living state of the heart: it is aroused by the remembrance of God into reverent awe, it grows stronger whenever His revelation is recited and heeded, and it expresses itself in complete trust that all affairs are in the hands of the Lord alone.

translation: Those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them.
interpretation: This describes the believers as people who keep up the prayer with regularity and devotion, fulfilling its conditions and preserving it, and who give in charity from the provision God has bestowed upon them, showing gratitude and trust in Him rather than hoarding. Their devotion to God is joined to compassion toward His creation, so worship and generosity together mark their faith.

translation: Those are the true believers. They have ranks with their Lord, forgiveness, and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith is not merely a verbal claim or outward label; it is a reality rooted in the heart and confirmed by obedience to Allah. Those whom Allah describes as believers in truth are the ones whose faith is sincere and whose lives reflect that sincerity. For them, Allah has reserved degrees of honor and nearness with their Lord, covering of their sins through forgiveness, and a generous, unending provision in the Hereafter. Thus, the verse teaches that authentic faith leads to divine exaltation, pardon, and noble reward.

translation: Just as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, though indeed a group of the believers were averse.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet Muhammad that it was He who caused him to leave his home in Madinah for the expedition of Badr with a true and just purpose, even though some believers disliked going out because they feared fighting or preferred the caravan. The verse teaches that Allah's decree and command may be difficult or unwelcome to some believers, but He knows best and will fulfill His promise; true faith requires submitting to His command with trust, even when one cannot see the outcome.

translation: They dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear, as if they were being driven to death while they look on.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who argue against a divinely ordained matter after its truth has been made plain. Their dispute is not grounded in evidence but in aversion and fear, so their state is likened to people compelled toward death with their eyes open—knowing the reality yet recoiling from it. It teaches that once Allah’s command and the truth are clear, the believer’s duty is submission and obedience, not contentious hesitation.

translation: And [remember] when Allah promised you one of the two parties—that it would be yours—while you wished that the one without weapons would be yours. But Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the root of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse shows that Allah’s decree governs events according to His wisdom, not according to human desire for ease or worldly advantage. The believers preferred the less dangerous, unarmed caravan, but Allah willed the confrontation with the armed enemy in order to establish the truth, fulfill His promise, and uproot the power of disbelief. Victory is thus tied to divine purpose and truth, not merely to material calculations or preferred outcomes.

translation: That He may establish the truth and abolish falsehood, even if the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: God’s purpose is to make truth prevail and to render falsehood void, and the hatred of those who persist in sin cannot prevent or alter this decree; His sovereign will ensures that falsehood is ultimately dismantled and truth is vindicated, no matter how much the guilty oppose it.

translation: [Remember] when you were seeking help from your Lord, and He answered you: 'I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another.'
interpretation: This verse recalls how the believers’ earnest supplication to God in a moment of severe need was immediately answered. The promised angels were a divine reinforcement, sent in succession, to strengthen the believers’ resolve and assure them that help and victory come from God, not merely from visible means. It teaches that sincere prayer is heard, that God supports His servants in ways beyond human calculation, and that apparent weakness can be overcome when divine assistance arrives.

translation: And Allah did not make it except as glad tidings and so that your hearts may be reassured by it. And victory is only from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse teaches that divine promises and aid—such as the promised angels—are given to comfort believers and strengthen their hearts, not as the true source of victory. Victory comes solely from Allah, not from visible means, numbers, or helpers. He is Almighty, able to grant triumph, and Wise in how and when He decrees it.

translation: When He caused drowsiness to cover you as security from Him, and sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you with it, and to remove from you the impurity of Satan, and to strengthen your hearts and make firm your feet thereby.
interpretation: This verse describes God’s protective care for the believers before battle. The drowsiness was a calm sent upon them, replacing fear with a sense of safety and trust in God. The rain from the sky was not merely a physical relief; it purified them outwardly and inwardly, washing away dirt, thirst, and ritual impurity, while also removing Satan’s whispers, discouragement, and corrupting influence. By this same mercy, God fortified their hearts with courage and resolve, and steadied their feet so they would not slip or falter. Thus, divine help came through both material and spiritual means: security, purification, removal of evil suggestion, inner strength, and outward firmness.

translation: [Remember] when your Lord inspired the angels, “I am with you, so make firm those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve; so strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of them.”
interpretation: This is a battlefield address at Badr: God announces His aid, commands the angels to steady the believers, and casts panic into the disbelievers. Striking the necks and fingertips signifies decisive, disabling blows—breaking the enemy’s ability to fight—so that the believers would recognize victory as coming from God’s command and support.

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger—then indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse declares that the punishment and defeat suffered by the rejecters was caused by their deliberate defiance of Allah and His Messenger. Their opposition was not mere intellectual disagreement but a rebellious standing against divine authority and the prophetic command. It then lays down a universal law: whoever takes a path of conflict with Allah and His Messenger will inevitably meet Allah’s severe punishment, for His authority cannot be overcome and His judgment cannot be averted.

translation: That is for you, so taste it, and indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: This is a stern divine address to the disbelievers: their defeat and suffering in this world are something they are commanded to taste as an immediate consequence of their rejection and hostility, but it is not the end—the Fire is prepared for them in the Hereafter. The verse thus combines present humiliation with eternal warning, affirming that unbelief and enmity toward God and His Messenger lead to punishment both in this life and the next.

translation: O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing [for battle], do not turn your backs to them [in flight].
interpretation: This verse commands the believers, when they confront an opposing force of disbelievers marching out for war, to stand firm and not flee from the battlefield. Turning one’s back means retreating out of fear or abandoning the fight, which is forbidden because it breaks ranks, weakens the community, and contradicts trust in God. The command establishes courage, steadfastness, and obedience to divine orders in the face of danger, with later verses specifying limited exceptions such as tactical repositioning or regrouping with another unit.

translation: And whoever turns his back to them on that day—unless it is a maneuver for battle or to join another company—he has certainly incurred wrath from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse establishes that fleeing from the enemy in battle is forbidden, except when it is a tactical withdrawal meant to gain a better position or to regroup with fellow believers. Such exceptions are not acts of cowardice but legitimate battlefield strategy. Anyone who retreats without these valid reasons has earned Allah’s anger, and his final abode is Hell, an evil end. The verse thus stresses that steadfastness in the face of the enemy is a serious obligation, and abandoning it without a lawful excuse is a grave sin deserving divine punishment.

translation: So you did not kill them, but Allah killed them. And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw. And [this was] so that He might test the believers with a good trial from Him. Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches that although the believers and the Prophet performed outward actions at Badr, the decisive power and effect belonged to Allah alone. Their victory was not produced by their own strength, numbers, or weapons; Allah brought it about. The Prophet’s throwing of dust or pebbles was his physical act, but Allah made it reach the enemy and break their morale, so the true agent was Allah. The good trial is a gracious test and blessing—victory, favor, and strengthening of faith—showing that Allah hears the believers’ supplications and knows their intentions and states. Thus it calls for tawhid, reliance on Allah, humility after success, and recognizing that human means are only means, not independent causes.

translation: That is so, and [know] that Allah is the One who weakens the plot of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the frustration and failure of the schemes of those who reject the truth come from Allah alone. He diminishes their cunning, drains it of effectiveness, and prevents it from achieving its intended goal against the believers. The phrase “that is so” points back to the divine help, terror cast upon the enemy, and victory granted at Badr, teaching that these outcomes were not merely the result of human strength but of Allah’s active governance. It is both a reassurance to the faithful that no plot against them can ultimately succeed without Allah’s permission, and a warning to the disbelievers that their designs against His religion are hollow before His power.

translation: If you seek a decision, the decision has come to you. And if you desist, it is better for you. And if you return, We will return; and your company will not avail you at all, even if it is numerous. And indeed Allah is with the believers.
interpretation: This is a divine address to those who challenged God to judge between truth and falsehood. The decisive judgment came at Badr: they were defeated despite their greater numbers, showing that victory is not won by strength or numbers but by God’s support. If they abandon their denial and hostility toward the Prophet, that is better for them. If they resume their aggression, God will again aid the believers against them. Their assembled forces cannot protect them or benefit them. God is with the believers, granting them help, steadfastness, and success.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to give sincere obedience to Allah and to His Messenger, and it forbids them to turn away from the Messenger’s call after having heard it. Hearing the revelation or prophetic instruction makes one responsible to respond; turning away is a rejection of that responsibility and a sign of disobedience. True faith requires attentive hearing followed by compliance, not merely hearing with the ears while the heart and conduct remain averse.

translation: And do not be like those who said, 'We have heard,' while they do not hear.
interpretation: The verse forbids imitating those who verbally acknowledge the divine message but do not truly listen with the ear of faith and acceptance. Their saying “we heard” is empty because they neither understand nor obey; true hearing is not mere exposure to words, but receiving them with a heart that submits and acts accordingly.

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb, those who do not reason.
interpretation: This verse means that the most degraded and blameworthy of creatures before Allah are those who close their ears to the truth, refuse to speak or uphold it, and fail to use the intellect and faculty of understanding He gave them to recognize guidance. Their deafness and dumbness are not merely physical; they are spiritual: they do not hear the message with acceptance, do not respond to it with faith, and do not reason about the clear signs of Allah. Thus they fall below even the animals, because animals follow their nature, while these people possess reason and revelation but reject both.

translation: And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And even if He made them hear, they would turn away, being averse.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge of His creation is complete and that His granting of guidance is connected to what He knows of their inward disposition. Since He knew no sincere readiness for good in them, He did not grant them the kind of hearing that leads to faith. And even if He had granted them such hearing, they would still have rejected it and turned away in aversion, because their resistance was not due to lack of evidence but to their own corrupt will and obstinate rejection of the truth.

translation: O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart, and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse directs the believers to answer the divine call with obedience and acceptance, because what Allah and His Messenger summon to is not merely a set of rules but the means of true life: faith, guidance, and righteous action that revive the heart and rescue it from spiritual death. It teaches that life in its fullest sense is tied to responding to revelation, and that refusal or delay hardens the heart and leads to loss. The mention that Allah 'intervenes between a man and his heart' affirms that the inward self, intentions, and capacity to believe or turn away are all under Allah's sovereign control; He can turn a heart toward or away from guidance, so the believer should not trust in personal strength but should ask Allah for steadfastness and sincerity. The closing statement that all are gathered to Him grounds the command in accountability: every response or refusal to the call is not unnoticed, and the ultimate return is to Allah for judgment, where the life-giving effect of obedience and the deadening effect of disobedience will be made manifest.

translation: And fear a trial which will not strike only those among you who have done wrong; and know that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that when wrongdoing becomes widespread and is left unchallenged, the resulting punishment or social calamity is not restricted to the wrongdoers alone; it can overtake the whole community. It calls believers to guard against sin, corruption, and injustice spreading among them, because collective silence or negligence toward evil exposes everyone to the consequences. It also reminds them that Allah’s punishment is severe, so they must take His warning seriously and strive to uphold justice and prevent harm before it becomes general.

translation: And remember when you were few, oppressed in the land, fearing that people might snatch you away, then He gave you refuge and strengthened you with His help and provided you with good things so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of God's favor upon them in their state of weakness and vulnerability: He rescued them from fear and humiliation, granted them a safe place, strengthened them with His support, and supplied them with pure and wholesome provisions. It teaches that deliverance, security, and sustenance are gifts from God alone, and that the fitting response is sincere gratitude shown through worship, obedience, and reliance upon Him.

translation: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts while you know.
interpretation: This verse prohibits believers from any breach of trust toward God and His Messenger—such as disobeying divine commands, concealing the truth, or abandoning religious duties—and it equally prohibits betraying the trusts placed in their care, whether they are material, moral, social, or confidential. The phrase “while you know” intensifies the warning: it means the betrayal is done knowingly and deliberately, not out of ignorance.

translation: And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial, and that Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that worldly blessings such as wealth and children are not ends in themselves but tests of faith: they can either draw a person toward gratitude, responsibility, and obedience to God, or distract them into neglect of God, injustice, and excessive attachment to worldly gain. True success lies in seeking God's pleasure, for the lasting and immense reward is with Him alone.

translation: O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will make for you a criterion and will remove from you your evil deeds and forgive you. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This means that when believers uphold God-consciousness by obeying Allah and avoiding disobedience, Allah grants them a spiritual criterion and inner discernment by which they distinguish truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance, and right from wrong; He also erases their sins and grants them forgiveness as an act of His abundant grace.

translation: And [remember] when those who disbelieved were plotting against you to imprison you, or kill you, or drive you out. They plot, and Allah plots; and Allah is the best of plotters.
interpretation: The disbelievers’ deliberation was a real conspiracy, but God’s decree encompassed it. Their efforts to stop the Prophet—by confinement, assassination, or exile—could not succeed because God arranged events to protect him and bring about the migration. “Plotting” ascribed to God means His wise counter-planning and just recompense, not deceit like creatures; He outmaneuvers every scheme. Thus the verse consoles the Prophet and warns schemers that ultimate control belongs to God, who brings His purpose to pass despite opposition.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, 'We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the arrogant and willful rejection of the disbelievers: they hear the Qur’an but refuse to submit to it, masking their obstinacy with the boast that they could produce something similar if they wanted. Their claim is hollow, for the Qur’an’s eloquence, wisdom, and truth are beyond human imitation, and dismissing it as mere ancient fables is a pretext to avoid its authority. It warns that hearing revelation without sincere reflection, and rejecting it out of pride or attachment to inherited ways, hardens the heart and leads to ruin.

translation: And [remember] when they said, “O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.”
interpretation: This is the arrogant challenge of the disbelievers who, instead of humbly accepting the Prophet’s message, demanded immediate punishment as proof. Their words reveal mockery, stubbornness, and a refusal to submit to the truth; they were not sincerely seeking guidance but trying to justify their rejection.
