The phrase 'people of understanding' points to those who reflect deeply, learn from the consequences of faith and disbelief, and recognize the consistent divine laws operating in human history. The Qur'an declares that these stories are not invented falsehood; rather, they authenticate the earlier revealed scriptures, clarify what human beings need regarding belief, law, and ethics, and function as guidance and mercy for those who accept the truth. Thus, the verse establishes the Qur'an's truthfulness, its role as a criterion and completion of previous revelation, and its transformative purpose for believers.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Alif, Lam, Mim, Ra. These are the verses of the Book; and that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.
interpretation: The opening letters are among the signs whose full meaning is left to Allah, and they point to the miraculous nature of a Book composed of such letters. The verses that follow are divine revelations, and the message sent down to the Prophet Muhammad is the absolute truth from his Lord, containing no doubt or falsehood. Despite this clarity, most people reject it—not because the truth is unclear, but because of heedlessness, arrogance, or attachment to their own desires and inherited ways.

translation: Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see; then He established Himself over the Throne; and He subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. He arranges the matter; He details the signs, so that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord.
interpretation: It declares that the heavens are held by Allah’s power, not by visible supports, so the order of creation points to the Creator. His rising over the Throne affirms His supreme authority over all existence in a manner befitting His majesty, beyond human comprehension. The sun and moon serve under His command until an appointed end, showing that all cosmic motion is purposeful and controlled. By governing every affair and clarifying His signs, He intends to awaken certainty in the heart that it must meet its Lord, so that belief in resurrection and accountability becomes firm, not merely inherited or assumed.

translation: And it is He who spread out the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers; and from all the fruits He made therein two mates. He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse directs the human being to contemplate the ordered design of creation as clear evidence of the Creator’s exclusive lordship, wisdom, and power. The spreading of the earth, the stabilizing mountains, the flowing rivers, the paired fruits, and the alternation of night and day are not random occurrences; they are purposeful signs pointing to the One God who alone governs all things, provides sustenance, and is able to bring life after death. For those who reflect, these signs call them to recognize their Creator, submit to Him alone, and live in gratitude and accountability.

translation: And in the earth are neighboring tracts, and gardens of grapevines, and crops, and palm trees, growing from one root and not from one root, watered with one water; yet We cause some of them to excel over others in taste. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse directs the rational mind to the visible order in the earth as evidence of God's power, will, and wise provision. Neighboring plots may share the same soil and receive the same water, yet they differ in what they yield, in ripeness, quality, and taste. That variation is not due to the water alone or to blind natural necessity; it reflects the deliberate decree and sustaining action of the Creator, who gives each created thing its distinct properties and advantages. The sign is addressed to those who use their intellect rightly: if people can observe such precise differentiation in ordinary agriculture, they should infer that the One who arranged it is able to originate, sustain, and restore creation, and that His signs deserve reflection, gratitude, and submission.

translation: And if you are astonished, then astonishing is their saying: ‘When we are dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?’ Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles around their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse identifies denial of resurrection as a symptom of a deeper disbelief in the Lord. The disbelievers find it incredible that dust can be reconstituted into a new creation, but the real wonder is their rejection of the One who originated creation and is fully able to restore it. Their disbelief binds them—symbolized by iron collars and shackles—so that in the Hereafter they are led to the Fire, where they remain forever because they persisted in rejecting their Lord and did not repent.

translation: And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good, while there have already been examples of punishment before them. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who mockingly demand that divine punishment come upon them before the good they are promised, as if challenging God's justice and mercy. It reminds them that earlier nations were destroyed for similar arrogance, so their demand is not a proof of sincerity but a sign of heedlessness. God's forgiveness and forbearance are vast: He does not hasten punishment for people's wrongdoing, giving them time to repent and turn back to Him. Yet His mercy should not make anyone presume they can persist in evil without consequence, for His punishment is also severe when wrongdoing continues and the term set by God arrives.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers’ demand for a miraculous sign as a condition for accepting the Prophet. It teaches that the Prophet’s duty is not to satisfy arbitrary demands or force faith through wonders; his mission is to warn people of the consequences of their choices. The demand for a sign often stems from stubbornness rather than a sincere search for truth. The verse also affirms that God’s guidance is never absent from humanity: every people has been given a guide—a prophet or messenger—who calls them to the truth and warns them. Thus the Prophet Muhammad is part of this consistent divine pattern, and his role is to deliver the warning clearly, while true guidance and accountability belong to God alone.

translation: Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase; and everything with Him is by measure.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge encompasses the most hidden realities of creation, especially conception and gestation. He knows every female’s burden—whether it is formed or unformed, alive or lost—and every change that occurs in the womb, whether decrease or increase, miscarriage or growth, shorter or longer term. Nothing in the womb is hidden from Him, and no stage of development escapes His knowledge. The closing phrase teaches that all things with Him have a precise, appointed measure: creation, provision, lifespan, and every event are determined according to His wisdom and decree. Thus the verse calls the heart to trust Allah’s knowledge and wisdom, for He alone fully knows what is concealed and brings every matter to its exact measure.

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Most High.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God alone encompasses all knowledge: He knows what is hidden from created perception and what is openly manifest, seen, and witnessed. It also declares that He is infinitely great in His essence and attributes, and supremely exalted above all creation, beyond any deficiency, limitation, or likeness.

translation: It is the same to Him whether any of you conceals his speech or declares it openly, and whether he is hidden by night or goes forth by day.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God’s knowledge encompasses every condition and action of His creation without exception. Whether a person keeps words or deeds secret or makes them public, whether he seeks concealment in the darkness of night or moves openly in the daytime, none of this changes God’s awareness of him. No place, time, veil, or private state can hide anyone from God; He knows the inward and outward alike. Therefore, it calls the human being to sincerity, God-consciousness, and awareness that every hidden intention and open act is fully known and subject to divine reckoning.

translation: For him are successive angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of Allah. Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves. And if Allah intends misfortune for a people, there is no repelling it; and they have no protector besides Him.
interpretation: The verse establishes that unseen guardianship and protection are real, but they are entirely subordinate to Allah’s command and never independent of His will. The decisive factor in a community’s fate is internal: Allah does not alter a people’s state of blessing or punishment until they themselves change their beliefs, intentions, and conduct. This affirms human responsibility without denying divine sovereignty. If a people persist in corruption and Allah decrees adversity, no angel, power, intercessor, or ally can avert it, because there is no protector besides Him. The verse therefore calls for sincere inward reform before outward consequences become irreversible.

translation: He is the One who shows you the lightning, causing fear and hope, and He brings up the heavy clouds.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to God’s exclusive power and mercy in governing creation: lightning is a sign that can produce both fear of harm and hope for rain and relief, showing how one created phenomenon can serve as warning and promise. The heavy, water-laden clouds are likewise brought into existence and raised by Him, not by any independent force. Believers are thus taught to live between fear of His punishment and hope for His mercy, and to recognize in the orderly sky the hand of the Creator who is able to give life, send provision, and bring about resurrection and reckoning.

translation: And the thunder glorifies Him with praise, and [so do] the angels out of fear of Him. And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, yet they dispute about Allah, while He is severe in might.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the forces of nature are not independent powers but creatures obedient to Allah: the thunder itself declares His praise, and the angels worship Him in awe. The same divine authority that governs the thunder and lightning also executes judgment, striking whomever He decrees. Human beings who argue against Allah's oneness, power, or promised punishment are therefore deluded, for He is irresistible and severe in power; no creature can escape His will or thwart His decree.

translation: To Him belongs the call of truth. And those whom they invoke besides Him do not respond to them at all, except like one who stretches out his hands toward water so that it may reach his mouth, but it will never reach it. And the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but in error.
interpretation: True invocation, worship, and reliance belong to Allah alone. Any supposed deity or intercessor invoked besides Him has no power to answer, benefit, or harm. The parable of stretching one's hands toward water hoping it will rise to the mouth depicts a futile effort: the desired result is unreachable because the means are absent and the one called upon cannot act. Likewise, directing supplication to anything other than Allah is not merely ineffective but is misguidance, since it turns the heart away from the only One who hears, responds, and governs all affairs.

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows [as well] in the mornings and the late afternoons.
interpretation: This verse declares that every creature in the heavens and earth is subject to Allah, either through willing worship or through forced submission to His decree. The believers prostrate willingly, while others submit unwillingly to His sovereignty whether they acknowledge it or not. Even their shadows prostrate, moving in the mornings and evenings as ordained by Allah, symbolizing that all created things follow His command and testify to His oneness and power. Thus lordship and worship belong to Allah alone, and the verse calls the reader to join the willing submission of creation rather than the involuntary subjection of the deniers.

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Then have you taken besides Him protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?' Say, 'Are the blind and the seeing equal, or are darkness and light equal? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation, so the creation seemed similar to them?' Say, 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah's exclusive lordship and creatorship and exposes the futility of false gods. The Prophet is commanded to ask who owns and governs the heavens and earth; the answer is Allah alone. Those taken as guardians besides Him cannot bring benefit or avert harm even for themselves, so they are powerless to help anyone else. The rhetorical contrasts—blind and seeing, darkness and light—show that worship of the Creator and worship of helpless creatures are not equivalent; one is guidance and illumination, the other blindness and darkness. If polytheists claim their false deities created something like Allah's creation, that only reflects their confused inability to distinguish the true Creator. The conclusion is decisive: Allah is the sole Creator of everything, and He is the One, the All-Subduing, to whom all power and authority belong. Therefore He alone deserves worship, reliance, and obedience.

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their capacity, and the flood carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in fire, seeking ornament or goods, there is foam like it. Thus Allah sets forth truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but as for what benefits people, it remains in the earth. Thus Allah sets forth parables.
interpretation: This verse presents a parable of truth and falsehood through two images: rainwater flowing through valleys and metals heated in fire. In both cases, a worthless foam or scum rises to the surface, but it is temporary and soon discarded, while the water that nourishes the earth and the pure metal that is useful remain. So falsehood may appear abundant, visible, and dominant for a time, but it is hollow and destined to disappear; truth, by contrast, is like what benefits people—it settles, endures, and produces lasting good. The valleys receiving water according to their capacity also indicate that people receive guidance according to their readiness and ability. Allah gives such parables to separate the enduring from the fleeting and to show that true worth lies not in surface appearance but in lasting benefit.

translation: For those who responded to their Lord is the best [reward]. But those who did not respond to Him—if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would offer it as ransom. Those will have an evil reckoning, and their refuge is Hell—and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the end of those who answer God’s call with the end of those who refuse it. Responding to the Lord means accepting His guidance, obeying Him, and turning back to Him; for such people is al-husna, the best and most beautiful outcome, ultimately Paradise and divine pleasure. Those who reject or fail to respond will discover on the Day of Judgment that no amount of worldly wealth can rescue them: even if they owned the whole earth and as much again, they would willingly give it as a ransom. But no ransom will be accepted from them. Theirs is an evil reckoning—a severe and painful account in which their denial and wrongdoing are fully exposed—and their final abode is Hell, the worst possible resting place.

translation: Is then one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only those endowed with understanding take heed.
interpretation: This rhetorical question establishes that the one who has inner sight to recognize the Qur’an as the truth from God cannot be equal to the one who is spiritually blind and heedless. True knowledge of revelation is not mere information; it illuminates the heart and produces heedfulness. The verse therefore teaches that only possessors of sound reason and purified intellect—those who use their minds to reflect on God's signs—will receive the reminder and act upon it, while blindness here means a willful incapacity to perceive and accept the truth.

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the pledge.
interpretation: This describes the believers who are faithful to their commitments to Allah and to others: they uphold the covenant of faith, obedience, and agreements, and they do not betray or violate the binding pledge they have made.

translation: And those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined, and fear their Lord, and dread the evil reckoning.
interpretation: Such believers preserve the bonds Allah has ordered to be maintained—such as kinship, covenants, and the rights of faith—because they know these ties are a divine command, not mere social preference. Their fear of the Lord is a reverent, obedient awe that keeps them from violating His limits, and their fear of an evil reckoning makes them vigilant in deeds, quick to repent, and careful not to wrong others, so that they may not be brought to account harshly on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And those who patiently persevere, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided them, secretly and openly, and repel evil with good—those will have the final home.
interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of those who attain the ultimate and blessed abode with Allah. Their patience is not for worldly praise but purely to seek Allah’s pleasure, and it is joined with steadfast worship, generous spending from what Allah has provided, whether given privately or publicly, and the noble practice of responding to wrongdoing with goodness rather than vengeance. Such people are promised the best final outcome: the eternal home of Paradise, where the reward fully matches their sincere devotion and righteous conduct.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter, along with whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward of the believers who persevered in faith and good deeds: God admits them into eternal gardens of bliss and, by His grace, joins them with righteous family members—parents, spouses, and children—so that the joy of Paradise includes reunion without diminishing anyone’s rank. Only those who are righteous share in this promise; lineage alone does not suffice. The angels enter upon them from every gate as a sign of honor, welcome, and continuous glad tidings, showing that the people of Paradise are surrounded by divine mercy and the company of noble angels.

translation: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. How excellent is the final home!
interpretation: This is the greeting given to the people of Paradise: God grants them perfect peace and security as a reward for their steadfast patience in faith, obedience, and enduring hardship for His sake. Their patience has led them to the most excellent final destination—the eternal abode of bliss—so the verse praises that outcome as the finest end and reward.

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause corruption in the earth — those are the ones upon whom is the curse, and for them is the evil home.
interpretation: This verse describes those who ruin themselves by deliberately reneging on the pledge made to God after it has been firmly established, whether that pledge is faith in Him, obedience to His messengers, or covenants between people upheld in His name. They then cut what God commanded to be maintained, such as kinship ties, brotherhood in faith, justice, truth, and the bonds of compassion and trust. They also spread corruption on earth through injustice, sin, oppression, and disorder. Because they nullify the covenant, sever ties, and corrupt, divine mercy is withdrawn from them; they are subjected to Allah’s curse and condemnation, and their final end is the worst abode — the Fire, where they will suffer lasting misery.

translation: Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it. And they rejoice in the life of this world, but the life of this world compared with the Hereafter is nothing but a passing enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sustenance is entirely in God's hand: He gives abundance or scarcity according to His wisdom, not as a sign of divine favor or disfavor. The human error it exposes is measuring reality by worldly comfort and rejoicing in it as though it were ultimate. In truth, worldly life is only a temporary, limited provision; set beside the eternal Hereafter it has no real weight. Thus the verse calls believers to trust God's decree, avoid being seduced by prosperity or crushed by want, and orient their joy and hope toward the lasting life to come.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].'
interpretation: The disbelievers’ demand for a miraculous sign is not the true means of faith; guidance belongs to Allah alone. He leaves in misguidance those who persist in arrogance and rejection, and He guides to Himself those who humble themselves, repent, and turn back to Him. The verse teaches that the heart’s willing return to Allah is what receives guidance, not the mere witnessing of wonders.

translation: Those who have believed and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of true believers: their hearts are tranquil, assured, and at peace through the remembrance of Allah. Such remembrance includes reciting His Book, calling upon Him, praising Him, and keeping Him in mind with faith and obedience. Allah then affirms with emphasis that genuine rest and serenity for the heart are found only in remembering Him, because the heart was created to know, love, and worship Him. When it turns to Him, it is freed from anxiety and confusion; when it turns away, it remains restless, no matter what worldly comforts it may have.

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds—blessedness is theirs, and an excellent return.
interpretation: This verse teaches that faith must be joined with righteous action. For such people, God promises ultimate happiness, well-being, and a beautiful final destination in the Hereafter—nearness to Him and eternal bliss in Paradise.

translation: Thus We have sent you among a community before which other communities have passed, so that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, 'He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him; upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Prophet Muhammad is part of the same continuous pattern of divine guidance as earlier messengers: he is sent to a people who have been preceded by many nations, and his task is to convey and recite the revelation given to him. Their rejection of the Most Merciful is especially grave because they deny the very Lord whose mercy sustains them, while the Prophet is taught to answer disbelief with pure monotheism: Allah alone is his Lord, the only true deity, the sole object of reliance, and the final destination of repentance and return. Thus the verse joins the reality of a rejected messenger with the believer's remedy—reciting revelation, affirming God's oneness, trusting in Him alone, and turning back to Him in repentance.

translation: And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved, or the earth was cleft, or the dead were made to speak, [it would be this Qur'an]. But to Allah belongs the command entirely. Have not those who believe yet known that if Allah willed, He would have guided all mankind? And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck by calamity for what they have done, or it will settle near their homes, until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the decisive matter is not the demand for spectacular miracles, since all authority and power belong to Allah alone. Even if a recitation could move mountains, split the earth, or make the dead speak, such signs would not compel true faith; guidance depends on Allah's will and wisdom. The believers are therefore reminded not to be distressed by the persistence of disbelief, because if Allah had willed He could have guided all people together. Yet He tries and guides according to His purpose. As for those who persist in rejection, their deeds bring repeated calamities upon them, or calamity draws near their dwellings, until Allah's promised decree arrives. That promise is certain, for Allah never breaks His word.

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, and how was My punishment!
interpretation: This verse consoles the Messenger and warns those who mock divine messengers that their rejection is not new. God’s granting them time is not approval or inability to punish; it is a respite that allows their wrongdoing to become fully manifest. When the appointed term ends, His seizure is sudden, decisive, and beyond escape. The rhetorical question at the end drives home the severity, certainty, and justice of that punishment, showing that mocking God’s messengers ultimately leads to ruin.

translation: Is He, then, who is watchful over every soul [and knows] what it earns [like the idols]? Yet they associate partners with Allah. Say, “Name them. Or do you inform Him of something He does not know on the earth? Or is it but an outward saying?” Rather, their scheming has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they have been turned away from the path. And whoever Allah sends astray, there is no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah: He alone is the ever-sustaining Watcher over every soul, fully aware of every deed and answerable for His judgment and recompense. The “partners” the idolaters ascribe to Him are mere names with no reality; they neither know nor can inform Allah of anything, nor do they share in His knowledge, creation, or rule. Polytheism is therefore exposed as empty speech, not knowledge. The disbelievers’ rejection is made to seem fair to them by their own corrupt plotting, and they obstruct others from the straight path. Guidance belongs exclusively to Allah; if He leaves someone in misguidance because of that person’s persistent rejection, no created being can guide him.

translation: For them is punishment in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, and they will have no protector against Allah.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing will suffer consequences in this worldly life—such as humiliation, loss, defeat, or hardship—but that is only a partial and temporary recompense. The punishment of the Hereafter is far more painful and lasting. No power, ally, or intercessor can shield them from Allah’s judgment or avert His decree. It affirms that divine justice is certain and that worldly penalties are merely a faint indication of the far greater accountability awaiting them.

translation: The description of Paradise which has been promised to the righteous: rivers flow beneath it; its fruit is perpetual and its shade. That is the end of those who fear Allah, and the end of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes Paradise as the final destination of the God-conscious, whose rivers, fruits, and shade never cease. It contrasts the everlasting reward of those who guard themselves against disbelief and sin with the final end of those who reject faith, which is the Fire. The mention of unending fruit and shade shows that the delights of Paradise surpass all worldly gardens, which inevitably fade and end.

translation: And those to whom We have given the Scripture rejoice at what has been revealed to you, but among the factions are those who deny part of it. Say, “I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I call, and to Him is my return.”
interpretation: This verse distinguishes between two responses to the Qur’an. Those among the People of the Book who are sincere and truthful recognize in the revelation what agrees with the earlier scriptures, so they welcome and rejoice in it. Others, however, are moved by factional loyalty, pride, or worldly interest and therefore reject parts of it, even if they may accept other parts. The Prophet is told not to be troubled by such denial or to dilute the message for the sake of approval. His task is pure and unwavering monotheism: to worship God alone, to associate no partner with Him, to invite all people to that truth, and to acknowledge that every person’s final destination and return is to God alone, where all disputes will be judged.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment. And if you follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you will have no protector or shield against Allah.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur’an was revealed as a decisive Arabic authority and criterion of truth, not something to be reshaped by human whims. After the Prophet received clear divine knowledge, any leaning toward the opponents’ desires would—by way of warning and instruction—cut one off from Allah’s protection; no created being can act as guardian or shield against Him. The verse thus teaches that revealed knowledge must govern desire, and that turning from it to please others brings neither true help nor protection.

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by Allah's permission. For every term there is a decree written.
interpretation: Prophethood is not incompatible with human family life: earlier messengers also married and had children, so the Prophet Muhammad’s household is no objection to his mission. No messenger can produce a miraculous sign by his own power; such signs occur only when God permits, at the time He has fixed. Every event, sign, and appointed time has its decreed limit and record in God’s knowledge, so demands for miracles cannot force God’s hand or hasten what He has scheduled.

translation: Allah eliminates what He wills and confirms [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse affirms God’s absolute sovereignty over all decrees and revelation: He may erase, cancel, replace, or remove whatever He wills, and He may establish, confirm, or preserve whatever He wills, according to His wisdom. Yet all such change occurs within His creation and His revealed laws; the ultimate, unchanging source and foundation of every book and decree—the Mother of the Book—remains with Him. Thus apparent abrogation, alteration, or change in worldly affairs and legislation does not imply any change in God’s eternal knowledge or in the transcendent origin of His command.

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We cause you to die, your duty is only to convey the message, and Ours is the reckoning.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet, reassuring him that his responsibility is limited to delivering the divine message clearly and faithfully. Whether God shows him in his lifetime some of the punishment promised to the deniers, or causes him to die before that happens, does not affect his mission. The fulfillment of God’s promises and threats, and the final accounting of every soul, belongs exclusively to God. Therefore, the preacher or messenger is not accountable for the results or for forcing people to believe; he is accountable only for conveying the truth. God alone will judge with perfect justice, and His reckoning is certain, wise, and perfectly timed.

translation: Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? And Allah judges; none can reverse His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The diminishing of the land’s borders is a visible sign of God’s sovereign control over nations and civilizations: as His command advances, the territories and influence of falsehood recede, and no power can overturn what He has decreed. His judgment is final and irresistible, and His reckoning is swift and exact, so people are warned to take heed before the account is settled.

translation: And indeed those before them plotted, but all plotting belongs to Allah. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know for whom is the final home.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and the believers by reminding them that the plotting of earlier nations against their messengers did not defeat God’s will. Ultimate authority over all plans and outcomes belongs to Allah alone. He is fully aware of every deed, intention, and secret scheme, so nothing is hidden from Him. When the disbelievers finally see the Hereafter, they will realize that the blessed final dwelling is not theirs; the good end belongs to the believers who remained faithful.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a Witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.'
interpretation: The verse answers the disbelievers' denial of the Prophet's messengership by pointing to Allah's testimony as the decisive and sufficient proof. Allah Himself witnesses that His messenger has been sent and that he conveys the truth, and those who truly possess knowledge of the earlier scriptures also recognize and attest to his truthfulness because they find his signs and description in the Book. Thus the disbelievers' rejection does not undermine his mission; the witness of Allah and of the knowledgeable people of scripture is enough to establish it.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif Lam Ra. A Book which We have sent down to you, so that you may bring people out of darkness into light, by the permission of their Lord, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse explains the purpose of the Qur’an’s revelation: it is a Book sent to the Prophet so that, through his call and by God’s enabling, people are brought out of the many darknesses of ignorance, disbelief, and sin into the single light of faith, knowledge, and obedience. This guidance does not occur by human power alone but by the permission and grace of their Lord, and it leads to the straight path of Allah, the Almighty who prevails over all, the Praiseworthy in His essence and in His acts.

translation: Allah is He to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that absolute sovereignty and ownership over all that exists—both in the heavens and on the earth—belong exclusively to Allah, and it follows that any worship, reliance, or ultimate loyalty directed elsewhere is misplaced. The warning of woe to the disbelievers indicates that rejecting this truth leaves one exposed to a painful and severe punishment, because disbelief is not merely an intellectual mistake but a denial of the Creator’s undeniable right to be recognized, obeyed, and worshipped alone.

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter and hinder [people] from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked; those are in far error.
interpretation: This verse describes people whose misguidance is deeply rooted: they choose the fleeting pleasures of worldly life over the everlasting reward of the Hereafter, actively turn others away from God’s straight path, and try to present that path as deviant or flawed. Because they not only stray themselves but also obstruct and distort the truth for others, their error is described as far-reaching—remote from guidance and true success.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people so that he might make [the message] clear to them. Then Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse establishes that divine revelation is conveyed through the language of the people to whom a messenger is sent, so that the message is understandable and the proof is clear. It teaches that true guidance and misguidance are ultimately under Allah’s will and decree: no messenger can force belief, and no person can guide himself or others independently of Allah. At the same time, Allah’s sending astray and guiding are not arbitrary, because He is al-‘Aziz, the Almighty, and al-Hakim, the All-Wise; His decree is perfectly wise and just. Thus the verse combines the principle of clear prophetic communication with the affirmation of Allah’s sovereign power over guidance and misguidance.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], 'Bring your people out from darknesses into the light, and remind them of the days of Allah.' Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful one.
interpretation: This means that God sent Moses equipped with clear proofs and commands to lead his people away from the manifold darknesses of unbelief, ignorance, and oppression into the light of faith, guidance, and obedience. He was also ordered to remind them of God's memorable days—His favors, deliverances, and judgments—so that they would reflect on how God deals with peoples. In these events are profound lessons for everyone who remains steadfast under hardship and grateful for blessings, recognizing God's wisdom and mercy in both ease and difficulty.

translation: And [remember] when Moses said to his people: “Remember the favor of Allah upon you, when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s favor is most vividly recognized in moments of rescue from oppression and suffering. Moses calls his people to actively remember, meaning that gratitude should not be passive memory but a form of worship that shapes loyalty and obedience. Pharaoh’s persecution—killing sons and sparing women—was intended to weaken and humiliate a people, yet God’s deliverance turned that humiliation into a manifest sign of His power and mercy. The “great trial” from the Lord includes both the severity of the oppression and the generosity of the liberation: hardship tests patience and faith, while rescue tests gratitude and steadfastness. Thus the verse presents history as the arena where God tries His servants through affliction and favor alike, and it calls believers to see every deliverance as a reason to remember, thank, and remain faithful to Him.

translation: And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe.
interpretation: This verse establishes that gratitude to God for His blessings is a direct cause of further increase from Him, while ingratitude and denial of His favors bring severe punishment, reflecting both divine generosity and justice.

translation: And Moses said, "If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy."
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah’s greatness and perfection are entirely independent of created beings. Moses tells his people that whether they believe or reject faith, and even if all people on earth did likewise, this neither adds to nor diminishes Allah in any way. He is absolutely self-sufficient, needing no worship, obedience, or acknowledgment from anyone, and He is praiseworthy in His own essence, attributes, and actions regardless of whether His creation praises Him. Thus disbelief harms only the disbeliever, while faith benefits only the believer; Allah remains eternally free of all need and eternally deserving of all praise.

translation: Has not the news reached you of those before you — the people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud, and those after them? None knows them except Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands in their mouths and said, 'Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you were sent, and indeed we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us.'
interpretation: This verse is a warning and rebuke: earlier communities were not destroyed for lack of clear guidance, but because they responded to it with arrogant rejection and hardened doubt. Their gesture of putting hands to their mouths signifies contemptuous refusal, as if trying to silence the messengers or block the truth from entering; their words then expose both open disbelief and a restless skepticism that made them reject what they could not honestly refute. The mention that only Allah knows the generations after them emphasizes that such warnings are beyond human counting, so the audience should not assume it is safe from the same pattern. The verse therefore calls for humility before prophetic truth, repentance from stubborn denial, and fear of the fate that overtook those who persisted in rejecting their messengers.

translation: Their messengers said, “Is there any doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you so that He may forgive you some of your sins and delay you until an appointed term.” They said, “You are only human beings like us; you want to turn us away from what our fathers worshipped. So bring us a clear proof.”
interpretation: The verse presents the prophets confronting inherited unbelief. The messengers point out that doubt concerning God is not a reasonable position, since the very existence of the heavens and earth bears witness to Him as their Creator and Sustainer. God’s invitation is not arbitrary or hostile; it aims at forgiveness and gives people time until a fixed term, showing mercy and patience rather than immediate judgment. The people’s reply exposes the core of their resistance: they measure the message by the messengers’ humanity, treating human agency as disqualifying, and they defend ancestral worship as an unquestioned authority. Their demand for a “clear proof” is not a sincere search for truth but a condition meant to evade the call. Thus the verse teaches that rejecting revelation because it comes through human beings, or because it challenges inherited custom, is a moral and spiritual evasion, not a rational objection; true divine authority is recognized through the truth of the message and the witness of creation, not through human expectations.

translation: Their messengers said to them: “We are only human beings like you, but Allah bestows favor upon whom He wills among His servants. It is not for us to bring you any proof except by Allah’s permission. And upon Allah let the believers rely.”
interpretation: This verse establishes that the messengers’ humanity is no defect in their mission: they do not claim divinity or any power of their own, but Allah chooses whom He wills for His favor and support. Therefore, the demand for signs or proofs is not theirs to fulfill independently; no miracle, authority, or convincing evidence can come except by Allah’s permission. The proper response of faith is not to dictate conditions to God or to follow only when spectacular proofs are given, but to place one’s trust wholly in Allah, recognizing that He alone controls guidance, signs, and outcomes.

translation: And why should we not rely upon Allah while He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely be patient over whatever harm you have inflicted upon us. And upon Allah let the reliant rely.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true trust in Allah is not passive resignation but a reasoned response to His guidance: since He has shown the believer the paths of right conduct, there is no valid excuse for withholding reliance upon Him. It also joins trust with steadfast patience, meaning the believer endures the harm and opposition of others without abandoning faith, and directs the heart’s dependence solely to Allah, for He alone is the true support of those who trust.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, “We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our religion.” So their Lord revealed to them, “We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the coercive logic of disbelief: when it cannot defeat the truth by argument, it resorts to threats of exile, displacement, or forced conformity. The messengers are told they must either leave the land or abandon their message and rejoin the dominant false way. But God’s revelation to them overturns that threat: He identifies the persecutors as wrongdoers and decrees their destruction, meaning that oppressive power may dominate temporarily, but it cannot ultimately prevail against the divine mission. The verse thus teaches that fidelity to God’s message may bring worldly pressure, yet God Himself undertakes to judge and remove the unjust, securing the future of His cause.

translation: And We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing and fears My warning.
interpretation: This promise teaches that God’s help and the believers’ establishment in the land come to those whose hearts are governed by reverent awe of God and by a serious fear of His warning. “Fearing My standing” means fearing to stand before God for judgment and honoring His majesty; “fearing My warning” means taking His threatened punishment seriously and letting that fear restrain disobedience. Such fear is not cowardice but spiritual vigilance: it produces steadfastness under persecution, loyalty to God’s command, and trust that He will fulfill His promise. Thus, victory and succession are not earned by power or numbers, but are granted to those who live with God-consciousness, dread His judgment, and remain faithful to Him.

translation: And they sought victory [or judgment], and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed.
interpretation: This verse declares that when the confrontation between truth and falsehood reaches its decisive point, Allah alone grants victory and judgment. The arrogant tyrant who stubbornly rejects the truth and uses power to oppress may appear mighty, but his defiance ultimately ends in failure and loss. Divine aid belongs to those who stand with truth and patience, while every entrenched oppressor is thwarted, humiliated, and deprived of the outcome he sought.

translation: Behind him is Hell, and he will be made to drink from water of pus.
interpretation: This describes the humiliating fate of the stubborn denier or tyrant: after his worldly authority and enjoyment end, Hell awaits him, and he is forced to drink a repulsive, festering liquid as part of his punishment and disgrace.

translation: He will sip it, but he will hardly be able to swallow it; death will come to him from every place, yet he will not die; and ahead of him is a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse conveys the extremity and layered nature of punishment in the Hereafter. The drink is so repulsive and scalding that the person cannot swallow it properly, yet he is compelled by torment to keep trying. The phrase that death comes from every direction means the suffering is total, affecting every sense and limb, so that he longs for death as a release. But God denies him death, because the punishment is not meant to end by annihilation; it is a perpetual state of agony. Then the final clause, that ahead of him is a severe punishment, indicates that this is not the only hardship but that further, unrelenting chastisement awaits. The meaning is that those who persist in arrogance, denial, and oppression will face a justice so complete that no escape, relief, or final rest remains—only an ongoing, heavy consequence for their choices.

translation: The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They will not be able to obtain anything from what they earned. That is the far-reaching misguidance.
interpretation: This parable teaches that rejecting one’s Lord nullifies the benefit of any deeds, however impressive they may appear, because deeds are only truly fruitful when rooted in faith and sincere devotion to God. On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will find nothing of their worldly efforts that can help them; their works will be like ashes scattered by a fierce wind, impossible to gather or use. Their condition is not a slight mistake but an extreme deviation, a misguidance that removes them far from the path of salvation.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring a new creation.
interpretation: This verse points to Allah’s absolute power and wisdom: He created the heavens and the earth with truth, meaning with a real purpose, order, and justice, not in vain. Since He is able to originate such vast creation, He is equally able to remove humankind and replace them with another creation if He wills. Therefore, no person or nation should consider itself indispensable; all existence depends entirely on Allah’s will. This calls for humble submission, awareness that Allah is not in need of His creatures, and certainty that His power over creation also guarantees His ability to resurrect and recompense.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse affirms that nothing Allah wills is hard or impossible for Him; His power is absolute, so creating, removing, or replacing any creation is entirely easy for Him and never beyond His capability.

translation: And they will all appear before Allah, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'We were your followers, so can you avert from us anything of Allah's punishment?' They will say, 'If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; we have no escape.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the complete collapse of worldly rank and influence before God on the Day of Judgment. Those who were weak in society and followed the arrogant elite in misguidance turn to their leaders for help, but the leaders admit that they possess no power to remove even the slightest punishment from them. Their words, 'If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you,' express the futility of their former authority: they could not guide themselves, so they certainly cannot guide or save their followers now. Both groups realize that neither panic nor forced patience changes anything, and there is no way out from God's decree. The verse warns against blindly surrendering one's conscience and responsibility to human authorities and teaches that only God's guidance, accepted and acted upon in this life, can save a person; on that Day, neither patronage nor regret nor endurance can substitute for it.

translation: And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: “Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I am not a rescuer for you, nor are you a rescuer for me. I reject your associating me [with Allah] before. Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.”
interpretation: This is Satan’s address to his followers after judgment has been settled and the people of Paradise and Hell are separated. It clarifies that Satan’s power was not coercive; he only called and deceived, while they willingly answered and obeyed. Therefore, he refuses to bear their blame and tells them to blame their own choices. He also admits that neither he nor they can rescue one another from Allah’s punishment, and he disowns the false partnership and obedience they had given him in the world. The verse establishes that on that Day personal responsibility is decisive: following deceptive promises instead of Allah’s true promise leads to ruin, and the wrongdoers who persist in that path will receive a painful punishment.

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever by permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be peace.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward of those who join sincere faith with righteous action: God admits them by His permission and grace into gardens with flowing rivers, a place of perpetual life and delight. Their eternal abiding is secured not by their own power but by their Lord’s enabling and mercy, and the greeting exchanged among them is “peace”—indicating that Paradise is free of every harm, conflict, fear, and sorrow. Righteous deeds are the fruit and proof of faith, and God’s permission is the ultimate cause of entering and remaining in bliss.

translation: Have you not seen how Allah sets forth a parable: a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches are in the sky?
interpretation: The good word is sincere faith and the testimony of Allah’s oneness—La ilaha illa Allah—spoken with conviction. It is likened to a good tree because it is deeply rooted in the heart, not superficial or easily uprooted, while its branches rise toward heaven through good deeds, remembrance, and prayer. Such faith continually yields benefit and draws the believer upward toward Allah, showing that true belief has both stability within and fruitful elevation without.

translation: It yields its fruit every season by permission of its Lord. And Allah sets forth parables for people so that they may remember.
interpretation: This illustrates that a good word rooted in true faith is not barren or temporary; it continually produces wholesome effects, benefits, and deeds at every appropriate time, yet this fruitfulness is not self-generated—it depends entirely on God’s enabling and decree. God uses such parables to bring profound realities within human reach, so that people may recall the truth, reflect on it, and let it move them toward heedfulness and righteous action.

translation: And the example of an evil word is like an evil tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability.
interpretation: This verse teaches that corrupt speech, false creed, and every word rooted in disbelief or sin are like a rotten tree without deep roots: it may appear for a while, but it has no foundation in truth, no stability, and no lasting benefit. Because it is cut off from the earth and uprooted, it cannot draw nourishment or produce good fruit; likewise, evil words and false beliefs cannot endure before God or yield any good in the end. Their only outcome is instability, loss, and removal.

translation: Allah keeps those who believe firm with the steadfast word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter; and Allah causes the wrongdoers to stray. And Allah does whatever He wills.
interpretation: This verse declares that God grants believers stability in faith through the firm testimony of His oneness and the truths He revealed, so that they live and die upon it and are able to answer correctly in the grave and the Hereafter. The wrongdoers are those who reject or corrupt this truth; God leaves them to stray in accordance with His wisdom and will, and no one can overturn His decree.

translation: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and led their people down to the abode of ruin?
interpretation: This verse condemns those who were blessed with Allah’s greatest favor—guidance, prophetic revelation, and the opportunity to accept the truth—yet deliberately traded it for ingratitude and rejection. Their crime was not only their own disbelief; they also dragged their followers and people with them into the dwelling of destruction, meaning Hell and everlasting loss. It warns that rejecting Allah’s favors and using one’s influence to mislead others leads to mutual ruin.

translation: Hell, they will enter it, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This is a severe threat and condemnation: their recompense is Jahannam, they will be cast into it and endure its torment, and it is an evil, miserable final abode and place of permanence.

translation: And they set up equals to Allah to mislead [people] from His way. Say, 'Enjoy yourselves, for indeed your destination is the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse condemns those who invent false rivals or partners for Allah and then use them as a means to turn others away from His path. Their sin is doubled: they commit shirk and become a cause of misguidance for others. The command “Say: Enjoy yourselves” is not permission but a stern threat: let them take their brief pleasure in this world, for it will not save them. Their final return and inevitable destination is the Fire. The verse thus warns that worldly enjoyment is temporary and deceptive, and that leading others away from Allah’s way only increases the severity of their punishment.

translation: Say to My servants who have believed, that they should establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before there comes a Day in which there is no trade nor friendship.
interpretation: Allah directs the Prophet to call the believers to uphold prayer and to give from the provision He has granted them, both privately and publicly. Prayer preserves their relationship with God, while spending privately protects sincerity from ostentation and spending openly provides a good example and strengthens generosity in the community. The urgency is because a Day is coming when neither commerce nor human friendships will be able to rescue anyone or secure any benefit; only the faith and righteous deeds cultivated in this life will have value.

translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. And He subjected to you the ships to sail in the sea by His command, and He subjected to you the rivers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah alone is the Creator and Sustainer: He originated the heavens and the earth, sends down rain, brings forth fruits as sustenance for humankind, and has made ships and rivers serviceable by His command. The repeated mention of these favors being "for you" shows that creation and natural forces are not independent powers but are governed by Allah for human benefit. Thus the verse is a proof of His lordship, power, and mercy, and it obliges people to worship Him alone, to be grateful to Him, and to rely upon Him rather than upon any created thing.

translation: And He subjected to you the sun and the moon, both constantly moving, and He subjected to you the night and the day.
interpretation: Allah has placed the sun, the moon, the night, and the day under human benefit and use by His command, causing them to run ceaselessly and precisely in their appointed courses without fatigue or deviation, so that people may derive from them light, warmth, time, guidance, and the rhythms needed for life and worship.

translation: And He gave you from all that you asked of Him. And if you tried to count the favors of Allah, you could not number them. Indeed, mankind is ever unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God provides for His creation from every need and request according to His wisdom, and that His blessings are so abundant they cannot be fully counted or repaid. It then exposes a deep flaw in human nature: people often meet these favors with injustice and ingratitude—misusing God’s gifts, forgetting the Giver, or denying His rights—so the verse urges humility, remembrance, and continual thankfulness.

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, “My Lord, make this city secure, and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.”
interpretation: Abraham prays to God to grant security to the sacred city—Makkah—and to preserve him and his offspring from the worship of idols. The prayer shows that even a prophet fears falling into shirk for himself and his children, so one should earnestly seek God's protection from all forms of idolatry and false worship, recognizing that guidance and safeguarding from disbelief are by God's grace.

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led many people astray. So whoever follows me — indeed, he is of me; and whoever disobeys me — indeed, You are Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: Here Ibrahim places guidance and misguidance before God: the idols have become a cause of straying for many, yet the human response is either to follow the prophetic call of pure monotheism and thus belong to Ibrahim’s way, or to disobey it. For those who disobey, Ibrahim does not pronounce final judgment or curse; he appeals instead to God’s forgiveness and mercy, showing that ultimate pardon belongs to God alone. The verse teaches that a caller to truth invites, warns, and entrusts outcomes to God, while God’s mercy is vast for those who turn back to Him; it is not a declaration that every disobedience is forgiven without repentance, but an expression of hope in God’s forgiving and merciful nature.

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits, that they may be grateful.
interpretation: This supplication of Ibrahim teaches that the settlement of his offspring near the Sacred House was not for worldly advantage but for the establishment of prayer and pure worship. Since the valley had no cultivation, he asked God to draw people’s hearts toward them—meaning love, longing, pilgrimage, and support—and to provide fruits in a barren place. The request for sustenance is joined to the purpose of gratitude, showing that all divine gifts, both inward attraction and outward provision, are meant to lead the community back to worship, dependence on God, and thankfulness.

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah on earth or in heaven.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge encompasses both the hidden and the open: He knows the secrets of the hearts, unspoken intentions, and private deeds just as He knows public words and actions. The statement that nothing in the earth or heaven is hidden from Allah expresses His absolute, all-encompassing omniscience over every creature, matter, and event. It teaches the believer to worship and supplicate with sincerity, humility, and awareness that no need, thought, or condition is beyond Allah’s knowledge or care.

translation: All praise is due to Allah, who has granted me, in old age, Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: This is Prophet Ibrahim’s expression of deep gratitude to Allah for answering his supplication and granting him two righteous sons, Ishmael and Isaac, despite his advanced age and the natural impossibility of having children at that stage. It teaches that Allah alone controls all causes and removes all obstacles, and that He truly hears, answers, and fulfills the prayers of His servants; therefore, blessings—especially righteous offspring—should be received with praise, humility, and renewed reliance upon Him.

translation: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: This is a supplication of Prophet Ibrahim in which he asks God to make him constant and sincere in establishing the prayer, and to extend that same devotion to his offspring. By asking for his descendants as well, he shows that his concern is not only for his own worship but for the continuation of true faith and prayer in his family after him. He then addresses God with humility, asking Him to accept this supplication, acknowledging that only God can grant such a request and that all acceptance rests with Him.

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning is established.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication taught by Prophet Ibrahim, showing that even the most devoted servant of God remains in need of divine forgiveness. It directs the believer to seek pardon for oneself, for one’s parents, and for the whole community of faith on the Day of Judgment, when accounts are settled and no one can benefit another except by God’s mercy. It thus combines personal humility, filial care, and communal concern, all anchored in reliance upon God alone for salvation in the Hereafter.

translation: And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when the eyes will stare in horror.
interpretation: This verse warns that God is never heedless of injustice; His delaying of punishment is not neglect but a respite until the Day of Judgment, when every wrongdoer will be confronted with his deeds. On that Day, eyes will be fixed in stunned terror, unable to turn away, as divine justice is finally and fully established. Thus the oppressed are assured that no injustice escapes God’s knowledge, and the oppressors are warned that their apparent impunity will end in a reckoning beyond their control.

translation: Hastening forward, their heads raised up, their gaze not returning to them, and their hearts are void.
interpretation: This describes the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, driven toward reckoning in extreme terror. They rush ahead helplessly, their heads uplifted and their eyes fixed in a vacant stare, unable to blink or turn away because of overwhelming dread. Their hearts are “void”—empty of faith, reason, resolve, and hope—collapsed under fear and humiliation before God.

translation: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, “Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.” [It will be said], “Did you not swear before that there would be no end for you?”
interpretation: This verse warns humanity before the arrival of the inevitable Day of Reckoning, when the wrongdoers will witness the punishment and desperately ask for a brief delay so they can respond to God’s invitation and obey His messengers. Their plea exposes the futility of postponing faith until the moment of seeing the consequence. They are then rebuked by being reminded of their earlier oaths and arrogant assumptions that they would never be removed from their worldly condition, that no end or accountability awaited them. The verse thus teaches that false security, denial of resurrection, and delaying repentance do not alter the certainty of judgment; once the punishment is witnessed, the offer of faith and obedience is no longer a sincere choice but a panicked concession, and the opportunity for repentance has passed.

translation: And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We presented for you the parables.
interpretation: This verse confronts its addressees with the ruins and histories of earlier communities that destroyed themselves through disbelief, injustice, and sin. Their ability to live in those very dwellings, and their knowledge of how God visited those people with punishment, removes any plea of ignorance. The 'parables' are the repeated divine warnings and lessons in revelation and history, clarifying that God's law against wrongdoing does not change. Hence the verse is a call to repent and reform before the same fate overtakes them: past destruction is not mere story but a mirror and warning for those who persist in the same self-destructive conduct.

translation: And they plotted their plot, but their plot is with Allah, even if their plot were such that the mountains would be moved thereby.
interpretation: This verse affirms that no matter how immense and destructive the schemes of the wicked may be—so great that they could almost uproot mountains—they remain fully known, encompassed, and controlled by Allah. He will not let their plots defeat His will; rather, He will bring their plots to nothing and turn their evil consequences back upon them, so the believers should place their trust in Him and not fear the power of the plotters.

translation: So do not ever think that Allah will break His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is All-Mighty, Possessor of Retribution.
interpretation: This is a firm assurance that God will fulfill the promises He made to His prophets and messengers: help, victory, protection, and the eventual establishment of truth, as well as the punishment of those who reject and oppose them. God is not unable, forgetful, or bound by time; He is All-Mighty, so nothing can prevent Him, and He is the One who exacts vengeance upon the arrogant and unjust. The apparent delay in the fulfillment of His promise is not a breach of it; rather, it is part of His wise decree, giving respite so that proof may be established, while His final justice and retribution remain certain.

translation: On the Day when the earth will be changed into another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.
interpretation: This verse describes the reality of the resurrection: the present earth and heavens will not remain as they are; God will transform and replace them with another earth and other heavens, and every human being will be brought out and made to stand exposed before Allah, who is uniquely One and utterly dominant, so that no created thing has any power to hide, flee, or resist His judgment. The event is a display of His sole lordship and irresistible might, and it establishes that the final reckoning occurs in a new creation entirely subject to Him.

translation: And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in chains.
interpretation: This verse depicts the humiliating condition of those who rejected faith and persisted in sin: on the Day of Judgment they will be visibly shackled and bound together in fetters, stripped of all freedom, power, and escape, as a manifestation of their subjection to divine judgment and the punishment they earned.

translation: Their garments are of pitch, and the Fire will cover their faces.
interpretation: This portrays the utter degradation and inescapable torment of the people of Hell: their clothing is made from black, sticky, highly flammable tar, which will cling to their bodies and intensify the burning instead of shielding them, while the Fire itself sweeps over their faces—the most honored part of a person—leaving them exposed, disgraced, and consumed by punishment.

translation: So that Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God’s judgment is perfectly just and universal: every soul will receive exactly what its deeds deserve, without any loss or addition. The phrase “swift in reckoning” means that God’s accounting is never delayed, burdensome, or dependent on records or witnesses; His knowledge encompasses every action, intention, and hidden motive, so He will settle all accounts instantly and with absolute precision.

translation: This is a proclamation for mankind, so that they may be warned by it, and so that they may know that He is only One God, and so that people of understanding may remember.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a universal address whose purpose is not mere information but transformation: it warns people of the consequences of heedlessness, leads them to the knowledge that all divinity belongs to the One God alone, and calls those who possess sound reason and discerning hearts to remember Him continually. True understanding is therefore not simply intellectual, but the ability to receive the warning, recognize God’s oneness, and let that recognition live on in remembrance and heedfulness.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: The disjointed letters at the beginning are a divine sign whose precise meaning is left to Allah, and they draw attention to the miraculous nature of the revelation. The verse affirms that what is being recited consists of the signs of the revealed Book, a Qur'an that clarifies truth, guidance, and the path to God, making its message evident and distinguishing right from wrong.

translation: Perhaps the disbelievers will wish that they had been Muslims.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers witness the reality of Allah’s punishment and the reward prepared for the believers, they will deeply regret their disbelief and wish they had submitted to Allah as Muslims in worldly life. That wish will then be of no benefit, so the verse warns people to accept Islam and live as Muslims before that time.

translation: Leave them to eat and enjoy, and let [false] hope divert them, for they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning that those who are heedless of divine guidance may be left for a time to their worldly appetites and false expectations, but their delusion will not last; soon they will come to know the truth and face the consequences of their heedlessness.

translation: And We did not destroy any city except that it had a known decree.
interpretation: This means that no community or town is ever destroyed except at the exact time already decreed and recorded with Allah; its destruction has a fixed, known term that cannot be advanced or delayed, and it occurs according to divine wisdom and justice, not arbitrarily.

translation: No community can advance its term, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: This verse affirms that every people has a fixed, divinely appointed lifespan and moment of reckoning. Neither their heedlessness nor their power can alter Allah’s timing: they cannot bring the end sooner to escape accountability, nor push it back to gain more time. It warns that the respite granted is finite, so they should respond to guidance before the appointed decree arrives, because God’s judgment is exact and inescapable.

translation: And they said, “O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are mad.”
interpretation: This is a mocking address by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad. They sarcastically acknowledge his claim that the Qur’an, the Reminder, has been revealed to him, but they use it as a taunt, accusing him of insanity. Their accusation does not come from evidence or reasoned objection; it is a rejection of the revelation and a way to avoid confronting its message. It shows how the arrogant deniers responded to the truth by insulting the messenger rather than reflecting on what was sent down to him.

translation: Why do you not bring us the angels, if you should be of the truthful?
interpretation: This is a demand of stubborn denial: the disbelievers are challenging the Prophet to produce angels as a sign on their own terms, trying to make the truth dependent on their requested miracle rather than on God’s revealed guidance. It exposes their arrogance and insincerity, since signs are sent by God’s command and wisdom, not according to human demands.

translation: We do not send down the angels except with the truth, and then they would not be granted respite.
interpretation: Angels descend only by Allah’s command and for a true, wise purpose—not to gratify the disbelievers’ challenge to see them. If the angels were sent as they demanded, the matter would become decisive, and the rejecters would receive no delay before the punishment.

translation: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its Guardian.
interpretation: God affirms that He alone revealed the Qur’an and has taken upon Himself the absolute responsibility to preserve it from corruption, alteration, loss, and falsehood, guaranteeing its continued protection and purity as the final divine guidance for humanity.

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] before you among the sects of the ancients.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet Muhammad by reminding him that his experience of being rejected and mocked was not unique: God had already sent messengers to earlier communities that had divided into different factions and groups. Those messengers delivered divine guidance to their peoples, yet many among those sects denied them. The verse therefore establishes a recurring pattern in human history—God sends warners within human societies, and rejection often follows—while also affirming that the Prophet’s mission stands in the same line as previous prophecies. It calls him to remain steadfast, knowing that the opposition of his people is neither new nor a sign that his message is false.

translation: And no messenger comes to them except that they mock him.
interpretation: This verse condemns the persistent arrogance of those who reject divine guidance: whenever God sends a messenger to call them back to truth, they respond not with serious reflection but with ridicule. Their mockery reveals that their rejection is not based on clear proof against the message, but on pride, heedlessness, and a refusal to submit. It also consoles the Prophet by showing that such scorn is the established way of fallen nations toward God’s messengers, and it warns that mocking the truth only leads to regret and ruin.

translation: Thus do We insert it [i.e., disbelief] into the hearts of the criminals.
