interpretation: This means that as a punishment for their persistent mockery and rejection of the messengers, Allah causes disbelief and denial to enter deeply into the hearts of the sinful. Their hearts become hardened so that they will not believe in the message, just as was the case with the criminal nations before them.

translation: They do not believe in it, and the precedent of the former peoples has already passed.
interpretation: This verse declares that the deniers persist in rejecting the revelation, and their rejection is not something new: Allah’s established way with earlier communities that denied His messengers has already unfolded. That pattern serves as a warning that the same divine judgment will overtake those who continue in disbelief, since the fate of the former nations stands as an already-passed precedent.

translation: And if We opened for them a gate from the heaven and they continued therein to ascend,
interpretation: It means that the disbelievers’ rejection is not caused by a lack of extraordinary signs. Even if the greatest sensory miracle were granted to them—a gate from heaven opened and they were made to ascend through it—they would still not surrender in faith. Their denial is rooted in stubbornness and spiritual blindness, so they would explain away the miracle as magic or illusion rather than accept the truth. Guidance therefore depends not merely on witnessing wonders but on a heart willing to submit to Allah.

translation: They would surely say, "Our eyes have only been dazzled; rather, we are a people bewitched."
interpretation: This verse exposes the condition of those who are determined to reject the truth: even if they were shown an unmistakable heavenly sign, they would not accept it as divine guidance. Instead, they would explain it away by claiming their perception has been impaired or that they have fallen under magic. Their denial is therefore not caused by insufficient evidence, but by an entrenched refusal to submit to God and acknowledge His power.

translation: And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations, and We have adorned it for those who look.
interpretation: This verse declares that God placed the great constellations in the heavens and made the sky beautiful and adorned for all who observe it, so that people may reflect on His power, wisdom, and bounty, and recognize the order and splendor of His creation.

translation: And We have guarded it from every accursed devil.
interpretation: The pronoun “it” refers to the heaven/sky mentioned in the surrounding context. God safeguards the heavenly realm from every devil who is rejected and driven away from His mercy, preventing such beings from ascending to eavesdrop on the angels or from corrupting the divine order of the heavens.

translation: Except one who steals a hearing, then a clear blazing flame follows him.
interpretation: This means that any jinn or devil who tries to eavesdrop on the heavenly assembly is pursued by a visible, piercing flame that drives him away and burns him, so the hidden news of the heavens cannot be stolen or conveyed.

translation: And the earth We spread out, and cast therein firm mountains, and caused to grow therein every thing in due measure.
interpretation: This verse is a call to recognize Allah’s power and wisdom in preparing the earth for human life: He spread it out as a habitable surface, placed firm mountains to stabilize it, and brought forth all kinds of growth and provisions in exact measure and balance. It teaches that creation is not random but deliberately ordered, measured, and sustained by Allah, and that these signs should lead people to gratitude, reliance upon Him, and awareness that the One who arranged the earth’s balance is able to resurrect and reckon His creation.

translation: And We have made for you therein means of livelihood, and [for] those whom you do not provide.
interpretation: Allah states that He has placed in the earth resources and means of sustenance for human beings, and that He also sustains other creatures—whether people, animals, or dependents—that humans are not responsible for providing. The verse teaches that provision ultimately comes from Allah alone, not from human power or ownership, and it reminds people of His all-encompassing care over creation.

translation: And there is not a thing but that its treasures are with Us, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every created thing—whether material provision, rain, sustenance, knowledge, life, or any blessing—has its source and storehouse solely with God. He alone owns and controls all resources without limit, and nothing reaches creation except by His decree, in a precise amount and timing determined by His wisdom. No creature can increase, decrease, hasten, or withhold what God has measured. Thus people are meant to rely upon Him, seek from Him alone, and recognize that whatever they receive is a measured trust from His unlimited treasury, apportioned according to divine knowledge and purpose.

translation: And We sent the winds as fertilizing agents, then We sent down water from the sky and gave it to you to drink, and you are not the ones who store it.
interpretation: This means that Allah alone directs the winds to carry moisture and pollen, cause clouds to bear rain, and send down water as a provision of life and drink; human beings have no independent power to create, preserve, or withhold that water, so the true Keeper and Sustainer of all provision is Allah alone.

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors.
interpretation: Allah alone is the sole source of life and death: He grants existence and decrees its end, and after all creation perishes, He remains as the eternal Owner and Inheritor of everything, to whom all things ultimately return.

translation: And indeed, We have known those who came before among you, and indeed, We have known those who will come after.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge fully encompasses every generation of humanity—those who have already passed and those yet to come, the earlier and the later, the dead and the living. None of them is hidden from Him, and He will gather them all for judgment and recompense.

translation: And indeed, your Lord will gather them together. Indeed, He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms the certainty of the resurrection and the gathering of all creation before Allah for judgment. It declares that the Lord—who created and sustains all—will inevitably bring every person back to life and assemble them, regardless of whether they believed or denied, were first or last. The mention of Allah’s wisdom and knowledge means His gathering is not arbitrary: it is the necessary consequence of His perfect wisdom, which requires accountability, and His all-encompassing knowledge, which records every deed, word, and hidden intention. Thus the verse assures the truthful that divine justice will be fulfilled and warns the heedless that nothing escapes Allah’s knowledge or power.

translation: And indeed, We created man from clay, from black mud altered.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of Adam, the first human being, from earthly matter: a dark, molded clay. It teaches that human beings are created from a lowly, physical origin by God's power, while their true honor comes from the divine spirit and command given to them. It also points to God's ability to originate life from inert matter and, by extension, to resurrect the dead.

translation: And the jinn We created before from scorching fire.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the jinn were brought into existence before humankind and that their original creation was from a fire of intense, penetrating heat. It establishes Allah's sole creative power, the precedence of the jinn in creation, and that the jinn are created beings subject to His command, not divine or equal to Him.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I am creating a human being from clay, from black mud altered.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that God alone is the Creator and that He fashioned the first human being, Adam, from earthly matter—clay that becomes dry and resonant and dark, molded mud—so that humanity’s origin is humble and wholly dependent on His creative will. It establishes that human worth is not derived from physical substance but from God’s act of creation and His later breathing of the spirit into him, and it prepares for the angels’ response and the command to honor Adam.

translation: So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down before him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse is God addressing the angels concerning the creation of Adam: after forming him in due proportion and breathing into him a soul from His command, the angels were commanded to prostrate before him as an act of honor and acknowledgment of his favored status, not as worship, for worship belongs to God alone. Their prostration signifies the dignity God bestowed upon the human being and the obligation of the angels to submit to God’s command.

translation: Then the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together.
interpretation: This emphasizes the angels’ perfect and unanimous obedience to Allah’s command: every single angel submitted without exception, and their prostration was an act of worship to Allah in compliance with His order, not worship of Adam himself.

translation: Except Iblis; he refused to be among those who prostrate.
interpretation: This verse shows that Iblis was not simply unable to obey, but he arrogantly refused the command of Allah to join the angels in prostrating. His refusal was an act of willful pride and rebellion, and by separating himself from "those who prostrate," he cut himself off from the company of the humble and obedient. The prostration here was an act of submission commanded by Allah, and Iblis's rejection reveals that arrogance can lead a creature to defy a direct divine order even when surrounded by examples of obedience.

translation: He said: O Iblis, what is the matter with you that you are not among those who prostrate?
interpretation: This is a question of reproach and rebuke from Allah to Iblis, not a request for information. It exposes that his refusal to prostrate was not due to any incapacity or valid excuse, but to willful arrogance and disobedience. The prostration was a command from Allah honoring Adam, not worship of Adam; those who prostrated were obeying Allah. Iblis’s refusal placed him outside the ranks of the obedient and marked the beginning of his rebellion and downfall.

translation: He said, "I was not going to prostrate to a human whom You created out of dried clay, from black mud altered."
interpretation: This verse exposes Iblis’s arrogant refusal to obey Allah’s command. His words reveal that he judged worth by physical origin rather than by divine command, treating Adam’s creation from clay as grounds for contempt. The prostration was never worship of Adam; it was an act of obedience to Allah and acknowledgment of His power to create and honor whom He wills. Iblis’s rebellion shows how pride and self-exaltation can make a creature rationalize disobedience, and it warns against measuring superiority by material descent while ignoring God’s authority and the honor He grants.

translation: He said, “Then get out of it, for indeed you are accursed.”
interpretation: This is a decree of banishment: Iblis is driven out from the station of divine favor and honor because of his arrogant refusal, and “rajim” means he is expelled, rejected, and cut off from God’s mercy.

translation: And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: This is a declaration of Iblis’s permanent exclusion from God’s mercy: the curse is not a passing punishment but a fixed sentence that remains upon him until the Day of Recompense. It teaches that willful defiance of God’s command brings spiritual ruin, and that any delay or respite granted to the disobedient is not a sign of divine approval but part of the decree leading to final accountability.

translation: He said: My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This is Iblis’s request after he was cursed: he does not seek forgiveness or reform, but asks God to delay his punishment and death so he may continue leading people astray until the Day of Resurrection. It exposes his arrogant persistence in enmity and shows that his power and respite are only temporary, lasting until the appointed time when all will be raised for judgment.

translation: [Allah] said, "So indeed, you are among those granted respite."
interpretation: This verse affirms that God granted Iblis the delay he requested, allowing him to remain until the appointed time. It shows that such respite is not a mark of honor or acceptance, but a decree of divine wisdom: Iblis is permitted to exist and tempt as a trial for humankind only within the limits God has set. His power is neither independent nor ultimate, and his punishment is merely postponed, not cancelled; the final reckoning remains certain under God's sovereign will.

translation: until the Day of the known appointed time
interpretation: This refers to the respite granted to Iblis until the Day of Resurrection, the fixed time whose exact occurrence is known only to Allah, when all creation will be raised and judged.

translation: He said, "My Lord, because You have caused me to err, I will surely beautify [evil] for them on the earth, and I will surely mislead them all."
interpretation: This is Satan's defiant pledge after his expulsion: he uses God's decree as a pretext, though his own arrogance caused his fall. His strategy is to make sin and worldly life attractive to human beings, so that disobedience seems desirable and divine guidance seems burdensome, and then to pull them away from God collectively. The verse exposes his enmity and method—deception through adornment and false promise—while showing that his influence operates only by God's permission; the following verse clarifies that God's sincere servants are exempt from his claim to mislead all.

translation: Except Your servants among them, the sincerely devoted / those whom You have chosen and purified.
interpretation: This exception declares that Satan’s power to mislead is not absolute: it cannot penetrate the hearts of those whom God has purified and made sincere in His service. Their protection lies not merely in their own effort but in God’s electing grace, which renders them immune to satanic domination and keeps their worship pure from hypocrisy and corrupt intention.

translation: He said, "This is a straight path [leading] to Me."
interpretation: It means that the way of truth, sincere worship, and obedience is a path established and guarded by Allah, leading directly to Him; He has taken it upon Himself to make it clear and to protect those who follow it from the misguidance of Satan.

translation: Indeed, over My servants you have no authority, except those who follow you among the deviators.
interpretation: Allah addresses Iblis, declaring that he has no coercive power or dominion over God's sincere servants. His influence can reach only those who willingly choose to follow him and are already among the misguided. Thus, Satan cannot force the faithful into sin; his authority is limited to those who surrender to his path by their own choice and turn away from divine guidance.

translation: And indeed, Hell is the promised appointment for them all.
interpretation: This verse declares that Hell is the fixed and unavoidable destination decreed by God for every soul that knowingly follows the path of disbelief and rebellion; they will all be gathered there without exception, and none of them can escape the appointed meeting with its recompense.

translation: It has seven gates; for every gate there is an appointed portion of them.
interpretation: This describes Hell as having seven gates or levels, each one assigned a specific share of its inhabitants. The verse indicates that those who enter Hell are divided among these gates according to their deeds, and each gate receives exactly the portion allotted to it by God's decree and justice.

translation: Indeed, the righteous are among gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse declares the reward of the God-conscious: those who guard themselves against disobedience to Allah and live with taqwa will abide in gardens of perpetual delight and flowing springs. The pairing of gardens and springs conveys complete bliss, constant freshness, and divine provision, as springs give life, beauty, and nourishment. Their being 'in' these blessings indicates a settled state of honor and security, not a passing gift. It also implies that taqwa leads to the enjoyment of Allah’s pleasure in an eternal abode, in contrast to the fate of the heedless and sinful.

translation: Enter it in peace and security.
interpretation: This is God’s gracious address to the people of Paradise, informing them that their entry is granted with perfect peace and complete safety. It means they will be secure from every fear, grief, punishment, and harm, and they will dwell in enduring harmony, divine acceptance, and everlasting well-being.

translation: And We shall remove from their hearts any rancor; they will be brothers, reclining on couches facing one another.
interpretation: This means that in Paradise God will purify the believers’ hearts from every trace of resentment, envy, hatred, and ill will, so that nothing remains to disturb their relationships. They will be joined in sincere brotherhood and placed on raised couches facing one another, which signifies perfect harmony, mutual delight, and the absence of any estrangement or turning away.

translation: No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they ever be expelled from it.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the people of Paradise will enjoy perfect, uninterrupted rest: no weariness, hardship, or exhaustion will ever affect them, and their bliss will be permanent, for they will never be removed or cast out of it.

translation: Inform My servants that I am indeed the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: Allah commands His Prophet to announce to all His servants that His forgiveness and mercy are certain and vast, so that those who sin may not despair of His pardon and those who believe may place their hope in Him.

translation: And that My punishment is the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God's punishment is certain, severe, and agonizing. It warns against presuming upon divine mercy while persisting in disobedience; God's justice ensures that unrepentant wrongdoing ultimately meets painful retribution. It emphasizes the reality of accountability and the seriousness of divine chastisement for those who reject His guidance.

translation: And inform them about the guests of Abraham.
interpretation: It means that Allah commands His Prophet to tell the people about the angels who came to Abraham as honored guests, so they may reflect on Allah’s power, the reality of unseen messengers, and the certainty of His decree—both glad tidings for the righteous and warning for the wicked.

translation: When they entered upon him and said, 'Peace.' He said, 'Indeed, we are fearful of you.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who visited Prophet Ibrahim in human form. Their greeting of peace was met with fear because their unexpected appearance and refusal to eat the food he offered made him apprehensive. His reaction reflects natural human caution toward strangers, while the scene also shows that God's angelic messengers ultimately come with reassurance and glad tidings, not harm.

translation: They said, 'Do not fear. Indeed, we give you good tidings of a knowledgeable boy.'
interpretation: The angels reassure Abraham, telling him not to be afraid, and announce to him the glad news of a son who will be endowed with knowledge—a divine gift showing God's power to grant blessings even beyond ordinary human expectation.

translation: He said, “Have you given me good tidings though old age has come upon me? So what good tidings are you giving?”
interpretation: Abraham is astonished that the angels bring him news of a child when he has reached extreme old age and the natural means of having children have passed. His question is not a rejection of God’s promise but an expression of wonder at how it will come to pass. It points to the fact that God’s power is not limited by age, weakness, or ordinary causes, and that His glad tidings are certain even when human reason sees no way.

translation: They said, "We have given you glad tidings in truth, so do not be among those who despair."
interpretation: The angels affirm that the good news they bring is true and grounded in God’s certain promise, not in ordinary human calculations. Abraham is therefore told not to fall into despair, because despair of God’s mercy and power is blameworthy; it doubts His ability to bring about what He has promised even when all apparent causes seem impossible. The verse teaches the believer to meet divine promises with hope and trust, since God’s truth is never overcome by age, weakness, or natural limitation.

translation: He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray?"
interpretation: This verse teaches that losing hope in God's mercy is a mark of those who have wandered from the right path. Abraham’s words are a rebuke to despair: no matter how impossible a situation may seem, a believer must remain confident in God's unlimited mercy, power, and grace, because despairing of His mercy is incompatible with true faith and guidance.

translation: He said, "Then what is your mission, O messengers?"
interpretation: Here Abraham asks the angels about the specific errand and decree for which God had sent them, beyond the glad tidings they had already conveyed. The word “mission” points to a serious, assigned matter, and addressing them as “messengers” acknowledges that they act only under God’s command. His question reflects prophetic courtesy and discernment: he recognizes that their visit carries a further divine purpose and seeks to know what it is.

translation: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a criminal people."
interpretation: These are the words of the angelic messengers who visited Prophet Ibrahim. They inform him that their mission from Allah is directed toward a people—the people of Lut—who have become criminals through their persistent disbelief, moral corruption, and grave sins, and who are therefore deserving of divine punishment.

translation: Except the family of Lot; indeed, we will surely save them all.
interpretation: This verse declares that Lot’s household is exempted from the destruction decreed upon his people: God will deliver them together from the punishment. It affirms that divine mercy and rescue accompany the believers among Lot’s family, separating them from the doomed transgressors; the later qualification concerning Lot’s wife shows that this salvation applies to those who truly follow God’s command.

translation: Except his wife; We decreed that she would be among those who remain behind.
interpretation: God’s decree excludes Lot’s wife from the deliverance granted to Lot’s family: she was foreordained to stay behind with the doomed people, not because of any lack of prophetic kinship, but because she persisted in disbelief and betrayal. The verse teaches that divine judgment is decisive and that family ties offer no protection when one chooses the way of the disbelievers.

translation: So when the messengers came to the family of Lot,
interpretation: The angels sent by God arrived at Lot’s household to carry out His decree: they came to rescue Lot and the believers among his family and to announce the impending destruction of his people for their grave sins. This moment marks the beginning of the fulfillment of God’s judgment against the city, with Lot’s household singled out for salvation except for his wife, who was among those doomed.

translation: He said, "Indeed, you are a people unknown."
interpretation: This is Lot’s statement to the angels who came to him in human form. He did not recognize them as familiar people, so he treated them as strangers and was cautious, fearing that they might be a threat or that his people might harm them. The word "munkarūn" here means unknown or unrecognized, not people who deny the truth.

translation: They said, "Rather, we have brought you that which they were disputing."
interpretation: The angels correct Lot's impression that they were unknown strangers: they have not come without purpose, but are bearers of the very punishment and decree that his people had long questioned, doubted, and argued against. Their arrival thus confirms the truth of the warning and signals that the matter the disbelievers treated as uncertain is now coming to pass.

translation: And we have brought you the truth, and indeed we are truthful.
interpretation: These are the angels assuring Prophet Lot that what they have come with is the true decree of God, not a false alarm or idle threat. They emphasize that their message concerning the destruction of his people and the deliverance of his family is certain and that they are entirely truthful in what they convey. Therefore, he should receive their command with firm conviction and act without doubt, trusting that God's judgment will inevitably come to pass.

translation: So set out with your family during a portion of the night and follow behind them, and let not anyone among you look back, and go where you are commanded.
interpretation: This is God’s command to Lot to leave the doomed city with his household under cover of night. He is instructed to follow behind them so that he may guard them, and none is to look back at the city or its people. The command teaches complete detachment from a corrupt society that is about to face divine punishment, and it shows that deliverance comes through prompt obedience to God’s order. The destination is left unspecified because it is known to God, emphasizing that the believers must move forward in trust and submission, not lingering over what is being left behind or over the fate of those who rejected the truth.

translation: And We decreed to him that matter: that the remnant of these people would be cut off by morning.
interpretation: Allah had already determined and informed Lot of the fate of his people: their destruction was certain and would come upon them at daybreak, wiping them out completely so that no trace or continuing line among them would remain. The verse stresses that divine judgment is unavoidable, precisely timed, and total in its eradication of the guilty.

translation: And the people of the city came rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the inhabitants of Sodom coming to Lot’s house in a state of eager delight, expecting to gratify their sinful desires with his guests; their rejoicing reveals their hardened corruption and defiance rather than any righteous joy.

translation: He said, "Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me."
interpretation: This is the plea of Prophet Lot to his people when they came intending to commit an indecent act with his angelic guests. He appeals to them to honor the duty of hospitality and not to shame him by violating his guests, for harming a guest was considered a grave moral disgrace. He is expressing his vulnerability and moral outrage, seeking to deter them from their evil intention.

translation: And fear Allah, and do not disgrace me.
interpretation: This is a command to live with God-consciousness and to let that reverence restrain one from any conduct that humiliates or dishonors another. It teaches that true piety protects people’s dignity, especially the trust owed to guests, and that violating that trust is both a moral shame and an offense against the fear due to Allah.

translation: They said, 'Did we not forbid you from [receiving] the people?'
interpretation: This is the response of the people of Lot to Lot after he protested their intent to harm his guests. They remind him that they had already warned him not to shelter, protect, or interfere on behalf of any outsiders. The phrase 'the worlds' is used here to mean all people or strangers, emphasizing their claim that he had violated their prior prohibition. Their words expose their arrogance, their insistence on continuing in immorality, and their attempt to silence his moral objection by appealing to an agreement they themselves had imposed.

translation: He said, "These are my daughters, if you would be doers [of lawful marriage]."
interpretation: Prophet Lot, confronted by his people's wicked demand to assault his guests, offered them a lawful alternative—marriage to his daughters—if they were determined to satisfy their sexual desires. This shows the depths of his people's transgression and that the only permissible outlet for such desire is marriage, not sexual assault or violation of guests.

translation: By your life, indeed they were in their intoxication, wandering blindly.
interpretation: Allah swears by the life of His Prophet to emphasize that the wrongdoers were so overwhelmed by their corrupt desires and heedlessness that their judgment was clouded like one intoxicated; they were not merely mistaken but blindly stumbling in error, unable to perceive the truth or recognize the gravity of their sin.

translation: Then the Blast seized them at sunrise.
interpretation: This means that Allah’s punishment, described as a devastating cry or blast, overtook them at the precise time of daybreak, when they had entered upon the morning. It conveys that the divine retribution came suddenly and irresistibly, after their persistent wrongdoing, leaving them no opportunity to escape or repent.

translation: So We made its highest part its lowest, and We rained upon them stones of baked clay.
interpretation: This verse expresses the totality and terrifying finality of the divine punishment sent upon the people of Lut. Their cities were overturned so that what had been elevated became lowest, and stones of hard baked clay were poured down upon them. Its meaning is that when a people persist in grave corruption and defiant immorality after prophetic warning, God can uproot the very order they trusted, reverse their stability, and bring destruction upon them from above and below as a precise and just requital. The "stones of sijjil" are not merely a natural disaster but a decree from God: hard, crushing, and inescapable. The verse thus warns that no society is secure in its power or prosperity if it continues to reject truth and violate the moral limits set by its Creator.

translation: Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern.
interpretation: The fate of the destroyed nations leaves visible traces and moral lessons for people of deep insight, who observe the outward evidence and infer the inner truth: that God's justice is real, His warnings are fulfilled, and corruption leads to ruin.

translation: And indeed, it is on an enduring road.
interpretation: This refers to the ruined settlements of the people of Lot, which were left on a still-existing and well-traveled route. Their remains serve as a lasting, visible warning to those who pass by, confirming that the punishment for their corruption was real and that the path of divine retribution is established and unchanged.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: The sign is a clear evidence and admonition that only faith enables one to receive: it confirms Allah's justice and the truth of His warning, and it calls the believers to take heed, remain steadfast, and avoid the paths that brought destruction upon those who rejected Him.

translation: And indeed, the companions of the thicket were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This refers to the people of Shu‘ayb, the dwellers of al-Aykah, who rejected Allah’s messenger and persisted in associating partners with Allah and in corrupt, unjust dealings. They were wrongdoers because of their denial and oppression, and so they incurred the punishment that came upon them.

translation: So We took retribution from them, and indeed they both are on a clear road.
interpretation: The dual pronoun refers to the two punished communities or their settlements: their destruction was Allah’s just retribution for their wrongdoing, and their ruins lie on an evident, traveled way, making their fate a manifest warning and lesson about the consequences of rejecting the messengers and persisting in corruption.

translation: And certainly the companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers.
interpretation: The people of al-Hijr—the rocky dwelling-place of Thamud—rejected God’s prophetic call, and in rejecting the messenger sent to them they rejected the whole prophetic mission, because every messenger came with the same essential demand: exclusive worship and obedience to God. Their denial was not merely a dispute with one man but a rejection of the divine guidance itself, and so God presents their destroyed civilization as a warning that denying His messengers brings ruin, even when the rejecters are powerful and secure in their carved mountain homes.

translation: And We gave them Our signs, but they were turning away from them.
interpretation: Allah granted the people of al-Hijr clear proofs and miracles, yet they persistently rejected them and turned their backs, refusing to accept the truth or benefit from the guidance.

translation: And they used to carve out of the mountains houses, feeling secure.
interpretation: This verse describes a people who trusted in their own strength and ingenuity, cutting luxurious dwellings into mountains and believing those strongholds made them safe from any harm. Their security was illusory: it was rooted in material power rather than in God, and therefore it could not protect them from divine judgment. The verse warns against the arrogance of relying on worldly defenses and assuming that wealth, architecture, or military strength can make one truly invulnerable.

translation: Then the Cry seized them at dawn.
interpretation: This means that the decreed punishment from God overtook the deniers suddenly at daybreak, at a time when they felt secure and heedless. It shows that no wealth, strength, or fortified dwelling can protect a people from divine judgment once it comes.

translation: So what they used to earn availed them nothing.
interpretation: It means that whatever wealth, deeds, or worldly gains they amassed brought them no benefit when Allah’s punishment came; none of it could protect them or avert their fate, showing that only faith and obedience to Allah are of true value.

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them except in truth. And indeed, the Hour is surely coming; so forgive with gracious forgiveness.
interpretation: God’s creation is not purposeless or in vain; it is founded upon truth, wisdom, justice, and the certainty of final reckoning. Because the Hour will inevitably come and all matters will be judged by God, the Prophet and the believers are told not to pursue personal retaliation against those who wrong them, but to pardon them in a noble and ungrudging manner—overlooking offenses without reproach, bitterness, or demand for repayment. This gracious forgiveness reflects reliance on God’s ultimate justice and is itself a moral and spiritual victory.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is the All-Creator, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God alone possesses absolute creative power and absolute knowledge: He originates and sustains all things, and His knowledge encompasses everything—what has been, what is, what will be, and every hidden intention and consequence. Therefore, His creation is never beyond His awareness or control, and He is perfectly able to bring forth, nurture, re-create, and judge all matters with complete wisdom and justice.

translation: And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur’an.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Prophet Muhammad that God has granted him the seven oft-repeated verses—understood by many interpreters as Surat al-Fatiha, recited repeatedly in every prayer—and the great Qur’an as a whole, as guidance, mercy, and an immense honor.

translation: Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given certain of them to enjoy, and do not grieve over them, and lower your wing to the believers.
interpretation: This is a divine directive to the Prophet, and by extension to the believers, not to let the temporary enjoyments, wealth, and status granted to those who reject the truth become the object of longing or the cause of grief; rather, one’s concern should remain with faith and with showing humble, compassionate care to the believers.

translation: And say, 'Indeed, I am the clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to proclaim openly that his role is to deliver a clear and unambiguous warning: that God's message has come, and that people are accountable for how they respond to it, so no one can plead ignorance or confusion about the warning.

translation: Just as We sent down [the Scripture] to those who divided [it].
interpretation: This verse condemns those who fragment God's revealed Book, accepting some parts while rejecting, distorting, or mocking others. It reminds the Prophet that earlier recipients of revelation also split their Scriptures, so the opposition of the Quraysh is not unprecedented. Allah will question every one of them about what they did, and the verse serves as a warning that dividing God's message into convenient pieces is a grave offense deserving divine accountability.

translation: Those who have made the Qur’an into fragments.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who divide the Qur’an into separate parts, accepting some of it while rejecting or distorting others according to their whims. They refuse to submit to it as a unified divine revelation, treating its verses selectively instead of embracing the whole Book as the word of God.

translation: So by your Lord, We will surely question them all.
interpretation: Allah swears by His own Lordship that He will bring every one of them to account and question them all concerning what they used to do, especially their response to the Qur’an and the messengers.

translation: about what they used to do
interpretation: This phrase establishes that accountability before God is personal: no one will be questioned about the deeds of others, especially the deeds of past communities. It emphasizes that every person is answerable only for his or her own actions, while God fully knows and will justly repay all that people habitually did. In the Qur'anic context 'you will not be asked about what they used to do,' it warns against assuming responsibility for or relying on the record of previous generations; each soul stands before God on its own deeds.

translation: So proclaim openly what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to deliver the divine message publicly and decisively, without concealment or compromise, and to disengage from the idolaters’ hostility and falsehood, leaving their response and judgment to God rather than allowing their opposition to hinder the proclamation of truth.

translation: Indeed, We are sufficient for you against the mockers.
interpretation: This is God's direct assurance to the Prophet Muhammad that He Himself will defend him against those who ridicule and mock him and his message. Their mockery cannot ultimately harm him or stop the truth; God will ward off their schemes and bring about His decree, so the Prophet should not be grieved or deterred by their scorn.

translation: Those who set up another god alongside Allah — they will soon know.
interpretation: This is a severe warning against polytheism: those who assign a partner or rival to Allah in worship, lordship, or devotion will inevitably come to know the truth of their error and face its consequence. It affirms Allah’s exclusive right to be worshipped alone and declares that their delay is not impunity; the knowledge they will receive is the certainty of punishment and the failure of their false gods.

translation: And We certainly know that your breast tightens because of what they say.
interpretation: This is a divine consolation to the Prophet: Allah, who knows the hidden, is fully aware of the inward constriction, sadness, and pressure he feels because of the mockery, denial, and falsehood uttered by his opponents. The verse reassures him that his pain is seen by his Lord, that their words cannot diminish his rank or thwart God’s purpose, and that Allah will judge and vindicate him. It also teaches the believer to bring the hurt caused by people’s words to Allah, seeking relief in His remembrance rather than letting grief take over the heart.

translation: So glorify the praises of your Lord and be among those who prostrate.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet—and every believer—to cure the distress caused by the mockery and opposition of the deniers by turning to God in glorification joined with praise, and by persisting in humble prostration before Him; it teaches that intimate worship, especially prayer and prostration, lifts the heart from grief and anchors it in God’s majesty and mercy.

translation: And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.
interpretation: This verse commands the believer to remain steadfast in worshipping and obeying Allah alone for as long as life lasts, until death arrives—called al-yaqin, “certainty,” because it is the inescapable reality that every soul must meet; thus worship is not to be abandoned or slackened before that appointed end.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Glory be to Him, and Exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s decree—whether the coming of the Hour, His judgment, or His promised punishment—is inevitable and already determined, so no one should demand it impatiently or mockingly. It directs people to prepare through faith and obedience rather than challenge divine timing. It also declares Allah’s absolute transcendence: He is far above any partners, idols, or equals that people ascribe to Him.

translation: He sends down the angels with the Spirit [revelation] by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, [saying], "Warn that there is no deity except Me, so fear Me."
interpretation: This verse teaches that guidance and warning are not human inventions but descend by God's sovereign command: He sends His angels carrying the Spirit—the revelation that gives life to hearts—to whichever servants He chooses as messengers. Their mission is to awaken people to the central truth that divinity belongs to God alone, and that this truth demands taqwa: reverent obedience, guarding oneself from His displeasure, and ordering life around His exclusive lordship.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. Exalted is He above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse establishes that the heavens and the earth were created by God alone with truth, purpose, and wisdom, not in play or falsehood; therefore He is far exalted and absolutely free from any partners, idols, or equals that the polytheists associate with Him.

translation: He created man from a sperm-drop; then behold, he is an open disputant.
interpretation: This verse reproaches human arrogance: despite being created from a lowly fluid, man often becomes a blatant arguer against his Creator, using his God-given intellect and speech to dispute divine truth and deny accountability. It highlights the irony that the same being who owes his existence to God turns into an outspoken opponent, showing ingratitude and contentiousness rather than humility and submission.

translation: And the grazing livestock He created for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: Allah reminds humankind of His providence in creating livestock, which meet essential needs: their wool, hair, and hides provide warmth and clothing; they yield many other benefits such as milk, transport, and agricultural service; and their meat is lawful food. This calls for gratitude to the Creator and responsible, merciful use of these creatures.

translation: And there is beauty in them for you when you bring them home in the evening and when you send them out to pasture in the morning.
interpretation: This verse points to a non-material blessing in livestock: the sense of delight, dignity, and joy their owners experience at the sight of the herds returning in the evening after grazing and heading out in the morning. Alongside the tangible benefits of milk, meat, wool, and transport, God mentions the aesthetic and emotional comfort they add to human life, showing that His provision includes both utility and beauty.

translation: And they carry your heavy loads to a land that you could not reach except with hardship to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights a sign of God's mercy in creation: He has subjected livestock and animals to serve people by carrying their heavy goods across long distances, journeys that would otherwise exhaust and distress them. The ability to transport burdens to distant lands is a divine blessing that makes trade, travel, and daily livelihood possible. By ending with “Indeed, your Lord is Most Compassionate, Most Merciful,” the verse directs the heart to recognize that God’s compassion and mercy are the source of these provisions, and it calls for gratitude, trust in Him, and acknowledgment of His care for human needs.

translation: And [He created] the horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride and as adornment. And He creates what you do not know.
interpretation: Allah reminds humanity of His favor in providing animals suited for riding and for beauty, while declaring that His creation is not limited to what people can perceive or imagine; He continually brings into existence forms of creation, knowledge, and means beyond human awareness, calling attention to His unlimited power and the limits of human knowledge.

translation: And upon Allah is the direction of the [right] way, and among them are deviating ways. And if He had willed, He would have guided you all together.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the straight path is made clear by Allah and that returning to Him is the ultimate aim, while also acknowledging that some ways swerve away from His guidance. It teaches that Allah is not unable to guide all people; rather, if He had willed, He could have compelled every soul to faith. But He has established the road of truth, sent messengers and signs, and left guidance to be sought and accepted by choice. Thus the verse calls the servant to seek the upright way from Allah alone, avoid deviating paths, and recognize that guidance is entirely in Allah’s hand.

translation: He is the One who sends down water from the sky; from it you have drink, and from it are trees in which you graze [your livestock].
interpretation: The verse points to Allah’s exclusive power and bounty in providing rain, which meets two essential needs: direct drinking water and the growth of vegetation that sustains grazing livestock; it is therefore a call to acknowledge His providence, rely upon Him, and give thanks by worshiping Him alone.

translation: He causes to grow for you by it the crops, olives, date palms, grapevines, and from all kinds of fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse directs reflection to God’s creative power and providential care: from one brought-down water He produces a vast diversity of life-sustaining fruits, each with its own form, taste, and benefit, beyond what human power could originate. The sign is not merely in the abundance of provision but in the order, variety, and generosity embedded in it, which should lead the thoughtful person from the blessing to the Giver—awakening gratitude, reliance upon Him, and recognition that all sustenance and life come from His command alone.

translation: And He has subjected to you the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who use their reason.
interpretation: This verse presents the ordered movements of time and the heavenly bodies as a continuous divine service to humanity: they are not independent powers but creatures compelled by Allah's command. Their regularity and benefit are signs that should lead people of sound intellect to recognize the Creator's oneness, wisdom, and mercy, and to worship Him alone.

translation: And whatever He has created for you on the earth, diverse in colors. Indeed in that is a sign for people who remember.
interpretation: This verse directs attention to the countless created things God has spread upon the earth for human benefit, varying in color, form, taste, and function. Their diversity and orderly usefulness are not random; they reveal the power, wisdom, and mercy of the Creator. For those who remember God and reflect on His blessings, these Signs lead to faith, gratitude, and devotion to Him alone.

translation: And it is He Who subjected the sea, so that you may eat from it fresh meat and extract from it ornaments which you wear. And you see the ships plowing through it, and [this is] so that you may seek of His bounty, and so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse presents the sea as a creation made subservient by Allah’s command, and its benefits—food, adornment, transport, and trade—are signs of His power and mercy. The mention of these blessings is not merely informational; it is a call to recognize that human ability to exploit the sea depends on God’s enabling, and that the proper response is shukr: grateful obedience, using His gifts within His guidance and acknowledging Him as the sole source of provision and favor.

translation: And He cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it shift with you, and rivers and roads, so that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse points to God's purposeful design in creation: He stabilizes the earth with mountains so it does not sway or disrupt human life, provides rivers as sources of water and sustenance, and lays out paths and routes so people can travel, trade, and find their way. The phrase 'so that you may be guided' carries a deeper meaning: these visible signs of order and provision should lead people to recognize their Creator, follow His guidance, and navigate both the physical world and the path to true faith and moral direction.

translation: And landmarks; and by the star they are guided.
interpretation: This verse points to Allah’s provision of both earthly and heavenly signs for guidance: visible landmarks help people find their way on land, and the stars direct them across the sky and seas. It signifies that just as He guides travelers through created signs, He also guides humanity toward the straight path through His revealed signs and messengers, calling them to recognize His lordship and follow His guidance.

translation: Is then He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical rebuke of any notion that the true Creator can be equated with beings or idols that have no power to create. It appeals to human reason and remembrance: if only God originates, forms, and sustains creation, then He alone deserves worship, and it is irrational to set alongside Him anything that cannot create at all. The closing question calls people to awaken from heedlessness and recall the fundamental distinction between the Creator and the created.

translation: And if you try to count the blessings of Allah, you will not be able to number them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This means that God’s favors—both visible and hidden, material and spiritual—are so vast and continuous that no human effort can fully reckon or repay them. The verse then names God as Forgiving and Merciful: He pardons the inevitable shortcomings in human gratitude, and His mercy continues to grant blessings despite that failure.

translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you reveal.
interpretation: This affirms that God’s knowledge is all-encompassing: He knows the secrets of the hearts and the deeds done openly. It calls believers to sincerity, guarding inner motives as well as outward conduct, since nothing—whether hidden or manifest—is beyond His awareness or accountability.

translation: And those whom they invoke besides Allah do not create anything, but they are themselves created.
interpretation: This verse declares the utter incapacity of every false object of worship. Whatever is called upon besides Allah has no creative power whatsoever; it cannot originate, sustain, or bring anything into existence. Rather, it is itself created, dependent, and subject to the power of Allah. Therefore, worship and divine attributes belong exclusively to the Creator, and directing them to created beings is futile and unjustified.

translation: Dead, not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse describes the false deities and idols that people invoke besides Allah: they are utterly lifeless and dead, possessing no life, power, or consciousness. They are so far removed from any divine attribute that they have no awareness whatsoever of the Hour or of the time when their worshippers will be raised for judgment. Thus the verse exposes the futility of worshipping created, lifeless things and directs all worship and reliance to the living, all-knowing Allah alone.

translation: Your god is one God. But those who do not believe in the Hereafter—their hearts are denying, and they are arrogant.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute oneness of God: He alone is the true deity, without partner, equal, or rival, and He alone deserves worship. It then explains that those who reject the Hereafter do not merely lack information; their hearts refuse the truth of God's oneness and accountability because arrogance has taken root in them. They are unwilling to submit to a single Lord and to the final judgment that would expose their pride. Thus, denial of the Hereafter and arrogance are linked: the heart that refuses to humble itself before God also refuses the truth of resurrection and reckoning.

translation: Assuredly, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge encompasses both the hidden and the open: nothing people conceal in their hearts, nor anything they proclaim publicly, escapes Him. The phrase “He does not love the arrogant” means that those who exalt themselves above the truth, refuse humble submission to Allah, and look down upon His messengers and believing servants incur His displeasure and are excluded from His love and favor. Thus the verse warns that arrogance is not merely a social fault but a spiritual condition that Allah rejects, and it consoles the believers that Allah fully knows the secret plots, mockery, and schemes of the proud, even when they hide them.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?' they say, 'Legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbelievers’ arrogant rejection of revelation. When asked about what Allah sent down to His Messenger, they do not answer with truth or reflection; instead, they dismiss it as “legends of the ancients,” meaning old fables and fabricated tales inherited from past nations. Their response is a false accusation against the Qur’an, a refusal to accept its divine origin, and a mockery of the Prophet. It shows that their denial is rooted not in lack of evidence but in willful obstinacy and contempt for the truth.

translation: That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who lead others astray in religious matters will not only carry the full weight of their own sins on the Day of Judgment, but will also carry an added burden from the sins of those they misled. Because they were the cause of others’ deviation, they share in the guilt and its consequences, and their load is described as profoundly evil. It establishes the severe accountability of misleading others, especially when done without sound knowledge or when the followers are ignorant, and it underscores divine justice: leaders of misguidance face a compounded punishment.

translation: Those before them had plotted, but Allah came upon their building from its foundations, so the roof fell upon them from above, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse refers to earlier nations who schemed against their prophets and plotted to defeat God’s guidance, relying on their power and elaborate plans. But God struck at the very foundations of what they had built, so their whole structure of deception collapsed upon them. Their own schemes became the means of their ruin, and the punishment seized them suddenly from a direction they had never anticipated. It shows that no plot can escape God’s decree, and that He can uproot the mightiest designs of the arrogant and turn them into a cause of their own destruction.

translation: Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them and say, 'Where are My partners whom you used to contend about?' Those who were given knowledge will say, 'Indeed, disgrace today and evil are upon the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the inevitable exposure of falsehood on the Day of Judgment. God’s question is a rebuke, not a request for information: the idols and alleged partners the disbelievers associated with Him, and for whose sake they opposed the messengers and disputed the truth, will prove utterly powerless and nonexistent as rivals to Him. Their humiliation will be public and irreversible. Those granted true knowledge—prophets, angels, and faithful scholars—will announce the just verdict: shame and punishment on that Day belong to those who knowingly rejected faith and persisted in shirk. The verse thereby warns that worldly argument, influence, and opposition cannot change the truth; divine justice will finally vindicate the believers and expose the emptiness of the disbelievers’ claims.

translation: Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves — they will offer submission, saying, "We were not doing any evil." But yes! Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse describes those who wronged themselves through disbelief, shirk, and persistent sin. When the angels seize their souls at death, they suddenly pretend to be peaceful and obedient, denying that they committed any evil. Their claim is a futile attempt to escape accountability, but God rejects it and affirms that He fully knows everything they did. Thus, deathbed excuses and denials are of no benefit; one must repent and correct oneself before that moment, because God’s knowledge encompasses all deeds and no one can conceal anything from Him.

translation: So enter the gates of Hell, abiding eternally therein; and wretched is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse declares the final outcome of those whose pride led them to reject faith and divine guidance. Entering the gates of Hell signifies being consigned to punishment from every side, with no escape, while abiding eternally therein means the punishment is unending and irreversible. The concluding condemnation identifies arrogance as the fundamental cause: it blinds a person to truth, prevents humble submission to God, and makes one regard oneself as above accountability. Thus the verse teaches that the most destructive spiritual condition is self-exaltation before God, and that its end is the worst possible dwelling and permanent disgrace.

translation: And it was said to those who feared Allah, “What has your Lord sent down?” They said, “Good.” For those who do good in this world is good, and the home of the Hereafter is better. And excellent is the home of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse shows that the God-conscious recognize divine revelation as pure good—guidance, truth, and benefit—because their hearts are prepared by taqwa to accept it. Their answer “good” is both a confession of faith and a testimony that Allah’s sending down the Qur’an is a mercy. The reward for those who do ihsan in this worldly life is divine favor, contentment, protection, and blessings, but the eternal abode is far superior because it is everlasting and free from every deficiency. The verse concludes by praising Paradise as the excellent home prepared for the God-conscious, teaching that taqwa and doing good are the path to the best final destination, and that the good of this world is only a foretaste of the greater good in the Hereafter.

translation: Gardens of Eden which they will enter, with rivers flowing beneath them; therein they will have whatever they wish. Thus does Allah reward the righteous.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward of those who guard themselves against Allah’s displeasure through faith and obedience: they will be admitted into everlasting gardens of bliss, beneath which rivers flow, and every desire they have will be fulfilled. This is how Allah recompenses the people of taqwa—those who remain conscious of Him, obey His commands, and avoid what He has forbidden.

translation: Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure, saying, 'Peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse describes the righteous at the moment of death: the angels receive their souls while they are pure in faith and conduct, free from disbelief and the defilement of sin. The angels greet them with peace, meaning they are safe from punishment and fear, and announce their entry into Paradise as a reward for the good deeds they performed in obedience to God. It affirms that the angel of death and his helpers take souls by God’s command, that the sincere believers are honored at death, and that Paradise is granted by God’s mercy while deeds are the means He has appointed for it.

translation: Do they await anything except that the angels should come to them or the command of your Lord should come? Thus did those before them. And Allah did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who persist in denial and demand miraculous signs before believing. It warns that the only thing they are truly waiting for is the arrival of the angels—whether at death, with punishment, or to execute God’s decree—or the coming of God’s command, meaning His judgment and the fulfillment of what He has promised. The same pattern occurred among earlier nations: they stubbornly rejected their messengers and demanded signs until the decree came upon them. God is not unjust in punishing them; He sent clear guidance and warnings, but they chose disbelief, arrogance, and wrongdoing, thereby bringing harm upon their own souls.

translation: So the evil consequences of what they did struck them, and what they used to ridicule encompassed them.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the punishment that overtakes the deniers is the harvest of their own actions. The “evil consequences” are not merely abstract records but concrete misfortunes that befall them. Their persistent mockery of the truth and of the warnings they were given does not make those warnings unreal; rather, the very reality they ridiculed closes in on them and becomes inescapable. Thus they are trapped by the truth they denied, and their own deeds testify against them, demonstrating God’s justice and the inevitability of His promise.

translation: And those who associated others with Allah said: 'If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have made anything unlawful besides Him.' Thus did those before them. Then are the messengers responsible for anything except clear conveyance?
interpretation: The polytheists' appeal to Allah's will is invalid as an excuse for shirk and for their self-made prohibitions. Divine decree encompasses all things, but it does not mean Allah approves of their deeds or that they are excused; He has sent messengers with clear proofs and commands, and the messengers' only duty is plain conveyance. Thus the verse refutes using qadar to justify idolatry and unlawful prohibitions, and establishes that accountability follows the clear message.

translation: And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], 'Worship Allah and avoid Taghut.' And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed. So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the call to pure monotheism was universal: every community received a messenger commanding the exclusive worship of Allah and the rejection of all false deities, idols, tyrannical powers, or any object of devotion besides Him. It then distinguishes two responses within those nations: some were guided by Allah because they turned toward the truth, while others were justly overcome by misguidance because they chose denial and persisted in it. The command to journey through the earth is a call to learn from history, for the ruins and ruined legacies of those who rejected their messengers testify that God's judgment is real and that denying the truth leads ultimately to loss and destruction.

translation: If you eagerly desire their guidance, then indeed Allah does not guide whom He sends astray, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and reminds him that guidance is not in his power to force upon others. His intense concern for their guidance cannot override Allah’s decree: those who persistently choose error and reject the truth are left in their misguidance, and no one besides Allah can aid or protect them. Thus the Prophet’s duty is to convey the message sincerely, while the final granting or withholding of guidance belongs to Allah alone.

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that Allah will not resurrect one who dies. Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him in truth, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse exposes the arrogance of those who deny the Hereafter: they reinforce their false claim with solemn oaths, as if their swearing could nullify divine power. It then firmly rejects their denial and affirms that resurrection is certain because Allah has bound Himself to it as a true promise. The ignorance mentioned is not lack of information only, but failure to understand Allah’s power, wisdom, and faithfulness, which makes the majority heedless of the certainty of being raised for judgment.

translation: So that He may make clear to them that wherein they differed, and so that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.
interpretation: Resurrection serves God's just disclosure: He will make plain the truth concerning the matters people disputed in religion and creed, and the disbelievers who rejected the raising and swore false oaths will be confronted with the reality that their claims were lies.

translation: Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, “Be,” and it is.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God’s will is immediately and absolutely effective: He does not need means, time, or effort to bring anything into existence. His mere decree “Be” is sufficient for it to come into being, demonstrating His unlimited power and the certainty of His promises.

translation: And those who emigrated for the sake of Allah after they had been wronged, We will surely settle them in this world in a good place; and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse declares that believers who endure persecution and are forced to leave their homes for the sake of Allah are not abandoned; Allah Himself guarantees them a good and honorable settlement in this worldly life, whether through safety, provision, dignity, or victory. Yet the greater reality is that worldly compensation is limited and temporary, while the reward awaiting them in the Hereafter is far greater and everlasting. The closing phrase, 'if only they knew,' indicates that true knowledge of Allah's promise should make a believer willing to sacrifice temporary comforts, endure hardship with patience, and remain firm in faith, because what Allah has prepared for the patient and the truthful is beyond comparison with any loss suffered in this world.

translation: Those who are patient and upon their Lord they rely.
interpretation: This describes the believers who endure trials and hardships with steadfast patience, and who place their complete trust and reliance in God alone, turning all their affairs over to Him and seeking His help and support.

translation: And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the Reminder, if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God’s way of guiding humanity has always been through human messengers chosen to receive revelation, not through angels sent as prophets. Therefore, rejecting a prophet merely because he is a man is contrary to the consistent pattern of divine guidance. The command to ask the people of remembrance means that those who possess knowledge of earlier revelations can testify that former messengers were also human beings, confirming the continuity and truthfulness of the prophetic message.

translation: [We sent them] with clear proofs and scriptures. And We have sent down to you the Reminder, so that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them, and so that they may reflect.
interpretation: The earlier prophets were supported by evident signs and revealed books, and now the Reminder—the Qur’an—is sent to the Prophet Muhammad with a distinct duty of clarification. Revelation is not left as an obscure or merely recited text; the Prophet is charged to explain its meanings, commands, warnings, and purposes so that people understand what God has actually sent for their guidance. The verse then names reflection as the intended human response: having received clear exposition, people are expected to ponder the revelation, grasp its coherence and moral demands, and allow it to shape conviction and conduct rather than passively hearing it.

translation: Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning against false security. It addresses those who persist in evil scheming and wrongdoing while assuming they are safe from consequences. Their security is delusion, because divine punishment can seize them in this very world through a sudden, terrifying calamity such as being swallowed by the earth, or through a torment arriving from an unexpected direction at a moment they never anticipated. The verse teaches that no plotter or oppressor can outmaneuver God's decree: the very safety they rely on may become the trap through which punishment reaches them unawares, and their schemes cannot protect them from the consequences of their deeds.

translation: Or that He may seize them in their going to and fro, for they will not be able to escape.
interpretation: This warns those who scheme against God's messengers and signs that divine punishment can overtake them at any moment, even while they are busy with their ordinary movements, travels, work, and worldly affairs, when they feel safe and think nothing can reach them. Their illusion of security is false, because no one can escape God's power or frustrate His decree. The verse stresses that God is fully aware of their actions, fully capable of seizing them unexpectedly, and that neither their plans, their strength, their wealth, nor their mobility can place them beyond His grasp.

translation: Or that He may seize them by causing gradual fear and loss. Then indeed, your Lord is Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah may punish the wicked not always by sudden destruction, but by taking them gradually—through losses in wealth, health, security, or worldly blessings—so that fear and dread enter their hearts before the final penalty. This gradual seizure is a warning and a chance to repent, showing that Allah does not hasten punishment despite His power. The verse ends by affirming that your Lord is Most Compassionate and Most Merciful, meaning His mercy is why He warns, gives respite, and calls people back to Him rather than destroying them immediately.

translation: Have they not seen that every thing Allah has created casts its shadow, inclining to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah, while they are humbled?
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect on a universal sign of Allah’s sovereignty: even shadows, which move and change direction under His command, are portrayed as prostrating to Him along with all created things. Their submission is not merely physical but points to the fact that everything in existence is subject to Allah’s will, whether willingly or by compulsion. The phrase “while they are humbled” emphasizes utter subjugation and lowliness before His majesty. Therefore, the verse rebukes those who fail to see these evident signs and do not themselves submit to the One who alone controls all creation. It affirms that Allah is the sole Lord and Master, and that true worship belongs to Him alone.

translation: And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of moving creatures, and the angels, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse declares that all creation is subject to Allah: every living being in the heavens and earth submits to His will and sovereignty, and the angels worship Him in humble obedience, free from pride or refusal. It teaches that recognizing Allah's Lordship and bowing to Him is the natural and rightful state of all creatures, and that the angels' lack of arrogance is a model of sincere servitude.

translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse portrays the essence of true servitude: acknowledging God’s absolute transcendence and authority over all things produces a deep, reverent awe of Him, and that awe is not merely inward emotion but is proven through immediate, willing obedience to His commands. It teaches that nearness to God does not remove accountability; rather, the highest beings fulfill their station by living in constant awareness of His supremacy and by carrying out every divine instruction without resistance. For believers, it establishes that genuine faith combines humility before the Lord who is exalted above all with faithful action in accordance with what He ordains.

translation: And Allah has said: 'Do not take two gods. Indeed, He is only one God. So fear Me alone.'
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute oneness of Allah and forbids associating any other being with Him as a god. Since He alone is the one true God, He alone deserves all worship, reverence, and fear of divine judgment. The command to fear Him exclusively means that the believer’s ultimate awe, obedience, and hope of salvation must be directed only to Allah, not shared with any created thing.

translation: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is due the religion/worship perpetually. Then is it other than Allah that you fear?
interpretation: This verse affirms that all creation in the heavens and earth belongs solely to Allah, so worship, obedience, and devotion must be given to Him alone, constantly and sincerely. Since He alone owns and controls everything, it is irrational and unjust to direct reverent fear, hope, or ultimate loyalty toward any created being. The rhetorical question rebukes turning away from Allah to others in fear or worship, and it calls people back to pure monotheism and God-consciousness.

translation: And whatever blessings you have are from Allah. Then, when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help.
interpretation: This verse teaches that every favor, benefit, and good thing that reaches a person originates from Allah alone, not from oneself, others, or false deities. It then points to human nature in moments of suffering: when hardship, illness, loss, or danger strikes, the person instinctively turns to Allah, calling upon Him earnestly for relief. Thus, gratitude for blessings should belong to Allah, and times of distress should direct one's supplication and reliance to Him alone.

translation: Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a party of you associates others with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse exposes the inconsistency of those who turn sincerely to God alone when suffering strikes, but then, once He alone relieves their distress, a group among them returns to associating partners with Him. It condemns the ingratitude of directing worship, gratitude, or reliance toward created beings after having witnessed God’s exclusive power to remove harm, and it shows that true faith requires exclusive devotion to God in both hardship and ease.

translation: So that they may deny what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.
interpretation: This is a severe warning and threat, not a grant of permission. It means: persist in your ingratitude and fleeting worldly enjoyment if you will, but soon you will come to know the reality of the punishment and the loss your denial has earned. The verse exposes that turning away from Allah after receiving His favors is not mere forgetfulness but a deliberate rejection that will end in accountability.

translation: And they assign to that which they do not know a share of what We have provided them. By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent.
interpretation: This is a severe divine rebuke and warning against worship built on ignorance and fabrication: people set aside portions of God’s own provision for beings whose true nature, power, and worth they do not know, thereby inventing a religious claim God never authorized. The oath “By Allah” intensifies the certainty that such invented obligations, offerings, and associations will not be overlooked; every fabricated lie about God and His rights will be exposed and held to account.

translation: And they attribute to Allah daughters—exalted is He—while for themselves they have what they desire.
interpretation: This verse condemns the polytheists’ false and insolent claim that Allah has daughters, referring to their belief that the angels were daughters of Allah.
