interpretation: This verse portrays Prophet Zechariah’s intimate supplication: in his old age, without an heir, he turns to God not in despair but in hope. He asks not merely for a child, but for one who would continue the legacy of faith and prophethood. His words “do not leave me alone” express the deep human need for a righteous heir and companion in serving God. By confessing “You are the best of inheritors,” he acknowledges that all things ultimately return to God, that God alone remains when all creation passes away, and that whatever God grants is the best outcome. The verse teaches that supplication should combine sincere need with humble trust and complete reliance on God’s wisdom and power.

translation: So We responded to him, and We granted him Yahya, and We cured his wife for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, and they called upon Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God answers sincere supplication beyond human limitation: He granted Zakariyya a son, Yahya, and restored his wife’s ability, showing that divine power is not constrained by age or barrenness. The true servants who receive such favor are marked by eagerness in good works, supplication that combines hope in God’s mercy with fear of His displeasure, and deep humility before Him. Thus worship is not merely ritual but action, prayer, and inner submission joined together.

translation: And [mention] she who guarded her chastity, so We blew into her of Our Spirit, and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to Mary, whose unwavering chastity and devotion made her a vessel for a miraculous divine act: God breathed into her from His Spirit, meaning He created life in her by His command through the angel Gabriel, without a father. The sign is not merely the virgin birth but the pairing of Mary and her son Jesus as a profound testimony to God's absolute power over natural laws, His ability to create as He wills, and His selection of pure servants for His purposes. It also confirms Mary's truthfulness and Jesus's status as a servant and prophet born by God's word, making them together a lesson and mercy for all peoples.

translation: Indeed, this is your community—one community—and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
interpretation: God declares that the believers’ true allegiance is not to be fragmented into rival sects or man-made loyalties: the prophetic call, from first to last, constitutes a single ummah bound by the pure worship of the one Lord. Since He alone is Rabb—Creator, Sustainer, Sovereign—He alone has the right to be worshipped; all religious identity and communal unity are valid only insofar as they are grounded in that exclusive devotion and expressed in obedient worship of Him.

translation: And they have divided their affair among themselves; every one will return to Us.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who fragmented the religion of God into competing factions and sects, each clinging to its own path while forgetting the final return to Allah. Their divisions do not change the reality that every group and every individual will be brought back to God for judgment. No sectarian allegiance, dispute, or self-made division will shield anyone from accountability, and all will be judged by the truth. It is a warning that people must unite upon divine guidance and remember that the ultimate reckoning belongs to God alone.

translation: Whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer—his effort will never be denied, and indeed We are recording it for him.
interpretation: This means that righteous deeds are only accepted and rewarded when rooted in faith; God does not waste or reject the labor of a believer, but preserves it and records it for him, guaranteeing its reward.

translation: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they will return.
interpretation: This verse means that once a community has been destroyed by Allah’s decree as punishment, its return to worldly life or to a state in which it could amend its ways is made impossible; the decree is final, and no second chance is granted after that destruction.

translation: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swarm down from every elevation.
interpretation: This verse describes a major sign before the Day of Judgment: the release of Gog and Magog from behind the barrier that had confined them. Once that barrier is opened by divine decree, they will pour out in vast numbers from every high place, spreading swiftly and causing widespread corruption and turmoil. Their emergence signals that the promised Hour has drawn near and that God's decree is being fulfilled.

translation: And the true promise has drawn near, and then the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly: 'Woe to us! We were indeed heedless of this; rather, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment when God's true promise—the resurrection and final judgment—arrives, and the disbelievers are seized by terror. Their eyes become fixed and staring in shock, and they confess too late that they had lived in heedlessness of this reality and that they were wrongdoers. Their cry of woe is an admission of guilt and regret, but it comes after the time for repentance and faith has passed, so it only declares their own culpability as they face the consequences.

translation: Indeed, you and whatever you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you are bound for it.
interpretation: This verse declares that the polytheists and the false objects of worship they invoke apart from Allah are destined for the Fire, and they will inevitably enter it. It shows the total helplessness of every supposed god besides Allah: they cannot rescue their worshippers or themselves, nor can they avert punishment. The passage warns that directing worship to anything other than Allah leads to ruin, and it affirms that Allah alone is the true Deity, with no partner or equal.

translation: If these had been gods, they would not have entered it; and all will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse is a decisive argument against the divinity of anything worshipped besides Allah. If those alleged deities had true divine power, they would never have been cast into Hell along with their worshippers. Their entry into it and their eternal confinement there expose their complete helplessness and prove that they are created servants, not gods. The word 'all' refers to the false objects of worship and their followers who are condemned to the Fire, all remaining therein without escape. This does not conflict with the later exception of those who were wrongly worshipped but were actually righteous servants of Allah, for they are removed from the Fire because they neither claimed divinity nor were pleased with such worship.

translation: For them therein is groaning, and they therein do not hear.
interpretation: This describes the people of the Fire as being in unrelenting agony: their breathing itself becomes a painful, harsh groaning, and they are deprived of hearing anything that could comfort, distract, or relieve them. Their punishment combines intense suffering with isolation, so that even sound—normally a means of connection or warning—brings them no benefit or respite.

translation: Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us — they are kept far away from it.
interpretation: This means that those whom God’s prior decree of grace and ultimate good has already encompassed will be spared the punishment of Hellfire and distanced from it. Their being kept away from the Fire is the realization of God’s earlier promise and favor toward them, showing that deliverance from punishment is rooted in His mercy and prior decree for those He has chosen for the best outcome.

translation: They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide forever in whatever their souls desire.
interpretation: This verse describes the bliss of those whom God has decreed salvation: they are kept far from the Fire, so much so that they do not hear even its slightest sound or movement. Instead, they live eternally in the fulfillment of their purest and most pleasing desires, enjoying everlasting contentment and delight.

translation: The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them: 'This is your Day which you were promised.'
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, when the greatest horror—the trumpet blast and the terrors of judgment—overwhelms creation, the believers who lived in God-consciousness will be safe from its anguish. The angels will welcome them with honor and glad tidings, announcing that the reward they were promised in the world has now arrived. This shows that faithful obedience and fear of God bring security from the ultimate fear and a joyful reception into eternal bliss.

translation: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a scroll for records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. A promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We were ever doers.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, God will roll up the heavens as a written scroll is rolled up, bringing the present order of creation to an end. Then He will bring creation back into existence just as He first originated it, restoring it after its passing. This is a firm promise He has taken upon Himself, and His power makes its fulfillment certain, for He is never unable to do what He wills.

translation: And We have already written in the Zabur after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God has decreed and recorded in the earlier scriptures, after the earlier revelation, that the ultimate inheritance of the earth belongs to His righteous servants. It means that true authority, dwelling, and blessed estate in the land—culminating in the inheritance of Paradise for the righteous—will be granted by God to those who believe and act righteously, not to the tyrannical or corrupt. Thus it is a promise of divine justice and victory for the upright, showing that God's decree ensures the final success of His righteous servants.

translation: Indeed, in this [Qur'an] is a message for a people who worship.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a sufficient admonition and clear communication for those who devote themselves sincerely to the worship of Allah; because their hearts are turned toward Him in obedience, they are the ones who benefit from its guidance, warning, and reminder.

translation: And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This means that God sent the Prophet Muhammad not as a punishment or burden, but as a mercy encompassing all creation—humans, jinn, and the wider universe—by guiding them to what benefits them and by embodying compassion, justice, and the path to eternal salvation.

translation: Say, "It is only revealed to me that your god is one God. Will you then be Muslims?"
interpretation: This verse declares that the core of divine revelation to the Prophet is pure monotheism: there is no true deity except the One God, who has no partner, no equal, and no rival. The rhetorical question then presses the hearer to respond to this truth with inward faith and outward submission. To be "Muslims" here means to surrender one's will, worship, and obedience to Allah alone, abandoning every false object of devotion. Thus the verse presents acknowledgment of God's oneness as inseparable from humble submission to Him.

translation: So if they turn away, say: 'I have warned you all alike, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far.'
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet to declare, when people reject the message, that he has conveyed the warning plainly and equally to everyone, without favoritism or concealment. He does not claim knowledge of the unseen timing of the promised judgment; whether it is near or distant is known only to God. The verse thus affirms the Messenger’s duty to deliver the warning clearly, while leaving the time of its fulfillment entirely to God’s decree.

translation: Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah’s knowledge is all-encompassing: it reaches every visible word and every hidden thought, intention, or secret. Nothing in human speech or inner life is beyond His awareness. The meaning is that people should be mindful of Allah in both their public and private lives, speaking and acting with sincerity, because outward show cannot conceal anything from Him, and hidden motives are fully known and subject to His judgment.

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a while.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly ease, delay, or respite can itself be a test. What appears as a blessing or postponement of consequences is not proof of divine approval; it is a temporary enjoyment destined to end at an appointed time. The speaker acknowledges human ignorance of God’s hidden purpose, warning that people should not be deceived by transient comfort into heedlessness, since it may be a trial leading to accountability.

translation: He said: My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One whose help is sought against what you describe.
interpretation: This is a prayer of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) at the conclusion of Surah al-Anbiya, asking God to judge with truth and justice between him and those who reject and slander him. It then declares that God, the Most Merciful, is the one from whom help is sought against the false claims and descriptions they invent. It teaches the believer to rely on God's mercy and justice, to seek His aid against falsehood and oppression, and to leave final judgment to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a tremendous thing.
interpretation: This verse addresses all humanity, summoning them to taqwa—God-consciousness and protective obedience to their Lord—because the final Hour will begin with a violent shaking and upheaval of the cosmos. That event is not a minor disturbance but an overwhelming reality whose terror and magnitude should jolt every person out of heedlessness and into seriousness about their accountability before God.

translation: On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will deliver her burden, and you will see the people as if drunk, though they are not drunk; but the punishment of Allah is severe.
interpretation: This verse depicts the overwhelming terror and cosmic upheaval of the Day of Judgment. The scene is one of such intense fear that even a nursing mother, whose natural instinct is to protect her child, becomes oblivious to the infant at her breast; every pregnant woman delivers or loses her unborn child; and people appear intoxicated and senseless, not because they have drunk wine, but because the reality of Allah’s punishment and the dread of the Hour has shattered their composure. The verse emphasizes that the severity of divine judgment is so immense that it overturns ordinary human instincts and faculties, reminding people to take the warnings of the Hereafter with utmost seriousness.

translation: And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who argue about God—His existence, oneness, or revelation—without any sound knowledge, and instead of seeking evidence they submit to every defiant, corrupting influence. It teaches that ignorance joined with arrogance leads a person to follow the promptings of rebellious spirits or human leaders who lead them away from truth; such disputation is not honest inquiry but a following of misguidance, and it warns against speaking of Allah without knowledge.

translation: It has been decreed of him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: God has ordained that the rebellious devil’s influence over anyone who chooses him as a protector and follows him results in misguidance from the straight path and an end in the blazing punishment; allegiance to Satan leads not to benefit but to ruin.

translation: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then [know that] We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, so that We may make [it] clear to you. And We cause whom We will to remain in the wombs until an appointed term, then We bring you forth as infants, then [We let you grow] so that you may reach your full strength. And among you is he who is taken in death, and among you is he who is returned to the most abject age, so that he knows nothing after having known. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it quivers and swells and produces every kind of beautiful pair.
interpretation: This verse presents the Resurrection as rationally and experientially credible by pointing to the same divine power already visible in human origins and in the earth’s revival. The One who originated human beings through successive stages, who governs the womb and the appointed term, who decrees maturity, death, and extreme old age, and who brings dead soil to life with rain is not incapable of raising the dead. The stages of embryonic formation and the contrast between formed and unformed, as well as the return to senility, show that life, knowledge, and death are entirely in Allah’s hands. The barren earth’s response to water is a tangible sign and likeness of resurrection: just as God gives life to lifeless ground and causes every beautiful pair to grow, He will surely bring forth the dead for judgment and recompense.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and because He gives life to the dead, and because He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every divine act and promise rests on the fact that God alone is al-Haqq—the absolute Truth and Reality upon whom all existence depends. His reviving the dead is not a remote possibility but a direct expression of His sovereign authority over life and death, and His being capable of all things means that resurrection, judgment, and every promised outcome are entirely within His power. The verse therefore grounds certainty in the Hereafter and confidence in God's absolute reliability.

translation: And that the Hour is coming—there is no doubt about it—and that Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Hereafter is an absolute certainty and that denying it is groundless, because the same Allah who originated creation is fully able to bring the dead out of their graves and raise them for reckoning. Belief in the Hour and in resurrection is therefore not merely a moral warning but a call to live with accountability, knowing that every deed will be met with divine justice and that no one can escape the reality of the final judgment.

translation: And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge, without guidance, and without an enlightening Scripture.
interpretation: This verse condemns arguing about God—His existence, oneness, attributes, or commands—on the basis of ignorance and conjecture, without sound knowledge, without divine guidance, and without an illuminating revealed scripture. Such disputation is blameworthy because it is rootless and arrogant; the truth about God must be approached through evidence, revelation, and enlightened guidance, not mere sophistry, speculation, or inherited hostility.

translation: Twisting his neck in arrogance to mislead [people] from the way of Allah. For him in this world is disgrace, and We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the arrogant rejecter of divine guidance who turns aside disdainfully and strives to divert others from Allah’s path. His misguidance is not a mere mistake but a willful rebellion that harms both himself and others, so he is recompensed with humiliation in this worldly life and with the painful torment of the Fire in the Hereafter. The verse affirms that leading others away from God’s way is a grave moral crime and that divine justice will inevitably expose and punish such pride.

translation: That is because of what your hands have sent forth, and because Allah is not unjust to His servants.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the punishment or consequence a person meets is the direct result of his own deeds, symbolized by what his hands have sent ahead. It denies any notion that God wrongs His servants; His justice is absolute, and He does not punish anyone without just cause. Human beings are responsible for their choices, and God's judgment is perfectly fair, never oppressive or biased.

translation: And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If good befalls him, he is reassured by it; but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He loses this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse exposes a faith that is conditional and unstable: a person may outwardly worship God only while circumstances are favorable, treating religion as a bargain that must immediately yield comfort or advantage. When ease comes, such a person feels secure, but when hardship or testing comes, the shallow foundation is revealed, and he turns away. The real meaning is that worship rooted in convenience rather than sincere submission cannot endure trials. The loss described is manifest because the person neither secures any lasting good in worldly life nor attains the Hereafter; he forfeits both by making his loyalty to God dependent on benefit and by abandoning steadfastness when tested.

translation: He calls upon besides Allah that which can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is the far-reaching misguidance.
interpretation: This verse condemns directing worship or supplication to any created being or false deity that has no power to bring harm or benefit. Such a person has strayed extremely far from the truth, because he depends for his most essential needs on something utterly powerless, instead of the One who alone controls all harm and benefit.

translation: He calls upon one whose harm is nearer than its benefit. How wretched is such a protector, and how wretched a companion!
interpretation: This verse exposes the folly of invoking or relying upon a false object of worship or patron: it offers no true benefit, while the harm of attaching oneself to it—misguidance, loss, and ruin—is closer and more certain. Such a supposed protector and companion is the worst, because it cannot protect, help, or bring any real good, and it leads its devotees away from the true source of benefit and protection. It is a warning to direct worship, reliance, and close allegiance only to Allah, whose benefit is real and whose protection is true.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse affirms that salvation and eternal bliss are granted by Allah to those who combine sincere faith with righteous action. The gardens with flowing rivers symbolize unending provision, delight, and divine generosity. The closing statement, “Indeed, Allah does what He wills,” establishes that His promise is certain and entirely subject to His sovereign will; no power can prevent or compel Him, and He fulfills His decree with perfect wisdom and justice.

translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help him [i.e., His Messenger] in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch a rope to the sky and then cut it off, and let him see whether his scheme removes that which enrages him.
interpretation: This is a forceful address to those who imagine that God will not grant His Messenger victory and support in this life and the next. It invites them, in effect, to exhaust every stratagem: let them extend a rope toward heaven and sever it, or strive by any means to cut off divine aid, and then observe whether their plotting can do away with the rage and frustration they feel at God's promise. The verse teaches that the help granted by God to His Prophet cannot be blocked or severed by human schemes; the plotters only expose the futility of their efforts and increase their own torment, while God's decree remains unshaken.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as clear verses, and indeed Allah guides whom He wills.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur’an is revealed as lucid, decisive signs that expose the truth and leave no valid excuse for rejecting it. It then affirms that the effect of these clear signs depends on Allah’s guidance: He guides to faith whom He wills, by His wisdom and grace, not because anyone can compel guidance or merit it independently. The clear verses are both proof and mercy; they are sufficient in themselves, yet hearts are turned only by Allah’s enabling. Thus the verse joins the clarity of revelation with the sovereignty of divine guidance, teaching that people should receive the clear signs with humility, seek Allah’s guidance, and acknowledge that He alone grants it.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associated others with Allah—indeed, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes that final judgment among the various religious communities belongs exclusively to God on the Day of Resurrection. It rebuts human partisanship and sectarian claims to ultimate truth, since no group can decide another's eternal fate; God alone knows every outward and inward reality and will judge with perfect justice. The closing affirmation that God is Witness over all things grounds that judgment in His all-encompassing knowledge, so no belief, deed, or hidden intention escapes His awareness. Thus it calls for humility, reliance on God's justice, and accountability before Him rather than self-assured pronouncements about others' standing before God.

translation: Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures, and many of mankind? But many deserve punishment. And whoever Allah humiliates, none can honor him. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all creation is subject to Allah’s command, power, and decree. The prostration of the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and animals is their submission to His will and their functioning according to the laws He ordained, not necessarily the ritual prostration of rational worship. Among human beings, many prostrate to Allah willingly through faith and obedience, while many others persist in rejection and thereby deserve punishment. Honor and humiliation are entirely in Allah’s hand; whom He humiliates cannot be raised by any created being. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah acts with absolute sovereignty and does whatever He wills, without anyone having the power to prevent or reverse His decree.

translation: These are two adversaries who have disputed concerning their Lord. So those who disbelieved will have garments of fire cut out for them; boiling fluid will be poured down over their heads.
interpretation: The verse presents the fundamental division between those who affirm their Lord’s oneness and accountability and those who reject it. The dispute is about the truth of God and His exclusive right to worship, not an idle quarrel. For the disbelievers, the punishment described—fire as clothing and scalding liquid poured from above—conveys that their whole being is enveloped by the consequence of their denial; there is no shield, no escape, and no relief. It warns that rejecting the Creator is a moral and spiritual decision that leads to severe, inescapable judgment, while implying that the believers’ position is the truthful one.

translation: By it, whatever is in their bellies is melted, and [also] their skins.
interpretation: This describes the boiling water of Hell: its heat is so penetrating that it dissolves the inner contents of the belly and melts the outer skin, showing that the punishment afflicts both the inward and outward dimensions of the person. It conveys the severity, totality, and inescapability of the chastisement for those who rejected faith.

translation: And for them are maces of iron.
interpretation: These are iron clubs or hammers in the Fire, by which the disbelievers are struck and driven back whenever they try to escape it, making their punishment severe and inescapable and adding humiliation to their torment.

translation: Whenever they want to come out of it because of anguish, they will be returned into it, and [it will be said], 'Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the inescapable torment of Hell: the damned suffer such intense grief and distress that they attempt to flee, but they are forcibly driven back into the Fire. Their punishment is not only bodily burning but also the anguish of being trapped without any hope of relief. The command “Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire” is a rebuke and a declaration of perfect justice, showing that their suffering is the deserved consequence of their denial and wrongdoing, and that no escape or respite will ever be granted.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse presents Paradise as the certain recompense of a faith that is lived out in righteous action: God Himself guarantees entry into gardens of flowing rivers, where the believers are honored with ornaments of gold and pearls and clothed in silk. The mention of such precious adornments and fine clothing signifies not mere luxury but divine approval, dignity, and the reversal of worldly deprivation or humility; in the hereafter these delights are pure, lasting, and free from the vanity and impermanence that stain them in this world. It also teaches that faith and deeds are inseparable in the life of the believer, and that the bliss of the Garden is both a gift from God and a manifestation of His justice and generosity toward those who orient their lives to Him.

translation: And they were guided to the good words, and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: God guided the believers to speak and adhere to the purest and best of speech—affirming His oneness, praising Him, and uttering truth and goodness—and He directed them to the straight path of God, the Praiseworthy, which is the way of faith, sincere obedience, and righteous action that leads to His pleasure.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder [people] from the way of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque, which We have made for all people—equal are the resident therein and the visitor—and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Sacred Mosque is not the property or privilege of any group, but a place of worship and sanctuary for all people, whether they dwell nearby or come from afar. It condemns those who join disbelief with obstructing God’s path and blocking access to the Haram, because such obstruction combines denial of truth with aggression against the universal right of worship. The warning against intending “deviation by wrongdoing” inside it means that the sanctity of the place is violated not only by outward acts but even by a resolved intention to commit injustice, sacrilege, shirk, or oppression within its precincts. Such a person is threatened with a painful punishment, indicating the severity of desecrating the Haram and using it as a means of injustice, exclusion, or sin.

translation: And [mention] when We assigned to Abraham the site of the House, [saying], “Do not associate anything with Me, and purify My House for those who circumambulate, and those who stand, and those who bow and prostrate.”
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that Allah Himself guided Abraham to the location of the Sacred House and commanded him to establish it upon pure monotheism, free from any partner or idol. The command to purify the House means cleansing it outwardly and inwardly from false worship, ritual impurity, and everything unbecoming of a place dedicated solely to Allah. It is to be kept pure for those who perform tawaf around it, for those who stand in prayer, and for those who bow and prostrate before Allah. Thus the Ka‘bah is presented as the central sanctuary of exclusive devotion to Allah, and Abraham is shown as the model of sincere worship and service.

translation: And proclaim to the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every distant deep pass.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the call to Hajj is a divinely rooted invitation whose reality is tested by the response of hearts across distance and hardship. The pilgrim’s coming on foot or on lean mounts through deep passes expresses sincere surrender, detachment from ease, and reliance upon Allah, while also demonstrating the universality and equality of the sacred journey: no one is excluded by remoteness or lack of luxury. It establishes Hajj as an ancient Abrahamic legacy and shows that Allah can draw worshippers from the farthest reaches to His House, making the physical journey a mirror of the inward journey toward Him.

translation: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on appointed days over what He has provided for them of the cattle. So eat from them and feed the distressed poor.
interpretation: This verse instructs the pilgrims to attend the rites of Hajj so they may gain the spiritual and worldly benefits God has ordained for them, and to remember God by pronouncing His name over the sacrificial animals during the known days of sacrifice, acknowledging that these animals are His provision. It then commands them to eat from the sacrificial meat and to feed the poor and needy, showing that the sacrifice is an act of worship, gratitude, and generosity, not merely a ritual.

translation: Then let them complete their purification, fulfill their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House.
interpretation: This verse commands the pilgrims during Hajj to complete the remaining rites that remove the traces of ihram—such as cutting hair, trimming nails, and cleansing—so that they exit the state of ritual consecration; to fulfill any vows they have made; and to perform the tawaf around the Ka‘bah, the Ancient House, which Allah has preserved and made a place of worship and return for humanity.

translation: That [is the command]. And whoever honors the sacred rites of Allah, it is better for him with his Lord. And the livestock have been made lawful for you, except what is recited to you. So avoid the abomination of idols and avoid false speech.
interpretation: This verse establishes that reverence for what Allah has made sacred—His rites, sanctuaries, prohibitions, and commandments—is an act of faith that brings true benefit with one’s Lord. It then reminds believers that livestock are lawful food except those categories explicitly prohibited elsewhere, and it links dietary law to purity of worship: one must shun both the spiritual filth of idolatry and the moral filth of false speech. Thus outward reverence for Allah’s limits and inward truthfulness are inseparable; honoring the sacred leads to good in His sight, while idolatrous pollution and lying corrupt the servant’s religion and social conduct.

translation: Being upright for Allah, not associating any partner with Him. And whoever associates partners with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky, then the birds had snatched him away, or the wind had swept him down to a far-off, deep place.
interpretation: This verse describes pure monotheism as a state of upright devotion to Allah alone, and it portrays shirk as a spiritual catastrophe. The one who associates partners with Allah is likened to a person who falls from the sky: once cut off from the safeguard of true faith, he becomes exposed and torn apart by falsehoods, desires, and misleading forces, or he is hurled by the wind into a remote abyss of loss and ruin. Thus shirk is not merely a mistaken belief; it is a plunge from the elevated station of guidance into confusion, disintegration, and utter remoteness from salvation.

translation: That is so. And whoever honors the symbols of Allah, then indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.
interpretation: This verse teaches that revering the rites and signs Allah has appointed—such as the rites of Hajj, the sacrificial offerings, and the sacred sanctuaries—is not merely an external custom but an expression of sincere God-consciousness. The honor shown outwardly is rooted in and flows from the heart's taqwa, so the one who magnifies Allah's symbols demonstrates that his heart is alive with reverence, humility, and obedience to Allah. It also implies that true piety is not limited to private feeling; it necessarily manifests in the way one treats what Allah has made sacred.

translation: For you therein are benefits for a specified term; then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.
interpretation: This verse refers to the sacrificial animals dedicated for the Hajj rites: Allah permits people to make lawful use of them—such as riding, milking, or other benefits—until the appointed time of their sacrifice. After that term ends, their place of offering is the Ancient House, the Kaaba in Makkah, and the surrounding sacred precinct. This establishes that these animals remain under a sacred vow and must ultimately be sacrificed at the divinely appointed place, affirming the sanctity of the Kaaba and the obligation to complete the rite as an act of worship and nearness to Allah.

translation: And for every community We appointed a rite of sacrifice, so that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided them of livestock. And your God is one God, so submit to Him. And give good tidings to the humble.
interpretation: The verse establishes that sacrificial rites were prescribed for every religious community, but their essential purpose is to remember and invoke God alone over the provisions He grants, especially the livestock He has subjected to human benefit. The sacrifice itself is not the goal; it is a means of acknowledging God as the sole Provider, thanking Him, and directing all worship sincerely to Him. Since the true God is one and has no partner, the only fitting response is wholehearted submission to Him. The glad tidings are for the humble—those who submit to God with tranquility, sincerity, and freedom from arrogance, accepting His commands and recognizing their dependence upon Him.

translation: Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble; and those who are patient over what has afflicted them; and those who establish prayer; and from what We have provided them, they spend.
interpretation: This verse portrays the believers whose faith is genuine and deeply rooted: the remembrance of God fills their hearts with awe and humble submission, not hardness or heedlessness; they bear trials, losses, and hardships with steadfast patience; they uphold the prayer consistently as the central act of worship and obedience; and they freely spend from the provision God has entrusted to them, recognizing that wealth is not solely for themselves. These qualities together describe a life turned toward God inwardly and outwardly—reverence, endurance, worship, and generosity.

translation: And the sacrificial camels — We have made them for you among the rites of Allah; in them is good for you. So mention the name of Allah over them as they stand lined up. Then when their sides fall [to the ground], eat from them and feed the contented poor who do not ask and the beggar who asks. Thus We have subjected them to you, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: These sacrificial animals are appointed as one of Allah’s sacred rites, a means of drawing near to Him and a blessing for people. Slaughtering them is to be accompanied by the name of Allah, acknowledging His authority and blessing. After the animal collapses and dies, its meat is to be eaten and shared with both the modest needy who refrain from begging and the poor who actively ask. Allah’s subjection of these animals to human beings is a favor that calls for gratitude, shown through obedience, remembrance of Him, and generosity toward the needy.

translation: It is neither their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah, but it is piety from you that reaches Him. Thus He has subjected them to you, so that you may magnify Allah for having guided you. And give good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the outward act of sacrifice is not valued by Allah for its physical flesh or blood, since He is free of all need; what He accepts is the inward taqwa of the worshipper—sincere God-consciousness, obedience, and purity of intention. The animals are made subservient as a means to express gratitude and to glorify Allah for the guidance He has granted. The good tidings are for the muhsinin, those who worship Allah with sincere excellence and act beautifully toward His creation.

translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who believe. Indeed, Allah does not love any treacherous, ungrateful one.
interpretation: Allah’s defense of the believers is a real protection and vindication: He repels harm from them, frustrates plots against them, and upholds them against wrongdoing, so their safety rests ultimately in His care, not in their own strength. This protection belongs to those whose faith is sincere, and it calls them to trust Him while remaining loyal and grateful. By contrast, His not loving the treacherous ingrate means He detests the character that habitually betrays trusts and denies favors—betrayal toward God and people, and ingratitude for blessings—so genuine faith must be accompanied by faithfulness and thanksgiving.

translation: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged. And indeed, Allah is over their victory fully capable.
interpretation: God grants permission to fight to those who are subjected to aggression and persecution, precisely because they have been wronged; it is a charter of defensive justice, not aggression, and it assures the oppressed that God has full power to grant them victory.

translation: Those who were expelled from their homes unjustly, only because they said, “Our Lord is Allah.” And if Allah had not repelled some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques—in which Allah’s name is mentioned much—would surely have been demolished. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, All-Mighty.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah defends the oppressed who are driven out solely for affirming His oneness, and it reveals the divine wisdom in allowing human resistance to check aggression: without such mutual restraint, religious sanctuaries of every kind would be destroyed and the remembrance of Allah would be suppressed. The promise of Allah’s help is therefore tied to striving in His cause—upholding worship, justice, and the right to acknowledge Him alone—and His strength and might guarantee that this defense will ultimately prevail.

translation: [They are] those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer and give zakah and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse presents the character of the believers whom Allah grants authority: their power is not for self-aggrandizement but for worship and moral reform. Establishing prayer signifies loyalty and submission to Allah; giving zakah signifies purifying wealth and serving the needy; commanding good and forbidding evil signifies actively preserving a just and virtuous society. Thus, rightful authority is measured by whether it upholds faith, charity, and moral responsibility. The final phrase reminds them that all outcomes, including the success or failure of their efforts and the rise or fall of nations, ultimately belong to Allah alone.

translation: And if they deny you, then already denied before them the people of Nuh, and 'Ad, and Thamud.
interpretation: This is a consolation to the Prophet: the rejection he faces is not unique to him, but a recurring trial faced by earlier messengers. It implies that he should remain steadfast and not grieve over their denial, for God has always aided His messengers and will judge the deniers.

translation: And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot.
interpretation: This verse mentions the peoples of Abraham and Lot among the earlier communities that rejected their messengers, placing them in a series of warnings. Its meaning is that rejection of God’s prophets is not new, and those who deny the Prophet Muhammad should learn from how God dealt with former nations: He granted them time, but then seized them for their denial. It also consoles the Prophet and strengthens him to remain steadfast despite opposition.

translation: And the companions of Madyan; and Moses was denied. So I granted respite to the disbelievers, then I seized them; so how was My rejection/punishment?
interpretation: This verse is part of God's consolation to the Prophet Muhammad: earlier nations also rejected their messengers—the people of Madyan rejected Shu‘ayb, and Moses was rejected by Pharaoh and his people. God explains that He did not punish them immediately but granted the disbelievers respite, giving them time to repent; when they persisted in denial, He seized them with His judgment. The rhetorical question “so how was My rejection/punishment?” affirms that His denunciation and retribution were severe, certain, and inescapable. Thus, divine delay is not approval or neglect, but a test and an opportunity, while God's final seizure of those who reject His messengers is inevitable and terrible.

translation: And how many a city We destroyed while it was committing wrong, so it lies in ruins, and [how many] an abandoned well and a lofty palace!
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a lesson: many towns and communities were destroyed by God because of their wrongdoing and rejection of truth. Their dwellings collapsed upon their roofs, their wells—once sources of life—were left neglected, and their lofty palaces stood empty. It teaches that worldly power, wealth, and impressive structures cannot protect a people from the consequences of injustice; such ruins remain as signs for later generations to reflect upon.

translation: Have they not journeyed through the land, so that they may have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear? Indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but the hearts within the breasts that go blind.
interpretation: The verse identifies the heart as the seat of true perception and moral responsibility. Physical travel and sight are only means; if the inner faculty of reason and faith is corrupted, then external observation yields no guidance. The greatest loss is not loss of eyesight but loss of insight: a heart hardened, veiled, or turned away cannot recognize divine signs, learn from history, or respond to truth. Thus people can see and hear yet remain blind and deaf to guidance because their hearts have lost the capacity to comprehend and submit.

translation: And they ask you to hasten the punishment. But Allah will never fail in His promise. And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
interpretation: The demand for immediate punishment reflects human impatience and a failure to grasp divine timing. Allah’s promise of judgment is certain and cannot be annulled; its delay is not negligence or inability, but part of His wise decree and appointed term. Human beings measure time by years, but God’s command transcends human reckoning, so what seems long to us is brief before Him. The believer should therefore remain firm when mocked for the delay of warning, and the wrongdoer should not mistake respite for escape, for the reckoning will come exactly when God wills, and He never breaks His word.

translation: And how many a town did I grant respite while it was doing wrong; then I seized it, and to Me is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s delaying of punishment for a wrongdoing community is not approval of its injustice, nor incapacity to punish, but a period of respite and testing. When the appointed term ends, His seizure is certain and irresistible. The final return of all people is to Him alone, where every deed will be judged with perfect justice.

translation: Say, "O mankind, I am only to you a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet Muhammad to address all of humanity, declaring that his role is not to compel belief or to exercise worldly dominion over them, but solely to deliver a clear and unmistakable warning about the consequences of rejecting God’s message. It emphasizes the universality of his prophethood: the warning is for every people, and it is “manifest” because the truth he conveys is plain, supported by evidence, and free of ambiguity for those who reflect.

translation: So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a generous provision.
interpretation: This verse declares the reward of those who combine true faith with righteous action: God will forgive their sins and grant them a noble, abundant provision. That provision is not merely worldly sustenance but the lasting reward of Paradise and divine favor, showing that faith must be embodied in good deeds and that God’s recompense is generous, pure, and honorable.

translation: And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them—those are the companions of Hell.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who actively exert themselves in hostility toward God’s revealed signs, not merely rejecting them but attempting to obstruct, discredit, and defeat the truth, as though they could escape God’s power or make His purpose ineffective. Their effort is not sincere inquiry but adversarial striving against divine guidance. Because they persist in this opposition and choose to fight the truth rather than submit to it, their rightful end is the company of Hell, the blazing Fire, where they will remain among its inhabitants.

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished or recited, Satan would cast something into his wish or recitation; then Allah abolishes what Satan casts, then Allah makes His verses firm and precise. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet that Satan’s attempts to corrupt prophetic desire or recitation are not new. Every messenger and prophet, when he earnestly longed to convey God’s message and recited it, faced Satan’s effort to inject falsehood, doubt, or distortion. But Satan’s interference cannot ultimately prevail over divine revelation: God cancels the false suggestion and then firmly establishes His own signs, making them clear and unshakable. The verse therefore teaches that God allows the trial of satanic whispering but Himself protects and purifies His revelation, and that His knowledge and wisdom govern both the trial and the final triumph of His truth.

translation: That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is disease and those whose hearts are hardened. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in far-reaching dissension.
interpretation: Allah permits the devil’s suggestion to be cast so that it becomes a test exposing the heart’s condition: the one with doubt and hypocrisy in his heart is disturbed by it, and the hard-hearted is confirmed in arrogance and resistance. Thus the wrongdoers persist in profound opposition to the truth, far from guidance and from the straight path.

translation: And so that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, and so they may believe in it and their hearts may humbly submit to it. And indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse teaches that knowledge given by God leads to recognizing the revelation as true from the Lord, and that such recognition should produce faith and humble submission in the heart rather than arrogance or resistance. It also affirms that God Himself guides the believers toward the straight path, directing them to firm faith, sincere obedience, and right conduct.

translation: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt concerning it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.
interpretation: This verse describes the persistent spiritual condition of those who reject faith: they remain suspended in uncertainty about the truth of the revelation and the promised resurrection, not because the evidence is lacking, but because they defer certainty and postpone submission. That condition is brought to an end either by the sudden coming of the Hour, which leaves no opportunity for correction, or by a punishment described as a “barren day”—a calamity that yields no good, no mercy, and no fruitful outcome for them. The warning is against treating doubt as a safe excuse, since divine judgment arrives abruptly and decisively.

translation: Sovereignty on that Day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them. So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, all authority and kingship belong exclusively to Allah; no created being has any share in rule or judgment. He alone will judge all people with perfect justice, settling their differences and distinguishing truth from falsehood. The verse then states the outcome for the faithful: those who had genuine belief and expressed it through righteous deeds will be admitted into the Gardens of Delight, where they will enjoy everlasting favor and pleasure. Thus salvation is tied to both faith and righteous action, while final sovereignty and judgment belong to God alone.

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses — then those will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This means that those who persist in unbelief and deliberately reject Allah’s revealed signs will be subjected to a punishment that degrades and humiliates them.

translation: And those who emigrated in the cause of Allah and then were killed or died — Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse promises that believers who leave their homes and homelands for the sake of Allah, seeking His pleasure and supporting His religion, and who then either are killed in His path or die naturally before that, will not lose their reward. Allah Himself guarantees them a generous, pure, and everlasting provision in the Hereafter, far better than any worldly gain they left behind. Whether their death comes through martyrdom or an ordinary death, they are all encompassed by this divine promise, and Allah is the most excellent Provider, whose provision never diminishes and whose reward is never wasted.

translation: He will surely admit them to a place of entry that they will be pleased with. And indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This is a firm promise from Allah to those who endured hardship, migration, and sacrifice for His sake: He will bring them into Paradise, an abode of perfect satisfaction, where they will experience a contentment that fully corresponds to their deepest hopes and exceeds their expectations. The wording emphasizes certainty and divine generosity, because the One promising is Allah, who knows every deed, intention, and struggle of His servants, and who is Most Forbearing—He does not hasten punishment for the disobedient and does not withhold reward from the faithful.

translation: That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, then is wronged again, Allah will surely grant him victory. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse permits a wronged person to seek equivalent redress, without exceeding the measure of the injury, but if he is then subjected to further injustice, God Himself guarantees his support. It balances justice with mercy: it affirms the right to proportional self-defense, while the closing names al-‘Afuww and al-Ghafūr invite the injured party toward pardon and assure him that God’s forgiveness and clemency encompass those who seek His way, and that He will not abandon the oppressed.

translation: That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone controls the alternation of night and day, lengthening and shortening them, bringing one into the other by His decree. The One who governs time and the cycles of creation is fully able to change the conditions of His servants, to bring relief after difficulty, and to grant victory to whom He wills. His being Hearing and Seeing means He perceives all that His creation says and does, nothing concealed from Him, so His decree and judgment are perfect.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and Allah is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse affirms that ultimate reality belongs to Allah alone: He is the Truth, the absolutely real and unchanging source of all existence, truth, and authority. Anything worshipped, invoked, or trusted besides Him is falsehood—empty, powerless, and unreal in the face of His divine reality. Because He is the Most High, He is exalted above all creation, beyond any deficiency, partner, or rival; and because He is the Most Great, He is greater than everything and alone worthy of worship, reliance, and ultimate allegiance. Thus, all true meaning, power, and worth come from Him, and every claim to divinity or ultimate dependence apart from Him is null and void.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Aware.
interpretation: This verse calls the human being to reflect on Allah’s power and care: He sends rain from the sky, and the parched earth becomes verdant, a visible sign of His ability to revive and bring forth life. Allah’s being “Latif” (Subtle, Gentle, Kind) means He brings benefit through hidden and delicate means, causing water to reach seeds and roots and bringing forth growth without effort from creation; “Khabir” (Aware) means He knows all states and needs of His creation, and nothing escapes His knowledge. The transformation of dead earth into green life is a proof of resurrection and a call to gratitude and trust in God’s providence.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse establishes that absolute ownership, dominion, and disposal over all creation—both the unseen and visible realms—belong exclusively to Allah. Everything in existence is His property, dependent upon Him, and subject to His will, while He is utterly independent of all things. His being "al-Ghani" means He needs no worship, obedience, provision, or partner from anyone, yet He sustains and provides for all. His being "al-Hamid" means He is intrinsically praiseworthy and deserving of all praise and gratitude, whether or not creation acknowledges Him, and all praise ultimately returns to Him because His essence, names, attributes, and actions are perfect and wise.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the earth, and the ships that sail upon the sea by His command? And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is Most Kind, Most Merciful to mankind.
interpretation: This verse is a call to recognize that the order of the world is both a sign of God's absolute control and a gift of His mercy. The subjugation of earthly things and the sailing of ships by His command mean that human benefit from creation is possible only within the divine order; it is not human ownership or independent power. The holding back of the sky from falling 'except by His permission' expresses that cosmic stability and any withheld judgment are acts of divine preservation, not accidents. Since He is Ra'uf and Rahim toward people, these favors should evoke gratitude, humble obedience, and reliance on Him, while warning against heedlessness of the One who sustains all things.

translation: And He is the One who gave you life, then He will cause you to die, then He will give you life. Indeed, mankind is ever ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the originator and master of life, death, and resurrection. Human beings are described as kafur—intensely ungrateful and denying—because they often ignore or reject the One who continuously sustains them, and they doubt or deny the final resurrection despite witnessing the signs of His power in their own creation and mortality.

translation: For every community We have appointed a rite of worship which they are to observe. So let them not dispute with you over the matter; and call to your Lord. Indeed, you are on a straight guidance.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the diversity of worship rites among communities is by God's decree, not a flaw in religion. Each people was given a prescribed way of drawing near to God, and they are responsible for observing it. Therefore, the Prophet is told not to be drawn into futile arguments about these rites, especially when such disputes are used to reject the core message. His task is to invite people to the One Lord with patience and certainty, because he stands on a clear, straight path. Outward forms may differ according to divine wisdom, but the essential call remains the same: sincere worship and obedience to God alone. Thus the verse comforts the Prophet and directs him to stay focused on his mission rather than let opponents dictate the terms of debate.

translation: And if they dispute with you, then say, 'Allah is most knowing of what you do.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that when people persist in arguing or disputing after the truth has been made clear, the believer should not be drawn into endless contention or attempt to force conviction. Instead, the matter is entrusted to God, who alone fully knows the hidden motives, intentions, and deeds of all people. It is both a consolation to the one being argued with and a warning to those who dispute: God’s knowledge encompasses every action, and He will judge with perfect justice. The response shifts the focus from winning a debate to sincere submission to God’s omniscience and ultimate judgment.

translation: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, God alone will settle every disagreement among people with absolute justice and perfect knowledge. Matters of faith, truth, and religious dispute that people argued about in worldly life will be decided by Him, and each person will face the consequences of what they believed, said, and did. This verse warns against arrogant disputation and affirms that final judgment belongs exclusively to God.

translation: Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a Book. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge is all-encompassing: nothing in the heavens or the earth, whether hidden or apparent, escapes Him. The “Book” denotes the Preserved Record in which all things are already written and decreed, not because Allah needs a record, but to show that His knowledge and decree are exact, complete, and beyond alteration. What may seem vast, hidden, or difficult to human beings is effortless for Allah to know, record, and bring to account. Thus the verse calls the believer to live with watchfulness and trust: no deed, secret, or injustice is overlooked, and every matter returns to the One for whom nothing is difficult.

translation: And they worship besides Allah that for which He has not sent down any authority, and that of which they have no knowledge. And the wrongdoers will have no helper.
interpretation: This verse condemns worshiping anything besides Allah without divine proof or true knowledge. Such worship is based only on ignorance, conjecture, and blind imitation, not on any authority from Allah. Those who persist in this wrongdoing—associating partners with Allah and rejecting His guidance—will have no helper or protector to save them from His punishment.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve disapproval. They are almost on the verge of assaulting those who recite Our verses to them. Say, 'Then shall I inform you of what is worse than that? It is the Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the inner hostility of those who reject God's clear signs: the truth does not merely fail to persuade them; it provokes visible resentment and a violent impulse against the believers who convey it. Their anger at the message is itself a sign of the message's power and their resistance to it. The warning then redirects them from their immediate rage to a far graver reality: the Fire that God has promised the disbelievers. Their present fury and desire to harm the reciters are fleeting, but the punishment awaiting persistent rejection is the worst possible end. Thus the verse contrasts the disbelievers' violent opposition to revelation with the severity of the consequence for denying it, showing that nothing they can do to the messengers is worse than the doom prepared for unbelief.

translation: O mankind, an example is struck, so listen to it. Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they all gathered together for it. And if the fly snatches away anything from them, they cannot recover it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.
interpretation: This verse exposes the absolute helplessness of every false object of worship and every created thing invoked besides Allah. It teaches that no matter how many powerless beings gather together, they cannot originate even the smallest living creature, and they cannot even retrieve something a tiny fly takes from them. The closing phrase means that both the one seeking help from a false deity and the false deity being sought are utterly weak. Therefore all worship, invocation, reliance, and hope must be directed to Allah alone, who alone creates, sustains, protects, and has power over all things.

translation: They have not appraised Allah with the appraisal due to Him. Indeed, Allah is surely Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who deny or neglect God's true majesty, living as though He were limited, dependent, or powerless, or associating others with Him in worship and authority. It affirms that absolute strength and invincible might belong to God alone: He is not weakened by any creature, nor can anyone resist or overpower His will. Therefore, failing to worship, obey, and reverence Him as He deserves is rooted in failing to recognize the reality of His strength and might.

translation: Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among the people. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This means that prophethood and messengership are not acquired by lineage, status, or personal effort; they are a pure divine selection. Allah, in His perfect wisdom, appoints messengers from the angels to carry revelation, and from humankind to convey it and guide their peoples. The verse corrects those who reject or question God's choice of a human messenger, or who set limits on whom He may choose. The closing names All-Hearing and All-Seeing affirm that Allah hears every claim and objection and sees the realities of His creation, so He alone knows whom to entrust with His message, who will remain faithful to it, and who will oppose it.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah all matters are returned.
interpretation: This means that Allah’s knowledge encompasses everything concerning His creation: what lies ahead of them and what lies behind them, the present and the future, the visible and the hidden. Nothing is outside His knowledge. Likewise, every affair and outcome ultimately returns to Allah alone, so He alone decides, judges, and disposes of all matters.

translation: O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good, so that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true success is attained by joining inward faith with outward obedience: humble submission to God in prayer, sincere worship of Him alone, and practical goodness toward others. Bowing and prostration train the soul in humility and surrender; worship keeps the heart directed to its Lord; and doing good confirms faith in daily conduct. Together these lead to flourishing and salvation in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship—the religion of your father Abraham. He named you Muslims before, and in this [revelation], so that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector—excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true religion demands earnest striving in God's cause according to His right, not through extremism or burdensome innovation, but through sincere obedience, worship, moral effort, and struggle against evil. God's choosing the believers is pure grace; the faith He legislated is merciful and free of oppressive difficulty. The religion of Abraham is pure monotheism and total submission to God alone, and the name 'Muslims' expresses that submission, given before and reaffirmed in the Qur'an. The community's purpose is to bear witness to humanity by living and conveying the truth, while the Prophet Muhammad is the witness over it. Prayer, charity, and reliance upon God are the practical means of sustaining this witness. God alone is the true Guardian, and His protection and help are perfect.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Successful indeed are the believers.
interpretation: This verse declares that true, lasting success belongs to those who possess genuine faith in Allah. It redefines success not as worldly achievement but as spiritual salvation and nearness to God, and it presents faith as the foundation of a life that ultimately triumphs. The verse also functions as a divine assurance and a call to make one’s belief sincere, living, and obedient, since such faith is the path to true felicity.

translation: Those who are humbly submissive in their prayer.
interpretation: It means the believers whose hearts are fully attentive, reverent, and humble before God during prayer, with their outward stillness reflecting an inward awareness that they are standing before their Lord.

translation: And those who turn away from vain talk.
interpretation: This describes the believers as people who actively distance themselves from everything useless, frivolous, false, or obscene in speech and action. They do not merely avoid idle talk when it appears; they are inwardly averse to it and turn away from it, guarding their tongues, ears, and time for what is beneficial, truthful, and pleasing to God.

translation: And those who are doers of zakah.
interpretation: This describes the believers as those who consistently fulfill the obligatory zakah: they give the prescribed share of their wealth to those entitled to it, seeking God's pleasure, and by doing so purify both their wealth and their souls. It indicates that true faith is not limited to ritual prayer but also expresses itself in social responsibility and generous obedience to God's command.

translation: And those who guard their chastity.
interpretation: This describes the believers who restrain their sexual desires and protect their private parts from every unlawful sexual act, such as fornication, adultery, and indecency; they keep themselves pure and chaste, limiting sexual relations only to what Allah has made lawful for them, namely marriage and lawful union, in obedience to Allah and preservation of honor.

translation: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that the prohibition against illicit sexual relations does not apply to a man's lawful spouse or to those lawfully joined to him (in the historical context of the verse, those whom his right hand possesses); such intimacy is permissible and carries no blame, while any relation beyond these bounds remains blameworthy.

translation: So whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse declares that anyone who desires or pursues sexual gratification outside the lawful bounds Allah has established—namely, through marriage or what is lawfully permitted—has crossed the limits set by Allah and is therefore among the transgressors.

translation: And those who are keepers of their trusts and their covenant.
interpretation: This verse praises believers who faithfully guard everything God and people have entrusted to them—whether duties, possessions, secrets, rights, or responsibilities—and who honor every covenant and promise they make. Such fidelity is presented as an essential mark of true faith, because violating trusts or breaking pledges undermines justice, trust, and accountability before God.

translation: And those who diligently guard their prayers.
interpretation: This describes the believers as those who consistently preserve and protect their prayers: they perform them at their appointed times, fulfill their conditions and pillars, maintain humility and focus in them, and do not neglect, delay, or corrupt them. Guarding prayer is a sign of sincere faith and ongoing remembrance of God.

translation: Those are the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse identifies the successful believers described just before it as the true heirs: they are the ones who will receive the eternal inheritance of Paradise, a lasting reward that never perishes, granted by God’s grace.

translation: Those who inherit Paradise; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate reward of the believers: they are granted the inheritance of al-Firdaws, the highest and most exalted part of Paradise, as a permanent dwelling. Their abiding there forever signifies that this reward is not temporary but eternal, bestowed by Allah’s grace upon those who lived in faith and righteous obedience, and it points to the permanence, security, and complete bliss of the Hereafter for its people.

translation: And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the human being’s origin is a purified, drawn-out substance from clay—an essence or extract—by God’s creative command. It points to the lowly material origin of the first human, Adam, and, by extension, the stages by which each human is generated from a drop of fluid that is itself sustained by the earth. The verse thus establishes God’s sole power in creation, the humbleness of human beginnings, and the lesson that human nobility is not in physical origin but in the soul and responsibility given by God.

translation: Then We made him a sperm-drop in a firm lodging.
interpretation: This means that God causes the human being, after the initial stages of creation, to originate as a sperm-drop deposited in the womb, a secure and stable place where it is preserved and developed.

translation: Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clinging clot into a lump of flesh, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We brought him forth as a new creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.
interpretation: This passage presents human formation as a chain of divine acts, each stage dependent on God’s ordering power rather than chance. The final “new creation” points to the moment the formed human is given life and spirit, becoming a being with reason, conscience, and moral responsibility. It teaches that human dignity comes from God’s deliberate creation and that the physical process exists within a purpose: to know, worship, and answer to the Creator. The closing declaration affirms that God alone creates in the absolute sense; all human making is derivative, and His creative wisdom, mercy, and perfection are beyond compare.

translation: Then indeed, after that, you are surely to die.
interpretation: This affirms that after the stages of human formation and the span of worldly life, death is an unavoidable decree for every person at their appointed time, and it is the certain transition to the Hereafter.

translation: Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be raised.
interpretation: This verse affirms that after death, human beings will be brought back to life on the Day of Resurrection, raised from their graves to stand before God for reckoning. It establishes the certainty of bodily resurrection and the reality of the Hereafter.

translation: And We have created above you seven paths, and We are not unaware of the creation.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah, by His power and wisdom, made seven layered ways or heavens above humanity, and that He is never absent, heedless, or unmindful of what He has created; rather, He knows, sustains, and governs all creation with perfect care and watchfulness.

translation: And We sent down water from the sky in due measure, and caused it to settle in the earth; and indeed, We are able to take it away.
interpretation: Allah sends rain down from the sky in a precisely determined amount, according to His wisdom and the needs of His creation, neither so little that life cannot be sustained nor so much that it destroys. He then places and stores it within the earth as groundwater, springs, rivers, and reservoirs, making it accessible for people, animals, and plants.
