The closing statement warns that Allah knows both your open and hidden intentions, so the concession must be used honestly and for a rightful purpose.

translation: Say to the believing men: Let them lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what they do.
interpretation: This is a divine command to believing men to practice modesty inward and outward: they are to restrain their eyes from looking at what is forbidden or arousing unlawful desire, and to protect their chastity by keeping their private parts away from illicit sexual conduct. Such restraint is not merely social etiquette; it is purer for the heart, preserves dignity, strengthens faith, and prevents the corruption that follows unchecked desire. Allah’s closing statement that He is fully aware of what they do warns that this command is not measured only by outward appearance but by sincere obedience, since Allah knows every glance, intention, and hidden act.

translation: And say to the believing women: let them lower their gaze and guard their chastity, and let them not display their adornment except what appears thereof; and let them draw their head-coverings over their bosoms; and let them not display their adornment except to their husbands, or their fathers, or their husbands' fathers, or their sons, or their husbands' sons, or their brothers, or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons, or their women, or those whom their right hands possess, or male attendants who have no sexual desire, or children who have not yet become aware of women's private parts. And let them not strike their feet so as to make known what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, so that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse presents modesty as a comprehensive discipline of the heart, body, and social conduct: restraint of the gaze, guarding chastity, and refusing to make beauty an object of public display. The exception for what appears is not license for deliberate exposure but acknowledges the outward and unavoidable; the command to cover the bosom with the head-covering corrects the pre-Islamic manner of displaying adornment and ties covering to a visible ethic of honor. Limiting the display of adornment to the named close relations and dependents preserves the distinction between the privacy of the household and the public sphere. The prohibition of striking the feet to reveal hidden adornment targets indirect allurement, showing that modesty governs movement and intention, not merely clothing. The closing call to repentance for all believers indicates that this standard is part of a larger life of faith, and success is attained by turning back to God and conforming to His guidance.

translation: And marry off the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse places a communal and guardianship responsibility upon Muslims to facilitate marriage for those without spouses—whether never married, widowed, or divorced—and not to exclude the righteous poor or dependents from that right. It specifically forbids using poverty as an excuse to prevent marriage, promising instead that Allah will provide for them from His limitless bounty. The names al-Wāsi‘ and al-‘Alīm affirm that God’s provision is vast and that He knows every person’s condition and needs. Therefore, marriage is presented as an act of worship and chastity, while removing financial barriers to it is an act of trust in God and social justice.

translation: And let those who do not find the means for marriage abstain from sexual relations until Allah enriches them from His bounty. And those slaves who seek a contract of emancipation from among those whom your right hands possess, then make a contract with them if you know there is good in them, and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you. And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, seeking the temporary gains of worldly life. And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse commands sexual restraint for those unable to marry, encourages the fair emancipation of slaves who seek freedom and show moral competence, and strictly forbids owners from forcing slave women into prostitution for worldly profit. It condemns the exploitation of women and makes clear that coerced women are not guilty of the sin; God is Forgiving and Merciful toward them because of the compulsion they endured, while those who coerce them are answerable before God unless they repent.

translation: And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses, and an example from those who passed away before you, and an admonition for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah has revealed clear and unmistakable signs, provided the histories of earlier communities as lessons, and made the Qur’an a warning and reminder that benefits those who fear Allah and guard themselves against disobedience.

translation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp; the lamp is within glass; the glass is as if it were a brilliant pearly star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: One classical reading is that the light here is divine guidance: Allah illuminates the heavens and earth with physical light and with the light of revelation and faith. The niche is the believer’s breast or heart; the lamp is the light of faith and knowledge of God; the glass is the heart’s purity and clarity, through which that light shines like a radiant star. The blessed olive tree is the source of revelation or the pure prophetic message, neither eastern nor western meaning it is not confined to one place, people, or direction, but is universal and uncorrupted. The oil almost glowing before fire touches it indicates the sound human nature and reason that already incline toward truth; when revelation and divine assistance come, it becomes light upon light. Thus Allah guides whom He wills to His light, and He uses parables so people may reflect, while His knowledge encompasses everything.

translation: In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered; He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings.
interpretation: These are the mosques, which God has ordained to be honored, built, and purified, and in which His name is remembered through prayer, recitation, and remembrance; there His worshippers glorify Him at dawn and sunset.

translation: Men whom neither trade nor sale diverts from the remembrance of Allah, nor from establishing the prayer and giving zakah. They fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be overturned.
interpretation: This verse describes the inward and outward condition of true believers: worldly commerce, profit, and the busyness of buying and selling do not take precedence over God-consciousness, worship, and obligatory charity. Their hearts remain oriented to Allah even while they work in the world, because they know that the real and decisive Day is the Hereafter—a Day of such terror that hearts will tremble and shift, and eyes will stare and turn about in fear. Their fear of that Day is not despair; it is reverent awareness that keeps them faithful, prayerful, and generous, refusing to let temporal gain distract them from what is eternal.

translation: That Allah may reward them according to the best of what they did, and increase them from His bounty. And Allah provides for whom He wills without measure.
interpretation: This verse states the purpose and outcome of the believers' devotion described just before it: God does not merely repay them exactly for their deeds; He rewards them according to the best of what they did, overlooking their faults and accepting the finest of their actions. Then He adds more than they deserve from His own favor. The phrase 'without measure' means His provision is not bounded by calculation, merit, or human expectation; He grants both worldly sustenance and eternal reward freely and abundantly to whom He wills. Thus the verse combines hope in divine generosity with confidence that no sincere good deed is lost, and that God's giving is far greater than any human accounting.

translation: And those who disbelieved—their deeds are like a mirage in a barren plain; the thirsty one supposes it to be water, until when he comes to it, he finds it nothing, and he finds Allah there, so He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse teaches that deeds done while rejecting faith may appear promising and fruitful in worldly terms, like a mirage that attracts a thirsty traveler, but when the ultimate reality is unveiled on the Day of Judgment they yield no benefit. The disbeliever will find nothing to rely on except God’s judgment, and God will settle his account with exact justice, swiftly and without delay.

translation: Or [their deeds are] like layers of darkness in a deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which are clouds—darknesses, one above another. When he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he to whom Allah has not granted light—for him there is no light.
interpretation: This is a parable of compounded misguidance: the heart is plunged into a deep sea of ignorance and doubt, overwhelmed by successive waves of desire, confusion, and falsehood, and covered by clouds of heedlessness. These darknesses are layered upon one another, so that even what is nearest—one’s own hand—can scarcely be perceived. Thus the one who rejects guidance cannot discern the truth, however clear it may be, because his deeds and understanding are stripped of the light of faith and sincerity. True light is not acquired by human cleverness or worldly means; it is granted by Allah alone. Whoever Allah leaves without His light has no light whatsoever, no clarity, no guidance, and no path to salvation.

translation: Do you not see that Allah is glorified by whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and by the birds with wings spread? Each has known its prayer and its glorification. And Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This means that the glorification of Allah is universal and real: every created being in the heavens and earth, including birds soaring with outstretched wings, has been taught by Allah its own mode of prayer and praise. Their worship may differ from human worship and may be hidden from us, but it is known to Allah, and He fully knows all that His creatures do.

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse affirms that all sovereignty, ownership, and authority over the heavens and the earth belong exclusively to Allah, and that every created being will ultimately return to Him alone for judgment, accountability, and recompense.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah drives the clouds, then joins them together, then makes them a heap, so you see the rain issuing from their midst? And He sends down from the sky, from mountains within it, hail, and He strikes with it whom He wills and turns it away from whom He wills. The brightness of His lightning almost takes away the sight.
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect on Allah's exclusive lordship over the unseen forces of nature. The movement, gathering, stacking, and precipitation of clouds are not autonomous processes; they unfold under His command, measure, and wisdom. The mention of hail and lightning, which can benefit or harm, teaches that the same created means may be a mercy or a trial according to Allah's will. Therefore, the verse establishes tawhid: no created power controls benefit and harm independently, and human beings should turn to Allah with humility, gratitude, and awe, recognizing that His signs both sustain and overpower them.

translation: Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have insight.
interpretation: The regular succession of night and day is a visible sign of Allah's sovereign power, wisdom, and precise governance of creation; it calls people of spiritual perception to reflect on His oneness, recognize His continuous control over all things, and turn to Him in gratitude and accountability.

translation: And Allah created every moving creature from water. Among them are those who walk on their bellies, and among them are those who walk on two legs, and among them are those who walk on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse directs the mind to God's unlimited creative power and wisdom. He originated every living, moving creature from water, showing that life itself is a gift dependent on His command. The diversity of creatures—some crawling, some walking on two legs, some on four—demonstrates that God's will is not confined to one pattern or form. He creates freely as He wills, and His power is complete over every possibility, whether in creating, sustaining, or bringing forth life. The verse therefore calls for reflection on the signs of divine artistry in the natural world and on human dependence upon the One who alone governs all things.

translation: We have certainly sent down clear verses; and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s revelation consists of unmistakably clear signs that expose the truth and distinguish right from wrong. Yet the mere coming of clear proofs does not compel a person’s heart; guidance to the straight path—the path of faith, sincerity, and obedience to Allah—is a favor granted by Allah to whom He wills, according to His wisdom and knowledge, while the clarity of the message leaves no excuse for rejecting it.

translation: And they say, 'We have believed in Allah and in the Messenger, and we obey'; then a party of them turns away after that. And those are not believers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith is not mere verbal profession. Claiming belief in Allah and His Messenger and pledging obedience is worthless if it is followed by turning away from Allah’s command and the Messenger’s judgment. Such turning away exposes the claim as hollow, so in Allah’s judgment they are not believers. Faith requires sincere assent joined with submission and obedience; whoever persistently rejects obedience after professing faith has not attained the reality of iman, even if he repeats the words of belief.

translation: And when they are invited to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, behold, a party of them turns away.
interpretation: This verse censures those whose professed faith is conditional: when they are summoned to Allah’s Book and the Prophet’s judgment to settle a dispute, a faction among them withholds compliance and turns aside. It teaches that accepting Allah and His Messenger as arbiters is an essential demand of faith; refusal reveals hypocrisy or sickness in the heart, because the believer submits to divine guidance even when the ruling opposes personal desire.

translation: And if the right is theirs, they come to him in willing submission.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who only accept judgment when it favors them. When they are called to Allah and His Messenger for a fair ruling, they turn away if they fear the decision may go against them; but if they know the right is on their side, they come eagerly and submissively. Their obedience is therefore conditional and self-serving, not rooted in sincere faith or love of truth. True submission to Allah requires accepting His judgment whether it benefits or inconveniences oneself.

translation: Is there a disease in their hearts? Or do they doubt? Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them? Nay, it is they who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hidden motive behind those who refuse to submit to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger. It asks whether their resistance comes from a spiritual sickness such as hypocrisy, from doubt in the truth, or from a false fear that Allah and His Messenger might deal unjustly with them. The answer is none of these: the true cause is their own wrongdoing. They are unjust because they reject the truth and resist divine guidance, not because Allah or His Messenger have wronged them in any way.

translation: The only statement of the believers when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them is that they say, 'We hear and we obey.' And those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith is shown when a believer is summoned to Allah and His Messenger for judgment: the believer responds with sincere acceptance and practical obedience, not with hesitation, objection, or preference for another authority. 'We hear and obey' means hearing the command with the heart, acknowledging its truth, and carrying it out. The verse therefore identifies willing submission to divine guidance as the mark of faith and declares that those who respond this way are the ones who attain success in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, and fears Allah and is conscious of Him — then those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that ultimate success is not measured by worldly gain but by a person’s standing with God. It joins outward obedience to Allah and His Messenger with inward fear and God-consciousness (taqwa), showing that true faith requires both action and reverence. Such a person is counted among the winners because they attain God’s pleasure and the reward of the Hereafter.

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if you commanded them, they would surely go forth. Say, 'Do not swear; obedience is known. Indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who try to make up for their lack of sincere compliance with emphatic oaths, claiming they would readily go forth if commanded. They are told not to swear, because real obedience is already known and recognized by its actions, not established by verbal promises. Allah is fully aware of what they do, including their true intentions, so oaths cannot conceal disobedience or substitute for genuine submission. The verse teaches that faith is proven through actual obedience, not through strong claims and swearing.

translation: Say, 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is only what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with. And if you obey him, you will be guided. And there is not upon the Messenger except clear conveyance.'
interpretation: This verse commands people to obey Allah and to obey the Messenger, since the Messenger conveys Allah’s commands and guidance. If people turn away, the Prophet is not accountable for their rejection; his responsibility is only to deliver the message clearly, while they are accountable for how they respond. Obeying the Messenger is the path to right guidance, and the Messenger’s duty is not to compel belief but to convey the clear message.

translation: Allah has promised those among you who have believed and done righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession [to authority] upon the earth just as He granted it to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that, then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse presents divine empowerment as a covenant conditioned on faith, righteous action, and pure worship. The promise of succession, establishment of the divinely chosen religion, and security after fear is not an unconditional privilege but the fruit of sincere servitude to Allah alone. It reminds believers that outward victory and peace are tied to inward loyalty and obedience; when a community fulfills that covenant, Allah grants it authority and stability, as He did for previous faithful communities. The concluding warning makes clear that rejection or betrayal after such a promise is not mere weakness but a departure into fisq—disobedience that forfeits the promised blessing.

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger, so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to fulfill three interconnected duties: to establish the prayer consistently with its prescribed times, purity, conditions, and sincerity; to give the obligatory zakah as a means of purifying wealth and aiding the needy; and to obey the Messenger Muhammad in what he commanded and forbade. The concluding phrase, “that you may receive mercy,” shows that these acts of worship and obedience are a path toward Allah’s mercy, forgiveness, and ultimate success. It also indicates that divine mercy is sought through faithful submission, not merely claimed by wishful thinking.

translation: Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape Allah on the earth. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse warns that disbelief, worldly power, wealth, or influence cannot place anyone beyond Allah’s authority or allow them to evade His judgment. Those who reject faith may appear secure or successful in this life, but they cannot frustrate Allah’s decree or escape the ultimate reckoning. Their final home is the Fire, which is the most miserable end. The verse thus calls believers not to be intimidated or deceived by the apparent dominance of disbelievers, and it affirms that divine justice is certain and that persistent rejection of truth leads to ruin.

translation: O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those among you who have not reached puberty ask permission of you three times: before the dawn prayer, and when you lay aside your garments at midday, and after the evening prayer. These are three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you or upon them after these times. They are constantly moving about among you, some of you upon others. Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse lays down the etiquette of privacy within the household. It requires servants and minors who have not yet reached puberty to seek permission before entering upon adults during three specific times when people are likely to be in a state of undress or private rest: before Fajr, during the midday rest when clothes are removed, and after Isha. These are designated as times of privacy. Outside these times, they may come and go without asking permission, since they must circulate to serve and attend to needs. The ruling trains the young and the household in modesty and respect for boundaries, and it shows that Allah's legislation is based on knowledge of human needs and wisdom in regulating them.

translation: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission, as those before them asked permission. Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses; and Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse marks the transition from childhood to adulthood in matters of household privacy and permission. Once children reach puberty, they are no longer treated with the leniency granted to young children who have not yet reached maturity; rather, they must seek permission before entering private spaces, just as adults before them were commanded. This trains them in modesty, respect for others’ privacy, and obedience to Allah’s boundaries. Allah’s clarification of these rulings shows His knowledge of human social needs and His wisdom in establishing stages of moral responsibility.

translation: And the elderly women who do not expect marriage — there is no blame upon them that they lay aside their garments, without displaying adornment. But that they remain modestly reserved is better for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This is a concession for women who have reached an age at which they no longer hope for marriage: they are not blamed for removing the outer garment, such as the cloak, because the reason for strict covering—fear of desire and temptation—has lessened. However, this permission is conditional: they must not display adornment or intend to attract attention. Their remaining covered and practicing self-restraint is better and more virtuous. Allah hears all words and knows all intentions, so the ruling is based on sincerity and what is truly in the heart.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor blame upon the lame, nor blame upon the sick, nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses, or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or that whose keys you possess, or the house of your friend. There is no sin upon you that you eat together or separately. But when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses, so that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse establishes that physical disability or illness must not become a barrier to social and familial participation, especially in the shared blessing of eating together. It also expands the circle of permitted hospitality: one's own household, close and extended family, trusted dependents, and sincere friends form a sphere of intimacy where believers may eat without fear of wrongdoing. The permission to eat together or separately shows that the religious concern is not rigid uniformity but fellowship, generosity, and removal of unnecessary hardship. The command to greet upon entering houses raises ordinary social conduct to an act of worship: the greeting of peace is a blessed and pure gift from God, renewing kinship and sanctifying the home with remembrance and goodwill. Thus the verse teaches that divine guidance orders human relationships through ease, trust, gratitude, and peace, so that believers may use reason to recognize God's signs in everyday life.

translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not leave until they ask his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission—those are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some matter of theirs, give permission to whom you will among them and ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith is not merely an inward claim but is proven by disciplined obedience to Allah and His Messenger. In matters that unite the community—such as gatherings, consultations, or shared undertakings—believers do not withdraw according to their own convenience; they seek the Prophet’s permission first. Their seeking permission is itself a mark of sincere faith and respect for divinely guided authority. The Prophet, in turn, may grant leave to whomever he judges wise, and he is commanded to seek forgiveness for them, showing that leadership must combine order, consideration, and mercy. Thus, Allah’s forgiveness and mercy are tied to humble submission and proper conduct within the believing community.

translation: Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of one of you to another. Allah surely knows those among you who slip away, hiding behind others. So let those who violate his command beware, lest a trial afflict them or a painful punishment afflict them.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the Prophet’s summons, call, or command is not to be treated like an ordinary call between people. It carries divine authority, so believers must respond to it with reverence, seriousness, and prompt obedience, not with indifference, evasion, or secret withdrawal. Allah is fully aware of those who sneak away or use excuses to avoid the Prophet’s call, even if they think they are unnoticed. The warning is severe for those who oppose or disobey his command: they may be struck by a trial that exposes their hypocrisy, causes division, or corrupts their faith, or they may suffer a painful punishment. Therefore, the verse calls for honoring the Messenger’s authority and submitting to his guidance sincerely.

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He already knows what you are upon, and the Day when they will be returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah’s absolute sovereignty over all creation and His complete knowledge of every condition, intention, and deed. Because all things belong to Him and all will return to Him, no action is hidden or forgotten; the Day of Return will expose the reality of deeds and bring exact recompense. The verse thus calls the human being to live with accountability before Allah, sincerity in worship, and awareness that God’s knowledge encompasses both the present state of the heart and every future outcome.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, so that he may be a warner to all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse declares God’s supreme blessedness and majesty in revealing the Qur’an as al-Furqan—the criterion that separates truth from falsehood, guidance from error, and right from wrong. By sending it upon His servant Muhammad, God honors him with the station of servitude before prophethood, showing that true messengership is rooted in humble submission to the Divine. The purpose of this revelation is universal warning: it addresses all peoples, not one tribe or nation, calling them to recognize their Creator, accept His guidance, and heed the consequences of rejecting it. Thus the verse affirms the Qur’an’s divine origin, the Prophet’s role as a warner, and the global scope of the final message.

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in dominion, and who created all things and determined them with precise determination.
interpretation: This affirms God's exclusive sovereignty and absolute oneness: all authority over the heavens and earth belongs to Him alone, with no creature sharing His rule or possessing independent power. His transcendence excludes any son or partner, denying all notions of divine lineage, plurality, or divided godhead. Creation is neither random nor self-governing; He originates everything and ordains for it a precise nature, function, term, and measure according to His wisdom, so nothing exists or operates outside His decree.

translation: And they have taken besides Him gods that create nothing, while they are themselves created; and they do not possess for themselves any harm or benefit, nor do they possess death, life, or resurrection.
interpretation: This verse condemns the idolaters’ taking false gods besides Allah and exposes the utter helplessness of those deities. They cannot create anything at all, because they are themselves created and dependent; they have no power even over their own harm or benefit, let alone over the affairs of those who worship them; and they control neither death, nor life, nor the raising of the dead. The verse thus establishes that lordship, creative power, benefit and harm, and authority over life, death, and resurrection belong exclusively to Allah alone, so worship and reliance must be directed to Him only.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, 'This is nothing but a lie he has invented, and other people have helped him with it.' They have indeed brought forth an injustice and a falsehood.
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbelievers’ accusation that the Prophet Muhammad fabricated the Qur’an with assistance from others. Their claim is not an honest inquiry but a deliberate slander born of rejection and arrogance. By calling it an invented falsehood, they unjustly deny the revelation and falsely attribute it to human collusion. The Qur’an declares that such an accusation is itself an act of injustice and falsehood, because it opposes the truth, maligns the Prophet’s character, and rejects God’s clear signs without any valid proof.

translation: And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon."
interpretation: This verse reports the disbelievers’ false accusation against the Prophet Muhammad: they claimed that the Qur’an was nothing but ancient tales and fables of earlier nations, which he had copied or commissioned to be written, and which were being recited or dictated to him at morning and evening. It exposes their attempt to dismiss the Qur’an as humanly sourced plagiarism rather than divine revelation, despite the fact that such a charge was baseless and contradicted the Qur’an’s inimitability and the Prophet’s known truthfulness.

translation: Say, 'It has been sent down by the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving, Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse answers those who claim the Qur'an is fabricated or humanly composed by pointing to its Revealer: the One whose knowledge embraces every hidden thing in the heavens and earth. Because He knows the innermost secrets, He alone is the true source of revelation and is fully aware of what hearts conceal, including the motives of those who deny it. The names Forgiving and Merciful then show that He does not immediately punish such denial but invites repentance, pardoning those who return to Him and extending mercy through the very revelation they were rejecting.

translation: And they said, 'What is this messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why was not an angel sent down to him to be with him as a warner?'
interpretation: This verse reports the disbelievers' objection to the Prophet Muhammad, using his ordinary human needs and his movement among people as a pretext to reject him. Their demand that an angel be sent alongside him reveals a corrupt standard: they wanted prophethood to be accompanied by supernatural exemption from human life, not by the guidance, character, and message that God actually sent. The verse shows that eating food and walking in markets are not faults; they are part of the messenger's humanity, which makes him able to serve as a clear example, speak to people in their own condition, and endure what they endure. Their objection was not a sincere search for proof, but a refusal of the human messenger and of God's chosen way of warning humankind. Even if an angel were sent, their deeper resistance would remain, because the problem was not lack of wonders but unwillingness to submit to divine guidance.

translation: Or a treasure should be cast down to him, or he should have a garden from which he eats. And the wrongdoers say, “You follow none but a man bewitched.”
interpretation: The demand for a treasure to be sent down or for a private garden to sustain him shows that the rejecters were measuring prophethood by worldly wealth and miraculous display, not by truth and moral evidence. Their refusal was therefore not due to a lack of proof, but to arrogance and a materialistic standard they imposed on the Messenger. Calling him “bewitched” was a false accusation used to dismiss the clear message and justify their rejection, revealing that the real obstacle was their unwillingness to submit, not any deficiency in the Prophet or the revelation.

translation: Look how they strike parables for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.
interpretation: The disbelievers’ invented comparisons and mocking descriptions of the Prophet are not evidence against him but signs of their own confusion. Because they reject the clear truth and resort to false analogies, their hearts lose the ability to perceive guidance, and they become unable to find the straight path to God.

translation: Blessed is He who, if He willed, could have made for you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and could make for you palaces.
interpretation: This verse declares God’s limitless power and generosity and answers the disbelievers’ mockery of the Prophet. They demanded signs, treasure, or a garden as proof, but God says that if He willed, He could instantly give His Messenger far better than what they proposed: orchards with rivers flowing beneath them and grand palaces. The conditional “if He willed” shows that God is not bound by their demands; He grants or withholds according to His wisdom. The verse comforts the Prophet and rebukes those who measure truth by worldly wealth, while pointing to the greater, everlasting gardens and dwellings God has prepared for the faithful.

translation: Nay, they deny the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who reject the coming of the Last Hour and the resurrection. Their denial is not due to a lack of signs but to stubborn rejection of accountability before God. Therefore, God declares that He has already prepared Sa‘ir—a blazing punishment—for everyone who persists in denying the Hour. The verse warns that rejecting the Hereafter is a grave matter with certain and severe consequences, and it affirms that divine justice and retribution are fully prepared for such deniers.

translation: When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear it raging and roaring.
interpretation: This describes Hell’s terrifying readiness to receive those who denied the truth: although they are still far from it, it perceives them and erupts with sounds of wrath and roaring, so that its dread reaches them before they enter. The verse uses this vivid image to convey the severity of the Fire and the horror awaiting the arrogant rejecters.

translation: And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein, bound together in chains, they will call out there for destruction.
interpretation: The meaning is that the people of Hell will be cast into a cramped, confining place, shackled and unable to escape, and their cry for destruction expresses utter despair: they will wish for annihilation or death as a release from their torment, but it will not be granted. This signifies the severity of their punishment and the complete loss of hope and relief after they rejected the truth and persisted in wrongdoing.

translation: Do not call today for a single destruction, but call for many destructions.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment: when they see the punishment, they will wish for annihilation to escape their torment, but they are told that one destruction will not be enough. Their suffering will be so severe and unending that they will cry out for many destructions, yet this wish will not save them. It expresses utter despair and the futility of seeking escape from the consequences of rejecting faith.

translation: Say, 'Is that better or the Garden of Eternity which has been promised to the God-conscious? It will be for them a reward and a destination.'
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that contrasts the fate of the deniers—the punishment and disgrace just described—with the everlasting Paradise promised to the God-fearing. It declares that the eternal garden is far better, for it is not a temporary relief but a perpetual home. The promise is certain because God has prepared it as the recompense for those who guard themselves against His displeasure and as their final return. Thus the verse urges the listener to weigh the two ends and choose the path that leads to the eternal reward.

translation: For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding eternally. It is upon your Lord a promise requested.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the people of Paradise will enjoy everything they desire, forever, without end or deprivation. Their bliss is not merely a hope but a firm promise binding upon the Lord, one that He has obligated Himself to fulfill and that His servants ask of Him in supplication. It shows God’s perfect truthfulness, generosity, and faithfulness: He will certainly bring about the eternal reward He has promised to the righteous.

translation: And on the Day He will gather them together along with what they worshipped besides Allah, He will say, 'Did you mislead these servants of Mine, or did they stray from the path?'
interpretation: In this verse, Allah describes a scene of accountability on the Day of Judgment. He questions the false objects of worship not to gain information, but to publicly expose the idolaters' excuse and to demonstrate that their devotion was based on no divine command. The questioned beings—whether angels, prophets, jinn, or inanimate idols—will disown any claim to divinity and deny having led anyone astray. The verse thus emphasizes that misguidance ultimately stems from people's own choices, that no created being shares in Allah's lordship, and that every soul is responsible for whom or what it worships. It warns against blind imitation and false attribution of guidance or divinity to anyone besides Allah.

translation: They will say: 'Glory be to You! It was not for us to take besides You any allies. But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment, until they forgot the Reminder, and they were a ruined people.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the disavowal by the false objects of worship on the Day of Judgment. They declare God's perfection and absolve themselves of any claim to divinity or allegiance, denying that they ever instructed people to take them as guardians apart from God. The responsibility lies with the worshippers: God granted them and their forebears worldly ease and respite, and instead of responding with gratitude and remembrance, they let those blessings distract them until they forgot divine guidance. Thus they became 'būr'—ruined, barren of good, and deserving of destruction. The passage teaches that false gods cannot benefit or defend their followers, and that prolonged prosperity can become a trial that leads the heedless to forget God and meet a wasted end.

translation: They have certainly denied you in what you say, so you cannot avert [the punishment] or obtain help. And whoever of you does wrong, We will make him taste a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse declares that the false objects of worship and the powers people relied upon besides God will disown their followers and reject the claims they made, leaving the wrongdoers utterly helpless on the Day of Judgment: they can neither repel the punishment nor find any helper. It then warns that whoever commits the grave injustice of associating others with God—or any wrongdoing that merits divine retribution—will be made to taste a severe punishment. The passage thus exposes the futility of depending on anything other than God and affirms that His judgment is inescapable and just.

translation: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they indeed ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you be patient? And your Lord is ever Seeing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all earlier messengers were human beings who shared ordinary human needs, such as eating and moving about in public to earn a living and carry out their duties. Their humanity was not a defect in their prophethood; rather, it was part of Allah’s wise way of sending guidance through people who could be followed and understood. The differences and inequalities Allah places among people—wealth and poverty, strength and weakness, authority and subjection, ease and hardship—are a trial for one another, revealing who will remain patient, grateful, and obedient. Patience here means trusting Allah’s decree, not using disparities as an excuse for arrogance or disbelief, and recognizing that Allah sees all intentions and deeds and will judge with perfect justice.

translation: And those who do not expect to meet Us say, 'Why were angels not sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?' They have indeed become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great transgression.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who reject the meeting with God and the Hereafter, yet demand that faith be made contingent on their own conditions: that angels be sent down to them visibly or that they be allowed to see their Lord directly. Their demand is not a sincere request for guidance but a symptom of pride and self-importance. They effectively set themselves up as judges over God's revelation, refusing to submit to a human messenger unless their preferred supernatural proof is granted. The verse exposes that their real obstacle is not lack of evidence but arrogance and insolent excess, a transgression that oversteps the limits of creaturely humility and lordship.

translation: On the Day they see the angels, there will be no glad tidings that Day for the criminals, and they will say, "A barrier, forbidden!"
interpretation: This verse describes the terror of the criminals when the angels appear to them, either at death or on the Day of Judgment. Unlike the righteous, who receive good news, the criminals are given no glad tidings; they cry out, 'hijran mahjura,' which was an Arab expression for seeking a protected barrier or sanctuary. They desperately wish for a barrier between themselves and the punishment, but it is forbidden and will not avail them. Their plea for refuge is rejected, and they face the consequences of their disbelief and sins.

translation: And We will turn to whatever deeds they did and make it scattered dust.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will bring the deeds of those who rejected faith and acted for other than Him to account, then render them utterly worthless—like fine dust scattered in the air, having no weight, no reward, and no benefit. Their works may have appeared substantial in the world, but because they were not built on true faith and sincere devotion to God, they are annulled and dispersed.

translation: The companions of Paradise on that Day will be better in dwelling and more beautiful in resting place.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the people of Paradise will have the finest and most excellent abode, enjoying perfect security, comfort, and rest, in contrast to the wretched destination of the people of Hell. Their eternal home is the best settlement and the most pleasant place of repose.

translation: And on the Day when the heaven will split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, descending in ranks.
interpretation: This verse describes a decisive event of the Hereafter: the sky will be rent open and clouds will appear, and the angels will descend in vast, orderly multitudes by God’s command. It affirms the reality of resurrection and judgment, the overwhelming transformation of the creation on that Day, and the perfect obedience of the angels as executors of the divine decree. The verse conveys the majesty and certainty of God’s judgment without implying any likeness to created things in His essence.

translation: True sovereignty on that Day belongs to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every false claim to power, lordship, or independent authority collapses on the Day of Judgment; absolute rule and judgment then belong exclusively to Allah, whose mercy is inseparable from His justice. The Day is hard for the disbelievers because they meet the consequences of rejecting Him: no intercessor or worldly power can shield them, and the reality they denied becomes undeniable. Thus, the hardship is not arbitrary but the inevitable fruit of denying the truth and persisting in opposition to the Most Merciful.

translation: And [beware] the Day when the wrongdoer will bite his hands, saying, 'Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way.'
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the one who wronged himself through disbelief, rejection, or obstinate opposition to the truth will be consumed by regret, biting his hands in anguish and wishing too late that he had followed the Messenger’s path and taken the way of faith and obedience alongside him.

translation: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a friend.
interpretation: This is the remorseful cry of a wrongdoer on the Day of Judgment, expressing deep regret over having taken a particular person as an intimate companion. The use of "so-and-so" leaves the identity open, showing that the warning applies to anyone—human or jinn—whose friendship leads a person away from God's remembrance and guidance. It teaches that choosing close friends who turn one from truth brings ruinous regret in the Hereafter.

translation: He has certainly led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me. And Satan is ever a deserter to man.
interpretation: This is a warning that no bond, influence, or friendship is worth being turned away from God's guidance after it has reached a person. The regret expressed on that Day is not merely about a companion's deception but about having surrendered one's own responsibility; the ultimate deceiver, Satan, entices people and then abandons them when they need help most. Thus the verse teaches that true loyalty belongs to God and His revelation, and that every misleading voice will prove treacherous to the one who follows it.

translation: And the Messenger has said, 'O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur’an as something abandoned.'
interpretation: This is the Prophet’s complaint to Allah that his people turned away from the Qur’an—rejecting it, neglecting its recitation, and refusing to follow its guidance—so it stands as a warning against abandoning the Book in belief, recitation, reflection, or practice.

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. And sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and Helper.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet Muhammad and all who carry the prophetic message: opposition from evildoers is not a new or unique trial, but a recurring pattern established by God for every prophet. The enmity of criminals does not diminish the prophet’s mission or indicate divine abandonment; rather, it exposes the moral divide between truth and corruption. The closing assurance teaches reliance on God alone: He is enough to guide the faithful to truth and to grant them victory, protection, and support against every opposing force.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why was the Qur’an not sent down to him all at once?' Thus [it is], so that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have revealed it gradually, in distinct and well-ordered portions.
interpretation: This verse answers the disbelievers’ objection to the Qur’an being revealed piece by piece rather than as a single whole. Its meaning is that gradual revelation was not a deficiency but a deliberate divine method: it allowed the Prophet’s heart to be continually reassured, strengthened, and steadied as each portion came with new guidance, consolation, and confirmation. The phrase “and We have revealed it gradually” also carries the sense that God sent it in clear, measured, perfectly arranged parts, suited to circumstances and human capacity, so that it could be received, understood, memorized, and acted upon with firmness rather than as an overwhelming burden. Thus the verse presents the Qur’an’s mode of descent as evidence of wisdom, mercy, and firm grounding, not as a reason for doubt.

translation: And they do not bring to you any example except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.
interpretation: This verse means that whenever the disbelievers raise an objection, devise a false comparison, or ask a question meant to cast doubt, God will provide the Prophet with the true answer and a clearer, more excellent clarification. It affirms that divine revelation is fully sufficient to refute falsehood, and that God’s explanation is the most accurate, wise, and beneficial.

translation: Those who will be gathered to Hell on their faces—those are worst in place and most astray from the way.
interpretation: This verse declares the disastrous end of those who persist in denial and arrogance: they will be driven to Hell in a condition of utter humiliation and helplessness, described as being gathered upon their faces. Their “worst place” is Hell, the most wretched destination, and their “most astray way” means their path in life was the furthest from truth and guidance, since they rejected the clear signs and the Messenger and preferred disbelief, mockery, and self-willed misguidance over faith and obedience. Thus the verse teaches that true standing is measured not by worldly reputation but by one’s final abode and by whether one followed the straight path.

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as a minister.
interpretation: This verse establishes that prophetic guidance and authority come from God alone: He granted Moses the Book and strengthened him by making Aaron his brother a wazir—a helper, deputy, and supporter in the mission. Aaron shared the burden of conveying the divine message, confirming that God may support a prophet with human assistance and that familial closeness can serve the call to truth, while ultimate legislation and command remain with God.

translation: So We said, 'Go, both of you, to the people who have denied Our signs.' Then We destroyed them with utter destruction.
interpretation: This refers to Moses and Aaron being sent to Pharaoh and his people, who rejected God's miraculous signs. Their persistent denial and oppression were met with total destruction—Pharaoh and his forces were drowned—showing that rejecting divine messengers and signs brings ruin, and that God's justice and power inevitably overtake those who persist in falsehood.

translation: And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse teaches that rejecting a prophet sent by God is equivalent to rejecting the entire prophetic message, because all messengers convey the same fundamental call to worship God alone and obey His guidance. The drowning of Noah’s people is therefore not merely a historical punishment but a lasting sign for all humanity that divine justice overtakes those who persist in denial. The same painful punishment is prepared for every wrongdoer who knowingly opposes God’s messengers and His guidance.

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud and the companions of the Rass and many generations in between.
interpretation: This verse cites bygone nations—'Aad, Thamud, the people of al-Rass—and numerous other generations as examples of communities that Allah destroyed after they persisted in rejecting His messengers and signs. It warns that no people, including the Quraysh addressed by the Qur'an, are exempt from the same consequence if they continue in denial and heedlessness.

translation: And for each [of them] We set forth parables, and each [of them] We destroyed with utter destruction.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah left no community without clear warning: He presented to every one of them parables, lessons, and signs so that the truth might be established and the proof completed against them. Yet when they persisted in denial, He annihilated each of them completely, uprooting them with total destruction. It emphasizes both the fullness of divine admonition and the severity of divine punishment for those who reject it, warning the hearers that they are not exempt from the same pattern.

translation: And indeed they have passed by the city that was rained upon with an evil rain. Did they not see it? Rather, they were not expecting any resurrection.
interpretation: This verse reminds the disbelievers of the fate of the people of Lot, whose town was destroyed by a shower of stones as punishment for their corruption. The Meccan polytheists used to pass by its ruins on their journeys, yet they failed to reflect on that clear sign. Their heedlessness is traced to their denial of resurrection and accountability; because they did not expect to be raised and judged, they did not take warning from the destruction of those who preceded them, and thus persisted in their own rejection.

translation: And when they see you, they take you only in mockery, saying, 'Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?'
interpretation: This verse describes the polytheists’ scornful rejection of the Prophet Muhammad. Whenever they saw him, they ridiculed him and sarcastically questioned whether an ordinary human being like him could truly be God’s messenger. Their mockery exposes their arrogance and unwillingness to accept divine guidance when it comes through a human prophet rather than according to their own worldly expectations.

translation: He would nearly have misled us away from our gods, had we not been steadfastly devoted to them. But they will soon know, when they see the punishment, who is farther astray from the way.
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbelievers' stubborn attachment to idolatry: they admit that the Prophet's message was so persuasive that it almost pulled them away from their false gods, yet they pride themselves on having remained patient in their error. Their own words become a warning against them: when the punishment appears, the truth will be undeniable, and they will realize that those truly led astray from the right path were not the Prophet and his followers, but they themselves, who chose devotion to invented deities over the clear guidance brought to them.

translation: Have you seen the one who takes his own desire as his god? Then would you be a guardian over him?
interpretation: This verse condemns the person who lets his whims and desires become the ultimate authority in his life, effectively worshiping them instead of God. The rhetorical question addressed to the Prophet means that he cannot compel such a person to believe, nor is he responsible for managing or guarding his faith. The Prophet’s duty is only to deliver the warning; guidance and accountability belong to God alone.

translation: Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are only like cattle; rather, they are further astray from the way.
interpretation: This verse exposes the delusion that most deniers can be guided merely by being made to hear or understand, because hearing and reasoning benefit only when the heart is willing to submit to the truth. They have ears but do not hear for guidance, and minds but do not reason to acknowledge their Creator’s right. Their likeness to cattle is that they are driven by appetite, habit, and immediate sensation rather than by truth and accountability. Yet they are worse than cattle, because animals follow the limits set for them by instinct and cannot rise to moral responsibility, while these people were given intellect, revelation, and choice; by rejecting guidance they corrupt the very faculties meant to lead them to God, so their path is farther from the straight way.

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord has extended the shadow? And if He had willed, He could have made it stationary. Then We made the sun an indication of it.
interpretation: This verse calls attention to God's power and wisdom in the ordering of the natural world: the shadow is spread out by His command, and had He willed it would remain fixed and unmoving. By making the sun a sign that points to the shadow, God establishes a measurable, changing order in creation, so that shadows become a means of recognizing time, motion, and the dependence of all things on His decree. It is a summons to reflect on divine providence and the signs of God in the horizon.

translation: Then We withdrew it to Us, a gradual withdrawal.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the shadow is entirely subject to Allah’s command: He alone extends it and then draws it back to Himself. The phrase “an easy/gentle withdrawal” indicates that Allah’s decrees unfold with perfect control, ease, and precision, not by random natural forces. It calls the servant to reflect on Allah’s power, mercy, and wisdom in ordering creation, and on the truth that all things ultimately return to Him.

translation: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing and sleep as rest, and has made the day a resurrection.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah, in His mercy, designed the daily cycle to serve human needs: the night covers people with darkness like a garment, shielding them and providing calm; sleep is a form of rest and temporary cessation of activity that renews the body and mind; and the day is a revival or rising after sleep, when people are brought back to movement, work, and seeking provision. Thus the alternation of night and day reflects divine care, order, and the resurrection of life after rest.

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as bearers of glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky purifying water.
interpretation: This means that Allah alone directs the winds, making them run ahead of rain as a sign of His mercy, and He alone sends down water that is pure in itself and purifies others. It shows His power and kindness in preparing causes and providing what gives life to the earth and its creatures, so that people may know His oneness, rely on Him, and respond with gratitude and worship.

translation: So that We may give life thereby to a dead land, and give it as drink to many of the cattle and human beings We created.
interpretation: This verse presents the sending down of rain as a sign of Allah’s power and mercy: He revives barren, lifeless earth through it, causing vegetation and life to appear, and He provides it as drink for livestock and for a multitude of human beings. It teaches that the same divine power that gives life to dead land can raise the dead, and that water is a shared provision sustaining both animals and people, calling them to recognize their dependence on their Creator and to be grateful.

translation: And We have certainly distributed it among them so that they may remember, but most people refuse except disbelief.
interpretation: The verse means that Allah turns and distributes rain among His servants, sending it to different lands and peoples in turn so they may take heed, remember His mercy and power, and respond with faith and gratitude; yet most people meet this blessing not with thanks and belief, but with denial and ungratefulness.

translation: And if We had willed, We would have sent into every city a warner.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah’s absolute power and wisdom: He was fully able to send a separate warner to every town, but He chose instead to send Muhammad as a universal warner to all humanity. Therefore, the Prophet should not grieve over rejection, and the people should not think that their disbelief can thwart Allah’s plan. The verse also teaches that the manner of sending messengers is determined by divine wisdom, not by human expectation, and that the Prophet’s duty is to convey the message while guidance ultimately rests with Allah.

translation: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it [the Qur’an] with a great striving.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet—and, by extension, the believers—not to yield to the demands of those who reject faith, especially any request to compromise or soften the divine message. The command to struggle against them “with it” means using the Qur’an itself as the primary means: proclaiming it, presenting its proofs, refuting falsehood, and exerting the utmost effort in patience, da‘wah, and moral-spiritual steadfastness. Thus the “great striving” here is not first a physical battle but an intellectual, spiritual, and missionary struggle to uphold and convey the truth.

translation: And it is He who has let loose the two seas: this one fresh and sweet, and this one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and a forbidden partition.
interpretation: This verse is a sign of God's sovereign power and mercy in the ordering of creation: He causes two bodies of water to exist side by side, one palatable and fresh and the other saline and bitter, yet by His command a hidden, inviolable barrier keeps each from corrupting or overrunning the other. The 'barrier' and 'forbidden partition' express a divine decree of separation and restraint, showing that God governs the laws of nature with perfect precision and that His power can preserve distinct things even when they appear to meet. It calls the servant to recognize the Creator who alone maintains this balance, provides drinkable water, and holds back harm, and it points to His ability to distinguish, preserve, and judge all things.

translation: And He is the One who created from water a human being, then made him into lineage and marriage. And your Lord is ever All-Powerful.
interpretation: Allah alone originated the human being from a lowly fluid, showing His power to create life from something seemingly weak. From this creation He established two fundamental bonds that hold human society together: nasab, kinship by blood and descent, and sihr, relation by marriage and in-laws. These ties preserve identity, regulate family life, cultivate love and responsibility, and connect people beyond their immediate relatives. The verse thus calls attention to Allah’s creative power and His wisdom in ordaining the social fabric of humanity through family relationships.

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them; and the disbeliever is a helper against his Lord.
interpretation: This verse exposes the futility of worshipping anything besides Allah: such false deities can neither bring benefit nor cause harm, so they are utterly powerless and unworthy of worship. It then describes the disbeliever as one who stands as a helper and ally against his Lord—meaning that by rejecting faith and supporting falsehood, he aligns himself in opposition to Allah, resisting His guidance and aiding the cause of disbelief, even though he depends entirely on Allah’s sustenance and mercy.

translation: And We have not sent you except as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse defines the Prophet Muhammad’s mission as one of conveying good news to those who accept God’s guidance and warning those who reject it, while making clear that he is not sent to compel belief or to take charge of people’s hearts; his duty is to deliver the message, and God alone guides and holds accountable.

translation: Say, 'I do not ask you for it any reward, except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord.'
interpretation: The verse declares that the Prophet’s call is not motivated by any payment, fee, or personal gain from the people. The only thing that can be considered an “exception” is not a wage for him but the free choice of those who wish to seek a path to their Lord. In other words, whatever benefit comes from accepting the message returns entirely to the listener: through faith, obedience, and turning to God, they take a way toward Him. This underscores the sincerity of the prophetic mission and human responsibility—guidance is offered, but each person must choose to take that path.

translation: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [Allah] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse directs the believer to place absolute trust in Allah alone, the Ever-Living who never dies, unlike all created beings whose lives end. It joins reliance upon Him with continually glorifying and praising Him, showing that trust in Allah is not passive but accompanied by remembrance and worship. Since He is fully aware of the sins of His servants, He is sufficient as a guardian and reckoner: no wrong escapes His knowledge, and He will judge with perfect justice while also being able to forgive whom He wills. Trusting in the One who never dies is the safest support, because every other object of reliance eventually perishes or fails.

translation: He who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days, then rose over the Throne—the Most Merciful. So ask about Him one who is well acquainted.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah alone created the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them in six days by His power and wisdom, and then ascended over the Throne in a manner that befits His majesty, without resemblance to any created thing. He is Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful, whose mercy encompasses all. The command to ask about Him one who is well acquainted means that true knowledge of Allah’s names, attributes, and actions must be sought from the one informed by revelation—namely, His Prophet—rather than from speculation or ignorance.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Prostrate to the Most Merciful,' they say, 'And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to what you order us?' And it increases them in aversion.
interpretation: This verse exposes the stubborn arrogance of those who reject the call to worship Allah under His name al-Rahman. Their question is not a sincere search for truth but a mockery and denial; they refuse to submit to the Prophet’s command and resent being called to humble themselves before the Most Merciful. Their refusal reveals a heart unwilling to acknowledge Allah’s mercy, authority, and right to be worshipped, so the call to prostration only deepens their alienation and aversion. It teaches that true worship requires humility before Allah alone and that rejecting His names and commands out of pride leads only to further distance from guidance.

translation: Blessed is He who placed in the heaven constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon.
interpretation: The verse declares God's supreme blessedness and transcendent goodness, made evident through the purposeful order of the heavens. The constellations are signs of precise divine arrangement, not random occurrences. The sun is described as a lamp—a source of light and heat—while the moon is luminous, reflecting light in a gentler way. Together they reveal the Creator's wisdom, power, and mercy, and they function as signs for humanity: to mark time, seasons, and direction, and to inspire reflection on the One who set them in place.

translation: And He is the One who made the night and the day succeeding one another for whoever desires to remember or desires to give thanks.
interpretation: The alternation of night and day is not merely a physical cycle but a continuous divine provision: each passing period is a renewed chance for the heedful soul to turn back to God in remembrance and for the grateful heart to recognize His favors. The one who wants to remember finds in every night and day a fresh occasion to awaken from heedlessness, and the one who wants to thank finds in the constant renewal of time a repeated invitation to acknowledge God's bounty. Thus time itself is presented as a mercy and a test: its succession exposes whether a person will use the recurring opportunities for remembrance and gratitude.

translation: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth gently, and when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace.'
interpretation: This verse describes the distinguishing conduct of those who truly serve Allah: their humility is visible even in how they walk, showing no arrogance, aggression, or self-importance. When provoked or addressed harshly by ignorant people, they do not answer with insult or violence; instead they respond with words of peace and safety, restraining anger and refusing to descend into conflict. Their character reflects mercy received from Allah, so they carry that mercy into their dealings with others, especially when tested by provocation.

translation: And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing [in prayer].
interpretation: This describes the believers as people who devote the night to their Lord in humble worship, willingly giving up sleep to stand before Him and prostrate themselves in prayer. Their standing and prostration signify complete submission, sincerity, and constant devotion to God, seeking His pleasure rather than showing off before others.

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is a persistent torment.'
interpretation: This verse describes the sincere servants of God who, alongside their other virtues, turn to Him in humility and fear, asking Him to protect them from the torment of Hell. Their prayer shows that they do not rely on their own deeds but seek God's mercy and grace. The statement that Hell's punishment is 'gharam' conveys that it is an inescapable, clinging, and perpetual suffering—an overwhelming retribution that never loosens its grip and cannot be resisted or escaped by any human power. Thus the verse teaches that awareness of the Hereafter should lead a believer to earnest supplication, seeking refuge in God from His severe punishment while hoping for His forgiveness.

translation: Indeed, it is an evil dwelling place and residence.
interpretation: The verse declares that Hell is the most wretched possible final abode: a place that combines the pain of being settled in torment with the agony of having no escape or reprieve. It teaches that the ultimate loss is not merely punishment but the horror of an eternal dwelling whose very atmosphere is evil. Thus it drives the believer to seek God's protection from it and to choose deeds that lead to a goodly residence with God.

translation: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor miserly, but are moderate between that.
interpretation: This verse praises a balanced disposition in the use of wealth: the believer neither squanders excessively nor withholds tightly, but keeps to a just middle course. It teaches that all spending—whether for oneself, family, charity, or other rightful needs—should be guided by moderation, neither exceeding proper limits nor denying what is due, so that wealth remains a means of obedience and benefit rather than an occasion for excess or hardness of heart.

translation: And those who do not invoke besides Allah another god, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that will incur a penalty.
interpretation: This verse defines essential signs of true servitude to Allah: exclusive worship and invocation belonging to Him alone, absolute respect for the sanctity of life except when the Lawgiver permits killing through a just legal cause, and abstention from unlawful sexual relations. It thus rejects shirk, murder, and zina as grave violations of Allah’s rights and human rights. The ending warns that whoever falls into these crimes will meet the punishment and consequence Allah has appointed, indicating that such acts are not trivial but carry serious accountability before Him.

translation: The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who commit the grave sins mentioned before it—associating others with Allah, unjustly killing a soul, and unlawful sexual relations—and do not repent will receive an intensified, multiplied punishment on the Day of Judgment. They will remain forever in the Fire, utterly disgraced and contemptible, because their crimes were not only severe but also compounded by persistence and defiance against God’s commands.

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; for them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This exception means that sincere repentance, when joined with faith and righteous action, does not merely erase past sins but transforms them: God replaces the evil deeds with good deeds as an act of pure grace. It teaches that no sinner should despair of God’s mercy, because He is not only forgiving but actively turns the penitent’s past into a means of nearness and reward.

translation: And whoever repents and does righteous deeds—then indeed he turns to Allah with a true turning.
interpretation: This verse teaches that repentance is not merely regret or words; it must be accompanied by righteous action. The one who abandons sin and then does good is not simply leaving evil behind but actively directing his life back to Allah. The emphatic wording indicates that this is the essence of true repentance: a sincere, decisive return to God, which He recognizes and accepts. Thus genuine tawbah is a total turning of the heart and conduct toward Allah.

translation: And those who do not witness falsehood, and when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity.
interpretation: This verse describes the refined conduct of the faithful: they keep away from falsehood, false testimony, and gatherings of sin, and when they encounter idle, obscene, or vain speech and behavior, they do not participate in it, nor do they lower themselves to quarrel or imitate it; instead, they pass by honorably, preserving their dignity, faith, and moral integrity.

translation: And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind.
interpretation: This describes the believers' responsive and heedful attitude toward divine revelation. When the signs and verses of their Lord are brought to their attention, they do not meet them with the indifference of deaf ears and blind eyes. They do not turn away, neglect, or reject them; instead, they listen attentively, understand with insight, and submit to the guidance they contain. Their hearts are alive to God's reminders, so the revelation increases them in faith, reflection, and obedience.

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us an imam for the righteous.'
interpretation: It means that Allah’s faithful servants pray for spouses and children who are righteous and obedient, so that seeing them brings deep joy and strengthens the heart in faith. They also ask Allah to make them leaders and examples in piety, so that the God-conscious may follow them in worshipping and obeying Allah, not for worldly status or praise.

translation: Those will be rewarded with the high chamber because they patiently persevered, and they will be met therein with greeting and peace.
