The verse thus calls the servant to worship and depend on God alone, since everything else is temporary, and final accountability rests entirely with Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif Lam Meem.
interpretation: The Basmala is a formula seeking Allah's name, grace, and mercy at the outset of recitation. Alif Lam Meem is among the disjointed letters that open certain surahs; its exact meaning is known to Allah alone, and it serves as a divine sign pointing to the Qur'an's miraculous nature and urging the listener to give heed to the revelation that follows.

translation: Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, 'We believe,' and will not be tested?
interpretation: This verse rejects the notion that a mere verbal claim of faith is sufficient and exempts a person from trial. God declares that believers will inevitably be tested in order to distinguish sincere faith from mere profession, to purify the heart, to expose hidden weaknesses, and to make true conviction visible through patience, obedience, and steadfastness. The test may come through hardship, loss, opposition, temptation, or religious duties, but it is not a sign of divine abandonment; rather, it is part of the moral and spiritual order by which faith is proven and strengthened. Therefore, claiming belief should not lead to expecting ease and safety from accountability, but to preparing for examination with trust in God and perseverance.

translation: And We have certainly tried those before them, so Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.
interpretation: This verse establishes that trials and testing are a divine pattern for all communities: God tests people so that the reality of their faith becomes manifest. Although God’s knowledge is eternal and nothing is hidden from Him, the test distinguishes in actual experience between those who are sincere in their claim of faith and those who are false. It consoles the believers who face hardship and persecution, assuring them that their patience and truthfulness are known to God, while the liars and hypocrites will inevitably be exposed and held accountable.

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can escape Us? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning against those who persist in wrongdoing while assuming they can elude God's power or avoid the consequences of their deeds. Their belief that they can outrun divine justice is itself a corrupt judgment, because it ignores God's absolute authority, His perfect knowledge, and the certainty of accountability. The verse declares that no wrongdoer can frustrate God's will or find refuge from His grasp; the apparent delay of punishment is not proof of escape but a summons to repent before the inevitable reckoning.

translation: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then indeed the appointed term of Allah is coming. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse assures everyone who sincerely longs for the meeting with Allah in the Hereafter—whether by desiring His reward, fearing His judgment, or seeking His pleasure—that the fixed time appointed for that meeting will inevitably arrive. No one should imagine it is far off or uncertain, for Allah’s decree cannot be delayed or avoided. The mention that He is the Hearing, the Knowing means He hears every claim of hope and knows every hidden intention and deed, so He will judge with perfect justice and reward according to what is truly in the hearts and expressed in action.

translation: And whoever strives, then he only strives for himself. Indeed, Allah is Free of need from the worlds.
interpretation: This verse teaches that all sincere struggle, effort, and striving in obedience to Allah—whether against one’s own lower desires, in worship, or in upholding truth and justice—ultimately benefits the one who strives. Its reward, purification, and spiritual growth return to the servant, not to Allah. Allah is absolutely self-sufficient and independent of all creation; He gains nothing from anyone’s obedience and loses nothing from anyone’s disobedience. Therefore, striving should be done sincerely for His sake alone, not as if Allah were in need of it, but because the servant himself is in need of that striving for his own salvation and nearness to his Lord.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds — We will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse conveys a firm divine promise: when faith is joined to righteous action, Allah does not merely forgive past shortcomings but erases them, so that they no longer stand against the servant. Then He rewards such people according to the best of their deeds — meaning He accepts the good they did at its highest level, overlooks deficiencies and failures, and grants them a reward greater than the strict recompense their actions deserved, out of His grace and generosity.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents. But if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that kindness to parents is a divinely ordained duty, but it is not an unconditional obedience that can override the core obligation of tawhid. If parents pressure or command a person to commit shirk—associating with God anything for which no true knowledge or authority exists—the believer must refuse that specific disobedience to God, while still maintaining rightful conduct toward them in worldly matters. The verse ultimately directs all accountability to God: every person returns to Him, and He will reveal the reality of all deeds, so no familial bond can justify compromising His oneness. It also consoles believers whose families oppose their faith, affirming that their final judge and protector is Allah.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds — We will surely admit them among the righteous.
interpretation: This is a divine promise that true faith is inseparable from righteous action: God will not only reward such believers individually but will join them with the company of the righteous, granting them a place among the virtuous and honoring them with their fellowship and end.

translation: And among the people are those who say, 'We have believed in Allah.' But when they are harmed in the way of Allah, they treat the persecution of people as if it were the punishment of Allah. And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, 'Indeed, we were with you.' Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of all worlds?
interpretation: This verse exposes a faith that is shallow and conditional. Such people may verbally profess belief, but when they are tested by hardship, insult, or persecution for Allah's sake, they treat human hostility as though it were an unbearable divine punishment, and thus they retreat from truth or compromise their loyalty. Their allegiance is not grounded in sincere devotion to Allah but in convenience and self-interest. If the believers later receive help and victory from Allah, these same people rush to claim solidarity with them, hoping to share in the success. The verse teaches that true faith demands patience, steadfastness, and sincerity under trial, and that Allah alone knows the hidden motives and true condition of every heart. Outward claims and opportunistic alliances cannot conceal what is inside a person from Him.

translation: And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: Allah already knows all things eternally; this verse means He will bring the truth of people’s inner states to light through trials and circumstances, distinguishing genuine faith from hypocrisy, and He will recompense each person according to what they truly are.

translation: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.' But they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the deceit of those who reject faith when they invite believers to abandon their religion by promising to carry the consequences of their sins. Such a promise is false: on the Day of Judgment no one can bear another's burden, and every person is accountable for their own deeds. It warns believers against being misled by false guarantees and affirms that those who make such promises are liars, since they cannot and will not carry the sins of others.

translation: And they will surely carry their own burdens, and other burdens along with their own burdens; and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection concerning what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: This is a severe warning to those who invent lies about God and lead others into misguidance: they will be held accountable not only for their own sins but also for the sins of those they misled, because they will carry the burden of their own wrongdoing plus the burden of the corruption they caused in others. On the Day of Resurrection they will be questioned about the falsehoods they fabricated, and every claim they invented against God and His religion will be exposed and requited.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years; then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse conveys that the effectiveness of the prophetic call depends not on the length of time or human effort but on Allah's guidance. Noah's 950-year perseverance among a rebellious people demonstrates the height of prophetic patience and steadfastness, while their continued wrongdoing—rooted in denial and injustice—made them liable to the flood as a just divine punishment. It warns that persistent rejection of truth and oppression eventually meets Allah's judgment, and it comforts the faithful that their responsibility is to remain constant in calling to truth, not to force hearts to believe.

translation: So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah delivered Noah and those who were with him in the ark from the overwhelming flood, and that the ark—together with the deliverance it brought—was left as an enduring sign of divine power, justice, and mercy, so that all peoples and generations might take heed that Allah saves those who follow His command and destroys those who reject it.

translation: And [mention] Abraham, when he said to his people, 'Worship Allah and fear Him. That is better for you, if you know.'
interpretation: Abraham is presented as a model calling his people away from false gods to the pure worship of Allah alone and to taqwa—mindful awareness of God that leads to obedience and avoidance of sin. The verse teaches that true good, success, and protection lie in this worship and God-consciousness, not in inherited idolatry. The closing phrase 'if you know' is an invitation to use reason and true knowledge: anyone who understands reality will see that devotion to the One God is better for both this life and the Hereafter.

translation: You only worship idols besides Allah, and you invent falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse exposes the emptiness of directing worship and reliance to anything other than Allah. The idols people set up cannot create, harm, benefit, or provide sustenance; calling them gods is itself a fabricated falsehood. True worship, dependence for provision, and gratitude belong exclusively to Allah, the sole Provider and Sustainer. Since every person will ultimately return to Him, life must be oriented around sincere devotion to Him alone, seeking His bounty and thanking Him for His favors, rather than clinging to powerless false objects of worship.

translation: And if you deny, then nations before you have also denied. And the Messenger is only responsible for clear conveyance.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and warns the rejecters: rejection is not a new phenomenon, and its consequences befell earlier nations; the Messenger’s mission is limited to delivering the divine message plainly and completely, while guidance and accountability belong to God alone.

translation: Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse points to the reality of resurrection by appealing to the visible fact of creation itself: the One who brought creation into existence in the first place is fully able to bring it back again after death. Since originating creation from nothing is the greater wonder, restoring it is not difficult for Allah; therefore, denying the return to life is unreasonable in light of God's power and the evidence of the first creation.

translation: Say, 'Travel throughout the earth and observe how He originated creation. Then Allah will bring about the final creation. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse directs people to study the signs of God in the natural world and in history, recognizing that the One who originated life and the universe is fully able to raise the dead for the Hereafter. The journey and observation are not merely for curiosity but to strengthen certainty in resurrection and accountability. The concluding phrase grounds this in God's unlimited power, meaning no stage of creation—whether the first or the final—is beyond His capability.

translation: He punishes whom He wills and shows mercy to whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse establishes that ultimate authority over punishment and mercy belongs exclusively to God. His will is not subject to any external constraint, yet it is never arbitrary, for it is grounded in His perfect wisdom and justice. Human beings cannot claim entitlement to mercy or exemption from accountability; both are dispensed by His decree. The closing phrase, “and to Him you will be returned,” fixes the final destination of every soul before God, where His mercy and justice will be fully manifest and every person will face the consequences of their deeds. Thus the verse calls for humility, repentance, and reliance upon God alone, rather than presumption about one’s fate.

translation: And you are not able to frustrate [Allah's will] on the earth or in the heaven, and you have no protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: This verse declares that human beings cannot escape God's power or thwart His decree anywhere—neither on earth nor in heaven. It emphasizes that no one, whether earthly or heavenly, can overpower God or evade His judgment. Then it states that besides Allah there is no guardian to protect them and no helper to aid them against Him. Thus all true protection and support belong to God alone, and those who rely on false gods or worldly powers will find no one to save them from His punishment. The verse calls for humility, accountability, and sincere reliance upon Allah.

translation: And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and in the meeting with Him—those have despaired of My mercy, and those will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse means that rejecting God's revealed signs and denying the encounter with Him in the Hereafter leads a person to cut off all hope of God's mercy. Such despair is the natural consequence of their own disbelief: because they refuse the truth and the accountability it brings, they remain far from divine mercy and are promised a severe, painful chastisement.

translation: So the only answer of his people was that they said, “Kill him or burn him!” Then Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse shows that when the opponents of truth are unable to meet prophetic evidence with sound argument, they often turn to coercion and violence; the demand to kill or burn Abraham was not a reasoned reply but an admission of spiritual bankruptcy. Allah’s rescue of Abraham from the fire is a demonstration that His power stands above all created causes: what normally consumes and destroys was rendered harmless by His command. For believers, this is a sign of God’s guardianship over those who call to His oneness, a proof that no earthly force can defeat His decree, and an encouragement to remain steadfast under persecution while relying upon Allah’s deliverance and promise of aid.

translation: And he said, “You have only taken idols besides Allah as a means of affection among yourselves in the life of this world. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will disown one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.”
interpretation: This is a warning spoken by Prophet Abraham to his idolatrous people. It exposes that their idolatry was often rooted not in genuine conviction but in social bonding: ancestral loyalties, tribal unity, and mutual affection built around false gods. Such worldly ties cannot survive the Hereafter. On the Day of Resurrection, those who shared in the same false worship will turn against one another, each denying and cursing the other, blaming one another for their ruin. Their love and companionship will become hatred and abandonment. Because they chose false objects of devotion instead of the one true God, their final abode is the Fire, and there will be no one to help or rescue them. The verse teaches that loyalty and love must be founded on truth and on God alone; any unity or affection based on shirk is temporary and ultimately leads to loss.

translation: So Lot believed in him. And he said, 'Indeed, I will emigrate to my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse shows that after Abraham called his people to the worship of God alone, Lot alone responded with faith in his message. Abraham then declared his intention to leave his people and homeland for the sake of his Lord, entrusting himself to God, who is All-Mighty and All-Wise. The verse teaches that true faith may sometimes be accepted by few, that migration or withdrawal from an environment of disbelief can be an act of worship when done for God, and that the believer should rely on God's power and wisdom to protect and guide those who sacrifice for His sake.

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed prophethood and Scripture among his descendants, and We gave him his reward in this world. And indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse refers to Abraham: after he endured trials and remained devoted to God, God rewarded him by granting him Isaac and Jacob as righteous descendants, and by continuing prophethood and revealed scripture within his lineage. His reward in this world includes honorable mention, a blessed family, and a lasting legacy of faith, while in the Hereafter he is among the righteous who receive God’s favor and salvation.

translation: And Lot, when he said to his people, 'Indeed, you commit such an immorality as no one among the worlds has ever committed before you.'
interpretation: This verse recounts Prophet Lot’s denunciation of his people’s brazen sexual vice. The 'immorality' (al-fahishah) is the sin of men seeking sexual gratification with men, which they introduced and normalized. The phrase 'no one among the worlds has ever committed before you' stresses that it was an unprecedented violation of the natural order and of God’s law, not a minor transgression. By confronting them, Lot establishes that moral corruption becomes especially grave when it is collectively practiced, publicly defended, and made a communal norm; it invites divine punishment and the collapse of the society that persists in it.

translation: Do you indeed approach men, cut off the road, and commit in your gatherings what is wrong? And the answer of his people was nothing but that they said, 'Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: The verse condemns the people of Lut for three grave sins: pursuing men sexually in defiance of the natural and revealed order, waylaying travelers and cutting off the roads so that security and safe passage are destroyed, and openly committing shameful acts in their assemblies without shame or restraint. Their only response to Lut’s call was not repentance but arrogant mockery: they challenged him to bring Allah’s punishment if he were truthful. This reveals a people so entrenched in defiance that they preferred testing the prophet over turning back to God, and it serves as a warning that persistent moral corruption, aggression against others, and contempt for divine warnings invite ruin.

translation: He said: My Lord, support me against the corrupting people.
interpretation: This is the supplication of Prophet Lot, who, after his people rejected his message and persisted in spreading moral corruption and evil, turns to God for help. He asks God to grant him victory and deliverance from those who corrupt society, expressing complete reliance on God and the hope that He will defend the truth and judge the corrupters.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with good tidings, they said, 'Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse describes the angels whom God sent to Abraham with the glad news of a son. After conveying that joy, they informed him that they had also been sent to destroy the city whose inhabitants were persistent wrongdoers. The city is understood to be the people of Lot, and their wrongdoing refers to their grave corruption and defiance of God's commands. The verse establishes that divine punishment comes upon a people only after their injustice and moral corruption become entrenched, and it shows that God's messengers carry out both glad tidings for the righteous and judgment upon the wicked.

translation: He said, “Indeed, Lot is in it.” They said, “We know better who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.”
interpretation: This exchange shows Abraham’s compassionate concern for Lot and the believers in the city marked for destruction. The angels, however, affirm that God’s knowledge is complete: He knows exactly who deserves to be saved and who deserves the punishment. Divine deliverance is not based on proximity to the righteous or family ties alone, but on faith and righteous alignment. Thus Lot and his believing household are rescued, while his wife is excluded because she chose to side with the corrupt people and remained behind for destruction. The verse teaches that God’s judgment is perfectly just and that even within a family, each soul is accountable for its own response to truth and obedience.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed because of them and felt constrained by them. They said, 'Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is among those who remain behind.'
interpretation: The angels sent to punish Lot's people arrived in human form. Lot feared that his guests would be harmed by his town's depravity, and he felt powerless to protect them. The messengers calmed him: he had no reason to fear for himself or grieve over the doomed, for God would deliver him and his believing household—except his wife, who had chosen the way of the corrupt and would remain with them in destruction. The verse shows that divine rescue comes to the faithful, while kinship or proximity to a righteous person does not benefit one who persists in unbelief and betrayal.

translation: Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town a punishment from the heaven because they have been defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse announces that the inhabitants of Lot’s town had reached a condition in which their transgression was no longer accidental or private but communal, settled, and defiant. The “rijz” sent down from heaven is a divine chastisement that exposes the moral filth they had embraced and confirms that their corruption had become a direct challenge to God’s order. Their “fisq” means they had deliberately left the bounds of faith, decency, and natural propriety, persisting in that course despite warning. The verse therefore teaches that such punishment is not arbitrary: it is the just consequence of a people who chose to normalize rebellion against God and violate the covenant of human dignity. It also shows that when a community hardens itself in disobedience, the decree of accountability comes from beyond human power to avert, and the messengers who warned them are vindicated.

translation: And We have certainly left of it a clear sign for a people who understand.
interpretation: The destroyed settlements of Lot’s people were left as a visible and enduring proof of the consequence of rejecting the messengers and persisting in corruption. It is a lesson that only those who use their reason and reflect on the fate of earlier nations can truly grasp and take warning from.

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb; he said, 'O my people, worship Allah and hope for the Last Day, and do not go about the earth spreading corruption.'
interpretation: This verse presents Shu'ayb’s call to his people as rooted in three inseparable obligations: exclusive worship of Allah, living with hope and accountability toward the Last Day, and refusing to spread corruption in the land. The command to worship is not merely ritual; it establishes the believer’s orientation toward God. Hoping for the Last Day means keeping the final judgment before the mind so that desire for divine reward and fear of divine punishment shape conduct. The prohibition against 'going about the earth spreading corruption' targets all forms of social, economic, and moral mischief—especially the dishonest trade and exploitation for which Shu'ayb’s people were known. Thus true faith must manifest in justice, honesty, and restraint from harming others, not in lip service or private piety alone.

translation: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became fallen prone in their homes.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the people of Madyan after they rejected the prophet Shu‘ayb: their denial of the messenger and his message brought upon them a devastating divine punishment. The “Rajfah” is a violent tremor or earthquake that overtook them suddenly, and the phrase “fallen prone in their homes” shows them utterly lifeless and helpless in the very dwellings they had trusted for security. It is a warning that persistent rejection of prophetic guidance leads to sudden ruin, and that no worldly home, strength, or refuge can protect a people once Allah’s judgment comes.

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud, and their dwellings are clearly visible to you. Satan made their deeds seem fair to them, so he diverted them from the path, though they were endowed with insight.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning that ruin comes upon those who allow Satan to beautify their wrong actions, turning them away from God's path. The remains of 'Aad and Thamud are visible proofs of what happened when people with the capacity to see and understand still chose arrogance, self-delusion, and obedience to false allurements over clear guidance. It teaches that Satan does not compel; he deceives by making evil appear attractive, and even those who possess insight can be led astray if they prefer desire and pride to truth. Therefore, one must remain watchful, take lessons from the fate of past nations, and refuse to let worldly deceptions blind the heart.

translation: And [We destroyed] Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman. And indeed Musa came to them with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they were not able to outrun [Our punishment].
interpretation: This verse presents three archetypes of corrupt power—Qarun’s wealth, Pharaoh’s political tyranny, and Haman’s executive/religious authority—all of whom were confronted by Musa with unmistakable divine signs. Their arrogance was not merely personal pride but a rebellious exaltation in the land: they rejected God’s authority and oppressed His servants while assuming their combined status made them invulnerable. The phrase “they were not able to outrun” means they could neither escape God’s decree nor precede Him in judgment; their power could not frustrate His will or avert the destruction that came upon them.

translation: So each We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those whom the blast seized, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would never wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse establishes that divine punishment is never arbitrary but is the just consequence of each people's own sin. The varied forms of destruction—stoning winds, an overwhelming cry, the earth swallowing, and drowning—show that God's power executes judgment in ways suited to the condition of every transgressing nation, yet the root cause is always the same: rejection of truth and persistence in wrongdoing. God does not wrong His servants by punishing them; rather, they wrong themselves by choosing disbelief, arrogance, and corruption after messengers had come to them. Their ruin is therefore the fruit of their own deeds, not a defect in divine justice.

translation: The example of those who take protectors besides Allah is like the spider that takes a home; and indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider, if only they knew.
interpretation: This parable exposes the futility of relying on any protector, power, or object of worship besides Allah. Such reliance may appear to offer shelter and security, but it is as flimsy as a spider’s web: it cannot bear real weight, protect from harm, or endure. The verse compares the whole structure of dependence built upon false patrons to a web, whose apparent intricacy conceals its utter frailty. “If only they knew” indicates that the tragedy is not simply lack of information but failure to reflect, so they mistake a fragile illusion for a reliable support. True strength, protection, and permanence belong only to Allah.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows whatever thing they invoke besides Him; and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah's knowledge encompasses every object, being, or imagined power that people call upon, worship, or seek help from besides Him. Nothing they invoke, nor their intentions and deeds, is hidden from Him. Because He is al-Aziz—the Almighty, invincible, and dominant, whom nothing can overcome or frustrate—and al-Hakim—the Wise in all His commands, decrees, and judgments—the verse serves as a warning and assurance: the false objects of worship are utterly known and powerless before Him, and His judgment concerning those who set up rivals to Him is perfectly wise and just.

translation: And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the parables and analogies in the Qur’an are not mere illustrations but profound vehicles of divine guidance. Their real meaning and lesson become accessible only to those who possess deep knowledge—knowledge of God, His revelation, and the spiritual realities behind outward things—so that they can move from the surface example to the underlying truth. Thus the verse places responsibility on the listener: the same parable can instruct one person and leave another unmoved, depending on whether it is received with a discerning, God-conscious intellect.

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: The creation of the heavens and the earth with truth means that the universe is not a random or purposeless occurrence, but an ordered act of divine wisdom and power. For believers, contemplating this creation becomes a clear sign that leads them to recognize God’s oneness, wisdom, and sovereignty, and to respond with faith and reverence.

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer restrains from indecency and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet and, through him, the believers to remain devoted to reciting and conveying the revealed Book and to make prayer a firm, ongoing practice. Prayer is presented as a moral and spiritual safeguard: when performed with sincerity and awareness, it turns the heart away from shameful acts and unjust conduct, because it repeatedly brings the servant before God and renews God-consciousness. The phrase “the remembrance of Allah is greater” teaches that conscious remembrance of God—and God’s own remembrance of the servant—is the greatest reality and support in worship and life, surpassing the outward act and its visible effects. Finally, God’s knowledge of all that people do means that worship must be sincere, for He sees both the deed and the hidden intention behind it.

translation: And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in the best manner, except for those among them who do wrong; and say: We believe in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to you, and our God and your God is One, and to Him we submit.
interpretation: This verse lays down the principle of respectful, reasoned dialogue with Jews and Christians, using the best arguments and manners, while excluding from this courtesy those who persist in oppression or hostility. Muslims are taught to acknowledge the earlier revelations and to affirm the shared foundation of God’s oneness—that the God of the Qur’an and the God of the earlier scriptures is One—and to declare their submission to Him. This does not require accepting every belief of the People of the Book as true, but it establishes common ground for invitation and discussion, with ultimate allegiance to God alone.

translation: And thus We have sent down to you the Book. So those to whom We gave the Book believe in it, and among these are those who believe in it. And none reject Our signs except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the revelation of the Qur’an to Muhammad is part of God’s consistent practice of sending scriptures. It explains that sincere recipients of earlier scriptures recognize the Qur’an as confirming what they have and believe in it; likewise, some among the contemporary addressees also accept it. The only ones who deny these clear signs are those whose rejection stems from deliberate disbelief and covering of the truth, not from a genuine lack of evidence. It teaches that acceptance of divine revelation depends on humility and openness, while rejection is a moral and spiritual condition called kufr.

translation: And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you write it with your right hand; then the falsifiers would have doubted.
interpretation: This verse is a decisive proof of the Prophet Muhammad’s truthfulness and the divine origin of the Qur’an. He had lived among his people for decades without reading any previous revealed book or writing anything with his own hand. Had he been literate or known for studying earlier scriptures, the liars and rejecters would have used that as a pretext to claim that he had copied or composed the Qur’an from human sources. By keeping him unlettered and free of such suspicion, God made the Qur’an’s miraculous character clear and left the falsifiers without any plausible excuse for their doubt. Thus the verse refutes their accusations and confirms that the Qur’an could only have come from God.

translation: Rather, it is clear verses [preserved] in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge. And none reject Our verses except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s signs are not obscure or doubtful; they are luminous and firmly rooted in the hearts of those granted true knowledge. Such people recognize them because their inner sight is sound. Denial does not arise from a genuine lack of evidence, but from injustice and willful opposition to the truth—so the wrongdoers alone reject God’s signs.

translation: And they say, "Why were not signs sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."
interpretation: The disbelievers demanded that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) be given miraculous signs from his Lord as proof of his prophethood. Allah answers that the sending of signs belongs exclusively to Him; He alone decides what signs to grant and when, according to His wisdom. The Prophet’s role is not to produce miracles on demand but to deliver a clear warning. Thus the verse establishes that true guidance comes from Allah, while the Messenger’s duty is to convey the warning plainly and leave the matter of signs and belief to Allah.

translation: Does it not suffice them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed, in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.
interpretation: The Qur’an itself, continuously recited and conveyed to them, is the sufficient and enduring proof of the Prophet’s mission; it is not merely information but a living mercy that purifies and guides, and a reminder that awakens hearts to truth. Yet this mercy and reminder become effective only for those who choose faith and are willing to receive it.

translation: Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah — it is they who are the losers."
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet to rely on Allah’s testimony as the decisive answer to those who dispute his message. Allah’s witness is sufficient because His knowledge embraces everything in the heavens and the earth, both what is visible and what is hidden, including the secret intentions and inward states of those who argue against the truth. The real measure of success is therefore not human acceptance, power, or numbers, but whether one is aligned with the truth Allah has revealed. Those who give their faith to falsehood—whatever is taken as an ultimate object of trust, worship, or allegiance besides Allah—and reject Allah are the true losers, for they have traded the enduring truth for something hollow and will experience the fullness of that loss in the Hereafter.

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment. Were it not for an appointed term, the punishment would have come to them. But it will surely come upon them suddenly, while they do not perceive.
interpretation: The disbelievers demand the punishment as a challenge, mocking the warning. God answers that its delay is due to a fixed decree and an appointed time, not inability or neglect. If that term were not set, punishment would already have overtaken them. Yet it will definitely come without warning, catching them unaware in their heedlessness. The verse thus affirms God's forbearance and the certainty of His judgment: delay is not denial, and mockery cannot avert the appointed hour.

translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment; and indeed, Hell is encompassing the disbelievers.
interpretation: The disbelievers mockingly demand that the punishment be brought immediately as a challenge to the Prophet, but the verse declares that Hell already surrounds them through its causes and will inevitably overtake them. Their haste cannot alter God's appointed time, nor can it avert what is certain. The punishment is inescapable for those who persist in disbelief, and the present-tense wording emphasizes that they are already within its grasp unless they turn back in repentance.

translation: On the Day when the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say, 'Taste what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse describes the overwhelming and inescapable nature of divine punishment for those who knowingly rejected truth and persisted in wrongdoing. The punishment coming from above and below signifies that no direction offers relief and no avenue of escape remains; it is a complete envelopment by the consequence of their own choices. God's statement, “Taste what you used to do,” expresses perfect justice: the suffering is not arbitrary but is the direct requital of their deeds, making them experience the reality of what they once dismissed or denied. It affirms that every action has moral weight and that accountability before God is certain and fully deserved.

translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed, My earth is spacious, so worship Me [alone].
interpretation: This verse calls believers who are constrained, persecuted, or prevented from worshipping God freely to recognize that the earth belongs to Him and is vast enough for them to find a place where they can serve Him. It commands them not to let any land, people, or oppressive circumstance keep them from sincere worship, and if necessary to migrate for the sake of their faith. The ultimate obligation is to direct all worship exclusively to God, trusting that He will provide a way out and that no earthly power can rightfully stand between the servant and his Lord.

translation: Every soul will taste death, then to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse declares that death is an inescapable divine decree appointed for every living soul; no one can avoid it or delay it. The return “to Us” means that after death every soul is brought back to God alone for reckoning and recompense, so ultimate accountability belongs to Him and not to any created being.

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds—We will surely settle them in high chambers of Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Excellent is the reward of the workers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God’s promised reward in Paradise is for those who join sincere faith with righteous action; He Himself guarantees to place them in lofty dwellings of the Garden, beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain eternally, and He declares this to be an excellent recompense for those who labor in obedience and good deeds.

translation: Those who patiently persevere and upon their Lord they rely.
interpretation: This verse describes the believers who remain steadfast under hardship and persecution, restraining themselves from despair or retaliation for the sake of God. Their patience is not self-sufficient; it is joined with complete trust in their Lord, meaning they depend on Him alone for support, guidance, and the outcome of all affairs, acknowledging that no harm or benefit comes except by His will.

translation: And how many a moving creature there is that does not carry its provision! Allah provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah undertakes to provide for every living creature, even those that cannot store or carry their food, and He provides for human beings as well. Therefore, anxiety about sustenance should not drive a person to disobedience, despair, or disbelief. Allah hears every supplication and knows every need, so He is fully aware of what each creature requires and provides it in due measure. The verse calls for trust in Allah while recognizing that He is the ultimate Provider, whose hearing and knowledge encompass all things.

translation: And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Then how are they turned away?
interpretation: This verse confronts the idolaters with their own admission: they recognize Allah alone as the Creator of the heavens, the earth, the sun, and the moon, and as the One who controls and subjects them. Since they already confess His exclusive creatorship and sovereign power, their worship of other beings alongside Him is exposed as an irrational contradiction. Their turning away is therefore not due to lack of evidence, but to willful deviation from the truth that the One who alone creates and governs all things alone deserves to be worshipped.

translation: Allah expands provision for whom He wills among His servants and restricts it for him. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah alone controls provision. He may enlarge or tighten it for any of His servants according to His wisdom, not according to their merit or power. Because He is fully aware of all things, He knows what each servant needs, what will test or benefit him, and what will lead him to good in this life and the Hereafter. Therefore, no one should envy another’s wealth, despair in poverty, or become arrogant in plenty; rather, one should trust Allah, seek lawful means, and remain grateful and patient under His decree.

translation: And if you asked them, 'Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its death?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'All praise is due to Allah.' But most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse argues that even those who associate partners with Allah recognize His exclusive power over sending rain and reviving the dead earth. Their own admission that Allah alone does this proves that He alone deserves worship and that He is able to resurrect the dead. The command to say 'All praise is due to Allah' is a declaration of praise to Him for His clear signs and undeniable blessings, and it also exposes the inconsistency of the disbelievers: they affirm His creative and life-giving power yet refuse to submit to Him alone. 'But most of them do not reason' means they fail to use their intellect to draw the necessary conclusion from what they themselves acknowledge—that the One who gives life to barren earth after its death can raise the dead and must be worshipped without partners.

translation: And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play. And indeed the home of the Hereafter—that is indeed the true life, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the present worldly life, when taken as the ultimate end, is only a passing diversion and play: its pleasures, possessions, and pursuits are temporary and not the purpose for which the human being was created. The Hereafter, by contrast, is the true and enduring life, because it is everlasting and free from the deficiencies of this world. The verse therefore calls people to see beyond immediate gratification and to recognize that real success and lasting existence lie in the final abode; if they truly understood this, they would not let the fleeting amusements of this world distract them from preparing for the eternal life to come.

translation: And when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them safely to the land, behold, they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse exposes the contradiction of those who turn to Allah only in moments of overwhelming danger: at sea, when all created means fail, they sincerely invoke Him alone, recognizing that no one else can rescue them. Yet once He saves them and brings them safely to shore, they revert to associating partners with Him. The meaning is that true faith demands exclusive devotion to Allah in both hardship and ease; to call on Him sincerely during distress and then commit shirk after deliverance is blatant ingratitude and a denial of the very truth they acknowledged when helpless.

translation: So that they may deny what We have given them and enjoy themselves; but they will soon know.
interpretation: This is a severe warning to those who receive God's favors and rescue yet persist in ingratitude and idolatry. They are granted a brief respite to indulge in worldly pleasures and continue in denial, but this is not an approval of their conduct; it is a test and a delay before inevitable accountability. The phrase 'they will soon know' assures that the truth of their rejection and the consequences of their ingratitude will become clear, and they will face the punishment for it.

translation: Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched away from around them? So do they believe in falsehood and reject the favor of Allah?
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to the Quraysh of Mecca. Allah reminds them that the safety and security of the Sacred Precinct is a blessing and sign from Him, even though violence, kidnapping, and plunder were happening among the tribes all around them. Their security was not caused by their idols or their own power, but by Allah’s protection. Yet instead of responding with faith and gratitude, they continued to believe in falsehood—idols and man-made deities—and to reject Allah’s greatest favor, including His sending the Prophet Muhammad with guidance. The verse therefore calls them to recognize the true source of their safety, abandon false worship, and be grateful to Allah rather than denying His blessings.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling place for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse is a severe rhetorical rebuke: no one is more unjust than the person who either fabricates falsehood against God—attributing to Him what He never said or legislated—or rejects the truth after it has reached him with clear proof. Both attitudes stem from disbelief and arrogant resistance to God. The closing question affirms that Hell is indeed the prepared abode for such disbelievers, warning that denial and invented claims against God cannot escape final accountability.

translation: And those who strive for Us—We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse establishes that sincere striving in God’s cause is met with divine guidance: those who exert themselves for His sake—struggling against their own lower desires, against falsehood, and in performing righteous deeds—will be led by God into the paths that please Him and lead to salvation. The guidance mentioned is not merely initial faith but an increase in clarity, righteousness, and nearness to God. The closing statement, that Allah is with the doers of good, means His help, protection, and support accompany those who combine effort in His cause with ihsan—perfecting their worship, character, and treatment of others. Thus, the verse presents striving and excellence in goodness as the means by which a believer attains divine companionship and guidance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif Lam Meem.
interpretation: Alif Lam Meem are among the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta‘at) at the openings of certain surahs. Their precise meaning is known to Allah alone; they serve as a divine sign and a challenge, showing that the Qur’an is composed of the same Arabic letters the Arabs used, yet it remains inimitable, and they direct attention to the revealed Book that follows.

translation: The Romans have been defeated.
interpretation: This verse announces the defeat of the Byzantine Romans by the Persians and serves as a prophecy that the Romans would soon achieve victory, confirming the truth of the Qur'anic revelation.

translation: In the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will be victorious.
interpretation: This is a prophecy that the defeated party’s setback would not be permanent; after their loss they would soon prevail, showing that God’s decree can reverse apparent ruin and that His promise is certain.

translation: within a few years. To Allah belongs the command before and after, and on that day the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: This affirms that every event, before or after the promised outcome, is governed entirely by Allah’s decree; no power or circumstance can prevent or hasten His command. The believers’ joy on that day is joy at the vindication of Allah’s promise and the clear manifestation of His help, confirming that ultimate authority over all affairs belongs to Him alone.

translation: With the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: True help and victory come only from Allah; He grants them to whomever He chooses by His wisdom and mercy, and His might is never overcome.

translation: Allah has made a promise. Allah does not break His promise, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse establishes that God’s promise is absolutely reliable and will inevitably come to pass; any apparent delay or non-fulfillment is not a breach but a matter of timing and divine wisdom. The fault lies with most people’s lack of knowledge: they do not know God’s attributes, His truthful promise, or the reality behind His decrees, so they doubt or misinterpret. Thus the verse calls for certainty in God’s word and awareness that human ignorance, not divine failure, is the reason for confusion.

translation: They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world, and they are heedless of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse condemns those whose knowledge is confined to the external, material, and transient affairs of worldly life—its sciences, commerce, pleasures, and visible systems—while they remain unmindful of the ultimate reality: God, the purpose of existence, resurrection, accountability, and eternal life. Their worldly learning may be extensive, but it is superficial because it does not lead them to reflect on or prepare for the Hereafter; instead, they neglect it entirely.

translation: Do they not reflect within themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for an appointed term. And indeed, many of the people disbelieve in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse calls people to honest self-reflection: the very structure of human existence and the created order points beyond itself. The heavens, earth, and all that lies between them are not accidental or meaningless; they are created by Allah with truth, justice, wisdom, and a definite purpose, and they are bound to an appointed term. Because creation has a term and a purpose, human beings are accountable and will meet their Lord. Yet many people deny or ignore that meeting, living as though this life were final. The verse thus links thoughtful reflection on the self and the universe to faith in resurrection and accountability before Allah.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how the end of those before them was? They were stronger than them in power, and they cultivated the earth and developed it more than these have developed it. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. So Allah would never wrong them, but they used to wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the rise and fall of past nations are lessons written into history: material strength, land cultivation, and worldly development cannot protect a people who reject divine guidance. Their destruction was not an act of injustice from Allah; rather, they brought ruin upon themselves by denying the clear proofs brought by their messengers and persisting in wrongdoing.

translation: Then the outcome of those who did evil was the worst [consequence], because they denied the signs of Allah and were mocking them.
interpretation: This verse warns that persistent wrongdoing leads to the gravest end: rejecting Allah’s revelations and treating them with ridicule. Their final ruin is not arbitrary; it is the just result of their denial and mockery. It teaches that sin darkens the heart until one not only refuses the truth but belittles it, and that this rejection and mockery are the cause of the worst outcome in the Hereafter.

translation: Allah originates creation, then He repeats it, then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God alone possesses the power to create, recreate, and resurrect. Creation is not self-sustaining or independent of Him; He initiates it and restores it after death. Human beings will ultimately be brought back to Him, meaning resurrection is certain and every person will stand before Him for judgment. Thus, ultimate authority, dependence, and accountability belong solely to God.

translation: And on the Day when the Hour is established, the criminals will be in despair.
interpretation: This means that when the Resurrection comes to pass, those who persisted in sin and denial will lose all hope and be reduced to silent despair before God’s judgment. Their excuses will collapse, their false arguments will fail, and they will realize that no escape, intercession, or refuge remains for them.

translation: And there will not be for them any intercessors from among their partners, and they will be disbelievers in their partners.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the false deities and associates that the polytheists worshipped besides Allah will possess no power to intercede for them, and the polytheists themselves will disown and reject those partners. This exposes the utter falsehood of shirk: what they relied upon will abandon them, and intercession belongs only to Allah, by His permission, for whom He wills.

translation: And on the Day the Hour is established, that Day they will separate.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, when the appointed Hour begins, humanity will be divided according to their faith and deeds. The close bonds and mixed groups of worldly life will break apart, and people will be separated into those destined for mercy and those deserving punishment, each receiving the consequence of what they believed and did.

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a garden [of Paradise], rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse states that those who combine sincere faith with righteous conduct will be placed in a lush, delightful garden of Paradise, where they are granted continuous joy, happiness, and honor. The word “روضة” evokes a verdant, refreshing meadow, suggesting the beauty, comfort, and serenity of their eternal abode, while “يحبرون” conveys being made joyful, gratified, and ennobled. Thus, the reward is a state of perfect bliss and dignity, in contrast to the punishment that awaits those who reject faith and do evil.

translation: And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought into the punishment.
interpretation: This states that rejecting faith, rejecting God’s revelations, and denying the encounter with the Hereafter leads to being forcibly brought into torment. The word “محضرون” conveys that they will be made present there under compulsion—not merely threatened but seized and confined in punishment, with no escape or absence from it.

translation: So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to declare Allah’s absolute perfection and transcendence above every defect at the two ends of the day—evening and morning—because the coming of night and day, with all their order and precision, are among His signs. It teaches that the One who controls the alternation of darkness and light is alone worthy of praise and remembrance at every phase of life.

translation: And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, and at evening and when you are at midday.
interpretation: This verse affirms that every form of praise and thanksgiving belongs exclusively to Allah, and that all creation in the heavens and the earth acknowledges His worthiness of praise. The mention of evening and midday teaches that His remembrance and praise are not limited to one time but should encompass the whole day, and that the regular turning of day and night is itself a sign calling people to recognize His lordship and worship Him alone.

translation: He brings the living out of the dead, and brings the dead out of the living, and gives life to the earth after its death. And thus will you be brought forth.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah's absolute power over life, death, and resurrection. It points to the visible signs in creation—life emerging from what is lifeless and dead land being revived by rain—as direct evidence that He can and will raise human beings from their graves. The final phrase, “And thus will you be brought forth,” ties the certainty of the Hereafter to what people already witness in the natural world: the One who transforms death into life and barrenness into fertility is fully able to restore the dead to life for judgment.

translation: And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings spreading out.
interpretation: This verse directs attention to God’s power and wisdom as displayed in human existence itself: He originated humankind from dust, a lowly and lifeless substance, then brought them into a state of living, rational, active humanity, multiplying and spreading across the earth. The contrast between the origin and the outcome is a sign of His creative ability, making the resurrection and the final accounting entirely possible. It also teaches that human beings, despite their achievements and widespread activity, remain dependent on God and ought not forget the humble material origin from which He formed them.

translation: And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse presents marriage as a divine sign and a manifestation of God's wisdom and mercy. The creation of spouses from among yourselves points to a shared human nature, mutual compatibility, and the possibility of deep companionship rather than estrangement. The purpose that you may find tranquility in them means marriage is meant to be a refuge of emotional, spiritual, and psychological peace, where each spouse comforts and steadies the other. The affection, mawaddah, is a loving attachment and inclination that binds hearts, while mercy, rahmah, is compassionate care, forgiveness, patience, and protection from harm. Together they form the moral and emotional foundation of the marital bond. The closing phrase calls those who reflect to recognize in this ordinary yet profound relationship the traces of God's power, providential design, and benevolence, and to respond with gratitude and faithfulness.

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to three grand signs: the cosmos, human speech and language, and human color. The heavens and earth with their order, vastness, and interdependence testify to a Creator whose power and wisdom sustain all. The multiplicity of languages and colors arises within a single human species, showing that diversity is by divine design, not accident, and not a basis for arrogance. These signs are not merely curiosities; they are evidence of God's creative authority and providence for those who use knowledge to reflect, infer the Maker from the made, and recognize that the same God who originated the heavens and earth also originated human difference. Because the verse closes with 'for the knowledgeable,' it teaches that such signs benefit those who possess sound knowledge and insight—knowledge that leads from creation to the Creator, from diversity to the unity of His lordship, and from observation to worship and gratitude.

translation: And among His signs is your sleep by night and day, and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who hear.
interpretation: The ordinary rhythm of human life—rest in sleep and exertion in seeking provision—is presented as evidence of God's wisdom and mercy. Sleep restores the body and interrupts worldly striving, while seeking His bounty through work and effort supplies human needs and reminds people of their dependence on Him. Both are divine signs because they rely on God's design and favor, not merely human power. Those who truly 'hear' are the ones who receive the message attentively, allowing it to awaken reflection, gratitude, and obedience.

translation: And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, causing fear and hope, and He sends down from the sky water, and revives thereby the earth after its death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse points to God’s power and mercy as seen in creation: lightning can strike fear of harm and yet awaken hope for rain and relief, while the rain He sends revives dead, barren land into life. These visible transformations are evidence of His ability to bring life after death, provide for His creatures, and govern all things. They are meaningful signs for those who use their reason to reflect, recognize the Creator, and understand that the One who revives the earth can also resurrect human beings and hold them accountable.

translation: And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then when He calls you with a call from the earth, behold, you will emerge.
interpretation: This verse presents the orderly persistence of the heavens and the earth as evidence of God's absolute power and oneness: they remain stable and function only by His command. It then moves to the resurrection: the One who effortlessly sustains the vast creation can, by a single summons, command the dead to rise from the earth, and they will immediately come forth. Thus the verse connects God's ongoing cosmic governance with His ability to bring about the final resurrection, showing that both are equally subject to His will.

translation: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse affirms that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone and is under His absolute authority. The word “qanitun” means being submissive, humble, and obedient. All created beings are subject to His will and decree: the believers obey Him willingly in worship, while the rest of creation submits to His power and control, whether willingly or by necessity. Nothing exists independently of Him, and no one can escape His dominion or resist His command.

translation: And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and it is easier for Him. And to Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms God's exclusive power over both the origination of creation and its restoration after death. The phrase “it is easier for Him” does not imply any change in God's ability or effort, since nothing is difficult for Him; rather, it addresses human understanding by showing that the second creation is no harder than the first. The “highest description” means that God alone possesses absolute perfection, majesty, and transcendence, and every noble attribute belongs to Him without any deficiency or likeness. He is therefore the Almighty who cannot be resisted, and the Wise whose creation, resurrection, and commands are all ordered with perfect wisdom.

translation: He has struck for you a parable from your own selves: Do you have, among those whom your right hands possess, any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal in it, fearing them as you fear one another? Thus We make clear the signs for people who reason.
interpretation: This verse presents a parable drawn from human social reality to expose the irrationality of associating partners with Allah. If a person would not accept that his own servants or slaves should share equally with him in his wealth, property, and authority, and would not fear them as he fears his own equals, then how can he set up created beings as partners with Allah in His dominion, ownership, and right to be worshipped? The argument is that shirk is inconsistent: people reject partnership and equality in their own limited possessions, yet they attribute partners to Allah in His absolute lordship over all that He provides and owns. The verse therefore calls people to use reason and recognize that Allah alone deserves exclusive worship, obedience, and gratitude, without any partner from His creation.

translation: Rather, those who do wrong follow their own desires without knowledge. So who can guide one whom Allah has sent astray? And they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse declares that the unjust turn away from revealed guidance not because of sound evidence, but because they submit to their own whims and desires without knowledge. Their misguidance is thus tied to their own wrongdoing and rebellious choice. Once Allah, in His justice, leaves such people astray, no created being can guide them, and no helper or protector can rescue them from that consequence. It affirms human accountability for following desire over truth and Allah's exclusive authority over guidance and misguidance.

translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth—the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no changing the creation of Allah. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse commands complete sincerity and steadfastness in worshipping Allah alone, turning away from every false object of worship. The religion He accepts is not an imposed external burden but the original natural constitution—the fitrah—with which He created every human being: an innate awareness of the Creator and a disposition to worship Him alone. “No changing the creation of Allah” means that Allah’s original creation and His intended pattern for humanity are perfect and unalterable; people may corrupt their fitrah through false beliefs, misguidance, and sin, but the truth remains that pure monotheism is the upright, established religion. Most people fail to know this, so they stray from their own natural disposition and from the straight path.

translation: Turning to Him in repentance, and fear Him, and establish prayer, and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse calls for a life wholly oriented toward God: constantly returning to Him in sincere repentance and obedience, guarding oneself against His displeasure through taqwa, and making prayer the concrete expression of that devotion. It also forbids adopting the path of those who associate partners with God, because true worship must be pure and undivided, directed to God alone.

translation: Of those who split up their religion and became sects, each faction rejoicing in what it has.
interpretation: This describes a blameworthy condition: people who break the unity of God’s religion into separate, rival denominations, each group taking its own path as if it were the truth and feeling content with its own beliefs, practices, and leaders. The verse condemns sectarian division and partisan self-satisfaction, warning believers not to be like those who turn religion into competing identities. It does not forbid honest scholarly disagreement; it condemns making religion into factions and being pleased with division and with one’s own inherited or chosen position simply because it belongs to one’s group.

translation: And when adversity touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him, behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse exposes a deep contradiction in human response to God: when suffering and need press upon people, they instinctively turn to Him alone, acknowledging their dependence and His power. But once relief and mercy come, some forget that turning and betray it by associating others with God—whether by attributing the blessing to created means, intercessors, or false powers, or by living as though they owe no exclusive loyalty and gratitude to Him. The censure is not of asking God in distress but of failing to remain faithful to Him in ease. True faith is tested both by hardship and by blessing: hardship should keep one humble before God, and mercy should deepen tawhid and gratitude, not lead back to shirk.

translation: So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.
interpretation: This is a severe Quranic warning against ingratitude and denial. The phrase “so that they may disbelieve” points to the outcome of their own corrupt choice: instead of responding to God’s favors with faith and gratitude, they use His blessings as a reason to persist in rejection. The command “enjoy yourselves” is not a true permission but an ironic, threatening concession: they may take temporary pleasure in worldly life, but this enjoyment is fleeting and delusive. “For you will soon know” is an emphatic promise of inevitable accountability—soon they will come to know the truth of what they denied and the consequence of trading lasting reward for passing gratification.

translation: Or have We sent down upon them an authority, so that it speaks of what they used to associate with Him?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke to those who associate partners with Allah: Do they possess any proof, scripture, or divine warrant that was sent down to them and that explicitly endorses their shirk? Since no such authority exists, their polytheism is shown to be utterly baseless. The verse means that they have no evidence from Allah for their claims; they only follow false assumptions, and nothing they attribute to Him as partners has any divine sanction.

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy, they rejoice in it; but if evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, behold, they despair.
interpretation: This verse exposes a shallow and inconsistent human attitude: when blessings and ease come, people often become elated and heedless, as though mercy were owed to them or produced by their own efforts, instead of receiving it with gratitude to Allah. Yet when hardship strikes because of their own misdeeds, they quickly lose hope and sink into despair, rather than turning back to Allah with repentance, patience, and trust. The verse thus rebukes ingratitude in prosperity and hopelessness in adversity, teaching that both ease and difficulty should lead a person to Allah.

translation: Do they not see that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse calls believers to recognize that the giving and withholding of provision are entirely governed by Allah’s wisdom, will, and sovereign decree, not by human worth alone or worldly causes. The variation in wealth and sustenance is a trial and a sign: it invites gratitude in abundance, patience in scarcity, and reliance upon Allah, so that the heart does not become attached to provisions themselves but to the Provider.

translation: So give to the relative his right, and to the needy and the wayfarer. That is better for those who desire the Face of Allah, and it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to fulfill the due rights of close relatives, the poor, and the stranded traveler. Such giving is not optional generosity but a divinely ordained obligation. It is better for those who give sincerely seeking Allah's pleasure alone, not worldly praise or return. Those who do so are the truly successful, attaining spiritual fulfillment and eternal reward.

translation: And whatever you give as usury so that it may increase within people's wealth — it will not increase with Allah. But whatever you give as zakah, seeking the Face of Allah — then those are the ones who will have multiplied.
interpretation: The verse sets a divine standard for true increase: wealth that is given or used in riba to grow through other people’s property may appear to increase materially, but it carries no growth, blessing, or reward with Allah. In contrast, what is given as zakah or charitable spending with sincere intention seeking Allah’s Face is what truly multiplies in His sight. Such people are the ones who attain the real manifold increase — not merely in worldly wealth, but in divine acceptance and reward.

translation: Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will give you life. Is there any among your 'partners' who does any of that? Exalted is He and far above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah's exclusive lordship over the entire span of human existence: He originates creation, sustains it with provision, decrees death, and alone will bring about resurrection. The rhetorical question challenges the idolaters to find any of their alleged partners who can do even one of these things, thereby exposing the utter helplessness and falsehood of every object of worship besides Him. Since no created being shares in these divine acts, Allah is glorified and far exalted above any association, partners, or rivals attributed to Him.

translation: Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, so that He may let them taste some of what they have done, so that perhaps they may return.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the widespread corruption, disorder, and harm seen in the world—whether in the physical environment, society, economy, or moral and spiritual life—is fundamentally linked to human choices and sins. God lets people experience some of the consequences of their deeds in this worldly life, not to destroy them immediately, but as a warning and mercy, so that they may recognize their wrongdoing, repent, and return to Him in obedience and reform.

translation: Say, "Travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those before you. Most of them were polytheists."
interpretation: This verse commands people to journey through the earth and consider the fate of earlier communities. The ruins and remnants of past nations are meant to teach a clear lesson: the root cause of their destruction was shirk—associating others with Allah. Though they may have possessed strength, wealth, and civilization, most of them persisted in idolatry and rejection of the messengers, so their end became a warning. The verse urges the living to take heed, repent, and devote worship to Allah alone before a similar consequence overtakes them.

translation: So set your face steadfastly toward the upright religion before there comes a Day which none can avert from Allah. On that Day they will be divided.
