interpretation: Allah commands complete sincerity and firm adherence to the straight religion—the enduring worship of Him alone—before the inevitable Day of Resurrection, whose decree none can repel or delay. That Day will expose every person’s chosen path: humanity will be separated into distinct groups according to faith and deeds, and no power will be able to turn back Allah’s command or alter His judgment.

translation: Whoever disbelieves, then his disbelief is against him; and whoever does righteous deeds, then for themselves they are preparing a place.
interpretation: This verse affirms that every person bears the consequence of their own choice: rejection of faith burdens the rejecter alone and does not harm God, while righteous action is an investment the doer makes for their own eternal good, preparing for themselves a dwelling of comfort and reward in the Hereafter.

translation: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the reward for faith and righteous action is a favor from God, not a debt He owes anyone; He bestows it by His grace. And God’s not loving the disbelievers is a declaration of His displeasure with disbelief and rejection of Him, not an injustice, since He remains just and generous.

translation: And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good tidings, and to let you taste of His mercy, and so that the ships may sail by His command, and so that you may seek of His bounty, and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse directs attention to God's power and mercy as seen in the order of nature and human livelihood. The winds are sent as heralds of rain and relief, showing that creation serves a purposeful divine plan and prepares people to receive His mercy. By causing them to taste His mercy, God allows His compassion to be experienced directly through rain, provision, and sustenance. The sailing of ships by His command signifies that the seas and all means of travel and trade are subject to His will, enabling people to seek lawful provision from His bounty. The final aim is gratitude: recognizing that every benefit, ability, and opportunity to pursue sustenance comes from God, so the proper response is thankfulness and reliance upon Him.

translation: And We certainly sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We took retribution from those who committed crimes, and it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s dealings with humanity follow a consistent pattern: He sends messengers with clear signs and evidence, and those who reject them and persist in wrongdoing bring upon themselves just punishment. At the same time, Allah binds Himself by His own promise to grant victory and support to the believers. It consoles the Prophet and the faithful that opposition and denial are not new, and that divine justice ultimately distinguishes between the criminals and the people of faith, ensuring that the believers are not abandoned.

translation: Allah is the One who sends the winds, so they stir up clouds, then He spreads them in the sky however He wills, and makes them into fragments, so you see the rain emerging from within them. Then when He causes it to fall upon whom He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse directs attention to Allah's sole authority over the winds, clouds, and rain, showing that the entire cycle of rain is under His command and measure. The winds are agents that gather and lift moisture, the clouds are spread and shaped as He wills, and the rain emerges from within them by His decree. When that rain reaches the servants He chooses, it brings relief and glad tidings, so their hearts open in joy. The deeper meaning is that Allah is not distant from His creation: He arranges subtle natural causes and then grants His provision to whom He wills, reminding people that mercy, sustenance, and life itself descend only by His will, and that human rejoicing should be joined to gratitude and reliance upon Him.

translation: And indeed they had been, before it was sent down upon them, before that, in despair.
interpretation: This verse describes people who had lost all hope before Allah sent down rain. Their despair shows human helplessness when mercy is withheld, and the coming of rain is a sign of Allah’s power to relieve distress and revive dead land—just as He can raise the dead.

translation: So look at the traces of Allah's mercy: how He revives the earth after its death. Indeed, that [Allah] is surely the reviver of the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse uses the revival of barren, lifeless earth by rain as a visible sign of Allah's mercy and power. If He can bring dead ground back to life, then He can certainly raise the dead on the Day of Resurrection. It affirms that Allah's power is not limited by any natural obstacle, so belief in resurrection rests on the same divine attribute that sustains all life and renewal.

translation: And if We send a wind and they see it turning yellow, they would after that persist in disbelief.
interpretation: This verse exposes the instability of those whose faith is tied only to favorable conditions. When Allah’s mercy revives the earth, they may acknowledge it, but if a damaging wind turns the vegetation yellow and strips away prosperity, they quickly fall back into ingratitude and denial. It is a rebuke of a heart that treats blessings as entitlement and hardship as an excuse to reject God, showing that true faith must remain firm in both ease and trial.

translation: So indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating.
interpretation: This is a consolation to the Messenger: those who persist in denial are like the dead in heart and deaf to guidance, so they do not respond to the invitation of faith, especially when they turn away from it in aversion. The verse teaches that guidance is not achieved by the human messenger’s power to compel; hearts are awakened only by God, and the messenger’s duty is to convey the message clearly.

translation: And you cannot guide the blind away from their misguidance. You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, so they are Muslims.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the Prophet’s role is to convey the message, not to force guidance into hearts that have chosen spiritual blindness and persisted in error. Only those who are willing to accept God’s signs truly hear and respond, and their response is submission to God. Guidance ultimately belongs to God, and sincere faith is shown by turning to Him in humble obedience.

translation: Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse presents the stages of human existence as direct evidence of God’s creative sovereignty and man’s complete dependence upon Him. Human life begins in a state of utter frailty and need, then passes into a season of strength, ability, and vigor, and finally returns to weakness and the visible signs of old age. None of these transitions occurs by human power or choice; they are appointed and brought about by the One whose will is effective and whose knowledge encompasses every stage before it appears. The mention of weakness followed by strength and then weakness again teaches that strength is not a permanent possession but a trust and a test, and that aging is not a defeat of divine purpose but part of His wise ordering of creation. Because God is All-Knowing, He knows what each soul needs and when; because He is All-Powerful, He is able to create, change, weaken, strengthen, and restore. The verse thus calls the human being to humility, gratitude in times of strength, patience in times of decline, and firm hope in the power of the One who can bring forth life from weakness and restore after every loss.

translation: And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they did not remain except an hour. Thus were they deluded.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, those who committed disbelief and sin will swear that their stay in the world or in the grave was only a brief hour, because worldly time will seem utterly negligible compared with the eternal Hereafter, and their perception will be overwhelmed. Their oath is not truthful in the sense of accepted knowledge; it expresses the same self-deception and turning away from truth that they practiced in worldly life. Just as they were deluded before by denying resurrection and judgment, they are deluded then. The verse emphasizes the fleeting nature of worldly existence and the utter inability of the criminals' false oaths and denials to change the reality of accountability before God.

translation: And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: “You have remained, according to the Book of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection. So this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know.”
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment when the resurrection denied by the disbelievers becomes manifest. Those granted both knowledge and faith testify that the deniers’ stay—whether in worldly life or in the grave—was exactly as Allah had decreed and recorded, extending to the appointed Day. Their words are a rebuke: the reality they dismissed is now before them. True knowledge is inseparable from faith; it recognizes Allah’s promise as certain and lives in accountability, whereas the deniers had enough to know but refused to accept it. Thus the verse affirms that Allah’s decree is precise, resurrection is inevitable, and the excuse of ignorance on that Day is exposed as self-deception.

translation: So on that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who wronged, nor will they be asked to make amends.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who committed wrongdoing cannot escape punishment by offering excuses or apologies, and they will not be given a further opportunity to return, repent, or seek Allah's pleasure. The time for accepted repentance and correction belongs to worldly life, so when that Day comes, the wrongdoers' pleas and justifications are useless.

translation: And indeed We have set forth for mankind in this Qur’an every kind of example. But if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, “You are only falsifiers.”
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah has not left humanity without ample guidance: the Qur’an contains every necessary kind of parable, proof, warning, and exhortation suited to human understanding. The problem is therefore not a lack of evidence, but the disposition of those who persist in disbelief. Even if a clear miraculous sign were brought to them, their rejection would not be due to genuine uncertainty; they would instead dismiss the messenger as one who deals in falsehood. Their accusation reveals a rebellious heart that refuses the truth after it has become plain, choosing denial over submission.

translation: Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah places a seal over the hearts of those who persist in ignorance of His signs and guidance, so that truth cannot enter them and they remain unable to perceive or accept faith. Their lack of knowledge is not a simple absence of information but a willful turning away from divine revelation; therefore, Allah seals their hearts as a just consequence of their own rejection and heedlessness.

translation: So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And let not those who have no certainty make you impatient.
interpretation: The verse establishes that steadfastness rests on certainty in God’s unfailing promise. Those who lack firm conviction—whether through disbelief, doubt, or worldly pressure—will try to unsettle the believer, provoke haste, or make faithfulness appear futile. The believer is therefore warned not to let their instability, mockery, or anxiety enter the heart and disturb patience; true resolve is guarded by unwavering trust that God’s promise will certainly come to pass.

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These are among the disjointed letters (al-muqatta'at) that open certain surahs. Their precise meaning is known to Allah alone; they emphasize that the Qur'an is composed of the same letters used by human beings, yet it remains inimitable, and they invite reflection on the revelation that follows.

translation: These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: The verse declares that the revelation being recited consists of the signs of a Book characterized by perfect wisdom: its teachings, laws, and reports are true and sound, free from error, inconsistency, and frivolity. Describing it as 'Wise' means both that it is wise in its composition and guidance and that it is the source of wisdom, containing decisive verses that lead to right understanding and righteous action.

translation: A guidance and mercy for the doers of good.
interpretation: It means the Qur’an is a source of right guidance and divine mercy for the muhsinun—those who perfect their worship of God and their dealings with others—because they accept its guidance, act upon it, and thus attain God’s mercy in this world and the Hereafter.

translation: Those who establish prayer and give zakah, and of the Hereafter they are certain.
interpretation: This verse identifies the defining marks of the believers who accept the Qur'an's guidance: they uphold the prescribed prayer as a constant, conscious act of worship; they give the obligatory charity as a concrete expression of faith and social responsibility; and they hold an unwavering conviction in the life to come. That certainty in the Hereafter is the inner root of their outward obedience, because they act in hope of God's reward and accountability before Him.

translation: Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true guidance is not self-generated but is a bestowal from the Lord, and that ultimate success consists in being firmly settled upon that guidance. Divine guidance and felicity are inseparable: whoever is placed by God upon His clear path is among those who attain deliverance and enduring prosperity.

translation: And among the people is he who buys idle talk to mislead others from the way of Allah without knowledge, and takes it in mockery. For such there is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns the deliberate use of frivolous, misleading, or distracting speech and entertainment as a means of turning people away from God’s path. The offense is worsened because it is done without true knowledge and because God’s guidance is treated with contempt. It teaches that whoever employs influence, wealth, or media to obstruct divine guidance and mock sacred truth will face a punishment that degrades and shames them.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away in arrogance as if he had not heard them, as if there were deafness in his ears. So give him good tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse depicts a person who rejects God’s revelations out of pride and self-importance. He does not turn away because the message is unclear or unproven, but because he refuses to submit. His posture is likened to someone who is physically deaf, though the deafness is spiritual and willful: he acts as if the words never reached him. The command to “give him good tidings” is bitterly ironic; instead of news of mercy and reward, he is warned of a painful punishment. Thus, the verse teaches that arrogance and deliberate indifference to divine guidance render a person accountable and deserving of severe consequence, while the signs of God only benefit those who listen with humility and openness.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds — for them are gardens of bliss.
interpretation: This verse establishes that eternal bliss is granted to those who combine authentic faith in Allah with righteous deeds. Faith is the root, and righteous action is its necessary fruit; the promise of 'gardens of bliss' signifies perpetual joy, pleasure, and nearness to Allah, free from sorrow and hardship. It also shows that Allah's promise is certain and that this reward belongs specifically to those who persist in belief and good works.

translation: Abiding therein forever—the promise of Allah, in truth; and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the eternal dwelling promised to the believers is not merely a hope but a certain reality guaranteed by Allah’s truthful promise. Because He is Al-‘Aziz, He has full power to bring it about and none can prevent Him; and because He is Al-Hakim, His promise, timing, and reward are perfectly wise and just. Thus the believer’s security in the Hereafter rests on Allah’s unfailing truthfulness, unrestricted power, and perfect wisdom.

translation: He created the heavens without any pillars that you can see, and He cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with you, and He dispersed therein from every creature. And We sent down water from the sky and caused to grow therein of every noble kind.
interpretation: This verse directs the mind to Allah’s sole lordship and creative power: the vast heavens are held in perfect order without any visible support, showing that His command, not material means, sustains creation; the mountains are placed as stabilizing anchors so the earth remains habitable and does not sway beneath human feet; life in its diverse forms is spread by His will; and rain is sent as a mercy that brings forth every beneficial and generous kind of vegetation. Thus the verse binds together cosmic order, earthly stability, the diversity of creatures, and the provision of sustenance as signs calling people to recognize the Creator’s oneness, gratitude, and the certainty that the One who originated and sustains all this is able to bring the dead back to life.

translation: This is the creation of Allah. So show me what those besides Him have created. Indeed, the wrongdoers are in clear error.
interpretation: The verse establishes that all creation originates solely from Allah, and it challenges the idolaters to prove that any being they worship besides Him has created anything at all. Since no false deity or created thing can originate, shape, or sustain creation, the worship of anything other than Allah is exposed as manifest misguidance. The “wrongdoers” are those who commit the injustice of associating partners with Allah, attributing to creatures what belongs exclusively to the Creator. Their error is not hidden or ambiguous; it is clear because the whole of existence testifies to Allah’s unique creative power, while the claimed partners possess no creative act whatsoever.

translation: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom, [saying], 'Be grateful to Allah.' And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: God granted Luqman true wisdom, the foundation of which is recognizing God's favors and responding with sincere gratitude. Gratitude purifies and benefits the one who gives it, while ingratitude harms only the ingrate, for God is entirely self-sufficient and worthy of praise regardless of His creation's response.

translation: And recall when Luqman said to his son, admonishing him: “O my son, do not associate partners with Allah; indeed, associating partners with Him is a tremendous wrong.”
interpretation: This verse establishes pure monotheism as the foundation of all true wisdom and moral instruction. Luqman begins his advice with the prohibition of shirk because it is the gravest corruption of a person’s relationship with Allah: it gives to created beings what belongs exclusively to the Creator. Calling it a “great wrong” means it is an injustice against Allah by denying His sole divinity, against oneself by degrading one’s purpose and dignity, and against truth by placing ultimate trust in what cannot ultimately benefit or harm. Thus, before advising his son on any other matter, Luqman directs him first to correct his belief in Allah alone.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse binds gratitude to God with gratitude and dutiful kindness to parents, presenting filial piety as a religious obligation and a debt owed most especially to the mother, whose pregnancy, childbirth, and nursing involve layer upon layer of weakness and self-sacrifice. The mention of weaning after two years underscores the child’s long dependence and the mother’s sustained hardship. Yet the closing words “to Me is the final destination” establish that parental rights, however great, remain subordinate to God’s rights: ultimate thankfulness, obedience, and accountability belong to God alone, so honoring one’s parents must never become a rival to loyalty to the Creator.

translation: And if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them; but accompany them in this world with kindness, and follow the way of those who turn to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that obedience to parents, though a grave duty, is never absolute: it is nullified when they command or pressure one toward shirk, because God alone has the right to be worshipped, and shirk has no basis in knowledge. Even then, the believer must not sever relations or act unjustly; he must maintain kind, honorable companionship with them in worldly matters. The path to be followed is that of those who sincerely turn back to God in repentance and exclusive devotion, not the path of family pressure toward falsehood. Ultimately, all return to God, and He will judge with perfect knowledge every deed, making His pleasure and final accountability the true measure of loyalty.

translation: O my son, indeed if it should be the weight of a mustard seed and it were within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Aware.
interpretation: This verse teaches that no deed, whether outwardly great or as tiny and hidden as a mustard seed, is beyond Allah’s knowledge or beyond His power to bring to account. Even if it were buried inside a rock or placed anywhere in the heavens or the earth, Allah would bring it forth and recompense it. The mention of Allah being Subtle and Aware means His knowledge penetrates the most concealed realities and His wisdom reaches every hidden matter, so a person should act with sincerity, God-consciousness, and certainty that nothing done for good or evil is ever lost.

translation: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is among the matters of firm resolve.
interpretation: This is Luqman’s counsel to his son: worship Allah by establishing prayer consistently, fulfill the duty of calling others to good and warning against evil, and remain steadfast when hardship comes because of upholding these obligations. Such patience and commitment are among the matters that require strong resolve and sincere determination in faith.

translation: And do not turn your cheek away from people in contempt, nor walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not love every arrogant boaster.
interpretation: The verse forbids two outward signs of inward arrogance: turning the cheek away from people in disdain, which means refusing to acknowledge them, looking down on them, or treating them as beneath one's notice; and walking with a swaggering, exultant gait that displays superiority and self-importance. It teaches that faith requires humility, respectful dealing with others, and modesty in one's bearing. The closing statement explains the root evil: God does not love the conceited boaster, because such a person usurps the honor that belongs to God, overlooks that all gifts come from Him, and is prone to injustice and contempt toward others. Thus the verse calls the believer to replace pride with gratitude, self-assertion with gentleness, and contempt with dignified humility.

translation: And be moderate in your walking and lower your voice. Indeed, the harshest of sounds is the braying of donkeys.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to adopt humility and self-restraint in both movement and speech. Walking with moderation means avoiding arrogance, strutting, or exaggerated display, while lowering one’s voice means avoiding loud, harsh, and unnecessary shouting. The comparison to the braying of donkeys is a strong rebuke of ugly, raucous noise: it teaches that uncontrolled loudness is repugnant and undignified, whereas gentle, measured conduct and speech reflect good character and God-consciousness.

translation: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and has amply bestowed upon you His favors, both outward and inward? But among the people are those who dispute about Allah without knowledge, without guidance, and without an illuminating Scripture.
interpretation: This verse calls attention to God's absolute authority and generosity: the heavens and earth are made serviceable to humanity by His command, and His blessings reach people in ways they perceive and in ways hidden from them. It then exposes the folly of arguing about God—His existence, unity, commands, or promises—without sound knowledge, without divine guidance, and without a revealed book that enlightens. Such dispute is not sincere inquiry but baseless contention, because true speech about God must rest on the light of revelation and the guidance He has sent.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has sent down,' they say, 'Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers upon.' Even if Satan invites them to the punishment of the Blaze?
interpretation: This verse condemns blind adherence to ancestral tradition when it is set up against God's revelation. It exposes the fallacy of treating the ways of forefathers as automatically authoritative, since inherited custom can be nothing but Satan's summons to the punishment of Hell. The rhetorical question shows that such people do not truly follow guidance; they follow a path that, if left unexamined, leads to ruin. The criterion is what God has sent down, not what a society inherited.

translation: And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good has certainly grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters.
interpretation: This verse means that whoever turns himself wholly and sincerely to Allah in worship, obedience, and reliance, while also perfecting his deeds and acting with goodness and excellence, has taken hold of the strongest, firmest support that will never break: true faith in Allah and submission to Him. Such a person is secure in his religion and guided to the straight path. The verse also reminds that every matter, in this life and the Hereafter, ultimately returns to Allah alone, who will judge all people with perfect justice and recompense them according to their faith and deeds.

translation: And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and the believers not to let the rejection and disbelief of others cause them sorrow or despair. It reminds them that all people ultimately return to Allah, who will fully inform them of their deeds and hold them accountable with perfect justice. Since Allah knows even the hidden thoughts and intentions of the hearts, He alone is the true judge of disbelief and faith, and the believers should leave the matter to Him rather than grieve over what is beyond their control.

translation: We let them enjoy for a little while, then We will drive them to a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that the worldly enjoyment given to those who persist in denial is only brief and is a temporary respite, not a sign of divine approval. When that short-lived pleasure ends, they will be inevitably driven to a harsh, heavy, and unrelenting punishment. The verse contrasts fleeting worldly gratification with the severity and certainty of the final consequence, showing that no amount of temporary enjoyment can shield them from the punishment their deeds have earned.

translation: And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'All praise is due to Allah.' But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse points out that even those who associate partners with Allah recognize that He alone created the heavens and the earth. Their own admission testifies that Allah is the sole Creator, so praise and worship belong to Him alone. Yet most of them do not know the full implication of this truth—that the One who created everything must be worshiped exclusively, without any partners.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all creation in the heavens and the earth belongs exclusively to Allah and is under His absolute dominion. He has no need of anything, while everything depends upon Him; thus He is al-Ghani, absolutely self-sufficient and free of all needs. Because His essence, attributes, and actions are perfect, He is al-Hamid, inherently worthy of all praise, gratitude, and worship.

translation: And if all the trees on earth were pens and the sea were ink, with seven more seas added after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah’s words—His knowledge, commands, promises, and signs—are limitless and cannot be encompassed or exhausted by any finite creation. Even if every tree became a pen and every sea became ink, multiplied many times over, creation would still fall short of recording or fully expressing the infinite words of Allah. It also affirms that Allah is All-Mighty and All-Wise: His power is absolute and His wisdom is perfect in all that He reveals, decrees, and does.

translation: Your creation and your resurrection are not but as a single soul. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s power is not limited by number or multiplicity: creating all people and raising them all on the Day of Judgment is as easy for Him as creating and raising one single soul. His will is absolute, and nothing is difficult for Him. The closing names, Hearing and Seeing, mean that He perceives every hidden and open word and deed, so His resurrection and judgment of all humanity will be perfectly just and complete.

translation: Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for an appointed term, and that Allah is Aware of what you do?
interpretation: This verse calls the human being to contemplate God’s continuous and precise governance of the cosmos. The intertwining of night and day is not random but a sign of divine will, whereby time, seasons, light, and darkness are measured and manipulated according to a wisdom that sustains life and order. The sun and moon are likewise subjected to God’s command, moving along their fixed courses toward an appointed end known only to Him. This refutes any notion that these heavenly bodies possess independent divine power; they are servants of God, bound by His decree. The mention of their appointed term also reminds the reader that all created things are finite and moving toward a determined conclusion, ultimately pointing to the Day of Judgment and the end of this worldly order. Finally, the verse seals these cosmic realities with the statement that God is fully aware of all human deeds. Since the same God who governs the vast universe with perfect knowledge also observes every action, word, and intention of people, this awareness should awaken accountability, humble gratitude, and steadfast obedience to Him.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and that Allah is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every divine act, judgment, and promise is grounded in the fact that Allah alone is al-Haqq—the absolute, unchanging Truth and Reality whose existence, lordship, and promises are certain. Every object of worship or reliance besides Him is batil: inherently void, unstable, and powerless to create, benefit, harm, or fulfill promises. Because He is al-‘Ali al-Kabir, He is infinitely exalted above all false comparisons and deficiencies, and His greatness encompasses all things; therefore He alone deserves worship, reliance, and ultimate hope.

translation: Do you not see that the ships sail through the sea by the favor of Allah, so that He may show you some of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful person.
interpretation: The verse points to God's sustaining power and mercy in making the sea carry ships, enabling travel, trade, and livelihood. Such signs are truly perceived by those who combine patience in hardship with gratitude for blessings: patience keeps them from despair and disobedience when tested, while gratitude makes them recognize God's favors and use them rightly. The sea's ordered service and human ability to navigate it are therefore not meaningless natural events but evidences of divine care, calling people to reflect, remain steadfast, and respond in worship and thankfulness.

translation: And when waves cover them like canopies, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, some of them are moderate. And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous, ungrateful one.
interpretation: This verse describes how people in extreme danger instinctively turn to Allah alone, acknowledging His exclusive power to save, because the overwhelming waves make all false supports seem useless. Yet once the danger passes and they are brought safely to dry land, not all remain firm or fully grateful; some adopt a middling, lukewarm stance, neither wholly devoted nor openly denying. The verse then declares that rejecting Allah’s signs is not the way of a sincere believer but of a person who betrays trust and is deeply ungrateful. Its lesson is that true faith must continue beyond moments of crisis, and that denying God’s favors and signs is rooted in treachery and ingratitude rather than honest reasoning.

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his child, nor will a child avail his father in anything. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.
interpretation: This verse summons all people to God-consciousness and to take seriously the coming Day when every worldly bond and claim of kinship will be powerless to help. Even the closest human relationships—parent and child—will not enable one person to substitute for another or shield another from accountability. Allah’s promise of resurrection and judgment is absolutely true, so the passing attractions, status, and distractions of worldly life must not deceive people into neglecting their ultimate purpose. Likewise, the great deceiver—Satan, or any deceptive force—must not mislead them about Allah, whether by false security, delayed repentance, despair of His mercy, or the illusion that divine judgment will never come. The verse therefore calls for faithful vigilance, moral responsibility, and reliance on Allah’s truth rather than on illusions.

translation: Indeed, Allah—with Him is the knowledge of the Hour; and He sends down the rain; and He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in which land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the decisive knowledge of the unseen and of future events belongs exclusively to Allah: the timing of the Hour, the sending of rain, the hidden condition of the unborn, what a person will do tomorrow, and where death will occur. It calls the human being to humility and God-consciousness, because no one truly controls tomorrow or even the place of his death. Therefore one should not live as though the future is guaranteed, but should rely upon Allah, prepare for the Hereafter, and act with the awareness that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge and is fully acquainted with every hidden reality.

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These disjointed letters are among the Qur’an’s opening signs whose precise meaning is known fully only to Allah; they establish that the revelation is composed of the same Arabic letters human beings use, yet it remains inimitable, and they summon the listener to attentive reflection upon the divine message that follows.

translation: The revelation of the Book—there is no doubt about it—is from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur’an is truly sent down by God, the Lord and Sustainer of all creation. Its divine origin is certain, not something to be doubted, and because it comes from the Lord of all the worlds, it is authoritative guidance meant for all people.

translation: Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Nay, it is the truth from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, that they may be guided.
interpretation: This verse confronts the Meccan disbelievers’ claim that Muhammad composed the Qur’an himself. It decisively rejects that charge: the Qur’an is not a human invention but revealed truth from the Lord. Its purpose is prophetic warning—to bring the message to a community that had not previously received a warner in their midst, namely the Arabs, who had no prophet sent directly to them after a long interval. The ultimate aim is not merely to announce judgment, but to open the way for them to accept guidance, turn to God, and follow the straight path.

translation: Allah is the One Who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days, then He rose over the Throne. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him. Will you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse establishes that absolute creation, ownership, and authority belong to Allah alone. He brought the entire universe into existence with wisdom and purpose, and His rising over the Throne signifies His supreme sovereignty and control over all affairs. Since no one besides Him can truly protect, guard, or intercede for anyone, people are called to awaken their hearts and remember that reliance, hope, fear, and supplication must be directed to Him alone. Any intercession can only occur by His permission, not by any independent power. Thus the verse invites reflection on His oneness and on the futility of depending on anything other than Him.

translation: He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth, then it ascends to Him in a Day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah’s absolute and all-encompassing governance of creation: every command, decree, and matter is arranged and administered from the heavens down to the earth, and all affairs ultimately return to Him. The mention of a day equal to a thousand human years teaches that divine command, the ascent of deeds, and the order of the unseen are not confined to the human experience of time; Allah transcends time, while human beings are reminded that their deeds are not lost but are recorded and returned to Him for reckoning.

translation: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah alone possesses complete knowledge of all that is hidden from creation and all that is visible or witnessed. He is Al-Aziz, the Almighty whose power is never overcome, and Ar-Rahim, the Most Merciful whose mercy is vast and enduring. Thus, His knowledge, power, and mercy are perfect and all-encompassing, so nothing in existence escapes His awareness or His sovereign care.

translation: Who perfected all things that He created, and He began the creation of man from clay.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah’s creation is flawless in design, wisdom, and purpose: everything He creates is made in the best and most fitting form for the function He intends. It then singles out the human being’s origin from clay to teach that humanity was brought forth from a humble, earthly substance, demonstrating Allah’s power to originate life from inert matter and His wisdom in shaping the human constitution. The mention of clay also implies that the One who first created man from dust is fully able to restore and raise him again.

translation: Then He made his progeny from an extract of a despised fluid.
interpretation: This verse states that after the creation of Adam from clay, God made his descendants to come forth through reproduction from a small, weak, and seemingly insignificant seminal fluid. The phrase “extract” indicates a portion drawn from that fluid, while “despised” describes its lowly and fragile nature in human estimation. The verse thus reminds people of the humble material beginning of their bodily existence and points to God’s power in producing and preserving human generations from such a modest means, and it supports the reality of resurrection by showing that the One who originated creation from clay and then from a drop can surely bring creation back to life.

translation: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His spirit, and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little do you give thanks.
interpretation: This verse signifies that after forming the human body, Allah completed and balanced its creation, then breathed into it a soul from His command, and He granted people the faculties of hearing, sight, and inner understanding so they may perceive His signs and guidance. True gratitude is shown by using these senses and the heart in obedience to Him and in worship; yet people are generally ungrateful.

translation: And they say, "When we have become lost in the earth, will we indeed be [raised] in a new creation?" Rather, they disbelieve in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse conveys the disbelievers' astonished rejection of resurrection: they deem it far-fetched that after their bodies have decomposed and vanished into the earth they could be brought forth anew. The Qur'an then identifies the deeper cause: their denial is not due to an intellectual impossibility but to their disbelief in meeting their Lord—that is, in being resurrected, held accountable, and brought before God. Thus their objection about creation is a pretext; the real offense is rejecting the certainty of return to their Lord and the judgment that follows.

translation: Say, 'The angel of death, who has been appointed over you, will take your souls; then to your Lord you will be returned.'
interpretation: This verse discloses that death is not a random end but a purposeful transition supervised by an angel acting under God’s authority. The angel cannot take a soul except by God’s decree, so ultimate power over life and death belongs to God alone. The return to the Lord after death means every soul will meet its Creator for judgment, making life a trust and death a doorway to accountability rather than extinction.

translation: And if you could but see when the criminals are hanging their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain."
interpretation: This verse portrays the criminals on the Day of Resurrection, standing before God with heads bowed in humiliation and regret. They admit that they now see and hear the truth they had rejected, and they beg to be sent back to the world to do good, claiming certainty. But their confession is forced by the sight of punishment and comes after the time of trial has ended. It teaches that faith and righteous action must occur in this life; the acknowledgment of the Hereafter will not rescue those who deliberately denied God when they had the chance to believe and obey.

translation: And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has become binding: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah’s power is not incapable of guiding everyone; had He forced guidance upon all souls, none would have disbelieved. Yet His wisdom decreed that this worldly life be a place of trial, with guidance made clear and the choice of faith or denial left to accountable beings. Thus His pronouncement is justly fulfilled: Hell will be filled with those among jinn and humans who knowingly reject the truth and choose evil, not with anyone who was helplessly deprived of guidance.

translation: So taste [the punishment] because you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours. Indeed, We have forgotten you. And taste the eternal punishment for what you used to do.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who rejected resurrection and accountability: their punishment is the just consequence of having disregarded the encounter with God on the Day of Judgment. God’s statement “We have forgotten you” means He leaves them abandoned in torment—not that He is unaware of them—and the “eternal punishment” corresponds to their persistent evil deeds, which they chose in the life of the world.

translation: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and glorify the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith in Allah’s revealed signs is not merely mental assent; it is a living response of humility and worship. When such believers are reminded of Allah’s verses, they immediately submit, prostrate before Him, and praise Him with gratitude. Their refusal to be arrogant shows that genuine faith removes pride and makes the heart soft, obedient, and ready to bow to divine guidance.

translation: Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend.
interpretation: This verse describes the inner discipline and outward generosity of true believers: they are willing to leave the comfort of sleep and rest in order to turn to God in supplication. Their worship is balanced by two profound states of the heart—fear of God’s displeasure and hope for His mercy—so that they neither fall into despair nor become complacent. Their devotion is not limited to private prayer; it also flows into how they use God’s provision, giving from what they have been granted rather than hoarding it. Thus the verse presents faith as a living force that reshapes both the night and the day: the night is given to humble prayer, and daily life is marked by charitable spending for God’s sake.

translation: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of the joy of eyes as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse declares that God has reserved for the righteous rewards whose beauty, peace, and delight surpass all human imagination, granted as recompense for their sincere obedience and good deeds. It teaches that the true reward of faith and righteous action is not fully visible in this world but is kept hidden with God, so that believers may strive with hope and certainty that no effort made for His sake will be lost or inadequately rewarded.

translation: Is the one who is a believer like the one who is a transgressor? They are not equal.
interpretation: This verse establishes that faith and transgression are not equivalent before God. A person whose life is rooted in belief, obedience, and accountability to God cannot be treated as equal to one who knowingly departs from His command and persists in corruption. They differ in moral worth, in divine guidance, and in their ultimate destination: the believer is on the path of guidance and success, while the transgressor is on a path that leads to loss unless he repents and returns to God. The verse thus rejects any attempt to level the righteous and the corrupt, affirming that God’s judgment is based on faith and deeds, not on outward status or human estimation.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge as a welcoming reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who combine sincere faith with righteous action will be received into the Gardens of Refuge, which God has prepared as an honoring welcome and a reward suited to their deeds. The term “nuzul” suggests hospitality and generous reception, showing that their eternal dwelling is not merely a payment but a gracious gift from God, granted in accordance with the good they persistently did.

translation: But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they want to exit from it, they are returned into it, and it is said to them, 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.'
interpretation: This verse pronounces the fate of those who rejected faith and persisted in disobedience: their final home is the Fire, from which there is no escape. Their repeated attempts to leave and their being forced back express the permanence and inescapability of their punishment, as well as the torment of hope repeatedly crushed. The command “Taste the punishment” is a rebuke that makes them experience the very reality they denied in worldly life. It shows that the punishment is not arbitrary but is the just consequence of their denial and transgression, and that the Hereafter will expose the truth of what they mocked. The verse thus serves as a severe warning: denying the Fire does not remove it, and the time to heed the warning is before that irreversible state.

translation: And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment, so that they may return.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah, out of His mercy, afflicts people with lesser hardships and trials in this worldly life—such as calamities, losses, or other corrective punishments—before the greater, eternal punishment of the Hereafter, so that they may wake up, repent, and return to Him in obedience and faith.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them? Indeed, We are avengers against the criminals.
interpretation: This verse declares that the utmost wrong is committed by one who, after God’s signs and revelations have come to him, deliberately turns away from them. The gravity lies in rejection after being reminded, not in simple unawareness, and such rejection places a person among the criminals. God then affirms that He will certainly exact retribution from those who persist in this course; His vengeance is just and certain.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not be in doubt about his meeting, and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the revelation he receives is true, citing Allah’s earlier granting of the Scripture to Moses. The ‘meeting’ refers to the Prophet’s encounter with Moses during the Night Journey, so he should not doubt that it occurred. The Scripture given to Moses was made a guidance for the Children of Israel, showing that Allah sends revelation and guidance to His messengers for their peoples.

translation: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient, and they were certain of Our signs.
interpretation: This means that Allah granted true religious leadership to some among them because they combined patient steadfastness in faith and obedience with firm certainty in Allah’s signs. Such leaders guide people by Allah’s command and authority, not by their own desires or claims; their qualification for guiding others is their endurance in truth and their unwavering conviction in divine revelation.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is the One who will decide between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the final resolution of all disputes—especially those concerning religion, truth, and God's commands—rests with God alone. On the Day of Resurrection, He will judge between the disputing parties with absolute justice, exposing the reality behind their differences and distinguishing the correct from the incorrect. No human authority, group, or inherited interpretation can replace that final judgment. Therefore, believers should strive for truth with humility, avoid arrogant certainty in disputed matters, and entrust the ultimate verdict to God, while holding fast to what He has clearly revealed.

translation: Does it not guide them [to see] how many generations We destroyed before them, in whose dwellings they walk? Indeed in that are signs; will they not then hear?
interpretation: The ruins of earlier peoples are a clear lesson: God destroyed them for persisting in denial, and the later disbelievers walk amid those same dwellings. The verse summons them to listen with hearts that heed, for God’s judgment on past nations is a sign of His power, justice, and the certainty that the same warning applies to anyone who refuses faith.

translation: Have they not seen that We drive water to the barren land, then bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock and their own selves eat? Will they not then see?
interpretation: This is a call to recognize Allah’s providential power in the ordinary cycle of rain and vegetation: the same God who revives dead, barren earth with water and sustains human and animal life is fully able to resurrect the dead. The rhetorical question censures those who ignore this visible sign, urging them to open their inner sight, submit to their Creator, and heed the warning of resurrection and accountability.

translation: And they say, 'When will this victory/conquest be, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This is a mocking question from the disbelievers about the promised decisive judgment or victory. They ask when it will occur if the believers are truthful in their claim. The verse means that they demand to know the timing of God's judgment, which will separate truth from falsehood and grant victory to the believers, but its appointed time is known only to God.

translation: Say, 'On the Day of Decision, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be granted respite.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers’ challenge about when the promised judgment will come. It declares that once Allah’s decisive decree arrives—the Day of Resurrection and final judgment—the time for repentance and faith has ended. At that point, professing belief will not profit those who rejected it during their worldly opportunity, and they will not be given any delay or second chance; they must face the consequences of their denial. The verse thus warns that faith benefits only when chosen within the appointed time of trial, before the fixed decree comes, and that mocking or demanding the promised day cannot avert it.

translation: So turn away from them and wait; indeed, they are waiting.
interpretation: This is a command to the Prophet—and by extension to the believers—to disengage from futile disputation with those who persist in rejection after the message has been made clear, to leave their case to Allah, and to patiently await His promised judgment and victory. The disbelievers are also waiting, but their waiting is rooted in doubt and defiance, and it will ultimately bring them loss, while the believers’ waiting is grounded in trust in Allah’s decree.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to maintain God-consciousness and steadfast obedience to Allah, and it forbids him from yielding to the influence, counsel, or demands of those who openly reject faith or secretly harbor hypocrisy. Their opposition may appear persuasive or strategically useful, but the divine command must remain supreme. Allah’s knowledge encompasses all their hidden motives and schemes, and His wisdom governs the precise guidance and laws He reveals, so trusting Him is the only sure path.

translation: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet—and, by extension, every believer—to make the revelation from his Lord the foundation of his conduct, especially when confronted by opposing voices. The wording “from your Lord” stresses that the guidance being followed is not human opinion but comes from the One who creates, sustains, and rightly commands. The closing declaration that Allah is “All-Aware of what you do” means that He knows every visible action and hidden intention, so no one can conceal whether they are sincerely following revelation or merely pretending. It is therefore both a directive to steadfast adherence and a warning that accountability rests with Allah, whose knowledge is complete and whose judgment is perfectly just.

translation: And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as a Trustee.
interpretation: This is a command to place one’s complete trust and reliance upon God in all affairs, turning to Him alone for protection, support, and the management of one’s matters. It affirms that God is fully sufficient as a guardian, disposer of affairs, and protector, so the believer’s heart should depend on Him rather than on created beings.

translation: Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his breast, nor has He made your wives whom you declare unlawful by zihar to be your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your real sons. That is only your saying with your mouths. And Allah says the truth, and He guides to the right way.
interpretation: This verse rejects false claims that contradict the realities Allah has established. A person cannot have two hearts in one body, meaning no one can truly live by two contradictory allegiances or identities at the same time. A wife does not become a mother merely because a husband utters words of zihar, and an adopted child does not become a biological son merely by being called one. Such statements are only words spoken by the mouth; they do not change lineage, kinship, or divine law. Allah alone speaks the truth, and He guides people to the straight path of correct belief, honest speech, and just social relations.

translation: Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in faith and your clients. And there is no blame upon you for what you did in error, but [there is blame] for what your hearts intended. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that a person’s true lineage and identity must be attributed to their biological father when known, because that is the fairest and most truthful before Allah. Adoption or guardianship should not erase or falsify real parentage. If the father is unknown, then the relationship is based on brotherhood in faith and mutual loyalty in the community rather than false lineage. It also teaches that Allah does not hold people accountable for honest mistakes or unintentional errors in such matters; accountability applies to what the heart deliberately chooses and intends. Thus the verse combines truthfulness in social identity, compassion for those without known lineage, and divine forgiveness and mercy for sincere believers.

translation: The Prophet has more right over the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. And those related by blood are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah than the believers and the emigrants, except that you do kindness to your allies. That was written in the Book.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Prophet’s supreme authority over the believers: his command and claim upon them take precedence over their own desires and choices, and his wives are honored as mothers of the believers, meaning they are due respect and are forbidden in marriage to the community. It also lays down the principle of inheritance: after the earlier bond of faith and migration, blood kinship becomes the basis of inheritance among relatives, so close relatives inherit from one another before others. The exception permits a person to benefit non-inheriting allies through a bequest or voluntary kindness, not as an obligatory share. This ruling is prescribed and recorded in Allah’s decree and Book.

translation: And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah took a binding, weighty covenant from all the prophets—including Prophet Muhammad and the specifically named Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus—to worship Allah alone, convey His message faithfully, and fulfill their prophetic missions. It also indicates that they were bound to believe in and support one another, especially the final Messenger, and to make this known to their followers. The phrase 'a solemn covenant' emphasizes the gravity of this trust and the accountability attached to it, showing the unity of the prophetic message and the lofty status of those chosen to bear it.

translation: That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness; and He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
interpretation: Its meaning is that Allah will hold those who claimed truthfulness accountable for the sincerity and fulfillment of that truthfulness, questioning them about whether they honored their covenant and upheld the truth in word and deed; and for those who reject faith, He has prepared a painful torment.

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when armies came against you, and We sent against them a wind and armies [of angels] you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of God’s protection during the Battle of the Trench, when a great coalition of enemy forces besieged Madinah. Although the believers could see only the vast enemy army and their own limited means, God sent a fierce wind and unseen angelic forces to disrupt, frighten, and scatter the attackers, causing their siege to fail. The verse teaches that divine help often comes through means beyond human perception and calculation, and that God sees every deed, intention, and act of faithfulness. It calls believers to remember God’s favors in times of crisis, to trust Him, and to remain steadfast, knowing that He is fully aware of their actions and will protect and support them according to His wisdom.

translation: When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes swerved and the hearts reached the throats, and you were forming various thoughts about Allah.
interpretation: This verse depicts the extreme trial during the siege of the Trench, when the believers were encircled by fear from every direction and the pressure reached the point of near-death terror. The rolling of the eyes and the hearts rising to the throats express a total collapse of human composure, while the "various thoughts about Allah" expose how crisis can either produce doubt and despair or draw out patient trust in Him. Its meaning is that faith is truly tested when circumstances become overwhelming, and the heart’s inward state at such a moment—whether it leans toward false suspicion of God or toward reliance upon His promise—is the real measure of one’s relationship with Him. The verse warns against letting fear shape one’s view of God and reminds the believer that Allah is fully aware of the inner struggle and that relief lies beyond the limit of human endurance.

translation: There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.
interpretation: This verse describes the extreme trial faced by the believers during the siege of Medina in the Battle of the Trench, when the allied forces surrounded them and circumstances became so dire that their faith, patience, and resolve were severely tested. It means that the believers were put through a harsh examination and were violently shaken by fear, hardship, hunger, cold, betrayal, and the apparent strength of the enemy, so that sincere faith was distinguished from weakness and hypocrisy. The shaking was not merely physical but also psychological and spiritual, exposing what was truly in the hearts and proving who would remain steadfast upon reliance in Allah despite the overwhelming distress.

translation: And [remember] when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, “Allah and His Messenger did not promise us anything but delusion.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the inner condition of hypocrisy and spiritual sickness: when faith is tested by hardship, siege, fear, or delayed victory, such people reinterpret God’s true promise as deception. Their words are not merely doubt about circumstances but an accusation against divine truth and prophetic honesty. The verse teaches that trials separate sincere trust from superficial allegiance; the believer may feel pressure, but he does not turn God’s promise into a lie. It also warns that a heart afflicted by doubt will judge God’s guidance by outward difficulty rather than by His truthfulness, whereas faith holds that God’s promise is real even when its fulfillment comes through patience and testing.

translation: And [remember] when a party of them said, “O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you [to stand], so go back.” And a faction of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, “Indeed, our houses are exposed.” But they were not exposed; they only intended to flee.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy and cowardice of a group among the people of Medina during the Battle of the Trench. They tried to demoralize the believers by claiming that there was no position left to hold and urging them to retreat. Another group came to the Prophet seeking permission to leave under the false pretext that their homes were vulnerable to the enemy, while in reality their homes were not exposed. Their true aim was not to protect their families but to escape the hardship and danger of battle. The verse thus unmasks their deception and shows that Allah knows the hidden motives behind their words and actions.

translation: And if they were entered upon from all sides [of the city] and then asked to commit treason/turn back from faith, they would have done it, and they would not have remained [steadfast] except a little.
interpretation: This verse exposes the fragile loyalty of the hypocrites: had the enemy penetrated Madinah from every direction and invited them to betray the Muslims or abandon their faith, they would have complied almost immediately. Their allegiance was conditional, tied to safety and convenience rather than sincere conviction. It warns believers that true faith is proven under pressure, and that God knows the hidden intentions of the heart, so one must guard against hypocrisy and remain steadfast.

translation: And they had already covenanted with Allah before that they would not turn their backs [in flight]. And the covenant with Allah will be questioned.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who were wavering during the siege, reminding them of their earlier pledge to Allah not to flee from battle. Their present desire to withdraw exposes the seriousness of breaking such a solemn oath. Allah declares that every covenant made with Him will be inquired into, so no one can escape accountability for disloyalty or cowardice. It teaches that promises to Allah, especially those requiring steadfastness and sacrifice, must be honored, and their violation is a grave matter deserving divine reckoning.

translation: Say, "Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be allowed to enjoy except a little."
interpretation: This verse addresses those who try to escape fighting or divine decree out of fear of death. It teaches that fleeing cannot avert what God has decreed; even if they escape death or being killed for a time, their remaining worldly enjoyment is only brief and cannot save them from God’s appointed end. True security lies in obedience to God and reliance upon Him, not in attempting to flee His decree.

translation: Say, 'Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends harm for you or intends mercy for you?' And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah alone has absolute power to bring about harm or mercy, and no created being can shield anyone from His will or withhold what He decrees. Those who seek protection, support, or deliverance from anyone besides Him will find neither a guardian to manage their affairs nor a helper to avert His judgment; therefore fear, hope, and reliance belong to Allah alone.

translation: Allah already knows those among you who hinder others and those who say to their brothers, 'Come to us,' and they do not come to battle except a little.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrites in the Muslim community during the Battle of the Trench. They obstructed others from supporting the Prophet, told their supposed brothers to abandon the fight and join them in safety, and when fighting did occur they participated only briefly or reluctantly, revealing their lack of sincerity and love of ease. Allah’s knowledge encompasses their hidden motives and words, so they cannot deceive Him. The verse warns against cowardice, hypocrisy, and undermining the steadfastness of the believers, while affirming that God is fully aware of those who obstruct good and incite others to withdraw.

translation: [They are] miserly toward you [believers]. When fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who swoons from death. But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues, miserly toward good. Those have not believed, so Allah has made their deeds worthless; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those whose loyalty is tied only to safety and self-interest. In hardship they are unwilling to give or support the believers, and in danger they are overcome by terror, looking to the Prophet with rolling eyes like someone losing consciousness at death. Yet once the threat passes, they turn bold and abusive, using sharp tongues to wound and blaming others while withholding good and wealth. Because their actions spring from unbelief and insincerity, Allah renders their deeds fruitless; no effort or scheme of theirs can thwart His will, and nullifying their works is effortless for Him. The verse teaches that true faith is shown by steadfastness, generosity, and sincerity in both fear and safety, not by loud claims or harsh words after danger has gone.

translation: They think the confederates have not departed; and if the confederates should come, they would wish they were among the Bedouins, asking about your news. And if they were among you, they would not fight except a little.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy and cowardice of those whose faith was weak during the siege: they remain gripped by fear and suspicion even after the enemy coalition withdraws, imagining that the threat is still present. If the confederates were to return, their only desire would be to escape to the desert and live among the Bedouins, far from danger, merely asking for news about the believers instead of standing with them. And even if they were physically present among the believers, their participation in battle would be only minimal and reluctant, because their hearts are not committed to the cause and they seek only their own safety.

translation: Indeed, you have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example to follow — for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah much.
interpretation: The verse means that the Prophet Muhammad is the divinely appointed model whose life embodies the Qur’anic guidance; taking him as one’s example is the practical proof of genuine hope in Allah and the Hereafter, and such hope is nurtured and sustained by abundant remembrance of Allah, which purifies intention and strengthens the will to follow his character, worship, patience, justice, and trust in God.

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth." And it only increased them in faith and submission.
interpretation: The verse presents the hallmark of true faith when facing overwhelming opposition: the believer recognizes the trial as something already encompassed by Allah's promise and the Messenger's warning, affirms Allah's truthfulness, and lets the hardship deepen, not diminish, faith and surrender. Such a response shows that certainty in divine revelation turns crisis into a means of spiritual strength; trials do not shake the sincere but expose and increase their trust in Allah's promise and their submission to His decree.

translation: Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah. Some of them have fulfilled their vow, and some of them are waiting, and they have not changed in the least.
interpretation: This verse praises believers whose faith is proven by unwavering loyalty to the covenant they made with Allah. It means that true faith is not mere claim; it is tested by sacrifice and steadfastness. Those who “fulfilled their vow” are those who remained faithful until death, giving their lives in Allah’s cause, while those “waiting” remain firm and faithful, ready to meet Allah’s decree whenever it comes. Their defining quality is that they did not alter, betray, or weaken their commitment. Thus the verse presents sincerity, patience, and constancy upon the covenant with Allah as marks of authentic belief.

translation: so that Allah may reward the truthful for their truth and punish the hypocrites, if He wills, or accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse declares that the ultimate purpose of divine testing and accountability is to manifest and reward sincerity: those who remain true in faith and conduct receive the reward their truthfulness deserves. For the hypocrites, their fate is presented under God's sovereign will—He may punish them as their duplicity merits, or He may forgive them if they turn back—because His justice and mercy are inseparable. The verse thus affirms both moral responsibility and the open door of repentance, grounding the final outcome in God's forgiving, merciful nature.

translation: And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they obtained no good. And Allah sufficed the believers in battle. And Allah is ever Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah alone turned back the hostile disbelievers, who withdrew enraged and frustrated, having gained no victory, spoil, or advantage. By sending unseen forces and striking fear and division among them, Allah spared the believers from having to fight them directly, granting them protection and victory without their own strength. It affirms that true power and honor belong to Allah, who is All-Strong and Almighty, and that He defends and suffices the believers when they rely on Him.

translation: And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts: a party you killed, and you took captive a party.
interpretation: This verse describes God's direct intervention on behalf of the believers during the siege of Medina. The tribe among the People of the Book that had broken its covenant and aided the enemy coalition was dislodged from its fortified strongholds, and panic was planted in its hearts, so that its resistance collapsed. The outcome was a decisive judgment: one group was killed and another was taken captive. The deeper meaning is that God alone grants victory and security, and that treachery and alliance with aggression against the believing community ultimately recoil upon those who commit them. It also affirms that divine help arrives when the faithful stand firm under pressure, and that His decree cannot be thwarted by any fortress or confederacy.

translation: And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, their wealth, and a land which you had not yet trodden. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah fulfilled His promise to the believers by granting them victory and causing them to inherit the properties of their enemies who had conspired against them. The immediate reference is to the aftermath of the Battle of the Trench, when the tribe of Banu Qurayza was defeated and their lands, houses, and wealth came into the Muslims’ possession. The phrase “a land which you had not yet trodden” points to further conquests and openings that Allah would grant them in the future, beyond what they could then foresee, such as Khaybar, Persia, and Byzantium. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah is fully able to accomplish whatever He wills, so His promise of future inheritance is certain and cannot be thwarted.

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives, 'If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a beautiful release.'
interpretation: This verse gives the Prophet's wives a clear choice: either remain with him in his simple and demanding life, seeking God and the Hereafter, or choose worldly luxury and be divorced honorably with provision. It teaches that attachment to the Prophet cannot coexist with an overriding love of worldly gain, and that separation, if chosen, must be carried out with kindness, generosity, and dignity rather than punishment or disgrace.

translation: And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed Allah has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward.
interpretation: This verse presents the true criterion of honor and success: not worldly comfort but the desire for God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter.
