translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse declares that Satan's enmity toward humanity is real, rooted, and unrelenting; therefore, a believer must not treat him carelessly or with familiarity, but must consciously adopt an attitude of opposition toward him and his ways. Satan's aim is not merely to prompt isolated sins but to draw people into his faction and lead them to the Blazing Fire. Thus the verse warns that following his invitations, whispers, and misleadings ultimately places a person among the inhabitants of Hell, and it calls for vigilance, resistance, and steadfast adherence to God's guidance.

translation: Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the two ultimate outcomes based on one’s response to God: rejection and disbelief lead to severe punishment, while faith joined with righteous action leads to God’s forgiveness of sins and an abundant, generous reward. It shows that true faith is not merely an inner claim but is expressed through good deeds, and that God’s justice warns the rejecters while His mercy and grace are promised to the believers who act rightly.

translation: Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good [like one whom Allah guides]? Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let your soul perish in sorrow over them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse exposes the spiritual condition of those who have become so deluded that they regard their own corruption as virtue. Such a reversal is not merely a private mistake; it places them under Allah’s decree of misguidance, while true guidance comes only from Him. Allah’s will here is not arbitrary but is joined to His perfect knowledge of what people craft and choose, so He knows who is fit for guidance and who persists in self-deception. The Prophet is then consoled: he must not consume himself with grief over their rejection, because his task is to deliver the message, not to force hearts. The verse thus teaches that human effort cannot compel faith, that divine guidance and misguidance follow Allah’s wisdom, and that the believer should not carry the burden of the heedless as if their response were his responsibility alone.

translation: And Allah is the One Who sends the winds, so they stir up clouds, then We drive it to a dead land and revive the earth by it after its death. Thus is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah’s exclusive power over creation and life-giving: He directs the winds, forms clouds, carries rain to barren land, and revives the dead earth. That visible act is a clear proof and likeness of the final resurrection, meaning that the One able to bring dead soil back to life is fully able to raise the dead from their graves. The verse thus affirms both His oneness in lordship and the certainty of the Hereafter.

translation: Whoever seeks honor, then to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends good words, and righteous deeds raise it. But those who plot evil deeds will have severe punishment, and their plotting will perish.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true honor and dignity belong exclusively to God, so anyone who seeks honor should seek it through faith, remembrance of God, and righteous action rather than through arrogance or evil schemes. Pure words of belief and praise ascend to Him, and righteous deeds uplift and establish them. By contrast, those who plot corruption will face a severe punishment, and their schemes are doomed to fail and come to nothing.

translation: And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then He made you mates. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no one is granted long life, nor is his life diminished, except that it is in a Book. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah alone is the Creator and Sustainer: He originated human beings from dust and then from a sperm-drop, and He made them male and female spouses so that generation continues by His will. It then declares that nothing in the process of pregnancy, childbirth, aging, or the span of any life escapes His knowledge or decree. Every conception, every birth, every long life, and every reduction of a lifespan is already recorded in a Book with Him, and bringing all of that about, maintaining it, and recording it is effortless for Allah.

translation: And the two seas are not equal: this one is fresh, sweet, and palatable to drink, while this one is salty and bitter. And from each you eat fresh meat and extract ornaments which you wear. And you see the ships therein plowing through the waves so that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse presents the two contrasting bodies of water as a sign of Allah’s wisdom, power, and generosity. Though they differ in taste and usefulness, both are made to serve humanity: they provide food, adornment, and a means of travel and trade. The fresh water satisfies thirst directly, while the salt sea yields resources and carries ships by Allah’s command. The deeper meaning is that such distinctions and provisions are not accidental; they are deliberate favors meant to lead people to seek Allah’s bounty with gratitude. True thankfulness is shown by recognizing the Giver behind the gift, using His provisions responsibly, and turning the heart toward Him rather than becoming heedless through enjoyment of the created world.

translation: He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs all sovereignty. And those whom you invoke besides Him do not own even a qitmir.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah’s exclusive lordship through signs of His power over time and the cosmos. By merging night into day and day into night, He alone controls the alternation of time, seasons, and appointed durations. The sun and moon are subjected to His command, moving precisely until their decreed end, which proves His wisdom, power, and ability to resurrect and reckon. Therefore, He alone is Allah, your Lord, and to Him alone belongs all dominion. The false deities and intercessors people call upon besides Him possess nothing at all—not even a qitmir, the tiny membrane on a date stone. They cannot create, provide, harm, benefit, or answer. Thus the verse directs all worship, reliance, and hope exclusively to Allah, and exposes the utter emptiness of associating partners with Him.

translation: If you call upon them, they will not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your associating them with Allah. And none can inform you like the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse declares the absolute helplessness of anything worshipped besides Allah: such false deities cannot hear the supplications of those who invoke them, and even if they could hear, they would have no power to answer or benefit. On the Day of Resurrection they will disown and reject the worship and shirk that was directed to them, so the polytheists will find no support from what they relied upon. The final statement affirms that this news is absolutely certain because it comes from Allah, the One fully aware of all things, whose knowledge and testimony are perfect and beyond compare.

translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah, while Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse declares that every human being is intrinsically poor and dependent before God: our existence, powers, sustenance, guidance, and salvation all come from Him, and we cannot achieve anything without His support. God alone is absolutely self-sufficient, needing nothing from anyone, and He is worthy of all praise. Therefore, the verse calls us to abandon arrogance and self-reliance, to recognize our servitude, and to turn to God alone for every need, while praising Him, since His command and generosity are never diminished by our needs or our worship.

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you and bring a new creation.
interpretation: This verse affirms God's absolute power and freedom: human beings are not indispensable to Him. If He wills, He can eliminate them and replace them with another creation, just as He originated them. It is a warning against arrogance and heedlessness, and evidence that resurrection and the bringing forth of a new creation are entirely easy for Him.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s power is absolute and nothing He wills is beyond His capability. Creating, destroying, resurrecting, or replacing creation is not hard or impossible for Him; no force can resist or frustrate His decree. It establishes that His will is always effective and that His might is never diminished or constrained.

translation: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a near relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself does so for the benefit of his own soul; and to Allah is the destination.
interpretation: This verse establishes that moral and spiritual responsibility is strictly individual: no person can carry another’s sin, guilt, or accountability before God, not even a close relative. Pleas for someone else to bear one’s burden in the Hereafter will be of no avail, because divine judgment is perfectly just and no one can substitute for another in faith or deeds. The Prophet’s warning, therefore, benefits only those who are inwardly disposed to God-consciousness—who fear their Lord even when unseen and who uphold prayer as a lived commitment. Purification of the soul is not a favor to God; it redounds to the person’s own benefit. The final return is to Allah alone, where each soul answers for itself.

translation: And the blind and the seeing are not equal.
interpretation: The blind person represents the one whose heart is blind to divine truth and revelation, while the seeing person represents the one who possesses inner sight and responds to God’s guidance; the verse declares that these two are not equal in knowledge, faith, or final outcome.

translation: Nor are the darknesses and the light [equal].
interpretation: This declares that the many forms of unbelief, ignorance, and moral darkness can never be equivalent to the light of faith, revelation, and divine guidance. Darkness is plural because misguidance takes countless paths; light is singular because truth and guidance come from one source, God. Thus falsehood and truth, heedlessness and knowledge, can never be treated as equal.

translation: nor the shade and nor the scorching heat
interpretation: This phrase declares that shade and scorching heat are not equal, symbolizing the absolute contrast between mercy and punishment, guidance and misguidance, comfort and suffering. It calls the reader to recognize that opposites in the moral and spiritual order cannot be treated as alike or interchangeable.

translation: And the living and the dead are not equal. Indeed, Allah causes whom He wills to hear, but you cannot make those in the graves hear.
interpretation: This verse contrasts those whose hearts are alive with faith and respond to divine guidance with those whose hearts are spiritually dead, unmoved by admonition. It teaches that true hearing and acceptance of the message come only by Allah’s will; the Prophet’s role is to convey, not to force guidance into hearts that are as unresponsive as the inhabitants of graves. Thus, the dead here signifies those spiritually buried in disbelief and heedlessness, who cannot be made to hear unless Allah grants them life and hearing.

translation: You are only a warner.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Prophet’s mission is solely to deliver the warning and convey Allah’s message; he has no power to force people to believe or to guide their hearts, since guidance belongs to Allah alone.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God sent the Prophet Muhammad with the truth, tasked to give glad tidings to those who believe and obey, and to warn those who disbelieve and disobey. It then declares that every nation or community in history received a warner from God, so no people were left without divine guidance or excuse. This shows God's justice and the continuity of prophethood, culminating in the final message brought by Muhammad.

translation: And if they deny you, those before them also denied. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, and with scriptures, and with the illuminating Book.
interpretation: This consoles the Prophet: rejection is not new or unique to him. Earlier communities also denied their messengers even though those messengers brought unmistakable signs, revealed writings, and a book full of light. The fault lies with the deniers, not with the message; therefore the Prophet should remain steadfast, and the verse warns that persistent rejection after clear evidence carries the same grave responsibility.

translation: Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how [severe] was My punishment!
interpretation: The verse declares that when people persist in rejecting God’s messengers and the clear signs, scriptures, and enlightening books they brought, God seizes them in His might. The rhetorical question “so how was My punishment?” is not asking for information; it affirms that His retribution was unavoidable, overwhelming, and a decisive rejection of their disbelief. It serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and as assurance that God will judge and requite the rejecters of His message.

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of diverse colors? And among the mountains are white and red tracts, of diverse colors, and black, intensely black.
interpretation: This verse calls attention to visible proofs of Allah’s power, knowledge, and wisdom: from a single water He brings forth fruits differing in color, taste, and form, and in the mountains He placed layers and streaks of varied colors—white, red, and deep black. Such ordered diversity from common origins shows that the Creator freely originates, varies, and revives. It establishes His oneness and the reality of resurrection, and it urges people to reflect, be grateful, and submit to Him.

translation: And among people, crawling creatures, and livestock are those of different colors. Likewise, only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Most Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the variety of colors and forms among humans, animals, and livestock is a sign of Allah's boundless power and wise creation. From observing this diversity, a person of knowledge recognizes the Creator and is moved to humble reverence. Thus the fear of Allah that truly counts is rooted in knowledge of Him—His majesty, wisdom, and authority—not in ignorance or blind imitation. Such reverent fear leads one to obey Him and avoid His displeasure. The verse closes by affirming that Allah is Almighty and Most Forgiving: His greatness should inspire awe, while His forgiveness invites repentance and hope, so that fear is balanced with trust in His mercy.

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided them, secretly and openly, hope for a transaction that will never perish.
interpretation: This verse describes the believers who combine reciting Allah's Book, performing the prescribed prayer, and giving charity from what Allah has provided, whether privately or publicly. Their aim is not worldly praise but the reward and pleasure of Allah, which is compared to a trade that is certain never to suffer loss or ruin. It affirms that such devotion and generosity are never wasted before Allah; He will preserve and multiply their reward, and their hope in Him is a hope grounded in His unfailing promise.

translation: That He may give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Most Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse conveys that Allah will not only grant the believers the complete reward due for their faith and righteous deeds, but will also add to it generously out of His own grace, beyond what their actions strictly deserve. His name “Forgiving” means He overlooks their shortcomings and failures, while “Most Appreciative” means He recognizes and abundantly rewards even the smallest sincere good they do, multiplying it far beyond its apparent worth. Thus the verse combines divine justice in fulfilling rewards with divine generosity in increasing them, and it grounds the believer’s hope in Allah’s mercy and gratitude rather than in human merit alone.

translation: And that which We have revealed to you of the Book — it is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah is, of His servants, All-Aware and All-Seeing.
interpretation: The Qur’an revealed to the Prophet Muhammad is the absolute truth from God, and it confirms the earlier divinely revealed scriptures in their original form, bearing witness to their true origin and correcting what has been altered. God’s knowledge fully encompasses His servants—their conditions, intentions, deeds, and needs—and He sees all things, so He guides whom He wills with truth and will judge all with perfect awareness and justice.

translation: Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen among Our servants; but among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah has honored a chosen group of servants by entrusting them with the Book, making it an inheritance of guidance, responsibility, and reward. The three descriptions show levels of fulfilling that trust: the first wrongs himself through sins and shortcomings but remains within the ranks of those who inherit the Book; the second is balanced, fulfilling obligations and avoiding major disobedience; the third races ahead in good deeds, excelling in worship, knowledge, and virtue. Even this highest rank is not reached by human strength alone, but only by Allah's enabling permission. The great bounty is the honor of receiving, preserving, and living by the Book, along with the degrees Allah grants to those who carry it. The verse thus warns against negligence and urges striving toward the highest level of obedience.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter, adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearl, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse signifies the honor and bliss that God grants to the righteous in the Hereafter: He admits them into eternal gardens where they are adorned with gold and pearls and clothed in silk. The meaning is that Paradise is a state of perfect dignity, purity, and delight, in which God’s generosity replaces worldly hardship with lasting honor, and the adornments and fine garments symbolize divine favor and the elevated station of those whom God has pleased.

translation: And they will say, “All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us all sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.”
interpretation: This verse describes the gratitude of the people of Paradise after Allah admits them into eternal bliss. Their sorrow—every grief, anxiety, regret, and hardship they suffered in the worldly life and during the reckoning—has been completely taken away. Their praise is not merely verbal but flows from perfect contentment and joy. By calling Allah “Forgiving,” they acknowledge that He pardoned their sins; by calling Him “Appreciative,” they acknowledge that He accepted their small good deeds and rewarded them abundantly. Thus the verse teaches that ultimate relief from sorrow belongs to the righteous in the Hereafter, and that Allah’s forgiveness and generous appreciation are the cause of their eternal happiness.

translation: Who has settled us in the home of permanence out of His bounty. No fatigue will touch us therein, nor will weariness touch us therein.
interpretation: This is the gratitude of the people of Paradise: their eternal dwelling is not earned by their own power but granted by Allah’s grace, and within it He removes every trace of worldly hardship—neither bodily exhaustion nor lingering weariness will ever affect them. It affirms that the bliss of the Hereafter is complete and unending, free from the toil and depletion that define mortal life.

translation: And those who disbelieve will have the Fire of Hell. It will not be decreed for them that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful denier.
interpretation: This verse describes the unending and inescapable punishment of persistent disbelief: the disbelievers are consigned to Hell, where death is withheld so that they cannot escape their suffering through annihilation, and the torment is never eased or reduced. This is God's just recompense for extreme ingratitude and denial of the truth, showing that those who knowingly reject faith and persist in it will receive a punishment matching their rejection.

translation: And they will cry out therein, “Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do.” Did We not grant you a lifetime long enough for whoever would remember to remember? And the warner came to you. So taste, for the wrongdoers have no helper.
interpretation: This verse depicts the people of Hell crying out in anguish after seeing their punishment, begging for a second chance and promising to do righteous deeds instead of their former evil. God’s response establishes that their plea is not due to lack of opportunity: He had already given them ample time in the world for anyone sincerely willing to reflect and take heed, and He had sent warnings through His messengers. Their failure came from willful persistence, not from insufficient guidance. Therefore, the punishment is just, and the wrongdoers will find no helper or intercessor to save them. The verse teaches that the Hereafter is not a place of testing or amendment; human accountability rests on the life and warnings already granted, and divine justice leaves no support for those who knowingly persisted in wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah’s knowledge is absolute and all-encompassing: nothing hidden in the heavens or the earth—whether past, future, unseen realities, or secrets beyond human perception—is outside His knowledge. It then singles out that He knows what lies within the breasts, meaning the innermost intentions, thoughts, motives, beliefs, doubts, desires, and hidden states of the heart. The verse therefore calls a person to inward sincerity and God-consciousness, not merely outward correctness, because Allah sees and knows the heart just as He knows the unseen creation. It is both a warning to those who conceal corruption or hypocrisy and a reassurance to believers that their sincere intentions and hidden struggles are fully known to Him.

translation: He is the One Who has made you successors in the earth. So whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is against him. And the disbelievers’ disbelief does not increase them in the sight of their Lord except in hatred, and the disbelievers’ disbelief does not increase them except in loss.
interpretation: This verse declares Allah’s power and favor in appointing humankind as successive stewards and generations on the earth, entrusting them with responsibility and testing them through His guidance. It then clarifies that rejecting faith harms only the rejecter himself: his disbelief remains upon him, bringing him divine wrath and estrangement from his Lord, and it adds nothing to him but ruin. Disbelief never diminishes Allah’s dominion or harms Him; it only increases the disbeliever’s own condemnation and loss in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: Say, "Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have any share in the heavens? Or have We given them a Book so that they are upon clear evidence from it? Nay, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion."
interpretation: This verse is a decisive argument against polytheism. It challenges the idolaters to reflect on the deities and intercessors they call upon besides Allah: those beings have created nothing on earth, possess no share or authority in the heavens, and have received no revealed Book from Allah that would justify their worship. Since none of these false gods can create, own, or provide divine authorization, invoking them is groundless. The verse concludes that the wrongdoers only deceive one another with false promises and vain hopes; their mutual encouragement in shirk rests on illusion, not on truth or evidence. Thus the passage establishes that worship belongs to Allah alone and that every claim to shared divinity or independent intercession is baseless.

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing, Forgiving.
interpretation: This means that the ordered existence of the heavens and the earth depends entirely on Allah’s continuous sustaining power; they do not remain stable by themselves. If He willed their collapse or disappearance, no created being could prevent it or restore them. His forbearance is shown in delaying punishment despite human disobedience, and His forgiveness is extended to those who turn back to Him.

translation: And they swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be more guided than any of the nations. But when a warner came to them, it only increased them in aversion.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hollowness of mere verbal commitment to guidance. The disbelievers claimed with the most solemn oaths that the arrival of a warner would make them more receptive and rightly guided than other communities, yet when the Prophet Muhammad came, their response was not acceptance but deeper repulsion. The obstacle was never a lack of warning; it was arrogance, stubbornness, and attachment to inherited ways. Their oath proved insincere because they did not truly desire the truth on its own terms, but only as an imagined vindication of their superiority. Thus the verse teaches that warnings and signs do not benefit a heart determined to resist, and that encountering the truth can increase the arrogant only in flight from it.

translation: Out of arrogance in the land and plotting evil; but the evil plot does not encompass except its own people. Then do they await anything but the way of the former peoples? But you will never find in the way of Allah any change, and you will never find in the way of Allah any alteration.
interpretation: This verse teaches that arrogance and evil scheming against divine guidance ultimately harm only those who commit them. The plotting of the deniers does not injure Allah or His messengers; its evil consequence returns to the plotters themselves. It also warns that those who persist in rejection are effectively waiting for the same established pattern by which Allah dealt with earlier nations: whenever corruption and rejection reached their limit, divine judgment came. Allah’s way is constant and unalterable; His laws of cause and consequence, and His decrees for nations, cannot be changed, circumvented, or redirected. Thus no power can prevent the promised outcome, and no people can escape the fixed divine pattern by which truth is vindicated and persistent evil is held accountable.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And they were greater than them in strength. But Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse calls people to learn from history by reflecting on the ruins and fates of earlier nations. Those nations were physically stronger and more advanced in worldly power, yet their strength did not protect them when they persisted in denial and corruption. The verse warns that no power in the heavens or the earth can escape Allah or thwart His decree. Since He is All-Knowing, He is fully aware of every deed, and since He is All-Powerful, He can bring about judgment and replacement exactly as He wills. Thus worldly might is no security against divine accountability; true safety lies in heeding the lessons of the past and turning to God.

translation: And if Allah were to take people to task for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth any moving creature. But He delays them to an appointed term. Then when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever, of His servants, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse expresses God's forbearance and mercy: if He were to punish people immediately and fully for every wrong they commit, the consequences would be so vast that no living creature on earth could remain. Yet He does not act hastily; He grants respite until a fixed, appointed time. This delay is not negligence or unawareness, but a wise opportunity for repentance and a test of conduct. When the appointed term arrives, judgment will be carried out with perfect justice, for God is fully aware of His servants—their deeds, intentions, and circumstances—and He never wrongs them.

translation: Ya Seen.
interpretation: These are among the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta‘ah) with which several surahs of the Qur’an begin. Their precise meaning is known only to Allah; they serve as a divine sign that draws attention to the revelation that follows and points to the Qur’an’s miraculous, inimitable nature.

translation: By the wise Qur'an.
interpretation: Allah swears by the Qur'an, which is characterized by wisdom—its commands, prohibitions, reports, and judgments are all founded on perfect wisdom—thereby affirming the truth of what is revealed to Muhammad and the reality of the resurrection.

translation: Indeed, you are among the messengers.
interpretation: This is a divine affirmation addressed to Prophet Muhammad, confirming that he is truly one of God's messengers, sent with the revelation and entrusted with conveying the message. It establishes the authenticity of his prophethood and rebuts those who denied or doubted his mission.

translation: Upon a straight path.
interpretation: This describes the Messenger as firmly established on the straight path—the religion of pure monotheism and divine guidance—free from deviation, crookedness, and falsehood, and steadfast in conveying the truth from God.

translation: A revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse identifies the Qur’an as sent down by God alone and joins His might with His mercy: His being Almighty establishes that the revelation is true, authoritative, and beyond any power to prevent or corrupt; His being Most Merciful shows that He did not leave humanity without guidance but sent it as a mercy. The two names together mean that the same revelation is both a sovereign decree and compassionate guidance, calling people to submit to divine authority while hoping in divine mercy.

translation: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless.
interpretation: This verse explains the purpose of the revelation given to the Prophet Muhammad: he is sent as a warner to a people who had inherited a state of unawareness because no divine warning had reached their immediate ancestors. Their heedlessness is not presented as an excuse, but as the very condition that makes the warning necessary and merciful. God does not leave people in neglect; He sends a messenger to awaken them to His oneness, to the reality of revelation, and to their accountability before Him. Once the warning comes, the responsibility shifts to them to listen, reflect, and respond.

translation: Indeed, the word has come true against most of them, so they will not believe.
interpretation: This means that God’s decree of punishment has become binding upon the majority of these people because of their persistent denial and rejection of the truth; their disbelief is settled, and they will not come to faith unless God wills otherwise.

translation: Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, and they reach up to the chins, so they are forced to raise their heads.
interpretation: This is a graphic image of the spiritual bondage of those who persist in denial. Their own arrogance and rejection of the truth have become like chains that bind their hands to their necks and force their heads upward, so they cannot lower themselves, turn toward guidance, or see the path of faith. It expresses that they are prevented from believing and held back from responding to the message, not merely a description of physical restraint.

translation: And We have set a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them, so they do not see.
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual condition of those who, after repeatedly rejecting the truth, are left unable to perceive it. The barriers before and behind them signify that every path to guidance is blocked and every retreat to former excuses is cut off; the covering over their sight means their inner faculty of discernment is veiled. It is not arbitrary punishment but the just consequence of willful denial: when people persist in turning away from clear signs, God seals their hearts and eyes, so they cannot see the truth even when it stands before them.

translation: And it is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them—they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse states that those who have firmly resolved upon disbelief are unaffected by warning or its absence, because their rejection is not caused by insufficient admonition but by a willful, settled refusal to accept the truth. The Prophet is thus told that their lack of faith is not a failure of his delivery or sincerity; rather, their hearts have become unreceptive, so warning and silence are equal in their case. It teaches that guidance ultimately belongs to God, and human effort to warn is an obligation whose results rest with Him.

translation: You only warn him who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful in the unseen; so give him glad tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.
interpretation: The warning of the Prophet is beneficial only to the one whose heart accepts the Qur’an’s reminder and who lives with sincere awe of Allah even when no one sees him. This fear is not outward display but inward faithfulness to the unseen reality of God. To such a person, the glad tidings are that Allah will forgive his shortcomings and grant him an honorable, generous reward in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life to the dead, and We record what they have sent ahead and their traces. And We have enumerated all things in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse establishes that resurrection is solely by God’s power and that His record extends beyond isolated deeds to include every consequence, influence, and trace a person leaves behind. It teaches that human responsibility is not limited to actions performed directly but also includes their continuing effects in the world, all of which are precisely preserved in God’s clear, all-encompassing register. Thus, divine justice is complete: nothing is lost, omitted, or forgotten, and every legacy—good or evil—will be accounted for.

translation: And set forth to them a parable: the people of the town, when the messengers came to it.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet to present the account of the town as an instructive mirror for his own people. It establishes that God does not leave a community without warning; He sends messengers as a mercy and a proof, so that rejection becomes a conscious choice. The arrival of the messengers to that town marks the moment of divine testing, and the verse prepares the disbelievers of Mecca to see their own rejection of the Prophet reflected in the story, while consoling him that earlier messengers were also met with denial.

translation: When We sent to them two, but they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, 'Indeed, we are messengers to you.'
interpretation: This verse conveys that divine guidance often comes through successive messengers whose truthfulness is confirmed and reinforced by God; when the first two were rejected, God increased the evidence and authority with a third, so that the united testimony of all three became a decisive declaration that they were commissioned by God to call the people to Him. It teaches that rejection of one messenger does not nullify the mission, and that God may strengthen His cause through additional witnesses, leaving the recipients accountable for responding to the clear, reiterated message.

translation: They said, "You are only human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not sent down anything. You are only lying."
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbelievers’ false criterion for prophethood: they measured the messengers by their own human nature and assumed that divine guidance could not come through people like themselves. Their denial that the Most Merciful had revealed anything was not founded on proof but on arrogance and a refusal to accept that God may choose human messengers. By calling the messengers liars, they rejected the truth simply because its bearers were not angels or beings of superior worldly status. The verse warns that rejecting revelation on such grounds leads a person to dismiss God’s mercy and to accuse His truthful messengers of falsehood.

translation: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you."
interpretation: The messengers appeal to God’s own knowledge as the decisive witness to their truthfulness. They do not present themselves as self-appointed speakers, but as ones commissioned by Him; since He knows their inner intention and His sending of them, His testimony is enough against the people’s denial. This expresses their firm confidence in the mission and their reliance on God when human proof is rejected, leaving them responsible only to convey the message clearly.

translation: And we are not responsible except for clear conveyance.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the messenger’s duty is limited to delivering God’s message plainly and unmistakably. It does not include forcing belief, controlling hearts, or guaranteeing acceptance. Guidance belongs to God alone, and the messenger is only accountable for faithfully and clearly conveying what was revealed; the response of the audience rests with God, who guides whom He wills and holds people accountable for how they receive the message.

translation: They said, "Indeed, we consider you an evil omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment from us will surely touch you."
interpretation: This verse exposes the mindset of those who reject divine guidance: instead of responding to the messengers’ call with reflection, they blame the messengers for their own unease and impending ruin, calling them bad omens. Their threat to stone them and inflict a painful punishment reveals how hardened disbelief turns into hostility and persecution against the truthful. It teaches that rejecting God’s message and persecuting His messengers does not avert consequences; rather, it brings down the very punishment they threatened others with, for God defends His faithful servants and holds oppressors accountable.

translation: They said, "Your omen is with you. Is it because you have been reminded? Rather, you are a people who exceed all bounds."
interpretation: The messengers reject the people's superstition that the messengers themselves bring misfortune. Any evil omen or harm is tied to the people's own selves—their choices, denial, and sins—not to those who deliver God's reminder. The warning does not create evil; it exposes a heart already inclined to reject the truth. Their hostile reaction shows that the real problem is their israf: exceeding the limits God set, rebelling against guidance, and answering admonition with threats and arrogance. Thus the verse teaches that blaming others for one's spiritual ruin is self-deception; the consequence of rejecting divine reminders returns upon the rejecter.

translation: And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, hastening. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers."
interpretation: This verse portrays the moral courage of a sincere believer who, despite living on the margins of his society, rushes to defend the truth and calls his people to obey the messengers of God. It teaches that guidance is not confined to the powerful or prominent; a person of lesser status can be the one who recognizes God's message, and that true concern for one's people is shown by inviting them to follow divine guidance before it is too late.

translation: Follow those who ask no reward of you, and who are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse directs people to follow the callers to God whose sincerity is evident: they seek no worldly payment, wealth, or status from those they invite, so their message is not driven by selfish gain. Because they themselves are firmly upon true guidance, accepting their call is the way to right guidance and salvation.

translation: And why should I not worship the One who created me, and to Him you will be returned?
interpretation: This is the believing man’s argument for sincere worship of Allah alone: the One who originated and created him is the only One deserving of worship, so there is no valid reason to refuse Him. The verse also places that worship in the context of final accountability—everyone will return to Allah after death—so devotion to Him is grounded in gratitude, purpose, and the certainty of resurrection and judgment.

translation: Should I take besides Him gods? If the Most Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me.
interpretation: This verse establishes that worship, reliance, and the hope for benefit or protection must be directed to God alone. Any presumed deity or intercessor besides Him has no independent power to ward off harm or bring benefit; if God wills a hardship, no created being can prevent it or deliver from it. Therefore, taking others as gods is futile, because ultimate authority over good and harm belongs exclusively to God, and no one can intercede or rescue against His decree except by His permission.

translation: Indeed, I would then be in manifest error.
interpretation: It means: If I were to worship others besides God—after He created me and to Him I will return—I would be in clear, obvious misguidance, because those alleged gods can neither bring benefit nor avert harm, nor rescue me. The verse exposes the irrationality of associating partners with God and confirms that such worship is a manifest deviation from the truth.

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.
interpretation: This is the declaration of the believing man who calls his people to heed the messengers and abandon false gods. He announces that he has committed himself in faith to the Lord who sent those messengers—the one true Lord, Creator and Sustainer—and he asks his people to listen to his testimony and take it seriously. It expresses personal conviction, public commitment to monotheism, and an urgent appeal for them to accept the truth he has embraced.

translation: It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "Oh, I wish my people knew."
interpretation: This expresses the believer’s profound compassion and selfless concern even after being granted Paradise: he does not rejoice in his own salvation while indifferent to others, but longs for his people to know the truth of God’s mercy and reward, so that they too might believe and attain the same good end.

translation: That my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored.
interpretation: This is the believing man’s joyful testimony that God’s forgiveness has cleansed him and that God has raised him to a station of honor; he utters it out of longing that his people might come to know the same mercy and be guided to faith.

translation: And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor would We ever send down.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God's punishment and decree are not dependent on descending armies or visible heavenly forces; His command alone is sufficient. It rejects the idea that divine vengeance requires hosts from the sky, showing that God is self-sufficient and omnipotent, able to bring about the destruction or reformation of a people without any external means.

translation: It was nothing but a single shout, and immediately they were extinguished.
interpretation: This signifies that Allah’s decree is so overwhelming that a single command or blast suffices to reduce a defiant people to complete stillness and ruin; no worldly strength, numbers, or defenses can resist it, and their end comes suddenly, leaving them as lifeless and silent as a fire that has died out.

translation: Alas for the servants! There never came to them a messenger except that they mocked him.
interpretation: This verse expresses divine sorrow and a stern warning over the tragic state of those who habitually reject and ridicule Allah’s messengers. Their mockery is not a sign that the messengers failed, but evidence of the people’s arrogance and heedlessness. The regret will be theirs when the consequences of their rejection become clear, for they turned away from every call to truth and met it with contempt rather than reflection.

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them—that they will not return to them?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith, calling them to reflect on the fate of earlier nations destroyed by God for their corruption and denial. Those destroyed generations are gone forever and cannot return to the living; their extinction is a sign of God’s power and justice. The present rejecters are therefore not safe from a similar punishment if they persist, and the ruins of history should move them to humility, repentance, and awareness that every people will be held accountable.

translation: And indeed, all of them will surely be brought before Us together.
interpretation: This verse affirms the certainty and universality of the resurrection and the gathering for judgment. It teaches that every created being—past, present, and future—will be made present before God, without exception or escape. No one will be absent, overlooked, or able to avoid accountability. This underscores God's absolute sovereignty, perfect justice, and complete knowledge, and it calls the individual to live with awareness that they will ultimately stand before their Lord.

translation: And a sign for them is the dead earth: We revive it and bring forth from it grain, and from it they eat.
interpretation: This verse presents the revival of barren, lifeless land by rain and its production of grain as clear evidence of God's power to give life after death. Just as He can bring a dead earth back to life and make it yield food for people, He is able to resurrect the dead for judgment. It also subtly calls people to recognize His provision with gratitude, since the grain they eat is not of their own making but a direct sign of His mercy and creative authority.

translation: And We made therein gardens of date palms and grapevines, and We caused springs to gush forth therein.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of God’s power and bounty: after describing the dead, barren earth, He revives it by producing orchards of date palms and grapes and by making water spring up from within it. The pairing of trees and springs shows that life depends on His provision, and the transformation of dry land into fruitful gardens is a sign of His ability to bring the dead back to life. It also calls people to recognize these visible blessings as proofs of the Creator’s oneness, gratitude, and the reality of resurrection.

translation: That they may eat of its fruit, and their hands did not make it. Will they not then give thanks?
interpretation: The verse teaches that the gardens, springs, and fruits are God’s creation and provision, not something human hands originated or brought into being by their own power. People may cultivate and benefit from them, but their labor is only a means; the real creation, sustenance, and blessing are from God alone. The closing question, “Will they not then give thanks?” calls people to recognize this favor and respond with gratitude, worship, and obedience to the One who provides.

translation: Glory be to the One who created all pairs—from what the earth grows, and from among themselves, and from what they do not know.
interpretation: This verse declares God’s absolute transcendence and creative power: He alone originated every kind of pairing and complementary counterpart in creation. The mention of vegetation, human beings, and things beyond human knowledge shows that duality, complementarity, and reproduction are universal signs of His wise ordering of the world, while also acknowledging that human knowledge cannot encompass all the forms of creation He has made.

translation: And a sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it, and at once they are in darkness.
interpretation: The verse points to the night as a manifest sign of Allah’s exclusive power and governance over creation. The Arabic expression “We strip the day from it” conveys that daylight is removed from the night like a covering being peeled away, so darkness follows by Allah’s command. This regular, precise transformation testifies that the One who controls light and darkness is able to bring about resurrection and reckoning, and it calls the heedless to reflect on their dependence on Him and on the possibility of losing His blessings.

translation: And the sun runs on its course to a resting place appointed for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The sun’s motion is described as proceeding under God’s command toward a fixed, appointed destination known only to Him. Its constant, ordered journey is not random or self-directed but is governed by divine decree, showing the power and all-encompassing knowledge of the Almighty who regulates all creation with perfect precision.

translation: And the moon — We have determined for it phases, until it returns like the old dried date-stalk.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah has ordained the moon’s stages with precise measure: it waxes and wanes through appointed phases until it becomes thin, curved, and pale like an old dried date-stalk. It demonstrates divine control over the heavens, the moon’s orderly submission to Allah’s decree, and His power to bring creation back after it has worn away.

translation: The sun is not to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; and each is floating in an orbit.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the movements of the sun, moon, night, and day are governed by Allah’s precise decree, not by chance or disorder. The sun cannot encroach upon the moon’s course, nor can night overtake day’s appointed time; rather, every celestial body travels in its fixed orbit in continuous submission to its Creator. This orderly cosmic motion is a sign of divine power, wisdom, and control, and it points to the certainty that the One who sustains such precise laws can also bring about resurrection and final reckoning.

translation: And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse points to the ark of Noah as a clear sign of God’s power, mercy, and care: when the flood destroyed the corrupt, God preserved the human line by carrying their ancestors in a ship loaded with people, animals, and provisions. It reminds people that their very existence descends from those saved by God, and that the One who can save life in a laden vessel is fully able to raise the dead and hold every soul accountable.

translation: And We created for them, from the like thereof, that which they ride.
interpretation: This verse reminds people that Allah, who carried their forefathers in the laden ark, also created for them vessels and mounts of a similar kind—ships, riding animals, and other means of transport—so that they may travel, carry goods, and reach distant places. It is a sign of His continuing mercy, provision, and power, and it calls them to acknowledge His favor and be grateful.

translation: And if We will, We drown them; then they will have no one to cry to for help, nor will they be rescued.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah’s power over His servants is absolute: if He wills, He can sink them in the sea, and at that moment no helper, intercessor, or rescuer can avail them. It warns that the very means of travel and safety people rely on are themselves subject to Allah’s command; deliverance from peril is not owed to human strength or technology but is granted solely by His mercy. Thus it calls the heedless to humility, gratitude, and reliance upon the One who alone can save or destroy.

translation: except as a mercy from Us and an enjoyment for a while.
interpretation: This verse teaches that whatever rescue, relief, or continued enjoyment people experience is not owed to them by right, but is granted solely out of God’s mercy and as a temporary provision until an appointed time. It directs the heart away from relying on worldly security and toward recognizing that every moment of ease is a divine gift meant for gratitude, repentance, and preparation for the eternal life.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Fear what is before you and what is behind you, so that you may receive mercy.'
interpretation: This verse reproaches those who ignore divine warnings. They are called to guard themselves against the consequences of what lies ahead in this life and the Hereafter, and what lies behind them in the fate of earlier nations and their own past deeds. If they take heed, repent, and obey God, they may attain His mercy; taqwa is therefore presented as the path to divine compassion.

translation: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse censures those who meet every divine proof, revelation, or portent with indifference and rejection. It shows that their problem is not a shortage of evidence but a settled habit of turning away: whenever a sign from their Lord reaches them, they avoid it, refuse to consider it, and persist in their own ways. The verse thus warns against heedlessness and stubborn rejection of guidance, and it invites the listener to receive God's signs with attentiveness, reflection, and acceptance rather than turning aside.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Spend out of that which Allah has provided you,' those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Should we feed one whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed? You are not but in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbelievers' evasion of the duty to give charity from God's provision. When called to spend in God's way, they reply with a fatalistic argument: if God had wished, He would have fed the poor, so why should we? Their words are not sincere submission to divine decree but a pretext for stinginess and a mockery of the believers. God's will that He can feed whom He wills does not abolish human accountability; He tests people with wealth and commands the wealthy to help the needy. Their accusation that the believers are in manifest error is itself the real misguidance, for they reject the clear moral obligation, belittle faith, and use God's decree to justify neglect and arrogance.

translation: And they say, "When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?"
interpretation: This is a mockingly impatient challenge from the deniers, asking when the promised resurrection, judgment, and punishment will occur, as if its delay disproves the truth. The verse exposes their disbelief and arrogance: the promise is real and fixed in God's knowledge, but it will come at its appointed time, and their demand will not hasten it. When it arrives, they will see the truth and be held accountable, while the truthful are vindicated.

translation: They do not await anything but a single blast that will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: This means the promised Hour will not be delayed further or preceded by any warning they can use to prepare; it will strike them suddenly with one overwhelming blast, catching them in the midst of their arguments and worldly preoccupations. They will have no time to repent, settle their affairs, or prepare for judgment. The verse thus emphasizes the unexpectedness and inescapability of the resurrection and the final reckoning, which overtake people while they are heedless and disputing.

translation: So they will not be able to make a will, nor to their families will they return.
interpretation: This verse describes the suddenness and overwhelming force of the Hour’s punishment: it seizes people all at once, leaving them no time to settle their affairs, leave final instructions, or go back to their households. All worldly ties and plans are instantly cut off.

translation: And the Horn will be blown; then behold, they will rush out from the graves to their Lord.
interpretation: This verse affirms the reality of the resurrection: at the blowing of the Horn, the dead emerge from their graves and move swiftly toward their Lord, answering His summons for judgment, with no delay or escape.

translation: They will say, "Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place?" This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth.
interpretation: This verse depicts the shock and remorse of the deniers at the moment of resurrection, when they are raised from their graves as if awakened from sleep and cry out in despair. Their own words then affirm that the promise of Allah, the Most Merciful, has come true and that the messengers He sent were truthful. It emphasizes that resurrection is an inescapable reality, that divine warning is an expression of mercy, and that rejecting the prophets does not make the hereafter any less certain. The verse also shows that at that moment, the truth they denied becomes undeniable, and their former arguments and arrogance collapse before the reality of Allah’s promise.

translation: It was but a single blast, and behold, they are all brought before Us.
interpretation: This verse affirms the certainty and ease of the resurrection: by one commanding blast from Allah, all people of every generation are instantly restored to life and made present before Him for judgment. It emphasizes that no one can escape this gathering, and that Allah’s power is such that a single summons suffices to bring all creation to account.

translation: So this Day no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God’s judgment is perfectly just: no person will suffer the slightest injustice, and every reward or punishment will correspond exactly to the deeds each person freely chose and performed in worldly life. No one will be held accountable for another’s actions, nor will any good or evil be overlooked or misweighed; the only basis for recompense will be one’s own intentions and deeds.

translation: Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are occupied in joyful delight.
interpretation: This verse describes the people of Paradise on the Day of Judgment as being completely absorbed in the joys and pleasures Allah has prepared for them. Their occupation is not a burden or toil but pure enjoyment; they are delighted, at ease, and free from every sorrow, worry, and hardship. It points to the perfection and permanence of the bliss of Paradise.

translation: They and their spouses will be in shades, reclining on couches.
interpretation: This signifies the perfect bliss of Paradise: God grants the righteous the companionship of spouses who share their joy, surrounds them with cool shade that removes every trace of hardship, and lets them recline upon elevated couches in complete rest and honor. It conveys security, intimacy, dignity, and relief from all toil, as a reward for faith and patience.

translation: They will have therein fruits, and they will have whatever they call for.
interpretation: The people of Paradise are granted both delightful fruits and the complete fulfillment of every request, wish, or desire they express. Nothing they seek will be denied, and this signifies perfect contentment, honor, and generosity in the eternal abode.

translation: Peace — a word from a Merciful Lord.
interpretation: This verse means that the people of Paradise will be addressed by their Lord Himself with the word of peace, a greeting of honor, security, and divine pleasure that comes directly from the Most Merciful; it is the ultimate declaration that they are safe from every fear, sorrow, and punishment, and that God is pleased with them.

translation: And separate yourselves this Day, O criminals!
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who persisted in disbelief and sin are commanded to be set apart from the believers and from God’s mercy. The address is one of rebuke and final exclusion: after the righteous are admitted to Paradise, the guilty are isolated for punishment, and their state is made clear before all. "O criminals" refers to those whose rejection of faith and evil deeds earned them this separation, and "today" stresses that this division is decisive and irreversible.

translation: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you.
interpretation: Allah addresses all humanity with a reproachful reminder that He had already commanded them, through revelation and the innate covenant, to refuse servitude to Satan. 'Worship' here means willing obedience and submission to his whispers, not merely ritual devotion. Since Satan's hostility and deceptive intent are manifest, obeying him is a betrayal of one's own Creator and a self-destructive choice; the verse establishes human accountability because the warning and the clear enmity were made known.

translation: And that you worship Me; this is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse means that God alone deserves to be worshipped, and that devoting worship to Him alone is the straight path—the unwavering way of truth that leads to Him. It identifies pure monotheism as the path of salvation, in contrast to following Satan, and calls people to make their entire lives an act of devotion to God.

translation: And he had already led astray a great many of you; did you not then reason?
interpretation: The verse is a rebuke to those who follow Iblis: Satan's deception is not a new or hidden matter, for he has already misled countless people before them. The question 'did you not reason?' means that God has given humans the intellect to recognize an open enemy, to learn from the ruin of earlier generations, and to distinguish between the one who calls to truth and the one who only lures toward destruction. To continue in his path is therefore not a failure of information but a failure to use the reason God entrusted to them, and it exposes that their allegiance to Satan was chosen against clear evidence.

translation: This is Hell, which you were promised.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers are addressed with rebuke: the Hellfire they were warned about and threatened with as punishment for their denial is now present before them, no longer a mere warning but a reality they must face.

translation: Burn in it today because you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This is a direct divine sentence upon those who persistently rejected faith: the Fire is not an arbitrary punishment but the inevitable consequence of their own chosen disbelief. The word “today” marks the moment of recompense after judgment, when denial can no longer be hidden or reversed, and the phrase “because you used to disbelieve” shows that their suffering is tied directly to the disbelief they cultivated in worldly life.

translation: This Day We shall seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will prevent the guilty from verbally denying their deeds, making all excuses useless. Their own hands and feet will testify by His command to what they did in the world, showing that every action is fully known and recorded. This establishes perfect justice: no one can conceal or distort the truth, and every person will be held accountable for what they chose to earn. It also displays God's absolute authority over His creation, as even the body's members submit to Him and speak as witnesses.

translation: And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, so they would race to the path; then how could they see?
interpretation: This is a declaration of God's absolute power over human faculties and guidance. If He willed, He could instantly efface the sight of those who reject Him, leaving them able to run toward the straight path but unable to find or perceive it. It warns that the ability to see, both physically and spiritually, is a gift from God, and that no one can guide themselves or escape His decree if He removes that gift. It also exposes the futility of their striving after guidance while persisting in denial, since true insight comes only from God.

translation: And if We willed, We could have transformed them in their places, so they would be unable to move forward or return.
interpretation: This verse affirms God's absolute power over His creation: if He wished, He could instantly alter the very form or condition of those who persist in denial, leaving them fixed where they stand, incapable of advancing toward any goal or retreating to safety. It warns that human movement, ability, and escape all depend entirely on God's will, and that His punishment can overtake anyone at any moment without possibility of resistance or return.

translation: And whoever We grant long life, We cause him to regress in creation. Will they not then reason?
interpretation: This verse points to aging as a reversal in the human constitution: the strength, faculties, and vigor of youth decline, and a person returns to weakness and dependence, much as they began. It is a sign of Allah's absolute control over life and death, a reminder that worldly power, beauty, and longevity do not last, and a call to reflect that the One who can reverse creation can also raise the dead. Those who witness this should use their reason, humble themselves before their Creator, and prepare for the Hereafter rather than cling to the temporary life of this world.

translation: And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. It is nothing but a Reminder and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: The verse repudiates the claim that the Prophet was a poet or that the Qur'an was poetry. God declares that He did not train him in poetry and that poetic composition is not suited to his prophetic mission. What was revealed to him is not a human literary artifact but dhikr—a reminder that awakens hearts to God—and a clear, manifest Qur'an whose guidance and truth are evident. Thus the verse establishes the revealed book's transcendent origin and the Prophet's role as a warner and reciter of divine guidance, not a poet crafting verses.

translation: That he may warn whoever is alive and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Qur’an’s warning benefits only those whose hearts are spiritually alive and willing to hear the truth, while the divine decree of punishment is deservedly carried out against those who knowingly persist in disbelief and rejection.

translation: Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners?
interpretation: This verse calls people to reflect on God’s direct creative power and His generous provision. The livestock they possess and benefit from were not created by themselves or by any idol; God alone brought them into being and subjected them to human use. The expression “what Our hands have made” affirms God’s exclusive authorship of creation and His special care in forming these creatures, not any physical likeness to Him. Human “ownership” of livestock is therefore a granted trust, not an independent right, and it should awaken gratitude, humility, and acknowledgment of the Creator’s sovereignty. The verse also serves as a sign of God’s ability to create and sustain life, and thus of His power to resurrect, while exposing the ingratitude of those who deny Him despite the plain blessings they handle every day.

translation: And We have subjected them to them, so from them is their riding, and from them they eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's favor in making livestock and similar creatures submissive and serviceable to humankind. Their usefulness for riding and food is a sign of divine power, mercy, and provision, not merely a result of human effort. It invites gratitude to God, responsible use of His blessings, and acknowledgment of the Creator who alone subjected creation for human benefit.

translation: And they have therein benefits and drinks. Will they not then give thanks?
interpretation: This verse points to the many uses and nourishing drinks people derive from the livestock God has subjected to them, such as milk, riding, wool, hides, and other provisions. The rhetorical question “Will they not then give thanks?” rebukes human heedlessness and calls people to recognize these daily favors as coming from Allah alone. True gratitude here means acknowledging the Provider, using His blessings in ways He permits, and worshiping Him without associating partners with Him.

translation: And they have taken besides Allah gods, that perhaps they might be helped.
interpretation: This verse condemns the polytheists’ practice of adopting false deities besides Allah in the hope that those deities would grant them victory, support, or intercession. Their expectation is utterly misplaced, because no created being has any power to help or harm independently of Allah. The verse therefore exposes the futility of associating partners with Him and affirms that all aid, protection, and victory belong to Allah alone.

translation: They cannot help them, and they are a host brought before them.
interpretation: This verse exposes the utter helplessness of false deities: they have no power to aid or defend those who worship them. On the Day of Judgment, both the idols and their worshippers will be gathered and presented together, the worshippers appearing as a host mustered around them, yet without any benefit or intercession. It teaches that reliance on anything besides Allah is futile, and that all created things will be brought before Allah, utterly subject to His judgment.

translation: So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and every believer against the pain caused by the words of opponents and deniers. It teaches that human speech, whether hidden in the heart or spoken openly, is fully encompassed by God’s knowledge. Therefore, no plot, mockery, or false claim escapes His awareness, and He will bring every secret and public matter to its just consequence. The believer’s duty is not to be crushed by what people say, but to trust that God sees the full reality and will vindicate truth in His perfect wisdom and timing.

translation: Does man not see that We created him from a sperm-drop, and yet he is an open adversary?
interpretation: This verse rebukes the human being who argues against God and denies the resurrection. It reminds him that his origin is from a tiny, insignificant sperm-drop, yet he becomes a clear, outspoken opponent and disputant. The One who created him from such a humble beginning is fully able to bring him back to life after death.

translation: And he struck for Us a similitude and forgot his creation. He said, “Who will revive the bones while they are decayed?”
interpretation: The verse exposes the inconsistency of denying resurrection by citing decomposed bones: the questioner treats physical disintegration as a conclusive proof against revival, yet he has forgotten the greater wonder of his own origination. The One who originated human life from nothing and formed him from a mere drop is fully able to reconstitute bones and restore life after decay. The verse thus asserts God’s absolute power over creation and resurrection, and it identifies forgetfulness of one’s own creation as the root of the doubt.

translation: Say, 'He will give them life who created them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse answers the one who denies resurrection by treating it as impossible. The One who brought creation into existence initially, without any prior model, is fully able to bring it back after death. The mention of the first creation is an argument from the lesser to the greater: if God originated life from nothing, restoring decomposed bodies is not difficult for Him. The closing phrase affirms that His knowledge encompasses every created thing—nothing about their bodies, souls, or condition is hidden from Him—so He can gather and recreate them with perfect precision. Thus the verse establishes resurrection through both God's creative power and His all-encompassing knowledge.

translation: He who has made for you fire from the green tree, and then from it you kindle.
interpretation: This is a proof of God's power to resurrect: He brings forth fire—hot and dry—from a tree that is moist and green, contrary to its natural property, showing that He is able to bring life out of the dead and gather scattered bones.

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes indeed, and He is the All-Knowing Creator.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical affirmation of God’s unlimited power, especially His ability to resurrect and recreate human beings after death. If He originated the vast heavens and earth from nothing, then recreating people like them is not difficult for Him. The emphatic answer “Yes indeed” removes any doubt, and the names “the All-Knowing Creator” show that He knows every detail of His creation and continually creates as He wills.

translation: His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God's creative will is absolutely effective and unimpeded: He does not need means, helpers, effort, or time to bring anything into existence. When He decrees something, His mere command 'Be' immediately brings it into being, demonstrating His complete power, sovereignty, and freedom from any limitation. It assures that whatever He wills—whether creation, sustenance, resurrection, or judgment—will certainly occur exactly as He intends.

translation: So glory be to the One in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse declares God’s absolute transcendence and sovereign ownership over the whole creation: every realm, authority, and affair is wholly in His hand, and no creature possesses any dominion independently of Him. It also affirms that all beings will ultimately return to Him, meaning that human beings will be brought back to their Lord for accountability and recompense; therefore worship, reliance, and hope belong to Him alone.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful: By those lined up in ranks.
interpretation: This is an oath by the angels who stand in ordered rows before Allah, fully obedient and prepared to carry out His commands; it points to perfect discipline, humility, and readiness in worship and service.

translation: And by those who drive away with a driving.
interpretation: They are the angels whom Allah has appointed to drive the clouds by His command, moving them forcefully to where He wills so that rain may fall. Their driving is a powerful, effective driving, like driving a herd with a stern command.

translation: And by those who recite the Reminder
interpretation: These are the angels who recite Allah’s remembrance and revealed message, continuously engaged in dhikr and conveying divine revelation; Allah swears by them to highlight the sanctity of His remembrance and the truth of what is revealed.

translation: Indeed, your God is One.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute oneness of God: He alone is the true deity worthy of worship, without any partner, equal, or plurality in His essence, attributes, or authority.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the places of sunrise/easts.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the Rabb—the Creator, Owner, Sustainer, and Disposer of all affairs—of the heavens and the earth, of every created thing between them, and of the easts, i.e., the points and times from which the sun rises. By mentioning the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between, it declares His absolute lordship over the entire creation, visible and invisible, high and low. By specifying the mashariq (places of sunrise) in the plural, it points to His precise control over the sun, its rising, the seasons, time, and the directions, and by implication over all cosmic movements and all that depends on them. Thus, the One who governs such vast creations is the only One worthy of worship, obedience, and reliance.

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the adornment of the stars.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the starry sky is a visible sign of Allah’s creative power, wisdom, and generosity: He made the nearest heaven beautiful with stars, so their light, order, and placement inspire wonder, serve as guidance, and testify that the universe is intentionally fashioned and sustained by its Creator alone.

translation: And as a protection against every rebellious devil.
