It exposes how deeply polytheism had settled into their minds, so that worshiping the One God seemed astonishing to them. The verse thus highlights the core of the prophetic message—that there is no deity but God—and shows that rejecting it merely because it is unfamiliar is a sign of heedlessness, not a valid argument.

translation: And the leaders among them set out, [saying], “Go on and remain steadfast to your gods. Indeed, this is a thing intended.”
interpretation: The influential elite of the disbelievers, after hearing the call to pure monotheism, urged one another to persist in idol worship and not yield to the Prophet. They claimed his message was not divine truth but a calculated plan to gain authority and allegiance, so they treated it as a matter to be resisted by clinging steadfastly to their inherited gods. The verse exposes their arrogance, their collusion in falsehood, and their hardening of hearts against the truth.

translation: We have not heard of this in the last religion. This is nothing but a fabrication.
interpretation: This is a statement of the disbelievers who rejected the Prophet's call to worship Allah alone. They argued that such pure monotheism was unheard of in the last religion they recognized—whether Christianity or the religion of their forefathers—and thus dismissed it as an invented lie. Their claim was not based on knowledge but on blind imitation of ancestral ways and ignorance of the true teachings of previous prophets. The verse exposes their stubborn denial and the weakness of their argument, as they rejected the truth simply because it contradicted their inherited polytheism.

translation: Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us? Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder. Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the arrogant rejecters who objected to revelation coming to a man from among them rather than to their own notables; their objection was not based on proof but on doubt concerning Allah's reminder, and they continued in denial because they had not yet experienced the punishment that would force them to recognize the truth.

translation: Or do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke to those who reject God's choice of prophethood and revelation. It asks whether they control the storehouses of God's mercy—such as prophethood, guidance, provision, and forgiveness—so that they could apportion or withhold them as they wish. Since they possess no such authority, their objections are baseless. Mercy belongs to God alone; He is Al-Aziz, the Almighty whose wisdom and power are perfect, and Al-Wahhab, the Bestower who grants His favors freely to whom He wills.

translation: Or do they possess the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them? Then let them ascend by the means.
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who deny the Prophet and reject Allah’s authority: if they truly own or control the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them, then let them climb up by the paths, ropes, or means that lead to the heavens and manage them as they claim. In reality, they have no such dominion and no such access. The verse establishes that all sovereignty belongs exclusively to Allah, and it exposes the helplessness of His creatures: they cannot ascend to the heavens, control its affairs, or prevent Allah’s decree, revelation, and disposal of all matters.

translation: An army there, defeated, from among the confederates.
interpretation: This verse declares that the gathered forces opposing the Prophet are already a defeated host, despite their numbers and alliance. The word “there” points to their inevitable humiliation and rout, while “the confederates” evokes earlier factions that united against the messengers of God and were likewise overcome. Its meaning is that power and unity built upon rejection of divine guidance cannot endure, and that God’s promise of victory for truth and defeat for its enemies is certain.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah, 'Ad, and Pharaoh, the possessor of stakes, denied.
interpretation: This verse places the Prophet's experience of rejection within a recurring pattern: earlier nations—Noah's people, 'Ad, and Pharaoh, whose 'stakes' denote his vast tyrannical power and torture—also denied their messengers. It therefore warns that might, wealth, and dominion cannot shield a people from God's judgment, and it consoles the faithful that opposition is not evidence of falsehood but a test that has befallen earlier communities as well.

translation: And Thamud, and the people of Lot, and the companions of the Thicket — those were the confederates.
interpretation: These earlier nations are named together as “the confederates” because they shared the same stance: they banded together in rejecting their messengers and opposing the truth. Mentioning them here serves as a warning to the Prophet’s opponents that their alliance against revelation is not new, and that such coalitions of denial ultimately do not prevail against God’s decree.

translation: Every one of them denied the messengers, so the punishment became due.
interpretation: This verse states that the communities cited earlier were not merely guilty of isolated sins; their common defining crime was rejecting the messengers sent to them. That rejection was not an innocent disagreement but a defiance of God's guidance, and it therefore made the threatened punishment justly deserved and unavoidable. The verse thus establishes a universal principle: when a people reject divine messengers, their ruin is not arbitrary but the just consequence of their own denial.

translation: And these [disbelievers] await not but one blast [of the Trumpet]; there will be no delay for it.
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers that they are only waiting for the single blast of the Trumpet that will announce the Hour and bring about their punishment. When it comes, it will not be delayed, postponed, or have any interval or respite. It stresses the certainty and suddenness of the Day of Judgment, and that once the command of Allah comes, no one can hold it back or escape it. It is a call to take heed before that inevitable moment.

translation: And they say, 'Our Lord, hasten to us our portion before the Day of Reckoning.'
interpretation: This is a mocking challenge from the deniers: they demand that their allotted punishment or the warned consequence be brought upon them at once, not out of faith or submission, but to test and belittle the warning. It exposes their rejection of the Day of Reckoning and their arrogance toward the Messenger, for instead of seeking mercy and preparing for accountability, they rashly ask for what would destroy them.

translation: Be patient over what they say, and remember Our servant David, possessor of strength. Indeed, he was ever returning [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad—and every believer—to endure patiently the harmful words and accusations of others, and it points to David as a model: his true strength was not merely physical or worldly, but a firm resolve in worship, obedience, and repentance. The title “ever returning” means he constantly turned back to Allah, sought His forgiveness, and renewed his devotion, so patience under opposition is sustained by a heart that repeatedly returns to God.

translation: Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with him in the evening and at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah made the mountains join Prophet David in praising and glorifying Him at the time of evening and at sunrise, demonstrating His power and the honor bestowed upon David, and showing that even inanimate creation submits to Allah’s command and participates in His remembrance.

translation: And the birds gathered, all obedient to him.
interpretation: This verse describes how God assembled the birds and made them subservient to Prophet David, so that they joined him in glorifying God. Each one returned to his call in obedience, harmonizing with him in praise of its Lord.

translation: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.
interpretation: This means that God granted Prophet David a firmly established and mighty dominion, supported him with authority and victory, and bestowed upon him two great gifts: wisdom—including sound understanding, prophethood, and right judgment—and the ability to speak with clarity and finality, so that he could distinguish truth from falsehood, settle disputes, and judge justly with persuasive, decisive words.

translation: And has there come to you the news of the litigants, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer chamber?
interpretation: The rhetorical question is not asking for information but is meant to heighten attention to an astonishing event and its lesson: two disputants breached the privacy of David’s place of worship by climbing in unexpectedly, turning his intimate sanctuary into the setting of a moral and spiritual test. It teaches that even a prophet and judge must not decide hastily, that access to judgment requires restraint and listening, and that awareness of God’s presence should produce humility, self-examination, and repentance.

translation: When they entered upon David, and he was alarmed by them. They said, 'Do not fear. We are two litigants, one of whom has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not be unjust, and guide us to the straight path.'
interpretation: This verse conveys that disputes must be resolved by truth and justice, not by partiality or intimidation. The two litigants come to Prophet David acknowledging that one has transgressed against the other and asking for a fair ruling. Their words 'judge between us with truth and do not be unjust, and guide us to the straight path' mean that the judge must base his decision on the truth, avoid deviation or favoritism, and lead the disputants to the correct and balanced resolution. It also shows that seeking justice is part of guidance to the straight path, and that a ruler or judge must not let fear or personal reaction prevent him from fulfilling that duty.

translation: Indeed, this my brother has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe; yet he says, 'Entrust it to me,' and he has overpowered me in speech.
interpretation: This verse depicts the injustice of greed and the abuse of power: one who already possesses abundance covets the single remaining possession of his weaker brother and demands it, using superior eloquence or status to overwhelm him. It condemns the oppression of the weak by the powerful and shows how speech can be misused to seize what is not rightfully one's own. In the context of David, it functions as a parable that exposes the gravity of desiring what belongs to another and leads him to recognize his own fault and turn in repentance.

translation: He said: “He has wronged you by asking to add your ewe to his ewes. And indeed, many partners/associates transgress against one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds—and how few they are.” And David thought that We had only tried him, so he sought forgiveness from his Lord and fell down bowing and turned back in repentance.
interpretation: This verse teaches that taking advantage of another’s need or weaker position to acquire what is rightfully theirs is a form of injustice, even if framed as a request. It then states a general truth about human associations: when people deal with one another without faith and righteous conduct, the stronger often wrongs the weaker; only those grounded in faith and good deeds are restrained from such injustice, and such people are few. David perceives the dispute as a divine test of his own judgment and heart, not merely a legal case between two men. His response is immediate humility: he seeks God’s forgiveness, bowing/prostrating before Him, and returns to Him repentantly. Thus the passage presents repentance and turning back to God as the proper response when one realizes a lapse or is tried by position, power, or judgment.

translation: So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah accepted the repentance of His servant David and erased the sin he had committed. It then affirms that David was not merely forgiven but was granted two great honors: closeness and favor with Allah, and an excellent final destination in the Hereafter. The verse thus shows that sincere repentance does not leave a person degraded; rather, Allah may restore him, draw him near, and give him a blessed end.

translation: O David, indeed We have made you a successor on the earth, so judge between the people with truth, and do not follow desire, lest it lead you astray from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: Allah addresses Prophet David as His appointed vicegerent on earth, meaning that authority to rule and judge is a trust from God, not an absolute right of the ruler. The command to judge with truth requires that decisions be based on divine guidance and objective justice, not on personal inclination, favoritism, pressure, or convenience. Desire is warned against because it blinds the heart and turns judgment away from God's path, causing rulers and people alike to mistake self-interest for right. The severe punishment for those who stray from God's way is tied to their forgetting the Day of Reckoning: when accountability before God is absent from conscience, injustice becomes easy and unrestrained. Therefore, the verse establishes that just governance depends on remembering the final judgment and submitting every judgment to God's revealed standard rather than to human whims.

translation: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and whatever is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve. So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.
interpretation: God affirms that the creation of the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them is not without purpose or truth; it is ordered toward a wise and just end. The notion that existence is meaningless or that God created it frivolously is a false assumption held by those who reject faith. Because they attribute futility to God's creation and deny the accountability that follows from His wisdom, they are warned of the punishment of the Fire.

translation: Or should We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who cause corruption in the earth? Or should We make the God-fearing like the wicked?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question whose answer is no: God’s justice does not equate faith and righteous deeds with corruption, nor piety with wickedness. It affirms that moral choices are real and that God will not treat the righteous and the corrupt as if they were the same; the two groups differ in His judgment and will have different outcomes.

translation: A blessed Book which We have revealed to you, so that they may reflect upon its verses and so that those of understanding may be reminded.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the Qur’an’s revelation is a source of blessing, and that its true benefit is attained through deliberate reflection on its verses. Such reflection is not merely intellectual curiosity; it is meant to lead the heart and mind to remembrance, admonition, and guidance. Those described as possessing understanding are the ones who allow the Book’s meanings to penetrate beyond surface recitation, drawing lessons that reshape belief, character, and conduct.

translation: And We granted to David Solomon—an excellent servant. Indeed, he was ever turning back to Allah.
interpretation: This verse presents Solomon as a gift from Allah to David and praises him as an excellent servant because his defining quality was being “awwāb”—one who continually returns to Allah in repentance, obedience, gratitude, and reliance. It teaches that true honor is not merely in prophethood, kingship, or knowledge, but in repeatedly turning back to one's Lord, and that a righteous child can be among the greatest gifts bestowed upon a parent.

translation: When the well-bred, swift steeds were presented before him in the late afternoon.
interpretation: This verse marks a moment of trial for Solomon: the finest and fastest horses of his kingdom were displayed before him, and their beauty and excellence became a test of whether his heart would be captured by worldly splendor or remain centered on the remembrance of God. It shows that even lawful blessings and royal gifts can distract a person from what is higher, and that true wisdom lies in recognizing the distraction and returning one’s devotion to the Lord.

translation: And he said, 'Indeed, I have loved the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord, until the sun disappeared behind the veil.'
interpretation: This verse means that Solomon was so absorbed in reviewing his fine horses—a worldly good—that he became distracted from the remembrance of God until the sun set and the time for prayer passed. He then acknowledged his negligence and turned back to God. It serves as a warning that even lawful pleasures must not lead one to neglect the remembrance of God.

translation: Return them to me. Then he began to pass his hand over their legs and necks.
interpretation: This verse portrays Prophet Solomon expressing deep admiration and tender care for the horses after they were brought back to him. By stroking their legs and necks, he acknowledges them as a gracious gift from God and demonstrates his gratitude and gentle stewardship over the blessings entrusted to him.

translation: And We certainly tried Solomon and cast upon his throne a body; then he returned [to Us in repentance].
interpretation: God tested Solomon by temporarily removing his kingship and allowing a jinn or false body to occupy his throne in his likeness, so that his authority was disrupted. This trial humbled him, and he turned back to God in repentance and supplication, after which God restored his kingdom.

translation: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."
interpretation: This verse records Prophet Solomon's supplication to God after his earlier trial: he seeks forgiveness for any shortcoming and asks for a unique sovereign dominion that would not be granted to anyone after him, not as a worldly boast but as a sign of God's favor and a means to establish justice, worship, and gratitude. By ending with God's name al-Wahhab, he acknowledges that every gift, especially kingship and forgiveness, comes solely from the One who gives without measure or obligation.

translation: So We subjected the wind to him, flowing gently by his command wherever he intended.
interpretation: This means that God made the wind obedient to Solomon as a miraculous gift: it moved softly and steadily at his command, without resistance or disorder, toward whatever destination he chose. It shows that the forces of nature are entirely under God’s control, and He grants mastery over them to whom He wills as a sign of His favor and power.

translation: And the devils—every builder and diver.
interpretation: God subjected the rebellious jinn to Solomon, so they served him in heavy labor such as constructing buildings and diving into the sea to bring up treasures. This shows God’s absolute authority over all creation and the special dominion He granted Solomon, making even defiant spirits obedient to his command.

translation: And others bound together in fetters.
interpretation: This refers to the rebellious jinn subjected to Solomon, held restrained in iron chains so that they could not act on their defiance or cause corruption, as part of the dominion God granted him.

translation: This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without account.
interpretation: The verse is a divine address to Solomon, granting him discretionary authority over the blessings God had given him—such as kingdom, wealth, power, and the subjugated forces. It means that what he possesses is purely God's gift, not something he earned or will be questioned about; therefore he is free to give from it or hold it back, and he is not held to account for how he distributes it. This demonstrates God's unbounded generosity and the special favor bestowed upon Solomon.

translation: And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good return.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the one referred to enjoys a special station of closeness to God and an excellent final destination in the Hereafter. It signifies divine pleasure, nearness, and a blessed end as a reward for sincere devotion, gratitude, and steadfastness in obedience to God.

translation: And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has afflicted me with hardship and torment."
interpretation: The verse teaches that Prophet Job, in the midst of severe suffering and loss, turned directly to Allah in supplication, tracing the distress and torment he felt to Satan’s influence—either through his whisperings that deepened his anguish, or through harm permitted by Allah as a trial. It shows that complaining to Allah alone is an act of humility and trust, not impatience, and that true patience does not mean denying pain but refusing to let it drive one away from reliance on God.

translation: Strike the ground with your foot. This is a cool washing-place and a drink.
interpretation: In its context, this is God’s command to Prophet Ayyub (Job) after prolonged illness and hardship. The spring that comes forth is a sign of divine mercy and healing: the cool water is for washing away his bodily ailment and for drinking to restore his strength. It signifies that relief, purification, and restoration come from God alone, and that His command carries both physical cure and spiritual comfort after patience and suffering.

translation: And We granted him his family and the like thereof with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for people of understanding.
interpretation: This means that after Ayyub’s severe trial, Allah restored his family to him and increased them with the like of them, as a gift of divine mercy rather than a human entitlement, and He made this restoration a lesson for those who possess sound reason: that patient endurance, trust in Allah, and steadfastness under hardship lead to relief and generous compensation, and that Allah’s mercy can surpass what people expect or calculate.

translation: And take in your hand a bundle [of twigs] and strike with it, and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient. Excellent is the servant. Indeed, he was ever turning back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse teaches that fulfilling an oath does not require causing unjust harm: Allah allowed Ayyub to strike with a bundle of twigs once, satisfying his vow while sparing his wife, and then praised him as patient, an excellent servant, and one who constantly returned to Allah in repentance and obedience.

translation: And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and insight.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet, and through him the believers, to recall and honor these chosen servants of God, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it identifies their distinguishing quality: they were people of steadfast ability and deep perception. Their “strength” means firmness and capability in worship, obedience, patience, and righteous action, while their “insight” means spiritual understanding, sound judgment, and discernment of God’s signs, truth, and guidance. They combined outward effort in God’s service with inward clarity of faith.

translation: Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Final Home.
interpretation: God made these chosen servants sincere and exclusively devoted through a heart cleansed of all mixed motives, so that the constant remembrance of the Hereafter was their purest characteristic. This mindfulness of the final abode shaped their intentions, detached them from the fleeting world, and directed all their labor toward God's pleasure and the reward of the everlasting Home.

translation: And indeed they, in Our sight, are among the chosen, the best.
interpretation: This means that these servants are, in God’s knowledge and estimation, among those He specially selected and purified for His closeness and service, and they are among the finest in virtue, sincerity, and excellence.

translation: And remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl; and all were among the best.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet and the believers to recall these prophets with reverence, not merely as names but as enduring examples of unwavering faith, patience, and moral excellence. Their mention together shows that true nobility before God is not based on lineage or worldly rank but on righteousness, sincerity, and fidelity to His command. Dhul-Kifl’s name suggests one who took upon himself a pledge or responsibility, pointing to trustworthiness and steadfastness in fulfilling what was entrusted to him. The verse affirms that all of them are among God’s chosen and excellent servants, and remembering them inspires believers to imitate their devotion, perseverance, and upright conduct.

translation: This is a reminder; and indeed, for the righteous is an excellent return.
interpretation: The verse declares that this revelation is an admonition and remembrance for humanity, and it promises those who guard themselves against sin and disobedience out of awe of God that their final return will be excellent—namely, Paradise and nearness to God in the Hereafter.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, with doors opened for them.
interpretation: The opened doors signify that the people of Paradise are received with honor and welcome, entering freely and securely into everlasting bliss; nothing bars them from its delights, and their dwelling therein is eternal.

translation: Reclining therein, they will call for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: This describes the bliss of Paradise: the righteous will recline in comfort and ease, and whenever they desire, they will request and be given plentiful fruits and drinks. It signifies perfect contentment, perpetual delight, and the fulfillment of every pleasurable desire without effort or exhaustion.

translation: And with them will be companions of restrained gaze, of equal age.
interpretation: This describes the pure spouses granted to the people of Paradise: they keep their eyes solely on their husbands, showing perfect fidelity and modesty, and they are equal in age and temperament, so that the companionship is harmonious and fulfilling.

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: It affirms that the reward described is the promise Allah made to the righteous, and its appointed time is the Day of Account, when deeds are reckoned and justice is established. The promise is therefore certain, and its fulfillment is reserved for that day rather than this worldly life.

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision; it has no end.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the blessings God grants to the people of Paradise are permanent and inexhaustible. Unlike worldly provisions, which are limited, temporary, and subject to loss, God’s reward in the Hereafter never runs out, never diminishes, and is never cut off. It expresses the perfection of divine generosity and the eternal security of the bliss He has promised.

translation: This [is so]. And indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who transgress the limits set by God, rebel against His commands, and persist in arrogance and oppression will ultimately return to the worst of destinations. It stands as the counterpart to the good final abode promised to the righteous: just as obedience leads to honor and reward, willful transgression leads to disgrace and punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: Hell, they will enter it, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse declares the final abode of those who persist in denial and arrogance: Jahannam, which they will inevitably enter and suffer. Calling it “the resting place” is a severe irony, because a resting place is meant for comfort, calm, and relief, yet theirs is the worst possible resting place. The verse emphasizes that their punishment is certain, fitting, and far removed from mercy, while also highlighting God’s perfect justice: the one who chooses rebellion and rejects guidance finds no honorable end, only humiliation and lasting torment.

translation: This—so let them taste it—is scalding water and a foul, putrid discharge.
interpretation: It is a decree of recompense addressed to the people of Hell, ordering them to taste the torment they earned. The "hamim" is water heated to the utmost intensity, burning and dissolving whatever it reaches as they are forced to drink it, while "ghassaq" is a revolting fluid—either unbearably cold or a filthy discharge—that adds another form of physical agony and humiliation. The verse stresses that divine justice will make them experience consequences both agonizing and degrading, matching their arrogant rejection of truth with a punishment that overwhelms and shames them.

translation: And other [torments] of its kind, in pairs.
interpretation: This verse declares that the punishment of the people of Hell is not limited to what was just mentioned; there are further chastisements of the same severity and nature, paired and varied in form. It conveys that their torment is multiplied and compounded, each kind matching the others in harshness and fitting the evil they committed, so that divine justice is fully executed upon them.

translation: This is a troop storming in with you; no welcome for them; indeed, they are to enter the Fire.
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene in the Hereafter in which the arrogant leaders who are already in the Fire announce the arrival of their followers, refusing them any welcome and affirming that they too are destined for the Fire. It exposes how worldly allegiance and leadership collapse in the Hereafter: those who were followed show no mercy or loyalty to those who followed them, and both face the Fire without any help from one another. The phrase “no welcome” signals disgrace and severe rejection, not hospitality, emphasizing the humiliation and helplessness of the people of the Fire.

translation: They will say, 'Rather, it is you who are not welcome. You prepared this for us; so wretched is the final settlement.'
interpretation: This verse conveys that blame-shifting among the people of Hell is futile and that responsibility for misguidance is shared according to one's role. Those who led others into disbelief are condemned for making the path to Hell seem ready and present, while those who followed are condemned for choosing obedience to created beings over obedience to God. The retort 'no welcome to you' signifies that the damned cannot escape mutual accusation, regret, and curse; rather than bringing relief, this only intensifies their suffering. 'Evil is the settlement' identifies Hell as the worst final abode, and the verse affirms divine justice: no one is punished except for what they earned, and those who cause others to stray bear a grave share of the blame.

translation: They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase for him a double punishment in the Fire."
interpretation: This is the plea of the followers in Hell against those who led them into disbelief and sin. It teaches that misleaders bear a doubled accountability: their own guilt plus the guilt of leading others astray, so their torment is intensified. Their words also expose the futility of regret and mutual blaming in the Hereafter, and show that divine punishment is perfectly just: it falls only where responsibility for corruption and misleading was incurred.

translation: And they will say, 'What is [wrong] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil ones?'
interpretation: This verse describes the humiliation and regret of the arrogant disbelievers in the Fire. In the world, they had mocked the believers and dismissed them as lowly or wicked; now, looking around in punishment, they do not find those believers among the damned. Their question exposes the reversal of their false standards: those they despised were actually the people of truth and righteousness, while they themselves are now among the losers. It is a rebuke of arrogant self-exaltation and a declaration that God's judgment overturns the worldly rankings invented by the heedless.

translation: Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes missed them?
interpretation: These are the words of the arrogant in the Fire, who no longer see the believers they used to belittle. Their question is not a request for information but an expression of bewilderment and regret: they wonder whether they had unjustly mocked people who were truly better than them, or whether their own eyes are now failing to see them. The meaning is that their mockery was misplaced and that God has reversed their standings—the mocked believers are honored, while the mockers are disgraced. It is a warning that worldly contempt for the righteous can lead to eternal loss.

translation: Indeed, that is surely true — the disputing of the people of the Fire.
interpretation: This is an emphatic affirmation that the arguments and mutual recriminations among those condemned to Hell are a certain reality. Their disputes will expose their falsehood, regret, and blame-shifting, but will bring them no benefit, and God's warning will be shown to be fully true.

translation: Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse defines the Prophet’s mission as warning rather than compelling faith, and grounds that warning in pure monotheism: Allah alone is God, absolutely one in His essence, attributes, and authority, and al-Qahhar—the One whose power subdues and prevails over all things. Therefore every creature stands under His sovereign rule, and the only proper response is to heed the warning, worship Him alone, and submit to His unchallengeable will.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Almighty, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God alone is the Lord, Creator, and Sustainer of all the heavens, the earth, and everything between them. His power is absolute and invincible, so nothing can resist or escape Him, yet He is repeatedly forgiving toward those who repent and turn to Him. Thus His majesty and might do not prevent His mercy; He is both the overpowering Sovereign and the ever-forgiving Lord.

translation: Say, 'It is a great tiding.'
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to proclaim that the revelation he brings is a momentous announcement of supreme importance—the greatest tiding—centering on God's oneness, the truth of prophethood, and the coming accountability in the Hereafter. Its greatness lies in its eternal consequences: accepting it leads to salvation, while rejecting it leads to ruin. It therefore calls every hearer to stop turning away and to give it earnest, serious heed.

translation: I had no knowledge of the Highest Assembly when they disputed.
interpretation: This means that the Prophet Muhammad did not know by himself about the exalted assembly of angels and their dispute in the heavenly realm; such knowledge came to him only through divine revelation. It establishes that his knowledge of unseen matters was not acquired or self-derived but granted by Allah, confirming the truthfulness of his prophethood and that he is a clear warner inspired by revelation.

translation: It is only revealed to me that I am a clear warner.
interpretation: This statement defines the limit and nature of the Prophet’s mission: his inspiration does not make him a sharer in divine authority, a knower of the unseen on his own, or one who compels hearts. The essential purpose of what is revealed to him is to make him a plain warner who clearly conveys the truth and its consequences. His duty is therefore to deliver the warning with clarity, while guidance, judgment, and the final outcome remain with God alone.

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that human creation is solely by God's decree and power, bringing forth a living being from earthly, lifeless matter. It also indicates that God informed the angels beforehand to prepare them for the honored station He would bestow upon Adam and to make clear that obedience to His command regarding this new creation would be a test of their submission.

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse addresses the angels concerning the creation of Adam. When God completed his physical formation and breathed into him of His spirit—meaning He granted him life, a soul, and a special dignity by His command, not that God has a bodily spirit or that a part of Him entered Adam—the angels were commanded to prostrate before Adam. That prostration was not worship of Adam, for worship belongs to God alone; it was an act of obedience to God's command and a sign of honor for Adam as the creature God specially favored and prepared for vicegerency on earth.

translation: So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the angels’ complete and unanimous obedience to Allah’s command: every one of them prostrated before Adam as an act of submission to Allah and as a mark of honor for Adam, without exception or hesitation.

translation: Except Iblis: he was arrogant and became among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse shows that Iblis’s fall came through pride: he regarded himself as above God’s command, and that arrogance turned his disobedience into disbelief. It teaches that willful self-exaltation against divine authority corrupts one’s state before God and can place a person among those who reject faith, even if they had once been in a position of nearness.

translation: [Allah] said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My two hands? Have you become arrogant, or are you among the exalted?
interpretation: This verse is a divine rebuke to Iblis after he refused to prostrate to Adam. Allah questions what excuse could have prevented him when the command was clear. The phrase “with My two hands” affirms Allah’s direct creation of Adam and honors him; it is not a claim that Allah has bodily hands like created beings. The question “Have you become arrogant, or are you among the exalted?” means: Is your refusal caused by pride, or do you imagine yourself to be of a rank that exempts you from obeying Allah’s command? It exposes Iblis’s disobedience as rooted in arrogance and self-elevation, not in a valid objection.

translation: He said, "I am better than him: You created me from fire, and You created him from clay."
interpretation: This statement embodies the sin of arrogance: Iblis takes a God-given physical origin and turns it into a claim of inherent superiority, thereby rejecting God's command to prostrate to Adam. The verse teaches that worth is not determined by material composition, race, lineage, or created nature, but by obedience, humility, and piety. Iblis’s reasoning is false because God’s command is grounded in His wisdom and authority, not in the elemental superiority of one creation over another; thus his comparison becomes a pretext for disobedience and the first archetype of pride-based discrimination.

translation: He said: So get out of it, for indeed you are expelled.
interpretation: This is Allah’s decree banishing Iblis from the realm of honor and from divine mercy, declaring him rajeem—cast out, accursed, and rejected—because his arrogance led him to disobey and refuse the command to prostrate to Adam.

translation: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: This is Allah’s pronouncement of perpetual rejection upon Iblis: he is deprived of divine mercy and grace, and that curse remains fixed upon him until the Day of Judgment, when all matters will be decided and every soul will be recompensed for its deeds.

translation: He said, "My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected."
interpretation: This is Iblis asking Allah to delay his death and punishment until the Day of Resurrection, not to repent or reform, but so that he may continue to tempt and mislead the descendants of Adam. His request exposes his persistent defiance, his declared enmity toward humanity, and his determination to lead people astray as an expression of rebellion against Allah’s command.

translation: He said, "Then indeed, you are among those granted respite."
interpretation: This is Allah’s decree granting Iblis the delay he requested: he is reprieved and not immediately destroyed, but this respite is not an honor or acceptance. It is a fixed term within Allah’s knowledge and command, serving as a trial and allowing the distinction between obedience and rebellion to become manifest until the appointed time. The phrase “among the granted respite” shows that his postponement remains entirely under Allah’s sovereignty and does not exempt him from final accountability.

translation: Until the Day of the Appointed Time.
interpretation: This is Allah’s declaration that Iblis’s respite is limited and extends only to the fixed, divinely known time—the Day of Resurrection and Judgment. The phrase “the known time” means that its exact occurrence is established in Allah’s knowledge and decree, even though it is hidden from creation. It shows that evil is not granted unlimited freedom; its activity continues only within the appointed span decreed by Allah before the final reckoning.

translation: He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all."
interpretation: This is Iblis swearing by God's might and glory that he will devote himself to leading all of humanity astray. It reveals his defiant resolve to deceive people and turn them away from obedience to God, while also showing that his power to mislead operates only within God's permission; he cannot compel anyone, but he will strive to corrupt and misguide them until the sincere servants of God are excepted.

translation: Except Your chosen sincere servants among them.
interpretation: This is Iblis’s admission that his misguidance cannot reach those whom Allah has purified for His worship and guarded by His grace; their devotion is sincere and free of corrupt motives, so they are protected from his deception.

translation: He (Allah) said: 'The truth [is My oath], and the truth I speak.'
interpretation: This is a divine affirmation or oath by the truth: Allah is the Absolute Truth, and His speech is truth. It underscores that His decree and warning are absolutely true and will certainly come to pass.

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and with all those among them who follow you.
interpretation: This is God’s decree against Iblis after he pledged to mislead humanity: Hell will be filled with him and with every one of his followers who chooses his path of rebellion and disobedience. It affirms that divine justice cannot be escaped and that those who imitate Iblis in arrogance and defiance will share in his punishment.

translation: Say, 'I do not ask you for any reward for it, and I am not of those who pretend.'
interpretation: The verse directs the Prophet to announce that he seeks no worldly payment or compensation from people for delivering the revelation, and that he is not among those who fabricate, affect, or burden others with claims and practices that God did not command. His message is sincere and free of self-interest or pretension.

translation: It is nothing but a reminder to all the worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is not a message invented for any human benefit or limited to one people; it is God’s universal admonition and remembrance for every created being, calling all to recognize their Creator, heed His guidance, and prepare for accountability.

translation: And you will surely know its news after a while.
interpretation: This is a solemn assurance that the truth of the Qur’anic message and the consequences of accepting or rejecting it will inevitably become clear to its hearers after some time. Those who deny it may dismiss it now, but later events, death, or the Hereafter will disclose the reality of what was foretold; thus it serves as both a warning to the deniers and a vindication of the Prophet’s message.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the Qur'an is not a human composition or invention but a revelation sent down by Allah alone. He is Al-Aziz, the Almighty whose power can never be overcome, and Al-Hakim, the All-Wise whose decrees, commands, and guidance are perfectly ordered and just. Therefore the Book's message carries divine authority, truth, and wisdom: it comes from the One able to reveal, preserve, and enforce it, and wise in all that it commands, prohibits, reports, and legislates. The basmalah preceding it invokes Allah's mercy and blessings, indicating that this revelation is an act of mercy and guidance from the Almighty, All-Wise.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion.
interpretation: Since the Book has been revealed by Allah with truth and contains no falsehood, the required response is to worship Him alone with pure and exclusive devotion, making all religious obedience, worship, and intention solely for Allah, free from any association, hypocrisy, or seeking the approval of others.

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs the pure religion. And those who take besides Him allies [say], “We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to Allah.” Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.
interpretation: The verse declares that sincere worship is due to God alone; no created being may be worshipped as an intermediary. The polytheists’ claim that their idols merely bring them nearer to God is a false pretext: seeking nearness does not license the worship of others. God will settle their disputes and expose the lie. Those who knowingly persist in falsehood and reject the truth are left without His guidance.

translation: If Allah had willed to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.
interpretation: This verse denies any need or possibility of God having a son, refuting all claims that attribute offspring to Him. Progeny belongs to created, dependent beings and implies pairing, limitation, and need, whereas God is absolutely transcendent and self-sufficient. Even if He had decreed an offspring by His will, He would not be bound to any creature or consort; He could create and select as He pleases. But His perfection excludes such a notion entirely. Thus the verse summons creation to acknowledge His absolute oneness and overwhelming power: He alone is the One, the irresistible Subduer, free of every imperfection and incomparable to anything.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for an appointed term. Unquestionably, He is the Almighty, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the entire creation is founded upon truth, wisdom, and divine purpose, not idle play. The image of night and day being wrapped or rolled over one another points to Allah’s sovereign control over time and the orderly succession of light and darkness, a sign of precise governance. The sun and moon are made subservient, moving according to a fixed decree until an appointed end, which shows that nothing in the cosmos is autonomous or eternal; all things submit to Allah’s command. Therefore, the verse calls the human being to recognize Allah alone as the Mighty One who sustains all things, and the Forgiving One who overlooks and pardons the shortcomings of those who turn to Him.

translation: He created you from one soul, then made from it its mate, and sent down for you eight pairs of livestock. He creates you in your mothers’ wombs, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; His is the dominion. There is no god except Him. So how are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah alone is the Creator, Sustainer, Provider, and Sovereign Lord. He originated humanity from a single soul, made its mate from it, and provided livestock in pairs as a mercy and means of life. He also forms every human being in the mother’s womb through successive stages within threefold darkness, showing His intimate knowledge and power over creation. Since He alone creates, provides, and governs, He alone deserves worship; the final question rebukes those who nevertheless turn away from Him toward false objects of devotion.

translation: If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need from you; and He does not approve disbelief for His servants. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse teaches that faith and disbelief ultimately benefit or harm the servant, not Allah, for He is utterly self-sufficient and needs no one’s worship. His not approving disbelief means He does not command it, love it, or reward it; it does not mean that disbelief never occurs by His permission. Gratitude, by contrast, is what He approves and accepts from His servants. The verse then establishes individual moral responsibility: no person will carry the sin of another, and every soul will return to its Lord alone for judgment. Allah’s final recompense will be perfectly just because He knows not only outward actions but also the hidden intentions, thoughts, and motives within the hearts.

translation: And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He grants him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he was calling upon Him for before, and sets up rivals to Allah to mislead [people] from His way. Say, 'Enjoy your disbelief a little; indeed, you are among the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse condemns the inconsistency of one who turns to Allah alone in distress but, once relieved and given blessings, forgets the Lord he had invoked and associates others with Allah, actively leading people away from His path. It warns that such ingratitude and shirk may seem pleasurable for a short time, but their end is the Fire, and it calls for steadfast faith, gratitude, and loyalty to Allah in both hardship and ease.

translation: Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who is not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only people of understanding will take heed.
interpretation: This verse sets up a contrast between the person whose knowledge of God bears fruit in humble, persistent worship—praying in the night, bowing and standing, balancing fear of the Hereafter with hope in God’s mercy—and the person who lacks that knowledge and therefore does not live in such devotion. The rhetorical question teaches that these two are not equal in rank, guidance, or outcome before God. The knowledge meant here is not mere intellectual information but a living awareness of God that transforms the heart and produces obedience. Therefore only those with sound reason and purified understanding—people who use their minds rightly and heed the divine reminder—recognize this truth and allow it to shape their lives.

translation: Say, "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and Allah's earth is spacious. Only the patient are given their reward without measure."
interpretation: This verse commands believers to maintain taqwa—God-consciousness expressed through obedience, avoidance of sin, and sincerity to Allah. It promises that those who perform ihsan, doing good and perfecting their conduct in this worldly life, will receive hasanah: a comprehensive good that includes divine pleasure, peace of heart, guidance, honorable provision, and ultimate success in the Hereafter. The statement that Allah's earth is spacious consoles believers who face persecution, restriction, or pressure to compromise their faith; it invites them to migrate or seek a place where they can worship and live obediently if their current circumstances prevent it. The final promise, that the patient are paid their reward without measure, identifies sabr—patience in faith, obedience, trials, hardship, and injustice—as the key to an unlimited and uncalculable reward from Allah's infinite generosity. Thus the verse directs believers not to trade their religion for worldly security, because God's provision and reward are wider and greater than any earthly limitation.

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion."
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet, and through him every believer, to declare that the command to worship God is inseparable from pure devotion: all worship, obedience, and religious service must be directed to God alone, unmixed with any show, ulterior motive, or association of partners. It establishes sincerity in religion as the essential condition of true worship, meaning one’s inward intention and outward acts must align exclusively toward God.

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit [to Allah].
interpretation: The verse conveys that the Prophet is not merely delivering a message but is himself under divine command to embody it first. His being “first of the Muslims” means he must be foremost in sincere submission, worship, and obedience to God, before anyone else, so that his call is authenticated by his own surrender. It also teaches that the highest rank in faith comes not from status or rhetoric but from being earliest and most wholehearted in yielding to God’s will.

translation: Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I were to disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day."
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to publicly declare that he fears the torment of the Day of Judgment if he were to disobey his Lord. Although prophets are divinely protected from falling into disobedience, this statement teaches profound humility, sincere servitude, and the seriousness of accountability before God. It establishes that no status, closeness, or prophetic rank exempts anyone from the obligation of obedience, and it warns every believer that turning away from divine commands exposes one to the terrible punishment of the Great Day. The fear expressed here is not doubt or despair; it is reverent awe, vigilance, and a recognition of God's majesty and justice.

translation: Say, "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion."
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet, and every believer by extension, to declare openly that worship, obedience, and religious devotion are directed to Allah alone. It establishes pure monotheism and sincere intention: one’s religion must be devoted exclusively to Allah, not mixed with worship of created beings, not performed for show, and not motivated by worldly praise or gain. Sincerity here means that the heart, word, and deed are all purified for Allah alone, recognizing Him as the only true object of worship.

translation: So worship whatever you wish besides Him. Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss."
interpretation: This verse follows a declaration of sincere worship to Allah alone and is directed at those who persist in false worship. It is not a permission to worship others besides Allah, but a severe warning and challenge: if they choose to worship other than Him, they alone will bear the consequence. The true and manifest loss is not the loss of wealth, status, or worldly gain, but the ruination of one's own self and one's family in the Hereafter. The self is lost because it was created to worship Allah and attain eternal happiness, yet by choosing false objects of worship it is led to punishment. The family is lost because the bonds that could have helped lead to Paradise are severed, or because one misleads one's family and is separated from them in the Hereafter. Thus, the verse teaches that real success is salvation with one's family in the Hereafter, while the clearest loss is to come on the Day of Resurrection bankrupt in faith, having lost both oneself and those closest to one.

translation: For them will be canopies of Fire above them and canopies beneath them. By that Allah warns His servants. O My servants, fear Me.
interpretation: This verse depicts the punishment of Hell as all-encompassing: those who reject God will be covered by layers of fire from above and from below, leaving no escape or relief. God mentions this severity as a warning to His servants, not because He delights in punishing, but so they may take heed, repent, and avoid what leads to it. The address “O My servants” is a call of mercy amid warning: God still calls them His servants and urges them to fear Him—meaning to protect themselves from His wrath by obeying His commands, avoiding His prohibitions, and living with awareness of His judgment.

translation: And those who avoid false deities lest they worship them, and turn to Allah—for them is glad tidings. So give glad tidings to My servants.
interpretation: This verse identifies the people of true deliverance: they actively distance themselves from every false object of worship—idols, tyrannical powers, or anything that usurps Allah’s exclusive right to be worshiped—and they turn back to Allah with sincere repentance, obedience, and reliance. Their reward is the good news of Allah’s acceptance, guidance, and ultimate success in this life and the Hereafter; the Prophet is then commanded to convey this glad promise to Allah’s devoted servants.

translation: Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it—those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the ones of understanding.
interpretation: This verse describes the people of sound intellect who do not accept everything they hear blindly; they listen carefully, weigh what is said, and then follow what is best—namely, the truth, the most upright, and the most pleasing to Allah. Because they use their reason rightly and submit to guidance, Allah attributes their guidance to Himself and calls them the possessors of understanding, indicating that true intellect is not mere cleverness but the ability to recognize and adhere to divine guidance.

translation: Is then one against whom the word of punishment has become due [to be saved by you]? Can you rescue one who is in the Fire?
interpretation: This rhetorical question addresses the Prophet Muhammad and teaches that those whom Allah’s decree of punishment has justly become due—because of their persistent disbelief and rejection of guidance—cannot be rescued from the Fire by any human effort, not even by the Prophet’s deep concern for them. The Prophet’s duty is to convey the message and warn, not to compel hearts or override Allah’s judgment. The verse thus affirms Allah’s absolute justice, the limits of human agency, and the fact that true deliverance from the Fire comes only through Allah’s mercy and acceptance of faith, not through prophetic power or personal attachment.

translation: But those who are mindful of their Lord will have lofty chambers, above which are more chambers built, with rivers flowing beneath them. This is the promise of Allah; Allah never breaks His promise.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the final abode of the God-conscious with that of the arrogant. Taqwa—reverent awareness of God—raises a person to eternal dwellings that are layered and exalted, symbolizing honor, tranquility, and ever-renewed delight, with flowing rivers indicating continuous provision and life. The certain fulfillment of this reward rests not on human merit alone but on God's unfailing promise; His pledge cannot be delayed, altered, or revoked, so hope in Him is never misplaced.

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs within the earth; then He brings forth thereby crops of varying colors; then they wither, and you see them turning yellow; then He makes them dry debris. Indeed in that is a reminder for people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse presents the cycle of water, vegetation, growth, decay, and destruction as a clear sign of Allah’s power to create, sustain, and resurrect. It reminds people of sound intellect that worldly life is fleeting: its beauty and freshness eventually fade, turn yellow, and become broken remains. Just as Allah revives barren earth with rain, He is able to revive the dead, and just as crops inevitably wither, human worldly prosperity is temporary. The lesson is to reflect, take heed, and not be deceived by the transient attractions of this life, while trusting in the Creator’s power and preparing for the Hereafter.

translation: Is one whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord [like one whose heart is hardened]? Then woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the state of the believer whose heart Allah has opened to receive Islam with the state of those whose hearts are hard and closed to His remembrance. The expansion of the breast is a divine gift: it gives the heart readiness, tranquility, and submission to God, so the person walks by a light, guidance, and certainty from his Lord. Hardness of heart, by contrast, is a spiritual disease in which the heart recoils from the remembrance of Allah, refuses His guidance, and loses sensitivity to truth. Such hardness deserves warning and ruin, and those who suffer it are in clear, manifest misguidance, far from the straight path.

translation: Allah has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book, oft-repeated. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah, by which He guides whom He wills. And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse describes the Qur’an as the finest speech because it comes from Allah and is unified in truth, harmonious in its teachings, and repeatedly returning to the same central realities of faith, warning, and promise. Its first effect upon the God-fearing is awe: their bodies tremble as they hear its commands, warnings, and majesty, because they revere their Lord. Then that awe gives way to tenderness and tranquility as their hearts and bodies yield to Allah’s remembrance, His promises, and His mercy. This shows that true guidance is not merely intellectual acceptance but a movement of the heart produced by divine speech: fear leads to humble attentiveness, and remembrance brings softening and submission. The verse then attributes guidance entirely to Allah: He guides whom He wills by this Book, while those whom He leaves astray have no one who can guide them. Thus it teaches both the powerful spiritual effect of the Qur’an on believers and human dependence upon Allah’s decree and guidance.

translation: Is he, then, who will ward off the evil punishment with his face on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, 'Taste what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical rebuke showing the helplessness of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. They will have no shield or protector against the punishment; they will try to avert it with their very faces, indicating utter humiliation and direct suffering. Then they will be commanded to taste the consequence of their disbelief and evil deeds, affirming that divine punishment is the just recompense for what they chose to commit.

translation: Those before them denied, so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse warns the deniers of the Prophet Muhammad by citing earlier nations who also rejected their messengers. They felt secure and thought no harm could reach them, but God’s punishment struck unexpectedly, from directions and means they had never anticipated. It teaches that rejecting divine guidance does not prevent consequences; rather, chastisement can come suddenly through unsuspected channels.

translation: So Allah made them taste disgrace in the worldly life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah caused those who rejected Him and persisted in arrogance to experience humiliation and disgrace in this world as an early consequence of their disbelief. Yet that worldly disgrace is not the full recompense; the punishment awaiting them in the Hereafter is far greater, more severe, and more lasting. The closing phrase, “if they only knew,” indicates that their failure to take heed stemmed from a lack of true understanding and certainty about the Hereafter. Had they truly known what awaits the deniers, they would have abandoned their defiance and turned back to Allah.

translation: And We have certainly set forth for mankind in this Qur’an every kind of example, so that they may remember.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the Qur’an contains ample parables, analogies, signs, and arguments sufficient to remind every seeker of truth. Their purpose is not mere storytelling but to stir the human intellect and conscience, remove heedlessness, and guide people to reflect on their Lord, their own creation, and the consequences of their choices, so they may return to what is right and hold fast to guidance.

translation: An Arabic Qur’an, without any crookedness, so that they may become God-fearing.
interpretation: This verse means that the Qur’an was revealed in clear, eloquent Arabic, free from any deviance, contradiction, or distortion in its meanings and guidance. Its uprightness is meant to lead people to taqwa: to guard themselves against disbelief, sin, and disobedience, and to live in reverence and obedience to God.

translation: Allah sets forth a parable: a man owned by quarreling partners, and a man owned exclusively by one man. Are the two equal in comparison? All praise belongs to Allah. But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This parable contrasts the state of one who associates partners with Allah and the state of one who worships Allah alone. The one owned by many quarreling masters is pulled in conflicting directions, confused, divided, and unable to find peace, while the one owned by a single master is settled, undivided, and secure in serving one will. They are not equal. Likewise, shirk produces discord, contradiction, and loss, whereas pure monotheism brings harmony and soundness because all worship, obedience, and reliance are directed to the one true Lord. “All praise belongs to Allah” affirms that all gratitude and praise belong to Him alone as the sole rightful object of worship, but most people do not know this truth, and therefore they wrongly associate others with Him.

translation: Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die.
interpretation: This verse establishes the certainty of death for every human being, including the Prophet and his opponents, and thereby removes any illusion of permanence, superiority, or exemption in this world. It directs the heart to prepare for the meeting with God and to entrust all disputes and judgments to Him, since death will bring every claim and conflict before the ultimate reckoning and resurrection.

translation: Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute.
interpretation: This is a warning that the disagreements, denials, and grievances people harbor and argue over in this world will not remain unjudged: on the Day of Resurrection, every disputant will stand before the Lord, who will judge with perfect justice and truth. No claim will be accepted merely because it was asserted, and no hidden motive or false argument will remain concealed; the real state of every soul will be exposed, and each will receive the consequence of what it contended for and against.

translation: So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse conveys that the gravest injustice is to invent falsehoods about God and then reject the truth once it has been made clear. Such a person has combined two great wrongs: misrepresenting the Creator and refusing the guidance He sent. The rhetorical question implies that no one can be more unjust than this, and the final question affirms that Hell is the fitting dwelling for those who persist in denying the truth. It warns that rejection of divine truth is not a light matter; it carries severe accountability and ultimate loss.

translation: And the one who has brought the truth and [they who] believed in it — those are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse praises the person who brings the truth—namely, the Prophet Muhammad—and those who accept and confirm it. Such people are the God-conscious: they guard themselves against disbelief, disobedience, and falsehood by embracing the truth and living according to it, and therefore they are the righteous in Allah’s sight.

translation: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse describes the honor and bliss prepared for the righteous: in the presence of their Lord, they will receive all that their hearts desire, without limitation or deprivation. Such complete fulfillment is not earned by mere wishful thinking but is granted as a reward for those who practiced ihsan—worshipping God with sincere excellence, acting beautifully toward others, and doing good consistently. Their reward is therefore both spiritual nearness to their Lord and the satisfaction of every longing, because God never wastes the reward of those who perfect their faith and conduct.

translation: That Allah may remit from them the worst of what they did and reward them with the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse expresses the vastness of Allah’s mercy and generosity toward those who believe and act righteously: He does not merely overlook their sins, but He erases even the gravest wrongs they committed, and He rewards them not according to their worst or average deeds but according to the finest and most sincere deeds they performed. It teaches that divine forgiveness transforms a person’s record—evil is covered and removed, while good is preserved and generously compensated—so the servant should never despair of Allah’s mercy nor presume that righteous deeds go unrewarded.

translation: Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? And they threaten you with those besides Him. And whoever Allah sends astray, then for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is fully sufficient to protect, support, and defend His servant; no threat from any supposed power besides Him can override His care. The intimidation directed at the Prophet—and by extension the believers—is exposed as empty fearmongering, because false deities or human powers have no independent ability to harm or benefit. At the same time, it teaches that guidance and misguidance ultimately rest under Allah’s decree: one whom Allah abandons to stray because of persistent rejection and turning away will find no one able to guide him. Thus the verse combines reassurance of divine sufficiency with a warning about the seriousness of being left without divine guidance.

translation: And whoever Allah guides, there is none to mislead him. Is not Allah Almighty, Lord of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse affirms that divine guidance is decisive and cannot be overturned by any created power. If Allah guides someone, no force can lead that person astray, because Allah is al-‘Aziz, the Almighty whose will is never overcome, and Dhu’l-Intiqam, the Lord of Retribution who will exact justice from those who reject His guidance and oppose His truth. Therefore, ultimate guidance and misguidance rest under Allah’s sovereign decree, and He is fully able both to protect whom He guides and to repay the rebellious.

translation: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, are they able to remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, are they able to withhold His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him rely those who rely.'
interpretation: This verse argues from the polytheists' own admission that Allah alone created the heavens and the earth to show the inconsistency of invoking others besides Him. Since no false object of worship can either remove harm decreed by Allah or withhold His mercy, all recourse, fear, hope, and dependence belong to Allah alone. The command 'Sufficient for me is Allah' teaches that true trust is not placed in created beings or imagined intercessors, but in the One who alone disposes all affairs; and this total reliance is the mark of those who truly rely upon Him.

translation: Say, “O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. So you will come to know.”
interpretation: This is a decisive warning and declaration of separation: the Prophet is told to tell his people to remain on their chosen path, station, or way, while he remains faithful to the path God has revealed to him. It does not command aggression; it announces that each side will continue according to its own course and that the outcome will soon make clear who is upon the truth and who will face the consequences. The knowledge they will gain is the certainty that comes when God’s judgment appears, exposing which deeds were built on truth and which on falsehood.

translation: who will be visited by a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom a lasting punishment will descend
interpretation: This is part of Noah’s warning to his people who mocked him. It declares that they would soon come to know who among them would be seized by a humiliating punishment in this world—the flood—and then be overtaken by an everlasting punishment in the Hereafter. The verse teaches that divine judgment is certain: arrogance and mockery of God’s messengers bring disgrace, while persistent denial leads to an abiding torment.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for the people in truth. So whoever is guided, he is guided only for his own soul; and whoever goes astray, he only goes astray against it. And you are not a trustee over them.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the Qur'an is revealed by God with truth as universal guidance for humanity. It teaches that guidance and misguidance are matters of personal responsibility: the benefit of following guidance returns to the individual, and the harm of straying falls upon the individual. The Prophet is not appointed as a guardian who forces belief or assumes responsibility for people's choices; his duty is to deliver the message, while God holds each soul accountable for its response.

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die, during their sleep. Then He keeps those for whom He has decreed death and sends the others back for an appointed term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse affirms that all souls are entirely in Allah’s grasp: He alone controls the departure of life at death and the temporary withdrawal of consciousness in sleep. Sleep is presented as a lesser separation from the body, a reminder that a person’s life is not self-sustaining but held by Allah at every moment. When the appointed decree of death is fixed, the soul is retained; otherwise it is returned so the person may continue toward the term Allah has set. Thus the verse calls people to reflect on their complete dependence on their Creator, on the nearness of death, and on Allah’s power to restore life after death.

translation: Or have they taken besides Allah intercessors? Say, 'Even if they do not possess anything and do not reason?'
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who set up mediators or intercessors besides Allah, whether idols, false gods, or created beings, imagining that they can bring benefit or avert harm independently. Allah commands the Prophet to confront them with a decisive argument: these so-called intercessors own nothing at all and have no independent power, nor do they possess true understanding or authority to decide anything. Therefore, relying on them is futile and irrational. The verse establishes that all intercession belongs to Allah alone; no one can intercede except by His permission, and only for whom He wills. It calls people to direct their worship, hope, and supplication exclusively to Allah, the sole Owner and Disposer of all affairs.

translation: Say, 'To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned.'
interpretation: This means that the right to grant, authorize, or accept any intercession belongs exclusively to Allah. No angel, prophet, or any other being can intercede for anyone unless Allah permits it. Since He alone owns and governs the heavens and the earth, He alone controls all affairs, including forgiveness, mercy, and punishment. The final return of all creation is to Him, where every person will be held accountable, and no claimed intercessor or partner can benefit anyone independently of His will.

translation: And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those besides Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse exposes the inner contradiction of the disbelievers: they recoil when Allah is invoked alone as the sole God worthy of worship, because pure monotheism exposes the falsehood of their idols and imagined intercessors. Yet when others besides Him are mentioned, they are delighted, showing that their joy is not for truth but for association with Him.
