Their aversion to Allah's exclusive mention reveals that their rejection of the Hereafter is tied to their refusal to submit to His sole authority and to abandon the false objects of devotion they prefer.

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.'
interpretation: This is a supplication that directs the believer to seek Allah’s judgment by invoking His creative power and omniscience. Since He alone originated the heavens and earth and knows both the hidden and the visible, He alone has the knowledge and authority to settle the disputes among His servants, especially matters of faith and truth. The verse teaches that final arbitration belongs to God, not to human speculation or partisanship, and that people should refer their disagreements to His revelation and await His just decree.

translation: And if those who did wrong had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would ransom themselves with it from the evil punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah what they never anticipated.
interpretation: This verse exposes the utter helplessness of the unjust before divine justice: all the wealth of the world, even multiplied, cannot buy escape from the punishment they have earned. Their deepest illusions are shattered when Allah discloses consequences they never reckoned with, proving that false hopes, denial, and self-deception cannot shield anyone from accountability. It affirms that God's judgment is inescapable and that the real loss is not the loss of worldly possessions but the loss of safety from His punishment.

translation: And there will appear to them the evil consequences of what they earned, and they will be encompassed by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the wicked will plainly see the evil of the deeds they committed, which they may have concealed, justified, or thought harmless. The very realities and warnings they mocked—such as resurrection, divine judgment, and punishment—will then close in on them and overwhelm them, leaving them without escape.

translation: When harm touches the human being, he calls upon Us; then when We grant him a favor from Us, he says, “I have only been given it on account of knowledge.” Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse exposes the human tendency to acknowledge God only in distress while crediting personal knowledge, ability, or worth for blessings in ease. Such a blessing is not proof of divine favor or personal entitlement; it is a test of gratitude, humility, and whether one recognizes the true Giver. Most people remain unaware because they judge by immediate comfort instead of seeing every favor as a trust and trial from God.

translation: Those before them had also said it, but what they used to earn did not avail them.
interpretation: This is a warning against self-delusion: when people attribute Allah’s favors to their own knowledge, wealth, or effort, they repeat the error of earlier nations. Those earlier peoples also trusted in their acquisitions and abilities, yet none of that shielded them from Allah’s punishment or changed His decree. So the verse teaches that human earnings—whether wealth, status, or cleverness—cannot save a person when Allah’s judgment comes; true security lies in gratitude, humility, and obedience to Him.

translation: So the evil consequences of what they earned struck them. And those who do wrong among these [people] — the evil consequences of what they earned will strike them, and they will not escape.
interpretation: This verse warns that wrongdoing inevitably brings ruinous consequences. It cites how earlier communities were overtaken by the evil results of their own deeds, then warns the wrongdoers among the Prophet’s contemporaries that the same pattern will befall them: their misdeeds will return upon them as punishment, and they cannot evade or frustrate God’s decree.

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse establishes that sustenance is entirely in Allah’s hand: He expands it for whom He wills and narrows it for whom He wills, according to His wisdom, not according to people’s imagined merit or worth. The variation in wealth and need is a trial and a sign for believers, teaching them that neither abundance nor scarcity is proof of divine pleasure or rejection. The believer therefore neither arrogantly relies on wealth nor despairs in poverty, but recognizes Allah’s lordship, trusts His decree, remains grateful in ease, patient in hardship, and seeks provision from Him alone.

translation: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse is a profound divine invitation to hope and repentance. By addressing sinners as "My servants," God affirms that disobedience does not sever one's relationship with Him; the sin is described as wronging one's own soul because its harm ultimately returns to the sinner. The prohibition of despair means that losing hope in God's mercy is itself a serious error, for no sin is too great for His forgiveness when a person turns back to Him. The phrase "all sins" expresses the vastness of divine mercy, understood in the context of sincere repentance and not persistence in wrongdoing. God's names al-Ghafur and al-Rahim confirm that He repeatedly forgives, covers faults, and extends compassionate mercy. Thus the verse teaches that God's mercy exceeds every sin, and the proper response is not despair but turning to Him in hope.

translation: And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse urges immediate, sincere repentance and total submission to God while the opportunity still exists, before divine punishment or death arrives. At that point, no helper, intercessor, or source of victory can save anyone, so the time to return to God is now, not after judgment is sealed.

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.
interpretation: This means: adhere sincerely to the most excellent guidance God has sent down—faith in Him and His messengers, obedience to His commands, avoidance of His prohibitions, and acting upon the Qur’an’s moral and spiritual teachings—without procrastination. The verse warns that divine judgment can overtake a person all at once, at an unexpected moment, while he is heedless and unprepared. “The best of what has been revealed” calls for choosing what is most pleasing to God, most beneficial, and most binding, and it is an urgent invitation to repentance, obedience, and readiness before sudden punishment arrives, when regret will no longer benefit anyone.

translation: [Lest] a soul should say, “Oh, my grief over what I neglected in respect of Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers.”
interpretation: This verse depicts the remorse of a soul at the moment when regret can no longer help it: it laments having wasted its life in neglect of Allah’s rights, commands, and worship, and confesses that it used to mock and belittle faith and its people. “What I neglected in respect of Allah” means the duties, obedience, repentance, and awareness of God that were owed to Him but were abandoned. The verse is a warning that heedlessness and mockery of religion lead to a painful, irreversible regret, so one must turn back to Allah before that time comes.

translation: Or [lest] it says: “If Allah had guided me, I would have been among the God-fearing.”
interpretation: This is one of the excuses the heedless soul will make on the Day of Judgment. It claims that its misguidance was due to Allah not guiding it, and that if He had guided it, it would have become righteous. The claim is false: Allah’s guidance had already reached it through revelation, messengers, and clear signs, but it turned away in arrogance and rejection. So the verse exposes self-deception and blaming God for one’s own choices, and it warns people to accept guidance while there is still time.

translation: Or it says, when it sees the punishment, ‘If only I had a return, then I would be among the doers of good.’
interpretation: This verse exposes the worthlessness of repentance that is forced by witnessing the punishment. The plea to be sent back is not accepted as genuine reform, because the time of testing and free choice has already ended; good deeds (ihsan) must be chosen in worldly life while the consequences are still unseen, not merely desired after the reality of judgment becomes undeniable.

translation: But yes, My verses had come to you, and you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a decisive rebuttal to the soul that wishes it had another chance after seeing punishment. It establishes that the guidance and clear signs had already reached it, so its ruin was not caused by ignorance or lack of opportunity, but by its own rejection of the truth, arrogant refusal to submit, and deliberate choice to remain in disbelief. The verse shows that denial and pride are the root causes of kufr, and that accountability is just because the person turned away from what was made clear to them.

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, those who fabricated falsehoods about God—attributing to Him partners, laws, or claims He never revealed, or rejecting His messengers and signs—will be publicly disgraced, their faces turned black as a sign of their inner corruption and the shame of their lies. The rhetorical question then affirms that Hell is the dwelling place prepared for the arrogant: those who, out of pride, refused to submit to God, reject His truth, and set themselves above His commands. Thus the verse links falsehood against God with arrogant self-exaltation, and it shows that both meet their just recompense in the Fire unless the person repents and turns back to God.

translation: And Allah will save those who feared Him by their attainment [of success]; no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This means that Allah, in His mercy and justice, delivers those who guarded themselves against sin and disobedience out of reverence for Him, and He grants them the ultimate victory and safety. Because they prioritized His pleasure and avoided what He forbade, He protects them from every form of punishment and harm in the Hereafter, and they will not suffer any sorrow over what they left behind or any fear of what lies ahead.

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is over all things a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the Creator of everything that exists, and that He alone manages, sustains, and governs all affairs. Nothing occurs outside His will, knowledge, and authority; all creation depends upon Him, while He is independent of all things. Therefore, worship, reliance, and ultimate trust belong to Him alone, and no created being shares in His creative power or sovereign control.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah—those are the losers.
interpretation: All control, authority, and the treasuries of all that exists in the heavens and the earth belong exclusively to Allah. He alone opens and closes the gates of provision, mercy, life, death, and every affair according to His wisdom. Those who reject His signs and revelations are the true losers, for they have shut themselves off from the source of all good and from eternal success.

translation: Say, 'Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?'
interpretation: This verse is a firm command to the Prophet Muhammad to reject every call to worship anything or anyone besides Allah. It rebukes those who demand that he associate partners with Allah as ignorant, because they fail to recognize that worship is due to Allah alone, the sole Creator and Sustainer. It establishes pure monotheism and declares that directing any act of worship to other than Allah is false and unacceptable.

translation: And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely become worthless, and you will surely be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse is a universal divine warning that the foundation of every prophetic message is pure monotheism. It declares that if a person associates any partner with Allah in worship, all their righteous deeds are rendered void and they end up among the losers in the Hereafter. Although the Prophet Muhammad is divinely protected from shirk, the address is directed to him to emphasize to his followers and all humanity the gravity of shirk, and to show that this warning was given to every prophet before him. Loss here means the loss of reward, salvation, and eternal success. The verse teaches that sincerity in worship is a condition for deeds to be accepted; without it, even great acts of goodness bring no benefit. It also implies that one who repents from shirk can be forgiven, but persisting in it leads to ruin.

translation: Nay, but worship Allah, and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse directs the servant to devote all worship exclusively to Allah alone, rejecting every false object of worship, and to make gratitude a defining quality of that devotion. True worship requires recognizing that all blessings come from Allah, so the worshipper must respond with thankfulness in heart, speech, and action, acknowledging Him as the only One worthy of both worship and praise.

translation: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who associate partners with Allah or deny His majesty have failed to know Him as He truly deserves to be known. On the Day of Resurrection, His absolute power and lordship will be made manifest: the whole earth will be held in His grasp and the heavens will be folded up by His command. These descriptions express His complete dominion and the total subjection of all creation to Him; they are not to be understood as bodily limbs or resemblance to creatures. He is far exalted above any partners, images, or false claims attributed to Him.

translation: And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse describes the two great blasts of the Horn on the Day of Resurrection. At the first blast, all living beings in the heavens and the earth are struck down and die, except those whom Allah chooses to exempt. At the second blast, the dead are raised to life, and they rise from their graves standing and gazing, fully conscious and awaiting the reckoning. It affirms Allah’s absolute power over life and death, the certainty of resurrection, and the coming accountability before Him.

translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be passed between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse depicts the Day of Judgment as a moment when all falsehood and ambiguity vanish: the earth is illuminated by the light of its Lord, meaning His presence and authority become manifest, and the records of deeds are laid open so nothing remains hidden. The prophets and witnesses are brought forward to testify, and judgment is rendered with absolute truth and justice. The closing phrase, 'and they will not be wronged,' affirms that God’s judgment is perfectly fair—no good deed is diminished, and no one is punished for what they did not do.

translation: And every soul will be fully repaid for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, every person will receive the complete and exact recompense for their deeds, with no injustice or omission. Although records will be presented and witnesses will testify, God already knows perfectly all that His servants did, including their hidden intentions and the true reality of their actions, so His judgment is perfectly just and all-encompassing.

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: 'Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?' They will say: 'Yes, but the word of punishment has become binding against the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the disbelievers being herded toward Hell in crowds after judgment. When they arrive and its gates open, the angels appointed over it confront them with the truth: God had sent messengers from their own people, reciting His revelations and warning them of the encounter with this Day. Their answer, “Yes,” is an admission that the warning truly came, but they had rejected it. Therefore the decree of punishment is justly established against them; their punishment is not because God failed to warn them, but because they knowingly denied His messengers and revelations, so they enter Hell with no valid excuse left.

translation: It will be said: “Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever. So wretched is the dwelling of the arrogant.”
interpretation: This is the final decree issued on the Day of Judgment to those who were too arrogant to submit to Allah and obey His messengers. They are commanded to enter the gates of Jahannam—its various entrances or levels—and are told that they will remain there forever, with no exit or relief. The verse then declares how evil and miserable their final abode is, naming the cause: they were the arrogant, those who refused the truth, rejected divine guidance, and regarded themselves as above worship and obedience. Their worldly self-exaltation ends in everlasting humiliation and punishment.

translation: And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until, when they reach it, and its gates are opened, its keepers will say, 'Peace be upon you. You have done well; so enter it, abiding eternally.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the ultimate honor of the God-conscious: they are not left to wander but are escorted in companies toward Paradise. The opening of the gates signifies welcome and admission, not mere access. The angels' greeting of peace is a divine assurance of safety and acceptance. 'You have done well' (ṭibtum) means their faith, repentance, and righteous deeds have purified them and made them fit for the eternal abode. The command 'enter it, abiding eternally' confirms that Paradise is everlasting, without interruption or end. The verse teaches that piety (taqwā) is the cause of this reward, while the actual admission is by God's grace, and the angels are merely instruments of His hospitality. It also indicates degrees among the people of Paradise, as they come in groups, each according to their rank and deeds.

translation: And they will say, 'Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has made us inherit the earth, so that we may settle in Paradise wherever we wish. How excellent is the reward of the workers.'
interpretation: This verse reports the gratitude of the people of Paradise upon entering it. Their praise is for God's truthfulness and generosity: He fulfilled the promise He made to the righteous and granted them the inheritance of the earth—understood as the vast dwelling of Paradise, or the inheritance of the earth promised to God's righteous servants—so they may choose their dwellings in Paradise freely, without confinement or hardship. The closing statement declares that this eternal, secure, and blissful abode is the best recompense for those who labored in obedience and patience in the worldly life; their efforts were not lost but were rewarded with an everlasting reward.

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, 'All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the culmination of divine judgment: the angels encircle the Throne in humble worship, acknowledging God's majesty and praising Him. Judgment is then rendered with absolute truth and justice, without any wrong or partiality. The final declaration of praise to Allah, Lord of all worlds, affirms that all matters return to Him and that His rule over creation is perfect, wise, and worthy of all gratitude and exaltation.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha Meem.
interpretation: These are among the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta‘at) that begin several surahs of the Qur’an. Their precise meaning is left to Allah, and they serve as a divine sign pointing to the miraculous nature of the Qur’an, which is composed of such Arabic letters, while highlighting the inability of human beings to produce anything like it.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur’an is a revelation sent down by God alone. Its source is not human thought or invention, but Allah, whose power is absolute and whose knowledge encompasses all things. The pairing of al-Aziz and al-Alim shows that the revelation is both authoritative and true: because He is all-knowing, the Book is free from ignorance and error; because He is almighty, His revelation carries binding authority and is protected and upheld by His power.

translation: Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of abundance. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the final return.
interpretation: This verse reveals that Allah's mercy and justice are inseparable: He forgives the sins of those who turn to Him and accepts their repentance, yet He is severe in punishment for those who persist in wrongdoing. His bounty and majesty are limitless, so His commands are not the demands of a needy tyrant but the guidance of a generous Lord. Since no god exists besides Him, every soul must ultimately return to Him alone, where forgiveness and punishment will be apportioned with perfect justice.

translation: None disputes the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so let not their movement throughout the land deceive you.
interpretation: This verse means that rejecting and arguing against Allah’s clear revelations is a mark of disbelief, not sincere inquiry. The worldly ease, success, trade, travel, and influence of such people should not mislead the faithful into thinking that their way is right or that they will escape consequences; their apparent prosperity is temporary and does not alter the truth of Allah’s signs or the certainty of judgment.

translation: Before them the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them. And every nation intended to seize their messenger, and they disputed with falsehood to refute the truth thereby, so I seized them; then how was My punishment!
interpretation: This verse is a warning and consolation: opposition to God’s messengers is an old pattern, not a new event. Earlier communities, including the people of Noah and later confederated groups, rejected the truth and conspired against their messengers, each nation intending to capture or destroy him. Their arguments against the message were not sincere seeking of truth but falsehood used to suppress and invalidate the truth. God’s response was to seize them decisively, meaning His punishment overtook them with justice and power. The rhetorical question “then how was My punishment!” affirms that it was severe, certain, and inescapable. Thus the verse warns the deniers of the Prophet Muhammad that the same divine law applies to them, while reassuring the believers that God will vindicate His message and deal with those who plot against it.

translation: And thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled upon those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This means that God’s decree and promise against those who persist in rejecting faith has become binding and justly established: because they knowingly deny the truth and refuse guidance, their final abode is the Fire. Their disbelief is not overlooked; it earns them the deserved recompense of being inhabitants of Hell.

translation: Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise, and believe in Him, and seek forgiveness for those who have believed: 'Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your path, and protect them from the punishment of Hell.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the angels who carry God's Throne and the angels surrounding it as continuously engaged in praising and glorifying God, firm in faith in Him, and compassionately seeking forgiveness for the believers. Their supplication reveals that God's mercy and knowledge embrace all creation, and it establishes the path of forgiveness: those who turn back to God in repentance and follow His revealed way are granted pardon and safeguarded from the torment of Hell. It teaches that true repentance is paired with steadfast adherence to God's path, and that the company of the faithful is cared for even by the highest angels, directing believers to hope in God's all-encompassing mercy while taking the means of repentance and obedience.

translation: Our Lord, and admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, and whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This is a supplication in which God teaches the angels to pray for the believers: He is asked to grant them the eternal Gardens He has promised and to unite them there with the righteous among their parents, spouses, and children. Its meaning is that Paradise is attained through God’s promise and grace, and that family bonds are perfected in the Hereafter only for those who are righteous in faith and deeds. The ending, “Indeed, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise,” affirms that God has full power to fulfill this promise and perfect wisdom in selecting and gathering whom He wills, so believers are encouraged to seek righteousness for themselves and their families and to hope for reunion in the eternal home.

translation: And protect them from evil deeds. And whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have indeed granted him mercy. And that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This is a supplication for God to shield believers from the evil consequences of their sins on the Day of Judgment. The one whom God protects from those consequences is the one who has been embraced by His mercy, not by personal merit but by divine grace. Such protection from punishment, together with the granting of mercy, is the supreme success, for it means deliverance from ruin and the attainment of eternal safety and bliss.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be addressed: 'Allah's abhorrence of you was greater than your abhorrence of yourselves, when you were invited to faith and you disbelieved.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment being told that God's revulsion toward them, when His messengers invited them to believe and they rejected faith, is far greater than the disgust and self-hatred they feel at that moment upon realizing their doom. It teaches that unbelief after receiving the call to faith is an enormity deserving divine wrath; their regret in the Hereafter cannot match the gravity of their rejection in worldly life. The address is a rebuke and a declaration of perfect justice: they hated themselves for the punishment they earned, but God's hatred of their willful disbelief was greater still.

translation: They will say, 'Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice. So we have acknowledged our sins. Is there then any way to get out?'
interpretation: This is the disbelievers’ confession in the Hereafter after they witness Allah’s absolute power over life and death. They admit that He brought them into existence after they were nothing, then caused them to die, then raised them again for judgment—thus acknowledging His Lordship and their own sins too late. Their plea for a way out of the Fire expresses regret and despair, not repentance that can still be accepted, and the verse implies that no exit remains for them.

translation: That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but if others were associated with Him, you believed. So judgement belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse exposes a willful inversion of the truth in the human heart: it rejects pure devotion to God alone and welcomes the association of false partners with Him. Such a response is not caused by lack of proof but by arrogance and attachment to falsehood. The verse then declares that all judgment and authority belong solely to Allah, who is exalted above every false claim and great beyond all limitation; therefore His decree against those who persist in this perverse rejection is perfectly just and final.

translation: It is He who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky. And none will remember except those who turn [to Him].
interpretation: God alone is the One who manifests His signs and sends sustenance from the heavens, and the only ones who truly heed and remember this are those who turn back to Him in repentance, humility, and obedience, acknowledging His lordship and their need of Him.

translation: So call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This is a command to direct all worship, supplication, and devotion exclusively to Allah, purifying religion from any partner, show, or ulterior motive. Sincerity here means that one’s prayer, obedience, reliance, and ultimate allegiance are for Allah alone. The phrase “even if the disbelievers dislike it” teaches that the obligation of pure monotheism is not dependent on others’ approval or comfort; the hostility of those who reject it must not turn the believer away from exclusive worship of God or from steadfastness upon tawhid.

translation: Exalter of ranks, Owner of the Throne. He sends the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, so that he may warn of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: Allah is far exalted above all creation, the Sovereign Lord of the Throne, who by His command sends the Spirit—meaning revelation and the angel who brings it—to whichever of His servants He chooses, namely the prophets and messengers, so that they may warn people of the Day of Resurrection, when all creation will meet Allah for judgment.

translation: The Day when they will be exposed; nothing about them is hidden from Allah. To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse depicts the Day of Resurrection as the moment when every human being is plainly visible and utterly exposed before God; no deed, intention, or hidden reality remains concealed. Then God Himself asks, as a declaration of His sole authority, “Whose is the dominion today?” and answers that all kingship, power, and control belong exclusively to Allah, the One who is uniquely indivisible in His lordship, and the All-Prevailing who subdues and overcomes all things. It teaches that earthly claims to power are temporary and illusory, and that on that Day God’s oneness and overwhelming sovereignty are fully manifest, leaving no room for any partner, intercessor, or rival to share His rule.

translation: Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will repay every individual exactly according to their deeds, whether good or evil. The verse affirms that no one will be wronged in the least: no person will bear another’s burden, no good deed will be lost, and no evil will be misjudged. God’s reckoning is swift because His knowledge encompasses all things and nothing escapes His awareness or power. This is a call to live with accountability, knowing that divine justice is precise and that each soul will face the consequences of what it has chosen.

translation: And warn them of the approaching Day, when hearts will rise to the throats, choking back [grief]. The wrongdoers will have no loyal friend nor any intercessor who is obeyed.
interpretation: This is a warning about the Day of Resurrection, whose coming is certain and near. It depicts the terror of that moment: hearts leap from their places and lodge in the throats because of overwhelming fear and anguish, while people restrain themselves, unable to speak or act. On that Day, those who wronged themselves through disbelief and sin will find no intimate, compassionate helper, nor any intercessor whose plea for them will be heard and accepted. Every ordinary means of rescue is cut off; relief can come only from God’s mercy and from intercession permitted by Him.

translation: He knows the deceitful glances of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.
interpretation: God’s knowledge is all-encompassing: He perceives even the fleeting, unfaithful look of the eye and knows every hidden intention, thought, and secret within the inner self. Nothing concealed in the heart is beyond His awareness, so this verse calls people to guard their gaze and purify their inward motives.

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him cannot judge anything. Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: Allah alone decides and decrees with perfect truth and justice, whereas the false gods and powers that people call upon besides Him have no authority or ability to judge, decree, or bring about any matter. Because He is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing, He knows every supplication, intention, and deed, and He alone is fully capable of responding and judging rightly.

translation: Have they not journeyed in the land and seen how was the consequence for those who were before them? They were greater than them in strength and in the traces they left in the land, but Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke and warning to those who feel secure because of their power, numbers, and monuments. It tells them that the ruins of earlier civilizations are a lesson: when nations persisted in sin and rejected God’s messengers, their strength could not delay punishment, and their achievements could not shield them. Their fate proves that God’s judgment is inevitable and that no army, wealth, or worldly protector can stand between a sinner and God’s decree. Thus it invites reflection on history so that people repent and submit before punishment comes.

translation: That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is All-Strong, Severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse identifies the reason for the destruction of the deniers: prophetic messengers had already brought clear, undeniable signs, yet the people met them with deliberate rejection. Their disbelief was not due to lack of evidence but to willful denial, so Allah seized them with a grip no power could resist. The names “All-Strong” and “Severe in punishment” show that divine power is absolute and that retribution for obstinate rejection after clear guidance is intensely severe. It warns that rejecting revealed truth carries grave consequences and that no one can escape Allah’s judgment when His decree comes.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse declares that God sent Moses equipped with miraculous signs and an unmistakable, manifest authority, proving that his prophethood was true and that his mission came with decisive evidence from God. It establishes that divine messengers are not mere claimants but are supported by clear proofs that expose falsehood and confirm the truth, so rejecting them is rejecting God’s own signs and authority.

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun; but they said, “A magician and a liar.”
interpretation: This verse describes how Pharaoh, his minister Haman, and the wealthy Qarun responded to Moses when he came to them with clear signs from God. Instead of accepting his message, they slandered him as a sorcerer who performed deceptive tricks and as a liar who falsely claimed prophethood. Their rejection arose from arrogance, vested interests, and attachment to power and wealth, so they judged the truth by their own status and dismissed the messenger rather than reflecting on the evidence he brought.

translation: So when he came to them with the truth from Us, they said, 'Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and spare their women.' But the plotting of the disbelievers is only in error.
interpretation: This verse teaches that when God's truth confronts arrogant worldly power, such power often responds with brutal repression, targeting the vulnerable and trying to cut off the future of the faithful. Yet its schemes are fundamentally misguided and doomed: they may cause suffering for a time, but they cannot cancel God's decree, extinguish faith, or gain lasting victory. Every plot against God's message ultimately ends in failure and loss for those who devise it.

translation: And Pharaoh said, "Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land."
interpretation: Pharaoh’s words reveal how a tyrant cloaks violence in the language of defending religion and public order. He asks his people to let him kill Moses while mockingly granting Moses permission to invoke his Lord, as if divine help could not stop him. His stated fear is not sincere concern for truth but fear of losing control: Moses’ call to worship God alone threatens Pharaoh’s claimed authority over the people’s religion and social order. By calling Moses’ reform “corruption,” Pharaoh redefines good as evil and evil as good, using the fear of upheaval to justify repression. The verse exposes the pattern of oppressive power: it accuses the messenger of corrupting the land while itself being the true source of corruption, injustice, and bloodshed.

translation: And Moses said, 'Indeed, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.'
interpretation: Moses turns to God for protection against the tyranny of the proud who reject accountability before God. By calling Him “my Lord and your Lord,” he affirms that the God he worships is the same Lord over Pharaoh and his people, though they deny Him. The verse links arrogance with disbelief in the Day of Judgment: one who refuses to see himself as answerable to God can easily oppress others and oppose the truth. Seeking refuge in God is therefore an act of trust, not weakness, and a declaration that ultimate judgment and protection belong to God alone.

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said: 'Will you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah, and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is a liar, then his lie is upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.'
interpretation: This verse shows the wisdom of a believer who concealed his faith while living among a hostile and tyrannical court. He defends Moses not by making a reckless declaration before an oppressive ruler, but by exposing the injustice and irrationality of killing someone merely for proclaiming God as Lord, especially when clear signs accompany that claim. His argument places the matter before their own reason: if Moses is false, his falsehood harms only himself; if he is true, then rejecting him will bring at least part of the punishment he warns about. This teaches that truth may be defended with prudence and measured argument when open confrontation would be dangerous or futile, and that concealing faith is permissible when one fears persecution. The closing statement means that Allah withholds guidance from the one who persists in arrogant excess and deliberate falsehood; such a person is not guided because he has chosen corruption and lies over truth.

translation: O my people, today the kingdom is yours, prevailing in the land. But who will protect us from the punishment of Allah if it comes to us? Pharaoh said, “I do not show you except what I see, and I do not guide you except to the path of right guidance.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the delusion of worldly power before divine judgment. The believing adviser warns that dominion, dominance, and security in the land cannot shield a people from God’s punishment when it arrives, so the real question is not who rules but who can avert the decree of God. Pharaoh’s response embodies tyrannical self-deification: he equates his own opinion with truth, presents his personal judgment as the only valid course, and labels his leadership as guidance, even though it leads away from God. The verse thus contrasts sincere warning grounded in accountability to God with the arrogance of a ruler who mistakes power for rightness and demands that people trust his perception instead of divine truth.

translation: And the one who had believed said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you the like of the day of the confederates."
interpretation: The believing man warns his people that if they persist in opposing Moses and rejecting God’s signs, they may be struck by a punishment like that which came upon earlier nations who allied together against their prophets. Those confederated groups united in denial and hostility, but God destroyed them, and their gathering did not save them from His judgment.

translation: Like the fate of the people of Noah, ‘Ad, Thamud, and those after them. And Allah does not will injustice to His servants.
interpretation: This is a warning that rejecting the messenger and persisting in wrongdoing can bring the same pattern of judgment that destroyed earlier nations. Their ruin was not arbitrary: it followed their own habitual denial, arrogance, and corruption. God’s will is never unjust, and He does not wrong His servants; when punishment comes, it is the just consequence of their choices, not oppression from Him. Thus the verse affirms both the seriousness of opposing divine guidance and the absolute justice of God.

translation: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling out to one another.
interpretation: This is the Day of Resurrection, named the Day of Mutual Calling because its terrors will make people cry out and call upon one another for help: the people of the Fire will call to the people of Paradise, the people of Paradise will call to the people of the Fire, and the wrongdoers will call for destruction. The believing adviser fears that his people, if they persist in arrogance and rejection, will meet that Day without any protector against Allah and without any guide after Allah has let them stray.

translation: The Day when you will turn back fleeing; you will have no protector against Allah. And whoever Allah sends astray, there is no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse declares the utter helplessness of those who rejected faith on the Day of Judgment: they will try to flee in panic, but no one can shield them from Allah’s punishment. It also affirms that guidance and misguidance rest ultimately with Allah; those whom He leaves astray because of their persistent defiance will find no one to guide them. Therefore, true safety lies only in seeking Allah’s guidance and protection in this life before that Day comes.

translation: And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you continued to doubt what he brought you, until when he died, you said, 'Allah will never send a messenger after him.' Thus Allah leaves astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter.
interpretation: This verse exposes a recurring human failing: rejecting a messenger after he has brought clear signs, persisting in doubt, and then treating the death of a prophet as proof that God will never send guidance again. Such an attitude is not sincere uncertainty but a combination of excess and skepticism that closes the heart to further revelation. God's way is that He lets the arrogant and doubtful wander from the truth, because they have chosen to resist clear evidence and to limit His power and mercy. It teaches that guidance is not inherited or permanently tied to one messenger; God sends whom He wills, and only those free of defiant transgression and chronic doubt can receive it.

translation: Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them: it is greatly abhorrent in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal the heart of every arrogant, tyrannical one.
interpretation: This verse condemns arguing against Allah's revelations from a stance of arrogance rather than sincere inquiry, because such disputation is not backed by any divinely granted proof or authority. It is a grave offense before Allah and is also repugnant to the believers. The consequence is that Allah places a seal upon the heart of anyone who persists in arrogance and tyranny, meaning such a person is cut off from receiving guidance and understanding. The sealing is a just result of their own self-exaltation and oppressive attitude, a spiritual blindness that prevents the truth from entering. It warns that rejecting divine signs out of pride leads to a hardened heart and divine abandonment.

translation: And Pharaoh said, “O Haman, build for me a tower, so that I may reach the means/causes.”
interpretation: This is Pharaoh’s arrogant attempt to challenge God through material power: he commands Haman to erect a lofty structure, imagining that height, architecture, and worldly authority can grant him access to the heavenly realm and to the God of Moses. It exposes his delusion that physical means can encompass or verify divine truth, and his tyrannical use of others to support his claim to lordship. In Quranic meaning, it exemplifies disbelief that demands a physical sign or ascent while inwardly rejecting the messenger.

translation: The ways of the heavens, so that I may look at the god of Moses, and indeed I think he is a liar. Thus was the evil of his deed made fair-seeming to Pharaoh, and he was turned away from the path. And Pharaoh's scheme was nothing but ruin.
interpretation: This verse exposes the spiritual blindness of Pharaoh: he imagines that God can be reached by building upward through the heavens, reducing the divine to something available to his imperial power and empirical inspection. His claim that Moses is a liar is not the result of honest inquiry but of arrogance and prior self-deification. The statement that his evil was made fair-seeming means that his persistent wrongdoing corrupted his moral perception, so he saw his rebellion as justified and wise. Being turned away from the path means he was blocked from the way of truth and salvation because he chose self-worship over submission to God. His plotting against Moses and the message is therefore not a real threat; it is doomed to failure and perdition, since truth is not reached by material ascent or tyrannical schemes, and God's purpose cannot be defeated by the machinations of the arrogant.

translation: And the one who had believed said, “O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the path of right conduct.”
interpretation: The speaker is the believing man from Pharaoh’s people. His call is an invitation to follow divine guidance, not his own ego: he directs them to the way of Rashad—sound belief, moral integrity, and obedience to God’s messenger—which leads to deliverance in this life and the Hereafter. It teaches that true leadership is guiding people toward truth and righteousness, and that sincere faith gives a person clarity and courage to call others to the straight path even amid a hostile, tyrannical environment.

translation: O my people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the home of permanent settlement.
interpretation: This verse warns that the present world is merely a passing provision and fleeting pleasure, not the true goal of human existence. Its comforts, possessions, and status are temporary and will end. The Hereafter, by contrast, is the enduring dwelling place where every soul will settle permanently according to its deeds. Therefore, people should not be deceived by worldly attractions or let them distract from preparing for the eternal life to come.

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like of it; and whoever does a righteous deed, whether male or female, while being a believer — those will enter Paradise, where they will be provided for without measure.
interpretation: This verse establishes God's justice and generosity. An evil deed is requited only with its equivalent, not multiplied, while a righteous deed joined with faith is rewarded with entry into Paradise and provision without limit. Faith is the essential condition that makes righteous action fruitful and acceptable. The explicit mention of male and female declares that spiritual worth and reward are not based on gender but on faith and righteous conduct. The phrase “without account” points to abundant, unrestricted reward granted by God's grace, showing that His justice is exact and His mercy surpasses the mere requital of deeds.

translation: And O my people, how is it that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?
interpretation: This verse expresses the believing man’s astonishment at his people’s inversion of truth: he invites them to faith in Allah and to the path that delivers from punishment and leads to Paradise, while they invite him to disbelief and disobedience, which lead to the Fire. It shows that the call to divine guidance is a call to salvation, whereas the call to reject Allah and follow falsehood is ultimately a call to ruin. His words also reveal his steadfastness and compassion: despite their opposition, he continues to clarify the two paths and warns them against choosing the way that leads to destruction.

translation: You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I call you to the Almighty, the Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse contrasts two invitations: the call of the people to disbelief and shirk, and the believer’s call to Allah alone. Their demand asks him to reject Allah and set up partners with Him without any knowledge—meaning they have no proof, revelation, or sound basis for the deities they associate. Their path is thus blind and baseless. His invitation is to “the Almighty, the Oft-Forgiving”: the One whose power is absolute and who forgives those who repent. The pairing shows that God’s majesty does not make Him distant from mercy; He is able to overcome falsehood and also ready to forgive. The verse teaches that true faith rests on knowledge and evidence, that shirk is an unjustified plunge into ignorance, and that the call to God unites awe of His power with hope in His forgiveness. It also models the believer’s firmness in refusing to exchange clear monotheism for inherited falsehood, even under pressure from a powerful society.

translation: No doubt, what you call me to has no call [or authority] in this world or in the Hereafter, and that our return is to Allah, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This declaration exposes the utter helplessness and falsehood of the deities or powers being urged upon the believer: they possess no true claim, no ability to answer prayer, no authority to benefit or harm, and no share in the affairs of this life or the Hereafter. Every created being’s final return is to Allah alone, who will judge all matters with perfect justice. Those who transgress the limits set by God—especially through shirk, denial of truth, and persistence in sin—are the ones who belong to the Fire, because their excess in falsehood and rebellion leads them to that fate.

translation: So you will remember what I say to you. And I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: This verse expresses the firm resolve of a believer who, though rejected and threatened, does not retreat from truth or rely on human power. He warns that his words will be recalled when consequences become clear, and he places his whole case in God’s hands. This is true reliance on God: the servant does what is right, speaks the truth, and then entrusts the outcome to Allah alone, confident that Allah sees His servants—their sincerity, their struggles, and the injustice done to them—and will never overlook or neglect them.

translation: So Allah protected him from the evil of what they plotted, and the people of Pharaoh were enveloped by the worst punishment.
interpretation: This verse declares that God safeguards the sincere believer from the malicious schemes of the tyrannical oppressors: their plots cannot harm the one whom Allah shields. It also affirms that divine justice inevitably overtakes the persecutors, so the very evil they intended recoils upon them. The 'worst punishment' that encompassed Pharaoh's household signifies the most severe, humiliating, and inescapable chastisement, showing that worldly power and conspiracy are powerless before God, who rescues the faithful and brings ruin upon arrogant oppressors.

translation: The Fire—they are exposed to it morning and evening; and on the Day the Hour is established, it will be said, 'Admit the family of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment.'
interpretation: This verse states that Pharaoh and his people are already shown the Fire each morning and evening in the interval between death and resurrection, as a foretaste and torment of their coming doom. Then, when the Hour of Judgment begins, they are commanded into the severest punishment. It teaches that Allah's punishment for arrogant tyrants and those who follow them in rejecting truth is both ongoing before the final judgment and fully realized on the Day of Resurrection; worldly authority and wealth cannot shield anyone from divine justice.

translation: And [mention] when they will argue in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, “Indeed, we were your followers, so can you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?”
interpretation: This verse portrays the helplessness and mutual recrimination of the people of Hell. Those who were weak and followed the arrogant in worldly life now turn to their former leaders, admitting that they had followed them, and ask them to bear even a small share of the punishment. But the arrogant, who were proud and led others astray, cannot remove any part of Allah’s punishment from themselves, let alone from their followers. The scene teaches that blind following of corrupt leaders provides no excuse before Allah; each person is accountable for choosing whom to obey. Worldly rank, influence, and numbers are worthless in the Hereafter, and no one can carry the sin or punishment of another. The only following that benefits is following the truth and those who call to it. Thus the verse warns against arrogant leadership and thoughtless imitation, and it affirms that divine justice will not be escaped by shifting blame to others.

translation: Those who were arrogant will say, “Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants.”
interpretation: This verse shows the arrogant leaders in the Fire admitting to their followers that they all share the same punishment and that no one among them can relieve another. Their words acknowledge that God’s judgment has already been passed with perfect justice, so neither worldly rank nor allegiance can change the outcome. It affirms that every soul is accountable before God, and in the Hereafter His decree is final, binding, and impartial, leaving no room for appeal, favoritism, or transferring one’s punishment to another.

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."
interpretation: This verse portrays the utter desperation and helplessness of the people of Hell. They do not ask the angels to save them or forgive them, but only to plead with God to reduce their torment for a single day. It conveys that once punishment is decreed, pleas and intermediaries are of no avail, and that the dwellers of the Fire recognize God's authority yet remain in their state of loss because their request is not for repentance or reform, but merely for temporary relief from suffering.

translation: They will say, "Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?" They will say, "Yes." They will say, "Then call; but the call of the disbelievers is only in error."
interpretation: This exchange exposes the hopelessness of the disbelievers' plea in the Hereafter. The keepers of Hell point out that the messengers had already brought unmistakable evidence, leaving no room for ignorance or excuse; the disbelievers concede this, which confirms that their punishment is just. Their subsequent invitation to 'call' is not a promise of relief but a declaration that any supplication now is futile: it is 'in error' because it is severed from the faith, repentance, and sincere worship that make du'a acceptable to Allah. Thus the verse teaches that calling upon Allah is fruitful only when grounded in true belief and obedience in the time of trial, whereas the disbelievers' invocation is misguided and unanswered.

translation: Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand forth.
interpretation: This is Allah’s firm promise that He supports His messengers and the believers in this worldly life by aiding them, strengthening them, preserving His religion through them, and ultimately vindicating them, even if they face opposition or harm. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, when the witnesses arise—angels, prophets, and created beings testifying to what was done—Allah will fully manifest their victory, honor, and deliverance, and the falsehood of their enemies will be exposed.

translation: On the Day when the wrongdoers will not be benefited by their excuse, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.
interpretation: This verse means that on the Day of Judgment, those who committed wrongdoing—especially by rejecting faith and persisting in sin—will find no apology, justification, or regret of any use. Their excuses will be rejected, they will be cast away from God’s mercy, and their final dwelling will be the worst place: the Fire. It establishes that divine justice is absolute, and at that stage no plea can avert the consequence of one’s deeds.

translation: And We had certainly given Moses guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah granted Moses the means of guidance—the revelation, signs, and clear proofs—and then caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book, meaning the Torah remained with them after him, passing down among their generations as an inheritance. It shows that divine guidance is a gift from Allah, and that receiving the Scripture is both an honor and a responsibility to preserve and follow it.

translation: A guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.
interpretation: It means that the Scripture is a means of directing those endowed with sound reason to the truth and of reminding them of what they must not forget, so that they reflect, take heed, and act rightly.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad]; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: This verse calls for a life of steadfast endurance anchored in the certainty that God's promise is true and never fails. It pairs patience with repentance: the servant must not become self-satisfied while facing opposition or hardship, but should constantly seek forgiveness for personal shortcomings. And it prescribes praise and remembrance of God at the day's two ends, teaching that inner stability comes from worship that begins and ends the day, protecting the heart from arrogance, despair, and heedlessness.

translation: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hidden motive of those who reject or argue against Allah’s revelations without any proof or legitimate authority: it is not sincere inquiry but arrogance—a desire to dominate, debase the truth, or elevate themselves above Allah’s guidance. That pride will never reach its goal, because Allah will frustrate their schemes and protect His signs. Therefore, the believer is taught to seek refuge with Allah from such arrogance and from the harm of its people, trusting that He hears every claim and sees every intention.

translation: The creation of the heavens and the earth is surely greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse presents a divine argument for the reality of resurrection: the origination of the vast heavens and earth, with all their immense scale, precision, and order, is far greater and more wondrous than the creation or re-creation of human beings. If God has power and wisdom to create the greater creation, then bringing people back to life after death is not difficult for Him. Yet most people fail to reflect on this clear evidence, so they do not know the truth of the Hereafter and God's limitless power.

translation: And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse draws a decisive contrast between two spiritual conditions: the blind person who lacks inner sight to perceive divine truth, and the seeing person who is guided by faith and righteous action; likewise, the believer whose life is shaped by good deeds is not the same as the sinner who persists in evil. They are not equal in Allah’s judgment, in value, or in the ultimate end they will meet. The closing rebuke, “Little do you remember,” reproaches those who fail to reflect on this clear difference and thus neglect the path of faith and righteousness.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming — there is no doubt about it — but most people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse asserts with emphatic certainty that the Hour of Judgment will inevitably come, and that its occurrence admits no uncertainty or grounds for doubt. The phrase 'but most people do not believe' identifies the human condition of denying or ignoring that reality: many are heedless of the Hereafter, attached to worldly life, and unwilling to accept accountability before God, even though the truth of the Hour is firmly established.

translation: And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated.
interpretation: This verse teaches that calling upon Allah in supplication is itself an act of worship, and He promises to answer those who turn to Him sincerely. The phrase 'those who are too arrogant to worship Me' refers to those who refuse to humble themselves before Allah and reject His worship out of pride. Their punishment is entering Hell in a state of humiliation and disgrace, showing that arrogance toward Allah is a major cause of ruin.

translation: Allah is the One who made for you the night so that you may rest in it, and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of grace toward people, but most people do not give thanks.
interpretation: This verse directs attention to God’s purposeful ordering of time as a mercy: the night is made for stillness, sleep, and recovery from labor, while the day is made luminous so people can see, move, work, and seek their livelihood. The affirmation that God is full of grace means these benefits and countless others are continuous favors from Him, not due to human merit. Yet most people fail to give thanks by acknowledging the Creator, using His blessings in obedience, and responding with gratitude rather than heedlessness or ingratitude.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him. So how are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the Lord and Creator of everything, and that true divinity belongs to Him exclusively. Since He alone originates, sustains, and governs all creation, worship and obedience are due to Him alone. The rhetorical question rebukes those who acknowledge His lordship yet still turn away from Him or associate others with Him; it exposes the contradiction of recognizing the Creator while denying His exclusive right to be worshipped, and it expresses astonishment at how they can be diverted from such a clear truth.

translation: Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah.
interpretation: The verse states that rejection of Allah’s clear signs produces a state of being turned away from truth and guidance. It is not arbitrary; it is the fitting consequence of persisting in denial: the same hearts that refuse to accept God’s revelations are diverted from the path of faith, so they wander in error. This serves as a warning that denying divine signs hardens one’s perception and leads to spiritual ruin.

translation: Allah is He who made for you the earth a resting place and the sky a canopy, and He formed you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse establishes that every blessing of stability, shelter, bodily form, and pure provision comes from Allah alone. The earth is made habitable and firm for human life, the sky is a protective structure, and human beings are created in the most excellent and balanced form. These favors are not merely physical but signs pointing to His exclusive lordship, so the only proper response is to recognize Him as your Lord and to exalt Him, for His goodness, majesty, and care embrace all creation.

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, being sincere to Him in religion. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true life, absolute existence, and divine authority belong solely to Allah, who is ever-living and self-subsisting. Since no being shares His divinity, worship, supplication, and devotion must be directed to Him alone, purified from any association, pretense, or divided loyalty. The closing praise declares that all gratitude and exaltation rightly belong to Allah, the Lord, Sustainer, and Nourisher of all creation, because He alone possesses the attributes of perfect life, oneness, and lordship that make Him worthy of sincere worship.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah, since clear evidence has come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse declares that after the Prophet received unmistakable signs and guidance from his Lord, he was prohibited from worshipping any being that people invoke besides Allah, because such worship is false and baseless. He was instead commanded to submit himself entirely to the Lord of all creation, affirming pure monotheism and total devotion to Allah alone.

translation: He is the One Who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you out as a child; then He lets you grow until you reach your full strength; then until you become elders. And among you is he who is taken in death before that, and all are made to live so that you may reach an appointed term; and perhaps you will use reason.
interpretation: This verse presents God as the sole Creator and Life-Giver, tracing human existence through successive stages: from dust, to embryonic development, to infancy, then youth and maturity, and finally old age. The progression is meant to awaken people to their utter dependence on Him, since they did not create themselves and cannot control their own formation or lifespan. The fact that some die early while others live to old age, and that all have a fixed appointed term, shows that life is neither random nor autonomous but ordered by divine will and wisdom. The closing call to reason means that reflecting on these signs should lead a person to acknowledge God's power, submit to Him, and affirm the resurrection and final reckoning.

translation: He is the One Who gives life and causes death. And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse affirms that life and death are entirely in God's hand, and that His creative command is absolutely effective. When He wills or decrees anything, He does not need means, helpers, or conditions; His single word 'Be' immediately brings it into existence. Thus all affairs, including resurrection and judgment, are effortless for Him and subject to His sovereign will.

translation: Do you not see those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah—how they are turned away?
interpretation: This verse is a reproach and an expression of astonishment at those who argue against Allah’s revelations. Their disputation is not a sincere search for truth, but a turning away from it; despite clear signs, they are diverted from faith because of arrogance, stubbornness, and following their own desires. It warns that arguing against Allah’s verses leads the heart away from guidance and renders one unable to see the truth.

translation: Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers — soon they will know.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject the revealed Scripture and the message brought by God’s messengers. Their denial will not prevent the truth; soon they will come to know the reality of what they denied and the consequences of their rejection, when regret will no longer benefit them.

translation: When the iron collars are around their necks, and the chains, they are dragged.
interpretation: This portrays the humiliation and helpless compulsion of the arrogant rejecters in the Hereafter: the very necks that once refused submission are bound, and they are dragged by chains without power or dignity. It signifies that worldly strength, status, and defiance cannot protect anyone from God’s judgment, and that those who resisted divine authority will be subdued by force and led to their punishment.

translation: Into the scalding water, then into the Fire they will be burned.
interpretation: This describes the humiliating and agonizing sequence of punishment for those who persist in denial and arrogance: after being dragged by chains, they are plunged first into boiling water that scalds them, and then cast into the Fire, where they are burned and made fuel for its blaze. Their torment is continuous and inescapable, a just requital for their defiance, and it shows that the Fire will consume them without relief or mercy.

translation: Then it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to associate [with Allah]?"
interpretation: This is a rebuke and humiliation for the idolaters on the Day of Judgment: after they are gathered and driven toward the Fire, they are asked where the false gods, idols, and partners they worshipped besides Allah have gone. It exposes the utter falsehood of their shirk, showing that those beings they relied upon cannot be found, cannot intercede, and cannot save them. Their supposed deities have vanished and failed them, proving that worship belongs to Allah alone.

translation: besides Allah. They will say, “They have vanished from us; rather, we did not use to invoke anything before.” Thus Allah leads the disbelievers astray.
interpretation: This verse describes the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment when they are confronted with the false gods they had worshipped besides Allah. Those false objects of worship disappear and cannot help them at all, so the disbelievers admit their loss and even deny having truly called upon anything real. The verse teaches that every false deity is ultimately nothing and cannot benefit or harm, and that Allah leaves the disbelievers in misguidance as a just consequence of their persistent rejection of the truth and their choosing false worship over the worship of the One true God.

translation: That is because you used to rejoice in the earth without right, and because you used to exult.
interpretation: This is a statement of just recompense: their punishment comes because they took pleasure in falsehood, oppression, and worldly power without any legitimate claim to truth, and because they exulted arrogantly and insolently, delighting in their transgression and heedlessness of God. Such rejoicing in wrongdoing and arrogant exultation are themselves causes of ruin, for they reveal a soul that has replaced truth with vanity and accountability with self-satisfaction.

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, abiding eternally therein; and wretched is the residence of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse declares the final end of those who were too arrogant to submit to God and His messengers: they are consigned to enter the gates of Hell and remain there forever. Their arrogance does not elevate them; rather, it leads them to the worst possible dwelling. The verse condemns pride and self-exaltation as the root of their punishment, showing that whoever refuses the truth out of haughtiness will find no honorable place in the Hereafter.

translation: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We cause you to die, to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse commands steadfast patience based on the certainty that Allah’s promise is true and will inevitably come to pass. Whether the believer witnesses the fulfillment of God’s warnings against the oppressors during his lifetime or dies before seeing it, the final outcome is unchanged: all people return to Allah, who will judge them with perfect justice. Patience is therefore sustained by trust in God’s timing and by the assurance that no wrongdoer escapes the ultimate reckoning.

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you. Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it will be judged with truth, and the falsifiers will lose.
interpretation: This verse consoles and instructs the Prophet Muhammad by reminding him that God has sent many messengers before him, some of whose accounts are revealed in the Qur’an and others whose accounts are not. This shows that God’s guidance has been continuous, that His knowledge encompasses all nations and prophets, and that revelation is given according to His wisdom, not human demand. It further teaches that no messenger can produce a miracle, sign, or proof on his own; every sign comes only by God’s permission. Therefore, when God’s decree of judgment or punishment arrives, He judges with truth and justice, and those who reject, deny, or falsify His signs and messengers will be the losers.

translation: Allah is the One who made for you the grazing livestock, so that you may ride some of them, and from some of them you eat.
interpretation: This verse teaches that livestock are among God’s signs and blessings: He alone created and subjected them to human benefit, enabling travel and nourishment. Recognizing this should deepen faith in His oneness and inspire gratitude, obedience, and responsible use of His provisions.

translation: And you have in them benefits, and that you may thereby satisfy a need in your breasts; and upon them and upon the ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah has subjected livestock and ships to human use as means of fulfilling needs that people carry in their hearts—such as travel, trade, seeking livelihood, and pilgrimage. The mention of both land animals and sea vessels shows the comprehensiveness of Allah’s provision and power, since no means of transport can function without His enabling. It calls people to gratitude, sincere reliance on Him, and recognition that every benefit and every journey ultimately depends on His mercy and lordship.

translation: And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?
interpretation: This is a divine rebuke and a call to reflect: Allah continually displays His signs through creation, providence, revelation, and within the human self, so no one has a sound reason to reject or deny any of them. The question exposes the absurdity of willful denial, for every sign points to His existence, power, wisdom, and right to be acknowledged, thanked, and obeyed.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and greater in strength and in traces left in the land, but what they used to earn did not avail them.
interpretation: This verse directs the disbelievers to read history as a lesson: earlier peoples surpassed them in numbers, power, and material monuments, yet their worldly achievements did not save them when they persisted in denying God and rejecting His messengers. The verse thus teaches that outward greatness, wealth, and civilization are not proof of divine favor, and they cannot shield anyone from accountability or from God’s judgment when the root of life is corrupted by arrogance and unbelief.

translation: Then when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in the knowledge they had, and what they used to mock enveloped them.
interpretation: This verse exposes the spiritual disease of self-satisfaction with human knowledge when it turns a person away from revealed guidance.
