Since all affairs ultimately return to Him, every choice, deed, and matter of justice is headed toward His final judgment; therefore, the believer walks this path with accountability, trust, and the awareness that no power can prevent the final return to Allah.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha, Meem.
interpretation: The Basmala invokes Allah’s name and mercy at the beginning of recitation, seeking His blessing and aid. “Ha Meem” belongs to the disjointed letters (al-muqatta‘at) that open several surahs; in this reading, they are a divine sign whose precise meaning is left to Allah, serving to draw attention to the Qur’an, affirm its miraculous nature, and mark the transition into a divine address.

translation: By the clear Book
interpretation: This is an oath sworn by the manifest Scripture, the Qur’an, which is clear in its wording and meaning, illuminating truth and distinguishing right from falsehood, and testifying to its own divine origin.

translation: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’an so that you may understand.
interpretation: Allah informs us that He revealed this Book in the Arabic language, clear and eloquent, so that its intended audience can comprehend its meanings, reflect upon its guidance, and use their reason to grasp its message. The verse thus highlights the divine wisdom in choosing Arabic for the Qur’an and places responsibility upon listeners to understand, ponder, and act upon it.

translation: And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, surely exalted and wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur’an has a preeminent place in the Mother of the Book—the primordial, preserved source of revelation in God’s presence. Its being “exalted” means it is far above any deficiency, distortion, or frivolity, and “wise” means its words, laws, and narratives are perfectly ordered and purposeful. Thus the revelation is not a new or local invention but an expression of the eternal, authoritative, and wise decree with God.

translation: Then should We turn away the Reminder from you, disregarding you, because you are a people transgressing all bounds?
interpretation: This rhetorical question is a rebuke: God does not abandon a people by withholding the Qur’anic reminder merely because they are steeped in excess and sin. Their transgression does not make Him indifferent to them; rather, the reminder continues to reach them as a warning and a call to return. If they persist, their being a transgressing people only makes them more responsible before God, not less deserving of admonition.

translation: And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples!
interpretation: This is a rhetorical statement emphasizing that God sent numerous prophets to earlier generations and nations before the Prophet Muhammad. It consoles the Prophet and warns his people that rejecting a messenger is not new; previous communities also received messengers, and many denied them. The verse affirms the consistent pattern of divine guidance throughout history and implies that those who reject God's messengers will face the same consequences as earlier nations.

translation: And no prophet came to them except that they mocked him.
interpretation: This verse states that mocking the messengers of God is a longstanding habit of those who reject the truth. Whenever a prophet was sent to a people, they belittled and ridiculed him instead of heeding his call. It serves as a consolation to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, that the opposition he faced was not unique, and as a warning that such mockery does not harm the prophet; rather, it exposes the mockers’ stubbornness and prepares them for the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in power, and the example of the former peoples has passed.
interpretation: God destroyed nations greater than the Quraysh in strength and might, showing that their own power cannot protect them from His judgment. The fate of earlier deniers has already become an established precedent: whoever rejects the messengers and persists in arrogance will meet destruction. Thus the verse warns the Meccans that if they continue in denial, they will suffer the same end as those before them.

translation: And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'The Almighty, the All-Knowing created them.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the inconsistency of the idolaters: even they readily acknowledge that the heavens and earth were created by the Almighty, All-Knowing God, because the grandeur, order, and precision of creation point unmistakably to His power and knowledge. Their own confession logically obliges them to worship Him alone, since the One who alone originated and sustains the universe is uniquely worthy of devotion. Thus the verse establishes a decisive argument against associating partners with Him: if they admit He alone is Creator, they have no sound reason to direct worship to anyone else.

translation: It is He who has made the earth a resting place for you and has made roads therein for you, so that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah, out of His mercy, made the earth suited for human settlement and livelihood—stable, spread out, and habitable—and placed within it pathways, routes, and means of travel so that people may reach their destinations and, more importantly, be guided to recognize His power, follow His guidance, and find the right way in both worldly and spiritual matters.

translation: And it is He who sends down water from the sky in due measure, and We revive thereby a dead land—thus will you be brought forth.
interpretation: The verse presents the sending of rain in precise measure and the revival of dead, barren land as a tangible proof of Allah's power and wisdom. If He can bring lifeless soil back to life through water, He is fully able to bring dead human beings out of their graves. The phrase “thus will you be brought forth” establishes that the resurrection is as certain and effortless for Allah as the greening of the earth after rainfall.

translation: And He who created all the pairs, and made for you, from ships and livestock, that which you ride.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah alone is the Creator of every pair and kind, displaying His wisdom in the ordered, complementary, and reproductive design of creation. It then points to His mercy in subjugating both sea vessels and land animals for human transport and benefit. The intended meaning is that these blessings should lead people to recognize His oneness, rely on Him, express gratitude, and use what He provides in obedience to Him rather than in heedlessness or by attributing such power and provision to others.

translation: That you may mount firmly on their backs, then remember the favor of your Lord when you have mounted them, and say, 'Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that when a person mounts an animal or uses a means of transport, they should remember God’s blessing and verbally acknowledge that it is God alone who made it serviceable and controllable. Human beings do not possess the inherent power to tame, subdue, or compel such creatures and conveyances by themselves; it is divine enabling and mercy that place them at our disposal. The prescribed praise—'Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it'—is an expression of gratitude, humility, and tawhid, directing the heart away from self-reliance toward the true Giver of every means and facility.

translation: And indeed, to our Lord we shall surely return.
interpretation: This verse affirms that every person’s ultimate destination is God alone: whatever worldly means, journeys, or blessings we enjoy, we do not remain here forever but must return to our Lord for accountability and recompense. It calls the soul to live with humility, gratitude, and readiness, remembering that all temporary provisions are not an end in themselves but a trust to be used on the path back to Him.

translation: And they have attributed to Him a part from among His servants. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse condemns the polytheists' claim that some of God's creatures—such as the angels—are a part of Him or His offspring. By assigning to the Creator a portion of His own servants, they commit a blatant denial of His absolute oneness and show extreme ingratitude for His blessings. It then declares that human beings, when following falsehood, are openly ungrateful and reject the truth despite clear signs.

translation: Or has He taken, from what He creates, daughters and favored you with sons?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of the polytheists who claimed that angels were Allah’s daughters while they themselves prided themselves on having sons. It exposes their double标准 and false attribution: they assigned to Allah what they would disdain for themselves and reserved for themselves what they considered superior. Allah is exalted far above taking any offspring, male or female; the verse confronts the absurdity and corruption of their belief.

translation: And when one of them is given good tidings of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as an example, his face becomes dark with gloom, and he is suppressing his rage.
interpretation: This verse exposes the pagans’ corrupt double standard: they regarded having daughters as a disgrace and were deeply grieved and angered by the news of a female child, yet they falsely ascribed daughters—or beings they deemed female—to Allah, the Most Merciful. Their own resentment at such an attribution for themselves is a self-evident proof against their blasphemous claim about God. Thus the verse condemns their ignorance and injustice and declares Allah far above the false likenesses and deficient attributes they invented for Him.

translation: And is one who is brought up in adornments and who in dispute cannot make himself clear?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke to the polytheists who despised daughters, viewing them as fit only for adornment and unable to argue clearly, yet they attributed female beings to Allah or called the angels females. It exposes their inconsistency and the contempt behind their claim, exalting Allah above such false and demeaning attributions. It does not establish a universal rule about women; it reports the attitude of that society in order to refute the idolaters.

translation: And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the idolaters who invented a false genealogy for God by calling the angels “daughters” and assigning them femininity. It exposes that they have no basis for such a claim: they were not present at the angels’ creation and possess no revealed knowledge about it. Since the assertion is mere conjecture and a false attribution, it is a testimony for which they are held responsible—it is being recorded against them, and they will be questioned about it on the Day of Judgment. The verse affirms that angels are servants of the Most Merciful, not objects of worship or “daughters” of God, and it warns that speaking about God and the unseen without knowledge is not harmless; it carries accountability.

translation: And they said, “If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them.” They have no knowledge of that; they are only guessing.
interpretation: This verse exposes the polytheists’ false excuse for worshipping others besides Allah. They argued that because their idolatry occurred under Allah’s universal decree and will, it must mean He approved of it. But this is mere conjecture without knowledge. Allah’s will in permitting something to happen is not the same as His command or pleasure; He may allow disbelief as a test while still forbidding it and holding people accountable. Their argument is therefore invalid, because if accepted, it would erase moral responsibility, nullify divine commands, and make the sending of messengers and revelation meaningless.

translation: Or have We given them a Book before it, to which they are clinging?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke: the idolaters have no earlier revealed scripture from God that authorizes their worship of false gods or their rejection of the Prophet. Their supposed divine warrant is baseless; they cling only to inherited conjecture, not to a Book from God. The verse shows that the Qur’an comes with clear authority, while their way lacks any authentic scriptural foundation.

translation: Rather, they say, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are guided by their footsteps."
interpretation: This verse exposes a false basis for faith: people arguing that because their ancestors followed a certain way, they too are rightly guided by imitating them. It condemns blind adherence to inherited tradition as a substitute for divine guidance, showing that ancestral custom is not evidence of truth and cannot justify rejecting God’s revelation. True guidance is not inherited automatically nor proven by numbers or antiquity; it must be based on revealed truth, not merely on following the traces of forebears.

translation: And thus, We did not send before you any warner in a town except that its affluent ones said, 'Indeed, we found our forefathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps.'
interpretation: This verse exposes a recurring pattern in human history: when a divine warner comes to a community, the first to resist are often the affluent and comfortable elite. Their objection is not based on evidence or reasoned argument, but on inherited custom and ancestral authority. By saying that they found their forefathers on a certain way and will follow their footsteps, they make tradition, not truth, the standard of right and wrong. The verse criticizes blind imitation and shows how wealth, status, and social privilege can make people defensive against calls to reform, because accepting guidance may threaten their inherited position and interests. It also consoles the Prophet: rejection is not unique to him but is the same pattern faced by earlier messengers. The real question is not what one’s ancestors followed, but whether one is following divine guidance.

translation: He said, 'Even if I brought you better guidance than that upon which you found your fathers?' They said, 'Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the stubbornness of inherited traditionalism: when truth is presented, such people do not test it by whether it is more rightly guided, but reject it simply because it challenges what their ancestors practiced. Their answer shows that their attachment was not to evidence or guidance but to ancestral authority, and that this attachment led them to outright rejection of the divine message and of those sent with it.

translation: So We took retribution from them; then look how was the outcome of the deniers.
interpretation: The verse declares that rejecting divine messengers brings a just and inevitable punishment, and the command to look urges people to reflect on the historical fate of those who denied so they may turn back before the same end overtakes them.

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship."
interpretation: Abraham publicly declares his complete disavowal and innocence from every object, idol, or being that his father and people worshiped besides Allah. This is not merely a rejection of their rituals but a total dissociation from shirk and a firm commitment to pure monotheism: worship, devotion, and ultimate allegiance belong to Allah alone, and anyone who directs them to other than Him is upon falsehood.

translation: Except the One who created me, for indeed He will guide me.
interpretation: This is Ibrahim’s declaration of pure monotheism: he disavows every false object of worship and turns exclusively to the One who brought him into existence. He affirms that true guidance rests only with his Creator and expresses certainty that He will guide him. It teaches that tawhid requires rejecting all false deities and relying solely on the Creator for guidance.

translation: And he made it an enduring word among his descendants, so that they might return.
interpretation: God preserved Abraham’s affirmation of His oneness as a lasting legacy in his offspring, so that by it they would be reminded and turn back to their Lord in faith, repentance, and obedience.

translation: Nay, I gave enjoyment to these [people] and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a clear Messenger.
interpretation: God’s delay in bringing them to account, and His granting of worldly ease to them and their ancestors, was not a sign of His approval of their inherited ways; it was a period of respite and testing. When the truth and an unmistakable messenger finally came, the criterion became clear: ancestral custom, communal prestige, or long-standing prosperity cannot justify rejecting God’s manifest revelation. Thus the verse teaches that divine generosity may itself be a trial, and that the arrival of a clear prophet removes all excuse, leaving people accountable for whether they submit to the truth or cling to what their forefathers practiced.

translation: And when the truth came to them, they said, “This is magic, and indeed we are disbelievers in it.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the attitude of those who reject revelation not because it lacks proof, but because it opposes their desires, status, and inherited ways. By calling the truth “magic,” they attempt to discredit it and avoid submitting to it, while openly admitting their disbelief. Their response shows that rejection can be a deliberate choice rooted in arrogance and resistance, not an honest conclusion after seeking guidance. It warns that when truth is met with mockery and denial, the problem lies in the heart’s refusal, not in the clarity of the message.

translation: And they said, 'Why was this Qur’an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?'
interpretation: This verse reports the disbelievers’ objection to the revelation being sent to Muhammad (peace be upon him) instead of some prominent, wealthy, or influential leader from Mecca or Ta’if. They judged prophethood by worldly status, tribal prestige, and material power, implying that God should have chosen someone they considered “great.” The verse exposes and refutes that worldly criterion: Allah’s selection of a messenger is based on His wisdom and His knowledge of who is truly fit to carry the message, not on human standards of rank, wealth, or social standing. Thus it condemns their arrogance and superficial judgment, and vindicates the Prophet’s spiritual and moral qualification for the divine message.

translation: Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in ranks, so that some may take others into service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.
interpretation: This verse refutes the idea that human beings have the right to decide whom God’s mercy—especially prophethood and revelation—should be granted to. Allah alone apportions worldly provisions and spiritual favors according to His wisdom. The differences in livelihood and social rank are not evidence of true superiority; they create mutual dependence, so people serve and employ one another in the functioning of worldly life. Yet the mercy of your Lord—faith, guidance, prophethood, and the reward with Him—is far better than all the wealth and goods people gather and hoard. Therefore, divine favor should not be measured by material abundance or social status, nor should anyone object to God’s choice of whom He blesses with His message.

translation: And were it not that mankind would become one community [of disbelievers], We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses, ceilings of silver and stairways upon which they ascend.
interpretation: This means that worldly luxury and splendor are not signs of Allah’s favor or of a person’s closeness to Him. If not for the disastrous consequence that people would all follow the disbelievers in rejecting faith because of envy over such wealth, Allah would have given the disbelievers silver roofs and grand stairways. He withholds that because it would deceive people into thinking material prosperity proves truth, causing humanity to unite in disbelief. The verse therefore teaches that wealth is a trial and that denying the Most Merciful is especially ungrateful, since He is the source of every mercy and provision.

translation: And [silver] doors for their houses, and couches upon which they recline.
interpretation: This describes worldly luxury and adornment—doors and reclining couches—that Allah could have lavished upon the disbelievers as part of their fleeting life. It teaches that material splendor, impressive homes, and comfortable furnishings are not evidence of divine favor or spiritual worth; they are merely passing enjoyments. True honor, permanence, and reward belong to the Hereafter with Allah for those who are mindful of Him.

translation: And ornament. But all that is only the enjoyment of the worldly life; and the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse teaches that worldly pomp, wealth, and ornamentation are transient provisions, not a sign of closeness to God; the lasting reward in the Hereafter belongs exclusively to those who live with taqwa—guarding themselves against sin and seeking God's pleasure.

translation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We assign to him a devil, and he is a companion to him.
interpretation: The verse means that deliberate heedlessness of Allah’s remembrance—rejecting His guidance and turning away from the mercy that calls one back to Him—brings about a satanic companion as a just consequence. Such a person is not merely left without remembrance; he is placed under the persistent influence of a shaytan who stays with him, tempting him, beautifying his misdeeds, and steering him further from return. This companionship is both a punishment and a reflection of the soul’s chosen direction: whoever refuses the remembrance of al-Rahman opens the door for another to occupy that inner vacancy and lead him astray.

translation: And indeed, they divert them from the path, while they think that they are rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse exposes a terrifying form of misguidance: Satanic companions keep turning people away from God’s straight path, yet those led astray remain convinced that they are on the correct way. Their self-assurance is not evidence of guidance; it is itself part of their deception and punishment, because heedlessness of God’s remembrance has darkened their insight until they call deviation guidance.

translation: Until, when he comes to Us [for judgment], he says, 'Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! How wretched is the companion!'
interpretation: The verse signifies that the evil companion who encouraged misguidance—whether a jinn or a human—will become a cause of bitter regret in the Hereafter. The misguided person will wish for the greatest possible separation from him, as far as the east is from the west, and will recognize too late that such companionship was wretched and destructive.

translation: And it will not benefit you this Day, because you wronged, that you are sharers in the punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who wronged themselves in the world by rejecting guidance and following others into misguidance. On the Day of Judgment, their shared suffering will bring them no relief: being companions in punishment will not lighten the torment, remove blame from one another, or serve as an excuse. Just as they participated together in wrongdoing, they will now participate together in its consequence. The verse affirms that punishment is just because they were wrongdoers, and that regret, mutual recrimination, or partnership in sin cannot benefit anyone once the Hereafter has come.

translation: Can you, then, make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and him who is in manifest error?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical address to the Prophet, showing that true guidance is not achieved merely by conveying words or by human effort. The deaf and blind here symbolize those who have closed their hearts and minds to the truth, refusing to hear or see it. Even the Prophet, despite his high station, cannot force such people to accept faith, because they are not merely mistaken but are in clear and manifest error. Their condition requires divine intervention; only Allah can open hearts and grant guidance. Thus the verse consoles the Prophet not to grieve excessively over those who reject the message, and it establishes that his duty is to deliver the truth clearly, while the outcome of guidance belongs to Allah alone.

translation: So if We take you away, then indeed We will take retribution from them.
interpretation: This is a consolation and assurance to the Prophet Muhammad: even if God causes him to depart from this world before he witnesses the punishment of his enemies, God will still hold them accountable and exact justice upon them. The verse teaches that divine retribution is not contingent on the Prophet’s presence or lifetime; God Himself is the Avenger of those who reject His message and persecute His messenger, and His promise of justice will certainly be fulfilled.

translation: Or if We show you what We have promised them, then indeed We are over them fully capable.
interpretation: This is a reassurance to the Prophet that Allah will either take him before the promised punishment falls upon the deniers or let him witness its fulfillment during his lifetime. In either case, Allah has complete power and control over them; they cannot escape His decree, and His promise of judgment is certain.

translation: So hold firmly to that which has been revealed to you; indeed, you are on a straight path.
interpretation: This is a divine command to the Prophet Muhammad—and by extension to every believer—to cling steadfastly to the revelation sent down from God, without deviation, neglect, or alteration. It affirms that the message he received is the true, upright way that leads to God, and it gives reassurance that adherence to it is not error but guidance. The verse thus couples unwavering commitment to revelation with the assurance that such commitment places one on the straight path of truth, justice, and salvation.

translation: And indeed, it is a Reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur’an is a source of honor, admonition, and remembrance for the Prophet and his people, and that all who are addressed by it are accountable before God for how they responded to it—whether they accepted it, conveyed it, and lived by its guidance—and they will be asked about that on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: Did We appoint any deities besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?
interpretation: This verse is a decisive rhetorical question establishing that all previous messengers were sent with one consistent message: worship none but Allah alone. It denies that God ever commanded, authorized, or approved the worship of any being besides Him. The command to “ask” is either directed to the people of earlier scriptures and the followers of past prophets, or it is a rhetorical device emphasizing the universal testimony of prophethood. By naming God “the Most Merciful,” the verse highlights that the One who alone deserves worship is the source of all mercy, while false deities have no power to create, provide, or benefit. Thus the verse refutes every form of polytheism and confirms pure monotheism as the shared foundation of all divine revelation.

translation: And indeed We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said, 'Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: In this verse, God affirms that He sent Moses with clear miraculous signs to Pharaoh and the powerful elite of his court. Moses announced that his authority came not from any earthly ruler but from the Lord of all worlds—the Creator and Sustainer of all existence. This declaration directly challenged Pharaoh’s claim to lordship and called him and his chiefs to recognize the true sovereign, demonstrating that the prophetic mission is universal and that divine authority stands above all human tyranny.

translation: So when he came to them with Our signs, behold, they were laughing at them.
interpretation: This verse condemns the response of Pharaoh and his people to Moses: when the clear divine signs reached them, they did not receive them with reflection or faith but mocked them. Their laughter expresses arrogant rejection of the truth, showing how power, disbelief, and heedlessness can make the heart treat God’s proofs with contempt. It is a warning that divine signs should humble and guide a person, not become objects of ridicule, and that mocking revelation is a mark of spiritual blindness and rebellion.

translation: And We did not show them any sign except that it was greater than its sister, and We seized them with punishment so that they might return.
interpretation: This verse conveys that Allah confronted Pharaoh and his people with successive miraculous signs, each one surpassing the previous in magnitude and clarity, yet their obstinacy persisted. The punishments that followed were not merely vengeful destructions but corrective afflictions meant to humble them, awaken their conscience, and lead them back to faith and obedience. It teaches that divine signs and trials serve as mercy-driven reminders, giving people repeated opportunities to repent, while also showing that hearts entrenched in denial may remain unmoved even by ever-greater wonders.

translation: And they said, 'O sorcerer, invoke your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you; indeed, we will be guided.'
interpretation: Pharaoh's people addressed Moses with contempt as a sorcerer, asking him to use the special covenant or rank God had given him to pray away the punishment. Their promise to be guided was not sincere faith but an expedient plea under suffering. It exposed their obstinacy and deceit, since they later broke their word once the torment was removed. Thus the verse condemns mocking God's messengers and making hollow promises of belief merely to escape hardship.

translation: But when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke their word.
interpretation: This means that their turning to God was not sincere: they only wanted the hardship lifted, not to submit to the truth. As soon as relief came, they immediately violated the covenant they had made and returned to their former denial and wrongdoing. It is a condemnation of breaking pledges to God and a warning that ease often reveals whether faith and repentance are genuine.

translation: And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying, “O my people, is not the dominion of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not then see?”
interpretation: This verse depicts Pharaoh’s demagogic self-exaltation: he appeals to his ownership of Egypt and the rivers flowing beneath his palaces as proof that he alone deserves obedience, thereby equating earthly power with truth and trying to dazzle the people away from Moses’ call. His rhetorical question “Do you not see?” invites them to judge by visible wealth and sensory spectacle rather than by God’s signs, and it exposes the tyrant’s habit of masking his false claim to lordship behind material prosperity and national pride. In reality, the kingdom and rivers are blessings bestowed by God, so Pharaoh’s boast is not evidence of his divinity but of his ingratitude and arrogance.

translation: Or am I better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly make himself clear?
interpretation: This is Pharaoh’s arrogant attempt to discredit Moses before his people by measuring worth through social rank and eloquence. It exposes the tyrant’s tactic of mocking God’s messenger as lowly and inarticulate so that the audience will dismiss the message without considering its truth. The verse warns against judging divine guidance by the messenger’s worldly status or rhetorical polish, and it condemns the conceit that power, wealth, and fluent speech are signs of superiority.

translation: Why then have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him, or angels come along with him as companions?
interpretation: This reports Pharaoh’s arrogant demand that Moses, as a supposed messenger, meet his own worldly standards of royal honor and supernatural display—golden armlets and an escort of angels. It exposes how Pharaoh judged prophethood by material pomp and status rather than by truth, and how such demands are often not sincere requests for guidance but pretexts for rejection. The verse criticizes those who will believe only if the messenger conforms to their own expectations of power, wealth, and visible glory, instead of humbly considering the message itself.

translation: So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse describes how Pharaoh manipulated and deceived his people, making falsehood appear easy and attractive so that they followed him without sound proof or reflection. Their obedience was not forced merely by his power; it exposed a deeper corruption in them, as they had already turned away from God's guidance and were inclined toward rebellion and moral deviation. Thus, a tyrant can mislead only those who are already disposed to disobedience, and the people bear responsibility for consenting to his false leadership.

translation: So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all together.
interpretation: This verse means that Pharaoh and his followers persisted in arrogant disbelief, oppression, and rejection of God’s signs until they provoked His just wrath; therefore He punished them by drowning them all, leaving none of that tyrannical nation escaping His judgment. It affirms that when people knowingly persist in rebellion and injustice, divine retribution is certain and comprehensive, and no worldly power can resist it.

translation: And We made them a precedent and an example for the later generations.
interpretation: Allah made the destroyed tyrants and their followers a forerunning lesson and a warning sign for all who come after them, so that later people may see the end of denial, arrogance, and oppression, take heed, and not follow the same path.

translation: And when the son of Mary is presented as an example, at once your people turn away from it.
interpretation: This means that when Jesus, the son of Mary, is cited as a case in point—showing that he is a created servant and prophet, not a deity—the disbelievers among your people recoil and dismiss it, not with serious inquiry but with aversion and argument. They use his mention only as a pretext to dispute the Prophet, revealing their hardened refusal of monotheism. The verse thus censures their obstinacy: they reject the truth even when it honors Jesus, because their real motive is not reverence for him but resistance to the call to worship Allah alone.

translation: And they said, 'Are our gods better, or is he?' They did not present it to you except as a dispute. Rather, they are a contentious people.
interpretation: Their question was not a sincere search for truth but a polemical trap. By asking whether their idols or Jesus is better, they sought to score a debating point against the Prophet, not to accept guidance. The verse therefore rebukes their mindset: they are a people who argue for the sake of argument and resist the truth through disputation. The comparison itself is invalid, since Jesus is Allah's honored servant, not a deity to be ranked alongside idols.

translation: He was nothing but a servant whom We blessed and made an example for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse refers to Jesus, peace be upon him, and affirms that he is only a servant of God, not divine. God favored him with prophethood, miracles, and a miraculous birth, and made him a sign and lesson for the Children of Israel—a proof of God's power and a call to worship the One God alone and follow His messengers, not to worship Jesus himself.

translation: And if We willed, We could have made angels from among you succeeding one another on the earth.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's unrestricted power and freedom in creation and succession: had He willed, He could have brought angels into existence from among human beings or made them the successors on earth instead of humans. Thus the appointment of humans as vicegerents on earth is purely by His will and wisdom, not because He is unable to create otherwise or to replace them with angels.

translation: And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour, so do not doubt it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse refers to Jesus, whose return before the Day of Judgment will serve as a clear sign that the Hour is near. It commands people not to doubt the resurrection and to follow God's guidance, for His message is the straight path leading to Him.

translation: And let not Satan divert you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This is a warning and prohibition: do not let Satan turn you away from God’s straight path through his whisperings, temptations, or false promises. His enmity toward you is open and manifest, so he should be treated as an enemy whose suggestions are rejected and whose traps are avoided by holding fast to divine guidance and obedience.

translation: And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, 'I have come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ. So fear Allah and obey me.'
interpretation: This verse presents Jesus as a messenger of Allah supported by clear signs and miracles. The 'wisdom' he brought refers to prophethood, revelation, and sound teaching. He came to clarify some of the religious matters about which the Children of Israel differed, not to claim divinity or lordship. His command, 'So fear Allah and obey me,' means that obedience to him is obedience to Allah’s message, and that people should follow him as Allah’s prophet while directing ultimate fear and worship to Allah alone.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse establishes pure monotheism: Allah is the sole Lord, Creator, and Sustainer of all—including Jesus and his followers—so all worship must be directed to Him alone. The path of exclusive devotion to Allah, without partners or intermediaries in worship, is the upright, direct way that leads to His pleasure and salvation.

translation: But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful Day.
interpretation: This verse warns that after the clear message of God’s oneness brought by Jesus, people split into competing factions—some believing, others rejecting, and others exceeding the limits by deifying him or distorting the truth. Their disagreement was not harmless; it became injustice, because it led them away from pure monotheism and the messenger’s call. The “woe” is the ruin and sorrow awaiting those who persist in such wrong when they face the painful punishment of the Day of Judgment. It calls people to hold firmly to revealed truth without sectarian distortion and to fear the consequence of siding with falsehood.

translation: Do they await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?
interpretation: This is a warning and rebuke to those who deny or delay belief: the Day of Judgment will not announce itself or come at a time they expect, but will overtake them abruptly when they are heedless. Therefore, they should not wait for it in mockery or negligence, but should repent and prepare before it arrives.

translation: Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, every intimate friendship and bond formed on worldly interests, sin, or disbelief will turn into hostility, because those companions will see how they led one another away from Allah or failed to benefit each other when it mattered. The only friendships that remain safe and beneficial are those of the God-fearing, whose love was grounded in faith, righteousness, and mutual encouragement upon truth; they will not become enemies, but will be close allies in the mercy and reward of Allah.

translation: O My servants, no fear will be upon you today, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: This is God’s gracious address to His believing servants on the Day of Resurrection, honoring them by calling them His servants and assuring them that they have nothing to fear concerning their final outcome and nothing to grieve over from their past losses or hardships. Their faith and submission have brought them to perfect security, joy, and acceptance with their Lord.

translation: Those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims.
interpretation: This describes the people who truly belong to God: their faith is fixed on His revealed signs, and it is not mere intellectual assent but is joined to wholehearted submission to Him. “Muslims” here does not denote a later communal identity; it means those who have surrendered their will to God, accepted His guidance, and lived in obedience to Him. Thus the verse presents faith and submission as inseparable: believing in God’s signs necessarily leads to yielding to His authority, and that inward belief and outward surrender together form the character of those who are honored and secured by God.

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing.
interpretation: This is a divine address to the believers on the Day of Judgment, granting them entry into Paradise together with their righteous spouses and announcing that they will be in a state of enduring joy, delight, and honor, free from every sorrow and hardship.

translation: They will be served with plates of gold and cups, and therein will be whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and you will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse describes the honor and perfect bliss of the people of Paradise: they are attended with golden vessels as a sign of dignity and abundance, their every inward desire and outward delight is fulfilled, and their enjoyment is everlasting. It teaches that Allah’s reward for the righteous is complete satisfaction, unending joy, and eternal security, far beyond any worldly pleasure.

translation: And that is Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do.
interpretation: This means that God grants Paradise to the believers as an inheritance because of the righteous deeds they performed in obedience to Him; their actions are the means He appointed for attaining it, while the gift itself remains from His grace and favor.

translation: For you therein is abundant fruit, from which you eat.
interpretation: This describes the people of Paradise enjoying plentiful and varied fruits that are always available to them; they eat from them freely as a lasting reward, delight, and honor from God, not out of necessity or scarcity.

translation: Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally.
interpretation: It means that those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing are consigned to the torment of Jahannam, where they remain forever, never leaving it; this is the recompense for their denial of God and their evil deeds.

translation: It will not be lightened for them, and they will be in it in despair.
interpretation: This verse describes the unrelenting nature of the punishment of the Hereafter for those who persistently rejected faith and committed evil. Their torment will never pause, decrease, or be interrupted, and they will be overcome by hopeless despair, realizing that no relief, rescue, or reprieve will come to them.

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers themselves.
interpretation: This verse establishes God’s absolute justice: the punishment they receive is not an unjust imposition from God but the direct consequence of their own persistent wrongdoing. They had been given guidance and warning, yet they chose denial, arrogance, and rebellion, thereby wronging themselves. The fault and blame therefore rest entirely upon them, not upon God.

translation: And they will call out, 'O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!' He will say, 'Indeed, you are staying.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the disbelievers in Hell pleading with Malik, the angel appointed over it, to ask God to cause them to die and thereby escape their torment. Malik’s reply, 'Indeed, you are staying,' means that there will be no death or relief for them; they will remain in punishment permanently.

translation: We have certainly brought you the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth.
interpretation: This verse is a divine reproach to those who reject the truth after it has clearly come to them. It affirms that the message brought by Allah’s messengers is true and undeniable, and that the majority’s rejection is not caused by any flaw in the truth itself but by their own arrogance, stubbornness, and unwillingness to abandon their desires and inherited ways. It warns that aversion to truth leads to ruin, and it calls people to humble acceptance and submission to what Allah has revealed.

translation: Or have they firmly resolved a matter? Then indeed, We are firmly resolving [Our matter].
interpretation: This verse affirms that whatever secret or open plan the deniers devise against God’s messenger and His religion, God’s own decree is decisive and unaffected by their scheming. Their resolve cannot escape His knowledge or power, and He will carry out His will, protect His truth, and bring their plotting to nothing.

translation: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, indeed, and Our messengers are with them, recording.
interpretation: This verse is a decisive rebuke to those who imagine that their hidden intentions, whispered plots, and confidential councils escape God’s knowledge. God affirms that He hears both what is kept secret and what is shared privately, and He has angels present with them who record everything. Its meaning is that divine omniscience encompasses the innermost and outermost dimensions of human speech and action, and no secret remains outside the scope of God’s awareness or the record that will serve as the basis for accountability and recompense.

translation: Say, “If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers.”
interpretation: This is a rhetorical conditional that negates the premise itself: it declares that if Allah had a son—which is impossible—the Prophet would be the first to worship that son. But since Allah is absolutely One and has no offspring, he is instead the foremost in worshipping Allah alone and in rejecting any son or partner ascribed to Him.

translation: Exalted is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they attribute.
interpretation: This verse declares Allah’s absolute transcendence and purity from every false claim or description invented about Him, such as attributing to Him partners, offspring, or any imperfection. As the Lord and Sovereign of the heavens, the earth, and the Throne, He is far above and beyond the limited, false depictions of Him given by those who reject or distort the truth. It calls believers to affirm His perfect oneness and majesty and to speak of Him only as He has revealed.

translation: So leave them to indulge in idle talk and play until they encounter their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This is a divine consolation and warning: the Prophet is told not to let the mockery and frivolous preoccupations of the deniers consume him, for their respite is only in a fleeting world. Their vain disputation and amusement cannot avert the appointed Day of Resurrection, when they will meet the promised reckoning and its consequences. The verse thus exposes the emptiness of their denial, assures the believer that God’s promise is certain, and warns that the time granted to the rejecters ends when that Day arrives.

translation: And it is He who is God in heaven and God on earth, and He is the Wise, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the true deity worthy of worship in the heavens and on the earth. His divinity, lordship, and right to be worshipped are not confined to one realm or place; all beings in the heavens and the earth are His creation, depend upon Him, and are subject to His command. He is al-Hakim, perfectly wise in all His decrees and actions, and al-Alim, whose knowledge encompasses all things, outward and inward, seen and unseen.

translation: And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them; and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse declares God's supreme blessedness and sovereignty: He alone owns and governs all creation, seen and unseen, and He alone possesses exclusive knowledge of the Day of Resurrection. It calls people to live with accountability, knowing that their final return is to Him for judgment.

translation: And those whom they invoke besides Him do not possess [the power of] intercession, except those who bear witness to the truth, and they know.
interpretation: The verse negates any independent power of intercession for false deities or any being invoked besides Allah. The only exception is those who knowingly bear witness to the truth of Allah's oneness—such as prophets and angels—who may intercede, but only by Allah's permission, not by any power of their own.

translation: And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse exposes the contradiction of those who deny the truth: even they instinctively acknowledge that Allah alone is their Creator, yet they still turn away from worshipping Him alone and from the guidance He sent. Their own admission leaves them without excuse, so their deviation is not due to lack of evidence but to willful distortion and turning away from the obvious truth.

translation: And his saying, 'O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe.'
interpretation: This verse conveys the Prophet’s heartfelt complaint and supplication to Allah concerning his people’s persistent rejection of faith. It shows his sorrow at their disbelief, his turning to his Lord for relief, and his acknowledgment that their refusal to believe is a condition only Allah can ultimately judge or cure. It also serves to console the Prophet and to warn those who stubbornly reject the truth.

translation: So overlook [their offenses] and say, "Peace"; for they will soon know.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet—and, by extension, believers—to respond to rejection and mockery with magnanimous forbearance rather than retaliation. The command to "overlook" does not deny the wrong; it entrusts judgment to God. The greeting of peace is a refusal to return hostility with hostility, preserving the caller’s dignity and leaving the door open for repentance. The closing warning, "they will soon know," affirms that God’s justice is certain: those who persist in denial will inevitably come to see the truth and face its consequences.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: These are among the Qur'an's disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'at) that open several surahs; their exact meaning is known to Allah, and they serve as a divine sign pointing to the inimitability and revealed origin of the Qur'an, preparing the listener for the guidance that follows.

translation: By the clear Book.
interpretation: Allah swears by the Qur’an, the Scripture whose verses are perspicuous, clearly separating truth from falsehood and guiding to the straight path; the oath confirms its lofty rank and the certainty of its message.

translation: Indeed, We sent it down in a blessed night. Indeed, We have always been warning.
interpretation: This verse declares that the Qur’an was revealed in a night filled with divine blessing, commonly understood as the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), a time of mercy, guidance, and decree. God’s sending down of revelation is not arbitrary but serves the purpose of warning humanity: to awaken them from heedlessness, remind them of their accountability before their Creator, and call them to faith, obedience, and righteousness. The statement “Indeed, We have always been warning” affirms that warning through prophets and scriptures has been God’s consistent method of guiding people, so that no one may claim they were not informed or warned.

translation: In it, every wise matter is made distinct.
interpretation: This verse means that in the blessed night (the Night of Decree), Allah separates and determines all the decrees of the coming year with perfect wisdom. The angels receive these decrees—provisions, lifespans, calamities, blessings—so that everything unfolds exactly as Allah has wisely ordained. It emphasizes that the night is one of decree and that Allah's governance is precise, wise, and comprehensive.

translation: A command from Us. Indeed, We have ever been sending [messengers].
interpretation: This verse means that the decrees and revelations sent down on that blessed night issue from Allah’s authoritative command, and that Allah’s sending of messengers is His established, ongoing way of guiding creation. He does not leave humanity without a summons to truth, but continually sends warnings and glad tidings so that His command and mercy reach them.

translation: A mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The revelation and messengers sent by God are a mercy from the Lord to His creation. Because He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, He hears every need, plea, and unspoken condition, and He knows what is best for His servants; thus His guidance and provision are rooted in perfect knowledge and compassion.

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are to be certain.
interpretation: This verse declares that the Lord to whom Moses calls is the sole Creator and Sovereign of the heavens, the earth, and every created thing between them. The phrase 'if you are to be certain' is a challenge to Pharaoh and his people: if they truly reflect and possess sure conviction, they must acknowledge that the One who originated, sustains, and governs all these realms cannot be anyone other than God. The vastness, order, and interdependence of the heavens, earth, and all that lies between them are signs pointing to His oneness, power, and knowledge, and they negate every false claim of lordship besides Him. Thus, true certainty should lead the heart to worship, trust, and submit to Him alone.

translation: There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death—your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.
interpretation: This verse establishes pure monotheism: no being deserves worship except Allah. He alone originates life and decrees death, so all authority over existence and mortality belongs exclusively to Him. By naming Himself the Lord of the addressed people and of their forefathers, it teaches that the same sole Creator and Sustainer has been the Lord of every preceding generation; therefore, inherited ancestral practices cannot justify associating others with Him. It summons people to worship the One who governs life, death, and all generations.

translation: Nay, they are in doubt, playing.
interpretation: This verse rebukes those who deny the revelation: their rejection is not grounded in certainty but in unsettled doubt, and they treat the matter of faith as amusement rather than with seriousness. It exposes a heedless attitude that avoids sincere reflection and accountability, warning that such playfulness cannot shield them from the truth they mock.

translation: So await the Day when the sky will bring a clear smoke.
interpretation: This is a command to await and watch for a promised sign: a manifest smoke that will come from the sky. In one interpretation, this smoke is a major portent of the Hour, a visible and undeniable divine warning that will precede severe punishment for those who persist in denial, while the believers are told to remain steadfast and await God's decree, which will surely come to pass.

translation: covering the people — this is a painful punishment.
interpretation: It means that the smoke will envelop and overwhelm the people, and that this enveloping is itself a severe, agonizing chastisement from Allah inflicted upon them for their denial and wrongdoing.

translation: Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed, we are believers.
interpretation: This is the plea of the deniers when the chastisement overwhelms them: they beg God to lift the torment and claim faith in exchange for relief. It conveys that faith uttered only under the pressure of punishment is not sincere, voluntary belief; it is a bargaining acknowledgment, not true submission. Therefore, such a claim does not carry the value of faith freely chosen before witnessing torment.

translation: How will the reminder benefit them, when a clear messenger has already come to them?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke: it points out that their belated remembrance, warning, or plea for faith will not avail them, because the truth had already reached them through a manifest messenger who brought clear signs and warning. Their rejection after such clear proof leaves no excuse, so the verse emphasizes that the time for beneficial reflection has passed once they persist in denial.

translation: Then they turned away from him and said, “A taught one, a madman.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbelievers’ rejection of the Messenger: rather than accepting the clear signs and guidance brought to them, they turned their backs on him and slandered him as someone merely taught by others and as insane. Their accusation was not a reasoned denial but an arrogant dismissal, attributing divine revelation to human instruction and madness in order to avoid submitting to its truth.

translation: Indeed, We shall remove the punishment for a little while; indeed, you will return [to disbelief].
interpretation: Allah tells the obstinate disbelievers that the relief from the punishment or famine they are experiencing will only be temporary; it is a brief respite and a test, not an acceptance of their false promises. Once the hardship is lifted, they will inevitably revert to their former denial, shirk, and rejection of the truth, showing that their repentance was not sincere.

translation: On the Day We shall seize with the greatest seizure, indeed We are the Avenger.
interpretation: This verse warns that when God brings His decisive punishment upon those who persist in denial and wrongdoing, it will be an overwhelming and inescapable seizure. It declares that this is not arbitrary destruction but just retribution: God will exact vengeance for their rejection of Him and their sins. The “greatest seizure” points to the most severe punishment, affirming that no power can resist or escape it when He wills to take retribution.

translation: And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger.
interpretation: This verse reminds the rejecters that God's way of testing nations is not new: before them, the people of Pharaoh were tested by the coming of Moses, a messenger honored by God and noble in character. Their refusal to accept him despite clear signs brought about their ruin. The verse thus warns the Quraysh and all who oppose the truth that rejecting a divinely sent messenger is a grave trial whose consequence is destruction, while it also consoles the Prophet and the believers that hostility toward God's messengers is an ancient pattern and that God will ultimately judge between truth and falsehood.

translation: Deliver to me the servants of Allah. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This is the demand of Allah’s messenger Moses to Pharaoh and his people: release the Children of Israel from enslavement and let them go with him. He supports this call by declaring that he is a trustworthy messenger sent by Allah, faithful in delivering His message, so they should heed his warning and obey the command of Allah rather than persist in oppression.

translation: And [saying], “Do not exalt yourselves against Allah. Indeed, I come to you with a clear authority.”
interpretation: This is a warning from a divine messenger, Moses, to Pharaoh and his people not to rise up in arrogant defiance against Allah’s command. It affirms that his message is not a claim based on personal power but is supported by a manifest divine proof—a clear sign and authority that validates his prophethood. The verse thus teaches that arrogance toward God and His messengers is unjustified, especially when the truth has been made evident, and that rejecting such clear authority leaves one without excuse.

translation: And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker turns to God for protection, calling Him both his Lord and the Lord of his adversaries. He seeks refuge from their threat to stone him, entrusting his safety to the One who has authority over all. The verse teaches that when facing hostility or harm, the believer should rely on God alone; the enemies’ power is limited and subject to God’s will, and seeking His refuge is the surest defense.

translation: And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone.
interpretation: This is Moses’s address to Pharaoh’s people: after they reject his message, he does not ask them to believe by force, but asks them to stop opposing, harming, or obstructing him. It teaches that the caller to truth is only responsible for conveying the message; if people refuse faith, they should at least leave him free to worship God and carry out his mission, while judgment belongs to God alone.

translation: So he called upon his Lord, [saying], “These are indeed a criminal people.”
interpretation: Prophet Moses turns to God after Pharaoh and his people persist in rejection and oppression. His prayer is not merely a complaint but a declaration that they are guilty of crime—denying God’s signs, tyrannizing the believers, and stubbornly resisting the truth. It expresses reliance on God against human tyranny and asks for divine judgment, since they have knowingly transgressed and deserve the consequences of their injustice.

translation: So set out with My servants by night; indeed, you will be pursued.
interpretation: This is a divine command to Moses to lead God's believing servants out of Egypt under cover of darkness, away from Pharaoh's oppressive dominion. The night journey signifies a decisive break from persecution and a movement toward freedom and deliverance. The statement that they will be pursued conveys that Pharaoh and his forces will follow them, but this is not a threat to God's plan; rather, it is part of the unfolding of divine judgment. God is informing Moses beforehand so that he will not fear the pursuit, for the same power that commands the escape will also protect the believers and destroy the pursuers. The phrase "My servants" honors the believers by linking them directly to God, showing that He is their true Master and Protector, while Pharaoh's claim to lordship is false. Thus the verse combines mercy toward the oppressed, certainty of divine aid, and the coming downfall of tyranny.

translation: And leave the sea as it is—indeed, they are an army to be drowned.
interpretation: After Moses had struck the sea and led the Children of Israel across on a dry, parted path, God commanded him to leave that path open and still, without striking the sea again to close it. This was so that Pharaoh and his pursuing forces would follow them into the seabed. Once they entered, the waters would close over them, drowning the entire army. The verse declares that Pharaoh’s host was already decreed for destruction, and it demonstrates God’s power to rescue the oppressed and destroy the tyrannical persecutors.

translation: How many gardens and springs they left behind!
interpretation: The verse underscores that worldly abundance is a fleeting trust, not a shield against divine justice. Oppressive power, however splendid, can be uprooted suddenly, and its owners are left with nothing but the consequences of their deeds. It warns that blessings may become evidence against a people when met with arrogance and transgression.

translation: And crops and a noble station.
interpretation: This describes the worldly blessings and honor that Pharaoh and his people enjoyed and then abandoned when Allah destroyed them for their arrogance and rejection of Moses. It conveys that cultivated lands, wealth, and high social standing are temporary and cannot protect those who persist in disbelief and oppression from Allah’s judgment.

translation: And blessings in which they were enjoying themselves.
interpretation: The verse treats worldly ease as a favor that can become an intoxicating state: those addressed were immersed in comfort and pleasure, taking their abundance as the measure of success. Its meaning is that such enjoyment, when it becomes heedless self-satisfaction, is fragile and accountable; it can be withdrawn at any moment, and the real value of blessing lies in whether it is received with gratitude and used in obedience to God, not in being absorbed by it.

translation: Thus. And We caused another people to inherit them.
interpretation: The verse affirms that after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, Allah transferred their gardens, springs, treasures, and noble dwellings to a different people, showing that divine punishment removes the oppressors from their worldly blessings and replaces them with others. “كذلك” confirms that the matter occurred exactly as described, and “قوما آخرين” emphasizes that the new inheritors were not the same people, highlighting Allah’s absolute authority to bestow and transfer dominion as He wills.

translation: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them, nor were they given respite.
interpretation: This verse describes Pharaoh and his followers after their destruction: their deaths were so devoid of righteousness and so insignificant before God that neither the heavens nor the earth grieved for them. It also states that they were granted no delay or reprieve once the decree of punishment came. Their worldly power could not earn them mercy or postpone judgment, showing the utter helplessness of tyrants before God and the worthlessness of lives lived in defiance of Him.

translation: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Children of Israel of His favor: He delivered them from the degrading oppression and torment they endured under Pharaoh, including the slaughter of their sons and the enslavement of their women, and brought them out of Egypt to safety. This was a manifest rescue from humiliation and a sign of His power and mercy toward them.

translation: From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty, one of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse exposes Pharaoh as the archetype of tyrannical self-exaltation. His being “haughty” was not merely social superiority but a spiritual disease: he set himself above truth, above his people, and even above God, claiming a lordship that was not his. Being “among the transgressors” means he exceeded every bound in disbelief, cruelty, enslavement, and the slaughter of the innocent. Thus the deliverance of the Children of Israel was not only release from physical oppression but liberation from a corrupt order whose root was Pharaoh’s arrogant refusal to acknowledge the true Lord. His end shows that whoever exalts himself beyond God’s limits is ultimately brought low.

translation: And indeed We chose them knowingly over the worlds.
interpretation: This means that Allah favored the Children of Israel with a special selection among the peoples of their time—by giving them prophets, scriptures, miracles, and leadership—not out of ignorance or favoritism, but according to His perfect knowledge and wisdom. It was a distinct favor and a test for them, not an absolute superiority of every individual among them over all humanity for all time.

translation: And We gave them of the signs that which in it was a manifest trial.
interpretation: This means that God granted the Children of Israel clear divine signs and miracles, but these were not only favors—they were also a manifest test. The signs exposed their true response: whether they would show gratitude, obedience, and faith, or whether they would deny, forget, and rebel. Thus the verse presents the miracles as a clear trial by which sincerity is distinguished from ingratitude and by which the divine proof is established against them.

translation: Indeed, these [people] surely say,
interpretation: This is a divine rebuke of the persistent, self-assured denial of the truth by those who reject revelation; it stresses that their claim is not a fleeting uncertainty but a repeatedly asserted position, and it prepares to expose its falsehood and hold them accountable for it.

translation: It is only our first death, and we will not be resurrected.
interpretation: This is a denial of the resurrection and the hereafter. The speakers assert that human existence ends completely with the first death, so there is no return to life, no raising from the graves, and no accountability before Allah. It expresses a rejection of divine power to recreate and of the reality of final judgment.

translation: So bring our forefathers [back], if you are truthful.
interpretation: This is a report of the disbelievers’ mocking challenge: rather than accepting the clear signs and the message of resurrection, they demanded that their dead ancestors be brought back to life as proof. They made this an unreasonable condition for belief, not out of sincere seeking for guidance, but out of stubborn denial and ridicule. It exposes their rejection of the resurrection and their refusal to submit to the truth despite clear evidence.

translation: Are they better, or the people of Tubba‘ and those before them? We destroyed them; indeed, they were criminals.
interpretation: This is a warning to the Quraysh who rejected the Prophet: do not think yourselves superior to the people of Tubba‘ and the earlier nations whom Allah destroyed. Their destruction was because they persisted in disbelief, oppression, and sin. The verse teaches that Allah’s punishment falls upon those who commit crimes and reject His messengers, so Quraysh are cautioned that their wealth, power, or lineage will not protect them if they continue on the same path.

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God’s creation of the universe and everything within it is not an idle game or a purposeless diversion. It is an act of profound wisdom, truth, and seriousness, established for a real purpose—so that creation may reflect divine wisdom, serve as a place of moral responsibility and testing, and lead to accountability before God.

translation: We did not create them except in truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: God affirms that the heavens and the earth were not created frivolously or without purpose; their creation is grounded in truth, wisdom, justice, and a definite divine purpose. Yet most people remain ignorant of this reality, failing to recognize the Creator’s wisdom and the seriousness of existence, and therefore do not live in light of that truth.

translation: Indeed, the Day of Decision is the appointed time for them all.
interpretation: This verse declares that the Day of Judgment—the Day when God will decisively separate truth from falsehood and judge every soul—is a fixed, inescapable appointment set by God for all of humanity and jinn without exception. It emphasizes that the resurrection and final reckoning are not uncertain or subject to change; rather, they will occur at the precise time God has decreed, and every created being will be gathered together to face the consequences of their deeds.

translation: The Day when no protector can avail his client in anything, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: On that Day, every worldly tie of patronage, kinship, or alliance will collapse, and no master, guardian, or ally will be able to benefit another in the slightest or shield him from Allah's judgment. All created beings will stand utterly dependent upon Allah alone, with no helper or intercessor able to rescue them except by His permission, underscoring His absolute sovereignty and the reality of individual accountability.

translation: Except those on whom Allah has mercy. Indeed, He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: On the Day when no created being can benefit another, the only exception is the one whom God covers with His mercy; this mercy is not owed to anyone but flows from His absolute power and boundless compassion, so salvation rests solely on His favor, not on lineage, status, or intercession.

translation: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum...
interpretation: This verse affirms the reality of the Zaqqum tree, a tree in Hell prepared as food for the sinful and rebellious, serving as a means of punishment and humiliation for them.

translation: The food of the sinful one.
interpretation: It refers to the Zaqqum tree, which God has made as the food of the wicked and defiant sinner in Hell—not a nourishing meal, but a torment that boils within the bellies.

translation: Like molten brass, it boils in the bellies.
interpretation: This similitude conveys an excruciating inward punishment: what the sinful are made to consume becomes a thick, superheated substance that churns and scalds within them. It signifies that their torment is not merely external but internal, turning the very seat of appetite and consumption into a source of agony, and expressing the severity, intensity, and inescapability of the chastisement.

translation: Like the boiling of scalding water.
interpretation: It signifies the severe, agonizing punishment of the Hereafter: the food of the sinful will boil and churn inside their bellies with an intense heat comparable to boiling scalding water, causing unbearable torment.

translation: Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Blazing Fire.
interpretation: This is a command to the angels of punishment on the Day of Judgment to seize the guilty one forcibly and drag him violently into the very center of Hell, showing that his punishment is certain, inescapable, and marked by humiliation and severity; he has no power to resist or delay it.

translation: Then pour over his head from the punishment of scalding water.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the keepers of Hell concerning the arrogant denier: after seizing and dragging him into the Fire, they are commanded to pour boiling water over his head. It signifies a humiliating and intensely painful punishment, targeting the head where pain is most severe. The verse follows a sarcastic rebuke: “Taste! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble” (44:49), exposing the emptiness of worldly pride and showing that the one who exulted in power and denied the Hereafter will be disgraced and tormented by the very reality he rejected.

translation: Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble.
interpretation: This is a mocking, rebuking address to the arrogant sinner in the Fire: the one who fancied himself powerful and honored is now commanded to taste the punishment, and his claims to might and nobility are exposed as empty. It declares that any strength or dignity he imagined for himself cannot save him, and that true might and honor belong to Allah alone.

translation: Indeed, this is what you used to doubt.
interpretation: This is addressed to the arrogant denier after he is seized into punishment: the very torment and judgment he disputed, mocked, or treated as uncertain in worldly life has now become an undeniable reality. His doubt did not alter the truth; it only left him unprepared for the recompense he now tastes.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure station.
interpretation: This verse affirms that those who guard themselves against Allah’s displeasure by fulfilling His commands and avoiding His prohibitions will ultimately dwell in a state of absolute safety and honor. Their station is secure because it is established by Allah’s promise, protected from every fear, loss, harm, and grief, and free from any threat of removal or decline. It points to the lasting bliss of Paradise, where the God-conscious enjoy nearness to their Lord and a peace that nothing can disturb.

translation: In gardens and springs.
interpretation: This describes the bliss of the righteous in the Hereafter: they will dwell amid flourishing gardens and flowing springs, a state of perpetual refreshment, delight, and abundant divine provision.

translation: They will wear [garments] of fine silk and brocade, facing one another.
interpretation: This describes the honor and perfect fellowship of the righteous in Paradise: they are clothed in the finest and most luxurious fabrics, and they sit or recline facing one another in mutual affection, joy, and respect, with no envy, resentment, or discord among them. Their outward adornment reflects inward purity and divine pleasure, while their facing one another signifies harmonious companionship and complete social bliss.

translation: Thus it will be; and We will marry them to fair ones with wide, lovely eyes.
interpretation: This verse describes one of the rewards of the people of Paradise: Allah will unite them in marriage with the Hur al-‘Ayn—beautiful, pure companions with wide, lovely eyes—as an honor and a completion of their bliss. The past tense “We married them” is used to convey absolute certainty, as though it has already come to pass.

translation: They will call therein for every [kind of] fruit, secure.
interpretation: This verse describes the bliss of the people of Paradise: they will request and be given every kind of fruit they desire, and they will remain in complete safety—free from fear, harm, deprivation, death, or any interruption of their enjoyment.

translation: They will not taste death therein except the first death, and He will protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.
