interpretation: This is a divine address to the Prophet Muhammad, assuring him that God will forgive whatever sins may have preceded and whatever may come later—not because he was guilty of sin, but as a special honor and protection for him—and will perfect His blessing upon him through victory, prophethood, and moral excellence, and will guide him firmly upon the straight path of truth, justice, and unwavering obedience to God.

translation: And Allah will help you with a mighty victory.
interpretation: This is a divine promise of help that is not merely success, but a help endowed with might, dignity, and invincibility. It signifies that God Himself will grant victory to His chosen servant, making the truth prevail and frustrating the designs of the enemies, so that the aid becomes a source of honor and strength for the faith and its adherents, and no opposition can overturn it.

translation: He is the One who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers, so that they may increase in faith along with their faith. And to Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true tranquility of heart is a gift from Allah alone, granted to believers to strengthen them in times of difficulty, fear, or uncertainty. Such calm is not merely emotional relief; it is a divine blessing that deepens and increases faith. Faith is therefore not static: it can grow when the heart is settled upon trust in Allah, especially amid trials. The verse also reminds believers that all powers and forces in the heavens and the earth belong to Allah, so no earthly or heavenly force can oppose His will or prevent His help. His knowledge is complete and His wisdom governs everything He decrees, including when and how He grants victory, relief, and inner peace.

translation: That He may admit the believing men and the believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and expiate from them their evil deeds. And that, in the sight of Allah, is a great triumph.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward prepared by Allah for sincere faith: both believing men and believing women are granted entry into paradisal gardens with flowing rivers, lasting forever, and their sins are forgiven and wiped away. The mention of both men and women shows that the essential reward of faith is not restricted by gender; it is granted to all who believe and act rightly. The phrase “with Allah” indicates that the true measure of success is not worldly approval or gain, but divine acceptance. Thus, the verse presents forgiveness and eternal bliss as the ultimate “great triumph,” encouraging believers to remain firm in faith and hope in Allah’s promise.

translation: And He will punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women—those who assume evil thoughts about Allah. Upon them is the evil turn; Allah is angry with them, has cursed them, and has prepared Hell for them—and evil is it as a destination.
interpretation: The verse exposes the inward root of hypocrisy and polytheism: thinking wrongly of God. Such people doubt His promise, imagine He will not aid His religion, or attribute to Him what is unworthy of His wisdom and mercy. Their evil assumption is answered by the very evil they projected: calamity returns upon them. God’s anger signifies His just displeasure, His curse means exclusion from His mercy, and Hell is the prepared end for them. The final phrase declares that this destination is the worst place to arrive.

translation: And to Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is ever All-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every power, force, and army in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone and is subject to His command. No created being possesses any strength independent of Him, and whatever help or victory He grants comes from His unlimited dominion. His being "All-Mighty" means He is never overpowered and no opposition can frustrate His will; His being "All-Wise" means all His decrees, whether they bring victory, delay, or trial, are ordered with perfect knowledge and purpose. Thus the believer is not dismayed by the apparent strength of enemies or the scarcity of means, because the true armies are Allah's, and He disposes of them according to His wisdom. The use of "was" indicates that these attributes are eternal and inseparable from Him, not temporary or acquired.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good tidings, and a warner.
interpretation: Allah affirms that He Himself sent Muhammad (peace be upon him) with a mission that combines testimony, glad tidings, and warning. He is a witness over those to whom he was sent: he conveys the divine message to them and will testify regarding their acceptance or rejection of it. He gives glad tidings to those who believe and obey, announcing God's mercy, forgiveness, and the reward of Paradise. And he warns those who disbelieve, disobey, or persist in sin of God's judgment and punishment. Thus the prophetic message is established as a clear proof and a mercy, so that no one may plead ignorance after it has reached them.

translation: So that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and support him, and honor him, and glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This means that faith in Allah and His Messenger must be embodied in concrete loyalty: supporting and revering the Messenger, and continually glorifying Allah at the beginning and end of the day. Such faith, honor, and worship are the intended fruit of the prophetic message and the path by which the heart attaches itself to Allah and His Messenger.

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So whoever breaks his pledge, he only breaks it against himself; and whoever fulfills what he has pledged to Allah, He will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse addresses the pledge of allegiance made to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and elevates it to a covenant with Allah Himself. It means that the Prophet does not receive allegiance on his own behalf or for any worldly gain; rather, he is Allah’s messenger, so loyalty to him in obedience to Allah is loyalty to Allah. The statement “the hand of Allah is over their hands” affirms Allah’s supreme authority, power, and presence over the pledge: He witnesses it, accepts it, supports it, and will hold people accountable for it. It must not be understood as Allah having a physical hand, for Allah is beyond bodily form and resemblance to creation. Whoever violates such a covenant, betrays it only to his own detriment, incurring loss upon himself. Whoever remains faithful to what he has covenanted with Allah will receive from Allah an immense reward in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: Those who remained behind among the Bedouins will say, 'Our properties and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us.' They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, 'Then who has any power at all for you against Allah, if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you? Rather, Allah is Aware of what you do.'
interpretation: The desert Arabs who stayed behind from the Prophet’s expedition offered a false excuse: they claimed that wealth and family obligations prevented them, and they asked the Prophet to seek forgiveness for them only with their tongues, not with sincere repentance in their hearts. The verse exposes the futility of trying to appease Allah or His Messenger while inwardly unwilling to obey. No one can avert Allah’s will or bring harm or benefit against His decree. Therefore, insincere requests for forgiveness, made merely to escape blame or gain favor, cannot change one’s standing before God. Allah knows the hidden motives behind outward words and deeds, so He judges by truth, not by performed excuses.

translation: Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made fair-seeming in your hearts, and you thought an evil thought, and you were a people doomed to ruin.
interpretation: This verse condemns the inward state of the hypocrites and those who held back: their false excuse was rooted in a corrupt assumption. They imagined that the Prophet and the believers would be destroyed and would never return to their families, and this deceptive hope was beautified in their hearts, leading them to prefer safety, abandonment, and disobedience. They entertained an evil suspicion about Allah, His promise, and His Messenger. Because they chose suspicion over trust, and desertion over steadfastness, they became “بورا”—ruined, barren of goodness, and deprived of divine favor. The verse warns that evil thoughts about Allah and His righteous servants lead the heart to ruin.

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger—then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse means that true faith requires belief in both Allah and His Messenger, and whoever rejects that faith is counted among the disbelievers. The "Blaze" (Sa'eer) is a blazing, raging Fire that Allah has prepared as the just consequence for those who knowingly persist in disbelief. It affirms that this punishment is certain and ready, and that rejecting the message of Allah and His Messenger is not a minor matter but leads to severe and lasting punishment.

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse affirms that absolute sovereignty over all creation belongs to God alone. His forgiveness and punishment are expressions of His perfect will and wisdom, not of any external constraint. His mercy is enduring and essential, so He forgives those who turn to Him in sincere repentance, while His punishment is reserved for those who persist in defiance; yet even in His justice, He remains ultimately forgiving and merciful.

translation: Those who remained behind will say when you set out to take the spoils, 'Leave us, that we may follow you.' They desire to change the words of Allah. Say, 'You will never follow us; thus Allah has said before.' Then they will say, 'Rather, you are jealous of us.' But they do not understand except a little.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who stayed behind from the Prophet’s march to Hudaybiyyah and then wanted to join the later expedition to Khaybar only to obtain its spoils. Their request was not prompted by faith or repentance but by greed, and by it they sought to alter Allah’s prior decree that the spoils would belong to those who had been present with the Prophet at Hudaybiyyah. Allah therefore commands His Prophet to refuse them and confirms that this decision was already made. When they accuse the believers of envy, they reveal their own hypocrisy and shallow understanding: they do not grasp Allah’s wisdom, the meaning of obedience, or that His reward is tied to sincere faith and struggle, not to claiming a share after the time of trial has passed.

translation: Say to those of the Bedouins who remained behind: 'You will be called to face a people of great military might; you will fight them, or they will submit. If you obey, Allah will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment.'
interpretation: The address exposes the false sense of security of those desert Arabs who had held back from the Prophet's earlier summons. It announces that a future call to arms against a formidable enemy will test whether their faith is genuine. The command is not merely advisory: they must either fight that people or accept their submission, meaning that avoidance of duty will no longer be tolerated. Obedience to Allah and His Messenger in this hard trial carries a generous reward, while a second withdrawal, like the first, deserves severe chastisement. The passage teaches that faith requires readiness to answer the Messenger's call, especially when struggle and sacrifice are demanded, and that excuses for evading clear divine obligations are not accepted.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow. And whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse absolves people with genuine physical disabilities—blindness, lameness, or illness—from blame for not undertaking duties such as fighting in the way of Allah, since their incapacity is a valid excuse. It then establishes the broader criterion: true success comes through obedience to Allah and His Messenger, which leads to eternal gardens of Paradise, while turning away from that obedience brings a painful punishment. Thus, the exemption is not a license for disobedience; it only removes culpability for what a person is genuinely unable to perform.

translation: Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory.
interpretation: This verse declares God's pleasure with the believers who gave their pledge of loyalty under the tree, affirming that He was fully aware of the sincerity, faith, and resolve hidden in their hearts. Because of that inner truthfulness, He bestowed upon them sakinah—divine calm, reassurance, and steadfastness—and granted them a victory close at hand. The verse teaches that God's acceptance and aid are tied to the heart's genuine devotion, and that He rewards faithful commitment with both inward peace and outward triumph.

translation: And abundant spoils of war which they will take; and Allah is ever Almighty, Wise.
interpretation: This is a promise from Allah to the believers who remained loyal and obedient at Hudaybiyyah that He will grant them plentiful gains of war that they will seize. The verse affirms that Allah is al-Aziz, possessing overwhelming might and never overcome, so He fulfills His promise and grants victory and wealth to whom He wills; and He is al-Hakim, wise in all His decrees, timing, distribution, and testing, so He gives blessings in a manner that serves the believers' ultimate good and establishes justice and wisdom.

translation: Allah has promised you abundant spoils of war that you will take; so He hastened this for you, and restrained the hands of people from you, so that it may be a sign for the believers and He may guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse conveys that God’s promise of plentiful gains to the believers is certain. The immediate gain He granted was a foretaste of that promise and a clear demonstration of His aid. By holding back the hostile people from harming them, He made His protection evident, strengthening the believers’ conviction. Thus the event serves as a sign that deepens faith and as divine guidance toward the upright path of obedience and trust in God.

translation: And another [conquest] which you were unable to [take], Allah has already encompassed it. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse assures the believers that further victories and gains beyond their present ability are already encompassed by God’s knowledge, power, and decree; He will bring them to pass, for His capability over all things is absolute and nothing can escape His will.

translation: And if those who disbelieved had fought you, they would have turned their backs [in retreat]; then they would not find any protector or helper.
interpretation: This is Allah’s assurance to the believers that the enmity and plots of the disbelievers cannot overcome them when His help is with them; had they dared to fight, they would have been routed and would find no ally to protect them or helper to save them, because Allah’s decree stands against disbelief and His promise of victory for the faithful is true.

translation: [This is] the way of Allah which has occurred before, and you will never find in the way of Allah any change.
interpretation: It signifies that Allah’s manner of dealing with His creation is fixed and unalterable: He consistently supports truth and its adherents, humiliates falsehood and its followers, and does not change His divine norms to accommodate wrongdoing or opposition to Him. Therefore, the believers should remain firm, knowing that the same outcome decreed for earlier communities who stood with faith—and for those who fought against it—will not be reversed.

translation: And He is the One Who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within the valley of Makkah after He had given you victory over them. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse points to God's protective intervention at Hudaybiyyah: although the believers had the upper hand over those who came to harm them, Allah restrained both sides from fighting inside the sacred precinct, averting bloodshed and preserving the sanctity of Mecca. It teaches that victory is not merely military dominance but includes God's control over hearts and circumstances; He can prevent conflict even when power exists, according to a wisdom connected to the treaty and what followed. His sight encompasses all deeds, so no hidden intention, restraint, or aggression is overlooked.

translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and hindered you from the Sacred Mosque, and [detained] the offering, prevented from reaching its place of sacrifice. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, lest you trample them and thus incur blame because of them without knowledge — [it would have been otherwise]. [It is] so that Allah may admit whom He wills into His mercy. Had they been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse reveals God’s wisdom in restraining conflict at Hudaybiyyah because Mecca still contained hidden believers whose faith was unknown to the Muslim army. Had the Muslims entered forcefully, those innocent believers would have been killed unintentionally, causing the Muslims grief, guilt, and public blame. God therefore delayed the punishment and conquest so that His mercy could reach whom He willed, including those secret believers. If the believers and disbelievers had been clearly separated, God would have permitted the disbelievers to be struck with painful punishment. The verse thus teaches that divine mercy, knowledge of the unseen, and protection of hidden righteous people take precedence over immediate retribution, and that God’s decree is governed by wisdom beyond human perception.

translation: When those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry—the zealotry of the Age of Ignorance—Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and made them adhere to the word of piety; and they were most deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.
interpretation: The disbelievers’ zealotry was a prideful, partisan anger that made them reject the truth and cling to the customs of pre-Islamic ignorance, especially when they were prevented from recognizing the Prophet’s mission or honoring God’s name. In contrast, Allah granted the Prophet and the believers calmness and self-restraint, so that their conduct would not be governed by arrogant tribal passion. The “word of piety” is the affirmation of God’s oneness and the commitment to God-consciousness—a covenant of sincere faith and obedience. Allah made it firm in the believers because He knew their hearts were truthful; they, rather than those blinded by pride, were truly fit to bear and uphold it. Thus true honor lies not in inherited status or worldly prestige but in taqwa, and Allah’s knowledge encompasses all hearts and all outcomes.

translation: Indeed, Allah has fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth. You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved and hair shortened, not fearing. So He knew what you did not know, and He made before that a near victory.
interpretation: The verse assures the believers that the Prophet’s dream of entering Mecca was from God and would certainly come true. The promise is that they will enter the Sacred Mosque safely, in the state of pilgrimage, some shaving their heads and others trimming their hair, with no fear. Because they were delayed from entering that same year, God, in His wisdom, knew a greater good they did not know, and He granted them a near victory beforehand—understood as the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah—which became the opening that led to the fulfillment of the vision and later victories.

translation: He is the One Who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion. And sufficient is Allah as a Witness.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone sent the Prophet Muhammad with His guidance and with the true religion, Islam, and He has guaranteed that this religion will be made manifest, victorious, and supreme over every other creed and way of life. The phrase “and sufficient is Allah as a Witness” means that Allah’s testimony is fully sufficient to confirm the truth of Muhammad’s messengership and the certainty of this promised triumph, so no other witness or validation is needed.

translation: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its shoot, then strengthens it, then it becomes thick and rises upon its stalk, delighting the sowers, so that He may enrage the disbelievers by them. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse portrays the true believing community as one whose devotion to God produces both inner sincerity and outward transformation. Their strength against disbelief is not cruelty, but firmness in truth; their mercy toward one another is the fruit of shared faith. Their bowing and prostration are performed not for show but out of longing for God’s grace and approval, and this worship leaves a visible imprint of humility, discipline, and spiritual light. The verse teaches that such a community was foretold in earlier scriptures and is likened to a growing crop: it begins small, is nurtured, gains strength, and finally stands firm, bringing joy to those who cultivate it and unsettling those who oppose the truth. The promise of forgiveness and great reward is therefore tied to faith joined with righteous action, showing that divine favor is not mere affiliation but is realized in lives shaped by obedience, worship, and moral steadfastness.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse lays down a foundational rule of faith and conduct: the believer does not place personal opinion, desire, custom, status, or any human authority ahead of Allah and His Messenger. It commands submission to divine guidance and prophetic teaching as the criterion, not merely as one voice among many. The call to taqwa shows that this submission must be rooted in God-consciousness, while the names al-Sami' and al-'Alim mean that Allah hears every word and knows every hidden motive. Thus the verse trains the believer inwardly and outwardly to approach revelation with humility, obedience, and reverence, and it makes adherence to Allah and His Messenger the practical proof of sincere faith.

translation: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds become worthless while you do not perceive.
interpretation: The verse establishes that true faith requires reverent restraint before the Prophet: his voice and dignity must not be overshadowed by the voices of believers, and he must not be addressed with the casual loudness used among equals. The warning that deeds may be nullified unknowingly shows that disrespect toward the Prophet is not merely a breach of etiquette but a spiritual danger that can destroy the reward of righteous actions. It teaches that love of God must express itself in honor, obedience, and careful manners toward His Messenger, and that heedlessness in this regard can harm one’s faith and deeds without one realizing it.

translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah — those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for righteousness. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that reverent restraint before the Prophet, and by extension before Allah’s commands and His messengers, is not mere outward etiquette but evidence of a heart refined and proven sincere in taqwa. Allah’s testing of the heart means He has purified it and prepared it for true God-consciousness, so such people are granted forgiveness for their shortcomings and an immense reward.

translation: Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the private chambers — most of them do not understand.
interpretation: This verse rebukes those who approached the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by shouting from outside the rooms of his household instead of addressing him with the respect and restraint due to him. Their behavior showed a lack of understanding: they failed to grasp the dignity of prophethood, the sanctity of the Prophet’s private life, and the proper manners of seeking his attention. It teaches that faith requires courteous conduct, patience, and awareness of the rights and privacy of others, especially toward the Messenger of Allah.

translation: And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that impatience and disrespect toward the Prophet ﷺ are harmful to those who display them. Those who called out to him from behind his private rooms should have waited calmly and respectfully until he emerged. Doing so would have been better for them in conduct, dignity, and outcome. Despite the rebuke, Allah is forgiving and merciful: whoever regrets such rudeness and turns back to proper respect and obedience will find Allah ready to forgive and show mercy.

translation: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to verify reports before acting upon them, especially when the bearer is not trustworthy or reliable. It warns that accepting news uncritically can lead to unjustly harming innocent people out of ignorance, and then one will regret the harm caused. The verse establishes a principle of due diligence, caution, and justice in social dealings: no decision or accusation should be based on unverified information, because rash action based on rumor corrupts relationships and produces remorse.

translation: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in many matters, you would surely be in hardship. But Allah has endeared faith to you and beautified it in your hearts, and has made hateful to you disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. Those are the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the Prophet’s presence and guidance are a mercy and criterion for the community; believers should not assume that their opinions or desires must dictate his decisions, for if he followed them in many affairs, they would fall into difficulty and corruption. It further explains that true guidance is a gift from God: He makes faith beloved and beautiful within the heart and makes rejection of truth, moral corruption, and rebellion against divine commands detestable. Those whose hearts are so disposed are the mature, rightly guided ones.

translation: [It is] a bounty from Allah and a favor, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This means that the guidance, faith, and purification of the heart are not due to human power or merit, but are purely a gracious gift and blessing from Allah. He knows who is deserving of His favor and places it where His perfect wisdom decrees.

translation: And if two parties of the believers fight one another, then make peace between them. But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them justly and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably.
interpretation: This verse establishes that conflict between believers must never be left to fester or escalate. The first duty is reconciliation: impartial mediation aimed at restoring peace and brotherhood. However, peace is not to be achieved by tolerating aggression. If one side persists in wrongdoing and oppression, the believing community must intervene collectively to restrain the aggressor until it submits to God’s command and ceases its transgression. The goal is not punishment for its own sake but correction, protection of the wronged, and restoration of justice. Once the aggressor desists, reconciliation must be conducted fairly, without revenge or bias, and with full respect for the rights of all parties. God’s love for the equitable shows that justice and fairness are essential to peace; reconciliation is valid only when it upholds truth and restores rightful claims.

translation: The believers are only brothers, so make reconciliation between your brothers, and fear Allah, so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith establishes a bond of brotherhood among believers that requires them to resolve conflicts and restore peace between disputing parties. Reconciliation is not merely a social courtesy but a religious duty linked to taqwa, God-consciousness, and the hope of divine mercy; believers are thus called to prioritize unity, justice, and forgiveness among themselves.

translation: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule another people; perhaps they may be better than them. Nor let women ridicule other women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another, nor call each other by offensive nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith. And whoever does not repent — then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse forbids the social sins that destroy honor, unity, and brotherhood among believers: mockery, defamation, and degrading nicknames. It warns that outward appearance, status, or weakness is no proof of superiority, for the person being mocked may be better in God’s sight. Since believers are one body, belittling another believer is a form of wronging oneself. Derogatory labels are especially incompatible with faith, because faith should produce dignity, restraint, and respect, not contempt. The verse therefore calls for humility, guarding the tongue, honoring others, and sincere repentance; persisting in these sins without repentance places a person among the unjust.

translation: O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy on one another or backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of Repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes a core moral discipline for the believing community: guarding the heart, the eyes, and especially the tongue in relation to others. It commands believers to stay away from excessive suspicion, because suspicion that is baseless and allowed to settle in the heart can become sin, leading to false judgment and injustice. It then forbids spying, which violates people’s privacy and seeks out faults that Allah has concealed, and forbids backbiting, meaning to mention an absent person in a way that would harm or dishonor them. The striking image of eating the dead flesh of one’s brother expresses how spiritually repulsive and treacherous such speech is, since it violates both the sacredness of brotherhood and the dignity of the person. The verse closes by commanding taqwa, God-consciousness, and reminding believers that Allah is ever accepting of repentance and most merciful, meaning that whoever has fallen into these sins should turn back to Him, and that protecting others’ honor is an essential part of piety.

translation: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse teaches that all human beings share a common origin and therefore possess equal human worth; the diversity of nations and tribes is not a basis for superiority but a means for mutual recognition and cooperation. True honor before Allah depends solely on taqwa—God-consciousness, piety, and righteous conduct—and Allah fully knows both the outward identities and the inward realities of all people.

translation: The Bedouins say: 'We have believed.' Say: 'You have not believed; but say: "We have submitted," for faith has not yet entered your hearts. But if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything from your deeds. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse distinguishes between outward submission (Islam) and inward faith (iman). The Bedouins claimed complete faith merely by verbal declaration, but God corrected them: true faith had not yet settled in their hearts. They were told to say they had submitted outwardly, while acknowledging that faith requires inner conviction. The verse teaches that claims of faith are not enough without the heart’s assent, yet it also encourages them: if they sincerely obey God and His Messenger, their good deeds will not be diminished. It ends with God’s forgiveness and mercy, showing that He accepts people as they grow toward deeper faith.

translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted, and have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is they who are the truthful.
interpretation: This verse defines true faith as a combination of sincere belief in Allah and His Messenger, unwavering certainty that admits no doubt, and practical sacrifice through wealth and life in the path of Allah. It declares that those who embody these qualities are the truthful in their claim to faith, because their inner conviction is proven by their outward commitment and struggle. Thus, faith is not mere verbal profession; it is confirmed by certainty of heart and action.

translation: Say, "Are you informing Allah about your religion? But Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is Knowing of all things."
interpretation: This is a rebuke to any claim of religious devotion made as though it could inform or obligate God. Since God’s knowledge encompasses every hidden and open thing in the heavens and earth, He already knows the truth of people’s faith, sincerity, and deeds. Religion is therefore not a report submitted to God for His approval as if He were unaware; it is a reality He knows perfectly and by which He tests and judges the servant. The verse calls for humility and sincerity, reminding believers that outward claims and observances do not add to God’s knowledge or bind Him, and that He is fully aware of all things, including the motives behind every religious profession.

translation: They regard it as a favor to you that they have submitted. Say, 'Do not regard your submission as a favor to me. Rather, Allah has favored you by guiding you to faith, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse corrects the attitude of those who treated their outward acceptance of Islam as if it were a kindness or debt owed to the Prophet. No one can benefit Allah or His Messenger by believing; the benefit of faith returns to the believer. The real favor is not that a person outwardly submits, but that Allah grants guidance to true faith. Outward Islam may be expressed by the tongue, while iman is an inward gift from Allah, confirmed by sincerity. The phrase “if you are truthful” challenges any claim of faith that is not matched by sincerity: if their faith is genuine, they must acknowledge that being guided to iman is Allah’s grace upon them, not their own achievement or a favor they have done for the Prophet.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God’s knowledge encompasses all that is hidden and beyond human perception in the heavens and the earth, and that He sees every deed people perform, so nothing escapes His awareness or observation.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an.
interpretation: Allah opens the surah with the disjointed letter Qaf, whose precise meaning is known to Him alone, and He swears by the Glorious Qur'an. This oath exalts the Qur'an and establishes the truth and authority of the revelation, confirming that the message brought by the Prophet is not to be doubted and that the Qur'an is the majestic, divinely revealed book.

translation: Nay, they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, so the disbelievers say, 'This is a strange thing!'
interpretation: The verse reproves the disbelievers’ astonishment as misplaced: God’s sending a warner from their own midst is not odd but purposeful, so that the message comes through a human they can recognize, understand, and follow. Their rejection of him as merely a man reveals that the real obstacle is not a lack of proof but their aversion to the warning of resurrection and judgment.

translation: When we have died and become dust? That is a far-fetched return.
interpretation: This is a quotation of the disbelievers’ astonished denial of resurrection: they regard the idea that people will be brought back to life after death and decomposition into dust as utterly remote and impossible. By calling it “a far-fetched return,” they express their conviction that such a return is beyond possibility, thereby revealing their rejection of God’s power to recreate and raise the dead.

translation: We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserving Book.
interpretation: This verse affirms that even as human bodies decompose and the earth consumes parts of them, nothing is hidden from God or lost to His knowledge. The “preserving Book” is the guarded record in which all things are inscribed, so God’s knowledge is complete and exact. It establishes the certainty of resurrection: the One who knows and preserves every detail of what the earth takes can surely restore and raise the dead.

translation: Nay, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused state.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who reject the divine message not because it lacks proof, but because it confronts their desires and inherited assumptions. Having denied the truth after it reached them, they are left in a state of inner disorder and contradiction: they cannot agree on a consistent accusation against the Prophet, nor can they find peace in their own beliefs. The “confused state” is the natural consequence of turning away from clear revelation—uncertainty, instability, and loss of a firm criterion between truth and falsehood. It warns that rejection of God’s guidance ultimately throws a person’s whole affair into perplexity and spiritual chaos.

translation: Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts?
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who deny resurrection and divine power, directing their attention to the heaven above them as a clear sign. It asks: do they not observe how Allah created it firm and ordered, beautified it with stars and luminosity, and left it free of any cracks, gaps, or defect? The flawless structure and adornment of the sky demonstrate the Creator's perfect ability, so the One who made this vast, unflawed canopy is fully able to resurrect the dead and bring them to account.

translation: And the earth — We spread it out, and cast into it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it of every beautiful kind.
interpretation: This verse declares God’s power and providence in the ordering of the world: He made the earth a broad, settled place for human life, fixed within it mountains that stabilize and balance it, and brought forth from it every kind of vegetation in paired forms, displaying beauty, interdependence, and purposeful design. These signs are meant to awaken reflection on the Creator’s sustaining mercy and on His ability to bring about resurrection and reckoning.

translation: An insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back [to Allah].
interpretation: The signs in creation and revelation are meant to open spiritual sight and awaken remembrance of God, but this benefit is received only by the servant whose heart is turned back to Him—repentant, attentive, and constantly returning from heedlessness to obedience and reliance upon God.

translation: And We sent down from the sky blessed water, and caused gardens and harvested grain to grow thereby.
interpretation: This verse declares that rain is a blessed provision from Allah, by which He brings forth orchards and crops that are reaped for food. It is a sign of His power to give life to dead earth, and thus a proof and reminder that He can likewise resurrect the dead.

translation: And the palm trees, tall and lofty, having clustered spathes piled one upon another.
interpretation: This verse presents the tall date palms and their densely layered fruit clusters as a sign of God's power, generosity, and precise ordering: from the blessed rain He sends, He brings forth abundant, life-sustaining provision, and the same ability to give life to dead earth points to His power to resurrect.

translation: [As] provision for the servants, and We revived thereby a dead land. Thus is the coming forth [from the graves].
interpretation: This verse uses the revival of barren, lifeless earth by rain as a sign of resurrection: the same Allah who sends down water as sustenance for His servants and brings a dead land back to life will likewise bring the dead out of their graves on the Day of Judgment.

translation: The people of Noah denied before them, and the companions of the Rass, and Thamud.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and warns the deniers by recalling that earlier nations—Noah’s people, the people of al-Rass, and Thamud—had likewise rejected their messengers. It teaches that rejection of revelation is an ancient pattern, and that those who persist in it invite the same accountability and punishment that befell earlier communities.

translation: And [the people of] 'Aad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot.
interpretation: These are named as examples of nations who rejected God’s messengers and were destroyed by divine punishment: 'Aad denied Hud, Pharaoh arrogantly denied Moses, and the people of Lot—referred to as his brothers because they were his kin and community—persisted in corruption and denied Lot. Their mention is a warning that rejecting the Messenger is not a new or isolated offense, and that God’s judgment against those who knowingly oppose His messengers is certain and just.

translation: And the companions of the thicket and the people of Tubba‘ — all of them rejected the messengers, so My warning became due.
interpretation: These communities are cited as examples of nations who met the messengers with denial, not because the messengers lacked proofs but because those people chose rejection. Their shared sin was not merely rejecting a particular prophet but rejecting the prophetic message itself, and so the divine threat that had been announced to them was no longer an empty warning: it became deservedly binding and was carried out. The verse therefore establishes a fixed moral and divine pattern: whenever a people collectively treat God’s messengers as liars, the promised judgment is justified and inevitable, and the later deniers are warned that they will not escape the same decree.

translation: Were We then weary with the first creation? Rather, they are in confusion about a new creation.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who reject the resurrection by reminding them that Allah originated creation in the first place. If He was not incapable or exhausted by bringing them into existence initially, He is certainly able to bring them back to life after death. Their doubt about the new creation is not due to any weakness in God's power, but because they are unsettled and confused, failing to grasp that the One who created from nothing can recreate with even greater ease.

translation: And We have already created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God, who created the human being, has full knowledge of even the hidden whisperings and inner promptings of the self. His closeness to the servant is not spatial or physical, but a closeness of knowledge, awareness, and power: He encompasses the person more intimately than the jugular vein, the vital vessel in the neck. Thus no thought, intention, or secret motion of the heart is beyond His knowledge, and this should awaken in the believer awe, sincerity, and watchfulness before God.

translation: When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left.
interpretation: This refers to the two angels appointed by Allah to every person, one on the right and one on the left, constantly present and ready to record all deeds. The right angel records good deeds, and the left angel records evil deeds. The verse instills awareness that no word or action escapes divine observation and that every deed is being preserved for the Day of Reckoning, emphasizing God's absolute knowledge and the certainty of accountability.

translation: He does not utter a word except that there is with him an observer, ready.
interpretation: This verse affirms that no human speech escapes divine oversight: every word a person speaks is attended by an appointed angel who records it, emphasizing that speech is a matter of accountability before God and that even seemingly insignificant words have lasting moral and spiritual consequences.

translation: And the stupor of death comes with the truth—that is what you were trying to avoid.
interpretation: This verse describes death as the moment when the veil is lifted and the reality that people denied or postponed becomes undeniable. The overwhelming agony or stupor of death brings the truth with certainty: the soul is confronted with what it spent its life turning away from—God’s promise, accountability, and the inevitability of meeting its Lord. It is a rebuke to the heedless: what you tried to flee has now come upon you, and there is no escape or evasion left.

translation: And the Horn will be blown—that is the Day of Warning.
interpretation: The sounding of the Horn marks the decisive beginning of the Hereafter: it is the moment Allah has forewarned humanity about, when His threat to the deniers and disobedient becomes manifest, the dead are raised, and every soul is brought to account before Him.

translation: And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.
interpretation: This verse describes the inescapable scene of the Day of Judgment: every human soul is brought before God for reckoning, accompanied by an angel who drives it toward the court of divine justice and another angel who testifies to its deeds. It affirms that no one will be absent, no action will be forgotten, and every person will face a precise accounting in which God’s justice is fully established.

translation: You were certainly in heedlessness of this, so We have removed from you your cover, and your sight today is sharp.
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment when the veil of worldly distraction, denial, and false security is lifted from the human being on the Day of Judgment. What was once merely spoken of—resurrection, accountability, the reality of God’s promise—now stands exposed with undeniable clarity. The person who lived unmindful is made to see the truth with piercing vision, no longer able to ignore, rationalize, or turn away. The removal of the cover is not merely an external act but the collapse of every excuse and blind spot, so that the soul confronts its own record and the divine reality with absolute certainty. Thus the verse is both a warning against heedlessness and a declaration that ultimate perception belongs to God, who can strip away all delusion in an instant.

translation: And his companion will say, 'This is what I have with me, ready.'
interpretation: The companion is the angel appointed to accompany every soul and record its deeds. On the Day of Judgment he presents the record he has kept, fully prepared and complete, so that the person's actions stand as clear testimony before God. The verse emphasizes that nothing done in life is lost or forgotten; every deed is accurately preserved and brought forward for just reckoning.

translation: [It will be said:] "Cast into Hell every obstinate disbeliever."
interpretation: The dual command is addressed to the two angels charged with driving and witnessing each soul, ordering them to thrust into Hell every person who persistently rejected faith and stubbornly resisted the truth. The verse emphasizes that final punishment falls upon those who combine denial of God with arrogant, willful obstinacy—not upon the merely weak or ignorant, but upon those who knowingly entrench themselves against the truth.

translation: Withholder of good, transgressor, doubter.
interpretation: This describes a person whose corruption is rooted in three connected vices: he habitually prevents or withholds good—whether wealth, knowledge, kindness, or any benefit—from reaching others; he oversteps God’s limits and violates the rights of others; and he is steeped in doubt and suspicion about the truth, causing uncertainty and unrest. These traits together portray a defiant, morally disordered character that resists faith through arrogance and wrongdoing, not merely through honest confusion, and thus deserves divine condemnation.

translation: Who set up another god along with Allah—so cast him, both of you, into the severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns shirk, the sin of associating any other being with Allah in divinity or worship. The command is directed to the two angels accompanying every soul—the driver and the witness—to hurl the person who persisted in this false worship into the intense torment of Hell. It stresses that Allah alone is worthy of worship and that deliberately setting up rivals beside Him leads to severe chastisement.

translation: His companion will say, “Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in far-reaching error.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the jinn or devil companion assigned to the person disowns responsibility for his ruin. He admits that he whispered and tempted, but he did not compel or force him into disobedience. The person himself had already gone far astray, deeply away from the truth, and willingly followed his own desires. This verse establishes that Satan cannot force anyone into sin; his role is only to invite and beautify evil. Therefore, human beings remain responsible for their choices, and no one can justly blame another for his own misguidance.

translation: He will say, "Do not dispute before Me, for I had already given you the warning."
interpretation: This is a divine rebuke on the Day of Judgment: disputes, excuses, and mutual blame are futile because God had already conveyed the warning of punishment through His messengers and revelations. The verse affirms that accountability is just—no one can plead ignorance or argue against the final decree—and that the verdict has already been made clear before it is carried out.

translation: The word [decree] is not changed with Me, and I am not unjust to [My] servants.
interpretation: Allah affirms that His decree, promise, and threat are final and cannot be altered or revoked, and that He never wrongs His servants. Any punishment He gives is perfectly just and deserved according to His knowledge and wisdom; He does not oppress anyone or punish a soul for what it did not do.

translation: On the Day We will say to Hell, 'Have you been filled?' and it will say, 'Are there any more?'
interpretation: This verse depicts the terrifying reality of the Hereafter: Hell, a creation of Allah, is addressed by its Lord, and its reply expresses that it still has room to receive more. It signifies the vast capacity of Hell and the sheer multitude of those who will enter it due to their disbelief and wrongdoing, while also displaying the absolute authority of Allah over all things and the perfection of His justice. Hell’s response is not an act of rebellion but a metaphorical expression of how many souls are deserving of punishment, and it intensifies the warning to humanity that the consequences of rejecting faith are immense and unending for those who persist in evil.

translation: And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far off.
interpretation: This means that on the Day of Judgment Allah will draw the Garden close to those who guarded against His displeasure through faith and obedience, so that it is near enough for them to behold and enter; their taqwa has made what was unseen and distant in worldly life proximate and certain.

translation: This is what you were promised—for every one who constantly turns back [to Allah] and keeps guard.
interpretation: The promised reward, Paradise, belongs to the one who continually returns to Allah in repentance and obedience and who vigilantly guards Allah’s commands, limits, and covenant. These two qualities describe a lifelong stance: repeatedly turning back to God after lapses and protecting one’s faith with mindful care. It is not enough to claim the promise; it is realized by persisting in repentance and heedfulness.

translation: Who feared the Most Merciful in the unseen and came with a heart ever returning [to Him].
interpretation: This verse describes the inward reality of the believer who is praised and promised Paradise: he lives with reverent awe of Allah even when no human eye observes him, so his God-consciousness is sincere rather than performative. His fear is not a paralyzing dread but a faithful awareness of Allah’s majesty that keeps him from disobedience and draws him toward obedience. He then comes before his Lord with a heart that is munib—constantly turning back, repentant, humble, and oriented away from rebellion toward loving submission. The emphasis is on the heart, for the worth of deeds before Allah is rooted in the sincerity, humility, and continual return of the inner self to its Creator.

translation: Enter it in peace. That is the Day of Eternity.
interpretation: This is a call to the people of Paradise to enter it with perfect peace and security, free from every fear, harm, and sorrow. The verse declares that this state of bliss is the Day of Eternal Abiding, in which the believers will remain forever, never to leave or experience any end to their joy.

translation: They will have whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more.
interpretation: This means that in Paradise the believers will receive everything they desire, and Allah will grant them an additional favor beyond their wishes: the greatest of these is beholding His noble face and enjoying His good pleasure, which surpasses every worldly and paradisiacal delight.

translation: And how many a generation before them did We destroy—they were greater than them in power, and they explored the lands. Was there any escape?
interpretation: This verse is a warning that worldly strength, numbers, and movement cannot protect anyone from Allah’s judgment. Earlier peoples were mightier and more capable than the addressed disbelievers, and they searched and traveled throughout the land seeking security or a way out, yet they could not escape when Allah’s decree came. The rhetorical question affirms that there is no refuge or escape from Allah’s punishment.

translation: Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is witness.
interpretation: The verse means that divine signs, revelation, and the lessons of history benefit only the one whose heart is spiritually alive and able to understand, or who listens attentively with full awareness and presence of mind. It calls for receptive inner understanding and conscious hearing, not mere outward listening while the heart is heedless.

translation: And We have certainly created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone created the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them in six days, and it denies any fatigue, exhaustion, or need for rest touching Him. It refutes the notion that God became weary after creation and rested, establishing instead His perfect power, self-sufficiency, and freedom from any weakness or limitation.

translation: So be patient over what they say, and glorify with the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet—and every believer by extension—to endure the false or hostile words of opponents without collapsing into resentment, and to counteract them through worship: continuously glorifying and praising God at dawn before sunrise and before sunset. These times are singled out because they frame the day with remembrance, keeping the heart anchored in God, renewing patience, and drawing divine help and tranquility.

translation: And in the night, glorify Him, and after the prostrations.
interpretation: This verse directs the believer to exalt and praise Allah during the night and to continue remembering Him after the prostrations of prayer. It teaches that worship is not limited to the daylight or to the prayer itself, but extends into the night and into the moments following ritual prostration, so that the servant remains connected to Allah, fulfills the command of glorification, and keeps the heart and tongue engaged in His remembrance when heedlessness is most likely.

translation: And listen for the Day when the caller will call from a near place.
interpretation: This verse commands people to be attentive and prepared for the resurrection: the angel charged with blowing the trumpet will call out from a place near to creation, so that all will hear the summons and come forth from their graves. The nearness emphasizes that the promised Day is certain and close in God's decree, and that its call will be sudden and unavoidable.

translation: The Day when they will hear the Cry in truth. That is the Day of Emergence.
interpretation: This refers to the resurrection: the trumpet blast will be heard as an undeniable reality, and the dead will come forth from their graves to meet their Lord for judgment. It is called the Day of Emergence because on it all creation exits the state of death and the grave into the open arena of accountability, where the truth of God's promise is fully manifested.

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone has absolute authority over life and death: He grants life, decrees death, and will resurrect all creatures. The ultimate return of every soul is to Him for judgment and recompense, so human beings should live with accountability, relying upon Him and preparing for the Hereafter.

translation: On the Day when the earth will split open from them, they will come out hastening. That is a gathering easy for Us.
interpretation: This verse affirms the reality of bodily resurrection: at God’s command, the earth will cleave open and release the dead, who will emerge swiftly and hurriedly toward the gathering for judgment. Their scattered remains, however dispersed or decayed, are no obstacle to God. The phrase “easy for Us” emphasizes that the resurrection and assembly of all humanity is effortless for Allah, requiring neither preparation nor aid, and it reinforces His absolute power over creation and return.

translation: We know best what they say, and you are not over them a compeller. So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning.
interpretation: This verse defines the Prophet’s mission as reminder, not coercion: Allah alone knows the hidden and outward speech of people, so the Prophet is not to force faith upon them or dominate their hearts. The Qur’an is the means of admonition, and it benefits those who already dread Allah’s warning and accountability. Thus guidance is not produced by human pressure but by the Book reaching a heart disposed to fear God.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the winds that scatter, scattering,
interpretation: Allah swears by the winds that disperse dust, seeds, and clouds, pointing to His absolute power over creation and preparing the listener to affirm the certainty of resurrection and judgment.

translation: And those bearing a heavy burden.
interpretation: This refers to the clouds that carry the heavy load of rain, which God sends down as a mercy and provision for the earth and its inhabitants.

translation: And by the ships that sail with ease.
interpretation: Allah swears by the ships that glide smoothly across the sea by His command, carrying people and provisions with ease. This is a sign of His power, mercy, and provision for His creation.

translation: And by those who distribute the command/matter.
interpretation: This is an oath by the angels whom Allah has appointed to apportion and distribute His decreed matters among creation—such as provisions, rain, and other affairs—according to His command.

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is surely true.
interpretation: This verse affirms that every promise Allah has made—especially the resurrection, the final reckoning, and the recompense of Paradise or Hell—is absolutely truthful and certain; it is not merely a possibility but an unalterable reality that will inevitably come to pass.

translation: And indeed, the Recompense is surely to occur.
interpretation: Here, “al-din” refers to the reckoning and recompense on the Day of Judgment, and “lawāqi‘” means that it is certain to come to pass and cannot be avoided. The verse affirms that God’s promise of accountability, reward, and punishment will inevitably take place, so people should live with awareness of that certainty.

translation: By the heaven full of interwoven paths.
interpretation: Allah swears by the sky, which is marked by interwoven courses, orbits, and textured patterns, displaying perfect order and design as a sign of His power and wisdom.

translation: Indeed, you are in a discordant speech.
interpretation: The address is to the rejecters of the Prophet: their claims about him, the Qur’an, and the Hereafter are inconsistent and mutually contradictory, so their denial rests not on coherent truth but on confused and conflicting assertions. This exposes the instability of their stance and warns that such discordant speech cannot be a reliable basis for rejecting God’s message.

translation: Turned away from it is he who is turned away.
interpretation: This verse declares that rejection of the revelation is not random or forced upon an unwilling believer: those who allow themselves to be diverted from the truth are, by God’s just order, left to their diversion. The passive form shows that such turning away is both their own doing and its consequence; the truth remains clear, but only the one who chooses aversion is prevented from benefiting by it. It warns that guidance is received by hearts disposed to accept it, while persistent resistance brings about being turned away from the Qur’an and the Prophet’s message.

translation: Perish the conjecturers!
interpretation: This is a severe divine curse and declaration of ruin against those who speak about Allah, revelation, the Hereafter, and the unseen based on mere guesswork, falsehood, and baseless speculation. It condemns the habit of replacing certain truth with conjecture and mockery, warning that those who persist in such lies and heedlessness are doomed to loss.

translation: Those who are in a flood [of ignorance and confusion], heedless.
interpretation: This verse describes the rejecters of truth as being submerged in a covering flood of ignorance, vain desires, and worldly distractions, so that they are heedless of God, the Hereafter, and the clear signs calling them to faith; their heedlessness is not a passing lapse but a deep-seated state that keeps them from reflecting on the truth and responding to guidance.

translation: They ask, "When is the Day of Judgment?"
interpretation: This is a question posed by the deniers out of mockery and doubt, not a sincere request for guidance. It expresses their rejection of resurrection and accountability. The verse affirms that the Day of Judgment is real and inevitable, but its exact timing is known only to Allah. Their asking is futile because it will not delay or avert the reckoning; when it comes, they will face the consequences of their denial.

translation: The Day when they will be tried over the Fire.
interpretation: This refers to the disbelievers being subjected to the Fire on the Day of Judgment as a punishment and a testing, so that they experience the torment they denied and scoffed at in worldly life; their trial is the Fire itself, and it is the just recompense for their rejection of faith and warnings.

translation: Taste your trial! This is what you were asking to hasten.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who denied the truth and mockingly demanded that the warned punishment come quickly: in the Hereafter they are made to experience the very suffering they belittled, and it becomes clear that the judgment they treated as a joke was real and inevitable.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who attain taqwa—by believing in God, obeying His commands, and avoiding His prohibitions—will dwell in gardens of lasting bliss and flowing springs, representing unending delight, purity, and divine pleasure in the Hereafter.

translation: Taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good.
interpretation: This verse describes the people of Paradise as receiving the rewards and blessings their Lord has granted them, and it explains the reason: even before entering Paradise, in their worldly life, they were people of ihsan—sincere in worship, righteous in conduct, and excellent in how they treated others. Their reward is therefore presented as God’s generous recompense for the good they used to do, showing that faith and virtuous action in this life lead to the lasting gift of their Lord in the Hereafter.

translation: They used to sleep but little of the night.
interpretation: This describes the devoted servants of God as those who restrained themselves from lengthy sleep, spending most of the night in prayer, supplication, and remembrance of God, so that only a small portion of it was given to rest.

translation: And in the pre-dawn hours they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse describes the righteous as those who turn to God in humble repentance during the last part of the night before dawn, seeking His forgiveness. It highlights their sincerity, vigilance in worship, and constant acknowledgment of their need for God's mercy at a quiet and blessed time when supplication is especially accepted.

translation: And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived.
interpretation: This verse establishes that wealth held by the righteous is not an absolute private possession; the needy have a God-given entitlement within it. The “beggar” is the one who openly asks for help, while the “deprived” is the one whose poverty or hardship does not lead him to ask, whether out of shame, weakness, or being overlooked. Their share is not merely voluntary generosity but a recognized right, making care for the poor an essential duty of faith and a means of purifying wealth and upholding justice in society.

translation: And on the earth are signs for those who are certain.
interpretation: The verse declares that the created earth—its structure, sustenance, diversity, and ordered phenomena—constitutes evidence of Allah's existence, power, and wisdom. Such evidence is perceived and benefited from by those whose faith is firmly certain; their inner certainty opens their insight to read the visible world as a book of divine signs, whereas heedlessness or doubt causes one to pass over them.

translation: And in your own selves. Will you not then see?
interpretation: This verse directs people to reflect on the signs of God's power and wisdom within their own creation and inner faculties, so that they may come to recognize the Creator and the reality of resurrection; the question is a rebuke for failing to use insight and reflection.

translation: And in the heaven is your provision and whatever you are promised.
interpretation: God places the source of your sustenance and the fulfillment of all that He has promised—reward, punishment, resurrection, and every decree—in the unseen realm above, so you should rely on Him and not limit provision or truth to visible means alone.

translation: So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed, it is truth, just as you speak.
interpretation: Allah swears by His own lordship over the heavens and the earth that the promise He has given—whether of provision, resurrection, judgment, or the truth of the Qur’an—is absolutely certain. The comparison “just as you speak” means that this truth is as undeniable and real as the everyday fact that human beings talk; no sane person doubts that they speak, so no one should doubt Allah’s promise. The oath is meant to remove all doubt and to impress upon the listener that divine promises are not vague or metaphorical but as concrete and sure as their own speech.

translation: Has the story of Abraham's honored guests come to you?
interpretation: The interrogative is rhetorical, meant to stir wonder and attention and to affirm that this remarkable account has indeed reached the addressee; it directs reflection to a divine sign and to the honor bestowed upon Abraham’s guests.

translation: When they entered upon him and said, ‘Peace,’ he said, ‘Peace—[you are] a people unknown.’
interpretation: This teaches the prophetic etiquette of returning a greeting of peace promptly and courteously, even before knowing the visitor. Ibrahim’s words ‘a people unknown’ indicate that they were strangers to him, not that he was hostile; they led him to extend hospitality while remaining aware that they were unfamiliar. It shows that believers should meet visitors with a good greeting and dignified caution, and that peace is the opening of righteous social conduct.

translation: Then he slipped away to his family and brought a fattened calf.
interpretation: The verse conveys the virtue of generous, unhesitating hospitality: Abraham did not merely offer words but immediately prepared a substantial and choice meal for his guests. His quiet movement to his household suggests sincerity and tact—serving without seeking praise or putting guests in embarrassment—while the fattened calf shows he gave from the best of what he had. It is a model of honoring guests and acting promptly in kindness.

translation: Then he brought it near to them; he said, 'Will you not eat?'
interpretation: This is an expression of Ibrahim’s eager hospitality and courteous invitation: he personally placed the food before his guests and gently urged them to partake, not by commanding them but by a rhetorical question that conveys warmth, respect, and generous concern. It also signals the moment when their abstention becomes apparent, revealing that these visitors are not ordinary human guests.

translation: Then he felt a fear of them. They said, 'Do not fear.' And they gave him glad tidings of a knowledgeable boy.
interpretation: This verse portrays Prophet Ibrahim’s natural human apprehension when his guests did not eat the meal he offered, a reaction rooted in concern rather than disbelief. The angels immediately reassured him, teaching that divine messengers bring peace and that God’s servants should not yield to fear when His command arrives. Their glad tidings of a son described as 'knowledgeable' signify a miraculous gift from God, since Ibrahim and his wife were advanced in age. The knowledge attributed to this son—Isaac—is not mere worldly information but divinely granted wisdom and prophetic understanding, indicating that he would carry forward the mission of guidance and monotheism. Thus, the verse emphasizes God’s power to grant offspring beyond natural expectation and presents sacred knowledge as the noblest quality of the promised child.

translation: Then his wife came forward with a cry, and struck her face, and said, "An old barren woman!"
interpretation: This verse portrays Sarah’s astonishment when the angels brought Abraham the news of a son. Her loud cry and striking her face express the overwhelming shock of a woman who was both advanced in age and known to be barren. Her words, “an old barren woman,” are not a rejection of God’s promise but an expression of utter wonder at how she could bear a child in such a condition. The verse thus highlights that God’s power is not bound by natural causes: He can grant life and offspring even when all human means seem impossible, and the reaction of Abraham’s wife underscores the extraordinary nature of the miracle.

translation: They said, "Thus has your Lord said. Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing."
interpretation: The angels affirm that the promise of a son is not measured by ordinary human expectations or natural causes, but rests on the decree of Allah. His being "the Wise" means He ordains all things with perfect purpose and timing, and His being "the Knowing" means He fully knows the condition of His servants, including the apparent impossibility of what He has promised. Therefore, what He has spoken is certain and true, and no weakness, age, or barrenness can prevent its fulfillment.

translation: He said, "Then what is your errand, O messengers?"
interpretation: This is Ibrahim’s inquiry to the angelic messengers about the purpose of their divine mission after they had given him glad tidings and reassured him. He understands that they were not sent only for his sake, so he asks what task they have been commissioned to carry out. The question reflects his attentiveness to God’s command and his readiness to learn the purpose for which these messengers were sent.

translation: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a criminal people."
interpretation: This states that the angels are informing Lot that their mission is directed at a people who have become guilty through persistent disbelief, defiance, and grave sins, especially the abomination for which they were notorious. They are described as "criminal" because they knowingly violated God's limits and corrupted both faith and morality, making them deserving of the punishment the angels were sent to bring.

translation: That We may send down upon them stones of clay.
interpretation: These are the words of the angels sent to Prophet Ibrahim concerning the people of Lut. It means that God decreed to rain down upon them stones of hardened clay as a punishment for their persistent corruption, especially their grave sexual transgression and their rejection of Lut’s warnings. The stones were not an ordinary natural event but a specific divine torment prepared for them.

translation: Marked from your Lord for the transgressors.
interpretation: These stones were divinely marked and set apart by Allah’s command, destined precisely for those who exceeded all bounds in disbelief, immorality, and rejection of His messengers; their punishment was therefore measured, deserved, and executed under Allah’s absolute knowledge and justice.

translation: So We brought out whoever was in it of the believers.
interpretation: This means that before Allah’s punishment descended upon the corrupt town, He rescued from it every person who had true faith, namely Prophet Lut and those of his household who believed with him. It teaches that Allah distinguishes the believers from the disbelievers and does not destroy the faithful along with the guilty; rather, He grants them safety and deliverance when His judgment comes upon a sinful people.

translation: Then We found not in it any but a single house of the Muslims.
interpretation: This refers to the towns of Lot’s people: despite the many inhabitants, only one household—Lot’s own—was found to be submitted to God’s command and free of the corrupt practice for which the people were destroyed. The verse underscores that true submission may be extremely rare even among large populations, and that God’s judgment distinguishes the believers from the guilty.

translation: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ruined settlements of the people of Lot, which God preserved as an enduring warning. It teaches that divine signs and historical remnants only benefit hearts that fear Allah's painful punishment, moving them to take heed, avoid sin, and repent.

translation: And in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh with a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse presents Moses as a sign and lesson: God sent him to Pharaoh equipped with manifest proofs and undeniable authority, so Pharaoh’s rejection was not caused by any deficiency in the evidence but by his own arrogant refusal to submit to the truth.

translation: So he turned away with his supporters and said, “A magician or a madman.”
interpretation: This verse portrays Pharaoh’s arrogant rejection of Moses: rather than submit to the clear signs brought to him, he withdrew in reliance upon his worldly power, troops, and followers, and tried to discredit Moses by slandering him as either a sorcerer or a madman. The contradictory accusation reveals that his denial was not grounded in evidence or sincere inquiry, but in pride, defiance, and a desire to protect his authority.
