interpretation: The verse means that Allah unleashed a violent punishment of wind-driven stones upon the people who rejected Lot and persisted in their corruption, while Lot’s household was exempted from that destruction. Their rescue in the pre-dawn hour shows that Allah separates the obedient from the guilty and protects His chosen servants before the disaster falls, even as His judgment overtakes the wrongdoers.

translation: A favor from Us. Thus do We reward whoever is grateful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that deliverance and blessings come from Allah’s grace, not from human merit alone. It establishes a divine principle: Allah recompenses those who show true gratitude—by acknowledging His favors, attributing them to Him, and responding with obedience and worship—with further favor, safety, and reward. Gratitude is thus a means of receiving and preserving divine blessings, and the verse shows that Allah’s recompense is both generous and just.

translation: And he had already warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warnings.
interpretation: The verse means that Lut had clearly warned his people that God's punitive seizure would come upon them because of their persistent corruption, yet they did not heed or accept it; instead, they argued against and doubted the warnings, treating them as untrue or impossible. Their dispute was not due to any ambiguity in the warning but due to their stubborn rejection, so the coming punishment was a just consequence of their denial.

translation: And they had sought to seduce him concerning his guests, so We erased their eyes. So taste My punishment and My warnings.
interpretation: This verse declares how God defends His messengers and those under their protection. When Lot’s people, already entrenched in shameless transgression, tried to assault the angelic guests, God instantly blinded their eyes, foiling their aggression before their final destruction. The command “taste My punishment and My warnings” shows that this blindness was only the first taste of chastisement and that their suffering was the direct consequence of rejecting divine warnings. The verse thus teaches that persistent sin, especially violating the sanctity of guests and defying a prophet, invites swift retribution, and that God’s power can disable the schemes of evildoers in an instant.

translation: And indeed, an abiding punishment came upon them in the morning.
interpretation: This means that the punishment descended upon them at daybreak and became fixed upon them—settled, inescapable, and lasting—so that it was not merely a passing affliction but a decreed destruction that overtook them after warning.

translation: So taste My punishment and My warnings.
interpretation: This is a divine command of retribution delivered after the people of Lut committed their brazen transgression and were struck with immediate blindness. "Taste" means they are made to experience the punishment directly, unavoidably, and with humiliation. "My warnings" refers to the repeated admonitions sent through the prophet, which they rejected; now the very consequence they were warned about has come upon them. The verse declares God's justice: persistent defiance of divine warning does not avert judgment but seals it, and the suffering itself becomes proof that the warnings were true. It also stands as a lasting lesson that God's threats are real and that violating His commands and attacking His messengers and guests leads to ruin.

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will take heed?
interpretation: The verse means that God has made the Qur'an accessible and unburdened for the purpose of dhikr—remembering, reciting, retaining, and reflecting upon it—and the rhetorical question calls every hearer to respond by turning to it with a heedful heart and making it their constant remembrance and guide.

translation: And indeed there came to the people of Pharaoh the warnings.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Pharaoh’s people were not destroyed without prior divine warning: Allah sent Moses and Aaron with clear signs and repeated admonitions, yet they persisted in denial and oppression. Its meaning is that divine punishment is preceded by warning and evidence, so rejecting the truth after it has come leaves no excuse; the fate of Pharaoh’s people stands as a warning to every later generation that stubbornly opposes the messengers.

translation: They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with the seizure of an Almighty, All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse means that those who reject every sign and proof of God’s authority will ultimately face His punishment with no means of escape. God’s seizure is that of One who is invincible in might and absolute in power, so no strength, wealth, or scheme can resist His judgment once He decrees it. It is a warning that persistent denial does not weaken God but only brings about a decisive and overwhelming reckoning.

translation: Are your disbelievers better than those [before them], or have you an exemption in the Scriptures?
interpretation: This verse rebukes the deniers by asking whether they are superior to the earlier nations that rejected their prophets and were destroyed, or whether they possess a revealed guarantee of safety from punishment. Since they are neither better nor granted immunity, the warning of Allah's judgment remains binding upon them unless they believe and reform.

translation: Or do they say, “We are all a victorious group”?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of arrogant self-confidence: they imagine that their numbers, unity, and mutual support make them invincible and able to defeat the truth. The verse exposes that claim as a delusion, since no collective power or worldly alliance can resist God’s decree. It warns that strength based on falsehood and opposition to divine guidance is ultimately doomed, and that being “all together” in error does not make one victorious.

translation: The assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs [in retreat].
interpretation: This is a definitive prophecy that the united forces of disbelief will be broken and routed; their numbers and alliance cannot shield them from God’s decree. When the confrontation comes, they will be overcome and flee in humiliation, turning their backs, which affirms that divine truth ultimately prevails over arrogant opposition.

translation: Nay, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter.
interpretation: This verse declares that the final reckoning is the fixed and unavoidable appointment for those who reject the truth; whatever delay or respite they enjoy in this world does not cancel that meeting. The Hour of Judgment is far more severe than any hardship, punishment, or calamity they can imagine in worldly life, and its bitterness is far greater. The verse therefore warns that denying or mocking the warning does not remove it, and it calls the human being to take the Hereafter seriously, prepare for it with faith and righteous action, and not be deceived by temporary worldly ease.

translation: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness.
interpretation: The verse means that those who persist in sin and denial are not on a sound path; their wrongdoing has plunged them into misguidance and a ruinous, self-destructive frenzy, so that their condition is one of spiritual insanity whose consequence is the Fire.

translation: The Day they will be dragged into the Fire on their faces, [and it will be said], "Taste the touch of Saqar!"
interpretation: This verse describes the utter humiliation and helplessness of the guilty on the Day of Judgment: they are dragged face-down into the Fire, stripped of dignity and unable to resist. The command “Taste!” makes the punishment directly experiential and inescapable, while “the touch of Saqar” signifies the scorching, painful contact of Hell, named Saqar to convey its crushing severity. Thus the verse serves as a severe warning: those who persist in arrogance and denial will face a punishment that is both physically agonizing and deeply debasing.

translation: Indeed, We have created all things by decree.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every created thing is subject to God’s precise decree and preordained measure; nothing comes into existence or occurs except according to His knowledge, wisdom, and will, including its nature, timing, and appointed end.

translation: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye.
interpretation: God’s command is a single, instantaneous decree: whenever He wills a thing, it comes to pass without delay, repetition, or gradual effort, as swift and effortless as the blink of an eye. This affirms His absolute power and the immediacy of His will, including the sudden coming of the Hour.

translation: And We have already destroyed your kinds, so is there any who will take heed?
interpretation: This verse warns that God has destroyed earlier peoples who resembled the disbelievers in their denial, arrogance, and sins. It asks whether anyone will learn from their fate, remember God’s warnings, and repent before a similar punishment comes.

translation: And everything they did is in the registers.
interpretation: This means that every deed, word, and action of human beings—whether good or evil, public or hidden—is recorded and preserved in the books of deeds kept by the angels. Nothing is omitted or lost, and on the Day of Judgment these records will be brought forth, so each person will face the consequences of what they earned.

translation: And every small and great thing is written down.
interpretation: This affirms that nothing is omitted from God’s record: every deed, word, hidden intention, and occurrence—whether minor or major—is inscribed and preserved, so that absolute justice and accountability rest upon complete knowledge.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers.
interpretation: This verse means that those who guard themselves against Allah’s displeasure by fulfilling His commands and avoiding His prohibitions will dwell in the Hereafter in gardens of everlasting bliss, with rivers flowing beneath and through them, as a reward and honor for their piety.

translation: In a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign Omnipotent.
interpretation: This describes the final station of the righteous as one of perfect honor, security, and truthfulness, established in direct nearness to God, the Absolute Sovereign whose power is unlimited and irresistible. The “seat of truth” signifies a state free from falsehood, disappointment, and instability, while being “with an Omnipotent Sovereign” means enjoying the favor, protection, and decree of the One whose authority and ability are complete and beyond any deficiency.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
interpretation: This invocation places every act under the name of the One whose mercy is both all-embracing and ever-flowing: al-Rahman names the mercy that originates and sustains all existence, al-Rahim names the mercy that reaches the servant in concrete guidance and forgiveness, and the closing al-Rahman reaffirms that this mercy is not an occasional act but the abiding identity of the Divine by which the servant seeks blessing, protection, and nearness.

translation: He taught the Qur'an.
interpretation: Allah, the Most Merciful, is the One who taught the Qur'an: He revealed it, enabled its recitation and preservation, and taught its meanings to whom He wills, making it a guidance and mercy for humanity rather than a human invention.

translation: He created man.
interpretation: This declares that Allah alone is the Creator of the human being, bringing humankind into existence by His power and will. It grounds human identity in dependence on God, not in chance, and presents creation as an act of divine authority and mercy that calls forth gratitude, humility, and accountability before the Creator.

translation: He taught him clear speech.
interpretation: Allah granted humankind the faculty of articulate expression and clarification, enabling people to communicate meanings, ideas, and intentions through language.

translation: The sun and the moon follow a precise calculation.
interpretation: This verse declares that the sun and the moon move according to an exact, divinely ordained measure. Their courses are not random or chaotic; they operate under God’s precise decree, reflecting His wisdom, power, and purposeful ordering of creation. This perfect regularity is a sign of His sovereignty and a mercy to humanity, since it makes time, seasons, and navigation possible.

translation: And the herbage and the trees prostrate.
interpretation: This verse means that the plants that have no trunk and the trees all submit to Allah's will, obeying the natural laws He created for them. Their prostration is their complete submission and obedience to His command, and it testifies to His power, wisdom, and sovereignty over all creation.

translation: And the heaven He raised, and He set up the balance.
interpretation: Allah raised the sky above the earth as a vast, ordered creation, and He established the measure of justice and equilibrium by which creation is governed and by which human beings are to weigh their affairs fairly.

translation: That you not transgress the balance.
interpretation: This is a command to uphold justice and fairness in all dealings, especially in weights, measures, and rights. It forbids exceeding the limits of equity, cheating others, diminishing their due, or letting greed and desire corrupt the balance God has established among creation.

translation: And establish the weight with justice, and do not cause loss in the balance.
interpretation: This is a command to uphold exact justice and fairness in all weights and measures, and more broadly in every transaction, judgment, and right. It forbids fraud, shortchanging, and any diminishment of what is due to others, because corrupting the balance destroys trust and violates divine justice.

translation: And the earth He laid out for the creatures.
interpretation: God spread out and made the earth habitable and suitable for all living beings, preparing it as a place of dwelling, sustenance, and benefit for His creation.

translation: In it are fruits and palm trees with sheaths.
interpretation: This verse points to God’s provision on the earth: a variety of fruits and date palms whose clusters are enclosed in protective sheaths, showing His power, wisdom, and mercy, and calling people to gratitude.

translation: And the grain, with its husk and the fragrant herbs.
interpretation: It points to God’s provision in both nourishment and delight: the grain is protected by its husk so it may be eaten, while the fragrant plants please the senses. This signifies that He cares for the body and the senses together, so people should recognize His bounty and respond with gratitude.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: It is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn, confronting them with the countless blessings and signs of their Lord so that they may acknowledge His generosity, submit to Him, and abandon ingratitude, denial, or rejection of His favors.

translation: He created man from clay like earthenware.
interpretation: This means that God originated the human being from a dry, molded earthly substance resembling pottery, showing His power to create and shape life from matter and reminding humans of their humble origin.

translation: And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire.
interpretation: This verse declares that the jinn were brought into existence from a pure, smokeless flame—meaning their original substance is a subtle, fiery energy unlike the clay from which humans were formed. It points to God’s power to create unseen beings with a distinct nature and constitution, and it reminds humans that the jinn are creatures created by God, not divine or independent of Him.

translation: So which of the blessings of your Lord do you two deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn: because God’s favors are countless and continual, no one can justly reject or deny them. It confronts the hearer with the impossibility of truly disowning God’s blessings and calls for acknowledgment, gratitude, and faith rather than ingratitude and denial.

translation: Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests.
interpretation: This affirms that Allah alone is the Lord and sovereign controller of all the horizons and times of sunrise and sunset; the dual form indicates the two limits or points of sunrise and the two limits or points of sunset, showing His dominion over every direction, season, and celestial movement.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn: after God enumerates His manifold blessings, He asks which of them they could possibly reject or deny. The intended meaning is that none of His favors can be truthfully denied, so the question presses them to acknowledge His bounty with gratitude and humble submission.

translation: He released the two seas, meeting.
interpretation: This verse means that Allah causes the two bodies of water—commonly understood as the salt sea and the fresh water—to flow and come together at their meeting points, while by His power and wisdom He preserves their distinct natures and keeps them from overstepping the limits He has set for them.

translation: Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress.
interpretation: This means that God has placed a hidden, inviolable boundary between the two seas, preventing each from overstepping its limit and mixing into the other, so their meeting remains governed by divine order and restraint.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke to both humans and jinn: every blessing, provision, mercy, and power they possess comes from God alone, so to deny or reject any of His favors is ingratitude and falsehood. The question confronts them with the impossibility of rightly rejecting His bounties and calls them to acknowledge His lordship and give thanks.

translation: From both of them emerge the pearl and the coral.
interpretation: This signifies God's power and bounty: from the two seas, though distinct and separated by a barrier, He brings forth precious pearls and coral as provision and adornment for humankind. It points to His sole authority over creation, His ability to produce valuable things from the depths, and His mercy in sustaining people. It also invites reflection on the resurrection, since the One who brings forth such treasures from the sea can surely bring forth life from the dead.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This is a reproachful rhetorical question addressed to both jinn and humankind: after enumerating countless blessings, God asks them how they can reject or deny any of His favors. It means that every blessing they enjoy comes from Him alone, so denying His bounty through ingratitude, disobedience, or associating others with Him is unjustified.

translation: And to Him belong the ships raised high on the sea like mountains.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the enormous ships that sail the oceans, appearing like mountains because of their size, are ultimately under Allah’s ownership, command, and enabling power. Though people build and operate them, their movement across the waters depends on the laws and favor He established, making them signs of His might, mercy, and providence, and calling people to acknowledge His lordship and show gratitude.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke and reminder addressed to both humans and jinn: after recounting numerous signs of divine mercy and power, God asks which of His blessings they could possibly reject or deny. The intended meaning is that every blessing—whether material, spiritual, outward, or inward—comes from the Lord alone, and no one can truly dismiss or repay it. The question therefore calls the hearer to acknowledge God's favors, respond with gratitude and obedience, and stop treating His bounties as if they were not from Him.

translation: Everyone upon it will perish.
interpretation: Every created being on the earth is subject to death and extinction; no inhabitant escapes annihilation, regardless of power or duration. Permanence belongs to God alone, so the heart should not cling to what is fleeting but should rely upon the Eternal, who is beyond death and change.

translation: And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.
interpretation: This verse affirms that all created beings are transient and will perish, while Allah alone is eternal and self-subsistent. His “Face” refers to His essence and self, which remains forever and is never subject to annihilation. He is Dhul-Jalal wal-Ikram: the Possessor of majesty, greatness, and awe, and the Possessor of honor, generosity, and bounty. Therefore, ultimate permanence, reverence, and worship belong to Him alone.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to humans and jinn together: after recounting countless blessings—creation, provision, guidance, mercy, and the means of return to God—it asks which of your Lord’s favors you can honestly reject or deny. The intended meaning is that none of His favors can be rightly denied, so ingratitude is exposed as irrational and unjust, and the only fitting response is grateful acknowledgment and obedience.

translation: All those in the heavens and the earth ask of Him. Every day He is in a matter.
interpretation: This verse affirms that every created being in the heavens and the earth is in constant need of Allah, turning to Him for its needs, whether by speech or by the very state of its dependence. It also declares that Allah is never inactive or detached from His creation: at every moment He is engaged in the affairs of His dominion—granting, withholding, raising, lowering, providing, answering, forgiving, and decreeing according to His wisdom and will. Thus, absolute reliance and supplication belong to Him alone, and His continuous disposal of all matters shows His perfect power, sovereignty, and watchful care over everything.

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn, asking them which of their Lord's numerous blessings they could possibly reject as false. It does not seek information; it exposes ingratitude and calls the hearer to recognize every favor—religious and worldly, open and hidden—as from God alone, and to respond with gratitude, obedience, and worship rather than denial.

translation: We will attend to you, O you two weighty ones.
interpretation: This is a warning from Allah addressed to both jinn and humankind, the two weighty creations, that He will turn to judge them, call them to account for their deeds, and requite each according to what they earned, so let them prepare for that reckoning.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to humans and jinn, confronting them with the countless blessings of God and exposing the absurdity of ingratitude. It does not seek information but calls them to acknowledge, thank, and obey the Lord rather than reject or belittle any of His favors.

translation: O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority.
interpretation: This verse is a divine challenge to both jinn and humans, declaring that they cannot escape God’s dominion, decree, or judgment. Even if they attempted to penetrate the boundaries of the heavens and the earth, they could never do so by their own power; any crossing or escape is possible only by a sultan—an authority, permission, or power granted by God. Thus it exposes the utter dependence and limitation of all created beings before their Creator.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn, calling them to recognize that every blessing they possess comes from their Lord and that no one can truthfully reject or deny His favors except through ingratitude, heedlessness, or disbelief. It urges them to respond with acknowledgment, gratitude, and obedience rather than denial.

translation: There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and smoke, and you will not be able to defend yourselves.
interpretation: This is a warning to both humans and jinn that divine punishment, when it comes, is an overwhelming force—blazing fire and suffocating smoke or molten metal—against which no one can shield himself or another. It declares that all claims of mutual support, power, and escape will collapse on that Day, and no created being will be able to repel Allah’s decree or save anyone from it. The dual address ‘you both’ underscores that both species are accountable and equally powerless before God.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This is a divine rebuke and reminder addressed to both jinn and humankind: every blessing—creation, provision, guidance, mercy, and every means of good—comes from the Lord alone, so it is inconceivable to deny or ungratefully reject any of them; the question is rhetorical, pressing them to acknowledge His favors and respond with gratitude and obedience.

translation: Then when the heaven is split asunder and becomes rose-colored like oil.
interpretation: This describes the cosmos losing its present order on the Day of Resurrection: the sky will rupture and take on a reddish, molten, rose-like appearance, like oil or paint. It signals the terrifying collapse of the created world before Allah’s command, when the familiar heavens are transformed and all creation is brought to accountability.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to humans and jinn, confronting them with the impossibility of rightly rejecting or ungratefully denying any of God's countless favors; it calls them to acknowledge His blessings and respond with gratitude and submission.

translation: So on that Day, neither a human nor a jinn will be asked about his sin.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, sinners will not be questioned in order to discover or establish their sins, for Allah already knows all that they did and their deeds are recorded; they will be known by their marks. The questioning that occurs elsewhere in the Qur’an is for rebuke and recompense, not for gaining information. Thus no human or jinn can conceal or evade the reality of his sin on that Day.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both jinn and humankind: after Allah enumerates His many visible and hidden blessings, He asks which of His favors they reject or fail to acknowledge. It exposes ingratitude and summons the creation to recognize that every bounty comes from its Lord alone, so denying or disregarding any of them is unjustified.

translation: The criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the guilty are recognized by visible signs that expose them, and they are dragged and thrown into punishment by their forelocks together with their feet—an image of utter humiliation, helplessness, and inescapable accountability before God.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both jinn and humankind, challenging them to name any of God’s countless blessings that they can rightly reject or deny. Its intended meaning is that no divine favor can truly be denied, so the question exposes ingratitude and calls the hearer to acknowledge God’s bounties with gratitude and submission.

translation: This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the guilty are confronted with the very Hell they rejected and mocked in worldly life. Their denial did not make it unreal; now it stands before them as an undeniable reality, and this address carries rebuke and just recompense for those who disbelieved in God’s warning and the Hereafter.

translation: They will circulate between it and scalding water, intensely hot.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment of the people of Hell: they are driven to move back and forth between the Fire and a boiling liquid that has reached the utmost degree of heat. The word “يطوفون” indicates restless wandering and inability to settle or find relief, while “حميم آن” refers to water heated to its absolute extreme, which burns and scalds those who drink it or are plunged into it. Their torment alternates between burning fire and burning drink, and they can neither escape nor find comfort. This is the recompense for those who denied the Hereafter and rejected the truth brought by the Messengers, and Allah’s judgment is perfectly just.

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn, challenging them to identify any of God’s countless blessings that they could truly reject. It calls them to acknowledge His continuous favors with gratitude, worship, and obedience rather than responding with denial and ingratitude.

translation: And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.
interpretation: This means that the one who fears Allah’s majesty, His reckoning, and the standing before Him for judgment, and therefore restrains himself from disobedience, will be rewarded with two gardens in Paradise. The verse presents fear of the Lord’s station as a cause of divine reward and indicates that such God-consciousness leads to honor, safety, and bliss in the Hereafter.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical reproach addressed to both humans and jinn, asking how any of God's countless blessings could be denied or rejected, and it calls them to acknowledge His favors with gratitude and submission.

translation: Both of them are possessed of branches.
interpretation: The two gardens are lush with spreading branches, foliage, and varied trees, indicating abundant fertility, shade, fruit, and layered delights prepared for the righteous.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question addressed to both jinn and humankind, compelling them to recognize that every blessing and mercy comes from God alone and that none of His favors can rightly be rejected or denied. It calls them to gratitude, obedience, and acknowledgment of His Lordship, and it exposes the folly of ingratitude by asking which specific bounty they could possibly deny.

translation: In both of them are two flowing springs.
interpretation: These are two springs in the two gardens of Paradise whose water flows continuously and never dries up, signifying the perpetual, ever-renewing delight and provision that God has prepared for the righteous.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn, challenging them to deny any of Allah’s countless blessings. It affirms that every favor, visible and hidden, comes from the Lord alone, and it calls the recipient to acknowledge His grace with gratitude rather than reject it through ingratitude, heedlessness, or disobedience.

translation: In both of them are two kinds of every fruit.
interpretation: This describes the two gardens of Paradise, stating that each contains every type of fruit in paired varieties, signifying abundant, varied, and complete provision and delight for the people of Paradise, so that they enjoy both diversity and perfection in what is given to them.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This rhetorical question is addressed to both humankind and jinn, challenging them to reflect upon the countless blessings, gifts, and mercies their Lord has bestowed upon them. It reproaches any inclination to reject, belittle, or fail to acknowledge those favors, and it calls them to gratitude, humble recognition of God’s grace, and obedience to Him alone.

translation: Reclining upon beds whose linings are of brocade, and the fruit of the two gardens is near.
interpretation: This verse describes the honored state of the righteous in Paradise: they recline in comfort upon couches whose inner linings are made of brocade, a luxurious silk fabric, indicating that even what is hidden is exquisite and that their outward covering is far more excellent. The two gardens are the paired paradises prepared for those who fear their Lord, and their fruit is near—easily reached, always available, and never withheld. The image conveys perfect rest, dignity, abundance, and a reward that is both intimate and everlasting.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both jinn and mankind, calling them to acknowledge that every blessing comes from their Lord and that none of His favors can justly be denied. It exposes the ugliness of ingratitude and disbelief in the face of continual divine generosity, and it urges the listener to respond with gratitude, faith, and obedience rather than rejection.

translation: In them are those who restrain their gaze, whom neither man nor jinn has touched before them.
interpretation: This describes the pure, chaste women of Paradise, whose eyes are kept only for their husbands, and who remain untouched by any human or jinn. It emphasizes their complete purity, modesty, and exclusive devotion, and it shows the honor and bliss Allah has prepared for the people of Paradise.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke and reminder addressed to both humans and jinn. God asks how they can reject or deny any of His abundant blessings when every provision, mercy, and sign comes from Him alone. It calls them to acknowledge His favors with gratitude and obedience rather than responding with ingratitude or denial.

translation: As if they were rubies and coral.
interpretation: This describes the maidens of Paradise as possessing exceptional beauty, purity, and radiance, likened to precious rubies and coral because they are flawless, luminous, and free from any defect or blemish.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you two deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn after God has recounted numerous visible and hidden blessings. It means that no one can rightly reject or deny His favors, since every provision, mercy, guidance, and power comes from Him alone; to deny them is ingratitude and falsehood, while the only fitting response is acknowledgment, thankfulness, and submission to His lordship.

translation: Is the reward for goodness anything but goodness?
interpretation: This rhetorical question affirms that God will never let sincere good deeds go unrewarded. Those who do ihsan—excellence, kindness, and righteousness—will receive good in return, ultimately the greatest good of God’s pleasure and Paradise. It establishes the principle that goodness is met with goodness, and it encourages believers to persist in doing good with the assurance that divine reward is both just and generous.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to humans and jinn: after all the countless blessings God has granted, none can truly be rejected or denied. It calls them to recognize every favor as coming from their Lord and to respond with gratitude and obedience rather than ingratitude.

translation: And below them both are two gardens.
interpretation: These are two further gardens, lower in rank than the two gardens previously mentioned, granted to a lesser station of the people of Paradise. They demonstrate that Paradise has varying degrees and that God rewards His servants according to their faith and deeds, with the foremost receiving the highest gardens and others receiving gardens beneath them in excellence and nearness.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical reproach addressed to both humans and jinn, meaning that none of God's favors can truly be denied or rejected; every blessing comes from Him alone, so the fitting response is gratitude, obedience, and worship.

translation: Both intensely green, dark green.
interpretation: It describes the two gardens as covered in lush, deeply green vegetation, their foliage so abundant and well-watered that it appears almost black.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn: after Allah recounts His countless favors, He asks which of them they can possibly reject or deny, thereby compelling them to acknowledge His generosity and respond with gratitude and obedience rather than ingratitude.

translation: In them are two springs, gushing forth.
interpretation: In the two gardens of Paradise, there are two springs whose water gushes and flows abundantly, never drying up or diminishing, as part of the reward and delight prepared for the righteous.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both jinn and humankind, challenging them to reject or deny any of Allah’s countless blessings and favors. It calls them to recognize that every provision, mercy, and grace comes from their Lord alone, and therefore He alone deserves gratitude, obedience, and worship.

translation: In both of them are fruit, and palm trees, and pomegranates.
interpretation: This verse describes the abundance and variety of delights in the two gardens of Paradise: they contain fruits in general, and specifically palm trees and pomegranates, which are singled out among the most prized and beneficial fruits. It signifies that the reward prepared for the righteous is not only sufficient but rich, varied, wholesome, and pleasing, combining nourishment with delight in a manner that reflects perfect divine generosity.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to humans and jinn: after Allah recounts numerous visible and hidden blessings, He challenges them to identify any bounty of their Lord that they could truly reject or deny. The question exposes ingratitude and calls the conscience to acknowledge that every favor—creation, provision, guidance, mercy, and deliverance—comes from Him alone, so the only fitting response is gratitude, obedience, and worship.

translation: In them are good and beautiful women.
interpretation: This describes the women of Paradise: they are good in character and conduct, and beautiful in appearance. It emphasizes that the bliss of Paradise includes companions who are both inwardly virtuous and outwardly lovely.

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both jinn and mankind, calling them to recognize that none of the countless blessings, bounties, and signs of their Lord can rightly be rejected or denied; it urges gratitude, reflection, and acknowledgment of God's continuous favors.

translation: Fair maidens with wide eyes, confined in tents.
interpretation: They are the pure companions of Paradise, kept in pavilions or tents, chaste and reserved, their beauty and companionship exclusively for the righteous believers. This signifies honor, seclusion, and perfect purity, indicating that the bliss of Paradise is safeguarded and intimate, free from any intrusion or imperfection.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical reproach addressed to humans and jinn, compelling them to recognize that none of God's blessings can rightly be denied or rejected; it calls them to gratitude, obedience, and acknowledgment of His continuous favors.

translation: No human has touched them before them, nor any jinn.
interpretation: This verse describes the pure companions prepared for the believers in Paradise. The word “طمث” refers to sexual contact or deflowering. By stating that no human or jinn has touched them before their husbands, it emphasizes their untouched purity and that they are reserved exclusively for the believers, free from any prior intimacy or defilement.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn, calling them to acknowledge God's countless blessings and warning them against ingratitude or denial of His favors.

translation: Reclining upon green cushions and beautiful, exquisite carpets.
interpretation: This describes the people of Paradise in perfect rest and honor: they recline on green cushions and rare, beautiful furnishings. The greenness conveys freshness, life, and continuous delight, while the fine carpets signify dignity and excellent reward. It is a picture of the serene comfort, honor, and bliss that God has prepared for the righteous.

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke addressed to both humans and jinn: after enumerating countless divine blessings, it challenges them to reflect on whether they can truly reject or deny any of their Lord’s favors. It calls them to acknowledge God’s generosity with gratitude and obedience rather than ingratitude and denial.

translation: Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor.
interpretation: This verse declares that God’s name is infinitely blessed, exalted, and filled with goodness. It affirms that He alone possesses supreme majesty, glory, and greatness, and that He is the source of all honor and generosity. Therefore, His name is to be revered, invoked with humility, and praised, for blessing and dignity come through remembrance of Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. When the Occurrence occurs.
interpretation: The 'Waqi'ah' (the Occurrence) is the inevitable Day of Resurrection, named so because it is certain to happen and cannot be averted. The verse announces that when that great event takes place, it will be a reality that none can deny or escape, and all creation will be gathered before Allah for judgment.

translation: There is no denying its occurrence.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Hour will inevitably come to pass; when it occurs, no one will be able to reject it, deny it, or turn it away. Its reality is certain and its happening is true, established by Allah’s decree.

translation: Abasing, exalting.
interpretation: This describes the Day of Resurrection as an event that brings low the arrogant, the deniers, and the sinners by casting them into humiliation and punishment, and raises high the believers, the humble, and the obedient by granting them honor and nearness to God.

translation: When the earth is violently shaken
interpretation: This describes the first stage of the overwhelming cosmic event at the Hour: God will set the earth into a violent convulsion, demolishing its stability and everything established upon it, so that all created beings are left with no refuge and are compelled to face resurrection and reckoning.

translation: And the mountains will be crushed with a crushing.
interpretation: This verse depicts the overwhelming dismantling of the created order at the onset of the Hour: the mountains, though vast and seemingly permanent, will be violently uprooted and pulverized into scattered particles, demonstrating that no worldly power or solidity can withstand God's command when the appointed time arrives.

translation: So they become scattered dust.
interpretation: The mountains, after being violently shattered, turn into fine, weightless particles dispersed through the air, leaving no trace of their former solidity, mass, or form. This signifies the total dissolution of the created order at the Hour and the absolute power of Allah over all things.

translation: And you will be [divided into] three kinds.
interpretation: This means that on the Day of Resurrection, people will be separated into three distinct categories, each receiving a rank and outcome corresponding to their faith and deeds: the people of the right, the people of the left, and the foremost in goodness.

translation: Then the companions of the right hand — what are the companions of the right hand?
interpretation: The question here is not for information but for magnification and wonder: it declares the immense honor, dignity, and bliss of those who will be given their record in their right hand on the Day of Judgment. They are the people of faith and righteous deeds, singled out by Allah’s pleasure and mercy; their rank is so elevated and their reward so great that it overwhelms description. “Right hand” signifies good fortune, acceptance, and salvation, and the rhetorical repetition intensifies the awe at their condition and the certainty of the good awaiting them.

translation: And the companions of the left hand — what are the companions of the left hand?
interpretation: This verse refers to the people who will be given their records in their left hands and are associated with the left side, signifying loss and punishment. The rhetorical question expresses the terror and gravity of their state: their condition is so dreadful and catastrophic that it cannot be fully described, and it serves as a severe warning against choosing the path that leads to it.

translation: And the forerunners, the forerunners.
interpretation: They are the believers who were first to believe and to hasten to righteousness, so they will be foremost in reward and nearness to Allah in the Hereafter.

translation: Those are the ones brought near.
interpretation: They are the foremost believers who hastened to faith and righteous deeds; God honors them in the Hereafter with nearness to Him, granting them the highest ranks of honor and bliss.

translation: In Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: This describes the final abode of the believers who are firmly established in the Gardens of Bliss, a state of unending delight, security, and nearness to God, where every good is perfected and no grief or toil remains.

translation: A company of the former peoples.
interpretation: It refers to the foremost believers from the earlier communities and generations—those who preceded in faith and righteous deeds—who will be many and will receive the highest ranks of nearness to Allah in Paradise.

translation: And a few of the later ones.
interpretation: This describes the highest category of believers—the forerunners brought near to Allah—as being numerous among the earlier communities but only a small number among the later generations. It does not mean that later believers are few in number overall, since elsewhere the People of the Right include many from the later peoples; rather, it highlights the rarity of attaining the station of the foremost, so the believer should strive to be among that few.

translation: Upon thrones woven [with gold and jewels]
interpretation: These are the couches or thrones in Paradise, intricately woven or adorned with gold and precious stones, prepared for the righteous as a sign of honor, comfort, and eternal bliss.

translation: Reclining upon them, facing one another.
interpretation: This describes the people of Paradise resting on cushioned couches or thrones, seated face to face in perfect fellowship. Their mutual facing signifies complete harmony and affection: no one turns his back on another, no envy, resentment, or rivalry mars their joy; they delight in one another’s company in eternal peace.

translation: There will circulate among them immortal youths.
interpretation: In Paradise, these youthful servants remain forever young, never aging or dying, attending to the believers as a sign of honor, comfort, and everlasting bliss.

translation: With cups, pitchers, and a goblet from a flowing spring.
interpretation: This describes the honor and perfect refreshment prepared for the people of Paradise: they will be served drinks in different vessels—cups for drinking, pitchers for pouring, and a goblet filled from a pure spring that flows continuously and never runs dry. It signifies abundant bliss, flawless hospitality, and delight that is pure and untainted, bringing no harm, intoxication, or regret.

translation: They will not suffer headache from it, nor will they become intoxicated.
interpretation: This describes the pure drink of Paradise: unlike worldly wine, it brings no pain, no mental clouding, no loss of reason, and no harmful aftereffect. Its pleasure is untainted and its enjoyment is safe, lasting, and free from every defect.

translation: And fruit of whatever they choose.
interpretation: This describes one of the delights of Paradise: the righteous will be served fruits of every kind they desire, selected according to their own preference. It signifies that their enjoyment will be complete and free, with no restriction or lack, and that they will be given exactly what they wish for.

translation: And the meat of birds from what they desire.
interpretation: This describes one of the enjoyments prepared for the people of Paradise: they will be given the flesh of birds exactly as their souls crave it, showing that Paradise gratifies every pure desire with perfect and effortless abundance.

translation: And fair companions with wide, lovely eyes.
interpretation: They are the pure, beautiful-eyed companions prepared by God in Paradise for righteous believers, signifying perfect beauty, purity, and honor as part of the eternal reward of the Hereafter.

translation: Like well-protected pearls.
interpretation: This simile conveys that the maidens of Paradise are of flawless purity and preserved beauty, likened to pearls kept hidden within their shells—untouched, unexposed, and safeguarded from anything that would diminish their radiance—so that their beauty is reserved exclusively for those granted Paradise.

translation: As a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This means that the good outcome, bliss, and honor mentioned are given by God as recompense for the righteous deeds those people used to perform in the world. It affirms that God does not let sincere good action go unrewarded, and that His reward is both just and generous: their deeds are the means through which they receive it, while the reward itself ultimately comes from God’s mercy and favor.

translation: They will not hear therein any idle talk or any sinful speech.
interpretation: In Paradise, the believers are kept far from every corrupt form of speech: no vain, false, or frivolous words, and nothing that carries sin, blame, or moral harm. Their hearing is reserved for what is pure, peaceful, and pleasing, reflecting the perfect serenity and purity of the eternal abode.

translation: Except a saying: "Peace, peace."
interpretation: This describes the speech of the people of Paradise: they hear no idle or sinful talk, but only words of peace, safety, and goodwill, repeated as a greeting and affirmation of mutual harmony. It signifies that Paradise is a realm purified of harmful or vain speech, where every word is sound, benign, and reflective of perfect peace.

translation: And the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of exaltation and awe, meant to magnify the status of the people of the right. It declares that their rank, reward, and final destination are so lofty and blessed that their reality exceeds full description, and it prepares the listener to hear the honors and joys prepared for them.

translation: Amid thornless lote trees
interpretation: This describes one of the delights prepared for the people of the right in Paradise: the sidr tree, normally known for its thorns, will be there without any thorns, so it offers pure comfort, abundant shade, and pleasant fruit without harm or inconvenience.

translation: And banana trees with fruit stacked in layers.
interpretation: This describes a tree in Paradise, understood by many exegetes as the banana tree, whose clusters of fruit are arranged densely one above another. It signifies abundant, easily accessible, and unending provision prepared for the people of the right.

translation: And an extended shade.
interpretation: It denotes the continuous, vast shade in Paradise, stretched out without end, providing perpetual comfort and relief, never shrinking or disappearing.

translation: and water poured out
interpretation: It describes one of the blessings of Paradise: water that is ever flowing and abundantly poured forth, available to its inhabitants without effort or interruption, as a sign of perpetual refreshment and divine provision.

translation: And abundant fruit
interpretation: In the context of Paradise, this refers to the plentiful, diverse, and never-ending fruits that Allah has prepared for the people of the right hand, as a reward for their faith and good deeds. It signifies both quantity and variety, and that these blessings are perpetual and not seasonal or limited.

translation: Neither cut off nor forbidden.
interpretation: This describes the fruits of Paradise as being perpetually available and completely unrestricted: they never run out, cease to exist, or pass out of season, and they are never withheld or prohibited from the believers who desire them. Unlike worldly provisions, which are subject to scarcity, decay, limits, or divine prohibition, the delights of Paradise are granted continuously and freely.

translation: And raised beds.
interpretation: These are elevated couches or furnishings prepared for the people of Paradise, indicating honor, comfort, and perpetual repose.

translation: Indeed, We have brought them into being as a new creation.
interpretation: This means that the women of Paradise are not created through ordinary human generation, but Allah directly originates them in a special, perfect creation, making them pure and suited for the eternal bliss of Paradise.

translation: And We made them virgins.
interpretation: This means that God created the women of Paradise in a state of perpetual virginity and purity, untouched and ever youthful, as a reward prepared for the righteous. It denotes their freedom from the imperfections and changes that affect worldly women, emphasizing their purity and the honor bestowed upon them.

translation: Loving and equal in age.
interpretation: This describes the pure companions of Paradise as deeply affectionate toward their spouses, with hearts inclined in love and devotion, and as being of one equal age, so that their union is marked by perfect harmony, mutual delight, and freedom from the discord, aging, or inequality found in worldly life.

translation: For the companions of the right.
interpretation: This refers to the blessed believers who are given their record in their right hand on the Day of Judgment and are destined for Paradise; the phrase declares that the pure, devoted companions of Paradise are prepared as an honor and reward for them.

translation: A multitude from the former generations.
interpretation: This refers to a large company of the foremost believers from the earlier communities—those who preceded others in faith, obedience, and righteous deeds—who will be among the highest ranks in Paradise.

translation: And a multitude from the later generations.
interpretation: This verse means that among the blessed people of the right hand there will also be a large group from those who come after the earliest believers—later generations who follow the same faith and righteousness—showing that God’s mercy and reward are not confined to the first believers alone.

translation: And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question expressing the extreme horror, disgrace, and severity of the fate of the people of the left. They are those who receive their deeds in their left hands and are among the people of loss, destined for the Fire. The question "what are the companions of the left?" conveys that their condition is so dreadful and catastrophic that it cannot be fully described; it signals their humiliation, punishment, and ruin in the Hereafter.

translation: In a scorching wind and boiling water.
interpretation: This describes the punishment of those consigned to the left hand: they are engulfed in an intensely hot, dry blast that penetrates and burns, and in water heated to its utmost, scalding them—an unrelenting torment of burning air and boiling water, with no relief or escape.

translation: And a shade of black smoke.
interpretation: It describes the punishment of the people of the left: their shade is not a comfort or relief, but a canopy of intensely dark, scorching smoke, the opposite of cool, refreshing shade, adding to their suffering rather than easing it.

translation: Neither cool nor refreshing.
interpretation: This describes a shade that gives no relief from the Fire’s heat and carries no goodness, comfort, or honor. It is a punishment utterly devoid of mercy or benefit, emphasizing the desolation and suffering of its people.

translation: Indeed, they were before that living in luxury.
interpretation: This verse states that the people being punished had been spoiled by ease, wealth, and self-indulgence in their worldly life, which made them heedless of God, arrogant, and persistent in wrongdoing. Their luxury was not merely a condition but a cause of their spiritual corruption: because they were immersed in comfort and desires, they denied the truth and refused accountability. Thus the verse warns that blessings can become a trial when they lead a person away from gratitude, obedience, and remembrance of the Hereafter.

translation: And they used to persist in the great sin.
interpretation: This means they stubbornly continued in the gravest transgression—chiefly disbelief, associating partners with Allah, and rejecting the truth of resurrection and accountability—without repenting. The phrase emphasizes that their wrongdoing was not a passing lapse but a deliberate, repeated, and entrenched violation of what is most serious before Allah.

translation: And they used to say, 'When we die and become dust and bones, will we indeed be raised again?'
interpretation: This verse reports the disbelievers’ habitual, mocking denial of the resurrection. Their question is not a sincere search for truth but a rhetorical expression of astonishment and rejection: they assumed that once the body has decomposed into dust and bones, restoring it to life is impossible. The verse exposes the shallow, materialistic basis of their disbelief—they measured God’s power by their own limited experience and regarded physical disintegration as a final barrier. In its context, it is a rebuke: the One who created them in the first place without any prior model is fully able to bring them back after death. Thus the verse warns that denying the hereafter is not a reasoned position but a stubborn refusal to acknowledge divine omnipotence and accountability.

translation: And our forefathers of old?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of denial and astonishment from the disbelievers, expressing their disbelief that they and their ancient ancestors—long dead—could be resurrected. It conveys their rejection of the Resurrection as something they deemed impossible.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the former and the latter.'
interpretation: This is a divine command to the Prophet to declare that the resurrection and gathering are universal: every human being, from the earliest generations to the last, will be raised and assembled before Allah for reckoning, with no one excluded.

translation: will surely be gathered to the appointed time of a known Day.
interpretation: This verse affirms that all created beings will be resurrected and assembled at an exact, fixed moment on a Day whose timing is fully determined and known to God, for the purpose of reckoning and recompense.

translation: Then indeed you, O misguided ones, the deniers,
interpretation: This is a stern address to those who rejected the truth: they wandered away from right guidance and deliberately denied God’s message and the coming reckoning, so they are being confronted with the consequence of that disbelief.

translation: You will surely eat from a tree of Zaqqum.
interpretation: This is a severe threat to the deniers: their food in the Fire will be taken from the Zaqqum tree, a tree in Hell whose fruit is bitter, repulsive, and painful. The emphatic form shows that this punishment is certain and unavoidable for them, and eating from it is part of their humiliation and torment, not nourishment or enjoyment.

translation: And filling from it their bellies.
interpretation: This describes the people of Hell being compelled to eat from the tree of Zaqqum until their stomachs are full, despite its bitterness and harmfulness. It signifies that their hunger and punishment are so severe that they are driven to consume what neither nourishes nor satisfies, and it becomes a source of further torment within them.

translation: And you will drink upon it from boiling water.
interpretation: This describes the punishment of the people of Hell after they have eaten from the Zaqqum tree and filled their bellies: they will be compelled to drink scalding, intensely hot water on top of that food. It signifies that their torment is compounded—hunger is followed by a drink that neither refreshes nor quenches thirst, but instead burns and tears at their insides. The verse conveys the severity and humiliation of the retribution awaiting those who knowingly rejected the truth and persisted in denial.

translation: Then you will drink as the thirsty camels drink.
interpretation: This describes the disbelievers in Hell after they eat from the bitter tree of Zaqqum: they are made to drink scalding water, gulping it down uncontrollably like camels consumed by extreme thirst. It conveys their humiliation, torment, and desperate thirst, yet the drink does not quench them or bring relief; it only intensifies their suffering.

translation: This is their reception on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: It means that the deniers who rejected the truth will be received on the Day of Recompense with the punishment prepared for them—the tree of Zaqqum and scalding water—as a just recompense and humiliation. The term “reception” is used ironically: what would normally be hospitality for a guest is here the torment they have earned by their denial and arrogance.

translation: We created you, so why do you not believe?
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who deny the resurrection: since God originated your creation in the first place, you should readily affirm His power to create you again and should believe in His promise of accountability.

translation: Have you then considered what you emit?
interpretation: This verse calls the human being to reflect on the seminal fluid he discharges: he has no power to make it into a living, conscious human being, nor does he control its formation, development, or the soul breathed into it. The rhetorical question thus exposes human inability and points to God alone as the Creator who originates life, sustains it, and can bring it back after death.

translation: Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of rebuke: human beings do not create the life they emit; God alone is the Creator who brings it into existence and forms it. It establishes that all creation, especially the creation of human life, is exclusively God's act, and no creature shares in that creative power.

translation: We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outstripped.
interpretation: This is a declaration of God’s exclusive authority over the term of every living being: death is fixed by His decree and cannot be averted, delayed, or hastened by any creature. The phrase “not to be outstripped” means that no power can overpower Him, escape His will, or prevent Him from carrying out what He has ordained, including resurrection and re-creation. It calls the heedless to recognize that their lifespan is in God’s hand and to prepare for the meeting with Him.

translation: That We may replace you with others like you and bring you into being in what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse affirms God's unlimited power over creation, death, and resurrection. He is not incapable of removing a people and bringing forth others like them, nor is He limited to the forms and conditions humans already know. It declares that He can recreate human beings after death in a new state, body, or realm beyond human comprehension, and it warns people that their existence is not necessary to God: He can substitute them and originate them anew however He wills.

translation: And you have already known the first creation, so will you not then remember?
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who reject the resurrection: the same power of God that brought them into existence initially can surely bring them back to life after death, so they are called to reflect on that evidence and remember their dependence on Him.

translation: Have you considered what you sow?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question that calls people to reflect on the seeds they plant and the crops they cultivate. Human beings may plough, sow, and tend the earth, but they do not possess the power to make the seed germinate, grow, or bear fruit. That belongs to God alone. The verse therefore awakens awareness of human dependence on divine provision, invites gratitude for sustenance, and reminds the listener that every harvest is a sign of God's power, mercy, and generous care.

translation: Is it you who sow it, or are We the Sowers?
interpretation: This rhetorical question establishes that human beings may plant and cultivate, but they have no power to create life, cause germination, or bring forth growth and harvest. That belongs to Allah alone. It calls people to recognize His oneness and providence, to abandon self-conceit over their labor, and to be grateful, since all sustenance and life depend upon His will.

translation: If We willed, We could make it dry, broken chaff, and you would remain in wonder and regret.
interpretation: This is a rhetorical affirmation of God's absolute sovereignty over the produce of the earth. Even after humans plow, plant, and cultivate, the harvest remains wholly dependent on His will; He could reduce it to dry, broken chaff in an instant. The consequence would be that people are left stunned, regretful, and helplessly lamenting the loss of what they had labored for. Thus the verse humbles human pride, exposes the illusion of self-sufficiency, and directs gratitude and reliance to God alone, who alone sustains and protects the fruits of labor.

translation: Indeed, we are ruined.
interpretation: In the Qur’anic context, this is the acknowledgment of people whose crops have been destroyed: they say it as a confession that they have suffered irreversible loss, as though they have been burdened with debt or stripped of the fruit of their labor. It expresses the helplessness of the human being when God’s decree nullifies worldly provisions, and it warns against relying solely on material gain that can be taken away.

translation: Rather, we are deprived.
interpretation: This is the lament of those whose crops are ruined: they admit they have been denied the expected harvest and provision, but they speak in despair and complaint rather than turning back to God. It shows that deprivation ultimately comes by God’s decree, often as a consequence of human ingratitude and sin, and that people should respond to loss with repentance and awareness of God’s power, not mere regret over what they have missed.

translation: Have you considered the water which you drink?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question that directs people to reflect on the water they drink and to recognize that they neither originate it nor control its descent and purity; it is Allah who sends it down and makes it available and drinkable, thereby demonstrating His power, mercy, and right to be thanked and worshipped alone.

translation: Is it you who send it down from the rain clouds, or are We the One who sends it down?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question establishing that no human has any power to cause rain to descend from the clouds; it is God alone who creates and sends it down, and therefore He alone deserves gratitude and worship.

translation: If We willed, We could have made it bitter and undrinkable; then why do you not give thanks?
interpretation: This verse calls people to gratitude for the blessing of fresh, palatable water. God reminds them that the water they drink is not something they created or guaranteed; had He willed, He could have made it salty, bitter, or unfit to drink. Its being fresh and life-sustaining is therefore a mercy and favor from Him, and the proper response is to acknowledge His generosity, thank Him, and not be ungrateful by heedlessness or disobedience.

translation: Have you considered the fire which you kindle?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical address prompting people to reflect on the fire they kindle. They may strike the flame, but they did not create its capacity to burn or the wood that sustains it; it depends entirely on God’s creation. The verse thus confronts human arrogance by showing that even an ordinary fire is a sign of divine power, and it points to God’s ability to resurrect and to the reality of the fire of the Hereafter.

translation: Is it you who created its tree, or are We the creators?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question affirming that human beings did not originate or create the tree from which they kindle fire; God alone is the true Creator and Originator. It establishes His exclusive power over creation and all natural means, showing that even the resources people use are His provision. Therefore, humans owe Him gratitude, worship, and reliance, and this also serves as a proof that the One able to create and sustain such things is able to resurrect.

translation: We have made it a reminder and a provision for the wayfarers.
interpretation: Allah made the fire that people kindle from dry trees a reminder of His creative power and of the fire of the Hereafter, and a beneficial provision for travelers in barren lands, who use it for warmth, light, and cooking.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This is a command to declare God's absolute perfection and transcendence, to purify His name from every deficiency or false attribution, and to remember and invoke Him with reverence, acknowledging that He alone possesses supreme greatness and majesty.

translation: So I swear by the positions of the stars.
interpretation: God swears by the precise locations, rising points, setting places, and ordered courses of the stars, directing attention to the vastness and exactness of the created cosmos as a sign of His wisdom and power. This oath serves to emphasize the certainty of the Qur’an’s message and the reality of the resurrection, for the One who arranged the stars with such precision is fully able to bring creation back to life and hold it accountable.

translation: And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense weight and seriousness of the oath being sworn; it is not an ordinary oath, but one of tremendous significance. The phrase “if you only knew” directs the listener to reflect deeply, indicating that if people truly understood the greatness of the oath and the reality to which it points, they would give it the utmost attention, reverence, and seriousness.

translation: Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the revelation is the noble Qur'an, meaning it is intrinsically honored and precious, possessing a lofty rank with Allah, free from any defect or falsehood, and worthy of being received with reverence, obeyed, and conveyed faithfully; its nobility is not derived from created things but from its divine origin and enduring guidance.

translation: in a concealed Book
interpretation: This means that the Qur’an is preserved in a hidden, guarded heavenly source—the Preserved Tablet—beyond human access and tampering, indicating that its origin is divine and that it is protected from corruption and alteration.

translation: None touches it except the purified.
interpretation: It means that the Qur’an is preserved in a protected heavenly Book, and none has access to it except the purified angels, showing its exalted and sacred station.

translation: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is sent down by the Lord of all creation, so its origin is divine and its authority extends over all beings; it is not a humanly invented message.

translation: Then is it this message that you are treating lightly?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who hear the Qur’an—the noble, revealed speech from the Lord of the worlds—yet respond with complacency, flattery, or indifference instead of earnest seriousness. “Mudhinun” describes people who soften their stance, conceal their true response, or treat the matter as something trivial to avoid commitment or please others. The question is a reproach: how can such a decisive revelation be met with half-hearted, lukewarm, or evasive treatment?

translation: And you make your provision that you deny [the truth].
interpretation: This verse rebukes those who meet God’s sustenance and blessings with rejection instead of gratitude and faith. They treat the very provision given to them as an occasion or means for denying the revelation, so their response to God’s favor becomes disbelief and ingratitude rather than acknowledgment and obedience.

translation: Then why, when [the soul] reaches the throat,
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke to those who deny resurrection and divine accountability. At the moment of death, when the soul reaches the throat and is about to leave the body, the dying person and all who surround him are utterly helpless. If they truly control their own destiny or can escape Allah’s decree, why can they not bring that departing soul back? The verse confronts them with their powerlessness and proves that life and death are solely in Allah’s hand, and that the return to Him is certain.

translation: while you are, at that moment, looking on.
interpretation: This verse describes the helplessness of those present when a person is dying and the soul reaches the throat: they can only watch, unable to prevent death, delay it, or restore the dying person. It awakens the listener to the nearness of God to His creation at the moment of death, even though people do not perceive that nearness with their eyes.

translation: And We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see.
interpretation: At the moment when the soul reaches the throat and those present can only look on helplessly, God is closer to the dying person than they are through His knowledge, decree, power, and the angels He sends; yet this unseen nearness is beyond human sight.

translation: Then why, if you are not to be recompensed,
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who deny resurrection and accountability: if they are truly not subject to God’s judgment and will not be recompensed, then let them return the departing soul to its body—something they cannot do. Their helplessness at the moment of death demonstrates that they remain under God’s dominion and that the reckoning they deny is real.

translation: You return it, if you are truthful.
interpretation: This is a divine challenge to those who deny resurrection and Allah’s exclusive power over life and death: when the soul reaches the throat and the dying person is beyond human help, if your claims and denials are true, bring that soul back into the body. Your inability to do so proves that life and death are entirely in Allah’s hand and that the return to Him is certain.

translation: Then, if he is among those brought near [to Allah],
interpretation: This clause identifies the highest category of souls before God: those brought near are not merely believers in name, but people whose hearts, worship, and conduct have been purified and drawn close to their Lord. Nearness here is relational and spiritual: it means a life oriented wholly toward God, marked by sincerity, obedience, and love. At the moment of death, such a person is met with honor rather than loss, because the soul that belongs to the brought-near ones passes into the care and pleasure of God. The verse thus presents this rank as the ultimate aspiration and implies that it is attained through faithful striving, not mere affiliation.

translation: Then there is rest and fragrant provision, and a Garden of Bliss.
interpretation: This verse describes the immediate reward of the soul that is brought near to Allah: at death it passes into tranquility, divine mercy, and pleasing sustenance, and is admitted into the Garden of eternal delight. It signifies that nearness to God yields a state of comfort and honor that begins in the grave and culminates in everlasting bliss, far beyond the sensory pleasures of this world.

translation: And if he is among the companions of the right,
interpretation: This describes the state of the righteous soul at death or in the Hereafter: if the person belongs to the People of the Right—those who receive their record in the right hand and are among the saved—then this is a condition of honor, security, and good news. The following verse completes it with peace and reassurance, meaning that such a person will be met with safety and glad tidings, and their final destination is the company of the blessed in Paradise.

translation: So peace be upon you, from the companions of the right.
interpretation: This is a greeting of honor and security for the one who is among the people of the right—the blessed. It means they are safe from every harm and punishment, and they are received with peace and joined with the righteous.

translation: And if he is among the deniers, the misguided.
interpretation: This describes the state of one who rejects the truth and turns away from divine guidance. The two descriptions are closely connected: denial of the message leads to misguidance, and misguidance deepens denial.
