Such a person is explicitly excluded from the ranks of the favored and the righteous, and is instead deserving of the punishment that follows in the next verse. The verse thus teaches that a person's eternal outcome is determined by whether they accept the truth and remain on the path of guidance, not merely by outward affiliation.

translation: Then a lodging of scalding water.
interpretation: This describes the reception and dwelling prepared for the one who denied the truth and went astray: it is a place of punishment in Hell consisting of intensely boiling water, which they will be made to drink and by which they will be tormented. It signifies disgrace, agony, and a painful end, in contrast to the honorable welcome and bliss prepared for the righteous.

translation: and roasting in Hellfire
interpretation: This describes the punishment of the obstinate rejecters as being made to endure the blazing Fire, not merely being near it. The word “taṣliyah” conveys actively being subjected to the flame’s heat until it penetrates and burns, while “jaḥīm” denotes an intensely kindled, unrelenting fire. It is therefore a state of severe, humiliating torment and painful recompense, the opposite of the delight and gardens promised to the faithful.

translation: Indeed, this is the very truth of certainty.
interpretation: It is an emphatic affirmation that the matter being stated is not conjecture, probability, or mere report, but reality itself, established with absolute certainty and free from any doubt. The construction “ḥaqq al-yaqīn” conveys that the truth is certainty itself—unwavering, incontrovertible, and impossible to deny for one who understands it.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet—and through him every believer—to declare God’s absolute transcendence and perfection, invoking His name with reverent worship and affirming His incomparable greatness, which surpasses all human conception and description; such glorification is an act of humble submission, continuous remembrance, and acknowledgment that all majesty belongs to Him alone.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that every existent in the heavens and earth—by its very being, order, and submission to Allah—declares His transcendence and freedom from any imperfection. This glorification is not limited to conscious beings; all creation testifies to its Maker. The names al-‘Aziz and al-Hakim then affirm that His might is exercised with perfect wisdom, so His creation, command, and judgment are never arbitrary but are ordered toward truth and purpose.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah’s exclusive sovereignty and absolute power: all creation and its affairs belong to Him alone; He alone originates life and decrees death, and nothing is beyond His ability, so He is the only one worthy of worship, reliance, and submission.

translation: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God is absolutely prior to all existence and absolutely enduring after all creation ends; He is al-Zahir, manifest through His signs, creation, and governance, yet al-Batin, hidden in His essence beyond human sight and full comprehension. His knowledge is all-encompassing: nothing outward or inward, past, present, or future, is hidden from Him.

translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah’s exclusive power of creation, His complete knowledge, and His ever-present awareness of His creation. He created the heavens and the earth in six days although He is able to create them instantly, showing that creation unfolds by His wisdom and decree. His rising over the Throne is an act of majesty and dominion that befits Him, without likening Him to created things or imagining Him confined by space. He knows every hidden and visible movement: what enters the earth, what emerges from it, what comes down from the sky, and what ascends toward it. His being “with you” means His knowledge, care, and oversight accompany every person at every place and time; it does not mean that He is physically mixed with creation. Therefore, since He sees all deeds, people should live with sincerity, accountability, and awareness that nothing escapes Allah’s sight.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse establishes that absolute sovereignty, ownership, and authority belong exclusively to Allah over all creation. Every affair—whether in the heavens or the earth, in this life or the next—ultimately returns to Him alone for decree, judgment, and final resolution. Therefore, no power, authority, or outcome exists independently of His will, and all creatures are accountable to Him. The verse directs the heart to rely solely on Allah, to submit to His rule, and to live in awareness that every matter ends with Him.

translation: He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He is Knower of what is in the breasts.
interpretation: This means that Allah alone governs the alternation and interpenetration of night and day, lengthening and shortening them by His command, which displays His absolute power and wise ordering of creation. The concluding phrase teaches that the same God who governs the vast universe also knows the hidden thoughts, intentions, and motives within human hearts, so nothing inward is hidden from Him. Therefore, the verse calls for acknowledging His lordship over time and for sincerity before Him, since He judges not only outward deeds but the secrets of the breast.

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend out of that which He has made you trustees over. For those among you who believe and spend, there is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse calls people to combine faith in Allah and His Messenger with generous giving from the wealth and resources they possess. It reminds them that whatever they own is not ultimately their own independent possession; Allah has placed it under their temporary trust and stewardship. Therefore, those who truly believe and use what they have been given to spend in Allah’s cause will receive a vast and generous reward.

translation: And why do you not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are indeed believers?
interpretation: This is a reproach and a decisive proof against hesitation in faith: the Messenger is actively summoning you to your Lord, and God has already bound you by a covenant—whether the primordial covenant in which you acknowledged Him as Lord, or the covenant conveyed through His prophets—so disbelief has no valid excuse. The phrase “if you are believers” means: if you claim faith or possess the capacity for it, then sincerity requires you to answer the call, because the covenant you accepted already obliges you to believe.

translation: He is the One Who sends down upon His servant clear verses to bring you out of darkness into the light. And indeed, Allah is to you Most Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: Allah sends down clear, manifest revelations upon His servant Muhammad to guide people from the darknesses of disbelief, ignorance, doubt, and sin into the light of faith, knowledge, and obedience. This divine guidance is itself a sign of Allah's compassion and mercy toward His creation, for He does not leave them in misguidance but provides the means by which they may be rescued and brought to true light.

translation: And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah, while to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. Those are greater in degree than those who spent afterward and fought. But to all Allah has promised the best reward. And Allah is Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse urges believers to give generously in Allah’s cause and not cling to wealth, since all possessions ultimately return to Allah, the true Owner and Inheritor of the heavens and the earth. It then distinguishes between believers according to the time and cost of their sacrifice: those who spent their wealth and fought before the victory did so when Islam was weak, danger was great, and sacrifice was most difficult, so they hold a higher rank than those who gave and fought after the victory, when the community had become stronger. Yet Allah’s promise of the best reward is extended to both groups, showing that sincere service is not wasted. The verse teaches that Allah evaluates deeds with full knowledge of intentions, circumstances, and the true weight of each person’s sacrifice.

translation: Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him, and he will have a noble reward?
interpretation: This is an exhortation to spend in the way of Allah with sincerity, giving from lawful wealth willingly and without expecting return from people. Calling it a “loan to Allah” is a merciful metaphor: Allah, who is free of all need, promises to repay the giver manifold and to grant a generous, honorable reward in the Hereafter. Thus the verse encourages charity and sacrificial giving by assuring the believer that no good deed is lost with Allah and that He will abundantly compensate it.

translation: On the Day when you see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and on their right hands: Glad tidings for you this Day: Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: The light is the radiance of faith and righteous deeds that God grants the believers on the Day of Resurrection, guiding them across the bridge and toward Paradise; its going before them and on their right signifies honor, safety, and receiving the record of deeds in the right hand. The glad tidings are eternal Gardens with rivers flowing beneath them, and this is the supreme success because it is deliverance from punishment and attainment of God's pleasure.

translation: On the Day when the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believed, 'Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light.' It will be said, 'Go back behind you and seek light.' Then a wall will be set up between them, having a gate; its inner side contains mercy, and its outer side, facing them, contains punishment.
interpretation: This verse portrays the ultimate separation between sincere faith and hypocrisy. The light of the believers in the Hereafter is not merely illumination but the fruit and proof of their faith; the hypocrites, who assumed outward conformity could substitute for inward belief, try to benefit from it but are told to seek light on their own, which they cannot do. The barrier with a gate signifies that the two groups may have coexisted in this world, but in the final reality they are divided by an unbridgeable moral and spiritual boundary. The inner side of mercy belongs to those whose hearts were aligned with God and His Messenger, while the outer side of punishment faces those who concealed disbelief and betrayed the trust of faith. The scene warns that religiosity reduced to appearance, social belonging, or opportunistic association will not avail when deeds are judged, and that divine mercy is reached only through sincere faith, repentance, and righteous action.

translation: They will call out to them, “Were we not with you?” They will say, “Yes, but you subjected yourselves to trial, and you waited, and you doubted, and false hopes deceived you until the command of Allah came, and the deceiver deceived you concerning Allah.”
interpretation: This verse exposes that outward companionship with the believers is worthless if the heart remains in hypocrisy. Such people corrupt themselves by choosing disbelief while pretending to belong, wait for the faithful to fall, doubt Allah’s promise, and let vain desires and false expectations delude them until death and Allah’s decree overtake them. Satan’s greatest deception is to make them feel secure from Allah’s judgment and to mistake His patience for approval, so their former association with the believers cannot benefit them in the Hereafter.

translation: So today no ransom will be accepted from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire; it is your protector, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, no compensation, ransom, or plea can avert punishment from the hypocrites or from those who openly rejected faith. Their final abode is the Fire, which will dominate them as their patron and master, leaving them with no helper or escape. This is the most wretched end, showing that worldly wealth, status, or deception cannot save anyone from the consequences of persistent disbelief and hypocrisy.

translation: Has the time not come for the believers that their hearts should become humble at the remembrance of Allah and at what has come down of the truth, and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, whose term was prolonged, so their hearts became hard; and many of them were disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is a tender yet stern call to believers to awaken spiritually before it is too late: their hearts should soften, submit, and tremble with reverence when Allah is remembered and when His revealed truth is recited. It warns them not to resemble the earlier People of the Book, who were given revelation but, because a long time passed and they neglected it, their hearts gradually hardened and many fell into disobedience. The meaning is that faith must remain alive, responsive, and humble; remembrance of Allah and engagement with revelation are means of keeping the heart soft. Prolonged heedlessness, procrastination, and familiarity with sacred things can cause spiritual petrification, so the believer must guard against becoming like those whose outward connection to scripture remained while inward receptivity died.

translation: Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have indeed made clear to you the signs, so that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse directs people to recognize Allah’s power to bring life back to dead, barren earth, and from that to infer His ability to resurrect the dead, revive hardened hearts with guidance, and bring about renewal after decline; the clear signs are given so that people may use their reason and respond with faith and reflection.

translation: Indeed, the charitable men and the charitable women and those who loan Allah a goodly loan—it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse establishes that both men and women who give freely in charity and spend in God's cause with sincerity are regarded as lending to God, not as losing their wealth. God promises to multiply their recompense beyond measure and to grant them an honorable reward in the Hereafter. It thus encourages generous giving, assures believers that no good deed is wasted, and confirms that men and women are equal in this spiritual promise.

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers — those are the truthful, and the martyrs with their Lord will have their reward and their light. And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs — those are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse affirms that sincere faith in Allah and in all His messengers elevates believers to the rank of the truthful, while the martyrs are especially honored with their Lord, receiving their reward and a light that signifies guidance, honor, and divine favor. It then warns that those who reject faith and deny Allah’s signs will be the inhabitants of Hell, showing the contrast between the eternal reward and light of the faithful and the punishment of the deniers.

translation: Know that the life of this world is only play, amusement, adornment, boasting among yourselves, and rivalry in wealth and children—like rain whose vegetation pleases the tillers; then it dries up, and you see it turning yellow, then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and pleasure. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly life, when treated as the ultimate goal, is a series of fleeting states: play, distraction, decoration, mutual boasting, and competition for more wealth and offspring. Its apparent success is like a crop after rain: impressive for a time, then it withers, yellows, and crumbles into worthlessness. The Hereafter alone is lasting and decisive, holding either severe punishment for those deceived by the world or forgiveness and divine pleasure for those who seek Allah’s approval. Therefore, the world’s goods are not forbidden in themselves, but they become “the enjoyment of delusion” when they blind a person to the Hereafter and are mistaken for the true purpose of existence.

translation: Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who have believed in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse urges believers to compete earnestly in seeking God’s forgiveness and the vast reward of Paradise. The description of Paradise’s immense breadth points to a reward beyond human comprehension, prepared for those whose faith is directed to Allah and to all His messengers. The reward is not something earned as a right; it is God’s favor, granted by His will and wisdom. Thus, the verse combines an urgent call to action with the profound truth that salvation and eternal reward rest ultimately on God’s generous grace, and His bounty is limitless.

translation: No calamity strikes in the earth or in yourselves except that it is in a Book before We bring it into existence. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse teaches that every misfortune—whether it occurs in the world, such as earthquakes, droughts, and disasters, or within a person, such as illness, loss, and hardship—was already known and recorded by Allah in the Preserved Tablet before He created the creation. Nothing escapes His knowledge or happens outside His will and decree. The phrase “that is easy for Allah” affirms that recording and bringing about all things, however vast or numerous, costs Him no effort. The believer is therefore called to accept divine decree with patience and trust, finding comfort that no calamity is random or forgotten, and that Allah’s wisdom and justice encompass all affairs.

translation: So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult over what He has given you. And Allah does not like every conceited boaster.
interpretation: This verse teaches that because all loss and all gain come under God's decree and ownership, the believer should not let the heart collapse in excessive grief over what was missed or swell with arrogant joy over what was received. It directs the believer to humility and reliance on God, and it warns that God does not love those who are self-important and boastful, whether before God or before people.

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin people to stinginess. And whoever turns away—then indeed Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Miserliness is condemned not only when a person withholds good from others but also when he encourages them to do the same. Whoever turns away from generosity, obedience, or faith harms only himself; he cannot diminish Allah in any way. Allah is completely independent of His creation and needs nothing from anyone, while He is praiseworthy in His essence, whether or not people respond with gratitude or obedience.

translation: Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Scripture and the Balance, so that people may establish justice. And We sent down iron, in which there is severe might and benefits for people, and so that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God guides humanity through messengers supported by clear evidences, and through revealed Scripture and the criterion of justice so that human societies may uphold fairness and equity. Iron represents both the reality of material strength and its many beneficial uses, but it also serves as a test: power, wealth, and worldly means must be used in support of God and His messengers even when the divine reality is unseen. God’s strength and majesty mean that He is fully capable of aiding His cause and that no support given to Him is ever overlooked.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham, and We placed among their descendants prophethood and the Scripture. So among them is one rightly guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: God reminds humanity that He sent Noah and Abraham as messengers and made prophethood and revealed Scripture continue among their offspring as a great favor. Yet this noble lineage did not automatically guarantee guidance: some of their descendants accepted the truth and followed it, while many broke God’s bounds and rejected it. The verse teaches that guidance is a matter of God’s grace and a person’s own response, not merely inherited status; prophetic descent carries responsibility, not privilege that saves without faith and obedience. It also affirms that God’s sending of messengers and books is part of His wise providence, and the disobedience of many does not nullify His truth or His plan.

translation: Then We made Our messengers follow in their footsteps, and We followed them with Jesus, son of Mary, and We gave him the Gospel. And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. But monasticism—they invented it; We did not prescribe it for them—except seeking the pleasure of Allah. Yet they did not observe it as it should be observed. So We gave those who believed among them their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse teaches that monasticism was not a divinely legislated obligation in the Gospel; it was a later human innovation. Its only sound motive could have been seeking God’s pleasure, yet sincerity of intention does not make an invented religious practice divinely ordained. The verse thus distinguishes between good intentions and legitimate revealed law: people may invent forms of devotion intending good, but if God did not prescribe them, they remain human additions that often cannot be upheld properly. At the same time, it affirms Jesus as a true prophet, the Gospel as revealed to him, and the virtues of compassion and mercy among his true followers. It also states that God rewarded those among them who truly believed, while many others deviated into disobedience and failed to observe even what they had imposed upon themselves. The passage therefore warns against religious extremism, unauthorized innovation, and claims of piety not grounded in divine revelation.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you two shares of His mercy and make for you a light by which you walk and forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This is a call to those who already have faith to deepen their God-consciousness and to place their faith in Allah's Messenger. The promised 'two shares' of mercy means a double reward: one for their earlier belief in the prophets and scriptures, and one for their belief in Muhammad. The 'light' is divine guidance that illuminates the path of life, enabling them to walk with clarity and safety, and their sins are forgiven. Thus the verse encourages steadfastness, faith, and hope in Allah's forgiving mercy.

translation: So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that the bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God's grace and favor are entirely under His sovereign control, not something any community—including the People of the Book—can bestow, withhold, or claim as an exclusive right. Divine bounty is granted freely to whom God wills, and His generosity is immense and unbounded; therefore no group can limit God's favor or boast of controlling it.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Allah has indeed heard the statement of the woman who disputes with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah. And Allah hears your conversation. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah’s hearing and knowledge are absolute: He hears every private plea, every complaint, and every dialogue, no matter how hidden or weak the speaker may seem. His names al-Sami‘ and al-Basir mean that He perceives not only words but also intentions, circumstances, and the full reality behind every dispute, so no appeal to Him is ever lost or ignored.

translation: Those among you who pronounce zihar against their wives—they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave them birth. And indeed, they utter a reprehensible word and a falsehood. And indeed, Allah is Most Pardoning, Most Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse condemns the pre-Islamic custom of zihar, in which a man would declare his wife to be like his mother, thereby treating her as permanently forbidden. It clarifies that such a statement does not create any real maternal relationship: a wife is not a mother, and true motherhood belongs only to the woman who gave birth to him. The declaration is therefore an evil and false utterance. At the same time, by ending with Allah’s pardon and forgiveness, the verse opens the door to repentance and the prescribed expiation for those who uttered this wrongfully.

translation: And those who declare zihar against their wives and then retract what they said, then they must free a slave before they touch each other. That is what you are admonished with; and Allah is Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse lays down the expiation for zihar, a pre-Islamic formula by which a husband made his wife unlawful to himself by likening her to a mahram, such as his mother. If he then retracts that declaration and intends to resume marital relations, he must free a slave before any sexual intimacy occurs. The ruling serves as a moral and legal admonition to prevent the misuse of words and to restore the marriage only through a serious act of atonement. Allah's awareness of all deeds means the requirement is not merely external but is subject to His knowledge and accountability.

translation: And whoever does not find [the means to free a slave], then fasting for two consecutive months before they touch each other. But whoever is unable, then feeding sixty poor persons. That is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger. And these are the limits of Allah. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse prescribes the expiation for the pre-Islamic practice of zihar, in which a husband unlawfully declared his wife like his mother. If he cannot free a slave, he must fast two consecutive months before resuming marital intimacy; if he cannot fast, he must feed sixty needy people. The expiation is meant to restore obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and these rulings are Allah’s fixed limits. Whoever rejects or transgresses them falls under the warning of a painful punishment for disbelievers.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger have been abased, just as those before them were abased. And We have already sent down clear verses, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who set themselves against Allah and His Messenger, rejecting or fighting the truth they brought, are struck down with disgrace and failure in the same manner as earlier nations that opposed their messengers. Since Allah has sent clear signs and evident verses, their denial is not for lack of proof but out of arrogance and stubbornness; therefore, the disbelievers are promised a punishment that will humiliate them.

translation: On the Day Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has kept account of it, while they forgot it. And Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes the certainty of resurrection and the precise accountability of every soul before Allah. No deed—whether open or hidden, remembered or forgotten—escapes Allah’s knowledge or record. People may forget their actions, but Allah has enumerated them exactly, and His being Witness over all things means His testimony is complete, final, and just. Therefore, the verse summons people to live with awareness that every action will be disclosed and recompensed, and that no secret can remain concealed from Allah.

translation: Do you not see that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? There is no private conversation of three but that He is the fourth of them, nor of five but that He is the sixth of them, nor fewer than that nor more, but that He is with them wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and His constant awareness of His creation. His being "with them" means He knows, hears, sees, and encompasses them by His knowledge and power; it does not mean He is physically present or merged with creation, for He is exalted above space and time. The mention of secret counsels of three, five, or any number serves to show that no hidden thought, whisper, or gathering is beyond His knowledge. The verse then connects this omniscience to accountability: on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will disclose to people what they did, so that every secret becomes manifest and every deed is recompensed. Thus it calls the servant to God-consciousness in private and public, knowing that Allah is always aware and that His knowledge of all things is perfect.

translation: Have you not considered those who were forbidden from private conversation and then returned to what they were forbidden, and they converse privately in sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which Allah has not greeted you, and they say among themselves, 'Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?' Sufficient for them is Hell, which they will enter; and evil is the destination.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who persist in secret whisperings after being forbidden, using them to plot sin, hostility, and rebellion against the Messenger. It exposes their hypocrisy and mockery: they approach the Prophet with a greeting God never authorized, then privately challenge God, assuming that their safety from punishment proves the falsity of the warning. The verse replies that their words and plots do not escape divine justice; Hell is sufficient for them, and it is the worst final abode. Thus, it teaches that conspiratorial secret talks for evil are forbidden, that mocking the Prophet and divine revelation is grave, and that delayed punishment is not divine approval but a respite before a severe reckoning.

translation: O you who have believed, when you converse privately, do not converse about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger, but converse about righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse teaches that even private, confidential conversation among believers must be governed by faith and moral responsibility. It forbids using secrecy or close counsel to plan, encourage, or normalize sin, wrongful aggression, or disobedience to the Messenger, because such private talk can corrupt individuals and communities while hiding evil from public view. Instead, believers are commanded to make their private counsel a means of promoting righteousness and God-consciousness—calling one another to good, justice, and obedience to divine guidance. The verse closes by directing them to fear Allah, the One to whom all will be gathered, meaning that no secret conversation is truly hidden from God and every word and intention will be subject to His judgment.

translation: Private conversation is only from Satan, so that he may grieve those who have believed, but he will not harm them at all except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: The verse teaches that secret whispering, plotting, or covert talk intended to unsettle the faithful originates in Satan’s instigation; his aim is to cause grief and anxiety. Yet such schemes have no real power to harm believers beyond what Allah permits. Therefore, the faithful should place their reliance solely on Allah, trusting His decree and protection rather than fearing the hidden plots of others.

translation: O you who have believed, when it is said to you, 'Make room' in the assemblies, then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when it is said, 'Rise up,' then rise up; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse teaches the etiquette of communal gatherings and the spiritual law of reciprocity. When believers are asked to widen space for others, they should comply willingly, and Allah will grant them spaciousness in return—both in this life and the next. When asked to rise or move to make place for those who arrive or deserve precedence, they should respond promptly. Such humility and cooperation become a cause for divine elevation: Allah raises the people of faith, and especially those endowed with knowledge, to higher ranks. The verse thus connects courteous social conduct with God's promise of honor, while reminding that Allah is fully aware of every action and intention, so no sincere deed is lost and no hypocrisy is hidden.

translation: O you who have believed, when you privately consult the Messenger, then give charity before your private consultation. That is better for you and purer. But if you do not find [the means], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes an etiquette of reverence and spiritual purification for approaching the Prophet privately: the believer is commanded to precede such private consultation with voluntary charity. The charity disciplines the soul, purifies the intention, prevents frivolous or self-serving private questioning, and provides material help to the needy. It is better because it brings reward and moral training, and purer because it cleanses the heart of improper boldness, attachment to worldly advantage, and insincere motives. If a person genuinely lacks the means, the requirement is waived, and God's forgiveness and mercy remain open to him.

translation: Are you afraid that you would not give charities before your private consultation? If you did not do so and Allah has relented toward you, then establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse gently closes the instruction about giving charity before seeking a private audience with the Prophet. It recognizes that the believers may have feared financial hardship or been unable to fulfill that specific requirement, and when they fell short, Allah turned to them in forgiveness. The temporary or situational obligation was thus eased, but the enduring duties remain: establishing prayer, giving zakah, and obeying Allah and His Messenger. The verse teaches that divine commands are tempered by mercy when human weakness is involved, yet the core of faith—worship, charity, and obedience—must still be upheld. Allah’s awareness of all deeds means that sincerity and ongoing commitment matter more than a missed occasional act.

translation: Have you not seen those who take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to falsehood while they know.
interpretation: This verse condemns hypocrites who seek the protection and friendship of a people under Allah’s wrath—often identified as the Jews of Medina—while claiming to belong to the Muslim community. In reality, they belong to neither side: not to the believers, because of their disloyalty and lies, and not to the group they ally with, because they do not truly share its faith or identity. Their deliberate swearing to falsehood shows that their deception is not a mistake but a knowing, hardened practice. The verse warns that such double-dealing, false oaths, and misplaced loyalty are signs of hypocrisy and incur Allah’s anger, and it calls for sincerity, truthfulness, and clear allegiance to the believers.

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they used to do.
interpretation: This means that because they persisted in hypocrisy, deceit, and betrayal, violating their covenants and allying themselves with God's enemies, God has readied for them a painful and severe punishment in the Hereafter. Their deeds are described as utterly evil, showing that their conduct deserves this retribution and that they have no valid excuse before God.

translation: They took their oaths as a shield, and so they turned people away from the path of Allah; therefore they will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who misuse solemn oaths as a protective cover for their hypocrisy and falsehood. By swearing deceitfully, they conceal their true intentions, evade accountability, and lend themselves an air of credibility. Yet this very deception becomes a means of blocking others from Allah’s path, as their conduct repels people from faith and misrepresents the truth. Their punishment is described as humiliating because they degraded something that should be honored—the oath sworn in Allah’s name—and used it as an instrument of obstruction and betrayal. The humiliation in the hereafter directly answers the false honor and influence they tried to secure in this life through lies.

translation: Their wealth and their children will never avail them anything against Allah. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse means that on the Day of Judgment, worldly possessions and offspring—things people often take pride in and rely upon for protection, status, or influence—will be of no benefit in shielding a person from Allah’s decree or punishment. For those who persist in disbelief, neither wealth nor children can ransom them, intercede for them, or stand in place of faith and obedience to God. Their end is the Fire, and they will remain there eternally.

translation: On the Day Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are on something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the condition of the hypocrites: on the Day of Resurrection, they will address Allah with the same false oaths and claims by which they used to deceive believers in the world, imagining that their oaths will still benefit them or that they stand upon some valid position. But their self-deception is exposed, for Allah declares that they are the liars in reality. Their falsehood is not merely an occasional act but their defining state, and no amount of swearing or imagined standing can conceal the truth from Allah.

translation: Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan—they are the losers.
interpretation: This means that when a person continually yields to Satan’s whispering and follows his path, Satan gains mastery over him and causes him to become unmindful of God, so that remembrance of Allah, obedience to Him, and awareness of His presence fade from the heart. Such a person then belongs to Satan’s faction, and allegiance to that faction brings inevitable ruin and loss, because it leads away from God’s pleasure and toward eternal deprivation.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger — those are among the most humiliated.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who actively contend against Allah and His Messenger, resisting His command and seeking to diminish His religion, are inevitably placed among the lowest and most disgraced. Their humiliation is a divine decree: no matter how much worldly power or prestige they may appear to possess, their opposition to the truth ends in defeat and shame, while Allah’s word and the faithful ultimately prevail.

translation: Allah has decreed: “I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.” Indeed, Allah is Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: This verse establishes a firm divine decree that God’s cause, carried by His messengers and those who truly follow them, will ultimately triumph over falsehood and every opposing force. The victory promised is not always immediate or worldly for each messenger individually, since prophets faced persecution, rejection, and even killing; rather, it is the final vindication of God’s message, the establishment of truth, and the success of His messengers in the overall decree of Allah. Because He is “Qawiyy” — possessing absolute strength — and “Aziz” — invincible and almighty — nothing can thwart His promise. This gives the believers certainty that despite trials, the final outcome belongs to God and His faithful servants.

translation: You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their clan. Those — He has written faith in their hearts and supported them with a spirit from Him, and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah — they are the successful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith in God and the Last Day requires a believer’s deepest loyalty, love, and allegiance to God and His Messenger to take precedence over every human tie. It does not forbid natural family affection or just kindness, but it forbids religious friendship, approval, and support for those who actively oppose God and His Messenger. When believers uphold this priority, God Himself plants faith firmly in their hearts, strengthens them with His spirit, and grants them eternal gardens and mutual pleasure with Him. Their identity becomes that of “the party of God,” and true success belongs exclusively to that party.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that tasbih—declaring Allah free of every imperfection—is the universal state of all creation. Everything in the heavens and earth, whether animate or inanimate, rational or non-rational, testifies to its Maker’s perfection, even if we do not grasp how. The names العزيز and الحكيم together mean that His might is never separate from His wisdom: He is invincible yet never unjust, powerful yet perfectly purposeful in creation, command, and decree.

translation: He is the One Who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first exile. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah. But Allah came to them from where they did not expect, and cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, O people of insight.
interpretation: This verse declares that the expulsion of the disbelievers among the People of the Book was by Allah’s decree, not merely by human planning. Their confidence in fortresses was false because no barrier can prevent Allah’s command. When His judgment came unexpectedly, He cast fear into their hearts, so they themselves helped destroy their dwellings along with the believers. The lesson for people of insight is that worldly defenses, wealth, and power cannot protect anyone from Allah; true security lies in faith, obedience, and reckoning with divine laws. It also warns against covenant-breaking and arrogance, and affirms that Allah fulfills His promise to His messengers and believers.

translation: And if Allah had not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the expulsion of the Banu Nadir, making clear that their banishment was not merely a political or military outcome but a punishment decreed by Allah. Had He not prescribed removal from their homes as their worldly penalty, He would have subjected them to a more severe punishment in this life, such as killing and captivity. Yet even that worldly punishment does not exhaust divine justice: for those who persist in disbelief, treachery, and violation of covenants, the Fire remains their final and everlasting punishment in the Hereafter. The verse thus teaches that Allah’s decrees govern the fate of nations, that worldly losses can be a lesser recompense for sin, and that the ultimate accountability is with Allah in the next life.

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah — then indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse explains that the humiliation and punishment mentioned earlier came upon them because they set themselves against Allah and His Messenger, resisting their command and authority. It then establishes a universal principle: whoever opposes Allah, breaks away from His obedience, or resists His Messenger will inevitably face Allah’s severe punishment. The description “severe in punishment” affirms that Allah’s retribution is certain, just, and utterly beyond human power to escape.

translation: Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah’s permission, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse concerns the Muslims’ actions against the property of the treacherous Banu Nadir. Their cutting or preserving of the palm trees was not outside divine decree; both were permitted by Allah and served His purpose of weakening an enemy who had broken faith and resisted the truth. The point is that such tactical measures in a legitimate conflict are sanctioned by God when they help subdue corruption and bring disgrace upon the fasiqin—those who persistently disobey Allah and violate their covenants.

translation: And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur any horse or camel for it, but Allah grants authority to His messengers over whom He wills. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the wealth Allah returned to His Messenger from the disbelievers—specifically the property of Banu al-Nadir—was not acquired through Muslim military effort, since no horses or riding mounts were driven against it; therefore it belongs to Allah and His Messenger by God's decree, not as ordinary battle spoils. It affirms that Allah alone grants His messengers dominance over whomever He wills, without needing the means of war, and that His power encompasses all things.

translation: Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns is for Allah and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin, and the orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer, so that it will not be a circulation among the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse lays down the principle that wealth and property returned to the Muslim community without fighting, namely fay', must not become a monopoly circulating only among the wealthy. Its ownership and disposal are governed by Allah and His Messenger, and it is assigned to specified recipients: Allah's cause, the Messenger, close relatives, orphans, the poor, and stranded travelers. The purpose is to prevent economic and political power from being confined to an affluent class. The verse then binds believers to accept whatever the Prophet assigns or commands and to abstain from whatever he prohibits, making obedience to prophetic authority an essential part of faith and communal justice. It closes with the command to fear Allah and a warning that Allah's punishment is severe for those who disobey, hoard wealth, or violate these divine distributive rulings.

translation: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their possessions, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure, and supporting Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful.
interpretation: This verse identifies the deserving recipients of the fay' as the impoverished Muhajirun, who were driven out of Mecca and deprived of homes and wealth solely because of their faith. Their migration was not for worldly gain; they sought God's favor and His good pleasure. They also actively supported God's religion and His Messenger. By describing them as 'the truthful,' God certifies their sincerity: their claim of faith was proven by costly action, sacrifice, and steadfastness. The verse thus establishes that true truthfulness is not mere verbal profession but is demonstrated through endurance, selflessness, and service to God's cause, and that those who sacrifice for God are honored by Him and will not lose their reward.

translation: And those who settled in the home and in faith before them love those who emigrated to them, and they find no need in their breasts for what they were given, and they prefer them over themselves even though they themselves are in need. And whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul—those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse presents the highest expression of communal faith as inward purification from shuhh, the soul's selfish greed. The Ansar's generosity was not merely material; it flowed from a heart freed from envy, resentment, and possessiveness, so they could love the Muhajirun sincerely and prefer their needs even while they themselves were in hardship. True success is therefore not measured by abundance or by what one receives, but by God's protection from the tyranny of the ego, enabling selfless love and sacrifice for others.

translation: And those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith binds later believers to earlier believers in a single community of faith. The later generation does not look down on those who came before them; rather, it prays for their forgiveness and asks God to remove from its own heart any rancor, envy, or ill will toward any believer. The prayer joins one's own need for forgiveness with the need of fellow believers, showing that salvation is sought humbly and communally, not through rivalry or resentment. By calling God Ra'uf (Kind) and Rahim (Merciful), the verse grounds this hope in God's compassion: He is the one who purifies hearts and forgives a community that turns to Him in mutual love and mercy.

translation: Have you not seen those who hypocritically profess faith? They say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Book: 'If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone concerning you; and if you are fought against, we will surely help you.' But Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the false solidarity of the hypocrites in Medina with the disbelievers among the People of the Book. They swore that if their allies were expelled, they would leave with them, and if they were attacked, they would defend them, refusing to obey anyone against them. Allah declares that their promises were lies. Their oaths were not born of sincere faith or true loyalty, but of hypocrisy, fear, and shifting worldly interests. When the test came, they did not fulfill their pledges; they either abandoned their allies or secretly worked against them. The verse teaches that God's testimony fully exposes the hidden reality behind human words. People may make strong oaths and confident promises, but when those promises are rooted in hypocrisy, they cannot be trusted. Believers are warned not to be deceived by displays of allegiance from those whose hearts are inwardly divided, and they are reminded that Allah alone knows and judges the truth of all claims.

translation: If they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought against, they will not help them; and if they help them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse exposes the emptiness of the hypocrites’ promises and the weakness of their alliances: their claimed support is mere words, abandoned at the first sign of trial. Even if they were to assist, their help would collapse into flight, and they themselves would ultimately receive no aid. It is a divine assurance that the plans of those who oppose the truth are fragile and that their mutual backing cannot avert God’s judgment.

translation: You are surely more dreaded in their breasts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse exposes a misplacement of fear in the hearts of the hypocrites and disbelievers: they fear the believers and the harm they might inflict more than they fear Allah. The reason is their lack of deep understanding. If they truly comprehended Allah’s majesty, power, and perfect control over all things, and that His punishment is the most real and severe, they would fear Him above all creation. Their failure to do so shows that their perception is limited to worldly causes and consequences, while they remain heedless of the greater reality of divine judgment.

translation: They will not fight you all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls. Their might is severe among themselves. You would think they are united, while their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse exposes the condition of the disbelievers and hypocrites who oppose the believers: they lack the courage and unity to confront the Muslims openly, so they only fight from behind fortifications or walls. Although they may appear as one bloc, their hearts are fragmented by mutual envy, hatred, and conflicting interests. Their disunity is a consequence of their rejection of truth and their failure to reason correctly. The verse teaches believers not to fear their outward numbers or alliances, because God has made their unity superficial and their resolve weak. It also shows that true unity comes from sound faith and reason, not from shared opposition to God's message.

translation: Like those who were shortly before them: they tasted the evil consequence of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that the fate of those who oppose God’s Messenger and violate their covenants is like that of earlier communities who were destroyed or disgraced not long before them. Their schemes recoiled upon themselves: they suffered the worldly penalty of their own deeds, and in the Hereafter a painful torment awaits them. It teaches that divine justice is consistent, that betrayal and arrogance bring ruin in this life and the next, and that the apparent success of the wicked is only temporary.

translation: Like the example of Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ Then when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.’
interpretation: This verse presents Satan as the archetype of every deceiver who invites others to ruin and then abandons them once they have fallen. He urges the human being toward disbelief, but when the person actually commits it and its consequences become unavoidable, Satan disowns him and claims to fear Allah. His claim is not sincere repentance or true piety; it is the despairing evasion of one who, when punishment is certain, acknowledges Allah’s lordship only to escape blame. The verse thus warns people not to follow those who call them to sin, for such callers will not share their burden or defend them before Allah. It exposes the hypocrisy of leaders and tempters who incite evil, then leave their followers to face the outcome alone, while the final recompense for both the deceiver and the deceived, if they persist, is the Fire.

translation: So the outcome for them both is that they will be in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The final end of the deceiver and the deceived is shared ruin in Hell forever, because evil influence does not bring any lasting benefit to either party. This is the just recompense of the zalimun—those who persist in wrongdoing, whether by leading others away from truth or by willingly following them in sin—and it shows that divine justice holds each accountable for choosing transgression over guidance.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul consider what it has sent forth for tomorrow. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to maintain consciousness of Allah and to hold themselves accountable by examining what deeds they have prepared for the Hereafter, referred to as “tomorrow.” The repetition of the command to fear Allah emphasizes the seriousness of this self-reckoning, and the verse closes by reminding them that Allah is fully aware of every action, so no deed—good or evil—is hidden from Him.

translation: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget their own selves. It is they who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against following the way of people who neglected God's remembrance, rights, and commands, allowing their hearts to become heedless of Him. As a just consequence, God left them to themselves and caused them to forget their own souls: their true purpose, their moral obligations, and what would benefit them in the Hereafter. Such people are the fasiqun—those who have broken out of obedience to God and deviated from the straight path.

translation: Not equal are the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise are the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse declares that the people destined for Hell and the people destined for Paradise are not equal in their state, their recompense, or their final outcome. Those who enter Paradise are the ones who have truly achieved success, for they have attained God's pleasure, eternal bliss, and deliverance from punishment, while the people of the Fire are in loss and ruin.

translation: Had We sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split apart from fear of Allah. And these examples We set forth for people, so that they may reflect.
interpretation: This verse awakens the heart to the immense majesty of the Qur’an and the greatness of the One who revealed it. If a hard, lifeless mountain were able to perceive this revelation, it would soften, submit, and crack under the awe of Allah. The human being, who is created to understand, believe, and be accountable, is therefore called to a far deeper humility, reflection, and response. The parables and signs are given not merely to inform but to shake the conscience, so that people may think seriously about their Lord, their purpose, and their need to turn to Him with fear and hope.

translation: He is Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
interpretation: This verse affirms that true divinity belongs exclusively to Allah, denying any partner, equal, or rival. His knowledge is all-encompassing: He knows what is hidden from creation and what is seen, the inward and the outward, the past, present, and future. The names al-Rahman and al-Rahim express His limitless mercy: He is the source of all mercy and the especially Merciful to those who turn to Him. The verse calls the servant to worship Him alone, to live in awe of His knowledge, and to hope in His mercy.

translation: He is Allah, there is no deity except Him: the Sovereign, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supreme. Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse declares that true divinity belongs to Allah alone, and it interprets His names as a revelation of His perfection and rule: He is the absolute Sovereign whose authority is unrestricted; the Holy, utterly free from every defect; the Source of Peace who grants tranquility and soundness; the Granter of Security who protects and safeguards; the Guardian who watches over and governs all things; the Almighty whose power is irresistible; the Compeller whose decree none can thwart; and the Supreme whose greatness is beyond all comparison. Therefore, any claim that others share in His divinity or deserve the worship, obedience, or reliance due to Him is false, because He is exalted far above every partner or likeness attributed to Him.

translation: He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner; to Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the one true God is Allah alone, whose names express perfect power, wisdom, and creativity. As al-Khaliq, He creates and determines all things; as al-Bari', He brings creation into existence without any model or helper; and as al-Musawwir, He gives every created thing its distinctive form and appearance. All beautiful and praiseworthy names belong to Him, and every being in the heavens and earth declares His transcendence and praise, whether through speech, state, or the testimony of its existence. His might is never overcome, and His wisdom governs all creation, command, and decree.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, and have driven out the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have gone forth striving in My cause and seeking My pleasure, [then do not take them as allies]. You secretly show them affection, but I know what you conceal and what you reveal. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the right path.
interpretation: This verse teaches that faith demands a loyalty that is ultimately directed to Allah and His cause, not to those who actively oppose Him and persecute the believers for their faith. Secret affection toward such enemies splits the heart’s allegiance, contradicts the sincerity of striving in Allah’s way and seeking His pleasure, and betrays the community of faith. Since Allah knows both the hidden and the open, no inward attachment can be concealed from Him. The one who chooses this path has therefore left the balanced, straight way; the true criterion for allegiance is not social or familial closeness but whether a bond strengthens or undermines faith in Allah and loyalty to His Messenger.

translation: If they gain the upper hand over you, they will be enemies to you and will stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hidden hostility of those who only appear friendly when they are weak or outnumbered: if they ever gain power over the believers, their true enmity becomes open, and they attack with both deeds and words. Their aim is not merely to harm you worldly but to turn you away from faith, so the verse warns against trusting their outward professions and urges steadfastness in belief.

translation: Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will judge between you. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse declares that on the Day of Judgment, family ties—whether blood relations or children—will be of no avail in saving anyone from Allah's judgment. People often rely on kinship or offspring for help or influence, but in the Hereafter such connections cannot substitute for faith and righteous deeds. Allah will judge and separate between people according to truth: the believers will be distinguished from those who rejected Him, even if they were closely related in this world. The verse thus warns against letting love of family lead one to compromise obedience to Allah, and it reminds that Allah sees all actions, motives, and intentions; nothing is hidden from Him, and everyone will be recompensed justly.

translation: Indeed, there has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, “We are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship besides Allah. We have rejected you, and there has arisen between us and you hostility and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone” — except for the saying of Abraham to his father, “I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have no power to do anything for you before Allah. Our Lord, upon You we rely, and to You we turn, and to You is the final destination.”
interpretation: This verse establishes Prophet Abraham and his companions as a model of pure faith: they severed themselves from their people’s idolatry and openly declared that no bond can remain with disbelief until it is abandoned for the worship of Allah alone. It teaches that true monotheism demands loyalty to God above all worldly ties, even when that brings opposition and enmity. The exception concerning Abraham’s promise to seek forgiveness for his father shows that disavowal of false belief does not necessarily erase personal compassion or the honoring of a promise, yet it also makes clear that no human being can benefit another before Allah or alter His will. The verse then ends by directing the believer’s heart to complete reliance on Allah, turning to Him in repentance, and acknowledging that all final return is to Him alone.

translation: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This is a prayer by the believers asking God not to let their weakness, suffering, or defeat become a cause of confusion and misguidance for the disbelievers, such that the disbelievers would think their unbelief is right or that God has forsaken the believers. They also ask forgiveness for their sins, since sins can bring about humiliation and trial. By calling God al-‘Aziz (the Almighty) and al-Hakim (the Wise), they affirm that He alone has power to protect and honor them, and that all His decrees are wise, even when the reason is not immediately apparent.

translation: There has already been for you in them an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away, then indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse presents the life and stance of Ibrahim and his companions as a lasting model: they held firmly to faith in Allah alone, stood apart from false worship, and endured hardship with trust in Him. The example benefits only the one whose heart truly hopes for Allah's acceptance and the meeting with Him on the Last Day, for such hope motivates imitation. If anyone instead turns away from this model, he harms only himself; Allah is in no need of anyone's obedience or allegiance, and He is praiseworthy in His essence, commands, and decrees.

translation: Perhaps Allah will place affection between you and those among them whom you have taken as enemies. And Allah is All-Powerful, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse gives the believers hope that God can transform hostility into love and reconciliation. No human heart is beyond His power to change; He can soften the hearts of those who oppose the believers, guide them to faith, or bring about peaceful relations where there was once enmity. At the same time, His forgiveness and mercy mean that past hostility and wrongdoing can be pardoned for those who turn back to Him, so believers should not despair of God’s ability to mend broken ties and bring about affection after estrangement.

translation: Allah does not forbid you from those who did not fight you concerning religion and did not drive you out of your homes, that you treat them kindly and justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who are just.
interpretation: This verse establishes that hostility in Islam is not directed at people merely because they differ in faith, but at those who actively fight or persecute Muslims. It commands believers to show kindness, generosity, and fair dealing toward peaceful non-Muslims who neither wage war against them nor expel them from their homes. The verse thus affirms that justice and benevolence are universal obligations, not restricted to fellow Muslims, and that God loves and approves those who act equitably with all people.

translation: Allah only forbids you from those who fought you on account of religion, expelled you from your homes, and aided in your expulsion—that you take them as allies. And whoever takes them as allies, those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse sets the boundary for the kindness and justice enjoined toward peaceful non-Muslims: it forbids loyalty and alliance only with those who actively waged hostility against the believers because of their faith, drove them from their homes, and conspired in their expulsion. Such enmity is not merely a difference of belief but aggressive persecution, and showing them allegiance means siding with oppression against faith and community. Whoever does so wrongs himself and violates God's command, for loyalty belongs to God and to the believers in truth and justice.

translation: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah is most knowing of their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them. And give them what they spent. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their due compensation. And do not hold to marriage bonds with disbelieving women. And ask for what you spent, and let them ask for what they spent. That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that faith, not former marital or social ties, is the decisive bond among people. When a woman leaves a land of disbelief and comes to the Muslims as a believer, her claim of faith must be examined to protect the community from deception and to preserve the integrity of marriage and guardianship. Since Allah alone truly knows the heart, the examination is only a means of establishing what is outwardly apparent. If her faith is confirmed, she is not to be returned to a disbelieving husband, because a marriage between a believing woman and a disbelieving man cannot continue; the two are no longer lawful for one another. At the same time, the verse insists on financial justice: the disbelieving husband is to be compensated for what he spent, and Muslim men who lose disbelieving wives are likewise to seek what they spent. Muslim men are permitted to marry such believing emigrant women after giving them their bridal due, but they are forbidden to cling to marriages with disbelieving women. Thus the ruling separates loyalty to faith from contractual and financial claims, resolving them with justice rather than vengeance. It is Allah's wise judgment, ordaining that allegiance to Him takes precedence while rights are still settled fairly.

translation: And if any of your wives have escaped to the disbelievers, and you then retaliate or gain compensation, give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the financial justice owed to Muslim husbands whose wives apostatize and leave them for the disbelievers, taking with them the dowers or wealth the husbands had spent. When the Muslim community later obtains compensation or spoils from the disbelievers, those husbands whose wives have gone over are to be reimbursed from that wealth an amount equal to what they had spent. The verse thus restores fair compensation rather than leaving individual believers to bear the loss alone. It closes by commanding taqwa of Allah, the One in whom they believe, grounding the ruling in faith and obedience to divine justice.

translation: O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor kill their children, nor utter a slander they invent between their hands and their feet, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge and ask Allah to forgive them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse sets the terms of the women's covenant of faith, making clear that allegiance to the Prophet is not a mere verbal act but a commitment to pure monotheism and a transformed moral life. The prohibitions cover the gravest social and familial sins: associating partners with God, violating property, chastity, the sanctity of life, and the integrity of lineage and reputation. The phrase about inventing a slander 'between their hands and feet' refers to false claims about pregnancy, parentage, or sexual misconduct—crimes that harm families and the community. Obedience to the Prophet 'in what is right' means in all that is good and lawful, not in sin or disobedience to God. The Prophet's duty to accept the pledge and seek forgiveness for them shows that the door of repentance and divine mercy remains open; Allah's forgiveness and mercy are the ultimate goal and support of this moral covenant.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry, who have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired concerning the inhabitants of the graves.
interpretation: This verse forbids believers from taking as intimate allies or protectors those whose disbelief and enmity have brought Allah’s wrath upon them. Since such people have no hope in the Hereafter, their condition is like that of the disbelievers who deny that the dead in their graves will ever be resurrected. Loyalty and support must therefore be reserved for Allah and His believing servants, not for those who reject the final life and oppose His religion.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse declares that every created thing in the heavens and earth—whether animate or inanimate, willingly or by its very existence—testifies to Allah's perfection, transcendence, and freedom from every imperfection. This universal glorification shows that His lordship and sovereignty are recognized throughout creation. The closing names Al-Aziz and Al-Hakim establish that His power is never separated from His wisdom: He is invincible in might and perfect in ordering all things, so His commands, decrees, and laws are wise and just. Therefore He alone is worthy of worship, gratitude, and submission.

translation: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?
interpretation: This verse is a divine reproach against inconsistency between profession and practice. It condemns the believer who claims, promises, or commands something but then fails to act accordingly, especially in matters of faith, obedience to Allah, and fulfilling one’s word. It teaches that true faith demands integrity: speech must be truthful and must be matched by action, and one should not boast of doing good or make commitments that one does not sincerely intend or actually carry out.

translation: Greatly hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do.
interpretation: This means that Allah strongly condemns hypocrisy and inconsistency between words and deeds. It is a severe offense to claim faith, make promises, or speak of righteousness while failing to act accordingly; sincerity requires that one’s speech be truthful and matched by obedient action.

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as though they are a solid structure.
interpretation: This means that God loves those who strive in His path with unity, discipline, and steadfastness, standing together in ordered ranks like a tightly joined structure that cannot easily be broken. It praises collective strength, solidarity, and firm resolve in the service of God, where individuals support one another and remain unshaken, rather than acting in disunity or fragmentation.

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, why do you harm me while you know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you?" But when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse recounts Moses rebuking his people for knowingly opposing and hurting him despite their certainty that he was Allah’s messenger. Their persistent deviation from truth and obedience was not merely a failure toward Moses; it became a cause of Allah turning their hearts away from guidance as a just consequence. It teaches that guidance is a favor from Allah, and when people deliberately choose corruption and reject His messengers, He leaves their hearts to stray. Thus, Allah does not guide those who persistently rebel against Him and depart from His command.
