translation: And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, ‘O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah, and bringing good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad.’ But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, ‘This is clear magic.’
interpretation: This verse establishes that Jesus, son of Mary, was a true messenger sent specifically to the Children of Israel. He did not abolish the Torah but confirmed and authenticated it, and he announced the coming of another messenger after him named Ahmad—understood in Islamic interpretation as the Prophet Muhammad, whose name Ahmad means “praiseworthy.” The verse thus teaches the continuity of divine guidance: Jesus prepared his people to accept the final messenger who would come with unmistakable signs. Yet when that promised messenger came with clear evidences, the rejecters dismissed him with the charge of sorcery, showing that their denial was not due to lack of proof but to stubborn rejection of the truth.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah while he is being invited to Islam? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse condemns the extreme injustice of knowingly attributing falsehood to God—such as denying His oneness, rejecting His messengers, or distorting His revelation—especially when the person is simultaneously being called to Islam, that is, to sincere submission and monotheistic faith. Such a person has no valid excuse, because the invitation to truth has reached him, yet he persists in inventing lies about God and opposing His guidance. The statement that God does not guide the wrongdoing people means that those who deliberately choose falsehood and injustice cut themselves off from divine guidance; their persistent oppression of the truth prevents them from receiving the light of faith, so God leaves them in their chosen deviation.

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This means that the enemies of truth may try to erase, distort, or silence Allah’s guidance through mere speech, false claims, and rejection, but their efforts cannot succeed. Allah’s light—His revelation, guidance, and the truth He has sent—will inevitably prevail, be completed, and shine forth, regardless of how much those who reject faith resent it.

translation: He is the One Who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah alone is the sovereign sender of the Prophet Muhammad with true guidance and the divinely revealed way of life, and that He has guaranteed the ultimate elevation and victory of this truth over every false religion and man-made ideology, regardless of the resentment and resistance of those who associate partners with Him.

translation: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?
interpretation: This verse is a divine invitation addressed to the believers, using the imagery of trade to awaken their deepest concern: true profit and ultimate loss. The “transaction” it offers is not worldly commerce but the exchange of one’s wealth and life for the pleasure of Allah, an exchange whose gain is deliverance from a punishment that is agonizing and eternal. It teaches that faith becomes salvific when it is lived as a deliberate covenant: the believer invests what is most precious—self and possessions—in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and receives in return protection from ruin and the promise of an unfailing reward. Thus the verse calls the believer to evaluate every pursuit by its final outcome, recognizing that no worldly bargain can compare with the bargain of faith, sacrifice, and steadfast striving in the path of Allah.

translation: You believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse sets forth the true bargain that delivers one from painful punishment: inward faith in Allah and His Messenger joined to outward striving in His path with both wealth and life. Faith here is not a passive declaration but a living commitment that proves itself through sacrifice—spending one’s resources in obedience to God and exposing oneself to hardship for His sake. Such striving includes every effort to uphold truth, defend the weak, resist evil, and purify the soul from selfishness and sin. Allah declares this path “better” because it secures eternal success and divine pleasure, which infinitely outweigh any fleeting worldly advantage. The closing words, “if you only knew,” summon the reader to weigh matters by the measure of true, lasting profit rather than by immediate comfort, for only those who understand the reality of this life and the Hereafter will recognize that giving up wealth and self in God’s cause is not loss but the greatest gain.

translation: He will forgive you your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse conveys God’s promise of a twofold reward for those who believe and strive in His way: first, the removal of sins through forgiveness, which purifies the soul from the consequences of disobedience; second, entry into eternal gardens where rivers flow beneath palaces and trees, symbolizing unending sustenance, delight, and life. The 'pleasant dwellings' in 'gardens of Eden' indicate not only physical comfort but also permanence, security, and nearness to God, free from any defilement or fatigue. The phrase 'That is the great attainment' declares that this outcome—divine forgiveness and everlasting bliss—is the ultimate success, surpassing every worldly gain and worthy of every sacrifice.

translation: And another [favor] that you love: help from Allah and an imminent victory. And give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse promises the believers, in addition to forgiveness and the gardens of eternal bliss, a beloved worldly favor: divine assistance and a conquest that is near. It teaches that true victory comes from Allah alone, not from numbers or material strength, and that He may grant relief and triumph soon after sincere faith and striving. The command to give glad tidings to the believers is a mercy and encouragement, strengthening their hearts to remain steadfast with the assurance that Allah’s help is real and close.

translation: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, 'Who are my supporters for Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are supporters of Allah.' And a faction of the Children of Israel believed and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: This verse calls the believers to devote themselves fully to God’s cause and to support His religion and Messenger with the same sincerity shown by Jesus’ disciples. Jesus’ question was not asking for help for God—who is beyond any need—but inviting them to join him in God’s way. The disciples’ response, “We are supporters of Allah,” expresses complete commitment to that mission. The verse then notes that among the Children of Israel, some accepted the call and some rejected it, so God strengthened and granted victory to the faithful over their adversaries. The lesson is that those who sincerely uphold faith and struggle in God’s cause may face opposition, but God’s help is with them, and He will make them prevail.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, the Sovereign, the Most Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse means that every created thing in the heavens and the earth—whether animate or inanimate, visible or hidden—continuously declares Allah's transcendence and praise, each in the manner suited to its nature. Their very existence, order, and submission to His laws are a form of glorification. The verse then names Allah with attributes that are the foundation of that praise: He is al-Malik, the absolute Sovereign whose dominion admits no partner; al-Quddus, the Holy, utterly free from every imperfection, deficiency, and anthropomorphic limitation; al-Aziz, the Almighty, whose power none can repel; and al-Hakim, the All-Wise, whose creation, commands, and decrees are perfectly ordered. Thus the verse calls the rational creature to join this universal glorification consciously—by tawhid, worship, obedience, and purification of the heart—and to recognize that no being deserves ultimate praise, fear, or reliance except the One who is at once King, Holy, Mighty, and Wise.

translation: He is the One who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although before they were clearly in error.
interpretation: This verse describes prophethood as a direct act of divine mercy and guidance. God did not leave the unlettered people in their inherited ignorance; He raised from their own midst a messenger they could recognize and trust, so that guidance would be accessible rather than foreign. The messenger’s mission has four intertwined purposes: reciting God’s revelations, purifying hearts and conduct, teaching the revealed Book, and imparting wisdom—meaning the deeper understanding and right application of revelation. Their previous state of clear misguidance is mentioned not to shame them ultimately, but to magnify the greatness of the transformation and to show that true reform comes from God’s chosen guidance, not from human sophistication or inherited status.

translation: And [also] others among them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Prophet Muhammad’s mission is not confined to the Arabs of his immediate time, but extends to later peoples and future generations who had not yet joined the first believers. They too are included in the same prophetic call and will share in its blessings. God, being the Almighty and the All-Wise, has decreed this universal reach according to His perfect power and wisdom, showing that His selection of the Prophet and the scope of his message transcend ethnic and temporal boundaries.

translation: That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse declares that the guidance, prophethood, and faith mentioned are not earned by human merit or lineage but are a pure gift from Allah, granted according to His wisdom to whom He chooses. It also affirms that Allah's generosity is vast and inexhaustible, so believers should hope in His grace and respond with gratitude and humble obedience.

translation: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it out is like the donkey carrying books. How wretched is the example of the people who denied the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse likens those who were given the Torah but failed to fulfill its obligations, live by its guidance, or recognize its true intent to a donkey carrying scrolls: it bears the weight of knowledge but has no understanding of what it carries. Thus, religious knowledge that is not acted upon becomes a burden rather than a means of honor or salvation. The verse then condemns those who reject Allah’s signs, meaning that willful denial and injustice cause a person to be deprived of divine guidance, for Allah does not guide those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: Say, 'O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the claim of exclusive closeness to God and chosen status. If someone truly believes they are God’s specially beloved allies and that the next life holds honor and reward for them alone, then death should be something they eagerly desire, because it would bring them to that promised favor. The command to “wish for death” is not an encouragement to self-destruction; it is a test of sincerity. A genuine claim to divine friendship and certainty of reward would make the transition to the Hereafter desirable rather than dreaded. Their refusal to wish for death exposes that their assertion is not based on true conviction but on inherited presumption and worldly attachment. True closeness to God is not a monopoly claimed by any group; it is earned through faith, obedience, and sincerity, and it produces longing for God’s meeting, not fear of it.

translation: And they will never wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have sent ahead; and Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Their refusal to call for death is itself a proof against their claim, for if they truly believed they had exclusive nearness to Allah and a guaranteed good end, they would eagerly seek death to reach that reward. They avoid it because their own deeds have stored up for them a reckoning they fear, and because their consciences testify to their rejection and wrongdoing. Allah’s knowledge of the unjust is complete, so their hidden motives and deeds are fully known, and His judgment of them will be perfectly just.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse confronts the human illusion that death can be avoided or postponed by fleeing from its remembrance. It teaches that death is an appointed meeting no one can escape, and that worldly fear or denial cannot alter that reality. After death, every soul returns to God, who knows both what is hidden and what is visible; nothing in human intention, secret thought, or outward action is beyond His knowledge. Therefore, the verse awakens accountability: life is not ended by death but leads to a reckoning in which God discloses the true nature and consequence of one’s deeds, urging readiness, sincerity, and responsibility before that inevitable return.

translation: O you who have believed, when the call to prayer is made on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers that once the Friday prayer is announced, they must stop worldly business and go to the mosque to attend the sermon and prayer. The 'remembrance of Allah' here refers to the Friday khutbah and salah, and 'leave off trade' means abandoning all buying, selling, and distracting worldly activity after the call. The verse teaches that responding to Allah's call and prioritizing His worship is far better and more rewarding than any material gain, if people truly understood the lasting value of obedience over temporary profit.

translation: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah much, so that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse teaches that after fulfilling the congregational prayer—especially the Friday prayer—believers are not to remain idle in the mosque but are to go about their lawful worldly affairs, earn a living, and seek Allah’s provision. At the same time, worldly activity must not distract them from God; they are to remember Allah frequently with heart, tongue, and conduct. True success in both this life and the Hereafter comes from balancing worship, lawful effort, and constant remembrance of Allah.

translation: And when they see a trade or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. Say, “What is with Allah is better than amusement and trade, and Allah is the best of providers.”
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who abandoned the Prophet while he was standing and delivering the Friday sermon as soon as a caravan or worldly diversion appeared. It shows how easily worldly gain and entertainment can distract people from obedience and prophetic guidance. The verse directs believers to judge by what is with Allah: His reward, provision, and pleasure are better than any temporary trade or amusement. Since Allah is the best of providers, seeking His bounty must not come at the cost of neglecting worship, the sermon, and the Prophet’s presence.

translation: When the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.' But Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are truly liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes hypocrisy as a contradiction between outward speech and inward reality. The hypocrites' testimony is not a sincere confession of faith but a false verbal claim; they say with their tongues what their hearts do not accept. Allah's own witness settles the matter: the Prophet is truly His Messenger, while their pretended testimony is a lie because it does not proceed from belief. The verse teaches that faith is not validated by mere words or public declarations; it must be sincere and rooted in the heart.

translation: They have taken their oaths as a shield, so they have turned [people] away from the path of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they used to do.
interpretation: The hypocrites misuse oaths and pledges as a protective cover, not out of sincerity but to hide their disbelief and safeguard their interests. Through this deception they block others from Allah’s religion and discourage them from following His path. Their actions are profoundly evil because they corrupt both themselves and the community, using false solemnity to oppose the truth.

translation: That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and so they do not understand.
interpretation: This means their repeated turning away from faith after having entered it caused a spiritual barrier to settle over their hearts, so the light of guidance could no longer penetrate them; their failure to understand is not due to a lack of information but because their inner faculty of discernment was corrupted by their own hypocrisy and rejection.

translation: And when you see them, their bodies impress you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech. They are like blocks of wood propped up. They think every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded!
interpretation: This verse exposes the inner reality of the hypocrites: they may have attractive appearances and persuasive speech, but their hearts are empty of faith, sincerity, and courage. Their likeness to propped-up timber indicates that they are hollow, lifeless, and dependent on outward support, not rooted in truth. Their constant fear that every cry or disturbance is directed against them reveals a guilty conscience, cowardice, and instability. Though they may live among the believers and appear friendly, they are in fact dangerous enemies to the community, so believers are warned to be cautious of them. Their ultimate condition is one of delusion: despite clear signs and warnings, they remain turned away from the truth, deserving of Allah's punishment.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come, the Messenger of Allah will seek forgiveness for you,' they turn their heads away, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant.
interpretation: This exposes the hypocrisy of those who refuse the Prophet’s prayer for forgiveness out of pride, not ignorance. Their turning away is a deliberate rejection of prophetic guidance and of the means Allah has appointed for seeking mercy. It shows that arrogance hardens the heart against repentance: even when forgiveness is offered through the Prophet, they mock and withdraw. The verse teaches that divine pardon benefits only those who approach it with humility, and that no intercession can force itself upon a soul determined to remain proud and resistant to truth.

translation: It is the same to them whether you seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse declares that the hypocrites’ rejection has become so deeply settled that the Prophet’s seeking forgiveness for them would make no difference. Their being unforgiven is not due to any limitation in prophetic intercession, but because they themselves persist in corruption, hypocrisy, and disobedience. Allah in His justice withholds guidance from those who knowingly and willfully abandon obedience to Him; their hearts remain closed because they chose rejection. Forgiveness and guidance are therefore tied to sincere turning to God, which they have refused.

translation: They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse.' But to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, yet the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: The hypocrites tried to use withholding financial support as a weapon to break the Prophet's community, assuming that if they stopped helping the believers, those believers would scatter and abandon him. The verse exposes their plot and declares that all provision and resources belong to Allah alone; He can sustain His Messenger and the faithful without them. Their failure to grasp this shows their hypocrisy and spiritual blindness: they judge by material control, while God controls the treasures of the heavens and earth.

translation: They say, 'If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the weaker from it.' But to Allah belongs all might, and to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: The hypocrites falsely imagine that worldly power, wealth, and tribal standing make them the ‘mightier’ who can drive out the Prophet and the believers as the ‘weaker.’ The verse declares that true honor, strength, and dignity belong solely to Allah, then to His Messenger and the believers through faith, obedience, and divine support—not to those who boast in hypocrisy and disbelief. The hypocrites’ claim is therefore empty, and their failure to recognize this shows their ignorance of the real source of power.

translation: O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that — then those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse warns believers that love of wealth and children must not distract them from remembering Allah, which includes prayer, reciting the Qur'an, obeying His commands, and keeping Him present in one's life. Whoever allows worldly attachments to take precedence over this remembrance loses the greater good in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you, and he says, “My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short while, so I would give charity and be among the righteous.”
interpretation: This verse commands believers to use the provision God has given them in charitable giving and righteous action while they still possess life and capacity. Death’s appointed time is fixed, and when it arrives, the request for a delay to give charity and join the righteous is not granted. Therefore, the opportunity to spend in God’s way and to perform good deeds exists only in this worldly life, and neglecting it produces a regret that can no longer be remedied.

translation: And Allah will never delay a soul when its appointed term has come; and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This means that the fixed time of every person’s death is absolutely decreed and cannot be postponed when it arrives; no one can add even a moment to their life, nor avoid the meeting with Allah. Since Allah is fully aware of every deed, word, and intention, the verse urges people to use their remaining time in obedience and repentance before that appointed hour comes, for accountability is certain and nothing is hidden from Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. To Him belongs sovereignty, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: Every created thing in the heavens and the earth bears witness to Allah's perfection and freedom from any deficiency, and this witness means that absolute dominion and all praise belong to Him alone. His power is unbounded, so He alone creates, sustains, governs, and determines every affair; nothing can resist Him or share in His authority, and therefore all gratitude and worship are due to Him.

translation: He is the One Who created you; then among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone created all humankind, yet unbelief and belief arise from the choices people make within the life He granted them. It teaches that human beings are not coerced into either path, but are tested by how they respond to truth, and that Allah sees every outward action and inward intention. Therefore, no deed, whether of rejection or faith, is hidden from Him, and every person will meet the consequence of what he or she has chosen and done.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and He formed you and made your forms excellent; and to Him is the final destination.
interpretation: Allah’s creation is grounded in truth and wisdom, not in vanity or randomness. His formation of human beings is an act of deliberate care, beauty, and generosity, so the human form is a sign of His kindness and a reason for gratitude and humility. But the excellence of that form is not an end in itself: the ultimate return is to Him, meaning that human beings are accountable to their Creator and that all matters ultimately resolve in His judgment and presence.

translation: He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you declare. And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse establishes that God’s knowledge is all-encompassing: it extends over the entire creation and penetrates the innermost dimensions of the human self. It means that no secret thought, hidden motive, private intention, or outward action is beyond His awareness. Therefore, a person cannot conceal anything from Him, and true religion is not limited to outward performance; it demands sincerity, inward God-consciousness, and purity of heart, because He knows and will judge what lies within the breasts.

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns people by recalling the fate of earlier communities that rejected faith and opposed God's messengers. They suffered the disastrous results of their disbelief and evil deeds in this world, and they will also face a painful punishment in the Hereafter. It is a call to take heed before it is too late, because denying the truth leads to loss and torment.

translation: That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they said, 'Are human beings to guide us?' So they disbelieved and turned away; and Allah was Self-Sufficient. And Allah is Free of Need, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse exposes the root of the earlier nations' rejection: clear proofs had reached them through their own messengers, yet they arrogantly refused guidance because it came through human beings like themselves. Their objection was not based on lack of evidence but on pride, so they disbelieved and turned away. Their rejection did not diminish Allah in any way, for He is absolutely Self-Sufficient and Free of Need; He gains nothing from belief and loses nothing from disbelief. He is Praiseworthy in His essence, worthy of all praise whether or not creation acknowledges Him. The verse thus warns that rejecting truth merely because the messenger is human is a grave form of unbelief, and it affirms that Allah's majesty, sufficiency, and praise are entirely independent of His creatures' response.

translation: Those who disbelieved claimed that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah."
interpretation: This verse establishes that resurrection after death is an absolute reality that no denial can alter. It calls the disbelievers’ claim false and swears by Allah’s lordship that they will indeed be raised, then brought to account for every deed. The final statement emphasizes that creating, restoring, and judging all creatures is effortless for Allah, so the promise of resurrection and recompense is certain and cannot be beyond His power.

translation: So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse commands people to have faith in Allah, in His Messenger, and in the Light He sent down, which is the Qur’an. Faith here is not merely an inward claim; it means accepting Allah’s revelation as guidance and living in accordance with it. The Qur’an is called Light because it removes the darkness of ignorance, doubt, and misguidance and shows the straight path. The verse closes by reminding that Allah is fully aware of every deed, so belief must be sincere and reflected in action, since nothing done openly or secretly is hidden from Him.

translation: The Day He will gather you for the Day of Gathering — that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great success.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection as the Day of Gathering, when Allah will assemble all creation — the first and the last — for reckoning. It is called the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain because the true outcomes of people’s choices become manifest: those who pursued faith and obedience gain eternal bliss, while those who rejected or neglected it suffer irreplaceable loss, and some will discover that their apparent gains in worldly life were actually losses. The verse then specifies the path to salvation: sincere faith in Allah joined with righteous action. Such faith is not mere assent; it produces deeds that conform to Allah’s command. For such people, Allah promises to erase their sins — not because sins are inconsequential, but because His mercy and forgiveness cover them — and to admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, a symbol of continuous provision, delight, and life. Their stay is eternal, without interruption or end. The final phrase, “That is the great success,” identifies this as the ultimate achievement: deliverance from punishment and the attainment of everlasting nearness to Allah in Paradise. It teaches that worldly loss and gain are temporary, while the gathering on that Day reveals who has truly profited and who has truly lost.

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein; and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse means that those who reject faith and deliberately deny Allah’s revealed signs and evidences are the people of Hell; they will remain there forever, and that is the worst and most terrible end.

translation: No misfortune strikes except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah, He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This means that no calamity, loss, or hardship reaches a person outside Allah’s decree and permission. When a person truly believes that all things unfold under Allah’s will, and receives misfortune with faith, patience, and submission rather than panic or resentment, Allah grants his heart firmness, tranquility, certainty, and the ability to see the trial as a means of drawing nearer to Him and receiving reward. Allah’s knowledge encompasses every heart, every affliction, and every consequence, so nothing is hidden from Him and nothing He decrees is without wisdom.

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance.
interpretation: Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is an obligation, and the Messenger’s duty is only to deliver Allah’s message clearly. If people reject it, the Prophet is not responsible for forcing them to believe; their accountability is with Allah, while the Prophet has fulfilled his role of plain warning and communication.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse establishes that divinity, worship, and ultimate authority belong exclusively to Allah, and it teaches that genuine faith requires tawakkul—placing one’s trust, reliance, and affairs entirely in Allah’s hands. Because He alone is the sole God, believers must direct their dependence to Him alone, confident in His wisdom, power, and sufficiency, while still fulfilling their responsibilities and means.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse warns believers that some of their closest family members—spouses and children—may become a source of harm by turning them away from God, encouraging disobedience, or prioritizing worldly ties over faith and righteousness. The warning is not to treat family with hostility, but to be cautious against being misled by affection into compromising one’s duty to God. Then it urges a generous response: if they wrong you or fall short, pardon them, overlook their faults, and forgive. This reflects that mercy and forgiveness among family are beloved to God, and that God Himself is Forgiving and Merciful toward those who forgive others.

translation: Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that wealth and children, though they may be blessings, are a means of testing a person: they can distract from obedience to God, lead one to prioritize worldly attachments over divine commands, or become an excuse for wrongdoing. The verse directs the believer not to let these temporary attachments dominate the heart, and to seek instead the far greater and everlasting reward that is with Allah.

translation: So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen and obey, and spend; it is good for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul — then those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God-consciousness is measured by sincere effort within one’s capacity, not by impossible perfection. Believers are called to listen to revelation with acceptance and to obey God and His Messenger in practice. That obedience is then joined to generosity: giving from what God has provided is not a loss but a benefit to the giver, because it purifies the soul, strengthens faith, and stores reward with God. The verse identifies true success as being saved from shuhh — the inward miserliness and selfish greed that makes a person withhold good, resent others, and worship possessions. Whoever God protects from that spiritual disease attains real flourishing in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: If you lend Allah a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse urges spending in Allah’s cause as though it were a loan to Him—not because He needs anything, but to express that whatever is given for His sake is never lost. A “good loan” is one given sincerely for His pleasure, from lawful wealth, without expecting human return and without later reminding the recipient or harming them. Allah promises to multiply the reward far beyond the original gift and, even more, to forgive sins. His name Shakuur means He recognizes and abundantly rewards even small sincere deeds; His name Haleem means He is forbearing, not quick to punish, giving people time to repent and return to Him.

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This means that Allah alone encompasses all knowledge: He knows the hidden realities beyond human perception and the visible realities that are witnessed, including secrets of the hearts and outward deeds. His being al-Aziz affirms that He is invincible, all-dominant, and unopposed in His power, while al-Hakim affirms that His knowledge, decrees, and actions are perfectly wise, purposeful, and free from any flaw or injustice.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period, and count the waiting period precisely. And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their homes, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has surely wronged his own soul. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a matter.
interpretation: This verse lays down the foundational Qur'anic law of divorce as an act that must be governed by taqwa and carried out within the framework of the 'iddah, the waiting period. The plural address, 'when you divorce,' speaks to the Muslim community through the Prophet, showing that the ruling is universal. Divorcing 'for their waiting period' means the pronouncement should occur at a time when the waiting period can be properly counted—normally during a woman's state of purity, not during menstruation—so that the decision is deliberate and not a rash act of anger. The command to count the 'iddah precisely protects rights related to lineage, maintenance, and the possibility of return. The prohibition against expelling the woman from her home, or her leaving it, safeguards her dignity and security during this vulnerable time; only a clear act of gross indecency removes this protection. The verse then declares these rulings to be Allah's limits, warning that transgressing them wrongs the transgressor himself. The final statement—'perhaps Allah will bring about after that a matter'—reveals the wisdom of the waiting period: it gives space for regret, reconciliation, or a new divine decree, so that a hasty divorce does not close the door on what God may mend.

translation: So when they have reached their term, then retain them in a good manner or part with them in a good manner, and call to witness two just persons from among you, and establish the testimony for Allah. That is an admonition for whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah — He will make for him a way out.
interpretation: This verse addresses the husband at the end of a divorced woman’s waiting period. At that decisive moment, he must either take her back honorably, with her rights fulfilled and without harm or coercion, or finalize the separation honorably. The command to bring two just witnesses and to give testimony for Allah’s sake shows that marital rights and separation are not private matters to be manipulated, but acts of justice and accountability before God. The verse is an admonition for those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, reminding them that God-consciousness in these dealings is tied to faith and accountability. Its closing promise means that whoever observes taqwa by fulfilling these commands and avoiding injustice will find a way out of difficulty and constriction.

translation: And He will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever places his trust in Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah accomplishes His purpose. Allah has certainly appointed a measure for everything.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true reliance on God is not passive fatalism but a confident turning of the heart to Him: when a person does what is right and trusts God with the outcome, God opens ways of provision and help that the person could never have planned or foreseen. Divine sufficiency is not limited by apparent causes; God's decree inevitably comes to pass, and since He has set a precise measure and timing for every matter, the believer should neither despair in hardship nor become arrogant in ease, but remain steadfast, patient, and assured that God's wisdom will unfold exactly as He wills.

translation: And those among your women who have despaired of menstruation—if you are in doubt—their waiting period is three months, and [also] those who have not yet menstruated. And those who are pregnant, their term is that they give birth. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair.
interpretation: This verse specifies the waiting period for women whose term cannot be measured by menstrual cycles. A woman who no longer expects menstruation due to menopause, and a woman who has not yet menstruated, observes a waiting period of three months when there is uncertainty about her case. A pregnant woman’s waiting period ends when she gives birth. The verse then lays down a general principle: God-consciousness and obedience to God’s commands bring relief and make a person’s affairs easier.

translation: That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah—He will remove from him his misdeeds and make great for him his reward.
interpretation: This verse declares that the rulings just mentioned are not human opinions but Allah’s revealed command, and it attaches to them a profound promise: conscious reverence of Allah (taqwa), expressed by obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, becomes a means of forgiveness and immense reward. It teaches that piety does not merely earn reward in the Hereafter; it also wipes away sins and magnifies the value of good deeds, showing that Allah’s grace responds to the believer’s God-consciousness with purification and generous recompense.

translation: Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means, and do not harm them so as to constrain them. And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. Then if they breastfeed for you, give them their wages, and consult together in a good manner. But if you disagree, then let another woman breastfeed for him.
interpretation: This verse establishes the rights of divorced women during the waiting period, especially regarding housing and financial support. The husband must provide accommodation from what he can afford, without using it as a means of harming or pressuring her. If she is pregnant, her maintenance continues until she gives birth. If she nurses the child after birth, she is entitled to fair compensation, and the parents must decide the child’s welfare through kind mutual consultation. If they cannot agree, the father may arrange another wet nurse, so that the child’s needs are met without coercion or injustice. The verse thus protects the dignity of divorced women, enforces responsible fatherhood, and prioritizes the well-being of the child.

translation: Let the one of ample means spend from his ample means, and let the one whose provision has been restricted spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden a soul with more than what He has given it. Allah will bring about ease after hardship.
interpretation: This verse establishes that financial and moral obligations are measured by capacity. A person with wealth must give according to wealth, while one of limited means gives only from what Allah has provided; no one is required to spend beyond ability. It reveals Allah's justice and mercy: His commands never exceed the strength or resources He has granted. The closing promise teaches that tight circumstances are not permanent, and that patient, responsible obedience will be followed by relief.

translation: And how many a town defied the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to account with a severe reckoning and punished it with a terrible punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that communities which transgressed against God’s command and rejected His messengers were not overlooked. God subjected them to a strict, exacting reckoning and a punishment that was severe and shocking, unlike ordinary suffering. The phrase “how many a town” shows this was a recurring pattern, not an isolated event. It teaches that defiance of divine authority, especially after messengers have conveyed the truth, brings inevitable consequences in this life and the Hereafter. It also reassures the faithful that God’s justice is never negligent and calls every person and society to heed His commands before the reckoning comes.

translation: So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss.
interpretation: This describes the fate of a people who persisted in rejecting God's commands and messengers: their wrongdoing returned to them as punishment, and their final end was utter ruin, having forfeited every good and gained nothing but loss.

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O people of understanding who have believed. Allah has indeed sent down to you a Reminder.
interpretation: This verse links the fate of the rebellious to a direct admonition for the believers: the severe punishment is a warning meant to awaken taqwa in those who possess sound understanding. The phrase “people of understanding” is directed specifically at the believers, showing that true intellect is not mere cleverness but the capacity to recognize God’s authority, take His warnings seriously, and respond with obedience. The “Reminder” sent down is the revelation—the Qur’an—which keeps divine guidance, warning, and accountability present within the community. Thus the verse teaches that both God’s punishment and His revelation call people to vigilant God-consciousness: the punishment warns against heedlessness, while the sent-down Reminder supplies the means of guidance. The fitting response of a believing mind is not complacency but reverence, attentiveness, and steadfast adherence to what God has revealed.

translation: A Messenger reciting to you the verses of Allah, clear and distinct, to bring those who believe and do righteous deeds out of darkness into light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly made for him an excellent provision.
interpretation: This verse shows that Allah’s guidance reaches people through a Messenger who recites His clear signs, and the purpose of those signs is to rescue the believing and righteous from the darknesses of ignorance, misguidance, and sin into the light of faith, knowledge, and obedience. It then binds the promise of eternal gardens to two inseparable realities: sincere faith in Allah and righteous action. The final statement that Allah has made an excellent provision for such a person means that this reward is not merely a bare return for deeds, but a generous, perfectly ordered, and everlasting sustenance from Allah’s grace.

translation: Allah is the One who created seven heavens, and of the earth the like thereof. The command descends between them, so that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the vastness of creation—seven heavens and earths like them—and the continuous descent of Allah’s command through all levels of existence are signs meant to awaken certainty in His limitless power and all-encompassing knowledge. It means that Allah alone originates, sustains, and governs every realm; nothing is beyond His ability or outside His awareness. Therefore, the human response is faith, humility, and reliance upon Him, knowing that His decree is wise and His knowledge covers every secret and every consequence.

translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a gentle divine reproach to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for declaring something lawful to be unlawful upon himself in order to satisfy his wives. It teaches that the authority to make things lawful or unlawful belongs to Allah alone, and that no person—even a prophet—may turn a permissible matter into a religious prohibition merely to please others or avoid domestic displeasure. The Prophet's action was not a sin of deliberate disobedience, but an error of judgment in a personal matter, and Allah's closing names “Forgiving and Merciful” show that He pardoned it and did not hold him accountable as a lawgiver. The verse thus affirms the Prophet's humanity, the supremacy of divine law over personal or familial preferences, and the principle that religious rulings must be based on God's command, not on the wishes of people.

translation: Allah has already ordained for you the expiation of your oaths. And Allah is your Protector, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This means that God, in His mercy and wisdom, has provided a prescribed way to absolve an oath when a person swears to do or avoid something and then finds that another course is better, or that fulfilling the oath would lead to harm or difficulty. The oath is not meant to trap the believer into a rigid commitment that prevents him from doing what is right; rather, he may offer the required expiation and act according to God’s guidance. God’s statement that He is your Protector affirms that He alone governs, aids, and cares for believers, and His laws are not arbitrary. Because He is All-Knowing, He knows human weakness and circumstances, and because He is All-Wise, He legislates what is best and most beneficial. Thus the verse teaches reverence for oaths while also showing that obedience to God and choosing the greater good take precedence, with a divinely appointed means of release from oaths.

translation: And [remember] when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a matter; then when she disclosed it, and Allah informed him of it, he made known part of it and overlooked part. And when he informed her of it, she said, “Who told you this?” He said, “The All-Knowing, the All-Aware has informed me.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah’s knowledge encompasses even the most private confidences and hidden conversations. A secret entrusted within the Prophet’s household was disclosed, but Allah, the All-Knowing and All-Aware, revealed it to His Prophet. The Prophet’s response was not harsh retaliation; he addressed only what needed to be addressed and overlooked the rest, displaying prophetic wisdom, restraint, and forbearance. When asked how he knew, he did not claim an earthly informant but attributed the knowledge directly to Allah. Thus the passage warns against betraying trusts and spreading private matters, affirms that Allah exposes what people conceal, and shows that the Prophet’s knowledge came through divine revelation from the One who is fully aware of all hidden things.

translation: If you two turn to Allah in repentance, then indeed your hearts have deviated. But if you support one another against him, then indeed Allah is his Protector, and Gabriel and the righteous believers, and the angels after that are his supporters.
interpretation: This addresses two wives of the Prophet who had erred, calling them to sincere repentance and showing that their hearts had turned away from what was right. It then warns that any mutual backing against the Prophet cannot succeed, because Allah Himself is his Guardian, and Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels are all his helpers. The verse thus affirms divine protection of the Prophet, the seriousness of opposing him, and the open door of repentance for those who err.

translation: It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you: Muslim women, believing, devoutly obedient, repentant, worshipping, fasting, previously married and virgins.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) against conduct that would displease him and God. It teaches that no one is indispensable to God's religion, and that He is fully able to replace them with women who surpass them in the qualities named: true submission to God, sincere faith, steadfast obedience, repentance from sin, worship, fasting, and chastity. The mention of both previously married and virgin women shows that superiority in God's sight is not determined by marital history or social status but by faith and righteous action. The verse is not a command or prediction that the Prophet must divorce them, but a corrective warning and a call to uphold the high standard of conduct required in the Prophet's household.

translation: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, but do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse obliges believers to guard themselves and those in their care from Hellfire by nurturing faith, obedience, worship, and moral and religious instruction within the household. The Fire is described as fueled by human beings and stones to convey its terrifying intensity and the utter worthlessness of whatever is thrown into it. The angels placed over it are harsh and severe, executing Allah’s command without hesitation or deviation; their perfect obedience stands as a warning that divine justice will be carried out exactly, and that no one can escape it through negligence or excuses.

translation: O you who disbelieve, make no excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who rejected faith will find no accepted apology or self-justification, for the time of testing and repentance has ended. Their recompense is strictly Just: it corresponds exactly to the disbelief and deeds they freely chose and persisted in during worldly life, so the punishment they meet is the rightful consequence of their own actions, not an unjust imposition.

translation: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.'
interpretation: Sincere repentance is a complete and resolute turning back to Allah: abandoning the sin, regretting it, resolving not to return to it, and restoring any rights owed. It is not mere words but a transformation that seeks Allah's pleasure alone. The verse teaches that this repentance opens the way to forgiveness and to the gardens of eternal bliss, and that on the Day of Judgment Allah will honor the Prophet and the believers rather than disgrace them. The light moving before them and on their right symbolizes the faith and righteous deeds that guide and accompany them, while their prayer to perfect their light and forgive them expresses their ongoing need for Allah's mercy and their hope not to be left in darkness. The closing affirmation that Allah is capable of all things guarantees that He can complete their light, forgive them, and fulfill what He has promised.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be severe with them. Their refuge is Hell—and how wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to wage struggle against two groups: the open disbelievers and the hypocrites. Each is confronted according to its nature—open opposition is met with strength and, where required, armed struggle, while hidden hypocrisy is met with firm argument, exposure, and resolute severity. Being harsh here means firmness in truth, justice, and deterrence, not unjust cruelty. The verse also declares that their final return is Hell, the worst destination, affirming that ultimate judgment and recompense belong to Allah.

translation: Allah has struck an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them. So they could not avail them anything against Allah, and it was said: 'Enter the Fire with those who enter.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that nearness to the righteous, even marriage to a prophet, does not benefit a person before Allah unless it is joined with faith and obedience. The betrayal of the wives of Nuh and Lut was betrayal in religion—disbelief and siding with the enemies of the prophets—not marital infidelity. The two prophets could not shield them from Allah’s punishment, because judgment is based on one’s own faith and deeds, not on family ties or worldly association. Thus those who persist in disbelief will enter the Fire along with the rest of the disbelievers, no matter how close they may have been to righteous people.

translation: And Allah sets forth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, 'My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse presents the wife of Pharaoh as a model of sincere faith for all believers. It teaches that true belief is not determined by one’s environment, spouse, or ruling power, but by one’s own loyalty to God. She lived in the palace of a tyrant yet sought nearness to God before all worldly comfort, asking for a house in Paradise rather than security in Pharaoh’s kingdom. Her prayer separates the oppressor from his deeds, showing that a believer must reject not only unjust persons but also the systems, policies, and actions of injustice. Seeking refuge from “the wrongdoing people” indicates that faith requires disavowal of collective evil and alignment with God’s justice. Thus the verse affirms that righteous women are spiritual examples for all believers, that worldly power cannot protect or fulfill the soul, and that ultimate success is deliverance from oppression and closeness to God in the Hereafter.

translation: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His Books, and she was among the devoutly obedient.
interpretation: This verse presents Mary as a model of faith, purity, and obedience. Her guarding her chastity signifies her preservation of honor and sexual purity. God’s breathing into her of His Spirit refers to the miraculous creation of Jesus by God’s command through the angel Gabriel, not to any literal divine indwelling or physical offspring. Her affirmation of the words of her Lord and His Books shows her complete acceptance of divine revelation, and her being among the qanitin means she was steadfastly devout, humble, and obedient to God.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes that absolute sovereignty, ownership, and authority belong exclusively to God. His “hand” signifies His perfect possession, control, and disposal of all affairs, not any physical attribute. Since He is “over all things competent,” nothing in creation lies outside His power, will, or knowledge: He alone originates, sustains, governs, and will bring all things to their final end. Thus all kingship and effective power are His alone, and every creature is entirely dependent upon Him.

translation: He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed; and He is the Almighty, the Forgiving.
interpretation: God created both death and life as a purposeful trial, testing not the abundance of deeds but their quality, sincerity, and conformity to His guidance. Death reminds people of accountability and the transience of worldly life, while life provides the opportunity to strive and choose the best conduct. His names al-‘Aziz and al-Ghafur show that He is mighty and sovereign over all, able to reward and punish, yet He is forgiving toward those who repent and seek His mercy.

translation: He who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return your vision; do you see any flaw?
interpretation: This verse presents the ordered cosmos as evidence of God’s perfect wisdom and mercy: the seven heavens are arranged in harmonious strata, and within the whole of His creation there is no imbalance, contradiction, or defect. The command to look again is an invitation to examine carefully and repeatedly, for human perception will find no crack, rupture, or fault in what God has made. Its meaning is that the flawless coherence of creation points to the Creator’s oneness, power, and absolute perfection, and it calls the observer to humble reflection rather than heedless denial.

translation: Then return your gaze again, twice; the gaze will come back to you humbled and weary.
interpretation: This verse commands repeated, diligent observation of the heavens and all creation. After looking again and again, the observer's sight returns to him subdued, disappointed, and exhausted, unable to find any flaw, gap, or disorder in what God has made. It thus affirms the perfect order, precision, and mastery of God's creation, and it humbles human perception before divine perfection.

translation: And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made them missiles for the devils, and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse declares that God adorned the lowest heaven with luminous stars, which serve as both beauty and as projectiles against devils who seek to eavesdrop on heavenly matters. It affirms God's sovereign protection of the higher realms and warns that the devils who persist in rebellion will face the blazing punishment prepared for them in the Hereafter.

translation: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse means that those who reject faith in their Lord—denying His existence, oneness, or right to be worshipped—will receive the punishment of Hell, and it is an evil final destination and a miserable place of return.

translation: When they are thrown into it, they will hear from it a horrible inhaling sound while it boils over.
interpretation: This verse depicts the terrifying reception of the condemned in Hell. As they are cast into it, the Fire itself emits a deep, gasping, roaring sound—like an inward breath—because it is boiling over with intense fury and heat. This conveys both physical and psychological torment: the damned hear the Fire’s rage as they enter, and its boiling signifies relentless, escalating punishment. It warns that Hell is a raging reality under God’s command, and that those who rejected the truth will face an overwhelming, frightening, and inescapable end.

translation: It almost bursts with rage. Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner?"
interpretation: This depicts Hell as fiercely enraged against those who rejected faith, while the angels guarding it confront each new group with the question of whether divine warning had reached them. Its meaning is that the punishment of the Hereafter is just and accountable: God sent warners and prophets so that people would not be destroyed without having been told the truth, and those who persisted in denial after warning are held responsible for their choice.

translation: They will say: 'Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said, Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.'
interpretation: This is the self-condemnation of those who reject faith after the warning has reached them. It teaches that accountability follows clear communication: they cannot claim they were never warned. Their rejection is shown as willful—they denied the messenger, denied that God had revealed any guidance at all, and then accused the messenger of gross misguidance. The verse thus exposes the moral inversion of disbelief: those who were actually guided are labeled astray by those who refused guidance. It also affirms that divine punishment is just, because it comes only after a warner has come and been knowingly rejected.

translation: And they will say: Had we listened or used our reason, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse reports the confession of those condemned to Hell: their ruin was not due to a lack of faculties but to their refusal to use them rightly. They had the ability to hear the divine message and to reason about the signs and proofs, yet they turned away in arrogance and heedlessness. Their words on that Day acknowledge God’s justice: had they listened with acceptance and reflected with sound intellect, they would have followed guidance and avoided the punishment of the blazing Fire. Thus the verse establishes human responsibility and shows that hearing and reason are trusts meant to lead one to faith and obedience, not to be neglected or misused.

translation: So they will confess their sin, but away with the companions of the Blaze!
interpretation: This verse means that on the Day of Reckoning the deniers will finally admit their guilt, yet their confession comes too late to benefit them; therefore God declares them ruined and far removed from mercy, as inhabitants of the blazing Fire. It teaches that deliberately rejecting the truth leads to irreversible loss, and that acknowledging sin only after judgment cannot avert punishment.

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord in the unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith and piety are proven when a person remains conscious of God even when no one is watching, when sin is tempting, and when accountability seems hidden from human eyes. Such reverence is sincere, not performed for people, and it restrains the soul out of love and awe of God. The promised forgiveness removes the guilt of human weakness, while the great reward points to an abundant, enduring honor that God alone can give.

translation: And conceal your speech or proclaim it—indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge encompasses both outward speech and hidden thoughts, so no secret intention or inner state is hidden from Him. It calls people to be mindful of their public and private words, since God knows the deepest contents of the hearts.

translation: Does He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This rhetorical question affirms that the Creator’s knowledge of His creation is necessary and all-encompassing. Since He originated and fashioned every creature, He cannot be unaware of its outward states or hidden secrets. His names al-Latif and al-Khabir mean He knows the subtlest realities, penetrates the innermost intentions, and is fully informed of every condition, so nothing about His creation is hidden from Him.

translation: He is the One who made the earth subservient for you, so walk in its paths and eat of His provision; and to Him is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God has subdued the earth and made it fit for human movement, labor, and benefit, so people may travel through its regions and seek their livelihood from what He provides. Yet this worldly activity should be accompanied by the awareness that all provision comes from God and that the final return, resurrection, and accountability are to Him alone.

translation: Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, and then it will heave?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical warning to those who mistakenly feel safe from Allah’s punishment. The One “in the heaven” is Allah, exalted above His creation, whose command and dominion are from above. He has absolute power over the earth beneath them: if He willed, He could cause it to sink and swallow them, or make it convulse and shake violently. Their safety is not real, and no earthly stability can protect them from His judgment. The verse calls them to fear Allah, submit to Him, and abandon the illusion that they can escape His power.

translation: Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how My warning is.
interpretation: This is a warning to those who reject the Prophet and mock the divine warning. It asks whether they feel safe from God, who is exalted above the heavens and has power to send a punishing storm of stones or pebbles upon them. When that punishment comes, they will realize the truth and severity of the warning they were given, but that realization will be too late. The verse calls them to abandon arrogance and to take God's warning seriously before it is too late.

translation: And certainly those before them denied, so how was My reproach?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the truth by reminding them that earlier communities also denied their messengers. God’s “reproach” here means His severe rejection, condemnation, and punishment. The rhetorical question declares that His response was devastating and inescapable. It affirms that God’s law of accountability does not change: rejecting divine guidance brings ruin, and no one can evade His judgment.

translation: Do they not look at the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He is Seeing of all things.
interpretation: This verse calls people to reflect on the birds soaring overhead as a sign of Allah’s power, mercy, and continuous care. Their spreading and folding of wings, and their remaining suspended in the air, are not sustained by any independent force but by Allah, the Most Merciful. It reminds the reader that the same God who governs and preserves even the birds sees all things, so nothing is hidden from Him, and He is fully able to hold, provide for, and account for His creation.

translation: Or who is it that could be an army for you to aid you besides the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are but in delusion.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical challenge to those who trust in created means of protection—armies, allies, wealth, or power—as though these could save them apart from God. It declares that no such force can avail against Allah or stand in His place, for He alone is the true Helper and Protector. The disbelievers are therefore deceived: they place confidence in what cannot ultimately save them while rejecting the One who alone has authority over all aid. Their condition is one of false hope and delusion, not real security.

translation: Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? Rather, they have persisted in insolence and aversion.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical rebuke to those who turn away from God while depending on others or on their own means. If God were to withhold His provision, no created being could supply it, so their continued defiance is not grounded in reason but in arrogance and a willful refusal of the truth. It affirms that sustenance rests entirely with God and warns that obstinacy and aversion cannot harm Him or alter His decree; they only harm the one who persists in them.

translation: Is he who walks fallen on his face better guided, or he who walks upright on a straight path?
interpretation: This rhetorical question contrasts two ways of moving through life: the one who is collapsed upon his face, unable to see or move properly, represents the disbeliever or the one enslaved by desires, arrogance, and misguidance; while the one who walks upright on a straight path represents the believer who follows Allah’s revealed guidance with balance, clarity, and purpose. True guidance is not found in merely moving or sincerely following one’s own way, but in uprightness upon the straight path of tawhid and obedience to the Messenger.

translation: Say, "It is He who originated you and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little do you give thanks."
interpretation: The verse calls humans to recognize God as the sole Creator and the giver of their faculties. Hearing and sight are outward senses by which people perceive the world, while the heart is the inward center of understanding, intention, and faith. These are not random endowments but purposeful blessings meant to lead a person to know, worship, and obey God. True gratitude is not merely verbal thanks; it is using these gifts rightly, acknowledging their Source, and not denying Him. The rebuke that humans give little thanks means that despite constant dependence on God for these faculties, gratitude is rare. It also implies moral responsibility: the same hearing, sight, and heart that receive God's signs will be the means by which people are held accountable.

translation: Say, 'He is the One who created you and dispersed you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.'
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to declare that Allah alone originated human creation and spread humankind across the earth, and that the same divine power will inevitably gather all people back to Him for judgment. It affirms God's sole lordship and the certainty of the Hereafter, reminding humans that their existence and dispersal on earth do not remove their accountability before their Creator.

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse conveys the mockery and denial of the disbelievers concerning the promised resurrection and judgment. They challenge the Prophet and the believers to specify its time, as though delay would disprove its truth, while the promise is certain and its appointed time rests solely with God, whose wisdom they refuse to acknowledge.

translation: Say, "Knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse establishes that knowledge of the unseen—especially the timing of the Hour and the final judgment—belongs exclusively to Allah; no prophet, angel, or created being possesses it independently. The Prophet Muhammad is therefore commanded to clarify his role: he is not the owner of hidden knowledge or the One who determines when events will occur, but a human messenger whose duty is to deliver a clear, unambiguous warning. The verse thus teaches pure monotheism in knowledge and prophethood: ultimate authority over the unseen rests with God alone, while the messenger’s task is faithful conveyance and warning, not control over divine decrees.

translation: But when they see it close at hand, the faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed, and it will be said, “This is that which you used to call for.”
interpretation: This verse describes the moment the disbelievers witness the punishment they denied and mockingly demanded to be brought quickly. Seeing it near, their faces become dark with grief, fear, and humiliation, and they are rebuked with the truth: this is the very torment they used to challenge and call for. It affirms that divine warning is real, that mockery cannot avert judgment, and that the deniers will be confronted with the consequence of their disbelief at the time they can no longer reject or escape it.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should destroy me and those with me, or have mercy upon us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"
interpretation: This verse confronts the disbelievers’ preoccupation with the Prophet’s fate as if it were their security. Whether God destroys him and the believers with him or grants them mercy, that outcome does not shield those who persist in disbelief from the painful punishment awaiting them. No one can protect them from God’s judgment, and no created being can avert it. Their only real concern should be their own accountability before God, for the Prophet’s life, death, or mercy is not a refuge for those who reject the truth; only faith and repentance can deliver them.

translation: Say, "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. And you will come to know who is in clear error."
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet, and the believers with him, to proclaim that Allah—al-Rahman, the Most Merciful—is the One in whom they have faith and on whom they place their complete trust. Their reliance is not on human power, wealth, or false deities, but solely on Allah’s mercy and authority. The disbelievers who reject this truth and mock the believers will eventually discover, when the reality becomes undeniable, who was truly misguided in an obvious and manifest way.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if your water were to sink away, then who could bring you flowing water?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical challenge establishing that only Allah has power over the water upon which all life depends. If He were to cause your water to disappear deep into the earth, no created being, false deity, or human power could restore it. The question exposes the helplessness of anything worshiped besides Allah and calls people to recognize His exclusive lordship, His provision, and their complete dependence on Him. It is both a proof of His oneness and a warning against ingratitude and associating partners with Him.

translation: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.
interpretation: Allah opens the surah with the letter Nun and then swears by the pen and by everything written with it. This oath honors the instruments of knowledge and the written record, especially the revealed books, and it implicitly answers the disbelievers who rejected the Prophet and the Qur'an. It indicates that just as writing preserves and conveys truth, Allah will preserve His revelation and vindicate His Messenger.

translation: By the grace of your Lord, you are not a madman.
interpretation: This is a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, rejecting the disbelievers’ accusation of insanity. It affirms that the favor and blessing of his Lord upon him—namely prophethood, sound reason, and moral excellence—completely negate such a slander. The oath-like phrasing emphasizes that his mission and state are gifts from God, not signs of madness, and that the accusation is false.

translation: And indeed, for you there is a reward that will never be cut off.
