interpretation: This is Allah’s direct assurance to the Prophet Muhammad that his labor, patience, and faithful conveying of the revelation will not go unpaid or be forgotten. The reward promised to him is with Allah—continuous, inexhaustible, and never diminished, interrupted, or followed by any reminder of favor or injury. The phrase “ghayr mamnun” emphasizes that his recompense is unending and free of any defect, affirming the lasting honor and dignity of his prophetic mission.

translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
interpretation: This verse is a divine affirmation praising the Prophet Muhammad, declaring that his conduct, disposition, and ethical excellence are of the highest and most noble order. It means his character was firmly established upon virtues such as truthfulness, patience, humility, mercy, justice, and generosity, and that his example is the perfect model for human behavior. His morality was not merely natural temperament but divinely guided and refined, making him the supreme embodiment of the Qur'anic teachings.

translation: So you will see, and they will see
interpretation: This is a divine reassurance and warning: the Prophet is told that the truth will soon become manifest, and his opponents will also witness the outcome with their own eyes. It means that the false accusations they level against him will be exposed, and it will become clear who is truly misguided and afflicted with delusion.

translation: Which of you is the afflicted [with madness]?
interpretation: This is a divine rebuttal to those who accused the Prophet Muhammad of madness. It warns that the truth will soon become clear, exposing which party is actually afflicted by delusion and falsehood. The charge of insanity is thus turned back upon the accusers: their rejection of revelation and slander of the Prophet are the real signs of a diseased understanding, while the Prophet remains on clear guidance and sound reason.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the true reality of guidance and misguidance is known perfectly only to God. He alone knows the inward states, motives, and final orientations of people, so no human being has the right to claim definitive judgment over whose path is truly His or whose heart is truly guided. It directs the believer to humility, to avoid self-righteous certainty about others’ ultimate standing before God, and to rely on God’s all-encompassing knowledge and justice.

translation: So do not obey the deniers.
interpretation: This is a firm divine command to the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension to every believer, not to yield to those who reject the truth and deny God's revelation. It means refusing to follow their wishes, adopt their false standards, or compromise the message under their pressure. The verse calls for steadfastness upon the truth and warns that obeying the deniers in matters of faith and sacred law leads away from God's guidance.

translation: They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise.
interpretation: This verse exposes the desire of the disbelievers that the Prophet would soften or compromise in matters of faith—specifically by not condemning their false beliefs and idols—so that they, in return, would offer him a reciprocal accommodation. It warns against any partial concession in religious truth, since their wish was not for genuine faith but for mutual dilution of the message.

translation: And do not obey every contemptible habitual swearer.
interpretation: This is a divine instruction to the Prophet, and by extension to the believers, not to yield to or follow the wishes of a person who is characterized by constant oath-taking and baseness. Such a person's oaths are not a criterion of truth or integrity; his moral worth is low, so his guidance, demands, or testimony should not be accepted merely because he swears. The verse warns against being influenced by those whose words are cheap and whose character is dishonorable, and it directs the believer to uphold truth and dignity rather than submit to such pressure.

translation: A slanderer, going about with malicious gossip.
interpretation: This describes a person who habitually insults and backbites others and who carries harmful talk between people to stir up enmity and discord. It condemns a character that ruins reputations, breaks trust, and corrupts relationships, and it warns believers not to follow or emulate such behavior.

translation: A preventer of good, a transgressor, a sinner.
interpretation: This describes a person who habitually withholds good from others—whether wealth, rights, or kindness—oversteps the limits set by God and by justice, and persists in sin, so that greed, aggression, and guilt become his defining traits.

translation: Coarse and violent, and moreover of base, ignoble origin.
interpretation: This is a severe condemnation of a person who is harsh, abusive, and arrogant, and who is also of low or illegitimate lineage, lacking nobility of birth and character; these defects together make him utterly contemptible and unfit to be obeyed or trusted.

translation: Because he is a possessor of wealth and children.
interpretation: In its Qur’anic context, this phrase exposes the mentality of a person who lets worldly riches and offspring become grounds for arrogance and self-sufficiency. He assumes that material abundance and many sons prove his superiority, so he feels entitled to reject divine guidance and dismiss God’s signs. The verse teaches that wealth and children are not signs of spiritual honor or divine approval; they are tests. True worth before God rests on faith, gratitude, justice, and humility, while using blessings as an excuse for pride and denial only leads to ruin.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse describes the arrogant rejecter who, upon hearing God’s revealed signs, does not consider them seriously but dismisses them as mere ancient fables or tales inherited from earlier nations. His response shows a willful refusal to reflect on the truth and a cheap evasion meant to avoid submitting to divine guidance.

translation: We will brand him on the snout.
interpretation: This is a threat of severe humiliation and lasting disgrace: Allah will place a mark of shame upon this arrogant mocker, likening him to an animal branded on the nose, so that his ignominy becomes visible and inseparable from him.

translation: Indeed, We have tested them just as We tested the companions of the garden, when they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning.
interpretation: Allah is declaring that worldly prosperity and ease are not necessarily signs of His pleasure, but are often a trial by which He tests gratitude, obedience, and reliance upon Him. The garden owners’ oath to harvest at dawn expressed self-confidence, ingratitude, and neglect of Allah’s will and the rights of the needy; therefore their plan was undone. The verse teaches that no human scheme can secure or preserve blessings against Allah’s decree, and that wealth, harvest, and favor must be received with humble acknowledgment of Him, remembrance of His will, and generosity toward others—not with arrogance, exclusion, or forgetfulness of the One who grants them.

translation: and they did not make any exception
interpretation: This means that when they swore to carry out their plan, they did not attach the condition “if Allah wills.” It exposes their arrogant self-reliance and their neglect of God’s decree: they treated their intended act as certain and within their own control, so God rendered their plan fruitless. The verse teaches that human intentions remain subject to God’s will and should be qualified by acknowledging it.

translation: So a visitation from your Lord came upon it while they were asleep.
interpretation: This means that the punishment descended by Allah’s command, not by chance, at a time when they felt secure and were unable to protect anything. It shows that Allah’s decree is sudden and irresistible, especially against those who scheme to withhold the rights of the poor; their wealth and sense of safety were only temporary, and a single divine visitation could destroy what they relied upon. It teaches that divine justice may come while the wrongdoer is unaware, and that God alone is the true Owner and Disposer of all things.

translation: So it became like the reaped harvest.
interpretation: The phrase describes the garden’s utter ruin after divine punishment struck it: it was reduced to a bare, blackened, mown-down state, as though everything fruitful had been cut off. “كالصريم” carries the sense of something severed, stripped, or dark, emphasizing total and irreversible loss. It signifies that human schemes to hoard blessings and withhold the rights of the poor cannot stand before God’s decree; what was cherished can be rendered desolate in an instant.

translation: Then they called out to one another at daybreak.
interpretation: Their early-morning summoning of one another exposes a collective resolve to carry out a wrong they had plotted, showing how heedlessness and greed can make people rush together toward an evil plan even after God’s decree has already overtaken it.

translation: Go early to your crop, if you are to reap.
interpretation: This is a call by the owners of the garden to one another at dawn, urging immediate harvesting because they were resolved to cut its fruit. It expresses their confident intent to gather the crop exclusively and deprive the poor of any share. The verse reveals that human resolve and planning, when severed from God-consciousness and justice toward the needy, are fragile; what they assumed they controlled was overtaken by God's decree before they could act.

translation: So they went off, whispering to one another,
interpretation: They departed with a secret, hushed conversation, deliberately concealing their plan from others. Their whispering reveals a scheming, miserly resolve: they intended to keep the garden’s harvest for themselves and prevent the needy from receiving any share, showing how greed had hardened their hearts and made them conspire in secret rather than act with gratitude and generosity.

translation: Saying, 'No needy person shall enter it today upon you.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the intention of the garden’s owners to monopolize the harvest and shut out the poor. Their words are not a divine command but the sinful resolve of people who regard the needy as intruders upon their wealth. It signifies the corruption of greed: when a blessing is treated as private entitlement, the rightful share of the poor is denied. It warns that plotting to exclude the poor from God’s provision is a rejection of the duty to give the needy their due, and such schemes ultimately bring loss instead of security.

translation: And they went early, resolved to withhold [from the poor], confident in their ability.
interpretation: The verse describes a hardened, grudging resolve to keep good exclusively for oneself and to shut out those in need, joined to a false confidence in one’s own power to carry out that intention. Its meaning is that such people mistake God-given blessing for personal sovereignty and imagine their planning is secure, whereas all true capability belongs to God alone and can be undone by His decree.

translation: So when they saw it, they said, 'Indeed, we are lost.'
interpretation: This is their first, shocked admission of being astray: seeing the garden unrecognizable, they thought they had lost the way or were mistaken about it. More deeply, it exposes that their scheme to withhold God's bounty from the poor had set them on a false path, so the ruin they beheld became a mirror of their own misguidance and coming deprivation.

translation: Nay, we are deprived.
interpretation: This is their confession that the expected good has been cut off from them: they are not merely wandering or mistaken, but have been deprived of blessing and harvest as a consequence of their own greed and their resolve to withhold the rights of the poor.

translation: The most moderate of them said, “Did I not tell you, ‘Why do you not glorify Allah?’”
interpretation: This is a rebuke from the most balanced and upright among the group, reminding them that he had already warned them to glorify God—that is, to acknowledge His lordship, submit to His will, thank Him for His provision, and seek His forgiveness—before they carried out their arrogant plan. Their failure to glorify God revealed a deeper spiritual heedlessness: they treated blessings as theirs by right and forgot that all provision belongs to God and can be withdrawn at any moment. The verse teaches that tasbih is not merely words on the tongue; it is humility before God, reliance on Him, and readiness to obey Him, especially in how one uses wealth and treats the poor.

translation: They said, “Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.”
interpretation: This is their acknowledgment of God’s perfect justice and transcendence, and their admission that they had wronged themselves by withholding what was due and opposing His command; they recognize that the loss they suffered was a just consequence of their own transgression, not any injustice from their Lord.

translation: Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.
interpretation: This describes the moment when the guilty realize the consequence of their wrongdoing: instead of admitting their shared fault before Allah, they begin accusing one another and trying to shift responsibility. Their mutual blame exposes both regret and moral failure—regret because they now see the loss, and failure because blame after the deed cannot restore what was destroyed or excuse the injustice they intended. It warns that collective sin cannot be escaped by mutual recrimination; true correction must come through repentance and restoring the rights of others.

translation: They said, “O woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors.”
interpretation: This is a confession of guilt and intense regret when the consequences of their wrongdoing become clear. “Transgressors” means those who overstep God’s limits and rebel against His command; by admitting “we were transgressors,” they acknowledge that their ruin was not an unfair misfortune but the result of their own disobedience and arrogance. The verse teaches that transgression leads to self-destruction, and that remorse after the harm is done cannot restore what was lost.

translation: Perhaps our Lord will replace it with something better than it. Indeed, we turn to our Lord in hope and desire.
interpretation: This is a statement of hopeful repentance and reliance on God after a loss caused by one’s own wrongdoing. It means that even when a blessing is taken away due to sin, the believer should not despair, but should turn back to God with longing, asking Him to grant something better in place of what was lost—whether in this world or in the Hereafter—and should direct all hope and desire toward Him alone.

translation: Such is the punishment; and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse declares that the worldly punishment sent upon the owners of the garden in Surah Al-Qalam is a warning and example, but the punishment awaiting in the Hereafter is far greater, more severe, and more lasting. It calls people to realize that present afflictions are minor compared to the eternal consequences of rejecting faith and persisting in wrongdoing, if they truly understood with certainty.

translation: Indeed, for the righteous before their Lord are Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: This verse affirms that those who are mindful of Allah and restrain themselves from disobedience, seeking His pleasure, will be granted with their Lord gardens of perfect delight and eternal bliss. Their reward is not merely future or distant; it is specifically prepared with their Lord, indicating honor, nearness, and security in His presence. The phrase “Gardens of Bliss” conveys enduring joy, peace, and pleasure that no worldly hardship or sacrifice can equal, and it assures the God-fearing that their piety will be met with Allah’s generous and everlasting reward.

translation: Then will We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical denial: Allah will not equate those who submit to Him and follow His guidance with those who reject Him and commit evil. The two are not equal in His judgment and recompense, for divine justice requires distinguishing the obedient from the guilty.

translation: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke and condemnation of those who judge falsely, implying that their standards are corrupt: they wrongly assume that God will treat the obedient and the guilty alike, and thus they deny His wisdom and justice.

translation: Or have you a Book wherein you study?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of rebuke, denying the disbelievers’ claim. It means: Do you possess a revealed scripture from Allah that you read and study, in which you find support for your assertion that matters will be as you wish and that you will receive whatever you choose? The implied answer is no; they have no such divine book, and their claims are merely wishful thinking without revealed proof.

translation: Indeed, you have in it whatever you choose.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who claim, without any proof, that they will receive whatever they desire or choose for themselves. It asks rhetorically whether they possess a Scripture from God in which they read that they may select their own outcome, such as being saved or favored over the believers. The verse denies that any such book or guarantee exists; their claim is mere wishful thinking, not revealed truth.

translation: Or do you have oaths binding upon Us, reaching until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed for you is whatever you judge?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke: Allah asks whether the disbelievers possess a firm covenant or sworn promise from Him, guaranteed to remain in force until the Resurrection, stipulating that they will be granted whatever they claim or decree for themselves. The implied answer is no; their assumption is false. It exposes the futility of their desires and the arrogance of treating Allah's judgment as subordinate to their own wishes; the decree and final authority belong to Allah alone, and no one has a binding claim upon Him to receive what he arbitrarily chooses.

translation: Ask them: which of them is a guarantor for that?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke exposing the baselessness of the disbelievers’ claim. If they assert that they will receive the same reward as the believers or that God will treat them as they wish, let them name the one among them who can stand as surety and take responsibility for that claim. The verse shows that they have no proof, no covenant, and no guarantor, so their assertion is false and without foundation.

translation: Or do they have partners [with Allah]? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful.
interpretation: This is a decisive challenge to those who associate others with Allah, claiming that their false deities, idols, or intercessors share in His authority or can benefit them. If their claim were true, they should be able to produce those partners and have them stand as witnesses or helpers. The verse exposes the emptiness of their assertion and affirms that no partner, intercessor, or rival has any real power beside Allah.

translation: The Day when the shin is uncovered, and they are invited to prostrate, but they will not be able to.
interpretation: It depicts a moment on the Day of Resurrection when matters become extremely severe and the reality of Allah’s majesty is disclosed. People are then called to prostrate before Him, but those who refused to submit and were arrogant in worldly life cannot do so; their ability to humble themselves is gone. This exposes their falsehood and brings them disgrace, showing that sincere prostration and submission are tested in this life, and in the Hereafter a forced or belated prostration will not benefit those who rejected faith.

translation: Their eyes will be lowered in humiliation, and disgrace will overwhelm them. For they had been invited to prostrate while they were safe and sound.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers and the negligent on the Day of Judgment: their gaze is cast down in shame, and abasement covers them. Their punishment is tied to the fact that in the worldly life they were called to prostrate to God—meaning the prayer and worship by which a servant humbles themselves before their Lord—while they were healthy, capable, and free from any excuse. They refused and turned away. So on that Day they will be unable to prostrate and will be overtaken by humiliation, because they abandoned the humility and obedience they were able to offer when it would have benefited them.

translation: So leave Me alone with those who deny this discourse. We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know.
interpretation: This is a divine warning that rejecting the revelation does not harm God or defeat His purpose; He alone will deal with the deniers. Their continued blessings, ease, and delay of punishment are not signs of divine approval but a gradual entrapment: God lets them proceed in their denial, and they misinterpret His forbearance as safety, until the consequences close in on them unexpectedly from a direction they never anticipated. The Prophet is therefore told to leave their case to God and not to preoccupy himself with avenging their mockery.

translation: And I will grant them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: This means that God may allow the deniers to continue for a time and grant them delay in worldly ease, but this is not neglect or weakness. It is a firm and unbreakable divine plan: their respite only allows them to increase in wrongdoing before they are seized by His decree, and none can escape or frustrate His purpose.

translation: Or do you ask them for a reward, so they are burdened with debt?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question denying that the Prophet seeks any payment or material compensation from them for conveying the message. It exposes the emptiness of their rejection: they are not being weighed down by any financial demand or debt imposed by him. Since he asks them for no wage, their refusal cannot be justified by any cost or burden; his reward is with God alone.

translation: Or have they the unseen, so they write it down?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of denial and rebuke. It means: Do they possess knowledge of the unseen, so that they can write down its secrets and issue judgments based on it? They do not; knowledge of the unseen belongs exclusively to Allah. Their claims about hidden matters, future events, or the ultimate outcome are mere conjecture, not true knowledge. The verse exposes the false confidence of those who reject the truth and speak as though they had access to Allah's hidden knowledge.

translation: So be patient for the judgment of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was distressed.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believer to remain steadfast under Allah’s decree and not to imitate the impatience of Jonah, who cried out from the belly of the whale in grief and constraint after leaving his people before Allah’s permission. It teaches that hardship and supplication are not blameworthy, but allowing sorrow to push one toward resentment or abandoning patient obedience to Allah’s command is. True submission is to endure Allah’s will until He brings relief.

translation: Had not a favor from his Lord overtaken him, he would have been cast onto the barren shore while he was blameworthy.
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Yunus (Jonah), who was swallowed by the fish after leaving his people in anger. It teaches that he was saved not by his own action but solely by Allah’s mercy and grace. Had Allah not favored him with forgiveness and acceptance of his repentance, he would have been thrown onto the desolate shore in disgrace and blame. The favor mentioned here is Allah’s mercy that rescued him, forgave him, and later chose him as one of the righteous. Thus the verse shows that divine grace is the true source of deliverance, and human mistakes are overcome by Allah’s compassion when one turns back to Him.

translation: Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.
interpretation: God’s choosing is an act of pure grace: after trial and rescue, He selects His servant and makes that election evident by placing him among the righteous—those whose lives are inwardly and outwardly aligned with His command. Righteousness here is therefore not merely human moral achievement but a gift of divine favor, granted to one who turns back to God and is accepted by Him.

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, “Indeed, he is mad.”
interpretation: This verse depicts the intense hostility, envy, and malice of the disbelievers toward the Prophet when he recites the Qur’an. Their glaring is so hateful that it is as though they would try to strike him down or make him slip with their very eyes, driven by rage at the truth they cannot refute. Then, unable to meet the Qur’an with any valid argument, they resort to slander, calling him mad. The verse thus exposes their corrupt motives, consoles the Prophet, and implies that Allah protects him from their plots and false accusations.

translation: And it is nothing but a reminder to all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur’an is a universal divine admonition sent for all created beings, not a product of human imagination, madness, or falsehood. It reminds every nation and generation of their accountability before God and calls them to the path of truth, guidance, and salvation.

translation: The Inevitable.
interpretation: Al-Haqqah is one of the names of the Day of Judgment; it denotes the certain, undeniable reality that must come to pass, in which Allah will establish the truth and judge all creation with perfect justice.

translation: What is the Inevitable?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of magnification and awe concerning the Day of Resurrection, named al-Hāqqah because it is the certain, inevitable reality that must come to pass, in which God’s promise and warning will be fulfilled and the truth of all matters will be made manifest.

translation: And what can make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question meant to magnify and emphasize the overwhelming, certain event of the Day of Resurrection. It conveys that its true nature, severity, and horror are beyond full human comprehension, so no one can truly grasp what it will be like until it comes to pass.

translation: Thamud and 'Aad denied the Striking Calamity.
interpretation: The 'Striking Calamity' is the Day of Resurrection, which strikes hearts with overwhelming terror, or the devastating punishment that strikes those who reject it. Thamud and 'Aad were ancient peoples who denied their prophets and the reality of that coming Hour, so their rejection became the cause of their destruction and a warning to all who follow them in disbelief.

translation: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast.
interpretation: It means that the people of Thamud were seized by a catastrophic punishment that exceeded all bounds—the dreadful Cry—because they persisted in disbelief and wrongdoing after clear signs had come to them through Salih. The term "al-Taghiyah" stresses that the punishment was an overpowering, transgressive force, fitting the way they themselves had transgressed against the truth.

translation: And as for 'Aad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind.
interpretation: This verse states that the people of 'Aad were annihilated by a wind of extreme force and severity, a punishment from God that no human strength could resist. Their destruction came after they persisted in rejecting their prophet and in arrogance, so the wind became an instrument of divine judgment, overwhelming them completely and leaving no power or refuge for them.

translation: He unleashed it upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.
interpretation: This describes the total destruction of the people of ‘Ad by a fierce, uninterrupted wind that Allah set loose upon them for seven nights and eight days. The prolonged punishment left them dead and prostrate like empty, rotten palm trunks, showing that no worldly power, wealth, or physical strength can resist Allah’s decree when He wills to punish a people for rejecting His messengers. It is a warning that divine judgment is severe, exact, and inescapable.

translation: So do you see any remnant of them?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question affirming that they were completely destroyed and left no surviving remnant, no trace, and no enduring legacy. It emphasizes the totality of Allah's punishment upon those nations and serves as a warning that no power can preserve those whom Allah decides to destroy.

translation: And Pharaoh, and those before him, and the overturned cities came with sin.
interpretation: This verse declares that Pharaoh, the generations before him, and the overturned cities—the people of Lot—all met Allah’s punishment because they committed the same root offense: denying the truth and persisting in rebellion and corruption. Their coming “with the sinful deed” means they deliberately brought their evil conduct before God, making it the basis of their ruin. It teaches that divine judgment is not arbitrary; it follows persistent transgression, and no worldly might can avert it once the truth has been rejected.

translation: So they disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, and He seized them with an overwhelming seizure.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who rejected the divine messenger sent to guide them: their defiance was not merely a passing sin but a deliberate disobedience to the authority of their Lord. Consequently, God’s punishment came upon them with a seizure that was severe, surpassing, and inescapable—an overwhelming destruction that none could resist or repel.

translation: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the great flood in the time of Noah. When the water rose beyond its limits and covered the earth, Allah saved Noah and the believers with him by carrying them in the ark, which sailed by His command. Addressing later people as “you” means that by preserving their ancestors, Allah preserved them as well, and it reminds them of His power and mercy. The event is a lesson that Allah can rescue the faithful and destroy the defiant, and it points to His ability to bring about the Resurrection.

translation: That We might make it a reminder for you, and that a retaining ear might retain it.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah preserved the event of the ark and the drowning of the deniers as an admonition for later generations. The “retaining ear” is not merely one that hears sounds, but a heart that receives the divine lesson, understands it, preserves it, and lets it shape belief and conduct. It is a call to attentive, obedient listening to the signs of Allah and to the warnings contained in sacred history, so that past judgments become a living reminder rather than a forgotten tale.

translation: Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast,
interpretation: This verse marks the commencement of the Hour through God’s command: the angel Israfil blows the Trumpet once, and that single blast instantly ends the present worldly order and initiates the events of the Day of Judgment. Its emphasis on “one blast” conveys that the transition from this life to the Hereafter occurs by God’s absolute power, suddenly and without need of repetition or delay.

translation: And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single crushing.
interpretation: This is a depiction of the overwhelming force of the Hour: the whole earth and the towering mountains are uprooted and smashed in one instant, reduced to scattered dust and leveled completely. It shows that every solid and seemingly permanent structure of worldly life will be destroyed at once by God’s command, and nothing can withstand His decree when the inevitable event comes to pass.

translation: Then on that Day, the Occurrence will have come to pass.
interpretation: This verse refers to the inevitable realization of the Hour—the Day of Resurrection—when, after the trumpet blast and the crushing of the earth and mountains, the great event of judgment will actually occur, and every soul will face the reality of God’s reckoning.

translation: And the heaven will split, so on that Day it will be frail.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, the heavens will be torn apart and their once firm order will weaken, signaling the collapse of the created cosmic system before God’s judgment.

translation: And the angels will be at its edges, and eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day.
interpretation: The verse signifies the overwhelming majesty and absolute sovereignty of God on the Day of Judgment: when the heavens are split open, the angels stand at its borders in complete submission and awe, while eight mighty angels carry the Throne of your Lord above them. This scene impresses upon the heart that all creation, including the highest angels, is utterly subject to God’s command, and that the Day of Reckoning is a reality of immense gravity and divine authority.

translation: On that Day you will be presented [for judgment]; nothing hidden of you will be concealed.
interpretation: This verse means that on the Day of Resurrection, every person will be brought before God for reckoning, and no deed, word, intention, or secret can remain hidden or denied. The apparent and concealed aspects of a person’s life will be fully exposed, proving God’s complete knowledge and making accountability absolute.

translation: Then as for the one who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, “Here, read my record!”
interpretation: This verse depicts the joy, relief, and honor of the successful believer on the Day of Judgment when his deeds are presented in his right hand—a sign of acceptance, divine mercy, and salvation. His invitation for others to read his record expresses confidence that it contains faith and righteous deeds, and that no injustice or shame will be found in it; it is the moment of vindication and the beginning of eternal bliss.

translation: Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my reckoning.
interpretation: This is the confession of a saved soul that its happiness in the Hereafter came from a firm conviction during worldly life that it would stand before God for judgment. That conviction was not merely mental; it produced God-consciousness, repentance, and good deeds, so when the record was presented, the person was safe and joyful.

translation: So he will be in a pleasant life.
interpretation: This describes the state of the one whose good deeds are heavy on the scales: he will enter a life of complete contentment, delight, and well-being in Paradise, a life that pleases him and is free from any sorrow, hardship, or displeasure.

translation: In an elevated Garden.
interpretation: It means that the people of bliss will be in a Paradise exalted in rank and station, raised above every place of loss and punishment, enjoying nearness, honor, and enduring delight.

translation: Its clusters of fruit are near at hand.
interpretation: This describes the fruits of Paradise as hanging low and easily reachable, so that its inhabitants may pick and enjoy them effortlessly. It conveys perfect ease, honor, and delight in the reward God has prepared for the righteous.

translation: Eat and drink with delight for what you sent forth in the days that have passed.
interpretation: This is a gracious address to the people of Paradise, inviting them to eat and drink with pure, wholesome enjoyment, free from any harm, exhaustion, or accountability. Their pleasure is the reward for the faith, obedience, patience, and good deeds they stored up during their worldly life—the days that have now passed and ended. It shows that the eternal joys of the Hereafter are both a gift from God and a fruit of what the servant sent ahead in this fleeting world.

translation: And as for the one who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had never been given my record!'
interpretation: This describes the disgrace and despair of those whose deeds are handed to them in the left hand, a sign of rejection and punishment. Their cry expresses not repentance but overwhelming regret: the record they receive has exposed every deed, leaving no room for denial or excuse, and they wish they had never been brought to account at all.

translation: And I did not know what my reckoning is.
interpretation: This is the regretful cry of one who receives his record of deeds on the Day of Judgment and sees the account of his sins set before him. He wishes he had never come to know that reckoning, because it exposes his evil deeds and seals his doom. It expresses the terror of accountability and the bitter remorse of a soul that wasted its chance and now faces the consequences.

translation: Oh, I wish it had been the final end!
interpretation: This is the desperate wish of the condemned sinner at the resurrection: he longs that death had been the absolute, irreversible end, so that he would never have been raised to face this account and punishment. It expresses utter regret and the horror of accountability, not a denial of God’s power, but a bitter craving for annihilation as relief from the shame and torment he now sees.

translation: My wealth has not availed me.
interpretation: This is the regretful confession of one who relied on worldly riches: at the moment of reckoning, his wealth could not protect him, avert punishment, or bring him any benefit, showing that material possessions are worthless when divine judgment comes unless they were used for righteousness.

translation: My authority has perished from me.
interpretation: It means that whatever worldly power, status, or dominion he relied upon has completely vanished, leaving him helpless before God; such authority cannot save its possessor or avert divine judgment in the Hereafter.

translation: Seize him and shackle him.
interpretation: This is a command to the angels of punishment to seize the condemned sinner and bind him in chains as the beginning of his humiliation and torment; it shows that on the Day of Judgment he has no power, no escape, and no defender, and that divine justice will overpower him completely.

translation: Then into Hellfire cast him.
interpretation: It is a command from God to the angels, after the condemned one has been seized and bound, to drive him into the blazing Fire and subject him to its torment—an expression of the inevitable, humiliating punishment that awaits the stubborn rejecter of faith.

translation: Then, into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, insert him.
interpretation: This is a command to the angels to thrust the condemned disbeliever into a massive chain measuring seventy cubits, as part of the severe, humiliating torment of Hell. The great length of the chain emphasizes the enormity of the punishment and the utter helplessness of the one being bound and dragged into it.

translation: Indeed, he used not to believe in Allah, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse identifies the root cause of the person's punishment: a settled, habitual refusal to believe in Allah, the Most Great. It is not merely a passing doubt but a persistent denial of God's greatness, lordship, and exclusive right to be worshipped. The mention of Allah as “the Most Great” intensifies the indictment: the one rejected is infinitely great, so disbelief in Him is a grave transgression that corrupts one's whole orientation and leads to the severe recompense described in the surrounding verses.

translation: And he does not encourage the feeding of the poor.
interpretation: This verse condemns a person whose denial of the Hereafter has hardened his heart toward the needy: he neither feeds the poor himself nor urges others to do so. It shows that true faith must produce compassion and social responsibility, and that neglecting the hungry is a sign of arrogance, selfishness, and spiritual corruption.

translation: So today he has no intimate friend here.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the disbeliever who refused faith and neglected the poor will find no close companion, relative, or intercessor to help him, defend him, or lessen his punishment; every supportive bond is cut off, and he stands utterly isolated in his accountability before God.

translation: Nor any food except from Ghislīn (a filthy discharge).
interpretation: This describes the food of the condemned in Hell: a repulsive, putrid discharge flowing from the bodies of its inhabitants. It is utterly foul and impure, gives no nourishment or benefit, and serves only to increase their humiliation and torment as part of their punishment.

translation: None will eat it except the sinners.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the vile food of punishment in the Hereafter is reserved exclusively for those who knowingly persist in sin and rebellion; it highlights divine justice, in that this humiliation is not for the righteous, and it warns that unrepentant wrongdoing leads to a debased and painful end.

translation: So I swear by what you see
interpretation: Allah swears by the visible creation and all that human eyes can witness, using it as a witness to His lordship and to the truth of the revelation, since the seen order points to the unseen realities and to the certainty of judgment.

translation: and what you do not see
interpretation: God includes the whole realm of the unseen in His oath, showing that His knowledge and testimony encompass all hidden realities—whether angels, unseen creatures, future events, or inward intentions—so the Qur’an’s message rests on absolute truth, and nothing lies beyond His awareness or judgment.

translation: Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur’an is conveyed through a noble and trustworthy messenger—namely the angel Gabriel—who received it from Allah and delivered it faithfully. It therefore establishes the Qur’an’s divine origin and honorable transmission, rejecting any claim that it is merely human poetry or ordinary speech.

translation: And it is not the saying of a poet; little do you believe.
interpretation: This verse rejects the claim that the Qur’an is poetry or the speech of a poet. It affirms that the revelation comes from Allah and is conveyed truthfully by His Messenger, so rejecting it as mere poetic expression reflects a deficiency in faith and a failure to believe rightly.

translation: Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.
interpretation: The verse repudiates any claim that the Qur'an is a kahin's utterance—a soothsayer's or diviner's speech produced through jinn or occult guesswork. It affirms that revelation is neither poetry nor fortune-telling but a clear message from God, and it rebukes the disbelievers' failure to remember and reflect: their neglect of the truth is so great that they do not distinguish between divine revelation and the deceptive pronouncements of a kahin. The implied remedy is to recall God's signs and recognize the Qur'an's unmatched truthfulness and its source in the Lord of the worlds.

translation: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur’an is sent down by Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all creation. It establishes the Qur’an’s divine origin and absolute authority, showing that it is not human speech, poetry, or invention, but revelation from the One who governs and nurtures all existence.

translation: And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings,
interpretation: This verse is a divine affirmation that the Prophet Muhammad did not invent the Qur’an; if he had falsely attributed any words to God, that would be an enormity deserving immediate punishment, so the revelation’s authenticity is guarded by God Himself.

translation: We would surely have seized him by the right hand.
interpretation: This is a statement of God’s absolute power and protection of revelation: if the Prophet had falsely attributed any words to Him, God would seize him by the right hand—meaning He would take him with irresistible force, authority, and exacting justice, as one seizes a culprit—and then cut off his aorta. It teaches that divine revelation is divinely guarded and that fabricating words in God’s name invites immediate and decisive punishment.

translation: Then We would surely have cut from him the aorta (al-Watin).
interpretation: This is a divine warning that anyone who falsely attributes words to God would be immediately and decisively cut off from the very source of life itself, showing that God’s revelation is absolutely protected and that tampering with it is met with total ruin.

translation: So there is no one among you who could prevent [Allah] from him.
interpretation: This verse declares that God’s decree is utterly irresistible and that no created being can interpose himself between God and the one He intends to seize or punish. If even the Messenger were to falsely attribute something to God, none of his followers or any other person could shield him or divert the punishment from him. Thus it both affirms God’s absolute sovereignty and confirms the Prophet’s sincerity: his refusal to fabricate revelation is grounded in the knowledge that no human protector could guard him from God’s justice, so his faithful delivery of the message is evidence of its divine source.

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for the God-fearing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur’an is an admonition and guidance that benefits those who possess taqwa—God-consciousness and protective reverence—by reminding them of His commands, promises, and warnings, and by calling them to live with accountability before Him.

translation: And indeed, We know that among you are deniers.
interpretation: Allah affirms that He is fully aware of those among the people who reject the truth and deny the revelation, so this is a warning that such denial is neither hidden from Him nor without consequence.

translation: And indeed, it is a regret for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This means that the Qur'an, which they rejected and denied in worldly life, will become a source of intense sorrow and remorse for them when the truth becomes unmistakably clear and they face the consequence of their disbelief, realizing too late the guidance they refused.

translation: And indeed, it is the truth of certainty.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur’an is absolute, unquestionable truth—certainty itself—so that it leaves no room for doubt and is the very reality upon which firm conviction rests.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This is a command to the Prophet, and by extension to every believer, to continuously exalt and purify the name of God from any imperfection or deficiency, and to acknowledge His supreme majesty and greatness. It directs the heart and tongue to tasbih—saying “Subhan Allah”—as an act of humble worship, gratitude, and reverence, especially when contemplating God’s power, blessings, and the truths of revelation.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A questioner asked about a punishment bound to happen.
interpretation: The questioner’s asking is a mocking challenge for the warned punishment to come; the verse declares that the punishment is decreed and will inevitably occur, as an answer that it is real and none can repel it from the disbelievers.

translation: For the disbelievers, there is none to avert it.
interpretation: This means that the punishment which the disbelievers have brought upon themselves by their rejection of faith cannot be turned away or blocked by any created being; when Allah’s decree comes, no power, intercessor, or false deity can repel it, and their denial will not save them from its reality.

translation: From Allah, Possessor of the ascending ways.
interpretation: This identifies Allah as the source of the inevitable punishment and describes Him as the Owner of the ma‘arij—the ascending paths and lofty degrees by which angels ascend to Him and by which His decrees descend. It affirms His exalted majesty, absolute sovereignty, and complete power over all ascent and descent, meaning that no one can repel or avert His judgment.

translation: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years.
interpretation: This verse describes the angels and the Spirit—understood here as Jibril (Gabriel)—ascending to Allah on the Day of Resurrection. The mention of fifty thousand years expresses the immense scale and duration of that Day when measured against worldly time, emphasizing its terror and severity for those who denied the truth, while Allah’s command, reckoning, and decree are exact and wholly beyond human time. It affirms the angels’ servitude and ascent to their Lord and establishes the reality of the Hereafter.

translation: So be patient with a beautiful patience.
interpretation: This command calls for steadfast endurance in the face of hardship, opposition, or delay, without letting the heart fall into panic, resentment, or despair. “Beautiful patience” is patience that is offered purely for God’s sake, free from complaining to people, questioning His wisdom, or seeking revenge, and joined with continued obedience and trust in His promise and timing.

translation: Indeed, they see it as far off.
interpretation: The deniers regard the promised resurrection and the coming punishment as remote—either impossible to happen or far away in time—because they measure only by worldly appearances and reject divine power, while in God's decree it is near and certain.

translation: And We see it near.
interpretation: This means that what the disbelievers regard as far off—the resurrection and the promised punishment—is, in God's knowledge and decree, near and certain to occur; its coming is not remote or doubtful, for He encompasses its appointed time and will bring it to pass.

translation: On the Day when the sky will be like molten brass.
interpretation: This describes the Day of Resurrection, when the sky will lose its familiar form and become a molten, boiling, formless mass. It conveys the overwhelming terror and cosmic upheaval of that Day, showing that the stable order of this world will collapse and that people will face God’s judgment with no worldly support remaining.

translation: And the mountains will be like wool.
interpretation: This describes the overwhelming transformation on the Day of Judgment: the mountains, though vast and seemingly firm, will become like soft, loose wool—easily torn apart, scattered, and blown away—showing the complete collapse of the worldly order and the certainty of resurrection.

translation: And no close friend will ask about another close friend.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the terror and personal accountability of every soul will be so overpowering that even the closest bonds of kinship and friendship will no longer move anyone to inquire about or plead for another; people will see and recognize one another, yet none will be able to help or intercede, because each is wholly consumed with his own fate.

translation: They will be made to see them. The criminal will wish that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by offering his children.
interpretation: On that Day, people will see their close relatives and companions, yet no bond will allow them to help one another. The wicked will be in such terror and regret that they would gladly surrender even their own children as a ransom to escape God's punishment. This reveals the overwhelming horror of the Hereafter and the utter helplessness of the guilty: nothing they possess, not even their dearest loved ones, can shield them from divine justice. Salvation lies solely in God's mercy, earned through faith and righteous action in the life of the world.

translation: and his spouse and his brother
interpretation: This refers to the terror of the guilty on the Day of Judgment: he will be so desperate to escape punishment that he would wish to offer even his closest loved ones—his spouse and his brother—as a ransom, yet no ransom will be accepted from him.

translation: And his clan that sheltered him
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the guilty will be so desperate to escape punishment that he would try to ransom himself even with his closest kin—those who gave him refuge, support, and protection in worldly life—but such relationships and loyalties will provide no deliverance then.

translation: and all who are on the earth, all together, then it would save him.
interpretation: This describes the criminal on the Day of Judgment wishing that he could ransom himself with every person on earth, thinking that such an impossible offering might rescue him from punishment. But no ransom will be accepted on that Day; nothing can deliver him except sincere faith in Allah and righteous deeds.

translation: No! Indeed, it is the Blazing Fire.
interpretation: This is a stern refutation of any hope of escape or evasion: the punishment is the blazing flame of Hell, called Laza, which burns with intensity and is made ready for the deniers and wrongdoers.

translation: A plucker/stripper of the scalp and limbs.
interpretation: It portrays the Fire of Hell as violently tearing away the skin, flesh, and extremities, inflicting continuous and severe punishment upon the rejecters; it emphasizes the intensity of the torment and the total helplessness of those cast into it.

translation: It calls whoever turned his back and went away.
interpretation: This means that the Fire summons the one who rejected the truth and turned away from it; such punishment overtakes those who deliberately withdraw from faith and obedience after being called to them.

translation: And he collected [wealth] and hoarded it.
interpretation: This describes the person who amasses wealth and tightly stores it away, withholding it from the poor and from spending in the way of Allah. His hoarding is a sign of greed and attachment to worldly possessions, which accompanies turning away from divine guidance and brings him under the warning of the Fire.

translation: Indeed, man was created anxious.
interpretation: This verse describes a fundamental weakness in human nature: a restless impatience, anxiety, and greed that makes a person quick to panic when hardship strikes and reluctant to give when prosperity comes. It is not a denial of human dignity, but a warning about the human tendency to be governed by fear and desire when left without faith, patience, and trust in God. The verse therefore points to the need for spiritual discipline, prayer, and reliance on God to refine and overcome this natural restlessness.

translation: When misfortune touches him, he is greatly distressed.
interpretation: This describes a blameworthy human tendency: when even a slight hardship or harm befalls him, he becomes overcome by impatience, panic, and despair, rather than remaining steadfast and trusting in God’s decree.

translation: And when good touches him, he is withholding.
interpretation: This verse condemns the human tendency to become miserly and ungrateful when blessed with ease, wealth, health, or any favor: instead of recognizing the blessing as from God, sharing it, and giving thanks, such a person withholds both wealth from others and gratitude from his Lord. It exposes a spiritual disease in which prosperity makes the self more tight-fisted rather than more generous, and it contrasts this blameworthy state with the character of the faithful, who remain thankful and open-handed whether in hardship or ease.

translation: Except those who pray
interpretation: This exception refers to the believers who perform prayer; their worship frees them from the destructive impatience, panic, and selfishness that otherwise characterize human beings, because prayer keeps them conscious of God, steadfast in hardship, and generous with His blessings.

translation: Those who are constant in their prayer.
interpretation: They observe their prescribed prayers with steadfastness and regularity, preserving their times, prerequisites, and essential parts, and not neglecting or abandoning them. This constancy reflects sincerity, God-consciousness, and a heart firmly turned toward God, making prayer a continuous and faithful practice throughout life.

translation: And those in whose wealth there is a known right.
interpretation: This verse describes a defining quality of the faithful: they recognize that a specific, obligatory portion of their wealth belongs by right to others, especially the needy. It is not merely optional generosity or a favor, but a fixed due placed in their wealth by God, instilling in them a constant sense of social responsibility and justice toward those in need.

translation: For the beggar and the deprived.
interpretation: This phrase establishes that in the wealth of the righteous there is a recognized right set aside for two groups: the one who openly asks for help, and the one who is deprived—whether because of poverty, loss, hardship, or being prevented from earning—even if they do not beg. It obligates the believer to acknowledge the needy person’s rightful share in wealth, not merely to offer optional charity.

translation: And those who believe in the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse describes the believers as those who affirm with certainty the reality of the Day of Recompense, when all deeds will be judged by God. That conviction is not merely intellectual; it shapes their worship, moral conduct, and sense of accountability, because they live in expectation of being held answerable for their choices.

translation: And those who are apprehensive of the punishment of their Lord
interpretation: This describes believers who live with a deep, reverent fear of their Lord’s punishment. Their fear is not despair or doubt in God’s mercy; rather, it is a state of God-consciousness that keeps them humble, cautious, and steadfast in obedience. They never treat themselves as safe from divine accountability, so this apprehension motivates them to repent, avoid sin, and seek their Lord’s pleasure.

translation: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something to be felt secure from.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true believers never consider themselves immune to God's punishment; they combine hope in His mercy with reverent fear of His wrath, recognizing that no one should feel completely safe from divine accountability.

translation: And those who guard their private parts
interpretation: This describes the believers who protect their chastity by keeping their sexual desires and acts within the limits Allah has prescribed, abstaining from all unlawful sexual relations and indecency, and preserving their modesty and moral purity.

translation: Except from their spouses or those whom their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sexual desire is not blameworthy in itself; blame applies only when it is pursued outside the lawful relationships God has sanctioned. Those who confine intimacy to spouses or, in the historical context of the revelation, those under their lawful authority are free from reproach, while transgression of those limits is what incurs blame.

translation: So whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse declares that anyone who seeks sexual gratification outside the limits Allah has made lawful has overstepped the divine bounds. Such people are described as 'al-'ādūn'—those who transgress, exceed limits, and wrongfully go beyond what God has permitted, thereby incurring blame and accountability.

translation: And those who are faithfully observant of their trusts and their covenant.
interpretation: This describes the believers as people who guard and fulfill every trust and covenant, whether it is a duty owed to God, a right belonging to people, something entrusted to their care, or a promise they have made. They do not betray, neglect, or break what has been placed in their keeping, because faithfulness in trusts and agreements is a sign of true faith and integrity.

translation: And those who stand firm by their testimonies
interpretation: They are steadfast in bearing witness to the truth, giving testimony honestly and accurately, not concealing or altering it, and fulfilling it as a trust before Allah, whether it is for or against themselves or others.

translation: And those who guard their prayers.
interpretation: This describes the believers who consistently preserve their ritual prayers, observing their appointed times, prerequisites, pillars, and obligations, and who do not neglect or waste them. Such guarding is a sign of sincere faith and God-consciousness, and it leads to success and the highest Paradise.

translation: Those are in Gardens, honored.
interpretation: This means that the people described as faithful and steadfast in worship will dwell in paradises where God grants them honor, dignity, and nearness to Him—an honor that surpasses every worldly distinction and remains forever.

translation: So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, hastening toward you,
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of the disbelievers who crowd and rush toward the Prophet with necks outstretched and eyes fixed, not out of sincere faith or willing submission, but out of mockery, denial, and contentiousness. Their haste is exposed as blameworthy because they draw near to hear or see the Messenger while still persisting in rejection of the truth; it is not the eager approach of true seekers, but the restless movement of those who oppose and dispute the message.

translation: From the right and from the left, in separate groups.
interpretation: This describes them as dispersed into factions on both sides, each group clinging to its own position and not united upon the truth. Their sitting in scattered bands around the Prophet reflects their division, confusion, and turning away from his call rather than gathering around guidance.

translation: Does every one of them aspire to enter the Garden of Bliss?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of censure and astonishment: how can each of these arrogant deniers hope to enter the Garden of Bliss while persisting in disbelief and opposition to the Messenger? Their aspiration is empty, based on wishful thinking, not on faith or righteous action. It affirms that Paradise is not granted merely by desire, group affiliation, or self-delusion; it is Allah’s gift to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and His judgment is perfectly just.

translation: No! Indeed, We created them from what they know.
interpretation: This is a decisive rebuke of the disbelievers’ arrogant hope: they do not enter Paradise by mere wishful thinking. Allah reminds them that He created them from the lowly seminal fluid they themselves know, so they have no grounds for pride or self-delusion. The One who originated them from such a substance is fully able to resurrect them and replace them, and success with Allah is not attained by claims and desires but by His will and the path He accepts.

translation: So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that indeed We are able.
interpretation: Allah swears by His lordship over every place and moment of sunrise and sunset—all directions, seasons, and cosmic order—to affirm that His power is absolute and limitless. The One who governs the rising and setting of the sun, moon, and stars, and the alternation of day and night, is surely capable of resurrecting, recreating, and bringing about whatever He wills; nothing in creation can frustrate His decree.

translation: To replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone.
interpretation: Allah affirms His absolute power over creation: He is fully able to remove those who persist in denial and bring forth a people better than them, and no one can escape His grasp, resist His will, or defeat His decree.

translation: So leave them to indulge in idle talk and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a consolation: the Prophet is told not to preoccupy himself with the mockery and vain disputes of those who reject the truth, for they are lost in fleeting amusement and heedlessness. They will inevitably face the promised Day—the Day of Resurrection and judgment—when their falsehoods and distractions will be exposed and they will be held accountable. The command to “leave them” is not an approval of their conduct but a declaration that their time is limited and that divine justice will certainly overtake them.

translation: On the Day they will emerge from the graves in haste, as if they were rushing to a goal.
interpretation: This verse depicts the overwhelming urgency and helplessness of resurrection: at God’s command, the dead will rise from their graves and move with frantic speed toward the place of gathering and judgment. Their hurried motion is likened to people racing toward a raised standard or goal, showing that the divine summons is irresistible and that no one can delay or turn aside; it underscores the certainty of the promised Day and the humiliation of those who denied it.

translation: Their eyes will be downcast, humiliation will overwhelm them. That is the Day which they were promised.
interpretation: This describes the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment: their gaze is lowered in shame and disgrace, and humiliation covers them as the punishment for their denial and arrogance. It is the very Day of Reckoning they were warned about in the world but refused to take seriously.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Indeed, We sent Noah to his people: “Warn your people before a painful punishment comes to them.”
interpretation: This verse opens Surah Nuh by declaring that Allah sent Noah to his people as a warner. The command “Warn your people” means Noah was to call them to repent, abandon idolatry, and obey Allah before the decreed painful punishment—the flood in this world and/or the chastisement of the Hereafter—overtook them. The sending of a warner before punishment is itself a manifestation of Allah’s mercy, giving people an opportunity to reform and be saved.

translation: He said: "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner."
interpretation: This is Noah addressing his people, declaring that he has been sent to them as a manifest warner: his message is plain and unambiguous, warning them of Allah's punishment if they persist in disbelief and calling them to turn back to Allah in repentance and obedience.

translation: That you should worship Allah, and fear Him, and obey me.
interpretation: This is a call from Prophet Nuh to his people, establishing the essence of true religion: to worship Allah alone, to live with taqwa—reverent awareness and fear of Him—and to obey His messenger. Worship affirms Allah’s exclusive right to be served; taqwa purifies the heart and behavior from disobedience; and obeying the messenger is the practical means of receiving and following divine guidance. Thus the verse directs people away from false gods and heedlessness toward sincere devotion, moral accountability, and adherence to prophetic instruction.

translation: He will forgive you of your sins and delay you to an appointed term. Indeed, when the term of Allah comes, it will not be delayed, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse explains that responding to the call of the messengers with faith and obedience brings two favors: forgiveness of sins and respite until a fixed term, allowing further opportunity for repentance and good deeds. But the appointed decree of Allah for every people is definite; when its time arrives, it cannot be postponed or averted. The phrase ‘if you only knew’ urges people to recognize this reality and not to let the delay deceive them into heedlessness.

translation: He said, “My Lord, indeed I have called my people night and day.”
interpretation: This is Prophet Nuh’s testimony before his Lord that he fulfilled his prophetic mission with tireless persistence, inviting his people to faith at every time and in every circumstance. Mentioning night and day shows that his call was continuous, patient, and all-encompassing, not limited to one moment or manner; he exhausted every opportunity to guide them, while placing the result with Allah alone.

translation: So my call did not increase them except in flight.
interpretation: This means that despite Prophet Nuh’s repeated invitation to them to worship Allah alone, their response was only further avoidance and rejection; the call exposed and intensified their aversion to the truth, making them flee from it rather than accept guidance.

translation: And indeed, every time I called them so that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were arrogant with great arrogance.
interpretation: This verse depicts a people whose rejection of the call to divine forgiveness is deliberate and progressive. They do not merely disagree; they shut down the means of hearing, hide themselves as if to avoid being seen with the truth, remain fixed in their former way, and answer the invitation with haughty self-exaltation. The sin described is not weakness or confusion but pride that refuses to submit even when forgiveness is offered. Noah’s repeated calling stands opposite their repeated refusal, showing that the obstacle is not the message’s clarity but the heart’s arrogance, which turns mercy itself into something to flee from.

translation: Then I called them openly,
interpretation: This statement expresses Noah's resolve to exhaust every means of conveying God's message: after calling his people privately and at all times, he then proclaimed the truth publicly and without concealment, so that the call would reach every ear and leave them without any plea of ignorance. It teaches that sincere advocacy of the truth requires persistent, varied, and fearless communication, and that the messenger's duty is to deliver the message clearly, while guidance ultimately rests with God.

translation: Then I announced to them publicly and I confided to them privately.
interpretation: Noah used every available mode of invitation: he addressed his people openly before groups, and he also approached them secretly, one by one, so that no one could plead ignorance and no heart would be left unsoftened. This reflects the wisdom and perseverance required in calling to God—varying one’s method between public warning and private counsel, and continuing despite rejection, out of sincere concern for their guidance.

translation: And I said: 'Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed, He is ever Forgiving.'
interpretation: Noah calls his people to repent and ask Allah to forgive their sins, reassuring them that Allah is Ghaffar—vastly and repeatedly forgiving—so no sincere seeker of forgiveness should despair of His mercy.

translation: He will send down upon you the sky in abundant rain.
interpretation: This is a promise that God will cause rain to descend from the sky plentifully and repeatedly, making it a means of provision, fertility, and blessing for those who turn to Him in repentance.

translation: And He will provide you with wealth and children and make for you gardens and make for you rivers.
interpretation: This is a promise of comprehensive worldly blessing tied to seeking God's forgiveness: He will not only send rain but also multiply wealth and offspring and grant fertile gardens with flowing rivers, showing that sincere repentance and obedience open the way to divine provision, family increase, and lush, life-giving abundance.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not fear Allah's majesty?
interpretation: This is a rebuke from Nuh to his people for failing to revere God as He deserves. It means: why are you not in awe of Allah's greatness, dignity, and power, and why do you not live with the awareness that He is the Sovereign Lord to whom you are accountable? The question exposes their heedlessness and calls them to restore reverence for God before it is too late.

translation: And indeed He created you in stages.
interpretation: This verse states that Allah created human beings through successive phases and gradual development, not all at once. It points to His wisdom, power, and care in forming and nurturing creation, and it also supports the reality of resurrection, since the One who originated human life in stages is fully able to bring it back to life. It calls people to reflect on their own creation, to be humble, and to recognize the purpose and accountability placed upon them.

translation: Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question urging people to reflect on the order and grandeur of creation. It reminds them that Allah alone, by His power and wisdom, arranged the heavens as seven superimposed layers, one above another, in perfect harmony. The verse calls the human mind to recognize the Creator through His signs and to submit to His lordship, for such organized creation could not come about by chance.

translation: And He made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp.
interpretation: This verse affirms that within the layered heavens Allah placed the moon as a luminous light and the sun as an illuminating lamp, showing His deliberate ordering of the celestial bodies: the moon gives reflected light suited to the night, while the sun is a blazing source of radiance and heat by which day, seasons, and the affairs of life are sustained.

translation: And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as a [kind of] growth.
interpretation: This verse affirms God's creative power and providential care: He originated human beings from the earth and causes them to develop, emerge, and be sustained through earthly means, comparable to how He brings forth vegetation. It also points to His ability to return them to the earth and bring them back to life from it for resurrection and reckoning.

translation: Then He will return you into it and bring you forth [from it] with a [new] bringing forth.
interpretation: This means that after death, Allah returns human beings into the earth—the same earth from which they were created—and then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will bring them out of their graves and raise them up again for judgment. The phrase emphasizes that this second emergence is certain, complete, and brought about directly by Allah’s power, just as the first creation and the return to the earth were.

translation: And Allah has made the earth for you a spreading carpet.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God, by His power and mercy, spread out the earth and made it a stable, level, and expansive surface suited for human residence, movement, cultivation, and the conduct of worldly affairs, so that people may live upon it with ease rather than being prevented by its original form or by its being unmanageable. It directs attention to God's providential ordering of creation and calls people to recognize His favor in making the earth serviceable for them.

translation: so that you may travel through it along wide paths.
interpretation: The verse means that Allah, by His mercy and power, made the earth traversable and provided broad routes and passes within it, so that people can move about, seek their livelihood, and reach their goals; it is a sign of His provision and a call to gratitude and obedience to Him.

translation: Noah said: “My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children only increase him in loss.”
interpretation: Noah’s complaint to God is not merely personal; it exposes a spiritual law: when people reject prophetic guidance and instead follow the wealthy and powerful who mistake God’s gifts of property and offspring for proof of superiority, those very blessings become instruments of greater ruin. The verse warns that worldly abundance is not a sign of divine approval; without faith and obedience, it hardens the heart, multiplies arrogance, and leads to perdition. It also portrays the prophet’s sorrow at seeing his people choose the company of those whose apparent success blinds them to the truth.

translation: And they plotted an immense plot.
interpretation: This refers to the disbelievers’ deliberate, deeply orchestrated scheming against Noah and his message. Their plot is described as “immense” because it was not a minor act of rejection but a massive, arrogant conspiracy aimed at entrenching disbelief, preserving their false idols and authority, and leading others away from the truth.

translation: And they said: Do not abandon your gods; and do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa, nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr.
interpretation: This verse exposes the entrenched idolatry of Noah’s people and the way their leaders urged one another to remain loyal to man-made deities. By naming specific idols, it shows that their rejection of Noah’s call was not vague but deliberately anchored in inherited objects of worship. Clinging to these false gods meant refusing the worship of Allah alone, and it illustrates how deeply devotion to created beings can blind people to the message of a prophet.

translation: And they have led many astray. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error.
interpretation: This is part of Noah’s supplication against his people after they persisted in idolatry and misled others. The verse means that the false gods they worshiped, or the leaders who called to them, caused many people to deviate from the truth. Noah then asks Allah not to grant the wrongdoers any increase except in misguidance. This is not arbitrary harm; it is a just consequence of their stubborn rejection, active spreading of falsehood, and refusal to heed warning. Since they chose misguidance and led others into it, their only growth is further distance from guidance, and their punishment matches the nature of their wrongdoing.

translation: Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a Fire, and they found no helpers for them besides Allah.
interpretation: This verse declares that the destruction of Nuh’s people was the direct consequence of their own sins, not an unjust punishment.
