Their drowning in the Flood was the worldly judgment, and their being made to enter the Fire immediately afterward signifies that the punishment continued into the next stage of existence. The sins that brought about their ruin also brought about the Fire. The phrase “besides Allah” denies any helper or protector from among the false gods they worshipped, their leaders, their wealth, or any created being. When Allah’s decree comes, none can repel it or independently intercede against it. The verse thus establishes personal accountability for sin, the gravity of rejecting a prophet’s call, and the exclusive power of Allah to punish or deliver.

translation: And Noah said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any dweller from among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This is Noah’s plea that God remove from the earth those who had fully committed themselves to disbelief and corruption, because their survival would only perpetuate rejection of God, spread moral ruin, and make it impossible for the truth to take root. It is not a request rooted in personal vengeance, but a recognition that a people who have exhausted every warning and still choose denial forfeit their right to remain as caretakers of the earth; their removal is both a just judgment and a mercy for the faithful remnant and for the future of pure worship.

translation: Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants, and they will not beget except wicked disbelievers.
interpretation: This is Noah's plea to God concerning his people after long preaching. It means that if they are spared, they will use their influence to lead others away from faith, and their descendants will inherit and perpetuate the same corruption and denial. The verse emphasizes that persistent disbelief can become generational, so protecting the faithful from its influence may require cutting off its source.

translation: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and the believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.
interpretation: This concluding supplication of Prophet Nuh teaches that true faith broadens the heart: one begins by seeking forgiveness for oneself, then for one’s parents, then for every believer who enters one’s household or sphere, and finally for all believing men and women. It also affirms that those who persist in wrongdoing and oppression will only find their path ending in loss and ruin, not in success; thus the believer’s mercy toward the faithful is paired with submission to God’s just judgment against entrenched evil.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say, "It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened, and they said, 'Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an.'"
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is divinely revealed to the Prophet Muhammad and that its miraculous nature is not limited to human recognition; the jinn also heard it and testified to its wondrous quality, indicating the universal scope of its message and the reality of unseen beings responding to divine guidance.

translation: It guides to the right course, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the Qur’an’s guidance leads directly to sound faith and pure monotheism. Whoever truly recognizes its guidance must respond with belief and must dedicate worship to God alone, rejecting every form of shirk—associating any person, power, or created thing with the Lord.

translation: And that He—exalted be the majesty of our Lord—has not taken a consort or a son.
interpretation: This verse declares Allah’s absolute transcendence and perfect oneness. His majesty and greatness are far above any need for a spouse, consort, or offspring. He is unlike created beings, who reproduce and depend on partners and children. Therefore, any claim that Allah has a wife or a son is false and incompatible with His divine nature; He alone is the Eternal, Self-Sufficient Lord, and worship is due to Him alone.

translation: And that our foolish one used to say against Allah an outrageous thing.
interpretation: This is a statement by the jinn who had heard the Qur’an, admitting that some among them—described as foolish—had spoken gravely false and excessive words about Allah, exceeding the proper bounds in describing Him, such as falsely attributing a wife or son to Him or speaking about Him without knowledge. It serves as a warning against reckless speech concerning Allah and shows the jinn’s correction of their earlier beliefs after accepting the truth.

translation: And we had thought that mankind and jinn would never utter a lie against Allah.
interpretation: This is a statement by the believing jinn, confessing their prior assumption that neither humans nor jinn would dare fabricate falsehood about Allah. After hearing the Qur’an, they realized that some among both groups had indeed invented lies concerning Him, such as attributing to Him offspring, partners, or other baseless claims. The verse thus exposes the folly of trusting human or jinn speculation about God apart from revealed truth, and it affirms that the Qur’an corrects such falsehood by declaring the truth about Allah’s oneness and majesty.

translation: And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in burden.
interpretation: This verse condemns the pre-Islamic practice of seeking protection from created beings, especially jinn, instead of Allah. In the days of ignorance, when a person stopped in a desolate place, he might seek refuge in the jinn of that place, believing they could protect him from harm. But such dependence only increased the jinn’s boldness and the humans’ fear, misguidance, and sin. The verse teaches that refuge, protection, and relief must be sought from Allah alone, and that turning to jinn for help leads only to greater burden and wrongdoing.

translation: And that they thought, as you thought, that Allah will not raise anyone (from the dead).
interpretation: This verse exposes the false assumption shared by the disbelievers among humankind and the jinn: that Allah would never resurrect the dead for judgment. Such a denial of the Hereafter is a root cause of rejecting divine accountability, messengers, and revelation. It warns that this thought is baseless, for Allah will certainly raise all creatures for reckoning.

translation: And we have sought to reach the heaven, but found it filled with strong guards and flaming stars.
interpretation: This is the jinn’s acknowledgment that their former attempts to ascend and eavesdrop on the heavenly realm have been blocked. The heaven is now protected by powerful angelic guards and shooting flames, preventing them from intercepting divine revelation. This signifies God’s safeguarding of the revelation sent to His Messenger, ensuring that the unseen news of prophethood remains protected and that the jinn cannot steal or distort it.

translation: And we used to sit therein in stations for hearing, but whoever listens now will find a burning flame lying in wait for him.
interpretation: This verse is spoken by the jinn, explaining that before the coming of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ they could ascend to certain positions in the sky and eavesdrop on some heavenly conversations. After the Prophet’s mission began, however, the heavens were strictly guarded, so any jinn who now tries to listen is met by a piercing flame prepared to drive him away. Its meaning is that divine revelation is protected from unauthorized access, and the unseen news of God is no longer left open to being stolen, mixed with falsehood, or conveyed by the jinn; the flaming guard is a sign of God’s safeguarding of the prophetic message.

translation: And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them a right path.
interpretation: This verse expresses the humility of conscious beings before God’s hidden decree. It teaches that when events in the world change or when access to unseen knowledge is closed, people cannot confidently judge whether the outcome is punishment, trial, or a merciful plan of guidance. Apparent harm may be a wake-up call, and apparent restriction may be protection or preparation for right guidance. The proper stance is not arrogance or panic, but reverence, repentance, and trust that God’s purpose may be to lead His servants to what is truly good, even when His wisdom is beyond human perception.

translation: And among us are the righteous, and among us are those less than that; we have been on divergent paths.
interpretation: This verse shows that the jinn, like humans, are morally accountable beings who differ in righteousness and belief. Their admission that some are righteous while others are not, and that they follow differing ways, indicates that they possess free will and are not all alike in guidance or deviation. It teaches that one's worth is determined by adherence to the truth, not by belonging to a particular group, and that diversity in creeds and conduct reflects choices made by individuals among both jinn and humankind.

translation: And we have become certain that we will never be able to escape Allah on earth, nor can we escape Him by flight.
interpretation: This verse declares the jinn’s acknowledgment of Allah’s absolute power and their total inability to evade Him. Neither remaining somewhere on earth nor fleeing from one place to another can remove a creature from Allah’s grasp, defeat His decree, or prevent His judgment. It affirms that all beings are subject to Allah’s sovereign will and cannot frustrate His purpose, so true safety lies only in submission and accountability before Him.

translation: And when we heard the guidance, we believed in it. So whoever believes in his Lord will not fear loss nor injustice.
interpretation: This states that true faith in the Lord brings security from two fears: that one’s good deeds will be diminished or unrewarded, and that one will be wronged, oppressed, or burdened beyond justice. The believer’s reward is safe with God, and God does not deal unjustly with those who turn to Him in sincere faith.

translation: And among us are those who submit [to Allah], and among us are the unjust deviators. So whoever submits [to Allah]—those have sought the right path.
interpretation: This verse declares that guidance is not secured by belonging to a particular kind or group; even among the jinn there are those who surrender to Allah and those who deviate into injustice. True success belongs to the one who submits to Allah, for such a person deliberately turns toward and seeks the straight, rightly guided way.

translation: And as for the deviators, they will be fuel for Hell.
interpretation: The "qasitun" are those who swerve away from the truth and from God's straight path, persisting in falsehood and injustice. Their end is Jahannam, where they become its fuel—an image of utter ruin, consumed by punishment, and deprived of guidance and mercy.

translation: And that if they had remained steadfast on the path, We would have given them abundant water.
interpretation: This means that if the jinn and humankind—or those addressed—had stood firm upon the straight path of faith and obedience to Allah, He would have granted them ample provision, symbolized by abundant water, the source of life and prosperity. The verse teaches that steadfastness on Allah’s path brings divine blessings, while abundant worldly gifts can also serve as a test, as the following verse indicates: “that We may test them thereby.” Thus true success is to remain upright whether in ease or hardship.

translation: That We may test them thereby; and whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will cause him to enter a severe, mounting punishment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly blessings, including abundant provision, are a divine trial, not proof of God's favor. The decisive danger is turning away from the remembrance of one's Lord—meaning neglect of faith, prayer, the Qur'an, gratitude, and obedience. For such a person, God will make the punishment enter him as something unbearable and escalating: 'صعدا' conveys a torment that rises, chokes, and intensifies. Thus, rejecting remembrance does not simply forfeit reward; it leads to an ongoing, mounting penalty that matches the soul's ascent in heedlessness.

translation: And that the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke alongside Allah anyone.
interpretation: This verse means that places of worship are to be dedicated exclusively to Allah, and therefore all acts of worship, supplication, and devotion must be directed to Him alone. It prohibits associating any partner with Allah in worship or calling upon anyone besides Him, since He alone is worthy of being invoked and worshipped.

translation: And when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost became upon him a compact mass.
interpretation: The servant of Allah is the Prophet Muhammad, and when he stood in worship invoking Allah alone, the jinn gathered around him in dense numbers, pressing close to listen to his recitation and supplication, so that they almost piled upon him layer upon layer. This shows how the call to pure monotheism drew the unseen creation to listen intently and how the Prophet’s worship had an overwhelming effect upon them.

translation: Say, 'I only call upon my Lord, and I associate no one with Him.'
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to declare that his worship, prayer, and supplication are directed exclusively to Allah alone, with no partner, idol, saint, or created being sharing in His divinity or right to be invoked. It establishes pure monotheism and the Prophet’s own servanthood, showing that he does not claim lordship or divine status but calls all people to the same exclusive devotion to the One God.

translation: Say, 'I do not possess for you any harm or right guidance.'
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to declare that he has no independent power to harm anyone or to guide anyone aright by his own will. All harm and all true guidance belong to Allah alone. The Prophet is only a servant and messenger who conveys the revelation; he cannot force belief, prevent punishment, or grant guidance from himself. Thus the verse establishes the absolute oneness of Allah’s authority and teaches that no created being—however exalted—should be relied upon for benefit or guidance apart from Allah.

translation: Say, "Indeed, no one can protect me from Allah, and I will never find besides Him any refuge."
interpretation: This verse declares that ultimate protection, shelter, and escape from divine judgment belong exclusively to Allah; no created being can shield anyone from His decree, and no refuge exists outside Him. The Prophet is commanded to announce this as a matter of absolute servitude, teaching that every soul must turn directly to God for safety, rely solely on Him, and seek His mercy, since all other presumed guardians are powerless.

translation: Except a proclamation from Allah and His messages. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed for him is the Fire of Hell, wherein they will abide forever.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the Messenger’s duty is solely to convey Allah’s revelation and warnings, not to force belief or exercise dominion over hearts. Therefore, rejecting the conveyed message is not merely rejecting a human preacher but disobeying Allah Himself, since the Messenger speaks by His authority. The eternal Fire is the just recompense for those who persist in that disobedience; the plural form “they will abide” gathers all such persons under one fate, showing that the warning applies to every individual and generation that knowingly turns away. Thus the verse marks the decisive line between heeding divine guidance and incurring permanent ruin.

translation: Until, when they see what they are promised, they will know who is weaker in supporter and fewer in number.
interpretation: This is a warning to those who reject the truth and boast in their numbers and allies. When the promised punishment comes into view, they will recognize that they themselves are the ones utterly weak and few: their false helpers cannot protect them, and their apparent strength collapses before God’s decree. True strength lies not in worldly count or support, but in God’s aid and in loyalty to Him.

translation: Say, 'I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will set for it an appointed term.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that knowledge of the timing of the promised event—especially the Hour and the fulfillment of divine warnings—belongs exclusively to God. The Prophet is commanded to declare his human limitation: he cannot know whether it is imminent or delayed by an appointed term known only to God. The meaning is that people should not demand or presume to know the unseen timing, but should live in readiness and trust that God’s decree will come to pass at the exact time He has set, according to His wisdom and justice.

translation: Knower of the unseen, He does not reveal His unseen to anyone.
interpretation: This affirms that the knowledge of the unseen belongs exclusively to God; no created being can discover, uncover, or claim access to it independently. It is His sovereign knowledge, and He alone decides whether and to whom any part of it is disclosed.

translation: Except whom He has approved of messengers, and indeed, He makes a guard proceed before him and behind him.
interpretation: This means that Allah alone possesses the knowledge of the unseen and does not disclose it to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has chosen and with whom He is pleased. He then places angelic guards before and behind that messenger, protecting the revelation from being intercepted, altered, or corrupted, so that it reaches him securely and he delivers it with certainty. Thus, access to the unseen is never by human or jinn pretension, but only by Allah’s permission, and the prophetic reception of revelation is divinely safeguarded.

translation: That He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; and He has encompassed whatever is with them and has enumerated all things in number.
interpretation: This verse affirms God's absolute knowledge, protection, and precise accounting. The phrase “that He may know” does not mean God acquires new knowledge, for His knowledge is eternal and all-encompassing; rather, it means that it becomes evident and established that the messengers have faithfully delivered the revelations of their Lord without omission or alteration. God surrounds all that is with them, meaning nothing in their outward or inward affairs escapes His knowledge, and He has counted everything exactly, meaning every deed, word, and circumstance is recorded and measured with perfect precision. Thus the verse assures that divine protection guarantees the conveyance of the message, and it warns that all people are fully within God's knowledge and will face exact accountability.

translation: O you who wraps himself [in clothing]
interpretation: This is a direct address to the Prophet Muhammad, who had wrapped himself in his cloak, calling him to arise and prepare for the immense responsibility of receiving and conveying the Qur'an, and signaling the beginning of the command to stand in prayer at night.

translation: Stand [in prayer] at night, except a little.
interpretation: Allah commands His Messenger to devote most of the night to standing in worship and recitation, leaving only a small portion for rest, so that the night becomes a means of spiritual strength and preparation for bearing the revelation.

translation: Half of it, or reduce from it a little.
interpretation: This gives latitude in the night prayer: the worshipper may devote half the night, or slightly less than half, to standing in prayer and reciting the Qur’an. The permitted reduction is a divine concession, showing that God does not intend hardship by worship; He seeks sincere, sustainable devotion rather than overburdening the soul.

translation: Or add to it, and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation.
interpretation: This gives permission to increase the night prayer beyond the portion already specified, and it commands that the Qur'an be recited in a slow, deliberate, and well-articulated manner, giving each letter its due and pondering its meanings, for such measured recitation nurtures the heart and deepens understanding.

translation: Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word.
interpretation: This refers to the Qur’an, which God would reveal to the Prophet: it is described as heavy because of its profound meanings, its majestic truths, its binding commands and prohibitions, and the grave responsibility of receiving, conveying, and living by it. Its weightiness also indicates the seriousness of the trust placed upon him and the need for divine support, patience, and steadfastness in fulfilling it.

translation: Indeed, the rising at night is more strenuous and more upright in speech.
interpretation: This verse means that voluntary prayer and recitation performed at night, after rising from sleep, have a stronger and deeper effect on the self and are more firmly established in devotion, because the night is quieter, distractions are fewer, and the heart is more attentive. It also means that recitation, supplication, and remembrance at night are more correct and upright in wording, being less mixed with heedlessness and more conducive to sincere focus before God.

translation: Indeed, you have during the day a long period of occupation.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet that his daytime is filled with extended duties and engagements, so night prayer is prescribed as a time of devotion; the verse acknowledges the many responsibilities that occupy him during the day.

translation: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion.
interpretation: This verse commands the believer to keep Allah’s name ever present in the heart and on the tongue through remembrance, and to dedicate oneself entirely to Him with sincere, exclusive devotion—freeing the heart from dependence on anything other than Allah and directing all worship, love, fear, and hope toward Him alone.

translation: Lord of the east and the west; there is no god but He, so take Him as your Trustee.
interpretation: Because He alone is the Lord and Sovereign over every direction, time, and place, and because there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, the verse directs the believer to place complete reliance, trust, and delegation of all affairs in Him alone. This trust is not passive; it is the confidence that His Lordship encompasses all things, so one turns to Him in worship, submits to His command, and depends on Him for protection, provision, and guidance.

translation: And be patient over what they say, and avoid them with a gracious avoidance.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet—and by extension the believers—to endure the false accusations, mockery, and harmful speech of opponents without responding with anger or vengeance. The command to “avoid them with a gracious avoidance” means to disengage from their harmful company and disputes in a dignified, peaceful way: not with hostility, insult, or severing ties in a manner that breeds more enmity, but with forbearance, restraint, and trust that God will judge and deal with their words. It teaches that patience and noble withdrawal are often better than arguing with those who are determined to reject and mock the truth.

translation: And leave Me with the deniers, those who possess worldly ease, and give them respite for a little while.
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning to those who reject the truth while enjoying wealth, comfort, and status. God commands the Prophet to leave them to Him and not preoccupy himself with avenging their mockery. Their prosperity is not proof of divine favor; it is only a brief respite before the punishment that will inevitably overtake them. Their enjoyment is temporary, and their denial will bring them to account before God.

translation: Indeed, with Us are shackles and a Hellfire.
interpretation: This is a severe warning from God to those who persist in denial and sin: He has prepared in His presence and by His authority chains that will bind them and a raging Hellfire that will punish them. It affirms that divine justice and the Hereafter are real, so no one should treat God’s warnings lightly or assume they can escape His grasp.

translation: And food that chokes, and a painful punishment.
interpretation: This is a description of the torment awaiting those who persist in denial and sin: their food will be such that it catches in the throat and cannot be swallowed, causing distress and choking, and alongside that they will suffer a painful, agonizing punishment.

translation: On the Day when the earth and the mountains will quake, and the mountains will become a heap of sand poured out.
interpretation: This verse portrays the terror and total dissolution of the Day of Judgment: the earth itself is convulsed, and the mountains—normally regarded as symbols of stability, permanence, and worldly power—are reduced to loose, shifting dunes of sand. Their collapse exposes the utter fragility of all created things before God’s command and shows that no material or geographical reality can serve as a refuge on that Day. It affirms the inevitability of resurrection and reckoning and calls humanity to recognize that only God’s authority endures.

translation: Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger.
interpretation: This verse warns the people addressed that God has sent Muhammad as His Messenger to convey the divine message and to serve as a witness over them: he will testify to what they were taught and how they responded—whether they believed and obeyed or denied and disobeyed. The comparison with Pharaoh emphasizes that rejecting God’s messenger is not a light matter; just as Moses was sent to Pharaoh as a clear messenger and Pharaoh’s rejection brought him ruin, so too will rejecting the Messenger sent to them bring severe accountability before God.

translation: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a severe seizure.
interpretation: This verse is a warning that rejecting Allah's messenger brings inevitable and devastating punishment. Pharaoh's disobedience to Moses was not merely a political rejection but a denial of divine guidance, and Allah's seizure of him was a severe, destructive penalty. It serves as a lesson for all who hear the truth and turn away: divine retribution is certain and proportionate to the gravity of rejecting the messenger.

translation: So how will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will make the children gray-haired?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical warning about the overwhelming terror of the Day of Judgment. If people persist in disbelief, they will have no protection from a day whose horrors are so severe that even children—normally untouched by the anxieties that turn hair gray—will be aged and whitened by fear. The verse awakens the conscience to the reality that safety on that day is not found in power, wealth, or denial, but only in faith, God-consciousness, and preparing for the meeting with Allah.

translation: The sky will be split asunder by it. His promise is ever fulfilled.
interpretation: This describes the overwhelming terror and reality of the Day of Judgment: the sky will crack open because of that Day. God’s promise to bring about the resurrection, reckoning, and final outcome is certain and will inevitably come to pass.

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills, let him take a way to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a reminder and admonition that awakens heedless hearts. It affirms that a person has the capacity to choose and that the path to God is open through faith, obedience, and seeking His pleasure. It does not compel; rather, it invites the willing to turn to their Lord, while ultimate guidance and success remain dependent on God’s will and grace.

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand in prayer for nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you. And Allah measures the night and the day. He knows that you will not be able to keep it exactly, so He has turned to you in mercy. So recite what is easy of the Qur'an. He knows that among you will be the sick, and others traveling through the land seeking the bounty of Allah, and others fighting in the cause of Allah. So recite what is easy of it, and establish prayer and give zakah and loan Allah a goodly loan. And whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find it with Allah — it is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse marks Allah’s merciful relaxation of the intense nightly prayer that the Prophet and some believers were initially undertaking. Allah, who perfectly apportions night and day, knows human weakness and the impossibility of maintaining such exacting devotion without hardship. Therefore He does not demand beyond capacity; He accepts His servants’ repentance and makes the recitation of the Qur’an in prayer easy according to ability. The verse then recognizes the varied circumstances of the community — illness, travel for lawful provision, and struggle in Allah’s cause — and so replaces an unbearable burden with obligations and virtues that remain within reach: reciting what one can, establishing the prescribed prayer, giving zakah, spending generously as a goodly loan to Allah, and seeking forgiveness. Its central meaning is that divine legislation is rooted in knowledge and mercy, and that whatever good a person sends ahead will be found with Allah as better and greater in reward, while returning to Allah in repentance opens the door to His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: O you who wraps himself [in clothing]!
interpretation: It is a divine address to the Prophet Muhammad, calling him out of his state of seclusion and wrapping, and signaling that his retreat is now to give way to the active duty of receiving and conveying the revelation.

translation: Arise and warn.
interpretation: This is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to rise with determination and convey the warning of Allah's punishment to humanity, calling them away from falsehood and toward the worship of Allah alone.

translation: And your Lord, magnify.
interpretation: This is a command to exalt and glorify God alone, acknowledging His supreme greatness and lordship, and to direct all worship, reverence, and obedience to Him exclusively.

translation: And purify your garments.
interpretation: This is a command to cleanse one’s clothing from physical impurity and to maintain outward purity, which reflects and supports inward purity of the heart and conduct, especially for one who is called to worship God and convey His message.

translation: And uncleanliness, avoid.
interpretation: This is a command to shun all spiritual and moral impurity, especially idolatry and sin, and to keep away from anything that defiles one’s faith or leads to divine punishment.

translation: And do not confer favor expecting to receive more.
interpretation: It forbids giving gifts, help, or kindness with the aim of getting a greater return, obligating people, or reminding them of one’s generosity. Such favor should be offered sincerely for God alone, not as a means of worldly gain or self-interest.

translation: And for your Lord, be patient.
interpretation: This means that endurance, perseverance, and steadfastness in carrying out the commands of God and facing hardship should be sought purely for the sake of your Lord, seeking His pleasure alone, not for worldly gain, reputation, or the favor of people.

translation: So when the horn is blown,
interpretation: This refers to the sounding of the trumpet/horn (al-Nāqūr) by the angel Isrāfīl at Allah’s command, signaling the end of this worldly life and the onset of resurrection and reckoning. It is a moment of great terror and upheaval, especially for those who denied the truth, as the following verse declares it a difficult Day.

translation: So that Day will be a difficult day.
interpretation: It denotes the Day of Resurrection, whose events are severe and terrifying, and it will be a day of hardship for the disbelievers because they will face the full consequence of their denial and sins.

translation: upon the disbelievers, not easy
interpretation: This describes the Day of Judgment as a severe and difficult day that will not be made light or easy for those who disbelieved. Their rejection of faith leaves them facing that hardship without relief or escape.

translation: Leave Me [to deal] with the one whom I created alone.
interpretation: This is a severe warning to the arrogant rejecter: Allah tells the Prophet to leave the matter to Him and not to concern himself with the man’s hostility. “ذرني” means “leave Me alone” to settle his affair. “ومن خلقت وحيدا” means the one whom Allah created solitary—without wealth, offspring, helpers, or any partner in his creation—and then He alone granted him favors. Since Allah alone created him and alone sustains him, He alone is sufficient to call him to account and punish him for his ingratitude and arrogance.

translation: And I gave him vast wealth.
interpretation: This means that Allah granted him abundant, extended riches—wealth that was not confined to a single sum but was continuous, plentiful, and expansive, as a test and favor, so that he might acknowledge Allah’s bounty and use it in obedience rather than in arrogance and denial.

translation: And sons who are present [with him].
interpretation: God had granted this man abundant wealth and many sons who remained present, attending him and strengthening his status and influence; the phrase shows how worldly blessings can become a means of pride and heedlessness when their recipient fails to thank God and submit to Him.

translation: And I made his path smooth for him with great ease.
interpretation: This means that Allah had granted him extensive worldly comfort and prepared for him the means of an easy, prosperous life—wealth, children, status, and influence—so that his affairs were smoothed out and expanded for him. It is a divine favor that should have led to gratitude and humility, not arrogance and denial of the truth.

translation: Then he hopes that I will increase [him].
interpretation: This verse censures the attitude of a person who, despite having been given ample worldly blessings, still greedily expects God to grant him even more. It exposes an insatiable sense of entitlement and ingratitude: his desire for increase is not a humble request for what he needs, but a defiant craving for endless worldly gain. The wording implies that God has already favored him greatly, yet he remains unsatisfied, so the verse highlights how wealth and power can lead a person to arrogance and blind greed rather than gratitude and submission to God.

translation: No! Indeed, he has been stubbornly hostile toward Our signs.
interpretation: This is a stern rebuke: the person is not excused by his claims or reasoning, for his real condition was obstinate rejection. He knowingly set himself against God’s revealed signs, refusing them not out of lack of evidence but out of arrogant defiance and entrenched resistance to the truth.

translation: I will soon burden him with a steep ascent.
interpretation: This is a severe threat of punishment: God will force this stubborn denier of revelation into an exhausting, painful climb in the Hereafter, a torment that never eases and from which he cannot escape or find relief.

translation: Indeed, he thought and calculated.
interpretation: This describes one who rejects the truth after pondering it and weighing it according to his own corrupt standards. His thinking was not sincere seeking of guidance; it was calculation and scheming to oppose the Prophet and discredit the revelation, showing that rejection can be a deliberate, self-serving decision rather than an honest conclusion.

translation: So may he be destroyed; how he determined!
interpretation: This is a divine curse and condemnation of the arrogant rejecter who deliberated and calculated how to oppose the truth. It declares that his scheming only brings ruin upon himself, and it exposes the futility and corruption of his judgment: however he tried to measure, plot, and devise, his estimation was false and could not avert God’s judgment.

translation: Then, may he be destroyed — how he determined!
interpretation: This is a divine curse and denunciation, repeated to intensify the condemnation. “قُتِلَ” here means “may he be doomed/destroyed” or “woe to him,” not a report of physical murder. “كيف قدر” is an exclamation of rebuke and amazement at the way he calculated and schemed against the revelation. The meaning is that his plotting was utterly futile, and by conspiring against the truth he brought ruin upon himself.

translation: Then he looked.
interpretation: This describes the disbeliever after he had pondered and determined to reject the revelation: he then cast his gaze again, inspecting the Prophet and the message in search of a fault or weakness to use against it, but he found no true grounds for rejection, only the arrogance that drove him to dismiss it.

translation: Then he frowned and scowled.
interpretation: This describes the arrogant rejecter of the truth after he had looked and reflected: instead of submitting to the clear message, he showed displeasure and contempt on his face. His frowning and scowling reveal that his rejection was not from lack of evidence but from pride, ill will, and a hardened heart. It is a rebuke of those who meet divine guidance with hostility and disdain rather than openness and humility.

translation: Then he turned away and was arrogant.
interpretation: This verse portrays the attitude of one who, after being confronted with the truth, rejects it not because it is unclear but because he is too proud to submit. His turning away is a deliberate withdrawal from faith, and his arrogance is the inner cause: he exalts himself above the message and refuses to humble himself before God.

translation: Then he said: This is nothing but magic handed down from old.
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbeliever’s obstinate rejection of the Qur’an: after being unable to meet its challenge, he dismisses it as sorcery allegedly inherited from earlier people. It signifies that denying revelation by labeling it transmitted magic is a baseless accusation arising from arrogance, not from evidence, and it warns that such rejection will not diminish the Qur’an’s divine truth.

translation: This is nothing but the speech of a human being.
interpretation: This verse reports the disbelievers’ rejection of the Qur’an, claiming it is merely human words rather than divine revelation. It exposes their denial and their refusal to accept that the message comes from God, reducing it to something produced by a person.

translation: I will cast him into Saqar.
interpretation: Saqar is one of the names of Hell; the verse is a declaration of divine punishment for the one who persists in denial and arrogance. The expression "sa'uslihi" carries the sense of being thrown into the Fire and made to endure its scorching torment, indicating that his punishment will be certain, severe, and inescapable.

translation: And what can make you know what Saqar is?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question meant to magnify the terror and gravity of Saqar: it declares that its true reality is beyond human estimation, so its horror can only be understood through Allah’s own description. It emphasizes that Saqar is one of the names of the Fire, a place of severe punishment whose intensity cannot be fully grasped by the human mind.

translation: It does not leave anything and does not spare.
interpretation: This describes the consuming severity of the Fire of Saqar: it destroys completely, leaving no flesh, bone, or remnant of those it seizes, and it spares none of them from its torment.

translation: Scorching the skin of human beings.
interpretation: This describes the Fire of Saqar as intensely burning and blackening human skin and flesh, causing severe torment. “Al-bashar” refers to humans in their physical, bodily form, and the verse emphasizes that the punishment reaches and consumes the very surface of their bodies, leaving them disfigured and suffering.

translation: Over it are nineteen.
interpretation: The pronoun refers to the Fire, Saqar, mentioned just before. The nineteen are the angelic keepers appointed over it, entrusted with guarding and administering it by God's command. Their precise number is a matter known to God and serves as a trial for people: it distinguishes those who accept revelation from those who dispute it, and it confirms the truth for those who believe, so that no one may object or doubt regarding the appointed guardians of the Fire.

translation: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve, so that those who were given the Book may be certain, and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Book and the believers may not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is a disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this example?" Thus Allah lets go astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it is nothing but a reminder to mankind.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the guardians of Hell are angels, not human beings, and that the specific number given is a divinely appointed test. For the People of the Book and the believers, it becomes a means of certainty and strengthened faith, removing doubt; for the hypocrites and disbelievers, it becomes an occasion for mockery and confusion, as they question why God would give such an example. Their differing reactions show that God's signs and decrees guide those who are disposed to accept the truth and leave astray those who are disposed to reject it, according to His will. Only God knows the full reality of His armies, and the revelation with its warnings is ultimately a reminder for all humanity to heed and believe.

translation: No! By the moon.
interpretation: This is a firm divine refutation of the disbelievers’ denial, followed by an oath sworn by the moon, which serves as a created sign testifying to God’s power and to the certainty of the warning and resurrection.

translation: And by the night when it departs,
interpretation: Allah swears by the night as it retreats and comes to an end, making it a sign of His power over the turning of time and the alternation of darkness and light. Just as the night inevitably passes away, the promise of resurrection and judgment is certain; the One able to end the night and bring the day is fully able to raise the dead and bring them to account.

translation: And by the morning when it shines.
interpretation: Allah swears by the dawn as its light spreads and the darkness recedes, pointing to His power to bring clarity after obscurity, life after death, and truth after falsehood.

translation: Indeed, it is one of the greatest [calamities].
interpretation: It emphasizes that the Hellfire, or the warning concerning it, is among the most tremendous and severe realities—a serious divine warning meant to awaken people to accountability and turn them back to God.

translation: A warning to humankind.
interpretation: This means that the message is a universal warning addressed to all human beings, calling them to heed divine guidance and be mindful of the consequences of their choices before God.

translation: For whoever among you wills to advance or lag behind.
interpretation: This verse declares that the warning and reminder are directed to every accountable person, and that each one has the choice to move forward toward faith, obedience, and good deeds, or to fall behind in disbelief, sin, and heedlessness. It affirms human free will and responsibility: divine guidance and warning are made clear, but the individual decides whether to advance toward salvation or retreat into ruin.

translation: Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned.
interpretation: This means that every individual is personally accountable for their deeds: their actions determine their fate, and no soul can escape the consequences of what it has chosen and done. The good it earns becomes a means of release and honor, while the evil it earns holds it bound until it is judged and recompensed.

translation: Except the companions of the right hand.
interpretation: They are the believers who will receive their records in their right hands on the Day of Judgment; they are secure from punishment and will enter Paradise.

translation: In gardens, they question one another.
interpretation: Their questioning is a sign of the perfect security and fellowship of Paradise: no longer anxious about their own fate, the righteous converse with one another in gratitude and awe, pondering God's favor and the justice by which He distinguishes the people of obedience from the people of ruin.

translation: about the criminals
interpretation: The phrase refers to speaking or asking concerning those who have willfully committed grave sins and rejected the truth, so that their end and condition become a subject of inquiry and a warning. "Al-mujrimīn" are the guilty who deserve punishment because of their persistent wrongdoing and denial of God's guidance.

translation: What has caused you to enter Saqar?
interpretation: This is a question of rebuke and reproach addressed to the inhabitants of Saqar, making clear that their entry into it was the direct consequence of their own deeds and choices, not injustice from God. It confronts them with personal accountability and the severity of Saqar as a place of punishment.

translation: They will say, "We were not of those who prayed."
interpretation: This verse conveys that the people of the Fire will confess that in their worldly life they did not belong to the community of those who consistently performed the prescribed prayer, and this abandonment of prayer is presented as a reason for their ruin, since prayer is the foremost act of worship that keeps a person mindful of God and accountable to Him.

translation: And we did not feed the poor.
interpretation: This is a confession by the people of the Fire that they withheld food and aid from the destitute, thereby neglecting a grave moral and social duty; it points to how refusal to care for the needy is a mark of the heedless and a cause of ruin.

translation: And we used to engage in idle talk along with those who engaged in idle talk.
interpretation: This is an admission by the people of the Fire that they joined in frivolous, false, and vain discourse, plunging into it alongside others who did the same. They did not restrain their tongues from mockery, lies, or arguments against the truth; rather, they followed the crowd in belittling revelation and the Hereafter. Their guilt is not only in private disbelief but in actively participating with those who corrupted speech and spread doubt, making them partners in the same heedlessness and deserving of the same punishment.

translation: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This is a confession by the people of Hell that they persistently rejected the truth of the Hereafter and the reality of divine accountability. Their denial was not merely intellectual doubt but a settled refusal to accept that they would be resurrected and judged, which enabled them to live without regard for God's commands and the moral consequences of their deeds.

translation: until there came to us the certainty.
interpretation: This refers to death as the unavoidable certainty: those who persisted in rejecting the truth continued in their denial until death overtook them, at which point the reality they had denied became inescapably clear, but too late for them to repent or amend.

translation: So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, no intercessor—whether prophet, angel, or anyone else—will be able to save those who persisted in disbelief and rejected the truth; intercession only occurs by Allah’s permission and benefits those whom He accepts, so it cannot rescue those who died rejecting Him.

translation: So what is [wrong] with them that they are turning away from the Reminder?
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke and expression of astonishment at those who reject the Qur’an: what excuse or justification do they have for turning away from the divine reminder and admonition, when it contains guidance, warning, and clear proofs? It censures their wilful aversion and urges them to examine why they avoid the message that would benefit them.

translation: As if they were frightened donkeys
interpretation: This simile describes those who turn away from the Qur’an and the Prophet’s warning: they flee from it in panic and aversion, like terrified donkeys stampeding from a predator. It conveys their irrational refusal to listen, their heedlessness, and their strong flight from guidance.

translation: fleeing from a lion
interpretation: This describes a panic-stricken flight from truth: those who reject the Qur’an turn away from its reminder as though a lion were pursuing them, showing that their aversion is not based on clear proof but on pride, fear, and a willful refusal to listen.

translation: Rather, every one of them wants to be given pages spread open.
interpretation: This verse exposes the disbelievers’ demand for direct, personalized written revelation as a condition for faith. Their wish is not a sincere search for truth, but an arrogant evasion: they want miraculous, individualized scriptures sent down to each of them, while rejecting the clear message already revealed through the Prophet. It shows that their insistence is rooted in stubbornness and a refusal to submit, not in a genuine lack of proof.

translation: No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the disbelievers’ arrogant demands and exposes the root cause of their stubbornness: they do not fear the Hereafter. Because they deny or disregard the coming accountability, punishment, and reward, they feel free to reject the Prophet and persist in disbelief; the absence of fear of the final judgment deadens their hearts to warning and reform.

translation: No! Indeed, it is a reminder.
interpretation: The emphatic rebuke rejects the disbelievers’ heedlessness and confirms that the Qur’an is an admonition that recalls people to their Lord. It is not something to be dismissed, but a clear reminder whose benefit is open to whoever wills to receive it.

translation: So whoever wills, let him remember it.
interpretation: This means that the Qur’an is an admonition and reminder; taking heed of it is left to the willing choice of the individual. Whoever chooses to pay attention can remember and benefit from it, yet such remembrance is not ultimately independent of Allah’s will.

translation: And they will not remember unless Allah wills. He is worthy of fear and worthy of forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse teaches that human guidance and remembrance of God are not achieved by human will alone; no one can take heed or turn to the truth unless Allah grants the will and ability to do so. It then describes Allah as the One who alone deserves to be feared and obeyed with taqwa, and the One who alone deserves to be asked for forgiveness. Thus it combines reverence of God with hope in His mercy: the believer should live conscious of God's majesty and accountability, while never despairing of His forgiveness.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate: I swear by the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: Allah swears by the Day of Resurrection to affirm its certainty and to impress upon the human being that the appointed Day of Judgment will undoubtedly come, when every soul will be held accountable and receive the consequences of its deeds.

translation: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul.
interpretation: Allah swears by the soul that blames and reproaches itself, meaning the human conscience that censures its owner for wrong done, for good neglected, or for shortcomings before God. This oath points to the inner moral witness placed within man, which testifies that deeds are accountable and that there is a coming reckoning, and it urges the soul to turn back from heedlessness to repentance and self-correction.

translation: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of the human being who doubts or denies the resurrection, implying that God is fully able to gather and reconstruct the bones after death and decay.

translation: Yes, We are able to put together in perfect order the very tips of his fingers.
interpretation: This affirms that God is fully capable of resurrecting and reconstructing the human body, even to the finest detail of the fingertips. It points to His absolute power over creation and re-creation, showing that nothing is beyond His ability, including the precise restoration of what distinguishes each person.

translation: Nay, man wishes to continue committing sin ahead of him.
interpretation: This means that the human being, driven by his own desire, wants to persist in disobedience and transgression in the time that lies ahead of him; he does not wish to stop sinning or prepare for accountability, and so he lives as though he will not be resurrected.

translation: He asks, "When is the Day of Resurrection?"
interpretation: This is a rebuke of the one who asks about the time of the Resurrection not out of sincere faith, but out of denial and mockery, seeking to evade accountability; the verse implies that the Resurrection is certain and that its knowledge belongs to Allah alone, so the question should lead one to prepare for it rather than reject it.

translation: So when the sight is dazzled and confounded.
interpretation: This describes the terror at the onset of the Resurrection: human perception is violently shaken, so the eye stares in stunned horror and fails to function normally, signaling that the inevitable Hour has begun and escape is impossible.

translation: And the moon will be eclipsed/darkened.
interpretation: This describes the moon losing its light and becoming dark on the Day of Resurrection, signaling the collapse of the familiar cosmic order and the onset of God’s final judgment.

translation: And the sun and the moon are joined together.
interpretation: This describes a cataclysmic sign of the Day of Judgment: the sun and moon, which in this world move in separate orbits and serve distinct functions, will be brought together and their ordered existence will collapse. It indicates the end of the physical universe as we know it and the certainty of resurrection, showing that all cosmic bodies are entirely subject to Allah’s command.

translation: That Day man will say, "Where is the escape?"
interpretation: This verse portrays the terror and despair of the human being on the Day of Resurrection, when the reality of judgment becomes undeniable. The one who was heedless or denied now searches desperately for any way out, but the question itself exposes his helplessness: there is no escape from Allah’s reckoning, no refuge from His decree, and no hiding place from the consequences of one’s deeds.

translation: No! There is no refuge.
interpretation: This is an emphatic declaration that on the Day of Resurrection there will be no place to flee, no shelter, and no protector to shield anyone from God's reckoning; every soul will be returned to its Lord for judgment.

translation: To your Lord, on that Day, is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse declares that on the Day of Resurrection every soul’s ultimate return, reckoning, and final abode are with God alone. It denies any real escape or protector on that Day and affirms that one’s true place of settlement is before the Lord, who alone judges and determines the eternal outcome.

translation: On that Day, man will be informed of what he sent ahead and what he left behind.
interpretation: This verse means that on the Day of Resurrection every human being will be made fully aware of all his deeds: the good and evil actions he performed and sent forward during his life, as well as the obligations, opportunities, and consequences he left behind, omitted, or deferred. Nothing will remain hidden from him; he will be confronted with the complete record of what he did and failed to do, so that accountability will be exact and just.

translation: Nay, man is a witness against himself.
interpretation: This means that every person has an inner awareness and record of his own deeds; his conscience, knowledge, and own faculties will testify to what he has done. Even if he denies or makes excuses, he cannot escape the truth about himself, and on the Day of Judgment he will be confronted by the evidence of his own self.

translation: even if he were to put forward his excuses
interpretation: On that Day, a person’s own self-awareness will testify to what he did, so any denial, justification, or excuse he presents will be useless and cannot conceal the truth from God.

translation: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it.
interpretation: This is a divine instruction to the Prophet not to rush the recitation of the Qur’an as it is being revealed, before the angel completes delivering it, out of eagerness to memorize it. It teaches that God Himself will preserve it in his heart and enable him to recite it correctly, so he should not hasten ahead of the revelation.

translation: Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.
interpretation: This is God's assurance that He Himself will gather the Qur'an in the Prophet's heart, preserve it in his memory, and enable him to recite it exactly as revealed; therefore its collection and recitation are guaranteed by God, not left to human effort alone.

translation: So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation.
interpretation: This is an address to the Prophet Muhammad: he should not rush to repeat the Qur’an before the angel Gabriel finishes delivering it. Once God has caused it to be recited to him in full, he is to receive it, follow it, and recite it exactly as it was recited, trusting that God will preserve, collect, and explain it.

translation: Then indeed, upon Us is its explanation.
interpretation: This verse is a divine guarantee that Allah Himself will clarify and explain the meanings of the Qur’an to the Prophet and, by extension, to those who receive it with attentive hearts. It teaches that true understanding of revelation is not attained through human haste or self-driven effort alone, but through humble reception and reliance upon God’s own exposition.

translation: No! But you love the immediate.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the human tendency to cling to what is immediate, fleeting, and gratifying in the present world, and to let that love override concern for the Hereafter. The emphatic negation rejects the excuses people make for denying accountability, while the correction identifies the real issue: the heart’s attachment to the passing and hastily sought over the enduring. It warns that when love is fixed on the “immediate,” one becomes willing to ignore truth, postpone repentance, and trade eternal consequence for temporary pleasure.

translation: and you neglect the Hereafter.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who become so absorbed in the fleeting pleasures and immediate demands of worldly life that they abandon concern for the eternal life, its accountability, and the preparation it requires.

translation: Faces on that Day will be radiant.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, the faces of the believers will be bright, fresh, and beaming with joy, expressing the inward happiness and hope they have in their Lord’s mercy and reward.

translation: Looking toward their Lord.
interpretation: This means that the blessed faces of the righteous will be gazing upon their Lord in the Hereafter, experiencing the vision of God as their highest joy and honor.

translation: And [some] faces on that Day will be frowning.
interpretation: This describes the faces of the disbelievers and sinners on the Day of Judgment as grim, scowling, and downcast, darkened by fear and despair as they await the punishment and crushing calamity they are certain will befall them.

translation: Thinking that a devastating calamity will be inflicted upon it.
interpretation: This describes the faces of the doomed on the Day of Resurrection: they are gloomy and downcast, certain that a back-breaking punishment is about to descend upon them. The word “faqirah” denotes a calamity so severe it breaks the spine, expressing utter dread and the hopeless expectation of ruin.

translation: No indeed! When it reaches the collarbones.
interpretation: This describes the moment when the soul reaches the throat/collarbones at death, the point at which worldly action and repentance come to an end and the reality of the Hereafter can no longer be denied or delayed.

translation: And it will be said, “Who can cure [him]?”
interpretation: This is a scene of the soul reaching the throat at death, when those present—or the angels—ask in desperation who can heal or save the dying person. It conveys complete helplessness before Allah’s decree: no doctor, charmer, or any created means can delay death or bring the soul back once its appointed time has come. The question exposes the limits of human power and turns attention to Allah alone as the One who controls life, death, and the soul’s journey to its Lord.

translation: And he will think that it is the parting.
interpretation: This describes the dying person at the moment the soul reaches the throat: he becomes convinced that this is the final separation—the parting from worldly life, from his loved ones, and from everything he possessed. It is the certainty that death is now inevitably severing all ties.

translation: And the leg is entwined with the leg.
interpretation: This describes the intensity of the death agony: as the soul reaches the throat, the dying person’s legs become joined, overlapped, or immobilized, signaling the collapse of the body and the end of worldly movement. It is the moment when his affairs are joined to the next life and he is driven onward to his Lord.

translation: To your Lord on that Day is the driving.
interpretation: This means that on the Day of Resurrection every soul will be inevitably driven and brought before its Lord for judgment, with no escape, delay, or alternative destination.

translation: So he neither accepted the truth nor prayed.
interpretation: This verse condemns the person who refuses to affirm the truth of God’s revelation and also abandons prayer, showing that rejection of faith and neglect of worship are joined together in his ruin.

translation: But he denied and turned away.
interpretation: This describes the person who rejects the truth and turns away from God’s command and guidance, refusing faith and obedience.

translation: Then he went to his family, swaggering.
interpretation: This depicts the arrogant disbeliever who, after rejecting the truth and turning away, returns to his household boastfully and self-satisfied, strutting as though he has triumphed; his manner exposes a deeper heedlessness of God, accountability, and the Hereafter.

translation: Woe to you, and woe!
interpretation: This is a severe divine threat of ruin and punishment, repeated for emphasis, addressed to the one who persists in denial and arrogance. It declares that destruction is what such a person deserves and is drawing near; it is a warning of the fitting and imminent consequence of rejecting faith and the Hereafter.

translation: Then woe to you, and woe to you.
interpretation: This is a severe, repeated divine threat of ruin and punishment for those who persist in denying the truth and turning away from Allah; the repetition intensifies the warning and affirms that such a person deserves imminent chastisement unless he repents.

translation: Does man think that he will be left neglected?
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to the human being who imagines that he has been created without a purpose, left without divine command or accountability, and will not be resurrected or judged. It affirms that human existence is not purposeless or abandoned; rather, God has created man with intent, will hold him accountable, and will bring him to the final reckoning.

translation: Was he not a drop of sperm emitted?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical reminder that the human being began as an insignificant drop of emitted semen, so the One who created him from such a humble origin is fully able to raise him again for judgment.

translation: Then he became a clinging clot; then He created and proportioned him.
interpretation: This verse describes a stage of human formation: after the drop, the embryo becomes an 'alaqah—a clinging, leech-like clot—and then God brings about its creation and harmonious proportioning. It points to God's deliberate, wise power in shaping the human being, forming the body and its faculties in balanced order as part of His ongoing creative care.

translation: Then He made from it the two mates, the male and the female.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah, from the single drop of sperm, brought forth both sexes—male and female—as a manifestation of His precise creative power. It serves as evidence that the One who can originate distinct genders from one fluid is fully able to bring the dead back to life.

translation: Is not that [God] able to give life to the dead?
interpretation: This rhetorical question is an affirmation of God’s absolute power: the One who created and fashioned human beings from the beginning is certainly able to bring them back to life after death, so the resurrection is not beyond His capacity but is a necessary expression of His creative power and justice.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing mentioned?
interpretation: This rhetorical question affirms that the human being passed through a prior state in which he had no existence, no name, and no mention among creation. It directs attention to Allah’s power to bring forth something from nothing and to elevate a creature from utter nonexistence to life, identity, and remembrance. The verse humbles man by reminding him that his existence, recognition, and standing are not intrinsic or self-derived but are granted by his Creator, and it calls him to reflect on his origin, purpose, and gratitude toward the One who brought him into being.

translation: Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture, testing him, and We made him hearing and seeing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that human beings are created from a lowly, mingled fluid, and that this creation is not without purpose: it is a trial. God grants hearing and sight as faculties by which a person receives revelation, perceives the signs in creation, and becomes accountable for how he responds. Thus the verse joins human origination from a weak substance with moral responsibility, showing that the same God who formed man also endowed him with senses that make the test meaningful.

translation: Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether he be grateful or ungrateful.
interpretation: God has shown every human being the path of truth and falsehood, providing revelation, reason, and prophets as means of guidance. This guidance is an invitation and clarification, not coercion; the human being is then free to respond either with gratitude, which leads to faith, obedience, and thankfulness to God, or with ingratitude, which leads to denial, rejection, and disobedience. The verse affirms both divine guidance and human responsibility: God does not force anyone onto the path, but He holds people accountable for how they respond to the guidance He has granted.

translation: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, shackles, and a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who knowingly reject God and His message will face severe, humiliating punishment in the Hereafter: chains and shackles symbolize their captivity and loss of freedom, while the blazing Fire represents intense, lasting torment. It emphasizes that this recompense is already prepared and certain, and it serves as a sober warning to turn away from disbelief before that Day.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor.
interpretation: This verse describes the honor and bliss of the righteous in Paradise: they will drink from a cup of pure delight whose blend includes camphor, a fragrant and cooling substance, symbolizing refreshing purity, pleasure, and divine reward for their piety in the worldly life.

translation: A spring from which the servants of Allah drink, causing it to gush forth abundantly.
interpretation: This describes one of the springs of Paradise, reserved for God's devoted servants, who drink from it and are able to make it flow and burst forth wherever they wish with effortless abundance. The emphatic wording 'tafjeeran' conveys that its flow is vast, continuous, and placed at their disposal as an honor and reward from Allah.

translation: They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread.
interpretation: This describes the righteous as people who keep the commitments and vows they make, especially those made to Allah, and who are deeply mindful of the Day of Judgment, when its hardship, terror, and punishment will spread far and wide. Their faithfulness in fulfilling vows is joined with reverent fear of that overwhelming Day, showing that true devotion combines obedience in this life with accountability before Allah in the Hereafter.

translation: And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive.
interpretation: This describes sincere, selfless charity: they part with what they themselves love and need in order to feed the poor, the orphan, and the prisoner, seeking only God's pleasure and not any human reward. It teaches that true righteousness is shown by sacrificing for the vulnerable and helpless, even for those who may have no claim upon them or may be regarded as enemies.

translation: We feed you only for the sake of Allah; we desire from you neither reward nor gratitude.
interpretation: This verse expresses sincere devotion in giving: the righteous feed others purely seeking Allah’s pleasure, not expecting any return, compensation, or even verbal appreciation from those they help. It teaches that true charity is freed from self-interest and social validation, directed solely to God.

translation: Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning, grim and severe.
interpretation: This describes the righteous servants of Allah who perform acts of charity solely for His sake and out of fear of the Day of Judgment, a day whose horror and severity will make faces frown and expressions grim. They dread that day’s harshness and distress, so they seek Allah’s protection by obeying Him and showing compassion to others.

translation: So Allah protected them from the evil of that Day and granted them radiance and joy.
interpretation: This means that God, in His mercy, shielded the righteous from the punishment, terror, and distress of the Day of Judgment, and in place of fear He gave them a luminous beauty on their faces and a deep happiness in their hearts.

translation: And He rewarded them for their patience with a Garden and silk.
interpretation: God grants the believers Paradise and silk garments as recompense for their steadfast patience in obeying Him, restraining themselves from sin, and enduring the trials of worldly life.

translation: Reclining therein upon couches, they will not see therein any sun nor any bitter cold.
interpretation: This describes the people of Paradise as resting securely on elevated couches in perfect comfort, where the climate is entirely temperate: they are spared both the heat and glare of the sun and the harshness of extreme cold, so their dwelling is one of unbroken ease and delight.

translation: And its shade will be near above them, and its fruit clusters will be lowered within easy reach.
interpretation: This verse depicts the perfect, effortless comfort of Paradise. The nearness of the shade means the righteous will be continuously sheltered and refreshed without having to seek relief or endure exposure, and the lowered clusters mean that the fruits of Paradise are not withheld by height, distance, or labor. The emphatic wording “tadhlīlan” stresses that this accessibility is complete and assured: creation itself is made submissive to the ease and enjoyment of the people of Paradise. It points to God’s generosity in the hereafter as not only abundant but intimate, dignified, and free from the toil and limitation that accompany worldly blessings.

translation: And there will be passed around them vessels of silver and cups that are crystal-clear.
interpretation: This verse depicts one of the delights of Paradise: servants circulate among the righteous with drinking vessels and goblets made of silver, yet these cups have the transparency and purity of crystal. It signifies that the people of Paradise are honored with continuous service and surrounded by vessels of extraordinary beauty and value—precious like silver, clear like glass—as a reward from God and a sign of the perfection and purity of the eternal abode.

translation: Crystal vessels of silver, which they have measured with precise measure.
interpretation: These vessels of Paradise are made of silver yet are as clear and luminous as crystal, and they are apportioned with perfect exactness—neither excessive nor deficient—according to the desire or need of those who drink from them. This signifies the perfection, purity, and meticulously ordered provision of Paradise, where every delight is granted in just measure by divine arrangement.

translation: And they will be given therein a cup whose mixture is ginger.
interpretation: The people of Paradise are served a drink blended with ginger, indicating the excellence and desirability of the beverage, since ginger imparts a pleasing flavor and aroma; it signifies the honor, purity, and complete bliss that Allah grants to the righteous.

translation: A spring therein, called Salsabil.
interpretation: It is a spring in Paradise whose water is sweet, pure, and smooth-flowing, made easy and pleasant to drink for the people of Paradise, and it is named Salsabil.

translation: And immortal youths will circulate among them; when you see them, you would think them to be scattered pearls.
interpretation: This describes the servants of the people of Paradise as youthful beings kept forever in that state, never aging or passing away. Their appearance is so luminous, pure, and beautiful that, as they move about serving the believers, they resemble pearls scattered across a surface—precious, radiant, and abundant. The image conveys perfect service, enduring freshness, and the exquisite splendor of Paradise.

translation: And when you look there, you will see bliss and a great kingdom.
interpretation: This describes the reward of the righteous in Paradise: wherever their gaze falls, they encounter divine favor that never diminishes and an exalted dominion that surpasses every earthly kingdom. It signifies that God’s generosity in the Hereafter grants believers both perfect delight and enduring honor, a station of nearness and dignity whose reality cannot be fully grasped in this world.

translation: Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink.
interpretation: This verse signifies the highest honor and purification of the people of Paradise: their green silk and brocade garments represent dignity and untarnished delight, their silver bracelets represent reward and beauty, and the pure drink given directly by their Lord symbolizes a spiritual cleansing that removes every trace of impurity, grief, and worldly defect, making their joy complete and their nearness to God unspoiled.

translation: Indeed, this is a reward for you, and your striving has been appreciated.
interpretation: Allah informs the people of Paradise that the bliss and honor they are experiencing is a recompense for their deeds in the worldly life, and He reassures them that their efforts in faith, obedience, and righteous action were not overlooked or wasted; rather, they were accepted, valued, and generously rewarded.

translation: Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur’an in gradual revelation.
interpretation: Allah affirms with emphatic wording that the Qur’an is His own revelation, not a human composition, and that He sent it down to the Prophet in stages according to divine wisdom. This gradual descent strengthened the Prophet’s heart, made the revelation easier to receive, preserve, and apply, and allowed guidance to address events and needs as they arose. It also establishes the Qur’an’s divine authority and the Prophet’s role as the recipient and conveyer of Allah’s message.

translation: So be patient for the command of your Lord, and do not obey any sinner or disbeliever among them.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet and the believers to remain steadfast and patient in carrying out God's command and in accepting His decree, and it warns them not to yield to the influence, demands, or counsel of those who are immersed in sin or in denial of God. Patience here is not passive resignation but faithful perseverance in obedience and truth, especially when opposed by the corrupt and the ungrateful. The verse thus establishes that divine guidance takes precedence over human pressure, and that believers must not compromise their commitment to God's rule by following any sinful or unbelieving person, even if such people hold power, prominence, or social influence.

translation: And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening.
interpretation: This command establishes the believer’s life on continual remembrance of God at both ends of the day: beginning with the early morning and closing with the late afternoon or evening. It teaches that devotion to God is not limited to a single ritual moment but is to be renewed regularly, so that the heart remains attached to its Lord, the tongue stays moist with His praise, and one’s conduct is shaped by awareness of Him throughout the day and night.

translation: And during part of the night prostrate to Him and glorify Him throughout the long night.
