interpretation: This verse means that the Qur’an’s reminder and guidance benefit those who willingly choose to seek the straight path. It affirms that God’s invitation is open to every person, but a person must intend and desire uprightness—faith in God, obedience to Him, and steadfastness on the truth—for that guidance to take effect in their life.

translation: And you do not will except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes that human will is subordinate to Allah’s will: no person can will, choose, or accomplish anything unless it falls within what Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all creation, has willed. His will is comprehensive and sovereign over every world, so all created intentions and actions remain dependent upon His decree and permission.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. When the sky is split open.
interpretation: This verse opens Surah al-Infitar with a terrifying cosmic sign of the Hour: the sky, which appears stable and seamless, will be rent apart by Allah's command. It announces the end of the present order and the certainty of resurrection and judgment, calling humanity to heed that all worldly power and security will dissolve before God's decree.

translation: And when the stars are scattered,
interpretation: This describes the cosmic dissolution at the onset of the Day of Judgment: the stars, once fixed in ordered orbits, are torn from their positions and dispersed, signaling the collapse of the created universe and the transition to the Hereafter.

translation: And when the seas are burst open,
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will shatter the barriers that contain the oceans, causing their waters to surge, overflow, and merge, so that the seas lose their present order and become part of the overwhelming cosmic disruption before resurrection and reckoning.

translation: And when the graves are overturned
interpretation: This describes the resurrection: the graves are opened, their contents are brought out, and the dead are raised from them for reckoning.

translation: Every soul will know what it has sent ahead and what it has left behind.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, each person will be made fully aware of the record of their own deeds—what they did earlier and later, what they offered for the Hereafter, and what consequences or omissions they left behind. This awareness is a decisive moment of accountability: no one will be able to deny or forget what they chose, and every action will be seen in its true reality before God.

translation: O man, what has deluded you concerning your Lord, the Most Generous?
interpretation: This is a rebuke and a question of astonishment: what caused you to be heedless, ungrateful, or defiant toward your Lord, the Most Generous, whose abundant bounty and forbearance should have drawn you to gratitude, humility, and obedience rather than transgression?

translation: Who created you, then proportioned you, then made you upright.
interpretation: This verse points to Allah’s creative care: He brought the human being into existence, shaped and completed his form, and arranged his limbs and faculties in balanced order so that he stands erect and functions with harmony. Recognizing this should awaken humility and gratitude rather than heedlessness toward the Creator.

translation: In whatever form He willed, He composed you.
interpretation: This verse declares that Allah alone, by His wisdom and unrestricted will, fashioned and assembled each human being in the particular physical form and appearance He chose. It reminds man that his shape, features, and constitution are neither self-created nor a matter of his own choice, but a sign of Allah's power and favor, and therefore a call to humility and gratitude rather than heedlessness.

translation: No! Rather, you deny the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse rebukes human beings for their heedlessness: despite God’s favors and signs, they reject the truth of final accountability. The word “al-din” here means the Day of Recompense, so their denial of it is the root of their wrongdoing, because whoever rejects the reckoning lives as though no judgment awaits them.

translation: And indeed, over you are guardians.
interpretation: This verse affirms that every person is placed under the watchful guardianship of appointed angels who observe and record all deeds, so that no action is lost and every soul will be held accountable before Allah.

translation: Noble, recording scribes.
interpretation: These are the honored angels appointed by God to record the deeds of human beings. They are noble in rank and character, and they faithfully write down everything a person does, so that each soul will be held accountable for its actions.

translation: They know whatever you do.
interpretation: The appointed recording angels are fully aware of all your deeds, good and evil, and they preserve them exactly, so no action is hidden from God’s account and every person will be held accountable for what they have done.

translation: Indeed, the righteous are in bliss.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who are truly righteous—those whose faith is sincere and whose deeds conform to God's guidance—will ultimately abide in enduring happiness and divine favor, enjoying the reward of Paradise and the pleasure of God.

translation: And indeed, the wicked are in Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse declares that those who persist in sin, disbelief, and moral corruption are inevitably destined for the blazing Fire of punishment. Their being “in” it expresses the certainty of their recompense and the reality that their evil deeds already lead them toward that end, while God’s justice will fully manifest it in the Hereafter.

translation: They will burn therein on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse means that the wicked and disbelievers will be made to enter the Fire and suffer its burning on the Day of Recompense. "يصلونها" comes from experiencing the heat of the Fire, indicating that their punishment will be actual, severe, and unavoidable. "يوم الدين" is the Day when God will judge all creation with perfect justice, recompensing every person according to their deeds. Thus the verse warns that the punishment of the wicked is not delayed indefinitely but is fixed for the Day of Judgment, when no one will escape God's judgment.

translation: And they will not be absent from it.
interpretation: The pronoun “it” refers to the Fire. The verse means that they will not be away from it, will not escape it, and will not be released from it; they will remain present in its punishment.

translation: And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of magnification and awe, declaring that the true reality, terror, and grandeur of the Day of Judgment are beyond human comprehension; only Allah can convey its full significance, and the verse serves as a solemn warning to prepare for the inevitable reckoning.

translation: Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question of magnification and warning. It emphasizes that the Day of Judgment is so tremendous and beyond human comprehension that its reality cannot be fully grasped except by God’s informing. The repetition intensifies the awe, certainty, and urgency of that Day, pressing the listener to take its reckoning seriously and prepare for it.

translation: The Day when no soul will have any power to do anything for another, and the command that Day will belong to Allah.
interpretation: This verse teaches that on the Day of Judgment every created being will be utterly powerless to benefit, harm, or intercede for another. Any claim that someone or something could decide, protect, or save independently of Allah will be shown to be false. All authority, judgment, and command that Day belong exclusively to Allah, so help, forgiveness, and salvation come only from Him and by His permission.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Woe to the defrauders.
interpretation: The declaration of woe is a divine threat of ruin, loss, and severe punishment directed at those who cheat by taking their due in full while withholding what is owed to others. It condemns the inward corruption that treats fairness as optional and turns trust into an opportunity for exploitation. This warning reaches beyond commerce to every form of dishonesty, injustice, and self-serving manipulation, teaching that God’s justice is exact and that faith requires honesty, equity, and fidelity in all dealings.

translation: Those who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full.
interpretation: This verse describes the unjust merchant or transactor who is exacting and demanding when receiving what is due to him from others, ensuring he gets his full measure or weight without any reduction, yet is not equally fair when giving others their due. It condemns the double standard in dealings: strictness in claiming one’s own rights while neglecting the rights of others, which is a form of fraud and injustice in commercial and social transactions.

translation: And when they measure or weigh for them, they give them less.
interpretation: This verse condemns a double standard in human dealings: people who demand their full rights from others become unjust when they owe others, reducing measure or weight to take what is not theirs. It teaches that faith requires consistent honesty, justice, and fairness in all transactions, and that exploiting others while insisting on one’s own rights is a grave moral corruption.

translation: Do not those [people] think that they will be resurrected?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke and warning: it censures heedlessness of the Hereafter and treats belief in resurrection as a moral safeguard. If a person truly considers that they will be raised and held accountable, they will not persist in injustice, deception, or taking what is not rightfully theirs. The verse implies that neglecting the thought of resurrection hardens the conscience and leads to worldly greed and wrongdoing, while remembering it calls the soul to honesty, justice, and responsibility before God.

translation: For a great Day.
interpretation: This refers to the Day of Resurrection and Judgment, which is great because of its magnitude, its terrors, the gathering of all creatures, and the reckoning and recompense that will take place in it. It is mentioned as a warning that people will be raised not for a trivial matter but for an immense and momentous Day.

translation: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection, when all people will rise from their graves and stand before God, the Lord and Sustainer of all creation, for judgment and accountability. It emphasizes that every human being will be brought before Him, fully subject to His authority, and will have to answer for their deeds.

translation: No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is surely in Sijjin.
interpretation: This is a decisive warning that the deeds of those who persist in transgression are not lost or ignored; they are inscribed and held in Sijjin, a register and place of lowest confinement and degradation. It signifies that the wicked are trapped by their own evil, their record is kept among the doomed, and their end is humiliation and punishment rather than escape or honor. The verse thus affirms divine justice: corruption, defiance, and sin are recorded in the lowest depth, from which no purity or deliverance can come for those who choose that path.

translation: And what can make you know what Sijjin is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the terrifying and grave reality of Sijjin: the register of the wicked in the lowest depths, where their evil deeds are recorded and from which their punishment and ruin proceed.

translation: A book inscribed.
interpretation: It is the written record of the deeds of the wicked, set down and sealed in Sijjin, in which every action is precisely recorded without omission, and which will be brought forth as evidence against them on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Woe on that Day to the deniers!
interpretation: This is a severe threat of ruin, punishment, and regret on the Day of Judgment for those who reject God's signs, His messengers, and the truth of resurrection and accountability; their denial will then bring them utter loss.

translation: Those who deny the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This describes those who reject the reality of the final reckoning and divine accountability, denying that there will be a Day when deeds are judged and every soul is repaid. Their denial is not merely intellectual doubt but a deliberate rejection of the truth that should govern their conduct, making them heedless of God's judgment and emboldening them in wrongdoing.

translation: And none denies it except every transgressor, sinful one.
interpretation: Denial of the Day of Reckoning is presented here not as an honest intellectual conclusion but as the fruit of a corrupted moral state. The one who habitually exceeds God’s limits and is steeped in sin finds the prospect of accountability unbearable, so he rejects it in order to justify his rebellion. The pairing “transgressor, sinful one” shows that this rejection springs from both active violation of divine bounds and an ingrained attachment to wrongdoing; thus the verse warns that persistence in sin darkens the heart until it denies the very truth that demands repentance and reform.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Legends of the former peoples.”
interpretation: This verse condemns the one who, upon hearing God’s revealed signs, dismisses them as mere ancient fables instead of reflecting on their truth. It exposes a willful rejection rooted in arrogance: the recitation is not met with reasoned objection but with a belittling label, showing that the heart has turned away from guidance and seeks pretexts to avoid submission.

translation: No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts with rust.
interpretation: This verse means that persistent sin and denial gradually stain and corrode the heart, covering it so that truth cannot enter and guidance cannot be received. Their own actions—what they chose to earn—are the cause of this spiritual blindness, not any injustice from God.

translation: No! Indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord on that Day.
interpretation: This verse declares that the ultimate deprivation for those who rejected faith is separation from their Lord: on the Day of Judgment they will be screened off from seeing Him, as a just consequence of their heedlessness and denial in the world. It implies that the greatest honor for the righteous is nearness to Allah and beholding Him, while the deepest punishment and disgrace is to be veiled from Him.

translation: Then indeed they will be burned in Hellfire.
interpretation: Their being veiled from their Lord is followed by the inevitable torment of the blazing Fire; the emphatic "then" and "indeed" show that this punishment is certain, just, and inescapable for those who persistently rejected the truth and were consumed by their own deeds.

translation: Then it will be said: This is what you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to the rejecters after they have been delivered to the punishment: the very reality they mocked and rejected in worldly life—the warning of resurrection, judgment, and the Fire—is now disclosed as true, and they are made to taste the consequence of their denial. It shows that denying the truth does not cancel it; it only makes its arrival more painful and inescapable.

translation: No! Indeed, the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyun.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the deeds of the righteous are preserved in the highest, most exalted register, 'Illiyyun, meaning God honors them, safeguards their record, and places them in the loftiest station of nearness and reward. The emphatic 'No!' refutes any notion that the righteous are overlooked or that their deeds are lost, and it establishes that true worth is measured by God's exalted record, not by worldly standing.

translation: And what can make you know what 'Illiyyun is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question conveys the immense loftiness and sublimity of 'Illiyyun: its true station and reality are beyond the grasp of human knowledge, and only Allah fully knows its greatness. It denotes the exalted record or high place in which the deeds of the righteous are inscribed, emphasizing honor, elevation, and nearness to Allah.

translation: A written record.
interpretation: It means the register of deeds is clearly inscribed and fixed, with every action precisely recorded, so that nothing can be added, omitted, altered, or concealed.

translation: The ones brought near [to Allah] witness it.
interpretation: This means that the record of the righteous is attested and observed by the angels who are nearest to Allah, showing its truth, honor, and exalted station, and that the deeds of the righteous are not hidden but are known and witnessed in the highest assembly.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.
interpretation: This verse is an emphatic promise that those who are truly righteous—firm in faith, obedient to Allah, and upright in their dealings—will abide in everlasting bliss in the Hereafter. The term “naʿīm” denotes comprehensive delight: the pleasure of Allah, security, peace, and joys of both soul and body that surpass all worldly understanding. Their being “in bliss” indicates that this state is settled, lasting, and all-encompassing, not a temporary or partial enjoyment.

translation: Upon couches, they will be looking on.
interpretation: This describes the righteous in Paradise reclining on elevated, adorned couches, gazing with joy and serene contentment at the bounties, honors, and delights that God has granted them.

translation: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss.
interpretation: This means that the delight and honor God has granted them will be visible on their faces as a clear brightness, freshness, and joy, so that anyone who sees them will know they are among the people of lasting favor and happiness.

translation: They will be given to drink from a sealed pure wine.
interpretation: This describes one of the honors of Paradise: the righteous will be served a pure, refined drink that is sealed. The sealing signifies that it is preserved, untouched, and reserved exclusively for those for whom it has been prepared; it is a mark of purity, dignity, and divine favor, unlike any worldly drink.

translation: Its seal is musk; and for that let the competitors compete.
interpretation: This verse urges people to strive and compete for the eternal delights of Paradise, whose pure drink is sealed with the fragrance of musk. The true competition worth engaging in is not for worldly wealth, status, or pleasure, which pass away, but for God's pleasure, nearness to Him, and the everlasting reward He has prepared for the righteous. So the one who wishes to compete should direct his ambition, energy, and rivalry toward good deeds and the path that leads to that supreme success.

translation: And its mixture is from Tasnim.
interpretation: This denotes that the pure drink of Paradise is blended with water from Tasnim, the most exalted and choicest spring, reserved for those brought near to Allah. Its use as a mixture for the righteous shows the honor, purity, and high favor bestowed upon them, and that their reward is drawn from the noblest source.

translation: A spring from which those brought near [to Allah] drink.
interpretation: This describes a spring in Paradise—identified in the preceding verse as Tasnim—from which the muqarrabun, those nearest to Allah among His righteous servants, drink directly and undiluted. Their drinking from it exclusively signifies their elevated rank, special nearness to Allah, and the distinct honor they receive in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed.
interpretation: This verse exposes the moral inversion of the guilty: their criminal rejection of truth made them arrogant enough to mock the believers, not because the believers were foolish, but because faith itself was despised by them. It is a divine rebuke of that contempt and a reassurance that such mockery does not diminish the believers’ standing with God; rather, it records the mockers’ guilt and points toward the coming reversal in which those who laughed will face the consequence of their deeds.

translation: And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another.
interpretation: This verse depicts the arrogant ridicule of the guilty toward the believers: whenever they encountered them, they would signal to one another with their eyes and gestures in mockery and contempt. It exposes how sin and disbelief can breed derision toward faith and the faithful, and it consoles the believers that such mockery does not lower their true rank before God; rather, it reveals the mockers’ own moral corruption and prepares for the reversal of roles in the Hereafter.

translation: And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting.
interpretation: This verse depicts the criminals’ smug mockery: after encountering the believers, they would go back to their own circle elated and jesting, treating the believers’ faith as a joke and reinforcing their own arrogance and contempt for the truth.

translation: And when they saw them, they said, “Indeed, these are surely misguided.”
interpretation: This is the disbelievers’ arrogant dismissal of the believers as people who have gone astray. Their judgment is not based on truth or divine guidance but on mockery, self-superiority, and rejection of the message; in reality, it is they who are astray, and their false accusation will be exposed and reversed in the Hereafter.

translation: And they were not sent over them as guardians.
interpretation: This means that those who mocked the believers had not been appointed by God as overseers, watchers, or keepers over them, with any right to judge, censure, or hold them accountable for their faith. Their mockery arose from arrogance and a false sense of superiority, not from any divinely granted authority. Ultimate guardianship, reckoning, and judgment belong to God alone; no human being has been made a guardian over another’s faith and destiny.

translation: So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the mockery and derision the disbelievers directed at the believers in worldly life will be reversed: the believers will laugh at the disbelievers, not out of petty vengeance but as the just outcome of God's judgment, in which the truth of faith is vindicated and the disbelievers' arrogance is exposed.

translation: On couches, they look on.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the righteous in Paradise: they are seated on adorned couches, gazing at the bounties, comforts, and honors God has prepared for them. Their looking is not restless or anxious but a serene contemplation of divine favor, reflecting perfect contentment and the dignity of those whom God has pleased.

translation: Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question affirming that the disbelievers will certainly receive the full and just recompense for their deeds. The term "thuwwiba" conveys repayment in kind: their mockery, arrogance, and rejection of faith will return upon them as punishment and humiliation, while the believers will be vindicated. The verse declares God's perfect justice—nothing they did is forgotten, and their end will correspond exactly to their actions.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. When the sky is split open.
interpretation: This opening of Surah Al-Inshiqaq describes a cosmic event of the Day of Judgment: the heaven, the vast celestial realm, will be cleft asunder in obedience to its Lord. The splitting of the sky signals the end of the present world order and the beginning of resurrection and reckoning. It is not meaningless destruction but a deliberate, obedient response to Allah’s command, preparing all creation for the final judgment.

translation: And it hearkens to its Lord and is dutiful.
interpretation: The heaven is depicted as hearing and obeying its Lord when His command unfolds. “وحقت” declares that this response is not optional but is truth and rightness itself: the heaven’s submission is exactly what is due to its Creator. It shows that all creation, however immense, is subject to God’s command and fulfills its purpose by obeying Him.

translation: And when the earth is spread out
interpretation: This describes a cosmic event on the Day of Judgment: the earth will be stretched, flattened, and leveled, its mountains and uneven features removed, so that it becomes an open plain. It will be made to expand or spread out by the command of its Lord, preparing the ground for the resurrection and the reckoning of all creatures.

translation: And it [the earth] casts out what is within it and becomes empty.
interpretation: This describes the earth at the onset of the Resurrection: it will disgorge all that it concealed—the dead and whatever was hidden within it—and become utterly void. It signifies the earth’s complete submission to its Lord’s command and the inevitability that nothing buried or hidden can remain concealed when God’s decree comes to pass.

translation: And it hearkens to its Lord and is bound to do so.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, the heaven will respond to its Lord’s command to split open, yielding in absolute obedience, for it is obligated by its very nature and by divine right to submit to Him; nothing in creation can resist His decree.

translation: O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with great exertion, and you will meet Him.
interpretation: This verse teaches that every human life is a continuous striving, a toil of body, mind, and soul, moving inevitably toward its Lord. Whether one labors in obedience, neglect, or rebellion, no action is outside this journey, and every person will finally stand before God for reckoning. Its meaning is at once a consolation and a warning: the hardships of life are not meaningless, nor are deeds forgotten, for the end of all exertion is the meeting with the One who created and sustains you. Thus it calls the human being to recognize the direction of his or her life, to choose labor that leads to God's pleasure, and to live with the certainty that returning to Him is inescapable.

translation: Then as for the one who is given his record in his right hand,
interpretation: This describes the state of the blessed on the Day of Judgment: receiving one’s book of deeds in the right hand is a sign of honor, Divine acceptance, and success, because the right hand is associated with good and blessing; such a person will have an easy reckoning and a joyful end.

translation: Then he will be brought to account with an easy accounting.
interpretation: This means that the believing servant whose record is given to him in his right hand will not be subjected to a severe or exacting interrogation. His deeds will be presented before him gently, and his shortcomings will be overlooked and forgiven by Allah’s mercy. It is a reckoning in which God pardons rather than punishes, showing His immense kindness and forbearance toward those He chooses to spare.

translation: And he will return to his family rejoicing.
interpretation: This describes the joyful end of the believer who receives his record in his right hand: after an easy reckoning, he goes back to his family and loved ones in Paradise, happy and delighted by God’s mercy and the good reward awaiting him.

translation: And as for the one who is given his record behind his back,
interpretation: It depicts the humiliating manner in which the wretched receive their deeds on the Day of Resurrection: their book is thrust from behind, often in the left hand, because in the world they put the divine Book behind their backs, rejected its commands, and followed their desires. This reversed delivery is itself a declaration of their failure: what should have been a source of honor and open accountability becomes a badge of disgrace and a prelude to regret and punishment.

translation: Then he will cry out for destruction.
interpretation: This is the despairing cry of the one condemned: he calls for his own ruin and annihilation, wishing he could be destroyed rather than endure the terror and punishment he now faces. It expresses utter regret, helplessness, and the severity of the reckoning for those who rejected faith and disobeyed God.

translation: and he will be made to burn in a blazing Fire.
interpretation: The verse announces that the one who rejects faith and accountability will be cast into the Fire, where he will directly suffer its scorching heat. The word "يُصلى" conveys being thrown into and enduring the fire’s torment, while "سعيراً" denotes an intensely ignited blaze. This is not merely a physical punishment but the inevitable consequence of choosing denial, arrogance, and heedlessness over faith and responsibility before God.

translation: Indeed, he was among his people rejoicing.
interpretation: This describes the person who receives his record of deeds in the Hereafter with doom: in worldly life he was delighted, carefree, and boastful among his family and associates, enjoying pleasures and feeling secure, never seriously considering that he would be held accountable before God. His former joy becomes a source of regret, because it was rooted in heedlessness of the Hereafter rather than in gratitude and obedience.

translation: Indeed, he thought that he would never return [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse exposes the false confidence of the one who denies the Hereafter: he imagined that death would be the end and that he would never be brought back to his Lord for reckoning. His heedlessness and wrongdoing were rooted in the assumption that there would be no return, no accountability, and no recompense. The verse thus rebukes that delusion and warns that every person will inevitably return to Allah, who is fully aware of all that was done.

translation: Yes indeed, his Lord was ever seeing him.
interpretation: This is a decisive refutation of the delusion that a person will not return to God after death; God’s constant awareness of him means that none of his deeds or state is hidden, and he will inevitably be brought back for reckoning and just recompense.

translation: So I swear by the twilight.
interpretation: In this oath, Allah calls the twilight—the reddish glow after sunset before the darkness of night—as a witness. It directs attention to the precise, ordered transition between day and night as a clear sign of His creative power and control over all things. Just as the light of day fades and this world’s phase comes to an end, the One who governs these changes is fully able to bring about the Hereafter, resurrection, and final reckoning.

translation: And by the night and what it envelops/gathers.
interpretation: Allah swears by the night and by all that it collects, covers, and causes to settle within it—people, animals, and other created beings that seek rest or concealment in its darkness. This oath points to Allah’s absolute lordship, His precise ordering of creation, and His power over all things that the darkness gathers and hides.

translation: And by the moon when it becomes full.
interpretation: Allah swears by the moon at its fullest and most complete phase, a sign of His precise ordering of creation through gradual stages. It points to the certainty that human life, deeds, and history also move through appointed stages toward their final fulfillment, and that the One who perfects the moon’s cycle will surely bring about resurrection and recompense.

translation: You will surely ride from stage to stage.
interpretation: This verse means that human beings are carried by divine decree through one condition after another—from life in this world to death, then resurrection, reckoning, and the final abode—so they should recognize these transitions and prepare for meeting their Lord.

translation: So what is [the matter] with them that they do not believe?
interpretation: This is a divine reproach and astonished question aimed at those who reject faith: it exposes that, after all the signs, proofs, and warnings, they have no valid excuse for disbelief. It calls them to examine why they withhold belief and to respond to the truth with faith in God and His revelations, warning that continued denial is unjustified and culpable.

translation: And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate themselves.
interpretation: This verse condemns the disbelievers’ arrogant refusal to humble themselves before Allah: although the Qur’an is clearly recited to them with its warnings and signs, they neither submit their hearts in faith nor bow their bodies in worship, showing that their obstruction is not due to any lack of divine guidance but to their own hardness and pride.

translation: But those who disbelieve are denying [the truth].
interpretation: This verse exposes the root of the disbelievers’ rejection: it is not due to ignorance or lack of clear evidence, but to willful denial. They repudiate the Qur’an, the message of the Prophet, and the reality of resurrection and accountability, knowingly choosing falsehood over faith.

translation: And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.
interpretation: This means that Allah’s knowledge fully encompasses the inward secrets of His creatures—what they hide in their hearts of denial, intention, belief, or plotting. Their outward rejection and secret motives are not hidden from Him, and He will recompense them with perfect justice according to what He knows.

translation: So give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This is an ironic and severe warning: the wording of “glad tidings” is used to announce the opposite, meaning that those addressed will certainly meet a painful punishment for their disbelief and wrongdoing. It conveys rebuke and certainty of recompense, not any actual good news.

translation: Except those who believe and do righteous deeds—they will have a reward that will never be cut off.
interpretation: This verse identifies the sole category exempt from the state of loss mentioned before: those whose hearts are grounded in faith and whose lives produce righteous action. Their recompense is not a temporary wage that ends or is diminished; it is a continuous, generous reward from God, secure from any decrease, interruption, or cancellation.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the sky with its constellations.
interpretation: Allah begins this surah with an oath by the heaven and its burūj—the great stars, celestial stations, or constellation-like pathways. The oath directs attention to the immense, precise order of the created heavens as a clear sign of His power, wisdom, and absolute mastery. Since an oath in the Qur’an often introduces a momentous truth, this oath prepares the listener to take seriously the message that follows: the Creator who arranged the heavens so perfectly is fully able to resurrect, judge, and recompense, and He is never unaware of what is done to the believers.

translation: And [by] the promised Day.
interpretation: The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has pledged to bring about, when all people will be raised and recompensed for their deeds; swearing by it underscores its certainty and the inevitability of divine judgment.

translation: And by the witness and the witnessed.
interpretation: This is an oath by Allah: the witness is Prophet Muhammad, who will testify for or against his community, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection, which will be witnessed by all creation and in which every deed will be brought to account.

translation: Cursed are the companions of the trench.
interpretation: This verse pronounces God’s curse and doom upon the persecutors who dug a fiery trench to kill believers. It teaches that using force and torture to suppress faith is an abomination before God, and that those who inflict such persecution are under divine condemnation, while the believers’ steadfastness is honored and their oppressors face certain punishment.

translation: The Fire, possessor of fuel.
interpretation: It refers to the blazing fire that was stoked with fuel, describing the intense and deliberately prepared torment into which the believers were thrown because of their faith; it conveys the extreme cruelty of the persecutors and the severity of the trial faced by the faithful.

translation: When they were seated around it
interpretation: This describes the persecutors sitting at the edge of the blazing trench, watching the believers being thrown into the fire. Their seated posture conveys deliberate complicity, cruel satisfaction, and a hardened heart, showing that they were not merely present but willfully gathered to witness and participate in the oppression.

translation: And they were witnesses over what they were doing to the believers.
interpretation: This verse condemns the persecutors as fully present and consciously observing the atrocities they inflicted. Their being “witnesses” means they were not ignorant or absent; they saw the suffering of the believers and consented to it, which intensifies their guilt. It exposes their hardened cruelty: they punished believers merely for their faith and then watched the torture, showing that the persecution was deliberate and collective.

translation: And they resented them for no reason except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse exposes the injustice of persecuting believers: the oppressed were hated not for any crime or moral failing, but precisely because they had faith in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. It teaches that tyrannical hostility toward faith often has no rational basis; it is resentment against the light of true belief itself. At the same time, the divine names Al-Aziz and Al-Hamid affirm that Allah is invincible in power and worthy of all praise, so He is neither unable to aid the believers nor unjust in allowing their trial. The verse thus consoles the persecuted and warns the oppressors that their hatred cannot diminish Allah’s majesty or the ultimate worthiness of trusting Him.

translation: The One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse affirms that absolute sovereignty and ownership of the heavens and the earth belong exclusively to Allah. His dominion is not merely nominal but encompasses creation, command, and the disposal of all affairs. The description “Witness over all things” means He is ever-present, all-knowing, and fully aware of every existent, action, intention, and occurrence—nothing is hidden from Him, and He will testify to and judge all deeds with perfect justice. This grounds trust, accountability, and awe of God.

translation: Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent — for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire.
interpretation: This is a severe warning to those who torment and oppress believers because of their faith, then persist in that oppression without turning back to God in repentance. Their crime combines violating the sanctity of belief, harming people for worshiping God alone, and stubborn refusal to repent. Therefore they deserve Hell, the encompassing punishment, and the burning fire, the consuming torment. The verse also indicates that repentance removes this punishment, since it mentions their not repenting as the reason for the threat.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds—they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse teaches that genuine faith is inseparable from righteous action: belief in God must bear fruit in deeds that conform to His command. The promise of gardens with rivers flowing beneath them signifies an eternal reward of life, provision, purity, and delight that never diminishes. Calling it “the great attainment” means it is the ultimate success—deliverance from ruin and the fulfillment of every true hope—because it is the enjoyment of God’s pleasure and everlasting bliss, not merely a temporary or material reward.

translation: Indeed, the grasp of your Lord is surely severe.
interpretation: This verse declares that when God seizes or punishes those who persist in wrongdoing, His retribution is overwhelming and irresistible; no power can shield them from His justice. It serves as a solemn warning to the oppressive and a reassurance that divine justice is certain and mighty.

translation: Indeed, He it is who originates and repeats [creation].
interpretation: This means that God alone brings creation into existence from nothing and is fully able to bring it back again after death. The verse affirms His absolute power over the beginning of creation and its restoration, and by extension it guarantees the resurrection and the final reckoning: those who persecuted believers and those who endured patiently will all be returned to Him for justice and reward.

translation: And He is the Forgiving, the Loving.
interpretation: Allah is the One who abundantly forgives sins and accepts repentance, and He is full of love, kindness, and affection toward His believing servants; He is beloved to them and draws them near with mercy.

translation: Possessor of the Throne, the Glorious.
interpretation: This means Allah alone is the Owner and Sovereign of the Mighty Throne, and He is the Glorious, Majestic, and praiseworthy; His dominion is absolute, His majesty is supreme, and He is exalted above all creation.

translation: Doer of whatever He intends.
interpretation: This affirms that Allah’s will is absolutely effective: whatever He decrees, He brings into existence and accomplishes without any hindrance, and no power can prevent, override, or alter His purpose.

translation: Has there reached you the story of the soldiers?
interpretation: This rhetorical question is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, to impress upon him the certainty and significance of the account of the former hosts who gathered to oppose God’s messengers and persecute the believers. It serves as both a consolation and a warning: just as God delivered His faithful servants and brought judgment upon those tyrannical armies, He will likewise aid the truth and deal with those who conspire against it. The verse calls for reflection on those past events as evidence of God’s unwavering justice and power over all worldly forces.

translation: Pharaoh and Thamud.
interpretation: It points to two archetypal examples of arrogant, powerful communities that rejected God's messengers and persecuted the believers—Pharaoh and the people of Thamud—and were consequently destroyed by divine punishment, serving as a warning that tyranny and denial of the truth inevitably meet the same fate.

translation: Nay, the disbelievers are in denial.
interpretation: Their problem is not a lack of evidence but a settled disposition of denial: they reject the truth as false and remain entrenched in that rejection, so the verse rebukes their obstinacy and warns that they are not outside God's grasp.

translation: And Allah is behind them, encompassing [them].
interpretation: This means that Allah’s knowledge, power, and decree surround the disbelievers from every side; they are never outside His grasp, and none of their schemes or movements can escape Him. He will bring them to account for all they do, and no power can prevent His judgment or frustrate His will.

translation: Nay, it is a glorious Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is not merely human speech or a fabricated claim, but a noble, majestic, and exalted revelation from God. Its glory is in its truth, inimitability, and divine preservation, so it deserves to be received with reverence, faith, and submission.

translation: in a preserved Tablet
interpretation: It refers to the Preserved Tablet with Allah, in which the Qur’an is inscribed and safeguarded from any change, corruption, addition, or subtraction, and protected from the reach of devils; it is the exalted, guarded source from which revelation was sent down.

translation: By the sky and the night comer.
interpretation: Allah takes an oath by the heaven and by the night visitor—the star that appears at night and pierces the darkness with its light—directing attention to His creative power and to the reality of resurrection and judgment.

translation: And what will make you know what the night comer is?
interpretation: The question is rhetorical, serving to magnify the matter and awaken awe, indicating that the night comer’s reality is too significant to be grasped without divine instruction.

translation: The piercing star.
interpretation: It is the bright celestial body whose light pierces through the darkness, showing Allah’s power to create light that cuts through the night and implying that He is able to bring forth life from death.

translation: There is no soul but that it has a guardian over it.
interpretation: This means that every human soul is placed under God's watchful guardianship: a keeper appointed by Him observes, preserves, and records the soul's deeds and conditions. No one is left unguarded or unaccountable, and nothing done in secret or in the open is overlooked. It calls the soul to live with awareness of divine supervision and to trust that God's justice and care encompass every person.

translation: So let man look at that from which he was created.
interpretation: The verse directs human beings to reflect on their humble origin, so that awareness of how they were first formed leads them to acknowledge the Creator’s power and the reality of being raised again for judgment.

translation: He was created from an ejected fluid.
interpretation: This verse means that the human being is brought into existence from the seminal fluid that is emitted with force, showing Allah’s power to create life from a seemingly insignificant substance and His ability to resurrect creation after death.

translation: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs.
interpretation: This describes the origin of the fluid from which the human being is created: it issues from the region between the spinal column and the ribs. In classical exegesis, this is understood as pointing to the reproductive substances of both the male and the female, and thereby to God’s wise design and power in bringing forth life from a seemingly ordinary fluid.

translation: Indeed, He is surely able to bring him back [to life].
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah, who created the human being from a lowly fluid, has full power to restore him to life after death, confirming the certainty of resurrection and the Hereafter.

translation: On the Day when the secrets are laid bare.
interpretation: It refers to the Day of Judgment, when everything concealed in people’s hearts and lives—hidden intentions, beliefs, and deeds—will be exposed and examined, so that each person is judged with full justice by God, and nothing secret remains hidden.

translation: Then he will have no power, nor any helper.
interpretation: On that Day, when hidden realities are exposed and every soul is held accountable, no created being will possess any strength to save himself or repel Allah’s judgment, nor will there be any helper, ally, or intercessor able to rescue him independently. All worldly power, support, and means will vanish, leaving the person utterly dependent on Allah’s mercy and justice.

translation: By the heaven which returns [the rain].
interpretation: Allah swears by the sky, which He created with the attribute of returning: it repeatedly sends down rain, revives the earth, and sustains creation. This points to His power, mercy, and ability to bring life back after death, and it reminds people that His provision and decrees recur by His command.

translation: And by the earth that is split open.
interpretation: Allah swears by the earth that cracks and splits open to bring forth vegetation, water, and hidden provisions, indicating His power to bring the dead back to life and to bring forth what is concealed.

translation: Indeed, it is a decisive word.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a decisive, clarifying speech that separates truth from falsehood and guidance from misguidance; it is conclusive, serious, and free of any falsehood or idle play.

translation: And it is not a jest.
interpretation: The Qur'an is not idle amusement or frivolous speech; it is a serious, decisive revelation from God that demands to be taken with utmost seriousness and accountability.

translation: Indeed, they are plotting a plot.
interpretation: This verse warns that the opponents of the Prophet were devising schemes to suppress the truth and harm the believers, but their plotting is described as merely a human plot—limited and ultimately futile—because God’s own plan will overtake and nullify it. It affirms that no conspiracy against divine guidance can succeed, and any respite given to the plotters is only temporary.

translation: And I am planning a plan.
interpretation: This verse declares that God has His own decisive plan to counter the schemes of those who oppose the truth. Their plotting cannot escape His knowledge or power; His plan is wise, encompassing, and certain to prevail, bringing about the ultimate failure of falsehood and the triumph of His decree.

translation: So give the disbelievers respite; give them respite for a little while.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet and the believers not to be impatient for the punishment of those who reject faith. God commands that the disbelievers be granted a brief delay and left to enjoy their worldly life for a short time, not as an honor or acceptance, but as a respite within God's wisdom. Their appointed term is near, and when it comes, they will be held to account for their denial and deeds.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High.
interpretation: This verse commands the believer to declare God's name absolutely transcendent and free of every deficiency, and to acknowledge Him as the Most High—exalted above all creation in His essence, attributes, and sovereignty. It directs all glorification and remembrance to God alone, purifying worship from any association with others.

translation: Who created and proportioned
interpretation: This verse describes God as the One who originated creation and then fashioned it with order, balance, and due proportion, giving every created thing its proper form and completing it in perfect measure according to His wisdom.

translation: And [it is He] who measured [all things] and then guided.
interpretation: Allah decreed and proportioned everything in creation according to a precise measure, then guided every creature to the path and purpose for which it was made, including guiding human beings to recognize and worship Him.

translation: And the One who brought forth the pasture.
interpretation: Allah is the One who causes green vegetation and grazing lands to emerge from the earth for the nourishment of His creatures, showing His power to bring life out of dead soil and His providential care, and pointing to His ability to bring forth life in the resurrection.

translation: Then He made it dark, dry stubble.
interpretation: This verse shows that all worldly growth, freshness, and prosperity are temporary and wholly subject to Allah’s power. The One who brings forth life and greenery can also reduce it to blackened, worthless remnants, pointing to His absolute control over life, death, decay, and resurrection, and calling man to attach himself to what endures with Allah rather than to the fleeting life of this world.

translation: We will make you recite, so you will not forget.
interpretation: This is a divine assurance to the Prophet Muhammad that Allah Himself will cause the Qur’an to be recited to him and will firmly establish it in his heart, so that he will not lose or forget what is revealed to him. It signifies Allah’s direct role in preserving the revelation in the Prophet’s memory as part of his preparation to convey it faithfully to humanity.

translation: Except what Allah wills. Indeed, He knows what is manifest and what is hidden.
interpretation: The exception places all human memory and forgetfulness under Allah’s sovereign will: nothing occurs outside His decree. The following sentence grounds this in His omniscience—He knows both what is openly expressed and what is concealed within hearts—so His will and knowledge govern all apparent and hidden realities.

translation: And We will ease you to the easy way.
interpretation: This is a divine promise to the Prophet Muhammad that God will make the path of guidance, prophethood, and righteous action easy and facilitated for him, enabling him to bear the message and follow the path of ease and tolerance.

translation: So remind, if the reminder benefits.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet, and every caller to God after him, to continue reminding people and conveying the truth. The condition “if the reminder benefits” does not cancel the duty of reminding when some reject it; it clarifies that the fruit of the reminder is reaped by those whose hearts are receptive and willing to heed. The obligation is sincere delivery of the message, while acceptance, guidance, and change of heart are left to God.

translation: The one who fears [Allah] will remember [and take heed].
interpretation: This means that sincere awe of Allah softens the heart and makes it receptive to divine reminders, so the person remembers, accepts admonition, and turns toward guidance and reform. Such fear is not merely an emotion but a reverent awareness of God that moves the will to heed the truth.

translation: And the most wretched will avoid it.
interpretation: The verse describes the person who is deeply wretched in his choices and destiny: having rejected the truth and turned away from God’s reminder, he distances himself from admonition and guidance. His avoidance is not mere forgetfulness but a deliberate shunning rooted in arrogance and heedlessness, standing in contrast to the God-conscious person who accepts the reminder and benefits from it.

translation: Who will enter the great Fire.
interpretation: This describes the wretched one who rejects faith and turns away from God; in the Hereafter he will be cast into the greatest Fire and made to endure its blazing torment, cut off from mercy and relief.

translation: Then he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This describes the state of the people of the Fire: they are not granted death that would end their punishment, nor are they given a true, beneficial life that would bring them relief. They remain in continuous torment, suspended between death and life, enduring an existence of unending suffering.

translation: Successful indeed is the one who purifies himself.
interpretation: This verse declares that true success and salvation belong to the one who purifies their inner self, cleansing it from disbelief, sin, and moral corruption and nurturing it through faith, sincere obedience, repentance, and righteous deeds. Such purification is the path to divine acceptance and lasting felicity, because it aligns the soul with its Creator and frees it from the bondage of base desires and spiritual disease.

translation: and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays.
interpretation: It means that true worship begins with the heart’s remembrance and invocation of God: the servant brings his Lord to mind, then turns to Him in prayer. This shows that prayer is not merely a ritual but the fruit of a living awareness of God, and that such remembrance is a cause of success and purification.

translation: But you prefer the worldly life.
interpretation: This is a reproach and a diagnosis of the human tendency to give precedence to the fleeting pleasures, possessions, and status of the present world over the enduring reward of the Hereafter. It does not condemn worldly life in itself, but the misplaced preference that leads a person to neglect God, accountability, and preparation for the eternal life. The verse calls the listener to reverse that priority and seek what is lasting.

translation: And the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse means that the reward, bliss, and final outcome of the Hereafter are superior in goodness to anything in this worldly life and are everlasting, never ending or diminishing. It directs the believer to prefer the enduring and greater good of the Hereafter over the fleeting and lesser pleasures of the present world.

translation: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures.
interpretation: The essential teachings just mentioned—success through purification, remembrance of God, prayer, and preferring the eternal Hereafter over worldly life—are not new or unique to the Qur’an. They were already present in the earlier revealed books, confirming the continuity of divine guidance and the agreement of the Qur’an with the core message of previous revelations.

translation: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
interpretation: These are the earlier revealed scrolls given to Abraham and Moses, cited to affirm that the core message of divine guidance, monotheism, and moral accountability was already present in previous revelations and is consistently renewed in the Qur’an.

translation: Has there come to you the narration of the Overwhelming?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question addressed to the Prophet—and through him, to all people—to emphasize the certainty and immense gravity of the Day of Judgment. Al-Ghashiyah, meaning 'the Overwhelming,' is a name for the Resurrection because its terrors will cover and overwhelm all creation; no one will be able to escape or avoid it. The verse awakens reflection upon that inevitable event and urges preparation for it through faith and righteous deeds.

translation: Faces on that Day will be humbled.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the faces of those who rejected faith will be downcast and subdued by humiliation, fear, and disgrace, as they are overwhelmed by the reality of divine judgment and the punishment awaiting them.

translation: Laboring, exhausted.
interpretation: This describes the faces of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: humbled and abased, they are worn out from striving in the world for other than God, and their labor yields no reward, leaving them in exhaustion and regret as they face the punishment.

translation: They will enter a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse affirms the reality and severity of Hellfire: those who rejected faith and persisted in wrongdoing will be cast into a Fire whose heat is intensely scorching, a punishment that is both painful and unavoidable. The description of the fire as "blazing" conveys that its torment is far beyond any earthly suffering, and it serves as a just recompense for arrogance, denial of God, and heedlessness of the Hereafter.

translation: It will be given to drink from a boiling spring.
interpretation: This describes the torment of the people of Hell: their drink is taken from a spring heated to its utmost degree, so it scalds and burns them without relieving their thirst. It is a fitting recompense for those who rejected faith and persisted in arrogance, and it stands in stark contrast to the pure, refreshing drinks prepared for the righteous in Paradise.

translation: They will have no food except from a thorny plant (ḍarīʿ).
interpretation: The verse means that the people of Hell have no nourishment available to them except a bitter, dry, thorny plant that neither satisfies hunger nor provides benefit; it is itself part of their punishment and suffering.

translation: It neither nourishes nor avails against hunger.
interpretation: This is a negation of all benefit in that food: it cannot strengthen or fatten the body, nor can it remove the pain of hunger. Thus the one who consumes it remains hungry and gains no sustenance, so the punishment is intensified by hunger joined to the food's complete uselessness.

translation: Faces, that Day, will be soft and radiant with bliss.
interpretation: This describes the faces of the people of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection: they will be luminous, serene, and softened by joy, reflecting the divine favor, comfort, and contentment they have been granted in reward for their faith and righteous deeds.

translation: With their striving, well-pleased.
interpretation: This describes the blessed on the Day of Judgment: they are pleased and content with the deeds they sent ahead in the world. Their former effort and striving for Allah has borne fruit in eternal reward, so they feel no regret or loss, only satisfaction that their labor was accepted and has led them to bliss.

translation: In a lofty Garden
interpretation: This describes the exalted station of the people of Paradise: their final abode is a Garden raised high in rank and nearness to God, far above every lower condition, where they will enjoy enduring honor and bliss.

translation: No idle talk will be heard therein.
interpretation: This describes one of the perfections of Paradise: its atmosphere is free from any vain, false, sinful, or hurtful speech. The inhabitants will not hear idle chatter, lying, obscenity, or anything that disturbs the heart or wastes time, because Paradise is a realm of purity, tranquility, and complete bliss. Their words will be good and harmonious, and all company therein will be free of the defects that mar speech in worldly life.

translation: Therein is a flowing spring.
interpretation: This describes one of the blessings of Paradise: within it is a spring whose water flows continuously and abundantly, never drying up or ceasing, serving the enjoyment and refreshment of its inhabitants.

translation: Therein are raised couches.
interpretation: These are couches or seats in Paradise that are elevated high, signifying the honor, dignity, and perfect comfort that Allah has prepared for the believers in the Hereafter.

translation: And cups placed (ready).
interpretation: These are drinking vessels in Paradise set out and prepared for its inhabitants, ever available and within easy reach, as a sign of honor and lasting delight.

translation: And cushions arranged in rows.
interpretation: This describes one of the comforts of Paradise: cushions or pillows placed in perfect, orderly rows, indicating that the believers will be received with honor, repose, and serene luxury in an abode whose furnishings are arranged without flaw or disorder.

translation: And carpets spread out.
interpretation: This describes one of the comforts prepared for the people of Paradise: fine, luxurious carpets or furnishings laid out and spread open for them, conveying perfect rest, honor, and ease in the gardens of bliss.

translation: Do they not then look at the camels, how they were created?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical call to reflect on the camel as a manifest sign of God's creative power and wise design. Its distinctive formation—its strength, endurance, capacity to survive in harsh arid conditions, and its many benefits for human life—points to a deliberate Creator rather than blind chance. The One who fashioned such a remarkable creature is fully able to resurrect, judge, and recompense His creation; therefore, neglecting this sign is a failure of reason and gratitude.

translation: And at the sky, how it is raised?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical call to reflect on the heaven’s vast, flawless elevation above creation: it is held aloft without any visible pillar, ordered with perfect precision, and stretched out as a sign of the Creator’s power, wisdom, and ability to raise and re-create, inviting the human heart to turn from heedlessness to faith and accountability.

translation: And at the mountains, how they are set up?
interpretation: This verse directs people to reflect on the mountains and how Allah firmly established and raised them. Their towering, rooted stability is a sign of divine power, wisdom, and precise ordering, and it points to the Creator’s ability to bring about resurrection and accountability just as He set up these immense creations.

translation: And to the earth, how it was spread out?
interpretation: The verse calls the human observer to consider the earth’s surface as a prepared, extended dwelling place: God has spread it out and made it level and habitable, so that people may settle, travel, cultivate, build, and receive provision. This order is a sign of the Creator’s power, wisdom, and mercy, inviting gratitude and worship of Him alone.

translation: So remind, [O Muhammad]; you are only a reminder.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet to continue reminding people of God’s message and warnings. It defines his role as that of a reminder and warner, not one who compels belief or controls hearts. His duty is to convey the reminder clearly, while guidance and acceptance remain with God.

translation: You are not over them a controller.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet, clarifying that his task is not to compel people to believe or to dominate their hearts and consciences. He is sent to convey the reminder, while guidance, coercion of hearts, and final reckoning belong to God alone.

translation: Except whoever turns away and disbelieves.
interpretation: This exception marks out those who deliberately refuse the reminder and persist in unbelief. It clarifies that the Prophet’s task is only to remind and warn, not to force faith; the one who turns away from that reminder and rejects it is not beyond God’s power but is left to God’s judgment, and his punishment is with God, who will requite him with the greatest punishment.

translation: So Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.
interpretation: This means that the one who turns away from the reminder and persists in disbelief will face the most severe and overwhelming punishment from Allah in the Hereafter—namely, the eternal punishment of Hellfire. The description “the greatest” emphasizes its extreme severity compared to any lesser hardship or chastisement in this worldly life.

translation: Indeed, to Us is their return.
interpretation: This verse affirms that every soul’s final destination and return is to Allah alone; He is the ultimate end of all created beings, and their return to Him is certain for reckoning and recompense according to His perfect justice and knowledge.

translation: Then indeed, upon Us is their account.
interpretation: This verse affirms that after all people return to God, He alone is the One who will settle their accounts and hold them responsible for what they did. Their reckoning is not left to any created being; God will judge them with perfect justice, exposing every deed and recompensing each soul exactly as it deserves.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the dawn.
interpretation: Beginning with Allah’s name invokes His mercy and blessing, and the oath by the dawn calls attention to the daily miracle of light emerging from darkness—a sign of Allah’s power to bring life after death, hope after hardship, and a new beginning after every night.

translation: And by the ten nights.
interpretation: These are the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah, a sacred period in which Allah swears an oath to emphasize its great virtue and the importance of worship, remembrance, and good deeds during it, including the Day of Arafah and the days of sacrifice.

translation: And by the even and the odd.
interpretation: This is an oath by the two categories of created existence: the even, meaning all things that are paired and complementary, and the odd, meaning that which is singular and unmatched—ultimately pointing to Allah’s absolute oneness and to the balanced order He has placed throughout creation.

translation: And by the night when it passes away.
interpretation: Allah swears by the night as it departs and comes to an end with the arrival of dawn, pointing to His power over the alternation of night and day and inviting reflection on the passing of time and the signs within it.

translation: Is there in that an oath for one who has understanding?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question intended as an affirmative statement: indeed, in these signs and oaths there is sufficient evidence and a solemn confirmation for anyone who possesses a sound, restraining intellect. Such a person grasps that the oaths point to God’s power, wisdom, and the certainty of His promise and judgment, while the heedless pass over them without benefit.

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Aad?
interpretation: The rhetorical question calls the listener to heed the exemplary punishment of the people of 'Aad, showing that God's lordship includes sovereign justice over arrogant nations; their destruction stands as a warning that rejecting divine messengers and persisting in tyranny invites the same reckoning.

translation: Iram, possessor of the lofty pillars
interpretation: This refers to the ancient people of 'Ad, called Iram, who were marked by towering pillars—whether immense buildings or great physical stature—as a display of their worldly strength and pride; their mention is a warning that such grandeur cannot protect a people from divine punishment when they persist in arrogance and rejection of God.

translation: The like of which was not created in the lands.
interpretation: This verse describes Iram, the city of the people of ‘Ad: God had granted them an unmatched degree of worldly construction, power, and physical strength, so that no other city or people in the lands was created like them. Its meaning is that their exceptional worldly distinctiveness was a divine sign and a test, not evidence of righteousness; because they used it for arrogance and denied their messenger, it became a cause of their ruin.

translation: And Thamud, who hewed out the rocks in the valley.
interpretation: This refers to the people of Thamud, who were given great skill and power to carve secure dwellings and monuments from solid rock, yet their material strength and architectural genius did not protect them from God's punishment when they rejected His prophet and persisted in arrogance and disbelief. Their mention serves as a warning that worldly might, industry, and civilization are of no avail if they are not joined with faith and obedience to God.

translation: And Pharaoh, possessor of the stakes.
interpretation: The “stakes” signify Pharaoh’s ruthless tyranny: he entrenched his power so firmly and used such cruel means—such as pinning and torturing people—that he became a symbol of oppressive rule that God ultimately uproots and punishes.

translation: Those who transgressed all bounds in the lands
interpretation: This refers to the arrogant and powerful nations—such as ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh—who exceeded the limits set by God, spread corruption, and used their might to oppress people and oppose divine guidance, so their tyranny brought about their destruction.

translation: and they increased corruption therein
interpretation: This verse condemns the transgressing nations for multiplying corruption in the lands: they persisted in disbelief, tyranny, injustice, and oppression, corrupting both their societies and their relationship with God, until their excess in wrongdoing brought down divine punishment upon them.

translation: So your Lord poured out upon them a whip of punishment.
interpretation: This means that God afflicted those arrogant and corrupt nations with a severe, humiliating, and overwhelming chastisement, likened to a whip because it struck them suddenly and painfully as a just recompense for their tyranny and corruption.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.
interpretation: This means that God is fully aware of all that His creation does and that no one can escape His notice or evade His judgment; He watches over every action and will hold every soul accountable for what it has earned.

translation: As for man, when his Lord tests him and honors him and grants him favor, he says, 'My Lord has honored me.'
interpretation: This verse critiques the human tendency to judge one’s standing with God solely by worldly circumstances. Wealth, honor, and comfort are not automatic signs of divine pleasure; they are also a trial. The person who receives abundance and says, “My Lord has honored me,” may be sincere, but the verse exposes the deeper error of assuming that prosperity proves spiritual worth and that hardship proves rejection. True honor before God is tied to God-consciousness, gratitude, and humility, not merely to the gifts one receives in this life.

translation: But as for when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."
interpretation: This verse exposes the human tendency to measure God's favor solely by material abundance. When provision is narrowed, a person wrongly concludes that God has abandoned or humiliated him, forgetting that wealth and poverty are both tests. True honor is not in riches, nor is humiliation in limited means; rather, God tests by both ease and hardship to see whether one remains grateful, patient, and faithful. The one who says "My Lord has humiliated me" errs by interpreting a test as a judgment of worth, whereas God's wisdom may be purifying, disciplining, or elevating through patience.

translation: No! Rather, you do not honor the orphan.
interpretation: This is a stern divine rebuke of the human tendency to measure honor by wealth and status while neglecting the weak. The orphan is singled out because they are especially vulnerable and have no one to defend them. To “honor” the orphan means to treat them with dignity, protect their rights, show them kindness, provide for their needs, and defend them from injustice. The verse condemns those who withhold such honor, revealing that their claim to superiority is morally hollow before God.

translation: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.
interpretation: It condemns not only the failure to feed the needy but also the refusal to urge others toward that duty, showing that neglect of the poor becomes a collective moral failing when people neither give nor encourage giving; care for the destitute is thus presented as a shared obligation that must be upheld and promoted, not ignored or left to others.

translation: And you devour inheritance with greed.
interpretation: This verse condemns the unscrupulous habit of consuming the estates left by the dead voraciously and indiscriminately, without regard for what is lawful or unlawful or for the rights of others. The phrase “aklan lamman” intensifies the rebuke: it is not merely taking inheritance but swallowing it whole in greedy accumulation, often depriving the weak—such as orphans, widows, and women—of their rightful shares. It exposes a moral corruption in which love of wealth hardens the heart against justice and mercy.

translation: And you love wealth with an excessive love.
interpretation: This verse reproaches the human tendency to cling to wealth with a deep, immoderate attachment that dominates the heart. Such love of money becomes a spiritual disease: it breeds greed, hardheartedness, miserliness, and neglect of God, the Hereafter, and the rights and needs of others. The verse warns that when wealth is loved for its own sake rather than as a means to do good, it corrupts one’s priorities and turns worldly gain into an idol that competes with faith and generosity.

translation: No! When the earth is crushed, crushed and crushed.
interpretation: This is a forceful warning of the Day of Judgment: the earth will be violently shattered and repeatedly leveled until all worldly stability, structures, and elevations are utterly undone. The emphatic repetition conveys the certainty and severity of that event, and the opening rebuke rejects human heedlessness and denial of accountability before God.

translation: And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank.
interpretation: This depicts the awesome scene of the Day of Judgment: the Lord will come to pass judgment over His creation, and the angels will appear in orderly ranks, demonstrating His sovereign power and the certainty of the final reckoning.

translation: And Hell will be brought forth that Day. On that Day man will remember, but how will that remembrance benefit him?
interpretation: This verse confronts the human being with the terrifying reality of the Hereafter: when Hell is made present, every person will suddenly recall the truth they denied and the deeds they committed, but that memory will come too late to change anything. It teaches that the time for reflection, repentance, and action is now, in this worldly life, because once the Day of Judgment arrives, regret and remembrance cannot rescue anyone. The verse thus warns against heedlessness and procrastination, urging immediate turning to God and preparing for accountability before the moment when no amendment is possible.

translation: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [good deeds] for my [hereafter] life!"
interpretation: This is the regretful cry of the heedless one on the Day of Judgment. By “my life” is meant the eternal life of the Hereafter, not the fleeting life of this world. The verse teaches that true life is the everlasting one, and that it must be prepared for by sending forward righteous deeds, faith, and obedience before death. Too late, the person realizes that he wasted his opportunity and wishes he had lived for what truly matters.

translation: So on that Day, none will punish as He will punish.
interpretation: God’s chastisement on the Day of Judgment is uniquely severe and belongs to Him alone; no created being can inflict a punishment comparable to His, because His judgment is absolute, perfectly just, and executed with a power and knowledge no creature shares. The verse thus underscores both the terror of divine retribution for the guilty and the fact that ultimate requital is God’s exclusive prerogative.

translation: And no one can bind as He binds.
interpretation: This declares that God’s power to restrain, chain, and punish on the Day of Judgment is unique and unmatched. The “binding” signifies the fetters, confinement, and severe retribution inflicted upon the guilty, which no created being can duplicate, resist, or overturn. It affirms that absolute authority over punishment and judgment belongs to God alone.

translation: O reassured soul
interpretation: This is a divine address of honor to the believing soul that has attained inward peace and certainty through faith in God, contentment with His decree, and trust in His promise.
