Even if they claim to worship God, their association of partners with Him means they are not worshipping the same object of worship as the Prophet, so no compromise or mixing between monotheism and polytheism is possible.

translation: To you is your religion, and to me is my religion.
interpretation: This verse declares a clear separation between the way of the disbelievers and the way of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him): they may keep their religion, but he and the believers hold exclusively to Islam. It is not an affirmation that all religions are equally true; rather, it is a declaration of disavowal from shirk and of firm adherence to pure monotheism. The verse teaches that there can be no compromise in matters of creed and worship: the Prophet worships none but Allah alone, while they persist in their own beliefs. Thus it establishes distinct religious identity, freedom from forced conformity, and unwavering loyalty to tawhid, leaving judgment between the two paths to Allah.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest,
interpretation: This verse informs the Prophet Muhammad that Allah’s help and the opening of Makkah are about to occur, signaling the decisive triumph of the message he was sent with. Its deeper meaning is that victory is not a moment for self-congratulation but for humble awareness of Allah’s sovereignty: when divine support arrives and the opposition is opened to faith, the appropriate response is to turn back to Allah in praise and seek His forgiveness, recognizing that the success belongs entirely to Him and that even the greatest worldly triumph should lead the believer toward greater devotion, gratitude, and reliance upon Allah.

translation: And you saw the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes.
interpretation: This verse describes the fulfillment of Allah's promise to His Prophet after the conquest of Makkah: the Arab tribes, who had previously resisted or hesitated, began embracing Islam in successive large groups. It signifies that guidance and victory come from Allah alone, not from human effort, and it was a clear sign that the message had prevailed and the mission was nearing completion. The Prophet is thus directed to meet this great blessing with humble praise of Allah and seeking His forgiveness, acknowledging that the mass acceptance of Islam was solely by Allah's grace.

translation: So glorify the praises of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.
interpretation: This command joins together glorification of God, praise of Him, and seeking His forgiveness. It teaches that the servant should never become self-satisfied, even when granted success or victory; rather, all goodness is from God, and one must remain humble, grateful, and aware of one’s shortcomings. Seeking forgiveness is not merely for sins but also for any deficiency in gratitude, worship, and reliance upon God. The verse then grounds this command in God’s attribute of being Tawwāb: He continually accepts those who turn back to Him, forgives them, and responds to repentance with mercy. Thus the verse calls the believer to turn to God in praise and humility, with confidence that He does not reject a sincere return to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.
interpretation: This is a divine decree of ruin against Abu Lahab, a bitter opponent of the Prophet. His “hands” signify his actions, wealth, influence, and schemes, all of which will fail and bring him no benefit against Allah’s will. The verse pronounces his loss in this life and the Hereafter, and it stands as a warning that persistent enmity to the Prophet and the truth leads to utter perdition.

translation: His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned.
interpretation: The verse declares that neither accumulated riches nor any worldly gains, offspring, or deeds he acquired can rescue him or avert the punishment that has come upon him; all such means are utterly powerless before God’s decree and do not substitute for faith and righteous action.

translation: He will be burned in a Fire of flame.
interpretation: This is a severe warning that the one addressed—Abu Lahab—will inevitably enter and suffer the blazing Fire of Hell, whose flames will engulf him as punishment for his hostility to the Prophet and his message.

translation: And his wife, the carrier of firewood.
interpretation: This describes the wife of Abu Lahab as one who actively supported his hostility by carrying harmful burdens—understood as spreading malicious talk and placing obstacles in the Prophet’s path—so that she shares in the condemnation and punishment.

translation: Upon her neck is a rope of twisted fibre.
interpretation: This describes the humiliation and punishment awaiting the wife of Abu Lahab, who used her wealth and status to mock and harm the Prophet. The twisted rope around her neck signifies that in the Hereafter she will be bound and dragged into Hell, her arrogance and worldly adornments turned into a mark of disgrace; the very neck she prized will bear this degrading bond.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say, "He is Allah, the One."
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah’s absolute oneness: He is uniquely one in His essence, names, attributes, and actions, without any partner, equal, rival, or plurality; He is indivisible and utterly unlike His creation, and all worship and dependence belong to Him alone.

translation: Allah, the Eternal Refuge, upon whom all depend.
interpretation: This means that Allah is the absolute Master and Self-Sufficient One to whom every creature turns in need; He is perfect, needing nothing, while all things depend entirely upon Him.

translation: He neither begets nor is born.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is absolutely unique and eternal, free of all lineage and origin: He has no offspring and no parent, is not generated from anything, and does not generate anything in the manner of created beings. It negates any claim that He has a son, was born, or shares in the nature of created things, establishing His perfect self-sufficiency and incomparability.

translation: And there is none comparable to Him.
interpretation: This verse affirms God’s absolute oneness and incomparability: no being, force, or concept is equal to Him, resembles Him, or can serve as a peer in His essence, attributes, or divine rights.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say, 'I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak.'
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad, and every believer, to seek protection with Allah alone, addressing Him as the Lord of the daybreak—the One who splits open the dawn and brings light out of darkness. It teaches that the power that dispels the darkness of night is the same power able to dispel every form of harm, fear, and evil. Therefore, refuge is not sought in any created being, but in the Creator, who governs all things and alone can truly protect and deliver.

translation: From the evil of what He created.
interpretation: This phrase teaches that refuge is sought in God alone from every harm, wickedness, and destructive power that can proceed from any created being—whether human, jinn, animal, or any other created thing—and from the evils latent within creation itself. It directs the heart to depend on the Creator for protection against the evil of the created, since nothing in creation can harm or benefit except by His permission.

translation: And from the evil of the darkness when it settles,
interpretation: This is a plea for God’s protection from every harm that emerges, intensifies, or becomes concealed when night falls and darkness spreads—whether from hidden wrongdoers, fearsome creatures, or any evil that moves under the cover of darkness—so the believer seeks refuge with God from such harm.

translation: And from the evil of the blowers into knots,
interpretation: This verse seeks refuge in God from the harm of sorcerers who tie knots and blow upon them to cast malicious spells. It acknowledges the reality of such evil practices but directs the believer to rely solely on God for protection, since no created power can cause harm independently of His will.

translation: And from the evil of an envier when he envies.
interpretation: This verse teaches that envy is a dangerous spiritual and social evil: the envier resents God’s favor upon another and may wish or work for its removal, so one should seek God’s protection from both the hidden malice in the envier’s heart and any harm it may produce when it becomes active.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Bestower of mercy. Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet and every believer to declare total reliance upon Allah and to seek His protection alone, addressing Him as Rabb an-Nas—the Lord, Owner, Nurturer, and Sovereign of all humanity. It teaches that ultimate refuge belongs only to the One who creates, sustains, and governs all people, and that no created being can provide absolute safety. Seeking refuge in Him means turning to Him for protection from every harm, especially the hidden whisperings and evils that afflict people. The phrase “Lord of mankind” emphasizes that His care and authority encompass all human beings, and it directs the heart away from dependence on any human or created power toward exclusive trust in Allah.

translation: King of mankind
interpretation: Allah is the absolute Sovereign and Ruler over all human beings. He alone owns, governs, and disposes their affairs with perfect authority, wisdom, justice, and mercy; no one shares in His kingship or has any independent power over mankind.

translation: The God of mankind
interpretation: It affirms that Allah is the sole deity and true object of worship for all people; every human being's ultimate devotion, fear, hope, and reliance should be directed to Him alone, and no created thing shares in that divinity.

translation: From the evil of the whispering, withdrawing one.
interpretation: This verse seeks refuge in God from the harm of the whisperer who secretly casts doubts and evil suggestions into the heart, and who slinks away or retreats when God is remembered. It refers especially to Satan, who tempts inwardly and then withdraws, and it teaches that protection from such hidden evil is sought only from God.

translation: Who whispers into the breasts of people
interpretation: This verse describes the stealthy method of the whisperer: he does not compel outwardly but casts secret suggestions into the innermost chests—the seat of thought, intention, and belief—so as to plant doubt, desire, and misgiving in the human heart. It exposes that the real battleground is inward, and therefore people must seek God’s protection from this hidden, retreating insinuation that targets the core of their consciousness and faith.

translation: From among the jinn and mankind.
interpretation: This identifies the source of the whispering: it can come from unseen jinn or from human beings, so refuge is sought from both kinds of tempters, whether spiritual or human.
